Rio placed her glass down on the edge of the bed and stood to move over to Agatha, watching as her back straightened out and she looked cautious suddenly.

Rio gave her every opportunity to move away, to pull back, but when she didn’t her hand found purchase on Agatha’s cheek and she brushed her thumb delicately across her high cheekbone, a little frown forming on her face as she took Agatha in.

Maybe it was the two beers and the tequila talking, but she thought there was now a faint blush on Agatha’s cheeks where she still held her.

“Thank you.”

Agatha nodded gently, careful not to dislodge Rio’s hand and Rio watched in surprise as Agatha’s eyes fluttered closed and she raised her hand to hold Rio’s wrist lightly, her face turning a fraction of an inch so the corners of her lips grazed Rio’s palm.

It was so soft, so intimate that Rio forgot herself and moved closer, ducking her head slightly in order to press a kiss to Agatha’s other cheek.

But before she made contact, there was noise in the hall and Rio pulled back properly, her hand reluctantly dropping from Agatha as she turned to see who would be arriving now.

Just as Jen stepped into the room Agatha pushed herself off the ledge beside her and muttered: “don’t say anything”.

“Jen.”

“Agatha.”

Rio now took Agatha’s position on the window ledge, shrinking back a little from the furious looking woman in the doorway and noticing that Alice was just behind her.

“You can’t just offer-…”

“Come on, Rio is all anyone is talking about. It’ll be her or me and right now my money is on her. A couple vacation snaps and that’s it. You can have full creative control.”

Jen huffed and scowled over at Rio who was still hiding behind Agatha slightly, which, admittedly she wasn’t too proud of.

“Fine. Vidal, these pictures of you on the beach better not come out. Can’t have anyone thinking it was Agatha you were fucking.”

It was Rio’s turn to blush at this and she cleared her throat quietly as Agatha turned to her and offered her a hand, “Let’s get this over with.”

Rio blinked and momentarily forgot herself as everyone stared at her and Agatha actually wriggled her fingers at her. But she took her hand and found it to be just as warm and comforting as it had felt the previous night when she was off her face drunk.

They walked like that, unnecessarily hand in hand down to the pool area and Agatha only released her hand again when Jen pulled Agatha in the other direction.

“We’re getting one shot and that is it,” Jen announced firmly, “and we will only use it if I am happy with it. Goddamn Agatha Harkness does not hang about pools with nobody actors.”

“Hey,” Alice and Rio said quickly and even Agatha slapped Jen’s arm lightly. “Play nice.”

“Whatever,” Jen said in lieu of an apology and shot Alice a small smile over Agatha’s shoulder that promised she was at least half joking.

Whilst Jen worked on the composition of the shot, Alice turned to Rio and began fluffing up her hair, to what aim, Rio had no idea.

“You got a swimsuit on beneath that?”

“Yeah but isn’t that a bit much?”

“No, not when it’s your one shot to be across the internet with Agatha. Take it off.”

Rio rolled her eyes and crossed her arms over herself to seamlessly slip her t-shirt over her head and tossed it in the sun bed.

“These too,” Alice instructed, motioning to Rio’s shorts.

“Don't be ridiculous.”

“And don’t be a prude, Miss I Fucked A Stranger On The Beach.”

Rio huffed but supposed she deserved that and she shuffled out of her linen shorts, feeling a bit like an idiot just standing awkwardly in her bikini.

“Okay, okay!” Jen announced, having been strolling around the area with her phone and Agatha in tow as a test subject to check the light.

“Two options-…” but she stopped as she spotted what Rio was now wearing and rolled her eyes, “Really, Alice? This isn’t a porno.”

Rio looked down at herself, suddenly fearful she’d somehow stripped naked without meaning to. But she hadn’t. She was still very much covered up where it mattered.

“They’re by the pool, they’re friends, they’re on vacation. It would be weird for Agatha to be in a bathing suit and Rio to not be. Plus she looks more femme like this, it’ll help with the rumours.”

“What rumours?” Agatha asked suddenly, watching the scene from the glass barrier that separates the edge of the hills from the drop below it.

“Well two hot women on vacation together, one a lesbian?” Alice asked with raised brows and Rio had to look away for fear she was blushing too much at the insinuation.

“Agatha is happily married,” Jen accused with a frown and Rio was beginning to wonder if ‘happily married’ were tattooed somewhere on Agatha’s body.

“I know,” Alice agreed with a slight frustration in her tone, “everyone knows. So Rio not rocking up looking like a total-…”

“Don’t say it,” Rio interjected with a frown, slapping Alice’s shoulder.

“-… well, it’ll help the cause.”

Alice had clearly won the battle and had turned to Rio to take her arm and whisper in her ear, “Sorry. I just want you in that bikini for the shot. You look hot.”

Rio rolled her eyes and poked Alice in the ribs before she moved over to where Agatha and Jen were and offered herself up with a little display of opening her arms to Jennifer, “Where do you want me?”

Jen got to work immediately and had no qualms about moving Rio without asking if it were okay she touch her. It felt a lot like being in a set or in a makeup trailer and so Rio didn’t mind.

But things changed when Jen started moving Agatha and it was Agatha who was touching her now, rather than Jen.

Jen had positioned Rio to be leaning her elbows back against the top of the glass barrier, her right leg up and bent so her foot was back on it.

She’d forced Rio to face forward and her hair to drape across her shoulders, spending time in adjusting it until she was satisfied.

And then Agatha.

Agatha was positioned next to Rio, facing her.

Jen had made her place her right elbow on the barrier and her left hand on Rio’s shoulder.

Agatha’s hand was warm and Rio glanced to the side to see that she was watching her, her steely blue gaze intense in the early evening sun.

It was the golden hour and behind Agatha’s head was a halo of light. She looked breathtaking and Rio was glad she had the barrier behind her to hold her up, to keep her from melting before her.

“No,” Alice was saying suddenly, holding her own phone up to look through the camera.

“The hand on Rio’s shoulder looks weird. Agatha, put it on her stomach.”

“My stomach?” Rio asked in panic, breaking her pose and standing up properly, “Why my stomach?”

“It’s just less awkward than your shoulder. These needs to just look like two friends shooting the shit together by their ridiculous pool,” Alice shouted back across the pool, frowning at the dramatic reaction of her friend.

“You’re right,” Jen agreed, “makes it easier to see her ring too.”

Rio blanched a little and slowly settled back into position, glancing at Agatha as Jen continued to fluff her hair behind her and Agatha asked: “This okay?”

“Yeah, yeah,” Rio said quickly, properly blushing now she’d caused such a fuss and turning away again. “Totally fine.”

She tensed as Agatha moved her hand down to rest against her stomach, and glanced askance at Agatha again, seeing that she was looking down at where her hand pale hand was now resting against Rio’s tanned skin.

Rio cleared her throat quietly and forced herself to relax, feeling the slight movements of Agatha’s fingers as she tried to find the most natural pose on Rio’s flat abs.

Not unused to being touched during photoshoots, and not even unfamiliar with posing with Agatha now for photos, this shouldn’t have felt odd.

And after yesterday, with Agatha’s hands all over her torso, this should have felt natural.

But Rio’s body was screaming at her that Agatha Harkness was touching her publicly, for millions of people to see, and when Jen pushed Agatha a couple inches towards her she shifted uncomfortably so that Agatha dropped her hand from her.

“Shoulder’s fine,” she muttered quietly and went to place her hand back there before Rio grabbed it suddenly and placed it back just below her sternum, over where her diaphragm would be.

“It’s fine,” Rio reassured just as softly, keeping her hand over Agatha’s until she was sure she wouldn’t pull away.

Agatha only nodded once and kept her hand still against Rio’s skin.

Jen eventually moved away and went to stand by Alice to take the shot. Both Agatha and Rio tried smiling, tried smiling at each other, but neither Jen nor Alice were happy and both frequently pointed out the sun going in and the golden hour coming to a close.

“More energy! Look like you like each other!”

Rio laughed a little and shot Agatha a smile, raising a brow, “Nothing says ‘I like you’ more than a fake photoshoot on vacation.”

Agatha only rolled her eyes and moved the hand that wasn’t still over Rio’s stomach to poke Rio in the ribs suddenly, expertly finding her most sensitive point and causing Rio to burst out a laugh and lurch forwards.

Agatha laughed with her and caught Rio’s back as she threw herself back again, the shock of the jab making her forget she was on the precipice of a cliff with a thin, single pane of glass protecting her from here and infinity.

“Careful!”

Rio curled her arms around the arm that held her steady and caught her breath back steadily, not realising that Agatha had pressed against her side and now was basically just holding her where they stood.

“We got it,” Jen sang as the two women at the edge of the pool turned to smile at the other, suddenly both shy in their hold but neither pulling away.

It was Rio who broke the spell, peeling herself from Agatha gingerly, and feeling suddenly cool in the warm air without Agatha close by.

But she shook it off, forced herself to focus as she went to look over Alice’s shoulder at the photo they’d chosen of the hundreds they’d taken.

Rio was on the way to lurching forwards, her mouth open in a laugh and her eyes wide with surprise.

Agatha’s hand remained pride of place on her front and her right hand was close by her ribs where she’d just delivered the fatal blow.

Agatha looked pleased with herself, smug and beautiful in the light.

They looked good together, even Rio could see that. And perhaps Agatha could too because she’d appeared at her side and had briefly squeezed Rio’s hand where they stood, both silently acknowledging what was clear in the photo: Agatha Harkness and Rio Vidal were about to break the internet.

“Ring still obvious,” Jen said slowly, scrutinising every inch of the photo and now literally zooming in to see every inch of the two of them up close.

“Can we not zoom in on my breasts, please?” Agatha asked with more than a little annoyance as Jen focused in on her client’s body and ignored everything about Rio.

“Hey, check Rio over too. No nips slipping. No drool.”

“Drool? Rude.”

Agatha laughed beside her and Rio scowled, but looked back down again in time to see a zoomed in shot of Agatha’s face. She looked unreal. How could she look that good in a candid shot? But she looked up again and saw Agatha watching her closely and she raised her brows as she said: “You look good.”

Agatha fought a smirk and raised a brow at this, tilting her head as she surveyed Rio. “And you… are surprisingly shy about being touched when you fucked a girl on the beach.”

“Ooooohh,” Alice sang in amusement, looking between Agatha and Rio, all anger from the incident before clearly gone now she’d secured her client the photo of the century.

Rio narrowed her gaze at Agatha but saw no malice reflected back at her and only a smug smile on that annoyingly gorgeous face.

It infuriated her.

“Did Agatha Harkness just say ‘fuck’?” She asked with a smirk, and watched as Agatha narrowed her gaze further.

“Agatha, maybe you should start wearing your engagement ring,” Jen was saying, her phone zoomed back in on the hand over Rio’s stomach. “More sparkle.”

But Rio had turned around to be closer to Agatha and the older woman looked suddenly nervous, and a little surprised at the proximity again, but Rio didn’t leave her guessing for long.

In one, quick, strong, movement, she’d pushed Agatha into the deep end of the pool.

Two gasps rang out behind her and Rio laughed as Agatha resurfaced looking livid, throwing her wild her back over her head and practically growling at Rio on the edge of the pool.

“Rio! What the fuck!” Jen bellowed, as Alice slapped her hand over her mouth from beside her.

“Rio, what the fuck?”

Rio crouched down to get closer as Agatha moved towards the edge of the pool, ignoring the two behind her. “Sorry, I must have slipped.”

“You’re an ass,” Agatha accused just as she reached up and tugged Rio into the pool with her, both disappearing beneath the water for a few seconds before resurfacing with splutters of laughter.

It was the laughter that softened the reaction of the two people hired to be what they were both silently considering in that moment to be glorified babysitters to the two actresses now gasping for air and laughing in the water below them.

“She has an Oscar,” Jen said in disbelief as she watched her client throw a splash of water in Rio’s direction.

Alice only rolled her eyes and she took Jen’s hand, tugging her away to the kitchen, “Shame she’s straight. Think of what we could do together if they were together.”

“Rio wishes,” Jen muttered as the two disappeared into the villa.

In the pool Rio was laughing so hard she had to swim to the side and support herself with one hand, trying to catch her breath.

“God. You weren’t supposed to pull me in!”

Agatha was treading water somewhere behind her and laughed, “Like I wouldn’t. You think I’d let you get away with trying to drown me? I have an Oscar!”

Rio laughed harder again and turned, twisting her wrist to keep herself up still on the side. “Yes, I’ve heard! Where is it? The bathroom? The bedroom?”

She wriggled her brows suggestively and Agatha scoffed and threw a wave of water Rio’s way.

“The office. My office.”

“No fun,” Rio accused with a grin reaching her other hand behind her to hold the wall too.

“And exactly why would an Oscar be fun in the bedroom?”

Rio shrugged a little, smiling still, “Remind your husband how powerful you are. Remind yourself.”

“I don’t need reminding,” Agatha said with a grin, moving over to mimic Rio’s hold on the wall.

“Maybe. Still. Something sexy about it.”

“Well maybe you can put yours in your bedroom.”

“Mmm, I think I have a while yet. This one’s yours.”

Agatha hummed softly and pushed off the wall again, choosing to tread water in front of Rio instead, “Don’t be so sure.”

Rio raised her brows, “Are you gonna vote for me?”

Agatha released a laugh and tilted her head back, exposing her neck to Rio which made her glance down at it and lose her train of thought for a second.

“How about this?” Agatha asked, catching Rio’s eye again with a smirk when she looked back across at her, “If I vote for you, and you win, you have to thank me first.”

Rio scoffed and rolled her eyes, “Easy. Wanda will be a little pissed but-…”

“No, Rio Vidal, first. Before god, before your parents, everyone. Not just ‘your fellow nominees’.”

Rio laughed and poked her tongue into the side of her cheek, watching as Agatha’s eyes twinkled with mischief and something else she couldn’t name.

“On the very slim chance that I’m nominated and win, then yes. I’ll thank you first. Before anyone. Which might be hard to explain to my mom.”

Agatha hummed and nodded, “Good. Then that’s one vote in your favour.”

“And what if you win?”

“What if I win?” Agatha asked with a grin, “You can’t vote. So if I win, you’ve done nothing to help me.”

“Ah,” Rio sang out, kicking her feet out gently before her and stretching her body out near the surface of the water. Agatha’s gaze dropped along the length of her and she moved to the side, now only a foot or so away.

“That photo of us was gold. That’ll help you. And it’ll help your profile with the younger audiences.”

“Younger audiences?” Agatha gaped at Rio, reaching to grab the side so she could rest her arms and legs that were working to keep her afloat. “You know I’m not that much older than you?”

Rio brought her body back in to be back against the wall.

“Older, though. Old enough for me to make you seem very cool for hanging out with me.”

“That is so-…”

“So what?” Rio teased, finally understanding what Alice had meant. Relaxing more around Agatha was the way to go, it was the way to make all of this much easier.

She wasn’t just a girl with a crush on a movie star.

She was a movie star with a crush on a movie star.

Two very different things.

“I’ll have you know,” Agatha moved closer, her hand slipping below the water and resting on Rio’s side applying enough pressure that Rio knew she wanted her to turn her way.

“I’m seven years older. I looked it up. Both millennials. That’s barely an age difference.”

“It is in Hollywood,” Rio said with a smile, intensely aware that Agatha’s hand was still on her side as she turned to her. “You could play my mom in my next movie.”

Agatha’s jaw dropped and she froze for a second, and Rio thought she’d gone too far suddenly, the beer and tequila blurring the lines in her mind.

But Agatha’s reaction, her true reaction hadn’t hit yet and an apology was on the tip of her tongue before Agatha repeated her move from earlier and found that soft spot between Rio’s ribs and waist and dug her fingers in so deep that Rio inhaled in shock as she folded in on herself.

She swallowed a mouthful of water and disappeared below the water line, dragging Agatha with her where she’d placed her forward-leaning body weight over her arm.

They wrestled and flailed beneath the water for a while until they both broke out, Rio coughing much more than Agatha and Agatha gasping as she struggled to keep them both afloat.

She managed to manhandle Rio to the edge of the pool, lifting her so her top half was out and her elbows could rest on the edge. Agatha panted softly behind her, one arm tight around Rio’s waist and her other holding herself at the wall by Rio’s side.

“That…” Rio gasped, too intent on catching her breath to focus on the fact that Agatha’s body was pressed behind her, her cheek and soft breaths against her naked back. “Was… mean.”

Agatha laughed quietly and pulled her head away, pushing off a little only when she was sure Rio wouldn’t collapse back into the water.

Her hold around her middle loosened enough for Rio to be able to turn around and found herself trapped between Agatha’s arms holding the wall beside her head.

It was familiar, too familiar, only this time Rio wasn’t as drunk, wasn’t as awestruck, though she was close.

“You okay?” Agatha asked softly, the laughter fading from her lips as she watched Rio watch her.

“Yeah,” Rio said just as softly, her lungs still burning from the inhalation of pool water but her whole body more interested in the woman before her than its own salvation.

“You play dirty,” Rio accused and Agatha’s lips twitched slightly at the sides.

“Not bad for an old woman, huh?”

But Rio couldn’t give in to this blatant cheating and only scowled playfully, taking a shot and lifting her right hand to rest over Agatha’s left on the wall behind her, her wrist twisted uncomfortably. Just to be closer.

Just to see.

Agatha glanced at their hands and saw the extra strain Rio was putting herself under so pulled her hand away and dipped it below the water, her lower face slipping under until she got a good purchase, to tug at Rio’s thigh, her hand slipping to hold the back of her knee.

“Here. I’ll hold us.”

Rio only nodded and as loosely as she could she draped her legs around Agatha’s waist, careful not to press too close, moving her hands to rest lightly and demurely on her shoulders.

Being held up by Agatha in the pool was not how shed envisioned her evening going.

But her fingers had moved of their own accord, lightly toying with the straps of Agatha’s swimsuit. Her thighs were tense where she tried to get a hold of her own desire to press closer, and her gaze was determinedly focused on Agatha’s.

They were both silent for a time and Rio began to feel the awkwardness of the choice, her mind working overtime to establish it as friendly rather than flirty.

If Alice had done this, if Wanda or any other her other industry friends had done this, it wouldn’t have meant anything at all.

But something about Agatha’s frequent shifts in intensity, the way she was looking at her, the way Rio’s body reacted to her, it was different.

And she wasn’t sure Agatha would be comfortable with a photo of them like this on the internet, but she could count several other of her friends who wouldn’t mind at all.

She racked her brain with what to say, how to break the tension.

She couldn’t run away again, that at least wasn’t an option.

But what could she say that would make this seem normal, natural, and not result in Rio embarrassing herself once more in front of Agatha Harkness.

“Nicky,” she tried suddenly, “do you miss him?”

Agatha looked a little taken aback by this, she’d clearly been lost in her own thoughts too but she nodded and frowned a little, falling easily back into the conversation.

“All the time.”

And Rio shifted her hands, jumping them from Agatha’s shoulders to her neck, her fingers just touching the soft, wet hairs at the back of her neck.

Agatha didn’t acknowledge the move but her arms flexed and she pulled a little closer to the edge, and Rio had to assume it was to lessen the strain as she held them both above the water line.

But it meant that she’d pressed closer.

Rio swallowed and cleared her throat quietly, “Jen told Alice he was a good kid.”

Agatha smiled just a little and whether real or imaginary Rio noticed her whole face softening.

“He’s the best. He’s shy but a real ham when he wants to be.”

“Oh yeah?” Rio laughed a little as she felt the tension ease somewhat.

“Yeah. Into everything. Basketball’s his first love though. Tries to get me to play all the time but-…”

“I’d play with him.”

The words came out before she could even think about it and Agatha looked taken aback again for a second before she schooled her face and simply raised her brows.

“You’d play basketball with my seven year old son?”

“I mean… he can’t be any worse than some of the guys down the park.”

This seemed to give Agatha even more pause and she tilted her head to the side as she surveyed Rio closely, “You play? In the park?”

“When I can. I used to have a team but… work makes that harder.”

Agatha nodded slowly, apparently thinking it over for a second, “Maybe we can set up a date? Schedules are crazy right now but… I wouldn’t mind introducing you to Nicky if you wouldn’t.”

Rio cursed herself for getting herself into this position, literally and figuratively, but Agatha was offering another olive branch and who was Rio to say no.

“I’d like that.”

Agatha smiled softly and Rio’s gaze dropped to it, her cheeks flushing once more at just how close she was to Agatha.

It made her feel insane, made her feel like she was drunk again, misunderstanding things once more.

But had Agatha leant in a little? Had she parted her lips?

“Agatha! Drinks on the terrace!”

The moment was broken and Agatha had pulled away so suddenly that Rio almost dropped below the waterline again.

Her saviour was once again Agatha, who’d caught her waist and kept her buoyant but released as soon as Rio managed to grasp the wall.

They looked at each other but neither said anything as Agatha moved away and swam back to the shallow end of the pool.

Rio sucked in a sharp breath, watching as Agatha climbed the shallow steps to get out.

This crush was crushing. Agatha would be the death of her. And not even an Oscar at the end of it could bring her back to life.

Chapter 9: Positano (Part Quattro)

Chapter Summary

Rio and Agatha dance a fine line.

The trip comes to an end.

Chapter Notes

Sorry had to turn the yearning up a notch

See the end of the chapter for more notes

When Rio finally followed Agatha out of the pool, she was relieved to see that she’d left her alone to dry herself by the sunbeds.

She picked up the fluffy towel left for her and wrapped it tightly around her wet body, watching as Agatha retreated to the veranda where Alice and Jen now sat with their drinks before them.

She was sure she hadn’t imagined Agatha had leant in but then… surely not.

Deciding now wasn’t the time to dwell once again on her tragic crush on Agatha Harkness, she padded on over to join the group, taking the vacant seat beside Agatha.

Agatha glanced at her briefly as she reached for her spritz but said nothing that would indicate how close they’d just been in the pool, nothing that would suggest she thought they’d had a moment that was more than friendly.

“I think we should all quit and just move here,” Jen said with a smile, relaxed back in her seat and cradling her spritz in both hands.

“Learn italian, eat gelato everyday, spritzes every evening.”

“I could get onboard,’ Alice said with a smile, nudging Rio under the table with her foot, “Rio? Time to settle down?”

“I’m pretty sure we’d all kill each other after a week. Two days is enough.”

Agatha glanced at Rio and raised her brows, “Sick of us already?”

“Some of you,” Rio smiled a little, taking a well-timed sip of her spritz as she watched Agatha smirk across at her.

Maybe they were just becoming friends, feeling each other out, seeing how the other ticked.

Rio could handle that.

She was an adult. She could handle an unrequited crush.

Besides, she thought idly as she took another sip of her drink through the metal straw, who didn’t want a friend who was nice to look at?

“Let’s hope we’re not preventing you from meeting any more signoras on the beach, Rio. Far be it for us to stop you,” Jen said with a smirk that made Rio turn to her with a roll of her eyes.

“Actually I’m pretty exhausted from last night so… I think I’ll just hang with you guys, if that’s alright with you?”

Agatha shifted in her seat beside her but Rio didn’t have a chance to look her way as Jen laughed and said: “How you get away with it, I don’t know.”

“I’m charming,” Rio grinned brightly, and Jen rolled her eyes but smiled across at her, softening a little.

“Just don’t be too charming, okay? We’re getting that Oscar.”

“Actually, about that…” Rio leant in slightly and Agatha realised what she was about to do and leant forward too, angling herself towards Rio and holding her arm.

“Rio Vidal, I swear to god.”

Rio raised her brows and turned to Agatha in surprise, and Agatha narrowed her eyes at her which Rio took as a dare and she said what Agatha feared she was going to as she stared into narrowed blue eyes: “Agatha’s going to vote for me.”

“Jesus, Agatha. You cannot vote for the competition.”

“Technically,” Agatha drawled out, slowly turning away her narrowed glare at a grinning Rio to look at her best friend, “everyone’s the competition.”

“But Rio is the favourite. After you, of course. Which is why you vote for yourself.”

Rio felt Agatha squeeze her bicep softly and she glanced at her, watching as she settled back into her seat and pulled her hand away, “Hey, I’m just helping the younger generation out.”

She knew that was a dig. A gentle prod at Rio for calling her old earlier.

She scoffed and fought the butterflies that fluttered in her stomach at the idea that she had an inside joke with Agatha. Ridiculous, she thought to herself.

“Younger gen-…?!” Jen started up suddenly, because if Rio were in a younger generation compared to Agatha then the same could be said for her and Alice.

And she didn’t like the insinuation.

“Baby,” Alice said and Rio’s brows shot up as she watched her friend practically paw at Jen’s arm to soothe her, “I think it’s hot you’re a little older.”

“I-…” Jen turned to Alice with a furious expression that she couldn’t keep up for longer than two seconds and soon shut her mouth, relaxing slowly back down again.

“Whatever. Not that much older.”

“Old enough,” Alice said with a wide smile that was so infectious even Rio picked it up when it wasn’t aimed at her.

She nudged Alice gently beneath the table, making her turn to her and catch her eye. She wanted to tell her how happy she was for her, but it would be too mawkish to say out loud. So she simply wriggled her brows and shot her a wink, knowing she’d understand what she was trying to say.

“How long have you guys known each other?” Agatha asked suddenly, watching the interaction between them with interest.

“College,” Rio said with a smile, “We were assigned each other as roommates. Alice fell in love with my mother’s cooking and I’ve been unable to shake her since.”

“Empanadas to die for, tostones you’d crawl over hot coals for,” Alice clarified with a smile, “But honestly she can turn her hand to anything. Shame Rio never picked up her skill.”

“Hey, I’m not bad.”

“Not great either.”

Rio rolled her eyes and took a sip of her drink but almost choked on it when Agatha asked her next question: “Have you ever…?”

“God! No. No. Definitely-…” Rio began, spluttering a little.

“Ouch, Vidal,” Alice said in faux-offence, placing a hand over her heart, “Let a girl down easy.”

“Oh you’d rather die than touch me, you know it.”

“True. Something… gross about it. Makes me feel a bit sick.”

“Ah thanks.”

Jen scoffed and reached an arm over to pull Alice a bit closer in a display of possessiveness that Alice responded to with a smirk and Rio watched with a slight pang of jealousy.

No one was jealous over her.

But she fought it off, turning to Agatha who was watching this move closely too.

“No, we haven’t. Never was even a thought. I came out long before Alice anyway.”

“Oh?”

“Yeah, I got caught making out with my girlfriend by my mom when I was around sixteen so have been out since then and Alice-…”

But Agatha interrupted, clearly more interested in Rio than in Alice’s story: “How did your mom take it?”

“Totally fine. She said she knew and to be honest I think she walked in on purpose to try to force me to tell her.”

Agatha smiled a little and Rio’s brow furrowed slightly as she thought she caught something wistful in her gaze, but it was gone as Alice spoke across from them.

“I didn’t come out until I was in my early twenties. Rio knew earlier, obviously. Coached me through a lot of it. Helped with all the feelings and… confusion and… yeah, just took me a little longer.”

“Not me,” Jen said with a grin, “Came out the womb gay as the day is long. My parents knew by the time I was about five, I think. Never touched a man in my life, thank god.”

“Me neither,” Alice grimaced and Rio laughed at her as she did.

“Have you?” Agatha asked softly, turning again to look at Rio when her laughter had died down. Rio just shrugged and took a sip of her drink before answering.

“Yeah. There was a time in college I was experimenting… I wanted to see if I could be with a man that way. The thought didn’t disgust me totally like it did Alice so I slept with a couple guys but it wasn’t for me.”

This was putting it lightly.

The first time Rio had slept with a man she’d taken three hot showers in quick succession to try to wash the memory away, horrified with his clammy touches and frequent grunts.

The second time had been different but mostly because Rio had been off her face drunk and so had the man. They’d had a very clumsy fumble and Rio had experienced for the first time what it was to be in a situation where she felt no sexual attraction whatsoever even with his fingers inside her.

She’d pushed him away after two thrusts and stumbled her way home to crawl into bed beside Alice, reeking of beer and Paco Rabanne.

“Have you ever been with a woman?” Alice asked innocently over at Agatha and Rio watched Agatha’s reaction curiously, seeing her posture change ever so slightly and her jaw flexing a little.

“No, not for me.”

Agatha was saved from expanding her answer by Jen who had interjected with an amused smirk in her best friend’s direction.

“Agatha’s only ever slept with two guys anyway.”

“What?” Alice asked suddenly, totally shocked by this delicious nugget of information.

“No way,” Rio added, unable to help herself as she stared wide-eyed across at Agatha. “But… but you look like that. How have you only slept with two people?”

Agatha huffed and ran a hand through her hair, avoiding Rio’s eye contact and instead focusing on Jen.

“Thank you for that, Jennifer.”

“You’re very welcome, Agatha.”

“I… had a high school boyfriend and then I met my husband. That’s all.”

Rio blinked owlishly at what she could see now of Agatha’s side profile and remained silent as she tried to process this idea.

Two men. Two lucky sons of bitches had been deemed worthy enough to bed Agatha.

In a strange way it made sense. Agatha was better than mere mortals, especially better than male mortals. So it was right that only two of them had ever been able to take her to bed.

But still, she couldn’t help but think what a waste it was.

And how she wouldn’t mind being the third lucky son of a bitch.

“Agatha’s mom,” Jen started again but Agatha was quicker this time, her tone much sharper than it had been when she was trying to prevent Rio from sharing her voting intentions.

“Jen.”

“What?” Jen asked with faux innocence, smiling widely across at Agatha, “I think most of the world knows already anyway. She’s one of the largest Republican Party donors there is.”

Agatha huffed and her gaze dropped to her spritz and Rio watched as she began spinning it with her straw, clearly unimpressed with where this conversation had gone.

She felt a little sorry for her but said nothing and turned to focus in on Jen who looked like she was gearing up to tell an exciting tale.

“Evanora basically kept Agatha on a leash until she was old enough to leave home. Still would like to keep that leash tight, in fact. A real piece of work, that woman.”

Agatha shifted and Rio looked back to her, watching as she placed her glass down and began spinning her wedding ring with her left thumb instead.

“She’s not exactly ever going to win mother of the year and well, Agatha married young because-…”

“Enough,” Agatha said just as sharply as before and Rio’s eyes darted across to Alice who had flinched at her words.

Jen sighed heavily, “I’m just explaining why you’re a massive loser who’s only slept with-…”

“Jen,” Rio said quickly before even Agatha could interject, “You’re being incredibly quiet about your sex life. So go ahead: how many notches on your broomstick?”

Jen narrowed her eyes at Rio at the insult but Rio didn’t care, she’d felt a strange flare up of protectiveness for the woman beside her and as Jen huffed a bit as she answered she felt Agatha shift her position to turn more to her and the gentle graze of her fingers against her towel-covered leg.

She was thanking her.

Rio swallowed thickly but kept her gaze on Jennifer.

“Admittedly, I don’t have that many stories to tell. But… I always did okay for myself.”

Rio nodded once, not interested enough to push for more details now she’d derailed the Agatha bashing. She settled back in her seat and took another sip of her drink.

Jen must have known the conversation had died because she didn’t say anything else for a while and the table descended into silence.

But soon Alice spoke: “Maybe we would all kill each other in a week.”

Rio laughed and placed her empty glass down on the table.

“I told you.”

She stood, pushing her chair back as she did.

“More aperols? Wine? Beer? Are we just going to order in a pizza or something?”

Alice nodded and held her own empty glass to Rio, “Wine is good for me.”

“Me too,” Jen said, but Rio noticed that she didn’t offer her glass up.

Agatha reached for it instead and stood with Rio, “I’ll help.”

Rio only nodded and scooped her own glass up before moving through to the kitchen to discard the old and take the new.

She crouched down at the wine fridge and began pulling out bottles, inspecting labels as she went.

Agatha was emptying out the finished aperol glasses in the sink and they sat in a companionable silence for a while as Rio continued to focus her efforts on picking the wine.

White and dry was her preferred choice but all the labels were in Italian so she had to rely on the hopes that Italian and Spanish weren’t that different.

“When you slept with those men,” Agatha asked suddenly, just as Rio had pulled out her fourth bottle to inspect. “What did it feel like?”

Rio blinked slowly, halfway through translating ’vine piano fresco proveniente dalle verdi colline toscane’ in her own mind. She paused, making sure she’d heard Agatha right and then stood slowly, moving to close the door to the wine fridge as she moved closer, “What?”

“How did you know?”

Agatha had turned her head towards her where she stood at the sink but kept her body facing forwards, her fingers curled around the edge of the basin.

“I mean, it was pretty obvious,” Rio said with a smile, trying to break the tension a little. “If you’re attracted to someone… you just know.”

Agatha’s brow furrowed a little and she turned away again, reaching to lift each glass out to place upside down on the side. “Right.”

Rio chewed the inside of her cheek in thought for a second and decided to be bold.

She placed the bottle of wine down and reached for Agatha, turning her around to face her.

“I felt horrible when both of those men were touching me. It wasn’t something I had to think about. My body just told me.”

She’d placed her hands on Agatha’s arms, squeezing them gently and tilting her head as Agatha kept her gaze away, lost in her own mind despite Rio’s attempts to bring her back to the surface again.

“But hey,” Rio said, softening her tone slightly, “If this is about having not slept with many people… then you should know that actually I envy you for that.”

Your husband, more like, Rio clarified in her head.

And Agatha looked around at her suddenly and Rio smiled a little where she saw confusion in her face.

“You get to go home every night to someone who loves you and… I’m still picking girls up in bars or matching with them on Raya.” Rio shrugged and cleared her throat quickly, finding that saying it out loud actually felt worse than keeping it in.

Suddenly where she’d been trying to reassure Agatha, she felt like she needed the reassurance.

She moved away, swiping the bottle back and ducking back down quickly to the wine fridge that she’d opened again and hidden her face inside of.

“Anyway.”

Agatha remained standing by the sink and Rio now regretted being so honest, exposing herself in that way.

Agatha had probably only asked because she couldn’t imagine a world where someone wasn’t attracted to her handsome Ken doll of a husband.

“Hey.”

Rio jumped a little, Agatha’s voice soft and just behind her now, a warm hand resting on her arm where she was still riffling through the wine options to find the right one.

She turned back and saw that Agatha had moved to be kneeling down just beside her, and looked nervous, her gaze heavy with emotions Rio couldn’t decipher.

But the hand on her arm had moved to cradle her cheek and Rio found herself leaning into the touch just a little, unsure what she should say.

Agatha took a breath and then said in the softest tone Rio had ever heard from her as her thumb delicately caressed her cheekbone, “One day, you will meet the woman you want to spend the rest of your life with.”

She paused as Rio’s breath hitched and she felt her eyes suddenly sting with the promise of tears.

Agatha’s blue eyes darted cautiously over Rio’s face and she saw in them a tenderness that had become more common the more time she spent with her.

She wondered if this was the kind of privileged look Nicky and Ralph would get from her, safe in their home, living a life with Agatha unavailable to Rio.

“And she,” Agatha continued just as softly, “will be the luckiest woman alive.”

Rio sucked in a sharp breath and saw Agatha’s eyes fall to her lips.

From outside, Rio heard Jen ask what was taking so long but it was immaterial to her.

Because Agatha Harkness was kneeling before her and looking at her with what Rio could only describe now as aching and she felt like she couldn’t breathe.

You, she wanted to say as Agatha gently wiped her tear away with the pad of her thumb, let it be you. I want it to be you.

“Agatha,” Rio breathed out, just as Agatha’s thumb continued its movements against her cheek, her blue eyes as glassy now as Rio’s must have been.

But there was movement over Agatha’s shoulder and Rio looked up to see Jen marching towards them. She pulled away suddenly, mortified that she would be caught kneeling down before Agatha and crying in front of a wine fridge.

She busied herself with grabbing another bottle of wine, not even bothering to check the label.

“What the fuck is taking so long? You squeezing the grapes yourselves?”

Rio heard Agatha huff and stand behind her. She shot Jen an unamused look and went to grab four fresh glasses.

“We were checking the labels, your highness. They’re all in Italian.”

“So?” Jen asked with raised brows, “Rio’s Spanish.”

“I’m not Spanish, I speak Spanish and they’re different languages,” Rio clarified quickly as she stood to shut the door, satisfied that she at least wouldn’t be crying again any time soon.

“Whatever, you know what I mean.”

Rio rolled her eyes and avoided looking at Agatha as she went to grab a frozen wine sleeve from the freezer, slotting it on the bottle and taking the corkscrew with her as she followed the other two back out.

She placed the wine on the table and stood at the end of it, vaguely aware that Jen was now talking about Agatha’s next project. She could feel Agatha’s eyes on her but she didn’t look up and focused instead on getting the cork out and the wine poured.

When she was done, she made a quick excuse for herself and disappeared back into the house to hide in her bedroom for a few minutes under the pretence of changing out of her towel and damp bikini.

No one came to find her.

She allowed herself just ten minutes to collect herself, well aware that if she gave herself any longer that Alice might comes searching, or else, and absolute worst case scenario: Agatha would.

But she couldn’t dwell in her feelings either.

If she took the time to fully sit in them, to analyse and dissect them, she would be in for a world of trouble.

For now, a surface-level look at them would have to do.

She had the rest of the night and a plane ride back to get through still.

Rio had a crush. Agatha liked Rio. Rio sometimes thought Agatha might like like Rio. Agatha was happily married.

The math was simple. The people were not.

So she soon returned back to the little group and found them all to be at least halfway through their wines, where Rio’s sat untouched in front of her seat.

Agatha glanced up as she came through and Rio managed to send a small smile her way before she took her seat.

“I should change too,” Agatha said softly, disappearing off to the place Rio had just emerged from.

Alice shot Rio a quick ‘are you okay?’ look and Rio simply nodded with an easy smile. She had to just get through the next few hours and then she’d be fine.

Agatha couldn’t have a hold on her when she was back at work, back doing press, back in her normal life.

Everyone knew vacations were rife for confusing feelings and ill-fated romances that would mean nothing when you were back home.

That’s all this was.

Only Rio wasn’t getting any of the benefits that might come from an ill-fated romance because the subject of her infatuation was straight.

By the time Agatha was back at the table, Rio had managed to calm her racing heart and the conversation flowed as well as it had earlier.

But with conversation flowing so was alcohol and the little table in the little villa tucked away on the hillside of Positano’s infamous bay became rowdier.

“Would you just let me finish?” Jen was shouting across at Agatha, who had long since given up on sitting properly at the table and was now lounging back, her arms suddenly flung in the air.

“Go ahead,” she announced with aplomb. “Be my guest.”

Jen huffed and pulled the shawl Alice had fetched for her earlier tighter around her shoulders in the chill of the late evening. “Agatha would have won all three Oscars by now if she were just willing to play the game a little more.”

“I don’t need to play when I have the goods already.”

“Incorrect, Agatha! You only have one Oscar!”

Rio grimaced dramatically for the sake of Alice opposite her who was staring at her with wide eyes and she made her laugh which made both Jen and Agatha round on her immediately: “What?”

Alice flinched and looked to Rio for help where Rio just began to laugh.

Agatha huffed heavily, stealing her wine glass from the table before she leant back again, tucking her feet beneath herself.

“Calderu won because her movie was about the Holocaust so obviously. A nun saving kids from the gestapo? Who could compete?! Then-…”

But Jen had cut her off again and Rio, though she’d witnessed this dynamic since they’d all first met in Cannes, was starting to really enjoy it.

“Don’t give me that shit, Agatha. You pissed off the director’s branch because you-…”

“Because I called out a bad working environment and an abuse of power,” Agatha countered and Rio raised her brows at Jen, wondering how she’d work her way around this one.

But she didn’t. She just shrugged and turned her face away, taking a measured sip of her drink.

“Whatever.”

Agatha rolled her eyes and mirrored Jen’s movements, taking a large sip of her own drink.

“Need I remind you that you encouraged me to call out the behaviour?”

“I said whatever,” Jen muttered, clearly caught and clearly not interested in continuing this conversation.

“You told me to do it when it was just rumours and so I-…”

“Yes, yes, alright. I lost you the Oscar. Are you happy now?”

And to Rio, Agatha did look happy. She looked more than happy. She looked smug, incredibly so.

“Thrilled, thank you.”

“I think the win here is the behaviour being called out,” Rio said with more than a hint of amusement in her voice, and just to add to it, she stole Agatha’s wine glass from her hand and drank from it, there being no other wine left on the table.

“Obviously,” Agatha said with a scowl, turning to try and snatch her wine back.

Rio just held it away, holding her right arm out to the side so Agatha couldn’t get it without physically moving.

“You’re a child,” she accused and Rio beamed at her in response, amused at how Agatha could be so furious but still look so ridiculously hot.

“There’s no wine left. No queda vino.” She offered as an excuse.

“Give me my wine.”

Agatha looked serious and Rio only grinned still, raising her brows at the determination writ large across her features.

“Oh? This wine?”

“Rio Vidal. ¡Dámelo!”

Rio blinked and forgot the game suddenly so pulled the wine back around and held it between them, only remembering what she’d been trying to do when Agatha put her hand around the glass she still held, their fingers overlapping where Agatha’s dominate hand was her left and Rio’s her right.

“¿Tú hablas español?”

“Obviamente.”

Rio saw Agatha’s gaze drop down to their joined hands and blinked slowly, her brain taking a while to catch up to what was going on.

But Alice was their saviour.

“Holy shit. Have you seen how many likes we got? Rio this is more than the last two posts combined.”

Agatha looked up and raised her brows and released her hold on the wine glass so Rio could take it back.

She hesitated for a second before she placed it down before Agatha and leant her other hand up on the back of Agatha’s chair as she turned to Alice.

“How many?”

Alice was frowning down at what Rio guessed must be her Instagram page and Rio raised her brows expectantly, vaguely aware that as Jen leant across to look over Alice’s shoulder, Agatha was drinking what was left of the wine.

“Oh my god,” Jen said quietly, making Rio feel even more impatient that no one was answering.

“Honey,” Agatha said softly, and Rio was aware suddenly that where she’d leant over to place her hand on Agatha’s chair, she was now closer to her.

She felt Agatha’s hand on her leg.

“I think I just bought you another two million on your asking price with that post.”

Rio scoffed but turned to look at Agatha and found she couldn’t think of a witty retort. Agatha’s eyes were heavy, her gaze a little bleary, her hand still warm and soft against the skin of just above her knee.

“Rio. It’s almost a million.”

Rio blinked slowly, tearing her gaze away from Agatha to look round at Alice, unsure she’d heard her correctly. “What?”

“Almost a million.”

“Give it to me.”

Rio scooched her chair closer and held her hand out to Alice.

She felt the loss immediately of Agatha’s hand as it fell from her leg.

But Alice had handed her phone over and suddenly Agatha was close again as she leant across and Rio stared wide-eyed at the image of her and Agatha from only four hours ago, and the little number below it that confirmed Alice’s announcement.

“Holy shit.”

Agatha didn’t say anything as she looked down at the screen and Rio felt incapacitated for a while, staring at the attention the photo was getting.

She slowly raised her gaze to look across at Alice who looked positively horrified at the numbers it was doing.

“I can’t believe it.”

“Why not?” Jen asked with a wave of her hand and a shrug, “You are so welcome, by the way. But don’t get used to it. That’s the last time you’re using Agatha like that.”

“Do you understand how good this could be for both of us?” Alice asked suddenly, stealing the phone back from Rio and holding it up to Jen’s face.

“Rio’s already a hit online and Agatha… well. She’s a hit everywhere but. But Rio could help.”

Rio sniggered and went to steal Agatha’s wine glass and frowned where she’d forgotten Agatha had finished her wine already.

“Too slow,” Agatha said with a grin and swiped her glass back.

“Rude.”

Agatha laughed and rolled her eyes but Rio caught a slight softening in them and she turned quickly, feeling the need to have a replacement for the wine that was now missing.

“I’m gonna,” she started as she stood up, “more drinks.”

“I’ll help!” Alice shouted quickly, standing up to follow Rio eagerly into the kitchen and taking her sleeve in her hand, “Rio. What the fuck. How did this happen? We’re in fucking Italy and I have a girlfriend and you have… an Agatha.”

Rio laughed and wished she indeed had “an Agatha.”

But she’d take what she could get for now.

And what she currently had was a very pretty, reasonably drunk, friend who liked to touch her leg and share her smiles with her.

That could be enough.

“Did we just become famous?” She asked with a grin, sticking her tongue between her teeth as she went to raid the bar.

Alice laughed happily and grabbed more glasses, narrowly avoiding smashing any of them as she did so.

“We should take vacations more often.”

“Shall we just move here? Stay here forever?”

“I’ll ask Jen.”

Rio laughed and rolled her eyes but the reminder of Jen being asked meant that Agatha would be asked too and… Agatha had Ralph. And a son.

She shook the feeling off.

Decided that there was nothing she could do so she’d just have to enjoy what she had access to currently.

They soon had made up the strongest gin and tonics known to man and sauntered back out with them, Rio adding a flourish as she delivered Agatha’s drink to her.

“M’lady.”

Agatha rolled her eyes but stroked down Rio’s arm as she went to take her seat beside her again.

Rio decided she liked drunk Agatha.

She touched her more than regular Agatha.

But Jen’s spluttering as she sipped the strongest G&T in the world made Rio look to her with raised brows and Alice begin slapping her back helpfully.

“You okay, princess?”

Agatha laughed as Jen continued to cough, “Don’t… Call me… That.”

Rio hummed in amusement and then took a tentative sip of her own drink, sinking back down in her seat and grimacing a little at just how strong it was.

“Can’t handle it?” Agatha asked with an amused smile in her direction, having not yet touched her own drink.

“Oh, just taking my time, that’s all.”

Agatha smirked and raised two fingers to tap the underside of Rio’s glass, indicating she should keep drinking.

“You made it. You should drink it.”

“Are you trying to get me drunk?”

“Would I need to?”

Rio opened her mouth to respond but found it suddenly dry and herself unable to form any coherent response.

Agatha Harkness was flirting with her.

No… Agatha Harkness was telling her she knew she had a crush. She was letting Rio know that she hadn’t acted her way out of this one.

Shit.

But Agatha’s fingers were still on the bottom of Rio’s glass and she pushed it up slowly, watching until Rio allowed it to hit her lips.

It was the sexiest thing that had ever happened to Rio.

Agatha’s chin was lifting slightly with the rising glass and her lips parted, her blue eyes never leaving Rio’s deep brown.

So Rio had no choice but to drink the lethal drink in one go, intent on keeping Agatha’s hypnotic blue eyes on her for as long as possible.

Alice whooped across the table and Jen frowned at the sight, shaking her head in disgust.

But Rio was showing off for her crush, and when she placed her now empty glass down she closed her eyes, focusing on not vomiting now that she’d achieved her goal.

But it had been worth it just to see Agatha looking at her like that.

The noise around her felt tinny all of a sudden, distant in a way that Rio couldn’t quite comprehend.

But then something came into focus that was loud, or at least loud to Rio’s ears.

A whisper close by, a hand on her upper thigh.

“Drink mine too and I’ll love you forever.”

Rio’s eyes flashed open, unsure she’d heard correctly. Unsure she’d understood what she was being told.

But she couldn’t focus on the words because Agatha was close, so close she could see the little smattering of freckles across her cheeks, the green in her eyes again, and the way her lips parted in a teasing smile.

She sucked in a breath and watched as Agatha moved back to pass her her drink and she didn’t even think as she made to drink it down, just as she had her own.

“No, Rio, my god!” Jen shouted in horror as Alice cackled at her side.

But Agatha was smiling at her, tilting her head as she watched her and Rio had to do it. She had to just finish this glass, just put it down, just not spew it back up and Agatha would love her. Forever.

And she did. She placed it down harder than she meant to and she felt the gin repeat on her as she did.

But she held it together.

And she grinned lopsidedly at Agatha who was beaming back and laughing quietly, her whole body leaning towards Rio and both hands now on her thighs as she used her for balance and leant in to kiss her cheek.

The kiss was soft, more nose than lips as Agatha slipped slightly but Rio didn’t mind.

She’d take that kind of kiss from Agatha Harkness any day.

When Agatha leant back her hands were still on her legs and Rio felt hot below her gaze, but then again maybe it was the gin she’d just swallowed down.

“Rio Vidal, my hero.”

The words shot right down in between Rio’s thighs and she gaped a little stupidly up at Agatha, trying to focus in where her brain was trying not to make two of the most beautiful woman she’d ever seen.

But that was difficult with how drunk she felt.

Blue eyes flashed down to her parted lips and for a second Rio felt like throwing caution to the wind and closing the gap between them but Agatha had already pulled away and Rio was able to breathe again.

“More drinks!” Alice announced, waving her empty glass in the air where she sat, having clearly copied Rio in knocking back her own and Jen’s.

“Well considering I didn’t get mine, that would be nice,” Agatha said with a hint of a smirk and a wink in Rio’s direction.

Rio scowled playfully at her and poked her shoulder now she was sat oh so far away in her own chair.

“You told me to drink yours.”

“Well perhaps if you hadn’t made them so strong I wouldn’t have.”

Rio narrowed her eyes, still trying to figure out how Agatha’s brain worked.

She liked to tease her, she knew that much.

“Get it yourself.”

Agatha’s jaw dropped a little and suddenly Rio didn’t know if she were teasing or not as she smiled widely, her hand coming up to her chest in a dramatic movement.

“Moi? Little old me get my own drink?”

“You heard me.”

Agatha laughed and stood from her seat, offering a hand down to Rio unexpectedly. “You can at least come and help.”

Rio raised her brows but who was she to deny Agatha for a second time so she took her offered hand and followed her into the kitchen.

In the cool of the air conditioning she shivered slightly and went to rest against the counter as Agatha dropped her hand and moved about the place looking for superior alternatives to Rio’s lethal G&Ts.

“I can’t believe I drank both of those.”

“I can’t believe you did either.”

Rio laughed and rocked her head back, staring up at the ceiling as she fought off the threatening spin of the room.

“You’re a bad influence.”

“And you are going to have an almighty hangover tomorrow,” Agatha accused, a little closer than she’d been before.

Rio tilted her head back and raised her brows at her, seeing that she had in fact moved closer, her hand now next to hers on the counter.

“Your fault.”

Agatha smiled and bit the corner of her lip, “You’re a fun drunk.”

“Fun?”

“Cute.”

Rio felt her already warm cheeks heat up slightly and she wondered idly if Agatha were doing this on purpose; doing everything in her power to get her to blush, or suddenly feel like jelly in front of her.

“So?” Rio asked quietly, trying to pick back up some of the bravado she’d had whilst drinking two drinks in quick succession to impress a girl.

“So what?” Agatha asked in amusement, her fingers reaching out to just brush across Rio’s nails.

“Do you love me forever now?”

Agatha’s brows raised in surprise and she stepped in, raising her free hand to cup Rio’s cheek as she said in a gentle voice, “Yes, Rio Vidal. I love you forever.”

Rio knew she was placating her, toying with the sensitive emotions of a drunk woman, but it felt nice to be held this way by Agatha, to have her looking at her like that, to hear her say her name, to hear her say she loved her.

But Agatha’s thumb brushed her cheek just once and then she pulled away, and Rio reacted before she could think, she grabbed the hand on the counter and she swung her other round to pull Agatha to her, catching her in a tight but one-armed hug.

“Sorry,” she mumbled into still slightly damp brown hair, “can’t just say that and move away.”

Agatha released a breathy laugh against her and she squeezed Rio’s hand before she released it and wrapped both her arms around her. “Okay.”

Rio closed her eyes as Agatha squeezed her middle and she thought she imagined it for a second but Agatha had turned her head slightly and had nuzzled in by her ear.

Her stomach flipped for reasons other than the gin and she felt herself suck in a sharp breath, and the arms around her squeezed her before they loosened and Agatha pulled back slowly, holding Rio still where she leant away from her.

Blue eyes were still hooded from the alcohol and the long day spent in the sun and Rio moved her hand to hold Agatha’s cheek, watching her watch her with a slight furrow in her brow.

“I should,” Agatha breathed out, turning her head a little so her parted lips grazed the heel of Rio’s palm before she pulled away entirely and cleared her throat, “I should get you water.”

Rio could only nod, only feel the loss of Agatha from her arms and the ache of something she couldn’t name in her chest.

But she turned away and leant back against the sink, focusing on the soft noises of a glass being taken from the cupboard, the door closing, Agatha moving over, the water running, the glass being filled.

Agatha pressed the glass to Rio’s arm and Rio opened her eyes slowly to take it, quickly drinking down the water to try to keep the queasiness at bay.

Agatha had moved away, fetching other drinks for the group and by the time Rio had finished her water and taken a few deep breaths, she felt a little more confident that she wouldn’t be tasting that gin again.

“I’m glad you’re here.”

If the words took Agatha by surprise they took Rio by surprise too.

She hadn’t planned on saying them.

But clearly drunk mouths speak sober truths.

Agatha paused where’d she’d been filling a glass with ice.

“You are?”

“Mmhm.

“Because we definitely gatecrashed and you didn’t look much like you wanted us here.”

Rio tried to fight her smile but lost. “I’m better when there’s a camera pointed at me.”

“What changed your mind?”

Rio shrugged and tried to act nonchalant as she ran a hand through her hair, “Maybe the gin?”

Agatha smirked and turned back around to continue making the drinks, “Well I’m using vodka now so let’s hope your opinion doesn’t change again.”

“Never.”

Agatha glanced over her shoulder and Rio sent a clumsy wink her way which made Agatha laugh.

Nailed it, Rio thought, beginning to hum quietly where she waited patiently for the drinks to be made.

Soon enough Agatha was pressing one into her hand and smiling as she held her own up to cheers.

“To ruined vacations?”

“To thanking you first in my Oscar speech.”

Rio’s gaze dropped to Agatha’s smirk and she was so distracted that she forgot to take a sip of her drink. It took Agatha nudging her glass gently with her hand for Rio to come back to herself again and raise the glass to her lips.

“Aren’t you supposed to be some hotshot lothario?”

“Hmm?” Rio asked softly, swallowing down a small mouthful of limey vodka soda. Even in her drunken state she knew she needed to slow down a little.

“I’m not sure you have any game.”

Rio could only laugh at this insult and raised her brows at Agatha, swaying a little when she leant in slightly, “Why’s that?”

“Just a lil goofy.”

“Goofy?!” Rio demanded with a look of faux shock but whatever she was planning on saying next was lost in her own mind as Jen appeared back in the villa.

“Why do you two take so damn long?”

Rio hummed quietly, in spite of herself she smiled goofily over at Jennifer and Agatha laughed as she moved to pick up Jen’s drink from the side.

“Rio was just telling me how pleased she was that we are here.”

“Agatha was just insulting me,” Rio added with a playful glare at the back of Agatha’s head.

“Riiiiight,” Jen said slowly, accepting her drink from Agatha and watching the two other women closely. “Well the party’s outside so if you wouldn’t mind joining us?”

Rio only nodded and pushed herself off the counter to begin striding out to the terrace again, missing the look exchanged between Jen and Agatha. Jen looked confused and Agatha just smiled as she walked past, focusing on following Rio.

“You took aaaaages,” Alice sang as Rio arrived back at the table.

“Making drinks is hard work,” Rio shrugged as she sat down a little heavier than she meant to in her chair and took another small sip of her drink.

Jen and Agatha appeared only seconds later and Rio wondered when Agatha’s chair had moved so close to her own but she said nothing. She was only vaguely aware that where Agatha’s arm was on her own armrest and Rio’s hand was on hers, her fingers were now grazing Agatha’s warm forearm.

“I’m not sure I’m ready to get back to work again,” Rio said quietly as she cradled her cold drink to her chest, shivering slightly in the cool of the evening.

“Seems cruel to be so soon.”

“When do you leave for London?”

“Mm, Alice?”

“Day after tomorrow. Just enough time to,” she waved her hand vaguely, clearly the gin had hit her hard too, “y’know.”

Rio laughed a little and her fingers stretched until they curled around Agatha’s wrist, seeking the warmth.

Agatha didn’t move away.

“Call my mom and wash my clothes?”

“Yeah,” Alice said with a smile.

Rio hummed and closed her eyes as she relaxed more in her chair, her thumb now brushing idly over soft skin.

“Well,” Jen said, the most sober of all of them, “When we’re back I think we both need a detox cleanse. This is the most alcohol either of us have had in weeks. You’re bad influences.”

Rio only grinned, her eyes still closed and allowed Alice to take this one for the both of them: “It’s good to let loose a little.”

“Not as loose as Rio, though. Sex on a public beach?”

Rio’s eyes opened and she was suddenly aware of the place spinning around her, the only solid think she could grasp was Agatha’s arm beneath her hand.

“Hey, she was hot and I was horny. Nothing much to it.”

“That easy, huh?”

“When you look like this,” Rio turned to Agatha with a grin and crossed her eyes to make her laugh.

“Goofy,” Agatha confirmed and she moved her free hand over to run up Rio’s arm closest to her.

Rio only continued to grin at her, delighted with herself that Agatha was paying her any attention at all, let alone smiling back at her, let alone rubbing her forearm.

“Hey, hey,” Jen snapped her fingers across the table and both turned to look at her, “Tweedle dumb and tweedle drunk. You’re both goofy tonight. What’s happening?”

Rio laughed and leant forwards to place her drink down, groaning a little when the world lurched a little more around her.

“I should probably go to bed.”

“No, stay!” Alice demanded suddenly, leaning forwards to reach for Rio. “Stay, it’s our last night. Sleep it off tomorrow.”

Rio shook her head and briefly closed her eyes, “No, I need sleep.”

If she’d been cognisant at all, she’d have felt the soft squeeze of her arm before Agatha released her but she missed it as she stood slowly and waved in the direction of the table before making a wobbly path up to her bed.

It was best to go earlier, she thought. The night had already been full of temptation, full of a promise that could never become reality.

And she felt herself slipping closer and closer to being sloppy drunk.

To maybe just pulling Agatha to her. To maybe risking it all for a woman who’d already told her she had no interest in women.

So leaving whilst she had at least a brain cell still firing was the best option.

Rio woke in the night because a sudden chill in the room made her shiver beneath the thin sheet of the bed.

She rubbed at her eyes and hissed as her exposed hand felt the cool air hit it.

“Did I wake you?”

The voice felt far away, not behind her where it should be in the bed, but in front of her. And Rio opened her eyes to blink into the dim-light of the early hours and saw Agatha silhouetted against the pale moonlight of the little balcony.

“No,” Rio said softly, “It’s just a bit cold.”

She saw Agatha nod and watched as she dropped the lit cigarette in her hand, stomping it out with her foot before she stepped back into the room.

“You can stay out, don’t worry.”

“It’s fine,” Agatha said quietly, turning to shut the windowed doors and drag the light curtain across them. “Bad habit.”

“I didn’t know you smoked,” Rio said with a yawn, curling in on herself a little more to protect from the chill.

“I don’t. Not often anyway.”

Agatha moved back around to the other side of the bed and Rio turned to watch her as she opened a drawer and pulled out a little bottle of pills.

“What’re those?”

“I,” Agatha began and paused as she looked down at the little bottle in her hand, “I don’t sleep well. Doctor says it’s chronic insomnia and I’ve been this way since I was a kid so… sometimes I just pop a pill and it helps. I’d had too much wine earlier so didn’t take one.”

“Hence the smoking,” Rio concluded softly, frowning where she saw goosebumps along Agatha’s arm where she still sat in the cold of the room, her top half not yet under the blankets.

“Get under the covers. It’s cold.”

Agatha did as she was told and turned on her side to look at Rio, frowning a little in the dim as Rio reached for the hand that curled around the little pill bottle.

“Agatha you could have frozen to death out there. You’re freezing.”

“I’m fine,” she said softly, and Rio huffed, shuffling closer.

Perhaps it was the wine and gin in her system still, perhaps it was the vague haze of a disturbed sleep that emboldened her to do it, maybe it was just because it was the last time she’d ever get the chance to, but she pried the pills from Agatha’s hand and leant over her to place them on the side.

“Turn around.”

“What?”

“Turn.”

And Agatha did, turning back over onto her side, facing away from Rio in the same way she had the previous night when Rio had first shared this bed with her.

Only this time, Rio moved in behind her and draped an arm over her middle, aligning her body along Agatha’s to get as close as possible, in a selfless attempt to keep her warm and a selfish attempt to keep herself warm.

Their bodies fit together like two pieces of the same puzzle and Rio couldn’t help the flutter of need that settled low in her stomach.

It didn’t occur to her that this may not have been a welcome move until she’d done it.

And Agatha’s body had stiffened which made Rio regret her choice instantly.

But as if it had only been because it was a surprise, she soon felt her relaxing against her.

Rio smiled a little and turned her head slightly, keeping some semblance of distance between her face and the back of Agatha’s neck for fear she’d never want to leave this position if she didn’t.

But she turned into the pillow they now both shared and quietly breathed in the scent of Agatha that remained there, her arm flexing around her middle as she did.

“Rio?”

Drunk on the feel of Agatha against her and the soft smell of her hair, Rio hummed a response instead of speaking it and felt Agatha turn slowly, careful not to jog Rio too much as she did.

“Turn over.”

Rio blinked her eyes open and despite the chill of the air around them she felt her cheeks heat up in a blush and she nodded quickly, mortified that she’d been dismissed.

She turned onto her other side quickly and began to shuffle her way up the bed, feeling the mattress beneath her move from warm to cold as she went.

But just as she reached her pillow and made to move further along, a hand caught around her middle and Agatha wrapped her arm fully around her waist, tucking her fingers beneath Rio’s right side and pulling her back.

“Not that far,” she heard Agatha chastise gently behind her and suddenly felt the press of Agatha’s body against her, but properly this time, Agatha’s hold on her much bolder than Rio had dared to be.

She adjusted herself to curl her legs a little inwards and felt Agatha slip down slightly to curl her own to mould herself to Rio, the arm that was now trapped between them slipping below the pillow to support their heads.

Rio, who had been on the verge of slipping back into sleep not seconds ago, suddenly now felt wide awake, too conscious of Agatha Harkness wrapped around her for any hope of sleep to creep back in.

She focused on keeping her breathing even, but found it difficult when she could feel Agatha’s soft breaths against the skin at the back of her neck.

She cautiously moved her right hand up below the pillow to seek Agatha’s hand and found when she lightly brushed her fingers that Agatha reached down to hold her right back.

Rio’s heart leapt in her chest and she felt Agatha squeeze her waist, making a move to press a little closer.

She kept quiet for just a few more seconds before she spoke again: “You didn’t take your pill.”

“That’s okay,” Agatha murmured quietly. “I think I’ll be okay tonight.”

Rio nodded cautiously, not wanting to disturb Agatha anymore, aware she’d been the one to take her pills away in the first place.

But Agatha was warm and her body was soft against her and as she allowed herself to focus on that, she soon found that sleep wasn’t lost to her either.

There was no room between them for guilt over Agatha’s untaken pills, or for logic to creep in that this wasn’t a rational thing to allow for a person trying to fight a crush.

But when Rio woke the next morning, she woke alone.

For the first few seconds between waking and sleeping she wasn’t sure if she’d dreamed Agatha holding her all night.

It had felt so real, so warm.

But there was no evidence Agatha had even been in the bed, let alone curled around Rio as she slept.

As she turned to survey the room, she saw that even the little bottle of pills were gone.

Maybe she had dreamt it.

But worse than Agatha not being there, though that was definitely a close second, was the dull throb of a headache.

It felt like half-hangover, half-something else. And Rio didn’t need to guess what that may be.

Just as she was peeling the sheets from her body, the door opened and Alice bolted in.

“Oh thank god, you’re awake. We don’t have long. The car will be here in thirty minutes.”

Rio made a noncommittal noise and yawned as she followed Alice back out to the other room where her suitcase still lived.

She sourced a t-shirt and light sweatpants and underwear and then disappeared into the en suite to shower and change.

By the time she was done, Alice was now frantic in her haste to get Rio down the stairs and ready by the door.

“Yes, yes. Coming, coming.”

The dull throb of her head was back and wasn’t helped as Rio heaved her heavy suitcase down the stairs, greeted by Jen and Agatha who were lounging on the couch and armchair respectively.

Rio made brief eye contact with Agatha and found her smiling at her which eased her waking nerves a little but Alice was on her again and soon Rio was back in a dark mood.

“On the way to the airport we need to discuss timings for flights to London.”

“God, Alice. Can’t I just take it easy?”

“You’ve taken it easy for two days. We agreed that. Now it’s work time again.”

Rio groaned but her retort was lost when she felt a hand suddenly brush her arm as Agatha moved beside her.

“Technically, it’s still vacation time. I say at least until we’re halfway over the atlantic.”

“Amen,” Jen chorused from the couch and Rio smirked across at Alice, who didn’t look thrilled about being outnumbered.

“Fine,” she said with a huff, before pointing at Rio firmly, “halfway over the Atlantic.”

Rio only hummed her agreement and Agatha pulled her hand away as Rio said a quick, “thank you.”

“You’re welcome.”

They looked at each other for a fraction longer than was strictly necessary and Rio felt the same warm comfort she’d felt the night before. But this time Agatha wasn’t even touching her.

Just as Rio was about to turn away, for fear she’d stare forever, Agatha raised her hand to touch her cheek, “Did you sleep okay?”

She looked concerned, as if totally unaware that Rio had potentially had the best sleep of her life the night before.

The grin that took over her face at the absurdity of the question made Agatha frown and step back a little and Rio realised she must have thought she was making fun of her.

But laughter had spilled out anyway and Agatha was turning away so Rio had to scramble to get her to turn back, reaching one hand to her wrist and tugging to get her to turn back.

“I’m laughing because,” she glanced around quickly, seeing the back of Alice’s head close to Jen’s now on the couch.

They weren’t listening. They didn’t care.

But she lowered her voice anyway.

“I slept great.”

Agatha still looked cautious but she nodded slowly, a frown still present on her features.

“Good. I was worried you wouldn’t.”

There was the dull pain in her head again, and Rio knew what it was now: it wasn’t just about Agatha.

It was about leaving Agatha.

Because this little fantasy that she’d been able to carve out for herself whilst here, it was suddenly everything.

She cleared her throat softly and squeezed Agatha’s wrist where she still held it.

“And you? Did you sleep at all?”

“Actually,” Agatha started but was interrupted by the sound of a knock at the villa door.

Rio pulled away suddenly, turning quickly before she could change her mind.

This had to be it. This had to be enough.

She’d had one night of feeling like Agatha might feel even a piece of what she felt for her, and that would have to continue to be enough.

They all went out to the Mercedes van that had arrived for them and Agatha slipped in first, clearly used to having someone else always take her bags for her because she didn’t even bother to offer the driver any help.

Jen did the same.

Rio and Alice just looked at each other, then helped heave the last of the bags into the trunk and went around to jump in the car.

Of the six seats available, obviously only two were occupied.

The issue was that one person sat in the very back of the car and the other sat in the front row.

Jen was in front.

Agatha in back.

And Rio knew where she’d have to sit to avoid the wrath of Jen. And Alice.

She clambered in quickly, not wanting to draw attention to it, and took her seat along the same row as Agatha, sliding the seat in front of her back down until it clipped in at the bottom.

Rio slid her sunglasses from her head and relaxed back into the comfortable leather seats, pressing a variety of buttons until she felt the seat warmer switch on and she could rest her head back, bracing herself for an hour and a half in close proximity with Agatha for the last time.

The car was mostly silent the whole way there, and it turned out that Rio’s concerns were unfounded.

She and Agatha hadn’t spoken, they hadn’t even touched.

The next contact Rio made with Agatha had been when she’d lifted her suitcase out and their hands had briefly met over the handle.

It was fleeting, but their eyes met and Rio thought she saw a sadness in Agatha’s eyes that hadn’t been there before.

But Alice was pushing her along, making sure Rio didn’t dawdle through security so they could board the plane on time.

Alice, as usual, had timed everything perfectly so that by the time they arrived at the gate they were already ready to board.

Rio moved on autopilot, always aware of where Agatha was in relation to her.

Two feet away.

Right beside her.

Behind her.

The window seat on the other side of the plane.

Her only means of distraction on the long flight back were the movies in the entertainment system.

But halfway through the flight, three glasses of red wine in, she lost all sense of where she was and the danger she’d be putting herself in by doing what she did.

She put on one of Agatha’s movies.

It was her Oscar-winning role. The story of a ex-concert pianist cutdown in her prime by a car accident that left her unable to play.

Rio had seen it more times than she could count.

But it was comforting to see Agatha’s face without worrying what she was thinking about, or how badly Rio could misread the way she was looking at her.

“Really?” A voice came from somewhere above her. “This one? Not Susan Sarandon flying off a cliff?”

Rio sat bolt upright when she realised who it was, and narrowly avoided sloshing her wine down her front.

“Agatha,” she said lamely, quickly reaching to switch the little tv off, ripping her headphones from her head, though the damage had already been done.

Agatha only smiled a little, her hand resting on the partition that separated Rio from the aisle beside her.

“I just came to tell you that Alice is now sitting with Jen which I think means you’re safe from work chat at least until we land.”

“Right,” Rio said distractedly, her blush now taking over her face.

She took a shot and glanced briefly up at Agatha, barely able to make eye contact, but saw that Agatha was smirking at the sight of Rio looking so mortified.

“Don’t say anything. It’s a good film.”

“I know. I won the Oscar for it.”
