Chapter 26: The Best Actress

Chapter Summary

The Best Actress is chosen.

Rio indulges a fantasy and is groped by reality.

Chapter Notes

So sorry about the cliffhanger but obviously I was always going to do that!!

I’ve somehow (again) written so much for this chapter and also not enough… forgive me

See the end of the chapter for more notes

2021 | Alice & Rio’s Apartment

“Rio!”

“God, fuck! In a minute! I burnt the fucking-…”

“Jesus, Rio, you’ll miss it!”

Rio growled and threw the bag of piping hot popcorn onto the counter. The kernels burst from it like a buttery fireworks display and Rio growled again but turned her back on the mess to rush through to the living room where her friends were gathered on the tiny, uncomfortable couch and the floor in front of it.

“It’s insane to me that she’s a real person. Like, living, breathing, you know?”

Rio huffed again as she squeezed in between Alice and Wanda and moved one of the flat cushions to cradle in her lap.

“Popcorn’s burnt.”

“You tried your best,” Wanda reassured as Alice laughed, “We have beer. Don’t worry about it.”

Rio grumbled a little and wriggled to try and steal more space but was unsuccessful in her attempts as Alice nudged her elbow sharply into her ribs.

“Shh,” Carol hushed urgently, flapping her hand from where she sat on the floor. “They’re announcing it.”

Rio scowled as she reached over for her now-warm beer and settled back again to focus on the tiny television screen in the tiny apartment she shared with Alice.

The picture now showed five previous Best Actress winners all standing in a semi-circle on the stage. They all, in their own ways, looked glamorous, beautiful, confident. To Rio they were goddess of stage and screen and she’d seen their work more times than she could count.

Though, admittedly, she thought one of the group was overrated. But no one else agreed so she often just kept that opinion to herself.

This way of announcing the nominees and eventual winner was new, had only been done once before, and Rio felt it was a little too schmaltzy.

Each were taking it in turns to reel off some spiel about the nominee they’d been assigned to publicly compliment. And Rio leant forwards in her seat, feeling Wanda’s hand rub her mid-back, as the esoteric Lilia Calderu filled the screen.

“Agatha Harkness!” She announced, smiling indulgently as the Dolby Theatre erupted in applause.

The favourite to win. Rio’s favourite ever.

“If she doesn’t win, I’ll-…” Alice started but stopped immediately when Rio and Carol shushed her again.

“Your power knows no bounds,” Lilia continued, twinkling from the stage down at where Agatha must be sitting in the front row.

“Your understanding and control of the craft is a gift to us all.”

And suddenly the picture on screen changed and Agatha Harkness was there in all her glory. Rio bit down on her lip, felt Alice beside her lean forwards a little too.

Agatha was smiling, she looked modest, touched. The crowd around her was applauding Lilia’s words, confirming them to the world.

“She’s so fucking hot,” Alice muttered as Lilia continued and the camera stayed focused on Agatha.

“Your performance in ‘The Concert Pianist’ was nothing short of extraordinary, my dear. And you are extraordinary in everything you do.”

Agatha inclined her head and Rio dropped her gaze to her lower lip that was now pulled between her teeth. She’d seen that lip up close, almost felt it against her own four years ago now.

“You truly are the best of us,” Lilia continued and the theatre erupted again to confirm what everybody already knew: Agatha was the best.

“I’m so in love with her,” Carol said absently and Rio kicked her gently in the side, her eyes still trained on Agatha’s face as she beamed up at the stage before the camera moved to the next presenter.

“My culture is not your costume.”

“Oh, come on. Everyone’s in love with her. She doesn’t belong to you, Rio.”

Rio sipped her beer and muttered, “I wish.”

She felt Wanda’s hand move against her back and she relaxed a little, but kept her eyes on the screen as the showcase of each actress came to an end.

The main presenter appeared back on the screen and little boxes of each nominee appeared beside her, Agatha in the top most right hand side. She looked calm, a smile only just tugging at her lips, and Rio wondered if she actually felt it or if her heart was thudding as loudly in her ears as Rio’s currently was.

“And the Oscar for Best Actress goes to…!”

The four women in Rio and Alice’s little living room all inhaled sharply as the presenter slipped open the golden envelope.

Rio leant forwards.

“Agatha Harkness!”

Alice cheered and leapt to her feet beside her and Rio grinned at the tv, swerving away from Alice’s legs to get a shot of Agatha as she rose to her feet. She watched as she kissed the man she knew to be her husband and felt a jolt of something in her chest as she turned her head from his and accepted only the briefest of cheek kisses before she was in the arms of her director.

Rio laughed as Carol pushed and pulled at her knees and she placed her beer down onto the safety of the coffee table before she looked back up and watched now as Agatha climbed her way up to the stage, her red dress billowing out behind her as she did.

“Jesus she’s unreal,” Rio breathed out, and wasn’t aware of it but Wanda had pulled her hand away.

“Imagine how fucking lucky her husband feels. He’s such a dick. He stood on my foot at that mixer we went to last fall,” Alice said as she stole Rio’s beer and sat back down again. “I like her manager though. Mean in a sexy-…”

“Alice. Shut up.”

Agatha was now at the microphone, holding her new Oscar in both hands. As the camera zoomed in Rio noticed her blue eyes shining with unshed tears and she wondered how anyone got anything done with Agatha looking like that anywhere near them.

Even seeing her across the room at parties she felt struck dumb by her. And any time she’d felt like they’d locked eyes she’d almost collapsed on the spot.

“You really know how to make a gal feel special.” Agatha laughed modestly, taking a second to look out over the crowd of people on their feet for her.

Carol shuffled over and leant her elbow on Rio’s leg.

“I wouldn’t be here tonight without my incredible cast and crew. With all of your hard work and dedication to this little movie. I’m in awe of all of you.”

“She’s not in awe of anyone,” Alice scoffed, “she’s-…”

“Shut up!”

“I’d like to thank The Academy for recognising this movie that meant so much to us as we were making it. My fellow nominees who…”

Rio chewed on her lip and placed her hand on Carol’s shoulder.

“… you’re just a dream to be around. Thank you for making this experience so magical for me.”

Agatha looked down at the Oscar as the applause washed over the audience.

“To my husband…” she looked up again, and looked out to the crowd where the camera switched to a view of Ralph. He had a big grin on his face and Rio felt irrationally angry about someone so handsome. “I have no words.”

“If I were married to Agatha Harkness-…” Alice started and Rio shushed her again, stealing her beer back.

“Performing is something I’ve done my whole life. I live and breathe this craft and it means everything to me that I’m standing up here tonight.”

The crowd erupted and Rio shifted forwards a little, wondering why Agatha looked more emotional talking about her craft than her husband.

“I share this with my manager, Jen, who has been by my side since college. And everyone who sees themselves up there on the screen, or on the stage. Anyone who shares my dreams.”

The crowd applauded again and Agatha smiled, a dazzling, watery smile that made Rio’s stomach flip.

“Finally, before I go, if I may, I’d like to dedicate this to the love of my life, my son, Nicky. Honey, mama loves you beyond life itself. To the moon and all the farthest stars. I can’t wait to squeeze you so tight when I get home. Thank you.”

She raised the Oscar and nodded her last thanks to the crowd before she strode away to more earth-shattering applause.

The four women in the little apartment were silent for a while, watching Agatha Harkness as she was ushered from the stage. It was Rio who broke the spell eventually: “I actually might be in love with her.”

Alice laughed and Rio looked down as Carol smiled up at her, “I’m afraid she would never be interested. Did you see how handsome her husband is?”

“Yeah but he’s an ass,” Alice added in Rio’s defence. “Rio’s only a dick.”

“Great, thank you.”

“I think you’d stand more of a chance with her mean manager,” Wanda said with a grin, “I hear she’s on our team.”

“Hello what now?” Alice was suddenly back on the couch, eyes wide as she leant around Rio to get to Wanda.

Rio laughed and shoved Alice off of her and reconfirmed in her own mind what she had been suspecting since the moment she’d shared with Agatha in the bathroom: that maybe she stood a slim chance with Agatha. And the other thing she was now sure of, more so than anything before in her life, was that if she won an Oscar and the person she loved were in the audience, she’d have plenty of words for her.

2025 | The Dolby Theatre

“And the Oscar for Best Actress goes to…!”

The room was still, silent.

And all Rio could feel was her heartbeat so loud in her ears and the intense, steady pressure of Agatha’s fingers wrapped tightly around her own.

She knew that three rows back from her, deep into the tangle of bodies in plush red chairs, that Alice would be leaning forwards in her seat, her own hand probably crushing the life out of her dad’s.

She could picture the people at home all placing their bets on whether it would be Agatha Harkness or Rio Vidal who would take home the trophy. She imagined their snacks laid out before them, the cool beer in their hands, the soft pyjamas they probably wore.

She wanted to be them. Wanted to be watching this from afar, undetached, unimpacted by whatever name was read out from the little gold envelope before her.

But she was here. She was clutching the hand of the woman she loved. The eyes of the world were on them but their touch was just for them.

Her mom squeezed her hand, Agatha’s fingers twitched.

She sucked in a breath.

“Rio Vidal!”

Rio’s body went rigid, petrified by the shock. And the fingers that once clutched at Agatha were ripped open as Agatha and her mom moved.

Anna leant over the armrest and pulled her daughter into a hold so tight that it shocked Rio back into her body. She was breathing again, but stiff still, her eyes wide and her mouth hanging open.

She rose slowly from her seat, helped by the hands of those people who had run over to get to her. But one pair of hands disregarded the rest and pulled Rio into a hold so tight she lost her breath again.

“Agatha,” she whispered without knowing really what else to say. But she held on tight, ignoring the other hands that tried to pull her to them and from her.

“You have to go, Rio. You have to go.”

Agatha released her hold, loosening without letting go, and Rio stared wide-eyed at her, unsure why tears were forming in bright blue eyes. She reached for her cheek and Agatha smiled, let her do it, whispered the words: “Rio. Baby.”

A pair of lips found her right arm and Rio turned to see Wanda beaming at her as Agatha began to push at her waist, directing her away from the small crowd that had formed and up to the stage. Wanda managed to kiss her cheek too and Rio smiled absently at her, realising she was beginning to cry too as the familiar feel of Agatha’s hands on her fell away.

Two men darted out to help her up the stairs and Rio turned naturally to her right to accept the help of Wanda’s brother rather than the alternative option of Ralph Bohner.

She smiled at the man whose name she’d already forgotten and clung to him until she was at the top of the stairs and able to make her way over to the Oscar that was now hers.

The presenter squeezed her and kissed her cheek and she turned to her waiting audience.

The room was on its feet, all still applauding, some cheering. And Rio had seen this before but only through the lens of the television, only when she was one of the masses in their pyjamas, watching the glamorous, unreal famous people accept their golden statues.

But down in the first row were the people who grounded her. Anna and Agatha now stood, arm in arm, both grinning up at her, one openly crying, the other just about holding it in.

“Dios mío,” Rio began, unconsciously slipping into her mother tongue as she stared down at Anna and Agatha. Her brow furrowed in confusion as a tear slipped from her eye. It seemed unfair suddenly that she’d been given this award and yet had no say in where she stood. Because she wanted to be where they were. She wanted to be wrapped up in them.

“No sé.” I don’t understand. She tried again, her gaze now locked into watery blue eyes as they shone up at her. But Agatha was nodding, encouraging her, and she winked as her smile widened and Rio released a laugh, halfway between relief and disbelief.

She closed her eyes for a second and turned back to the audience still on their feet for her. “This is… too much for one person to handle.”

She felt rather than heard the ripple of laughter through the theatre and took a breath as she reminded herself that this was her one shot at it. That this most likely wouldn’t happen again.

“Mi primer agradecimiento se lo prometí hace mucho tiempo a alguien a quien he amado durante años.” My first thank you I promised long ago to someone I have loved for years now.

Love. not in love. She couldn’t say it.

Rio knew most wouldn’t understand her, some would be annoyed she was speaking Spanish rather than the traditional English, but she couldn’t help it. Her speech would be translated and dissected over and over again anyway.

This felt most natural. It felt most herself.

She took a breath and turned back to Agatha, her arm no longer looped with her mother’s but instead around her shoulders, holding her as she cried.

“Agatha,” Rio smiled around her name, watched as Agatha smiled at the sound of it too, her free hand moving to her diaphragm as if to steady her breathing, “You’re the best person, the best actress, the best mother. I…” and she felt the words choke her, felt how they swelled in her throat, how they prevented her from saying any more.

She’d made a promise years ago that she would tell the woman she loved how much she loved her, if she were lucky enough to have a woman to love. And she was. She had her. But only secretly. Only in the dark. So she settled for choking on her words instead, letting them dissolve in her throat and settle heavily in her chest.

She shook her head, trying to shake them away as she dropped her gaze to the award in her hands and let the applause for Agatha speak for her instead.

“And to the other best mother in my life,” she raised her gaze to her mom and grinned at her, laughing as she saw Anna shake her head at her and wipe quickly at her eyes, knowing as she did that she was on camera.

The crowd laughed with Rio as she took a second to steady and swallow down again the words that had almost escaped her earlier.

“Te amo. Tú y papá me habéis enseñado a amar y a ser amado. Y estoy aquí hoy gracias a ti. Te amo, mamá. Te amo, papá.” I love you. You and dad have shown me how to love and how to be loved. And I am here today because of you. I love you, mom. I love you, dad.

Through the applause again she heard a whistle and she looked up in the direction it came from. Her dad’s whistle. One she’d heard a million times before when she was on a generational run across the basketball court, when she was streaking ahead during track, when she was taking a bow at curtain call.

She grinned so hard she laughed again. “Thanks, dad.”

The crowd laughed with her and Rio knew she had them in her clutches, that for one brief moment in time the whole world was under her spell.

She took another breath and let herself take it all in, needing a second to calm her racing heart.

“I don’t accept this lightly. I know what a huge honour it is to even be amongst you all tonight. And I’m so grateful to be here. So hugely in awe of everyone. So thrilled to be here with my fellow nominees.”

More applause. Some hollering.

“Wanda, Jessica, Isla, Sylvia, and Agatha. All of you… it’s incredible to me I’m even considered worthy of being here amongst you.”

More clapping. She looked up and saw Agatha was frozen in place, the pale hand on her front now twisted in the velvet.

“My beautiful cast and crew, I love you all so much. I share this with you. I wouldn’t be here without your talent and support and joy.”

She tried to find them in the crowd but could only see the faceless masses and Agatha down at the front, still clutching her dress, still holding her mom, still beaming her teary grin up at Rio.

“I really should go before I say anything that’ll get me in trouble.” Not a lie.

Laughter. Her mom shaking her head again.

“Thank you for this. Thank you to the Academy. Really. I’m… speechless, thank you. Te veo.”

She held her award up and grinned at her audience and then turned to leave the stage.

Rio Vidal didn’t breathe again until Alice found her. She was aware she was being taken somewhere, aware there was a camera in her face, aware people were brushing her arms as she went past and smiling their congrats at her but she couldn’t take any of it in.

She smiled and nodded and grinned and laughed but she felt separate from it, so out of her mind with disbelief that she couldn’t feel her own body.

Only when a familiar touch grabbed her side and she was turned into the arms of her best friend did she understand what had happened.

“Alice.”

“Holy shit.”

“Alice.”

“Holy shit.”

“Alice.”

“No, Rio. Holy shit.”

“I’m going to have a panic attack.”

Alice pulled back with wide eyes and her tear-stained face and she held Rio firmly in front of her, nodding quickly as she assessed the promise in Rio’s words.

“Breathe with me,” she urged, taking in slow, obvious breaths so Rio could follow along. She did so and found her chest loosening after a while, her body giving into the adrenaline coursing through her veins as it quivered occasionally on Alice’s hold.

When Rio felt more in control she nodded and Alice pulled her back in for a hug and Rio was grateful she wasn’t making her keep to a tight schedule for once in their working relationship. She just held her, let Rio breathe against her, let her recover.

Rio pulled away only when she knew she could handle it and smiled dazedly down at Alice who still looked concerned. “Can you believe it?”

“Babe, I’ve believed it since we started this whole thing.”

Rio rolled her eyes and raised her arm to wipe away the lipstick on Alice’s face but Alice moved before she could and lifted her right arm to rub away the lipstick that Rio had on her.

“Agatha?”

“Probably.”

Alice laughed then, and it took over her completely. She almost bent double and Rio caught the laughter too and dissolved into it as if she hadn’t just been having a total crisis in her best friend’s arms.

They recovered together and moved together to the press rooms where Rio was applauded upon entering and cheered when she held her new trophy up for the world’s press to see.

“Rio! Congratulations!”

“Thank you,” Rio said with a laugh as she tried to find which of the press was now talking to her.

“Over here.” A man waved and she turned to him with a nod.

“Hello!”

“Hi. Your speech, was it a conscious decision to speak in Spanish?”

“Are you consciously speaking in English right now?”

There was a smattering of laughter and Rio smiled as she was directed to the next question.

“Congrats, Rio. Did you have any idea of the way tonight would go?”

“God, no. I thought it was Agatha’s all along.”

She turned to the next and smiled as she was congratulated again.

“You thanked Agatha first in your speech. We’ve had the translation through now. Do you consider her a mentor of sorts?”

And Rio laughed because what would Agatha say to this?

“A friend, first. But… I do look up to her, obviously. She’s twice the actor I’ll ever be.”

Another, and then another, and another, and Rio soon lost track of how many questions she’d answered. But they were all relatively innocuous, and she got away with mostly smiling and nodding and giving one-line sound bites for each publication and channel.

Alice was soon ushering from from the makeshift stage again and she left the room to more applause and soon found herself in another corridor where Jasmine her makeup artist was waiting to touch her up and make her photograph ready.

When her lipstick had been reapplied and her hair adjusted she was taken to pose with her fellow winners. The weight of the golden statue in her hand began to feel normal, began to almost anchor her down to the ground where she was still in danger of floating off into the clouds.

“Is that it? Please tell me I can get drunk now.”

Alice laughed as she pushed Rio along through another crowded area full of flashing cameras and people jostling for Rio’s attention.

“We gotta get the statue engraved, babe. Make it official.”

Rio pretended to be annoyed by this but really her name on an Academy Award was something she’d dreamt of since she was old enough to have dreams. So she grinned widely and made no more complaint as an attendant, after congratulating Rio profusely, took her over to the little area where there were hoards of other winners looking to get their metal made official.

Rio sidled up to the handsome Best Supporting Actor and exchanged comfortable small talk with him as she was handed a glass of champagne and photographed from every possible angle. She was so pleased, in that moment, that Alice had insisted Jasmine tag along with them that night.

But soon the award was back in her hands and now, amongst the details of the award, it read: RIO VIDAL.

“Holy fucking shit.”

She mingled some more, Alice telling her to relax and finish her champagne which she did in record time because she needed it and because she was desperate to see her parents and to get through all of this so she could find Agatha again.

Alice helped to extract her once she was done. She’d done her job and she’d done it well so she relaxed now and her grin became more soft as she swung her golden man through the hallways. That was, until Alice broke the bad news that the next room she was taking her to she’d need to be on her best behaviour for.

“A couple big journos, okay? Actually, there’s a third one and she’s a nightmare. But nothing you can’t handle.”

“Jesus. What? I thought I was done with the press.”

Alice sighed heavily and as they stopped outside the door she turned to Rio and held her arms, “You’ve got this. I believe in you, remember. Big deep breaths.”

Rio nodded and forced a smile, forcing it to turn into a grin wide enough to hide her fear.

Alice smiled back at her and turned to open the door. But she didn’t walk in first like she usually would to announce Rio’s arrival. She instead pushed it and held it and stepped aside for Rio to go in before her.

But Rio didn’t move. Because standing inside the little room were three of her favourite people.

Anna, Miguel, and Agatha.

“You bitch,” she muttered for Alice’s ears only but her best friend simply beamed at her and ushered her in.

“You have ten minutes. Go!”

Rio laughed as she made quick strides to launch herself at her dad, finding her mom’s arms around her almost immediately too. She cried in between them, felt her dad brushing down her hair and her mom rubbing her back.

“Nosotras estamos muy orgullosas de ti.” We are so proud of you.

Rio felt her mom grip her harder and she released a shaky laugh as she lifted her head to look at them both and grinned through their tears.

Alice didn’t even pull Rio away when Anna kissed over her daughter’s face.

Rio laughed again as she moved back and looked up to see the third person who’d been waiting for her. Agatha stood quietly off to the side, a faint smile on her face as she watched the reunion, her left hand clutching her right arm.

She looked shy, like she’d stumbled into something she shouldn’t be part of. But Rio wanted her here, she had to know Rio wanted her here.

“Ve a abrazarla.” Go hug her.

Anna pushed her daughter towards Agatha. But Rio didn’t really need the encouragement. She practically stumbled her way to her and paused when she was directly in front of her.

Agatha’s eyes looked glassy and Rio lost her train of thought for a second as she stared into them.

Neither of them moved.

“Did you schedule in this meeting? I’m an Oscar winner now. Very important. Very busy.”

Agatha smirked at her. “Alice gave me a special pass for tonight, superstar.”

“Is that right?”

Rio bit on her lip to hide her own smirk and turned to look over her shoulder at her parents, shooting Alice a look too. “Could we have a second?”

She watched as they all turned, her dad not without a squeeze of her arm, and left them to it.

Anna was the last to leave and had corralled the others before her and Rio turned back to Agatha missing her mom watching her for a second before she finally closed the door behind her.

“A special pass?”

Agatha pursed her lips, her gaze moved slowly down her right arm, seemed to linger there for a second, then dropped to the Oscar hanging from Rio’s right hand. “It’s actually a lifetime pass.”

“Lifetime, huh? Seems… official.”

Rio gasped quietly as blue eyes flashed back up to meet her own and Agatha grinned at her, teasing and wicked.

“We only have five minutes, Rio.”

“You just said a lifetime.”

Agatha laughed as Rio grinned. Agatha stepped forwards and Rio raised her chin as pale hands slid to hold her head, her thumbs brushing tenderly over her cheeks.

“How do you feel?”

“A little drunk, weirdly. A little emotional. Very surprised.”

“You deserve it.”

“I do?”

“Rio.”

“You’re not…” Rio grinned, watching as Agatha’s gaze honed in on her smile. “Jealous?”

“I’ll let you have this one. There are plenty more for me to win.”

Rio laughed as Agatha continued her movements against her cheeks. Her words were teasing but her face was soft and as Rio’s laughter died down she breathed in slowly, the soft scent of familiar perfume relaxing her even as her body quivered from the excess adrenaline still coursing through her.

“I’m so proud of you.”

Agatha smiled a little as she leant in to kiss Rio, capturing her lower lip and making Rio whimper quietly and it took her a second to get her brain in gear to be able to kiss Agatha back.

When Agatha pulled away she dropped her hands from her face and moved the cape part of her dress to wrap around Rio and they tangled themselves together, with Rio’s shining Oscar resting now against Agatha’s back.

“Your mom has been crying since you won.”

Agatha’s voice was soft and low against her ear and Rio smiled and turned her head into her more, blinking owlishly as she rested her forehead against Agatha’s. She took a deep breath.

“You looked pretty teary yourself from where I was standing.”

“You wish,” Agatha said with a grin as she angled up to kiss Rio. It was delicate, unassuming, and finished too quickly. But Rio smiled all the same as Agatha leant in again to kiss the corner of her smile, to press her nose in against Rio’s warm cheek.

“Did you like my speech?” Rio asked quietly, feeling her heart rate slow to a steady pace again in Agatha’s hold.

Agatha nodded against her, placing a kiss to her cheek before she pulled away to meet Rio’s gaze, “You looked incredible up there.”

Rio smiled and squeezed Agatha’s waist, moving her hand back to brush over the soft velvet against her hip. “It should have been yours.”

Agatha laughed and pressed her face in against Rio’s cheek again, falling into silence for a few seconds before she whispered, “It was always going to be yours. I wanted you to get it. Enjoy it.”

“And you’ll get the next one?”

“Oh, honey. I said enjoy it. Not get used to it.”

Rio laughed and Agatha grinned against her cheek, “I mean it.”

Rio exhaled a laugh and pulled back, finding it difficult with how tight Agatha’s hold was on her. “You can’t threaten an Oscar winner.”

“I have a special pass, remember?”

Rio rolled her eyes and held up her Oscar, moving it between them and beaming up at Agatha. “He’s handsome.”

“Mmhm.”

“Never been attracted to a man before.”

Agatha moved her arms down Rio’s body, linking her fingers over the small of Rio’s back where their hips pressed together.

“Has winning an Oscar awoken something in you that I won’t like?”

“I’m still a one woman gal, if that’s what you’re worried about.”

Agatha raised her brows and maintained eye contact with Rio as she leant in and kiss the statue on his back. “Then I’m okay with him.”

“Rio! We’re coming in!”

Rio rolled her eyes, the spell of Agatha’s gaze broken as the reality of where they were crashed down around her. Agatha pulled back and Rio smiled sadly as Agatha kissed her cheek quickly and then took a step back and brushed down her dress.

“Smooth,” Rio mouthed across at her and received a smirk in response just as the door opened again and Rio turned to greet her adoring parents.

She felt a hand on her side and a body briefly press against hers from behind as Agatha leant in to kiss her cheek again and Rio grinned because of it. “I’ll see you soon.”

She watched her leave, pausing briefly to hug her mom and kiss her dad before she hit the door, turned to smile briefly in Rio’s direction, and then left.

Rio felt like she’d taken her heart with her.

“Vidal!” Alice called, clapping her hands in front of Rio’s face to get her to snap out of it.

Rio rolled her eyes but smiled at her friend. “Yes. Ready. Let’s go.”

“Umm,” Alice said quickly, holding her hand up as she turned to shout for Jasmine.

“Really, Alice? We’re only going to the car.” Anna moved in to brush her thumbs over Rio’s cheeks and smile at her daughter. Rio huffed a little but closed her eyes as her mom began to fix her face until Jasmine could work her magic again.

“Lots of tears, huh?” Jasmine said with a grin. “Agatha didn’t look so polished either when she walked past just there.”

And Rio turned to Agatha and sat in stunned silence as Agatha stood and busied herself with serving. She looked at ease, unmoved by Rio’s incomprehension, focused instead on piling the plates with a meal Rio hadn’t had since she was last home.

“My mom told you,” Rio eventually deduced, her brain kicking into gear again as Agatha placed her bowl down before her on the placemat.

“Your dad, actually.”

Agatha sat down and Rio reached to tug her chair around some more which made Agatha look at her with a wry smile that Rio was soon leaning over to kiss away. “Thank you.”

Agatha sighed against Rio’s mouth, and kissed her again, her hand moving to hold the back of Rio’s head so they could rest together for a minute. “You’re welcome. If it tastes burnt…”

Rio grinned and Agatha grinned back, eventually letting go so they could both eat.

It had happened so easily. They’d fallen into a domestic reality that was far better that any of Rio’s fantasies. Agatha was at ease with Rio simply being there. They sat so that, every now and again, Agatha could reach to squeeze her hand - usually after she’d said something to tease Rio or when conversation lulled and she simply wanted to be touching her.

And Rio found that instead of trying to show off, as she usually might, she relaxed into it. She felt calm and less anxious than she had been for weeks.

Because regardless of what she’d said about compatibility before, she’d already decided nothing could sway her from wanting this. Wanting it forever. And she thought that perhaps Agatha felt the same.

“Okay,” Agatha said out of nowhere when they were both done with their food, soft but firm, “You wanted to talk.”

Rio pushed her plate away and watched as Agatha sipped her wine, her blue eyes alert as they looked everywhere but at Rio. She was nervous. Rio could see it in the way she played with the place mat, in the way she bounced her leg, in the way her sip turned into five more.

“Will we sit somewhere more comfortable?”

This question seemed to take Agatha by surprise. Perhaps she thought Rio would go for the jugular immediately. But ”Will you leave your husband for me?” wouldn’t be the best place to start, and besides, Rio wasn’t like that.

She stood, picked up her wine and the bottle, and motioned with her head for Agatha to follow her.

The walk to the couch felt longer than it was. Thirteen steps, all in. Each one heavier than the last. The concept of Agatha struggling to open up to her had weighed heavily on Rio’s mind for weeks now. The idea of her being frightened or ashamed or simply unwilling, was almost too painful to comprehend.

But she’d offered to talk now. So Rio had to tread carefully.

Rio sat at the end of the couch and leant back against the arm, placing the bottle of wine on the coffee table. She watched as Agatha hesitated and then mirrored her position at the other end and Rio forced a warm smile, watching as Agatha toyed with the stem of her glass.

“You don’t have to be so nervous.” I’m nervous too.

“I’m not.”

Rio nodded, focused on Agatha’s fingers. Agatha was a great actress, the best of them, but a terrible liar.

“Ooookay,” Rio raised her brows as Agatha’s eyes flashed up to meet her own. “Then why do you look so scared?”

Agatha cleared her throat and dropped her gaze again and Rio, despite her smile, could have cried.

She chewed on her lip as she focused in on the pale fingers that tapped a rhythm on the stem of her wine glass. She didn’t want to spook her. “Why the name Nicholas?”

The question just came to her, stolen from an errant thought she’d had when she’d first met Nicky. It was something she was curious to know, but it wasn’t what she wanted to ask.

Though the lowball question, the excuse to talk about her son seemed to loosen Agatha a little. Her fingers stopped twitching, her jaw relaxed. “It means ‘victory’, or ‘victory of the people’. He felt like my one success. I wanted him to grow up and know that from the moment I knew of him, he was my hero.”

Rio’s chest ached with a desire to reach out to Agatha again. But she only smiled, only bit down on the corner of her lip.

“And not ‘Bohner’?”

“No,” Agatha said softly, “I never took it and no son of mine would either.”

“Is Ralph a Harkness?”

“No.”

Rio nodded and watched as Agatha’s fingers returned to their tapping. Nicky had relaxed her. Ralph had spooked her.

“Favourite ice cream flavour?”

“What?”

Rio inclined her head, “It shouldn’t be a hard question.”

“Pecan.”

A laugh escaped her and Agatha briefly looked scandalised. “What’s wrong with pecan?”

“It’s just… pecan. Mine’s chocolate.”

“Basic,” Agatha retorted, her lips twitching. Her fingers had stopped tapping. She was relaxing again.

“Okay, favourite colour?”

“Rio.”

“What?”

“I thought you wanted to talk.”

“I’m talking. Getting to know you. Relaxing you.”

Agatha sighed and scratched at her scalp, turning her head away. “You don’t need to baby me.”

“I’m not. I just want you to relax. This doesn’t have to be stressful.”

Agatha closed her eyes and Rio’s lower lip pulled back between her teeth again. She waited until Agatha looked back at her and saw her gaze was warm, her blue eyes the colour of the sea.

“I can’t talk with you so far away.”

Rio raised her brows and tilted her head as Agatha adjusted herself. She moved from sitting with her legs crossed to her legs straight out before her, now parted to welcome Rio in. Rio smiled as Agatha held her free hand out and she shuffled on her knees towards her before she turned and sat back against her.

Agatha settled more around her and Rio swallowed down a swell of emotions when she realised this was the first time Agatha had held her like this. It was the first time she’d asked to hold her. She was only this needy when half asleep, when… but Rio realised suddenly she’d never really had the opportunity to be with Agatha for any length of time when she could be needy with her in a way that wasn’t between moans and stolen touches.

Maybe Agatha, in unstolen time, simply wanted her close.

Her heart ached at the prospect of a week with Agatha always wanting her nearby. Reaching for her, asking for her.

And as if Agatha could hear the hopeful promises of Rio’s internal monologue, Agatha’s arm was around her waist and she rested her wine against her hip, and Rio felt her press her nose into her hair and breathe her in. It felt extremely intimate. And Rio felt good about it, felt warm from the knowledge that Agatha was calming herself with her touch, taking her time to feel her against her, to luxuriate in the presence of her, to breathe her in.

“It’s purple,” Agatha said into her hair. “Violet, rather than lavender.”

“Like the lakers,” Rio said with a smile, remembering that first day in Agatha’s house.

“Mmhm.”

Rio entwined their fingers then, squeezing Agatha’s hand.

“What else do you want to know?”

“Tell me about your childhood.”

Agatha exhaled slowly and Rio couldn’t be sure but it felt like she was trying to buy time as she did. She was silent for a while and then she admitted: “It was unhappy. Hard.” Agatha tightened her hold on her and Rio turned her head to angle into Agatha, feeling her shift immediately and press in close to her ear. She lingered for a second and then pressed a soft kiss at the highest point of her cheekbone. “I don’t talk about it much. Don’t like to think about it.”

Rio nodded and Agatha pulled back so she turned her head away again, and was silent for a while, letting Agatha take her time with it.

And then Agatha began to talk about it.

“My father died not long after I was born.”

Rio squeezed Agatha’s hand.

“Probably a saving grace. He was apparently as cruel as my mother.”

Evanora, Rio thought. She’d heard rumours of her, of course. Read articles. There had even been a long read in the New York Times about her a couple years ago: Evanora’s Empire. It had been an exploration of her decades at the top of every list of business heavyweights, the political power she wielded, the empire she’d built by being friendly with the most hard-line in society.

She already knew Agatha didn’t like to discuss her. She’d seen it in Italy - when the sun had been warm and Agatha’s reaction to her mother being mentioned had been cold.

Rio began to chew on her lip again, trying to weave together the complex web that was Agatha’s life.

“I was raised mostly by a woman named Isobel. She was from Mexico. She was a maid. I had nannies, of course. But Isobel… she was kind, and soft. She used to sneak me candy and every week she’d teach me ten more words. My mother didn’t want me to speak to the staff… but she wasn’t around a lot.”

“Ten words?” Rio asked softly, “In Spanish?”

“Yes.”

The impact on Rio’s soul was immediate. She felt instantly aflame with hatred for Evanora. The woman who’d birthed Agatha but had not nurtured, not loved her. And Agatha had defied her because every child reaches for softness when all they know is the opposite.

“Anyway, Isobel died when I was fifteen. She had a sudden heart attack and… I didn’t get to go to the funeral because-…”

But Rio had shifted, had pulled away so she could lean around and look at Agatha. Agatha blinked slowly and Rio frowned at her, “Baby.”

“It was a long time ago, Rio.”

Rio shifted more and winced at the twist of it as she slipped her hand by Agatha’s hip to hold herself up, settling a few inches down from Agatha’s face in the soft cushions of the couch. “I’m so sorry you lost her.”

Agatha smiled a little and raised her hand to Rio’s cheek, brushing her thumb gently across her cheekbone. “It’s fine, Rio. Really. I’m fine.”

Rio didn’t believe her. But she pulled away slowly and turned back to her previous position and let Agatha pull her back against her. Agatha was quiet again for a while but she’d buried her nose in Rio’s hair and Rio turned into the touch, letting Agatha have a moment to gather herself.

“Anyway… My mother was always there in the background, checking my grades and making sure I was friends with the right people. And I toed the line… I kept my head down.”

Agatha cleared her throat quietly and Rio looked down at their entwined fingers, drawing soft circles against Agatha’s pale skin with her thumb.

“I started performing in plays… Shakespeare, mostly, and my drama teacher gave me scripts and drove me to auditions when she realised I had something. But I could never book anything because my mother wouldn’t… anyway.”

Rio shook her head a little, staring blindly ahead.

“Then I went to college and got a boyfriend. I hadn’t kissed anyone yet. I hadn’t ever... wanted to. Not really, anyway. No one I ever thought I could kiss.”

Rio squeezed her hand and felt Agatha sigh into her hair. “His name was Luke and he was so gloriously dumb but he was gentle and so he was my first. But my mother didn’t approve. He wasn’t from the right family.”

“Jesus Christ,” Rio murmured under her breath, and Agatha kissed the back of her head.

“My mother had made the call to Ralph’s mother before I even met him. I was engaged before I…”

And Agatha stopped, squeezed Rio’s waist and lifted her wine up. When the glass returned to Rio’s hip it was empty. Rio frowned at it, her hold on Agatha’s other hand now vicelike.

“He was the best I could have hoped for at the time. He was bland, vanilla, nothing. Being tied to him was better than being tied to my mother.”

“You shouldn’t be tied to anyone,” Rio said quietly, feeling as she did a heat rise in her cheeks, a fury fire in her belly. “That’s bullshit, Agatha.”

But it was hypocritical. A bare-faced lie. Because Rio wanted Agatha to be tied to her. In another, happier moment she might have imagined Agatha walking down the street with a little red string attached to her wrist, tugging a willing Rio along behind her, the same red string circling her own wrist.

Only Rio would never force it. She’d loop the string around every part of herself and hold it as an offering to Agatha, praying one day she’d take it but never demanding she did.

Agatha shifted behind her to place her empty glass down on the floor and Rio took the opportunity to move, to hasten to her knees and turn back to look at Agatha properly. She looked tense, her fingers now twisting in her lap, her right toying with her empty left ring finger.

“It’s what it is.”

“That doesn’t mean it’s okay.”

Rio cautiously placed her hands on Agatha’s thighs, trying to relax her face as Agatha’s jaw flexed.

“I don’t need saved.”

“I’m not trying to save you. I’m telling you… I’m…”

And Agatha looked up then, her sea glass eyes cautious as they met Rio’s earnest brown. “I’m so fucking sorry you thought marrying him was the only option. I’m sorry… I’m sorry you feel trapped.”

Agatha dropped her gaze again and Rio moved her hands up to her hips, twisting her fingers into the soft fabric of her sweatpants, “Come here. Come back to me. Don’t pull away.”

Agatha didn’t respond for a while but with Rio’s encouragement she slowly shuffled closer, finally letting Rio tug her into her lap. Agatha’s hands were cool as they rested on Rio’s neck and Agatha’s nose was colder still as she pressed it into Rio’s cheek.

“Is that enough?”

Rio frowned and turned her head to look at Agatha properly, watching her as she raised her hand to Rio’s cheek. “Enough what?”

“Talking.”

No.

Rio was quiet for a while, the volume of her ‘no’ getting louder and louder in her own brain until she eventually whispered, “Does she know you’re queer?”

Agatha looked away.

“I think so.”

Rio felt the fury burn her again and she had to grit her teeth to prevent herself from saying something she couldn’t take back. Agatha’s thumb moved down to brush across her lips as her gaze dropped to them. “Why are you reacting this way?”

Rio’s brows knitted together and she pulled back a little, watching as Agatha’s eyes flashed with sudden panic. “What other way would I react?”

“Surely the fact that I’m married is-…”

“Agatha.”

Rio sighed heavily and closed her eyes, trying in earnest to keep her temper at bay. “I hate that you’re married, of course I do. But I fucking hate even more that you’re married to a man that not only you don’t like but in a marriage that you were forced into by your bigot fucking mother.”

Agatha was silent. Immobile on top of her. And after a while Rio opened her eyes to look at her. And she saw that Agatha looked astonished.

“Ag-..?”

Rio’s question was lost as Agatha pressed their lips together. Fierce and heavy. Rio made a quiet noise against her and then came to her senses and kissed her back.

The kiss was initially firm but chaste until Agatha made it anything but. She pressed into Rio and wrapped her legs around her as they devoured each other with lips and teeth and tongue.

Until Agatha was clawing at Rio’s scalp, her hips beginning to rock desperately against her abdomen, her mouth relentless in its devotion.

Agatha tasted like red wine and something Rio couldn’t describe but that she thought of privately as heaven.

But Agatha pulled away long before Rio wanted her too, breaking the kiss with a strength Rio would never have had. And they panted into each others mouths, Agatha’s hips stilling even as Rio gripped them and held her flush to her stomach.

“I don’t,” Agatha began, barely able to get the words out for her heavy breathing, “I don’t need saving.”

Rio nodded, knowing Agatha was too proud to ever admit that her kiss had meant to opposite. “I know. Baby, I know.”

Agatha leant in and kissed her again, and Rio frowned into it, feeling the sting of Agatha clutching at the roots of her hair until she relented and broke away.

Rio blinked her eyes open again and saw Agatha already looking at her, saw the green in her dilated eyes, saw the flush across her pale cheeks. She kissed Agatha’s pouting bottom lip and sucked gently on it, pulling away reluctantly to look back up again.

“You’re safe with me,” Rio murmured as Agatha inhaled audibly, her eye lids fluttering closed at Rio’s quiet promise. “You always will be.”

“You’re doing it again.”

“Doing what?”

“Being too sweet.”

Rio smiled and Agatha’s lips twitched. They looked at each other for a while, until Agatha’s soft expression became more serious and Rio felt her heart thrum harder against her ribcage.

“Is it always this easy?”

“What?”

“Being with someone.”

Rio gasped quietly as Agatha brushed their lips together, barely a kiss, more an instinct.

“I think when it’s the right person it feels easy, yes.”

Agatha kissed her again then, slow this time, somehow sure. And Rio’s hold on her changed so she could rub Agatha’s back, brushing her hands slowly up and down, coming to a halt only when Agatha pulled away again.

“I’m tired,” Agatha said matter-of-factly, and it was clear on her face suddenly, the heaviness of her reality beyond the walls of their little sanctuary suddenly laid bare for Rio to see.

“We should go to bed.”

We.

This was the first night they could be that. Rio, a woman who so secretly feared she’d always be just a me, felt her heart stutter in her chest, feasting itself on the Agatha’s crumbs.

Rio released Agatha to let her climb from her. She took the hand that she held out to her. She walked silently with her, just one step behind, and arrived into the bedroom with her. Agatha let her go and disappeared into the bathroom and Rio found an old t-shirt she’d packed to wear and threw off her clothes to change into it.

As she waited for Agatha to return she heard her voice over and over in her brain repeating the things she’d clearly been telling herself after being raised like a pig to slaughter: “he was bland, vanilla, nothing”. But now this nothing man was the anchor holding Agatha down beneath the surface. Her mother was the unforgiving tide, churning without mercy, forcing her daughter deeper instead of teaching her how to swim.

“Hey.”

Rio startled and looked up. Agatha had appeared again, her hair up, her face shining from where she’d washed and cleansed. “You okay?”

“Yeah,” Rio said quickly, too quickly, that Agatha caught on and frowned as Rio stepped towards her. “Just a lot to think about.”

Agatha nodded and bit her lip as Rio kissed her cheek and stepped around her.

“We’re okay though?”

Rio’s hand was on the bathroom door handle, halfway to opening it as she turned back to Agatha with a frown, “Agatha, nothing you could tell me would make us not okay.”

Agatha smiled but it didn’t reach her eyes and she turned away before Rio could see.

When Rio crawled into bed beside Agatha that night she didn’t comment on the t-shirt Agatha wore that she’d clearly stolen from her bag, she didn’t say anything as Agatha silently manoeuvred them to entangle together, and she said nothing when Agatha began to draw soft circles along the small of her back.

But Agatha spoke when Rio finally closed her eyes: “You didn’t ask about Nicky’s middle name.”

Rio frowned into the dark, fighting to compute. “What?”

“His middle name.”

“His…? What is it?”

“River.”

Rio’s frown changed then as she raised her brows and slowly opened her eyes. Agatha was already watching her, already trying to gage her reaction. “River?”

“I met a woman once who was wild and brilliant and I wanted him to…”

“Agatha.”

“I just thought you should know. Go to sleep, Rio.”

Rio stared across at the woman before her through the dim, the woman currently wearing yet another piece of her clothing she’d just stolen. The woman who was raised in cruelty but was so far from cruel. The woman who was so tightly curled around her, trying to get closer, trying to melt into Rio.

“My love,” Rio whispered reverently, half dumbfounded, half desperate, “his name is River?”

“His name,” Agatha said slowly, tugging Rio’s leg until it was draped over her hip, “isn’t as important as you sleeping.”

She leant in and nudged their noses together, Rio’s frown as deep as ever. “Did you name him after me?”

Agatha nodded soundlessly, and Rio continued to stare, watching as Agatha grew shy and turned her face into the pillow.

Their first night together Agatha had said a week wouldn’t even be enough, a sentiment they’d both acknowledged since, and that Rio felt more viscerally now than ever before. Because how could any limited amount of time with Agatha be enough? With the feel of her against her, the scent of her floral perfume filling her lungs, the hypnotic blue eyes she would gladly drown herself in.

The soft, surprising ways she found to tell Rio what she was so desperate to hear, even without saying the words: “I love you too.”

And so, in the hopes that maybe she could make it clear where she stood in a night so fraught with confessions and thick with ghosts of Agatha’s past, she said: “I want you to know,” Rio murmured, moving her hand from Agatha’s back to rest on her cheek. “That if we made a go of this, a real one, then I’d be whatever you wanted me to be for Nicky.”

Agatha hadn’t raised her gaze yet and Rio wondered if it was because she’d already said too much, already revealed too much of herself. She gave her time. She let her sit in the silence for a while. And only when it became clear that Agatha wouldn’t, couldn’t, say anything, she pulled her hand back.

Agatha closed her eyes and Rio smiled sadly as she pressed closer, debating on rolling them over and pulling Agatha on top of her, wanting to feel the weight of her. Wanting to be the thing that supported her on this earth.

But she didn’t. She simply watched, counted the freckles on her nose.

“I love you.”

Agatha responded by rubbing her bare thigh. Rio let the motion soothe her, helping her brain to calm, her body to melt more into Agatha’s. As Rio drifted, Agatha slid her hand up to the bend at her hip and tapped gently, purposefully, four times.

Chapter 28: A Week: Wednesday, Thursday, Friday

Chapter Summary

Agatha realises what happiness is.

Rio realises too.

Chapter Notes

There is so much smut in this and it is so long I can only apologise

See the end of the chapter for more notes

WEDNESDAY

Rio woke with no thoughts in her empty head. But a lightly snoring woman in her arms.

Agatha Harkness was facing away from her, curled in on herself, her hair that had once been up in a neat bun, was now spread like wildfire behind her.

Rio was barely holding on. But she had her.

She lay still for a while, transitioning from sleeping to waking. The process was slow, a result of a long drive, a heavy night, and a bottle of red wine.

Sure Agatha was fast asleep still, she peeled away and slipped from the room.

When downstairs in the soft morning light she put on the coffee and tidied away the remnants of last night’s dinner.

Agatha was to be the chef for the week, so Rio could be the one who cleaned. She did so quickly, quietly, wanting Agatha to wake to a spotless kitchen and not have to witness Rio’s frustrated sighs when she couldn’t source the right locations for each thing she tidied away.

Agatha deserved a spotless kitchen. She deserved an easy life; a soft morning buried in the hills with someone who wanted to give that to her.

Rio debated going back to wake her. She considered bringing her a coffee or her best attempt at scrambled eggs. But it was still early. And bed was where Agatha could be warm and safe, away from the fears that plagued her.

So Rio took her own fears, alongside her mug of coffee and the large throw she’d stolen from the couch, and went to settle on one of the loungers on the balcony. It was cold, crisp. The morning air was relentless in its chill. And Rio tugged her knees close as she wrapped the blanket snuggly about her and cradled her coffee.

Over the hills she could see the famous bay, laid out like a painting. A Frisco fresco.

As she warmed herself, she thought of Agatha, snug in their bed. She thought of Agatha as she had been, back when she was in Evanora’s clutches. She thought of Agatha in Ralph’s large hands. She thought of Agatha wrapped in her own arms, where she hoped she always felt safe and loved.

She thought of Agatha as she was, as she is, as she would be.

And in thinking of her, she realised she loved her, not just the woman she knew, but every piece of her. Every past, present, future, her.

She took a sip of her coffee. She burnt her tongue.

She poked the tip of it to her top lip, feeling the cool air sting as it washed over it.

They were like two sides of the same coin, her and Agatha. Rio had been loved, endlessly, joyfully, unconditionally. And Agatha had been kept, molded, squashed, but certainly not loved.

And yet they both wanted it, and wanted it desperately.

Rio had found what she’d been looking for in Agatha. And she hoped Agatha had found what she had been looking for in Rio.

Because Rio would never keep, would never try to mold, would never squash Agatha. She would only love her the way she’d been taught. The way she’d dreamt about loving someone until those dreams had shifted into dreams of loving Agatha like that.

“Hey.”

Rio jumped, almost spilling her hot coffee over herself. She turned to see Agatha standing hesitantly by the door.

“Morning, mi corazon.”

She smiled with the grace of a person who was looking at something beautiful, something only for them to see.

Agatha seemed to deliberate before she moved, before she closed the door behind her. But then she hurried, tip-toeing along the cool floor of the balcony, rushing to dive into the space Rio had opened for her between her legs, beneath the blanket.

Rio chuckled as Agatha grumbled in the chill, curling herself beneath the blanket that Rio threw back over them.

“Here.” She passed her the mug so Agatha could warm her hands and soon placed her now free mug-warmed hand over Agatha’s stomach as she kept the blankets closed firm around them with her other.

“There was coffee on the side, you know.”

“I have yours now.”

Rio rolled her eyes but Agatha had leant back, had turned her head to kiss her cheek, and suddenly Rio had no problem sharing coffee.

“Did you sleep okay?”

Agatha made a soft noise from the base of her throat as she curled her legs up to get more beneath the blanket. Rio grinned, pressed her cold nose in behind Agatha’s ear and felt Agatha shiver as she muttered, “you know, I’m sure there are more blankets inside.”

“And deny you the chance to curl up with me? I wouldn’t do that to you.”

Rio huffed out a warm breath and Agatha hummed as Rio’s thumb moved slowly across her stomach.

Rio closed her eyes, the scent of the fresh coffee, the fresh air, Agatha’s perfume, it was ambrosia, and she was Tantalus. But she’d take her eternal punishment in exchange for just this, just this morning with Agatha.

There was nothing but the soft sound of birdsong nearby, the breeze in the trees, Agatha’s breathing, the soft movements of fabric when she began to sip the hot coffee. And Rio didn’t want it to ever stop being like this, just the two of them, just the wind and Agatha.

After another couple of minutes Agatha turned a little and offered the coffee up. Rio took it and was grateful she’d drank only half, and that she’d done so quickly, so it was still warm when Rio drank the rest.

“You should know,” Agatha said after a few more minutes of silence in that cool morning air. And her voice was soft, but carried in it something Rio knew she wasn’t going to like. “If ever I were to leave Ralph, my mother would bankroll him. He’d have her on side.”

So she’d been thinking about it. Thinking about leaving Ralph and how hard it might be. And though Rio felt sick about it, about Agatha’s own flesh and blood siding against her, she also felt a selfish sort of relief that Agatha was beginning to edge towards the idea of leaving her husband.

She sighed heavily, ducked her head down to rest her chin on Agatha’s shoulder and they both sat in it for a minute; Agatha in her fear, Rio in her fury.

“If it were ever to come to that, however hard it gets,” Rio kept her voice soft, conscious that the world around them was silent and they were they only ones disturbing the peace. “I’d be with you every step of the way.”

Agatha turned her head and Rio lifted her own up cautiously, watching as blue eyes turned soft and Agatha whispered: “I wouldn’t ask you to be.”

“I wouldn’t need asking.”

Agatha nodded just once and turned back away, taking the opportunity now to steal back Rio’s mug of coffee which was now cold. Rio sighed quietly, a happy noise, a contented one as she ducked her head back down and pressed a kiss to Agatha’s shoulder.

Silence wrapped around them again like the haar spreading its ghostlike fingers through the foothills beyond. Rio felt Agatha shiver against her and she tightened her hold on her, tugging the edges of the blanket they shared closer around them as Agatha pulled her legs up more towards herself.

“Why don’t you stay here and I’ll run you a bath?”

Agatha turned her head back into Rio again, curling her body around to lean against her more fully, her left shoulder now tucked below Rio’s right arm, her head against her shoulder.

“Just me?”

“I can join you if you’d like.”

“Stay here for a little.”

“It’s cold, baby.”

“Five minutes.”

Rio sighed, had no real fight in her about it, and simply brushed her hand up and down Agatha’s arm, knowing holding her like this was worth even frostbite.

Agatha began to toy with the fabric of her t-shirt, and it wasn’t long until she was lifting it, and making Rio gasp when her cold fingers found the warm skin of her side.

“You run hot.”

“And you are always cold.”

“Guess that means you need to warm me up.”

Rio laughed and pressed her face into Agatha’s hair, “That is that the bath was for.”

She felt Agatha’s hand move an inch or so up to her ribs.

“It’ll be a first.”

“A first what?”

“Shared bath.”

Rio raised her brows and placed a kiss to Agatha’s head. “Then I’ll make it a good one. Plenty of bubbles. Hot coffee. Some candles. We’ll use the bath with the better view.”

“Have you had many… baths?”

Rio smiled a little but had long since decided the only way to get Agatha to ask her what she really wanted to was to play dumb. “I prefer to shower but-…”

“Rio.”

“Sí, mi amor?”

“Have you?”

“Have I what?”

Agatha sighed quietly and pushed up, breaking Rio’s wall of warm around them. But this was better. Agatha was straddling her, and Agatha wasn’t wearing any pants.

“Have you had many shared baths?”

“Well,” Rio began with a growing smirk, “it depends what you define as-…”

Agatha rolled her eyes and Rio trailed off, her hands picking up the slack as they moved up Agatha’s goose-bumped thighs. “I’ve had a few, yes. But none I was more excited about than this one.”

Agatha began to chew on her lip and Rio only noticed as she sat up properly, as her gaze finally made it up to her face, having been enjoying the journey from pale thighs to the sight of Agatha in her shirt.

“I’m frozen, Agatha. Can we go now?”

Chapter 29: A Week: Saturday, Sunday, Monday

Chapter Summary

A visitor.

A punishment.

A panic.

Chapter Notes

Let’s all hold hands

See the end of the chapter for more notes

Saturday

The sun was high in the sky as Rio reclined on the bed overlooking the hills with the bay beyond.

Agatha was there because of course she was.

Her pale, attentive fingers were running gently through Rio’s hair and the world was good. Their day was just beginning. Her coffee-warmed hands rested now, absently tapping out a soft pattern across her stomach.

Birdsong nearby was all that disturbed them.

And then Agatha’s hand moved from her hair to her shoulder and the light touch became firmer, somehow insistent.

And Rio woke with a start.

“Rio. Honey.”

“Five minutes,” Rio mumbled, tugging the sheets up to her face, intent on blocking out the soft light of the morning, wanting to be back on the warm balcony where no one needed to be anywhere in particular.

“No, baby, wake up. I need to go.”

Rio frowned some more, took a second, allowed the sheets to be removed from her face.

When had we become I?

“Wait, wait, I’m sorry. I’ll get up. Give me five minutes. I’ll shower, and-…”

Rio’s eyes were open now as she’d moved to scramble up, assuming Agatha was wanting to get going and Rio was holding her back. But Agatha was frowning, was looking desolate, distraught, even. She was already dressed in Rio’s white knitted sweater.

Rio rubbed her eyes to make sure she wasn’t imagining it. To make sure Agatha wasn’t pulling some cruel trick. To make sure what she was seeing was real: her happy, calm, satiated lover was suddenly looking torn apart.

“Baby.”

Rio watched as Agatha crouched down by the edge of the bed, felt the gentleness of that hand that had taken her own, the fingers that curled around her ankle as she sat up properly and swung her legs over the edge.

“I have to go without you. Jen tried calling last night but my cell was dead. I-…”

“What’s wrong? Is Nicky okay?”

“He’s fine.” Agatha sighed and dropped her gaze and Rio pulled her hand up to kiss over her knuckles.

“Then give me five, and-…”

“Rio, my mother arrived late last night.”

“I-…”

“I can’t bring you with me because… it would just be too hard to have you there with her.”

Evanora

Rio swallowed thickly, closing her eyes. She felt Agatha lean up, felt her squeeze over her calf, “I wanted a day for us. I really did.”

Rio believed her. But she didn’t understand why they still couldn’t have one. Why Agatha would let her mother get between them.

“I’m still coming,” Rio said firmly, opening her eyes to look down at a frowning Agatha. “I’ll still spend time with you both. I want to see Nicky. I want to be with you.”

For a second it looked like Agatha might give in. Her blue eyes disappeared behind dark lashes and she pressed her face into Rio’s thigh, giving Rio the opportunity to do as Agatha had done to her in her dream.

Rio let Agatha take a second, heard her breathe in slowly and exhale as she lifted her head again and Rio’s fingers that had been buried in dark hair were pushed away.

And as soon as she saw her face she knew what she was about to say.

“No,” Agatha whispered, moving her hand to reach for Rio’s free one. “No, I’m going alone.”

“Mi amor, I can handle your mom, okay? I can-…”

“I’m telling you no, Rio. I can’t have you there with her. I won’t.”

“Agatha.”

“Please understand this. Please just wait here and I’ll be back later tonight, okay? And we can pick back up where we left off. Just the two of us.”

Rio shook her head and felt the sting of rejection in Agatha’s request. She’d thought they were moving forwards, that Agatha inviting her to her day with Nicky was a positive sign that she wanted her involved.

That maybe there was room for her in her life.

But she didn’t want her to meet Evanora. She didn’t want her to meet the woman who’d birthed her but had not raised her. Her mother, not her mom.

“I want to come with you,” was all she could get out, all she could respond with as Agatha dropped her hold on her hands and reached to pull her down into a soft kiss, like the ones they gave each other when they were leaving for only minutes - only this time it would be a whole day.

“I know, baby. I know.”

Agatha smiled sadly and Rio watched as she pulled away, stood up, and left.

A great, unbearable ache blossomed in her chest now, its creeping tendrils constricted her lungs. It took root in her chest where it would insidiously suckle at her heart for the rest of the day, spreading its poison into her bloodstream, promising the fears that had dissolved with Agatha’s tenderness would come back again.

And Rio tried to breath in slowly, tried to calm it as she heard the front door open and close.

But Agatha was gone. Their day together wasn’t happening. She’d have to wait.

She waited by cleaning, by making their home spotless again. She tidied away the candles she’d laid out yesterday.

She organised the throws and blankets she’d gathered.

She took out the empty glass bottles that had been piling up through the week.

And then, after she’d showered and changed, she found her script and curled up to read through it.

She didn’t get very far. She read and she had to reread. So much so that after an hour of trying she only managed three pages. Reading about a happy family, instead of being with one, wasn’t the best cure for her ills.

Her mind was on that family. On Agatha and Nicky.

Her thoughts were constantly with Agatha, on the pained expression that had been on her face, on the fact that Evanora had forced them apart when she’d not even stepped into the room.

But another hour of failed script reading later and her phone lit up with a text from Agatha.

10:37am
Agatha Harkness: I’m home safe.

10:38am
Rio Vidal: Let me know if you need anything. Tell Nicky I said hey

Rio stared at the WhatsApp interface, watching it in the hopes that Agatha would read her message and respond immediately.

But the ticks went blue and she heard nothing back.

Rio worried all day. She even debated messaging Jen to see if Agatha were okay but she didn’t want Agatha to think she were interfering.

So she sat. She drove herself crazy. She tried to eat something, but stress prevented her from even that.

She did some yoga but even in downward dog her thoughts wouldn’t right themselves.

She showered again.

She eventually got so hungry she ate ice cream directly from the tub. And an apple - to try and get some vitamins.

And then, at around 9pm, her phone rang.

“Agatha? Are you okay? Are you on your way back?”

“No, Rio.” Agatha’s voice was barely a whisper, and Rio’s heart sank. “I have to stay.”

Rio nodded into the phone, feeling the roots that had buried in her chest flare with their earlier promise: this was it, this was all she’d ever get with Agatha. Four days of bliss before reality stole her back.

She bit her lip. She took a second.

“What’s happened? Is she-…?”

“She’s gone. She caught the five o’clock flight home. But…” there was a noise at the end of the line and Rio strained to hear more, to try and figure out what it was.

Then she heard the soft sounds of a door being closed.

“Agatha?”

Silence.

Soft breaths.

Another door.

The sound of fabric against wood.

A sharp intake of breath.

“She cut his hair.”

Rio stopped breathing. Agatha began to cry.

The soft sounds of her tears and ragged breathing made Rio freeze, made her heart constrict and stop in her chest.

She took a second, closed her eyes. The little boy with the big brown eyes and the goofy grin. His long hair that constantly fell in his eyes. The hair that Agatha was always brushing back for him. The hair that he touched when he was nervous just like Rio did.

“Nicky.” Rio said his name plainly, reverently, unable to think of anything else she could say.

“She took him,” Agatha gasped out, clearly trying to get a handle on her reaction. “Jen didn’t know what to do. She… she took him to the nearest salon and had them…”

But she didn’t finish her sentence.

And Rio was no longer frozen. Rio was no longer locked on the image of Nicky. On the boy who had her name and her face.

She’d moved on to Agatha.

“I’m coming.”

“Rio. No.”

“Too late. Absolutely not. There’s no way.” Rio was rambling now, scrambling about the place to find her keys. The fury of a thousand suns burning her up. Burning her fear. Burning through her inability to tell Agatha no that morning; her desire to fix, to hold, to protect flaring in her chest. “That bitch. That witch. I’m coming.”

And she heard Agatha gulp in some air, her breathing now ragged, now urgent, now transforming into broken, shaking sobs.

Rio was blinded by her tears as searched in vein for her keys. She couldn’t think. Couldn’t breathe. And then…

“Rio,” Agatha gasped out, a small squeak of a noise following her desperate plea. “I-… I need you.”

This made Rio stop. It made her clutch at her chest. It made the jagged branches of fear that had sprouted in her and now bore fruit perish - purged from her by Agatha’s entreaty.

“I’m coming,” Rio repeated, breathless as she rushed to find her keys. “Stay on the line. I’ll be there. I’ll-…”

She sourced them, discarded on a shelf by the door.

In her sweats and a worn-in black hoodie, one of those indestructible ones bought for $20 that lasted a lifetime, she left the house she’d called home for the week and threw herself into her car.

She cursed loudly as she tried to get the key in the ignition but her hands were shaking so violently it took three attempts.

“Rio.” Rio didn’t respond to her name, didn’t have the mental capacity to be able to think. Because all she could focus on was getting to Agatha, was soothing Agatha, was-…

“Por favor… por favor, ten mucho cuidado.” Please, please be careful.

Rio shook her head, grunting a little as the car kicked into life. It made a noise that Rio knew meant her little hybrid was doing the work of connecting to her phone to host Agatha’s voice instead.

She dropped her phone from where it had been sandwiched between her ear and her shoulder and it landed apathetically in her lap.

She barely glanced at the dash as she drove off, not bothering to put in Agatha’s address, and only focused on getting out, going down hill until she hit the interstate, and putting her foot on the gas the whole way.

Agatha didn’t say anything but Rio could still hear her catching her breath, calming herself as some whimpers escaped her in what she assumed to be her bedroom. Rio was biting down on her tongue so hard she thought she might rip it out and then…

“Necesito… cariño, necesito oír tu voz.” I need… baby, I need to hear your voice.

Rio shook her head again, swallowing the bile that had been swirling in her throat as she gripped the wheel.

It took a second. It took three more gasping breaths from Agatha. And then she whispered: “No es tu culpa.” It’s not your fault.

Agatha realised a soft cry and Rio was temporarily blinded by her own tears that she quickly wiped away, trying her hardest to look ahead, to not die before she could get to Agatha.

“Mi vida. No es tu culpa.” It’s not your fault.

Agatha whimpered quietly and Rio heard her sniff. She wasn’t holding back anymore and Rio had to wipe at her eyes again.

“Ya voy. Ya voy. Te amo. Ya voy.” I’m coming. I’m coming. I love you. I’m coming.

The soundtrack of Agatha’s tears spurred her on to push the car harder, make it go faster. It whined and groaned as Rio pushed it but she didn’t care. She had to trust it would carry her to Agatha. Rio knew she was being reckless, she knew if the roads weren’t as quiet as they were she’d be putting herself in a lot of danger but she couldn’t bring herself to care.

Because how could she not be speeding? How could she not be breaking every law to get to Agatha as quickly as she could?

Minutes past and Agatha’s breathing began to even out. She sniffed more frequently, clearly now trying to get a hold on herself. And Rio only stared ahead, only kept her foot down, only came up with ways in which she could kill Agatha’s mother.
“¿Por qué no llamaste antes?” Why didn’t you call earlier?

She didn’t mean for it to come out as harshly as it did.

Agatha breathed out, long and slow and loud and Rio could only imagine how close she was pinning the phone to her ear, how cold she would be curled up all by herself.

“Sabía que vendrías. Pero no estaba preparada. Tenía que concentrarme en Nicky y contigo ahí... perdería el control.” I knew you'd come. But I wasn't ready. I had to focus on Nicky and with you there... I'd lose it.

Rio felt her head nod, just once, as if her body was reserving its energy for something else. Something like holding Agatha so tight she’d walk around for the rest of her life knowing Rio was always somewhere waiting to hold her again.

“How…” Rio began, in English this time, her mind a jumble of questions and fears. “Is he okay?”

“I…,” Agatha followed her into another language, “He…” Agatha’s voice raised up an octave and Rio glanced at the screen. “Jen said he was crying in the chair. That she held his hand and he just cried.”

Rio nodded, her jaw set, her hands choking the wheel.

“Why did she do it?”

Agatha was silent, except for the slow breath she exhaled. “Punishment.”

“For Nicky?”

“For me.”

“Mi amor-…”

“Please,” Agatha said, a little firmer this time, “please concentrate on your driving. I don’t-…”

“I’ll be fine,” Rio said in as soft a voice as she could manage. “Go back to Nicky.”

“Will you stay on the line?”

Rio’s muscles went slack, and she sank two inches where she’d been sitting ramrod straight, the weight of Agatha’s request forcing her to bear the unbearable.

“Yes.”

She heard Agatha move then, heard a door open, soft footsteps, then another door, and the sounds of Agatha climbing back into the bed.

Rio glanced at the screen but didn’t say anything and only wished she’d been more insistent that morning. Only wished Agatha had let her. Only wished she could be on the bed with her, holding her together, telling her over and over again that this wasn’t her fault, that only her mother was to blame.

But she was with Nicky now.

And Rio was on her way to them.

Agatha was curled with Nicky and Rio was five hours away driving to their side.

Rio kept her foot down, her ears straining to see if she could hear anything from either Agatha or Nicky.

But within an hour she could just about make out Agatha’s soft breathing and she knew she’d fallen asleep.

She relaxed a little, safe in the knowledge that Agatha was safe, no longer cognisant of what had happened. Of what had been done to her son.

Of whatever reason she had for thinking Evanora had done it to punish her.

In the space between getting to Agatha and being with Agatha, Rio was able to run it all through in her mind. The late night arrival of Evanora. Was that common? Did she just show up? The decision to take her grandson to have his hair chopped off. The image of her standing over his shoulder whilst Jen - as hardline and unfeeling as she could sometimes appear - held his hand as he cried.

And then there was Agatha, who’d prioritised her son that day. Who was even now protecting him as he slept. Who had initially refused Rio when she offered to come. Who’d refused her again that evening. Who had, on the third time that Rio had said she would come, changed her mind and asked her to instead.

The tree of fear that had died inside her now became little seedlings of hope. Germinating in the rich soils of Agatha’s request for her to come, with her desire to have Rio on the open line for her even as she slept.

And the little hybrid that could charged to its destination, its driver barely concentrating on the roads, thinking instead of the woman she should never have let go alone into the claws of her mother.

She arrived outside Agatha’s gate shortly after one in the morning. She assumed she’d have speeding tickets waiting for her in a week or so but she’d pay any fine necessary under the circumstances. She disconnected her phone from the car. She clutched it tightly in her hand after parking up.

She walked the few hundred yards to the front of Agatha’s house.

She hesitated, unsure how to buzz without breaking the spell of the peaceful, sleeping house.

But someone knew she was there without her even ringing to be let in.

The gate opened for her, and Rio pushed it until she was inside and could see a figure in the doorway.

Jen.

“I didn’t… I didn’t know what to do.”

Rio hung up from Agatha and moved quickly, and before she could understand what she was doing, she’d thrown her arms around Jennifer Kale and let her cry silently into her shoulder.

It took a while for Jen to speak but when she did it was soft, and she was hiccuping slightly.

“He was so upset.” She sniffed and shook her head against her. “But Evanora… she wouldn’t take no for an answer. She’s his grandmother and Agatha… Agatha was driving… I didn’t want to panic her or scare her or…”

“It’s okay,” Rio breathed, staring blindly into the dark house ahead of her. “Nicky knows you wouldn’t-…”

“I wouldn’t. I know I… I love that kid.”

Rio nodded and she pulled away slowly, frowning up into Jen’s tortured expression.

“I shouldn’t have let her come alone.”

“She wouldn’t let me call you. She knew you’d come if you knew. She hasn’t cried or shouted or-…”

Rio sighed and closed her eyes and then something happened that she wasn’t expecting. Jen placed her hands softly against her cheeks. She held her head in place and Rio looked back at her, allowing herself to relax into it.

“I’m glad you came. Go and be with them. They’re in Agatha’s room.”

Rio smiled as Jen dropped her hold on her and she stepped around her into the warm house only to hesitate and turn back.

“Have you not slept?”

“I thought at some point I’d have to open the gate for you so…”

Rio moved back in, took Jen’s arm, kissed her cheek, “Go to sleep.”

She felt sorry for Jen, she really did. She appeared genuinely contrite, genuinely distraught. But she was also furious with her. Fuelled by the knowledge that under no circumstances, if Nicky had been left in her care, would Evanora have been able to lay a hand on him, or touch a hair on his head.

But then as she stared up into Jen’s eyes she registered something that Jen hadn’t said but that was abundantly clear. She was a black woman with no real claim on Nicky other than his mother’s word. And Evanora was a white bitch with bigotry in her heart and hatred in her veins.

There was nothing Jen could have done not without Evanora doing something heinous in return.
