It made her own body tense, made her own fright fizzle to nothing, taken over by the strain of Agatha’s furious fears.

She moved closer again and wrapped her arms around Agatha, wanting her to know she was there, that she could rely on her. At least for now.

At least until anything came out about her past, about her wild child ways. For now she could support her. She had to focus on that.

“Mi vida,” she tried quietly, watching as Agatha twitched in response but didn’t turn around. But her hand was across Rio’s arm and it felt soft and hesitant as it lay there. “My past it’s…”

“It’s not about your past, it’s about what Jen is trying to do-…”

“She’s a megabitch with a huge jealous streak.” Jen had clearly decided to speak up now, making sure Agatha could hear at least this portion of her conversation with Alice.

Agatha’s hold on her arm tightened but Rio didn’t let it change the way she held Agatha. She was firm, yes. But not unyielding, not unnecessarily trapping her. Agatha had freedom of movement and she hoped that with the knowledge of that she wouldn’t feel the need to pull away again.

“There’s no need for you to have any kind of profile on Rio. You don’t need to know anything other than she is my girlfriend. That’s it.”

“It’s the girlfriend part that’s the problem, Agatha! This is a woman who doesn’t date! Who fucks around and-…!”

“Jen.” Alice.

Rio’s cheeks were flaming red again, and she slid her arms from around Agatha to turn around and collapse back in the armchair, her head in her hands.

Perhaps Rio had ruined this before it had even begun.

“She is my girlfriend. My son loves her and she is more a parent to him, has been more a parent to him in the last few months than Ralph ever has!”

Rio said nothing. Could think of nothing other than how her presence in Nicky’s life might mean Agatha would have to share her son with her deadbeat husband. No parent would allow that. No good, loving person would allow that to happen.

“And I am doing my best to make sure nothing fucks this up, Agatha. You know how these things can be twisted. You know how-…!”

“Jen. Jen.” Alice was intervening again. She could hear her urgent whispering to Jennifer on the other side of the room.

Rio forced herself to breathe. Forced herself to focus on what she could do: she could step back, she would wait. She could give Agatha time.

In her sprila, a soft brush against her hair told her that Agatha was closer again. She looked up as Agatha’s fingers skimmed down to caress her cheek and Rio blinked up at the woman who’d softened suddenly, looking suddenly like her Agatha again. Hers and Nicky’s.

Their soft, gentle Agatha.

She watched as she took a breath, as her lips parted and her pale cheeks tinged a little pink.

“¿Etás bien, mi amor?”

Agatha knew she was spiralling, perhaps even knew the decision that was swirling around in her brain, begging to be made.

Give her time. Step back. Protect Nicky by giving her time.

Her spiral spun its last as Agatha continued to gaze at her, as her eyes held her in place so Rio could lift her head from the depths of her clouded mind. Rio smiled once she surfaced because how could she not. She leant into Agatha’s touch as her fingers slipped down and she held her chin, her thumb just touching her lower lip.

“Sí, mi vida. Estoy bien.”

“I’m trying to help,” Jen’s voice filtered into Rio’s consciousness, her gaze still on Agatha as blue eyes moved over her face, taking all of her in, trying to see the lie in Rio’s whisper. She was trying to fix the spiral she didn’t know she’d already halted.

“She’s right,” Rio said softly. Rio knew she was. Agatha had to know too. It couldn’t be denied that anything anyone dragged up during the divorce, during the custody hearing, could cause a problem for Agatha. Rio could cause problems for Agatha.

Agatha’s brow twitched into a light frown and she dropped her gaze to Rio’s lips, raising her thumb tenderly to press into the cushion of her lower one. She didn’t say anything and Rio took her hand away and kissed the fingers that curled around her own.

She had to think clearly now, had to break the habit that had formed over the weeks of sinking instead of even trying to swim.

“Knowledge is power and if we have all the information and know what they could uncover or try to hit us with then-…”

“I don’t want to talk about it anymore,” Agatha said more firmly than when she’d been checking in on Rio. “You have it. You’ve done the research. You know now. I don’t need to hear it.”

Agatha’s gaze had fallen from Rio and she was pulling away to stand again, raising herself to her full height to look at Jennifer now leaning against the desk with Alice holding her hand in two of her own.

“We’ll be good. Until everything’s settled and I have full custody. You won’t need the information. And I don’t want it brought up again.”

Rio took Agatha’s hand, shuffling forwards in the chair to be able to reach it and Agatha didn’t turn but she squeezed her hand when she held it.

“It’s not enough to do the beforehand Agatha. After you’re out, after you announce your relationship it’ll all-…”

“Jen.”

Rio stood then, not because she thought Agatha would snap but because this was her part to play.

“Let them release it all when this is over. Let them interview everyone I’ve ever dated. I’m not ashamed of any of it. And once Agatha has custody they can’t take him away just because her girlfriend has a past.”

Her voice had faltered over her last sentence, suddenly unsure of herself.

Agatha squeezed her hand and Jen nodded just once.

“It won’t be easy,” Alice warned, the first thing she’d said in a while. Her face was tight, her brow pulled together, her cheeks a little pink. She was scared of Agatha, Rio knew that. But Agatha didn’t bite and Rio never would.

“I know.”

Agatha tugged her hand and Rio looked to her and realised she didn’t want her attention, she was just reminding herself she was there.

“I’ve only ever wanted this to work. As soon as I knew. As soon as-…” Jen.

Agatha stiffened beside her, and Rio looked back at her once more, seeing her jaw flex. But her eyes, previously alert again and focused only on Jen were now hidden from her as she stared at the floor. Rio moved her free hand to Agatha’s arm and squeezed her.

“I’m trying to protect you.”

Jen’s face was open again, her eyes wide even as she pursed her lips. Rio wondered if she’d ever said anything similar to Agatha before outside of the context of the usual manager/client relationship. Because she didn’t mean professionally. Rio knew that, Alice knew it, and Agatha did too.

It was why she was looking away, why she was hiding.

The air in the room was still until Agatha breathed life into it again with her next words: “I know you’re trying your best. I know I haven’t made it easy. But whether it destroys my career or not,” she took a breath and revealed herself again.

Agatha looked up to Jen and to Rio’s surprise she looked calmer, as if she’d been wrestling with a decision this whole time and she was finally experiencing the peace of making a choice.

“I choose Rio over my career.”

“Agatha.”

Agatha didn’t turn to Rio, didn’t even look around as she moved her hand to her cheek to try and make her turn. “Mi amor, No llegará a eso.” It won’t come to that.

Rio’s hand was still against Agatha’s cheek, warm and insistent. But Agatha was looking around her, not acquiescing. She had eyes only for her friend. “Which means you can’t just pull shit like this. Everything related to the divorce, to Rio, it goes through me. Through us.”

Rio’s gaze softened, her heart choking on its need to beat faster in her chest. She felt the flutter of it, the very moment it forgot itself and tried to canter where it had barely been jogging.

Her fingers slipped until they were lining Agatha’s jaw and only then did Agatha turn to her. Only then did she look away from Jen. And Rio frowned at the sight. Agatha looked lost, suddenly unsure of what she was doing and where she was.

So Rio nodded, because it felt like Agatha was looking for permission to be exactly where she found herself. A glimmer of relief flashed across Agatha’s face and then she turned again and Rio slipped back to kiss her shoulder, to go back to being steady by her side.

“You’re so fucking gay.”

Jen again. Though with a vague, bemused smile on her face.

“How no one’s ever seen it, I don’t know. Which is the fucking worry.”

Rio scoffed and received a scowl from Agatha and soon found that she was pulling away and marching over to Jen. “I’ll accept your apology, Jennifer. When you’re ready to give it. Preferably now.”

Jen was the one to scoff now and Rio sighed as she went to settle back in the armchair, watching the two friends with interest. The tension was gone now and the two were back to bickering rather than raging so she felt comfortable leaving them to it.

Her spiral was paused for now, but it was dormant, just waiting to continue spinning again if Rio lost control of it.

Alice slipped away, still skittish around Agatha. She settled on the arm of Rio’s chair and muttered from the corner of her mouth as across the room Jen was protesting.

“Girlfriends?”

“Mmhm.”

“Feeling better?”

“Getting there.”

“Are you ready for what’s to come?”

“We will be.”

Alice nodded and both looked across at their girlfriends, raising their brows in tandem as both Agatha and Jen formed fists at their sides.

“Should we break them up?” Rio asked as Agatha now threw her hands up and stormed around the desk to sit at her chair, soon finding a pen to tap as Jen was spouting words like: “longevity”, “working relationships”, “box office draw”.

“When she’s riled up I usually have a better change of getting laid.”

This made Rio bark a laugh and she looked up to her grinning friend. “I’m so glad this little evening has all basically been foreplay for the two of you.”

Alice shrugged and turned her attention back to the other two. “She seems determined.”

“Jen?”

“Agatha. On the relationship.”

Rio stiffened slightly, wondering what trust level Alice was currently at with Agatha but knowing it was definitely somewhere still in the fiftieth percentile.

“You still don’t trust her?”

Alice’s mouth opened and then closed again but before she could say anything Rio heard her name being called and she turned to see both Agatha and Jen looking at her expectantly. She raised her brows and Agatha repeated: “Can you please tell my manager what we’ve agreed?”

Rio’s mind ran through the possible answers: I can’t rail Agatha until I start taking care of myself, my cowboy shirt is now our cowboy shirt, purple skittles are now Rio’s to eat so Agatha doesn’t have to, they are two of three ducklings, Rio can’t move in.

The last. It had to be the last.

“I’m staying here until Saturday but I’m not moving in.”

“Moving in?” Alice.

“I really don’t think-…” Jen.

“We agreed, Jen. Drop it to TMZ on Saturday evening. He’s being served at four. They’ll have it by five past. Rio will be with Nicky and me in the new place. We’ll be hidden away. No one knows where-…” Agatha, agitated.

“My name on the deed doesn’t mean you’re totally hidden, Agatha.” Jen, again. Angrier.

“It’s in the hills. It’s secluded.” Agatha, even angrier.

“Do you know how fucking famous you are?! It’s bad enough you’re a dyke and now you’re moving one in!”

Agatha was on her feet before Rio was. She’d slammed her hands onto the desk and the slap of it reverberated around the room, settling in Rio’s chest and causing her heart rate to kick up again.

“Call me that again and I’ll fire your sorry ass before you have a chance to say ‘oh Agatha, what will people say when they see me on Alice’s arm?! Surely I can do better?!’”

Time with Agatha often felt slower. Felt different to time without her.

And time now felt slower too. Time felt heavy.

Rio watched in slow motion as Jennifer Kale launched herself at Agatha Harkness.

Agatha had thrown herself back and Rio was on her in a second. Just as Alice was on Jen.

“You fucking lying bitch! I never said that! I never said that!”

Agatha wasn’t fighting as Rio held her wrists down and pressed her against the shelves behind her desk, but she wasn’t backing down either.

“You said it, Jen. You told me-…”

Agatha grunted when Rio shoved her backwards in an attempt to get her to shut up.

“You bitch. You liar. You fucking-…”

“ENOUGH!”

Alice. Little, intimidated, terrified Alice. Agatha was shocked into straightening again where she’d already begun to lean around Rio once more. Rio still wasn’t budging but she turned her head to look at her friend.

Alice’s cheeks were being held by a panicking Jen and Rio could see the hurt in her eyes, the shock too, that she’d even raised her voice in front of Agatha. But she turned back because as Jen tried to make frantic amends, Agatha was the only person she wanted to turn to.

“Why did you say it?”

Agatha flinched at her tone, and looked at Rio properly for the first time since she’d thrown Jen’s words back at her.

“Agatha.”

Agatha looked like she might deny she’d even said anything. She looked like she might deny even having been in the room when such things were said. But maybe it was Rio’s refusal to look away. Maybe it was her tightening hold on her wrists, the way she pressed her body against Agatha’s to keep her where she was.

Only something told her Agatha wouldn’t try to push her away.

A flex in her jaw told her that Agatha was struggling with what to say, with how to manage this. But Rio wouldn’t look or move away. She made her deal, made her struggle, until eventually she said: “I’m sorry.”

Rio pressed in briefly before she released her wrists and let go. Agatha’s eyes clouded over and she stepped into Rio, her hands clutching now at her sweatshirt, “I’m sorry.”

Rio shook her head but had no time to respond because Jen had spoken before she could form the words.

“Tell her, Agatha. Tell her you’re a liar. Tell her.”

Agatha wasn’t looking at Jen; even as she slammed her hand on the desk. Her eyes were still on Rio, seeking her absolution before she even deigned to look at her angry friend. But Rio couldn’t give what she was looking for because it wasn’t hers to give.

She shook her head again, barely an inch either way.

“Agatha,” Jen insisted.

“Jen,” Alice tried to calm her.

“Mi vida,” Rio breathed, her fingers grazing the cheek where a tear now traced its miserable path. Agatha took the cue, like any professional might, and with her hands still twisted in Rio’s sweatshirt she turned to her friend and swallowed.

“Months ago,” Rio realised as she spoke how afraid she was. Her voice was hoarse and soft and Rio brushed another tear from her cheek, “Jen came to me and said she was nervous about, about being seen with you.”

Agatha dropped her gaze and Rio laid her hand gently on her chest, a silent request for her to breathe.

“She was nervous about…”

Rio pressed her palm a little harder against her chest. Breathe, Agatha.

“About what people might say, because of your jobs. The… other bit… she never said that.”

“Agatha.” Rio couldn’t keep the disappointment out of her voice and Agatha caught it as her eyes moved back to her. She looked devastated and her face began to crumple before her very eyes.

Rio gathered her in, and felt the first sob against her neck. The hands that had been clutching the front of her sweater were now against her back. Agatha was clinging to her like she was about to disappear.

If Jen and Alice said anything during that time, Rio didn’t hear it.

She wasn’t sure if it was the stress of the past few weeks or something else that had set Agatha off. But she’d raged and then she’d disintegrated before her eyes.

Shame, fury, fear. They were sobbed out against Rio’s willing skin as Agatha continued to clutch at her, not content until she could claw her way in.

Rio just held on, eventually pressing Agatha back into the shelves so she could feel contained, trapped between the hard wood and Rio’s consenting body. Agatha began to calm soon after, and as her breathing evened, her clawing hands disappeared beneath Rio’s sweatshirt to get to her skin. She clutched her still, her nails scraping and fingers desperate. And Rio held her through it all, ducking her head down to encourage Agatha to look at her, to press her hot, sticky face into her own.

To become one of sorrow.

“Rio,” Alice’s voice broke through as Agatha gasped against Rio’s parted lips, nuzzling her broken features as close as she could get.

“Rio.”

Rio moved her arms from around Agatha and placed her hands on her cheeks, keeping her head in place as she kissed her.

“Rio.”

Rio turned her head to an angle that would show she was listening but that meant she didn’t need to turn too far from Agatha.

“You need to rethink staying here. Both of you do.”

Rio turned her head back, frowning now as Agatha’s hands began to move across her back, seeking a place to rest. She felt Agatha’s response before she heard it, “No.”

But she said it only for her. Jen and Alice may as well not have been in the room. But Rio knew they were, so she pulled back, and was gentle as she pried Agatha off of her and managed to turn to the two other women in the room.

Jen looked as though she, too, had been crying. And Alice didn’t look far off. Perhaps Rio had simply cried too much recently for her body to allow it. But she felt the swell of tears that starts in the throat when Agatha said her name from behind her and tried to turn her back around.

“We’ll do as we’ve agreed until Saturday. I’ll take Nicky during the day, and bring him to the new house before the press start their hunt. After that, we’ll be careful,” Agatha said her name again, but Rio ignored it, “We’ll be so good and so discreet that even you two won’t notice.”

She heard Agatha suck in a breath and exhale it shakily as her hands crossed across her bare stomach beneath her sweatshirt. It made her fall back into her, made her falter for a second before she made a promise she didn’t know if she could keep: “We’ll let you manage when we can see each other.”

It was an overcorrection, a response to the fear that still lingered that she could be the cause of Agatha losing Nicky. Because even sharing him with Ralph was inconceivable. And it being Rio’s fault would be something she simply couldn’t live with.

“No,” Rio was tugged backwards this time and heard the thud as Agatha fell into the shelves, “No. No. No. We’re not. I’m not.”

“I think that is the best way to do this,” Alice agreed, her eyes on Rio, who felt the weight of guilt in her stomach as Agatha pressed her fingers there.

“No. I’m not agreeing. No. I-…”

“Agatha.” Jen. “You know it’s for the best. For a while, at least. Until we can get a gage on public interest. On press levels, on-…”

“I will not be told when and where I can see my girlfriend. Only by Rio. Only by Rio.”

Rio lost her breath then because Agatha had moved her hands. One now had reached to curl around her shoulder and the other was holding her opposite hip. She held her securely against her, as if frightened that this time she wouldn’t disappear, but instead be taken.

In front of them Jen and Alice looked defeated, and Rio felt sorry for them both. She really did.

“We’ll do it,” she said, before Jen could utter the words she had looked like she was about to shout. Over her sweatshirt she lay her hands on Agatha’s, letting her know she wasn’t going anywhere. “Because doing it is extra protection for Agatha and for Nicky. And neither of us want anything we do to upset him. He-…” Rio swallowed and felt Agatha tug impossibly at her, “We will do it because we love him.”

Agatha’s hold changed and Rio knew she was relenting but she wouldn’t say anything to Jen or Alice. Her hand on her shoulder moved to her ribs instead. It rested over her heart and Rio just knew she wanted to feel the beat of it, she wanted a metronome for her own.

Agatha pressed her face into her shoulder and silence descended again.

“When you’re feeling ready to apologise, I’ll be waiting for your call.” Jen. Looking less than the anger her words implied.

Alice had taken her hand and was pulling her towards the door and just as they reached it Rio felt Agatha lift her head up, felt her squeeze over her ribs as she said: “I’m sorry. Alice. Jen. I… thank you. For trying to help.”

Jen pursed her lips but inclined her head and though Rio didn’t think she’d say anything at all she eventually spoke up: “What I said earlier, everything about… about Rio. You’re right about her. It’s why we’re trying so hard. It’s why I’m being hard on you both. We need to be so careful. Now more than ever.”

Rio swallowed as Agatha’s hold lessened.

Jen was looking at her now. Agatha must have spotted it too because she was shifting behind her, uncomfortable with her friend’s eyes on the woman she’d been clinging to.

“Agatha’s right. You’re already a better parent to that boy than Ralph ever was.”

Rio choked on nothing and Agatha brought her hand out from its hidden resting place to wrap around her neck. Her touch was healing.

She could breathe again.

“Try to get some sleep. You both look like shit.”

Alice smiled weakly and Jen offered no other softness and then they were gone.

The clock on the desk told Rio it was creeping closer to morning and they had to be up in just a few, miserable hours. But she couldn’t think of her tiredness. She could only thing of Agatha who had now moved her hand to hold her head, making her turn around and fighting to keep her as close to her body as possible.

Agatha was pale, and looked beyond exhaustion. Her blue eyes were downturned, her heavy lids covering them from Rio’s view. Her voice was soft again, feeble.

“I want you to live with us.”

“I want that too.”

“It’s all my fault. Everything is-…”

“Mi vida, all anyone wants is for you and Nicky to be happy and safe and together. That’s all that matters.”

“You matter too.”

“I cannot be the reason he gets taken away. Even sharing him, I-…”

“I knew you were thinking that. I knew you were thinking that.”

Rio sighed heavily and dropped her head to Agatha’s shoulder, feeling her instantly cradle her close, instantly become the holder of the two of them. The were silent for a while, Rio wading through the waters of her misery and Agatha holding her steady as she passed through them.

Rio didn’t know who decided it was time they went up to bed. They just did.

Agatha only left Rio to go check on Nicky and returned to her when she’d seen him sleeping soundly in his bed, thankfully the opposite end of the house to the office.

Rio was already tucked under the sheets, wearing her underwear and a t-shirt she’d found under the pillow. Agatha joined but didn’t bother with the t-shirt and settled down beside Rio, curling as close as possible.

They hadn’t spoken, had barely looked at each other since they’d left the office. But Rio couldn’t find the words anymore and Agatha clearly couldn’t either. They’d have to talk another time.

Rio began to brush her fingers up and down Agatha’s side where she lay facing the same way as Rio, hoping to lull her to sleep first with her soft touch.

But Agatha found words soon enough.

“Those other women…,” Agatha’s voice was quiet in the still room, barely above a whisper. “Did any of them have kids?”

Rio traced her nose along the soft skin of the back of Agatha’s neck, taking a second to try and understand the reasoning behind the question. “Some.”

Agatha nodded, her hold on Rio’s hand tightening, “Did you meet them? Did you ever-…?”

“Agatha? I never met anyone’s kids. It was mostly just sex. I wasn’t interested in anything more with any of them.”

In the slowness of Agatha’s response, in the tightness of her hold on her, Rio knew she was worried that Rio had a pattern. That Jen wasn’t right, but was close to being so. Perhaps Rio liked the chase, enjoyed the comfort for a while before she had to bolt and seek something exciting again.

With her mouth she reassured, she pressed deliberate, open kisses along to column of Agatha’s neck. With her body she cradled, she pressed in closer, holding her more tightly. With her words she calmed, breathing them into Agatha’s ear, “I’ve never found someone I wanted to settle down with. I didn’t even know I was looking until I found you. You’re the only person I want to be with.”

Agatha pressed back, attempting to turn, so Rio shifted up so she had room. When they locked eyes Rio knew she’d been correct. Agatha was still nervous, still unsure about Rio’s true feelings.

Her heart sunk in her chest.

“Life with me and Nicky, when all this is finally over, it’ll be schedules and parent teacher conferences. Making dinner and doctor’s appointments. It’s all boring, all the same, all-…”

“Exactly what I want.”

Rio moved again, no longer satisfied leaning over Agatha. She wanted to be all over her, to wrap herself around her, to let her feel her need to be with her. She slid her hand down her side and held her still as she hovered her body weight above her, sinking down to press against her without fully letting go.

“Does it feel real to you?”

Agatha asked quietly, having taken a second to respond as Rio was nuzzling against her, her hand slipping below her shirt to feel her warm side.

“Does what feel real?”

“This? Us?”

“Yes.”

Rio kissed Agatha, partly because she wanted to and partly to see how in her head she was. She kissed back, and her hands flew up her waist.

“Imagine seeing the most beautiful woman you’ve ever seen on a screen in your tiny neighbourhood move theatre and then years later she’s lying beneath you as your girlfriend.”

Rio kissed her again, and Agatha kissed back again.

“No, it doesn’t feel real. But it also feels like the most real thing that’s ever happened to me. You are more real than anything or anyone I’ve ever met. And you are all I want.”

Agatha smiled and Rio felt her heart stammer in her chest as if it had been about to say something but had thought better of it. Only she took over for it, and said the thing she’d been worried about all evening: “Would this be easier if we weren’t together? If we waited?”

Agatha’s smile disappeared and Rio knew what her answer would be before she gave it.

“No. None of this. None of it would be easy without you.”

“I’m thinking of-…”

“I know what you’re thinking of but I am telling you, and I need you to believe me, that nothing would be easier without you.”

Rio dropped her gaze, finding it hard to believe Agatha’s words when she still felt so ineffectual. And after this evening, she felt like a burden.

Agatha’s hands were tracing the lines of her back now, retracing the journey they’d made earlier when they’d been desperate instead of delicate. Each muscle in her body began to relax until she collapsed fully above Agatha and turned her head on the pillow to nuzzle in against her.

“I can’t do this without you.”

Rio nodded but didn’t say anything. Agatha’s hands continued to move against her.

“Say it.”

“You can’t do this without me.”

“I love you. I will not allow the press, or Ralph, or my mother, to take you away from me.”

Rio nodded again and Agatha’s hands stilled against her. Her fingers splayed over her ribs and Rio focused on the warmth of them, the way Agatha held her steadily there as if supporting her body to continue breathing.

She felt like death was much farther away when Agatha was this close.

She wondered if Agatha knew her touch helped.

She wondered if she knew she was keeping her alive.

“I love you,” she whispered, a strange calmness to her voice. “Everything is easier with you too.”

Rio moved to lean up again, putting an arm’s length of distance between them as she rested her hands either side of Agatha’s face. Agatha’s hands moved once more, her nails dragging down the line to her hips, encouraging goosebumps in their wake.

Agatha’s face was more relaxed now. And Rio knew Agatha liked access to her so she rolled off but took Agatha’s hand to kiss it like a romantic hero might.

Agatha was silent, allowing Rio to keep her knuckles pressed to her lips for as long as she wanted. But knuckles turned to a palm and then a wrist and Rio whispered as Agatha made a soft noise of contentment.

“Goodnight, mi vida.”

She leant in to kiss Agatha then, lingering for twice as long as before. The hand she’d been holding was now buried in her hair and Rio gasped quietly as Agatha captured her lower lip. She wanted to deepen the kiss. She wanted to turn it into something hungry, build it to something feverish.

But her bones ached for sleep. So she pulled away to press a a kiss to Agatha’s nose, forehead, cheek. And the she was beside her again. Agatha had turned to press back into her and Rio wrapped her in her arms.

As Rio settled, as she nuzzled, as she let her body relax, her brain wouldn’t follow it. It turned over the conversation in Agatha’s office. It twisted its neurones around Jen’s desperate need to control a narrative not yet written. It curled around Alice’s desire to protect her girlfriend, and Rio, but also her fear and mistrust of Agatha.

It secured itself tightly to the reminder of Agatha’s outburst, of the tension in her body, of the way she’d lashed out and went for Jen’s throat when she was in the peak of her rage.

Rio nudged her nose along the soft skin at the base of Agatha’s neck, she breathed her in for a second, thinking of the way Agatha had broken down against her when she’d felt the shame of what she’d done.

Jen had once told her: “a feral cat attacks when it’s cornered.” But then she’d corrected herself. “An abused cat.”

It made Rio feel nauseous as she thought of those words from that night. Of Agatha breaking down then too, but alone, without Rio to hold her.

Rio made Agatha turn to her then. It was no longer enough to hold her from behind. She wanted Agatha to bury close. She wanted to feel the heat of her breath against her skin. She wanted to hold on to the woman she couldn’t stand to be apart from.

The woman she now had to leave and see only when her manager deemed it safe enough that she could.

Sex had been the spark that had lit Rio’s stubborn flame of self-improvement. But fear was the fuel that began the inferno. As she tangled herself in Agatha, as she tucked her under her chin and held her close, she burned with the knowledge that she’d get better, she’d get stronger.

She’d protect the fuck out of Agatha Harkness and her son.

Chapter End Notes

I'm sure Rio looking after Nicky will be totally fine and nothing will happen

Chapter 44: Speak of the Devil…

Chapter Summary

A summoning

Chapter Notes

Idk why this has been the hardest chapter to write but I hope you enjoy

See the end of the chapter for more notes

Agatha didn’t say a word to Rio the whole of the next morning. Or, what little of it they spent together. She wasn’t in the bed by the time Rio woke and when she went downstairs to find her she was already in her office with Jen.

Alice was waiting in the kitchen.

“What’s happening?”

“Nothing. Nothing shout-worthy anyway.”

Rio cleared her throat in a “don’t start” way and Alice said, “We should go. She wanted you to stop by before you left. So be quick about it and we can head straight to set.”

Rio didn’t need to be told twice. She marched straight to Agatha’s office and didn’t hesitate to knock on the door. Jen opened it, looked Rio up and down in Agatha’s borrowed t-shirt and the shorts she’d found before she left the bedroom, and stepped aside.

Agatha was at her desk, her glasses on the tip of her nose, her blue eyes tired but bright. She looked up when Rio walked over and made to pull Rio in before she was even close.

Rio grinned, the bridge of her nose bumping the arm of Agatha’s glasses as she turned into her. The hug was too tight to truly be comfortable but she’d take this over nothing. In fact, she wouldn’t protest if she had the indent of Agatha’s glasses on her face the whole rest of the day.

“You’re pap fodder, Rio. Did Alice tell you they’re outside your house?”

Rio broke the hug and turned to Jen.

“What? No?”

“They’re curious,” Alice said by the door. “You disappeared off with Agatha and Wanda was caught out for dinner with Jess.”

Rio nodded silently, piecing the two bits of information together as she felt Agatha’s hand brush her side. “We’re going straight to set?”

“Yeah. Can bundle you in before anyone spots you.”

Rio nodded again, aware Agatha was now back behind her desk.

“Starting to feel like stolen goods.”

Agatha snorted.

“It’s just easier to keep you between here and set.”

“So,” Rio shifted on the spot, “I can stay here this week?”

“Well,” Jen sighed as she settled back in the chair the other side of Agatha’s desk. “I’ve just been threatened with being fired and then, very dramatically, being hanged, drawn, and quartered. Whatever that means.”

Rio smirked and looked around to Agatha who seemed to be busy trying to hide her own smirk as she shuffled around some papers.

“Babe,” Alice nudged, “Let’s go, come on.”

Rio swept in to briefly kiss Agatha’s cheek before she turned to follow her friend out, with a slight spring in her step.

“Your neck is a disaster zone, by the way,” Alice said without looking round to her as she held out her jacket for Rio to take. “She’s a menace.”

Rio didn’t acknowledge whether she thought Agatha were a menace or not but she did wrap her scarf securely around her neck to make sure no one else caught the evidence of Agatha’s jealous temper.

“I really would have liked to have seen Nicky before we left.”

“It’s five in the morning.”

“Still.”

“Relax. You’ll have every evening this week to see him. He was asking for you before bed last night, by the way. Did Agatha tell you? Wanted to stay up until you arrived.”

Rio raised her brows as she pulled the heavy wooden door shut behind her, watching Alice as she marched along the path with her duffel over her shoulder.

“Hideous watches, by the way. And I’m buying you a DNA kit for your birthday.”

Rio jogged a little to catch up. “What? Why?”

“That kid’s getting more and more like you. He spent thirty minutes talking to me about his new watch his ‘melliza’ bought for him. Drones on and on just like you do.”

“I don’t drone on and neither does he.”

“Whatever. The face thing is creepy.”

“It is not creepy. He just… I don’t know. It’s just a genetic fluke. Maybe Agatha’s got some Puerto Rican in there somewhere.”

“I could make a dirty joke but honestly I’m too tired. She’s as white as they come and Ralph is practically Aryan. That boy is yours. I’m convinced.”

They’d reached the car now and Rio rolled her eyes as she slipped into the passenger seat.

“You think I hid a pregnancy from you?”

“That or you donated eggs.”

“Jesus, Alice.”

“I’m just saying.”

Rio huffed and pulled the mirror down to check herself over. Jen had been right the night before, she did look like shit. And not only did she look like shit but she also looked like she’d been let loose in a Sorority House judging by the marks on her neck as she pulled the scarf down to check. Makeup and Hair would have their jobs cut out for them but she tried not to think of how embarrassing it would be to expose her neck to the team for now.

She had other things to think on: learning her sides for the day, knowing her marks, being on her very best and most careful behaviour so as not to draw attention to the fact that her girlfriend was Agatha Harkness.

Those things and she had to get better. She had to fuel her body and move it too.

It felt like a lot. But Agatha was worth a lot. She was worth everything.

Rio didn’t see Agatha again until she was caked in makeup and on set by mid-morning. They were in matching Christmas sweaters and Agatha looked somehow to be glowing. Rio could see her freckles when she was close and she wondered if she even had any makeup on at all.

Her own makeup artist had done a tolerable job on her but she couldn’t help but think she didn’t glow like Agatha. Maybe the lights would do her a favour. Maybe she could make friends with the Editor and ensure she looked better on camera than she did in real life.

Maybe she could offer to pay for that CGI facial retouching thing she’d heard some older actresses use.

“You’re staring,” Agatha whispered to her as they were being prepped for the scene.

Agatha was about three feet away, someone fluffing her hair, another person down by her ankles, adjusting her socks.

“I’m admiring.”

Agatha arched a brow, motioning a little to the people around her with her head. But Rio ignored the warning.

“Did you have breakfast?”

“A bagel.”

“Will you be having lunch in your trailer again?”

“I might try a run around the lot.”

Agatha raised her brows and looked around at her properly, ignoring the assistant now adjusting the sleeves of her sweater.

“Really?”

“Mmhm. Gotta get fit.”

Agatha’s lips twitched and Rio just grinned.

“Take it steady, hotshot.”

“Not really my style, Harkness, but I’ll do my best.”

Agatha’s eyes narrowed but Rio knew she couldn’t do anything else with people so close. Still, she grinned at her girlfriend, and for a moment enjoyed that Agatha seemed to be struggling with not screaming.

“Don’t,” she whispered, her jaw tight, “call me that.”

The people around her moved away when it was called for positions to be taken.

“Your name?”

“Are you trying to-…? Don’t.”

A runner came close and went to adjust Agatha’s collar. Agatha twitched away, smacking his hand as she did.

“Who are you?”

Rio watched as the fury she’d just sparked in Agatha was taken out on the young try-hard and she grimaced as it was.

“Sorry, only Frankie said to-…”

“Then Frankie can do it. Don’t just touch me.”

Rio shifted on the spot, unable to intervene without embarrassing either one of them. The runner blinked, looked to Rio briefly, then scurried away.

“Go easy on him. He’s just a kid.”

“He touched me.”

Rio raised her brows, looking back to a hard jawline and fierce eyes. “If someone touched you without your consent I’d destroy them.”

“Mi corazón.”

“A runner doing his job and touching your collar is different to-…”

“My husband groping you?”

Rio blinked but couldn’t find a word to say in response before Frankie appeared and muttered, “Go easy on the runners, Agatha. They’re quite literally run off their feet as it is.”

Agatha didn’t say anything but when Frankie moved on to adjust Rio’s rolled up sleeves Rio managed to smile at the woman. Inside she felt sick, a sudden panic rising despite the current calm of their surroundings - the kitchen set was decorated for a quaint family Christmas.

When they were alone again Rio said, “Tell me you’re not doing anything reckless because-…”

“I’m destroying him for it.”

“Agatha.”

Agatha cleared her throat as quiet was called for on set. Rio stepped an inch to the right and glanced at her mark, a little green t-shape on the ground just inches from the counter, which meant she couldn’t lean against it. Who did this blocking anyway? Her mind was blank suddenly and she looked up in a panic at the script supervisor just as action was called.

Too late. The scene had started.

“You’re too soft with him,” Agatha said, easily in character now. Rio turned to her and saw she no longer looked furious, she was instead all of Kate’s exasperation.

But Rio didn’t know what she was supposed to say.

So she said nothing.

“You’re too soft with him,” Agatha repeated, not breaking character but finding a way to give Rio a second.

Rio just clung on until she felt the frenzy die. With the pads of her warm fingers she soothed over where she may have been too harsh earlier. With her lips she kissed over Agatha’s warmed chest and neck.

She stayed like that, trying to smooth over the damage she’d done, trying to love where she’d tried to latch.

And then she moved up again.

And then she saw the a sight too devastating to describe.

Agatha was still crying, her face screwed up, her lips delicately pouting. She was a soft pink, a watery glow about her. Rio turned her onto her back and hovered close over her, giving her some space to breathe whilst simultaneously letting her know she was there.

She was too far, there was too much distance. She leant back in and Agatha’s tears became her tears. Agatha’s breath became her breath.

Slowly, shyly, Agatha’s lips curled around her own. They began to kiss as if tasting the other for the first time. But their first kiss had been frantic, the result of weeks of tension and not being sure.

Earlier she’d been clawing and clutching at Agatha to feel every inch of her. And now she was guiding her through a kiss that healed something in them both.

There it was. The simple fear Agatha kept repeating. The fear Rio knew she couldn’t make her forget by simply repeating she never would. The fear her mother had sowed into her from birth.

Agatha’s eyes closed and Rio could feel the tension easing in the body beneath her. She settled some more, traced the wet of Agatha’s tears with her thumb. Agatha just breathed through it, her fingers twitching their tender attentions against Rio’s lower back.

The woman before her looked so much like the Grecian statues so admired the word over. Her pale skin, her strong jaw. Her face was a conversation Rio always wanted to be a part of. It was expressive when it needed to be but silent, stoic when she desired. Her warm cheeks and her perfect nose, she was graced with beauty that was timeless, indescribable. The words for it were lost to modern tongues but Agatha spoke them with every silent look, every flash of mirth in her sea blue eyes, every turn of her head in Rio’s direction.

Rio could listen to the story of her beauty forever.

The more she looked, the more she craved. Agatha had been graced with it but Rio was blessed by it. It was a beatitude from a land far away, a time long since forgot.

Agatha was her blessing.

“Mi vida, if I thought it would help I’d suggest running away so the three of us could just live a quiet life in the woods.”

The hairline cracks appeared in the marble of Agatha’s face. She was trying to make herself smaller, trying to hide. But Rio couldn’t allow it, wouldn’t be witness to Agatha shutting herself away.

“Tell me why you’re afraid.”

Agatha took a deep breath and said nothing but allowed Rio to press in, to nudge her nose tenderly into her cheek like a cautious puppy might. In the silence Rio’s mind churned over Agatha’s complicated reactions to things, to Rio’s love.

“You told me,” she whispered now, breathing the words out against Agatha’s temple where she’d just leant in to kiss her, “in Italy, you told me that one day I’d meet the woman I’d want to spend the rest of my life with and she’d be the luckiest woman alive.”

She moved down, maintaining contact with Agatha’s warm face, tracing her lips and now down until she could kiss Agatha, luxuriating in the feel of her kissing back.

“Rio.”

“Forever is what we agreed. You can’t take it back now, okay? You can’t think that I don’t want it.”
Above her girlfriend, Rio took a deep breath, she felt the air fill her lungs and held it until she was ready to speak again, to spill her truth: “You are strong enough and good enough to protect Nicky through this divorce. And I will be strong enough to protect you both. Te amo, mi vida. Más que vida.”

After a while of soft kisses and whispered promises, Agatha calmed down enough to fall asleep in Rio’s arms. The two remained asleep until an alarm went off somewhere in the room.

 

TUESDAY

Morning brought a renewed strength to the two of them. Agatha, unburdened now with the tales of her past and the therapy she’d been having, and Rio, sure as all shit with what she needed to do.

Rio was gone again before Nicky woke but that morning, before Alice arrived, they kickstarted a new tradition that would last the rest of the week. They made out, slowly, languidly, all tangled together in the bed. Then against the wall. Then by the front door.

He didn’t complain. Especially when the next course was ice cream.

“Argue about dinosaurs?”

“No, be together.”

Rio smiled and shuffled down so they could be face to face. She went to say something, something loving, something patient, something kind, but found words failed her as she drowned in deep blue.

When they fell asleep, they both dreamed of a time where they could read about dinosaurs every night and fall asleep, just like this, in each others arms.

 

SATURDAY

As if to make up for the fact that they’d barely kissed the day before, not five minutes after waking and barely bothering to brush her teeth, Rio was back on top of Agatha, pressing her up against the bathroom wall.

She’d decide the countertop was too dangerous.

But Agatha’s wrists were being held up against the wall so firmly that she’d dropped her toothbrush and it now lay destined for the trash by their feet.

The kiss today was furious, more feverish than it had been all week. Which meant it was dangerous too. Rio knew she wouldn’t be seeing Agatha until later and even then she wouldn’t have time alone with her. So she tried to put all she could into the kiss, trying to let Agatha know she was already feeling stronger, already healthier, already ready to protect her and her son.

Agatha moaned into Rio’s mouth as she arched against her and Rio soon introduced teeth where she’d previously only been using lips and tongue. It made Agatha protest, made her tug until Rio relented and she could use her hands to push Rio away.

She felt feral, like a rabid dog denied its treat.

All she wanted was Agatha, and yet, Agatha was everything she couldn’t have.

“No. Not-… not yet. Not today. I need… I have to think straight.”

Rio turned from her, running hers fingers through her hair and taking in a big, hopefully soothing breath. And then Agatha’s hands were sliding across her front, she was holding her the way she had when she’d held her for the first time.

On a jet ski in the Mediterranean Sea.

Her body reacted now how it had reacted then: she was on fire.

Agatha kissed along her neck until she pressed her face in against her shoulder and Rio held over her hands and looked at the two of them in the mirror.

“I’m scared.”

“I know.”

“Can you wear your shirt today? I’ll need it tonight.”

Rio closed her eyes, unable to see the sight before her anymore when she knew she’d need to leave Agatha and Nicky all alone, at the mercy of the world’s media.

“Mi vida.”

“Please, just, say you’ll wear it.”

Rio nodded and sighed out as Agatha moved slowly around her, finding her lips again in a soft kiss.

“I should go get Nicky up. I need to be at the lawyer’s office early. Will you have him up at the house by four? You have the address?”

Rio nodded, her eyes still closed until Agatha nudged their noses together and she fluttered her lashes until they were open, knowing what Agatha had been silently asking.

“I love you,” Rio whispered, watching the way Agatha’s sea blue eyes seemed to swirl with unshed emotion. “I can’t wait to start our lives together.”

Agatha’s face, carved from marble, was warm to the touch. Her cheeks were flushed still, her eyes soft, “Tell me one more time. Please. I need to hear you say it.”

“Para siempre, mi corazón. Te amo.” Forever, my heart. I love you.

Agatha’s head ducked in the briefest of nods and then she kissed Rio again and against her lips she promised: “Forever. I love you too.”

It was hard to leave the little bathroom after that. But Agatha needed to say goodbye to Nicky and they both needed to start their days.

Down the stairs, both of them now dressed, Agatha in a casual yet smart pantsuit, and Rio in jeans and her shirt, they fussed around Nicky, making sure he was as happy as he could be.

Agatha told him to be good for Rio but Rio really didn’t think there was any other way he could be for her. She told him she’d packed a bag for him of all his most precious things and that she’d see him later that evening in their new house. She told him to do everything Rio said and to not leave her side.

She told him she loved him more than anything and would see him soon. And then she hugged him and Rio had to look away for fear she’d be unable to hide the emotion in her face.

But Agatha was soon hugging her and Rio sighed out, forgetting herself briefly and pressing her lips for too long against her cheek. But Agatha didn’t pull away. She held her close and only stepped back when Rio loosened her hold first.

They made eye contact and though they didn’t say it, Rio knew Agatha felt it. She loved her beyond words.

Her thumb had been rubbing over and over Agatha’s fingers of her right hand, holding them loosely, reluctant to let go but not brave enough to cling on. She looked down at the motion and held Agatha’s hand between them as her thumb found a new ring on Agatha’s finger.

“I can’t wear the diamond,” Agatha said softly, knowing Rio’s question before she asked it. “This is the wedding band. Only on my right hand because-…”

“Because it’s a pretend one but only for now.”

Agatha nodded once and Rio looked up and smiled sadly, unable to stop herself from pulling Agatha back in for a tight hug. She was crinkling her suit but that didn’t matter. Holding her close was more important that proof she owned an iron - or her housekeeper did.

But Rio had to let Agatha go.

And Agatha left with her own bag of precious things after kissing Nicky one last time and then it was just them, dos patitos, and the whole day ahead of them. Rio had already fixed her face into a smile and moved around to steal one of Nicky’s toast soldiers from his plate by the time the door closed on Agatha.

“So. I was thinking… we spend all day in the park, we come back here, we grab your bag, head out for burgers, then head to the new house? How does that sound?”

Rio had never seen Nicky so happy. So happy, in fact, that she was able to steal another soldier.

“Yes!! Yes that sounds like the best plan ever!”

Rio laughed, biting into the soldier like an old King might his turkey leg. “Excellent because I’d have been very upset if you’d have said no to basketball and burgers.”

“Can we get milkshakes too?”

“And ice cream.”

It was quite difficult to make Nicky eat the rest of his breakfast before it got cold then. The rapid fire questions that came Rio’s way made her pour herself a larger coffee, for fear he’d tired her out before they even got to the park.

But somehow, they made it.

Rio had kept true to her word and kept her shirt on for Agatha, hoping she wouldn’t get too sweaty in it and secretly hoping even then Agatha wouldn’t mind. Or maybe that she’d prefer it.

Nicky had opted for his Celtics jersey, or, more accurately, Rio’s old Celtics jersey. The one that was too big for him. The one that he basically hadn’t taken off since he’d borrowed it from Rio the first time they met.

But Rio insisted he also wore a sweater. She did, however, allow him to have it partially open so people could see the green of his jersey. Though she neglected to point out that people could already see the bottom of it sticking below the hem of the sweater, as big as it was.

As a finishing touch, he also put on Rio’s Celtics hat, just to really show the world who his favourite team was.

In the meantime, Rio had packed a bag full of snacks and water and grabbed a basketball from outside.

So, making sure to lock the door and then the gate behind them, Rio and her little mellizo, stepped out into the sunshine hand in hand, with Nicky still chatting away happily and Rio still answering as best she could.

Everything changed as soon as they were in the car.

Rio had helped to strap Nicky in, not because she thought he couldn’t do it himself but because she wanted to make sure Agatha’s son was as safe as safe could be.

But that was when she realised that her little hybrid wasn’t the safest place for him.

Agatha had been right all those weeks ago. Her car was too small, too unsafe.

She felt sick suddenly.

Fuck fuck fuck, Rio thought the moment she’d started the engine of her little hybrid. This car was a death trap. It was so small and so obviously not suitable to transport her precious cargo anywhere.

She was going to kill Agatha’s son.

She broke out into a cold sweat as Nicky swung his legs and continued to talk about basketball.

Managing to respond but not really thinking about anything other than what an idiot she was for sending back Agatha’s gift of a big, sturdy, admittedly garish, car, she kept her focus on the road.

Clearly her responses weren’t good enough.

“What’s wrong, melliza?”

“Oh. Um. Nothing. I’m just… just trying to get us there safely.”

“Am I talking too much?”

“No, baby. Never. Sorry. I. Sorry.”

“It’s okay, we can be quiet.”

Rio chewed on her lip and kept her eyes on the road. She was a good driver, always had been. She was conscientious and deliberate. Her reactions were fast and she never went too fast or too slow.

There was no reason to think she’d crash when she never had before. She’d not so much as dented her car.

She took a breath and quietly asked: “Are you excited about the park?”

Nicky turned to her and grinned and for the first time Rio, briefly, took her eyes off the road. His smile relaxed her.

“Yes! We have so far to go to hit infinity.”

Rio nodded and forced herself to relax. Nicky was safe with her. She was a good driver. She would keep him safe. He would be returned to Agatha in one piece.

She’d promised Agatha she’d keep her son safe. She kept her promises.

Nicky was soon spouting off again, the shy little boy he was in company completely missing now he was on a roll with his favourite person. Even Rio’s softer responses, the way she wouldn’t look at him and kept her eyes on the road, didn’t seem to phase him.

He was simply happy to be there.

And Rio would only be happy once she’d trashed this damn car and bought a new one. A big one. An expensive, full of mod-cons, gas-guzzler that would keep Nicky safe. She could think of nothing else until they were parked up safely and Agatha’s son was back on solid ground.

Rio couldn’t help it when she checked him over briefly, wondering if she’d taken the last few corners too sharply and without knowing it had thrown Nicky about when actually he’d been very secure in his seat.

Nicky blinked up at her, allowing the check with a shy smile.

“You okay, melliza? You look upset.”

“I’m okay. I’m just… just making sure you’re okay.”

Nicky frowned as his smile faded, his eyes scanning over Rio’s face for a while before he said: “Melliza? What’s wrong?”

Rio bit down in her lip and paused where she’d been adjusting Nicky’s zipper on his sweater, tugging it up a little to protect from the cold and then down again so he didn’t overheat.

“I just want to make sure you’re okay.”

Nicky placed his hand over her own and made her stop. “Mama said you might worry.”

“She did?”

“Well, she told me last night,” Nicky shifted on the spot, “but I wasn’t supposed to tell you that.”

Rio’s lips twitched a little, “I won’t tell her you did.”

“Okay,” Nicky said softly, “only she said you might worry a little today and I was to be on my best behaviour for you so you don’t worry too much.”

“Is that right?”

Nicky was getting into it now, nodding his head enthusiastically as he said: “Yes and she said that I was to tell you that we are dos patitos today and we will have the best time and that I feel safe with you. Safe and happy.” He frowned as Rio smiled, “Seguro y feliz.”

He grinned when he remembered the words Agatha had taught him and Rio grinned right back at him, her heart rate hammering in her chest now for different reasons.

“Okay, mellizo. I guess if your mama says so then we will have the best time.”

“She is very smart.”

“Very smart.”

Nicky rocked up onto the balls of his feet and Rio straightened, taking his hand as she did.

Rio marched them away towards the empty basketball court and sat them both down on the mini bleachers set up to the side. The space around them was quiet, the sun was getting higher in the sky, though the air was cooler than usual for mid-March.

With her free hand she began to rummage in the tote bag for the cereal bars she’d packed earlier and when she found them she turned to pass one to Nicky and saw him measuring up his hand against Rio’s palm.

“One day your hand will be much bigger than mine.”

Nicky grinned up at her and filled the spaces between Rio’s fingers with his own, “But you’ll still hold my hand?”

“Oh I don’t think you’ll want me to.”

“No I always will! It’s soft and warm and it’s nice.”

Rio hummed and motioned for Nicky to take the offered bar. “For energy. We have a lot of points to get to infinity.”

Nicky decided holding her hand could wait in exchange for having enough energy to reach infinity. Rio smiled as he tucked into it and turned her gaze to the quiet surroundings, taking a bite of her own bar.

They ate in silence for two bites worth of the surprisingly delicious peanut butter flavoured bar until Nicky said something that was equally as surprising.

“My mama told me something else, melliza. Well, I told her something, I asked her something and she said that… she said I should tell you I love you.”

Rio almost choked.

Nicky patted her back in a manner that wouldn’t have made any difference at all if she had.

“She-…” Rio coughed, “She did?”

“Mama says it’s important to tell people you love them and… and also I think it’s nice to say so, I wanted to say it. My mama tells me everyday and I like it. So maybe you would like to hear it too. Because I do, I… so I wanted to say but I got nervous and mama said it would be okay.”

Rio nodded slowly, turning to the little boy with the big eyes and the hopeful grin. She opened her arm out and accepted him into a hug. Against his growing hair she whispered, “Yo también te amo, mellizo. Hasta el infinito.”

“Hasta el…?”

“Infinito. It means to infinity.”

Nicky nodded against her head and sighed out dramatically, “Hasta el infinito.”

“You sound upset, mellizo.”

“I just wish I’d said it sooner so then every night this week we could have said it.”

Rio placed her cereal bar down and held Nicky in a proper hug, “Then how about we promise to say it every day from now on?”

Nicky nodded again, “Okay, I’d like that.”

Rio hummed and gave Nicky a tight squeeze. Her gaze fell to a distant soccer game across the way and she lost herself in the sight of the tiny figures running about the place, surely having as good a time as she currently was. And all she was doing was sitting, holding her mellizo, knowing he loved her.

“Seguro y feliz,” Nicky whispered, “Dos patitos. Seguro y feliz.”

Rio turned her head and pressed a kiss to Nicky’s temple. “Dos patitos.”

The little boy in her arms pulled back and smiled his brilliant smile at her, dazzling her for a second. He placed a clumsy kiss to her cheek and Rio laughed, “Okay, okay, what about basketball? Are you ready to play?!”

Nicky grinned then and Rio laughed again as she stood with him and dragged him down to the court with the basketball from the car. She left behind their snacks and water for later on the bleachers.

On the court, with Nicky giggling and shouting, she wondered why she’d even been scared in the first place. They had the whole space to themselves, no paps, no fans, no one to have to protect Nicky from.

And for a while it was blissful.

Dos patitos running like wild animals around the deserted court. Rio could feel the pull of her body to the exercise. She could feel the rush of endorphins that came sooner now than they had been all week.

She’d been eating well, barely drinking, and she’d been sleeping better. Not to mention the calorie-killing make out sessions she’d been having.

She could feel that she was getting back to health again, less weak, sharper, more attuned to her body and her mind.

The first portion of their game lasted over an hour, then they stopped for water and snacks over at the bleachers. There were a few more people around now, a couple cars parked up. But no one was much interested in a woman and a child running like crazy people around a basketball court.

So Rio and Nicky sat happily with their snacks, blissed out still and unbothered by anyone near by.

Across the dusty little court there was someone with red hair leaning over her knees on the opposite bleachers, tapping away on her phone. But she was the closest person to them and she wasn’t a threat.

Rio had made sure to pack some fruit as well as the other chocolate and candy in the bag for fear Agatha might kill her for sending Nicky to the dentist with cavities. But the fruit got ignored because they both preferred the chocolate and Agatha wasn’t around to enforce the law.

Once refreshed they ran back onto the court and continued their quest to hit infinity points.

Play lasted for over an hour this time and even Rio was feeling the pangs of exhaustion and thirst as she shot the last hoop and bounced the ball back to Nicky.

“Time out, two secs. Give me your sweater, you must be so warm.”

She helped him shrug it off and swept his hair back from his brow, checking he wasn’t overheating after running around full pelt for so long.

“I’ll grab some water and some candy bars, okay? Keep practicing your jump shots.”

With a heavy, exhausted exhale, she turned from him and walked back to the side of the court and the bleachers. Placing Nicky’s now folded sweater down beside the bag, she first fished out her bottle and took a large, necessary gulp of water.

She could feel it trickle down her throat, and settle in her stomach. Perhaps she’d over-egged the feeling better a little. She took another mouthful and then grabbed Nicky’s and two chocolate bars from the bag, only feeling a little guilty that the apples in the bottom remained untouched.

And then she turned.

And her stomach dropped.

The red head from the opposite bleachers was now standing in the middle of the court with Nicky, bending down to get on his eye level.

Rio dropped everything in her arms and sprinted to his side, immediately pulling the little boy behind her.

Nicky gasped as he clung to her.

“Melliza!”

“Who the fuck are you and why are you talking to my kid?”

“Oh,” the woman straightened up. She was shorter than Rio by a few inches but was smirking as she looked her over, her eyes briefly flitting to Nicky peaking out from behind Rio’s hip. “I just wanted to say hello.”

Rio’s whole body felt hotter than it had felt even when she’d been tearing up the court earlier. She could feel her muscles tensing beneath her skin, either ready to fight or to run. But the woman before her seemed at ease, completely oblivious to Rio’s distress and the confusion of the little boy still hiding behind her.

The basketball had long since been forgotten and Nicky had his arms around Rio instead.

“Are you a journalist?”

“No,” the woman uttered, a vague look of amusement in her green eyes, “just a fan. I truly mean no harm.”

Her voice was sultry, pillow soft, and she looked Rio over again in a way that let Rio know she was coming on to her, or trying to, even with Nicky currently clutching at her. She sneered and took a step back, making Nicky take one too.

“You really don’t need to be worried.”

“You approached my kid and decided that-…”

“We were just getting to know one another, weren’t we, Nicky?” She looked back up at Rio and smiled, “I’m Natalie. I promise I mean no harm.”

“Melliza,” Nicky whispered, making Rio tilt her head slightly towards him but not taking her eyes off of the stranger. “She said she was a friend not, not a fan. Melliza she’s lying… Y-you’re lying!”

Nicky added the last part in a shout, leaning around Rio to look up at the woman who seemed absolutely nonplussed by the accusation. She simply raised her brows and looked expectantly up at Rio.

“Cute.”

Rio knew danger when she saw it. The woman had been watching them. She’d been waiting.

She’d lied to Nicky.

She didn’t waste another second.

She turned, gently prying Nicky off of her and ushering him ahead, keeping him out of view of the smirking stranger.

“Let’s go. Now. Quick.”

Nicky hurried along ahead of her but Rio wasn’t moving fast enough. She started to run, ushering Nicky along as quickly as she could.

“Nice to meet you, Rio Vidal. Drive safe now.”

If Nicky hadn’t been there, or if Rio could have handed him over to Agatha in that moment, she’d have turned around and smacked the bitch. But he was here. Agatha wasn’t. So she didn’t. She just ran with him, got to her car, helped him into his seat and ignored his panicked questioning.

“Melliza? Melliza? Did I-…? Did I do something w-wrong?”

When he was strapped in, and Rio checked three times that he was, she jumped in the driver’s seat, turning only once to see the woman still standing there, now simply watching them from the centre of the court.

Rio put the keys in the ignition and pulled out of the parking lot.

“M-melliza?”

“You’re okay, baby. We’re okay. We’re okay.”

“She said-… She said you were her friend a-and I didn’t say anything to her, she already knew my name a-and she said she liked my hat a-and-…”

“It’s okay, mellizo. It’s okay. You did nothing wrong. Nothing at all.”

Nicky beside her was digging his fists into his eyes and Rio looked around in horror at the sight of him hiding his face below the peak of his cap.

“Nicky, I mean, I mean, mellizo. Baby. Please don’t cry. It wasn’t your fault. I shouldn’t have, fuck, I shouldn’t have left you and she shouldn’t have approached you.”

Rio smacked her horn, and growled in frustration. The very thing she’d promised Agatha and Nicky she could do she clearly couldn’t. She was inept, incompetent, immature.

And then a hand wrapped around her arm and Rio took a breath before she glanced at Nicky and saw in his face that he didn’t think any of those things. He still loved her. To infinity.

“Melliza?” He asked softly, his wide eyes watery, “Please don’t be sad. O-or angry. Can I have-… can we stop please? Can we? Please?”

Rio just swallowed, her throat feeling tight all of a sudden. She drove on a little further to put more distance between them and the stranger but soon pulled in along the next side street and parked up. Without saying anything she hopped out of the car and went around to Nicky’s side.

He’d already freed himself from his seatbelt by the time she got to him. He flung his arms around her neck and she did the same around his middle.

He was safe. He was unharmed. She’d kept him safe.

Nicky clung to her for more than five minutes, making her shoulder damp, but she couldn’t care about anything other than him being safe in her arms.

“I’m sorry, melliza.” He hiccuped softly, sniffing. “I thought I was doing the right thing. Mama says don’t talk to strangers a-and I don’t but she knew you a-and my name and said she was a friend a-and so I didn’t run because I-…”

“Shh,” Rio rushed out, rubbing soothing circles along Nicky’s back, “It’s okay. It’s okay. I shouldn’t have left you. I’m so sorry, Nicky.”

“M-mellizo,” Nicky corrected with a sniff, now pulling back and frowning where he looked down at the mess he’d made on Rio’s shirt. “It’s okay, you protected me. You took me away from the lady and I’m safe now. We’re both safe now. I-I-I want you to be safe with me too.”

He began to cry again and Rio pulled him right back in, holding him so fiercely she worried she might be hurting him. But he didn’t protest, he just cried quietly against her until all that was left were soft sniffles and gentle hiccups.

Rio continued to rub his back, trying to think back on how long she’d left him, how long he’d been vulnerable and exposed for. How angry Agatha would be when she told her.

But she’d endure Agatha’s wrath. Because Nicky was safe. That was all that mattered.

“Some people,” Rio said as softly as she could, not wanting Nicky to feel like he was in any trouble, “some people will know your name, and my name too, and your mama’s, and even if they say they’re friends it doesn’t mean they are okay, mi angel?”

Nicky just nodded against her, “Mama said so too. She says all the time. I forgot. I forgot.”

“I know, baby. It can be confusing. It’s okay. It’s okay.”

Only when Nicky’s sniffing had died down enough, only when he was holding onto her instead of clutching, did Rio pull back again. She gently removed his hat and wiped over his face until it was as dry as she could make it and she held him up to look her in the eye.

He smiled weakly and Rio smiled the same.

“Let’s go grab your bag and get you to the new house.”

“Okay, melliza. That… sounds good. You’re not mad?”

“Never mad at you.”

Nicky nodded and Rio jumped into the car with him again. She checked his seatbelt three times once more and then put the keys in the ignition. The drive back was somehow less tense than the drive to the basketball court.

Perhaps because the big bad had happened. Perhaps because nothing else could possibly go wrong.

Perhaps because Nicky’s hand was holding her arm.

She parked up outside Agatha’s house and took in a deep breath. Nicky’s hand moved to her own on the wheel. She turned to him and he smiled, his cheeks a little pink from the earlier tears.

“You okay, melliza?”

“Are you okay, mellizo?”

Nicky nodded and Rio nodded too. She squeezed his hand and then released it so she could jump out and run around to get Nicky’s door. His seatbelt was already undone again and Nicky launched himself into Rio’s arms.

It was a desperate hug, a drier one than before. But Rio heaved him out of the car and held him as close as possible before she dropped him gently down again.

But away from Rio’s arms, out of the car, Nicky was tense again. This little boy couldn’t have been more different than the little boy he’d been before Rio had been an idiot. His little hand wasn’t holding hers anymore, it was clutching. He was squeezing the life out of it and she didn’t even know if he realised.

But Rio made long, fast strides towards Agatha’s house, making Nicky run alongside her to keep up. Inside was safe. Inside meant that no one would come to try and talk to the boy she’d been asked to look after for the day.

The boy who she’d left alone for all of ten seconds and had suddenly been approached by a stranger. She should have known. She should have done better.

They made it through the gate after Rio tapped in the code and Rio already felt herself begin to calm. But Nicky’s hold remained secure.

“Okay, kid,” she uttered in as calm a voice as she could, “Grab your bag and we’ll head back to the new house, okay? You excited?”

“Yeah, melliza.”

Nicky’s voice was quiet still, and Rio stopped before they got to the front door. She turned him to face her and dropped to one knee before him. “Baby, what happened in the park, it wasn’t your fault, okay? That lady shouldn’t have approached you. I’m sorry you got scared. You did nothing wrong. So, let’s head in, grab your bag, and then we’ll get burgers and ice cream, okay?”

Rio held Nicky’s sides and smiled hopefully up at the little boy who’s frown was slowly morphing into a shy smile. “You’re still not mad?”

“At you? Never.”

Nicky nodded and Rio smiled a little more, “So? Burgers and ice cream?”

“And movies?”

“And movies.”

Nicky nodded and his shy smile became a pleased grin as he launched himself at Rio and she grunted and then lifted him into the air with an exaggerated groan that made Nicky giggle.

He didn’t feel as heavy as he’d felt a week ago and just as Rio was wondering whether she was stronger now or if the emotions of the day had fuelled her body the door beside them opened.

Rio span with an expectant grin. Because who else but Agatha would be opening her own door?

Only it wasn’t Agatha.

It was the person Rio despised more than anyone else in the world. The person who'd tried to destroy her vida, who'd cut her mellizo's hair.

It was Evanora Harkness.

Chapter End Notes

I know people will ask so yes we will find out what Agatha discussed in therapy and why she won't tell Rio about it

as always thank you so much for reading

Chapter 45: …And She Shall Appear

Chapter Summary

Rio meets Agatha’s mother

Chapter Notes

Just a short, easy read for you

See the end of the chapter for more notes

A chill ran through Rio’s basketball-warmed body.

Of all the people in all the world, she hadn’t expected her. Agatha, yes. Her housekeeper? Maybe. Jen? Potentially. Even Alice wouldn’t have been as big a shock.

Hell, even Wanda wouldn’t have been as surprising.

But then, if the few Psych classes she took in College could have told her anything it was that abusers, narcissists, they thrived on their victim’s misery. Perhaps Evanora could just feel Agatha’s stress and fear and she simply manifested here, ready to feed off of it.

Rio had to shake her brain, had to make herself focus. Because it didn’t matter why she was here. It mattered that she was and that Nicky, who’d just relaxed, who’d just thrown himself at Rio, excited for burgers and ice cream and movies, was now tense and frightened in her arms.

Nicky was all that mattered.

The little boy adjusted himself in her hold to look over his shoulder just as Evanora said: “Nicholas. Come inside. Now.”

Rio’s grip on Nicky tightened and she stepped back, stumbling slightly as she fell down the small step of the porch. She managed to stand tall, to keep Nicky in her arms.

The witch before her just stared at her grandson, refusing to meet Rio’s shocked gaze.

She was tall, perhaps an inch taller than Agatha, so not as tall as Rio. Her long silvery hair was piled in a neat bun on top of her head. She was beautiful, there was no doubt about it. But sharp, her features all inclined to the dangerous, rather than the welcoming.

Agatha’s beauty was different. Completely so.

And Rio realised in an instant that, just like Nicky was nothing like his father, Agatha was nothing like her mother.

“Nicholas,” Evanora repeated, “I will not ask again. Get away from this woman.”

Evanora held out a bony hand towards them and Rio stepped back again.

Whether real or imagined Rio felt like she could feel Nicky’s heart hammering against her chest but she didn’t let go. She didn’t even loosen her hold.

She’d hold him forever, risk her muscles atrophying in this position just to keep him away from this woman.

And Nicky didn’t let go either.

His left arm, wrapped around her neck for leverage, adjusted so his fingers could bury in her short hair, tangling himself to her. It reminded Rio of what this woman had done to this little boy, of why he was currently growing his hair out. She held Nicky closer.

“Grandmother,” Nicky said quietly, “this is Rio. My… melliza.”

“Está bien, mellizo,” Rio murmured, speaking her dad’s language in a reflex, the words soothing just in the speaking of them, to her at least. She hoped Nicky understood, hoped he took comfort too in the language that she always returned to, the words that took her home.

Nicky turned to her. His cap was touching her forehead he was so close. She could feel his warm, fast breath across her cheeks and the look in his wide eyes sent shock waves through her body. He wasn’t scared, he was terrified. “Está bien,” she whispered again, giving Nicky a reassuring squeeze.

“Do you speak English?”

It wasn’t even subtle, the microaggression. Rio blinked and looked around to Evanora, seeing that she was looking at her for the first time. Her eyes were blue, but not like Agatha’s. They were an ice blue, almost unreal in their brightness. They had none of Agatha’s warmth, none of her depth.

And Rio realised that she was no longer beautiful. Her beauty disappeared the moment she saw the hatred in her blue eyes. This woman was twisted evil and there was nothing soft, nothing kind about her.

Rio swallowed. Adjusted her hold, making sure Nicky was secure in her arms. He was getting heavier but she wouldn’t drop him, she wouldn’t let him know he was anything other than safe in her arms.

Seguro hasta el infinito.

All Agatha had asked her to do was to look after her son. And as she felt Nicky’s fingers twist and tangle more securely in the hair at the base of her head, she couldn’t help but think: our son.

Her namesake.

Her mellizo.

The boy who loved her and wished he’d been able to say it every day.

“Grandmother,” Nicky’s cheek was practically against Rio’s now, she could feel the warmth of it, the growing heat as he continued bravely on, “Rio is, she-…”

Evanora took a step towards them and Rio took another step backwards. She’d narrowly missed grabbing Nicky’s arm and Nicky gasped quietly. Rio was suddenly under no illusion as to how frightened he was. His hold on her hair tightened and Rio would have endured the sharp pain of it for a thousand lifetimes if it meant she could also feel now how she felt with his cheek against her own.

Agatha had named him for her. She’d birthed this miracle of a child and forged him through love to create this dulce ángel clinging to her in her arms.

He was proof that Evanora had no real power over Agatha. She had none over Nicky.

She sure as shit had none over Rio.

Evanora wouldn’t get in their way. She stepped forwards and Nicky must have been fearful she was going to pass him off because he buried closer, tightened his hold of her hair. He was tugging it now with every desperate grasp and twist of his fingers, though Rio knew he wasn’t meaning to.

He was just frightened, and it made Rio feel stronger than she’d felt in weeks. She held him tighter. Nicky pressed closer. He suddenly wasn’t as heavy.

Evanora had the good sense, because it sure as shit wasn’t manners, to step aside and let Rio into the house. But she found her voice just as Rio was crossing the entranceway.

“You are trespassing!”

The venom in Evanora’s tone made her hold on Nicky tighten until she was worried she was hurting the boy. But he didn’t protest and kept pressed flush against her, moving in her arms only to turn back and look at his grandmother. Rio quickened her steps as Evanora shouted: “I’m calling the police!”

Empty threats, she repeated to herself. Empty threats. Agatha had given her the passcode, the key, she’d told her to look after her son for the day. She had every right to be here.

Nicky wanted her here. He’d asked for her to be here.

And how the hell was Evanora here?!

She got to the bottom of the stairs and bent to try and place Nicky down. But he held on.

Rio felt like she could no longer breathe. She straightened up, readjusted him.

“No me voy. Estaré aquí enseguida. ¿Puedes subir a buscar tu mochila? ¿Me entiendes? Estaré aquí enseguida. Ve a buscar tu mochila, mellizo.” I'm not leaving. i'll be right here. Can you go upstairs and get your bag? Do you understand me? I'll be right here. Go get your bag, twin.

All the while Nicky looked panicked, looked wide-eyed and frightened. Rio knew he wouldn’t want to let go but she didn’t trust herself to be at the top of the stairs with Evanora close by. She’d push her down them and then she’d lose Nicky forever.

She nodded slowly, hoping Nicky understood her words, at least the context of them, the soft plea for him to run and get his bag, to get away from his grandmother for even two minutes.

It seemed like he did. Nicky reluctantly let go, his feet were on the floor but his hands were still in her hair. So Rio was down on his level, hovering between a crouch and a cry. She held his sides, held him firmly, locked eyes with her twin.

In a quieter voice than before, just for Nicky, she whispered, “Tres patitos.”

She felt his fingers flex against her scalp, felt him start to untangle himself from her. But slowly, cautiously. Even as Rio nodded encouragingly again when his hands fell to her shoulders, even when she gave him a gentle squeeze, he didn’t want to let go.
