Evanora spoke from just over her shoulder. “Nicholas, come to me. This woman should not be here. It seems your mother needs to learn who she should and should not be associating with.”

Rio’s jaw clicked but she kept her eyes on Nicky, tried to keep them soft. “Okay, mellizo?” She lowered her voice even further. “¿Me etiendes?” Do you understand?

She felt a hand on her shoulder and Nicky’s hands flew back to her hair, his eyes breaking their stare and looking up to his grandmother again. “Baby,” she whispered at the same time Evanora barked: “Nicholas.”

Rio began to pry Nicky’s hands from her hair as the little boy looked torn, look panicked. And Rio began to feel the panic rising in her own chest. She needed Agatha and she needed to get Nicky out of here.

“Esta bien, mellizo. Rápidamente.” She nodded towards the stairs and Nicky finally loosened his grip, looked at her one last time, and then began to stumble his way up the stairs.

She watched as he used his hands to help him up, as he kept looking back at her, as his little body tried its hardest to carry him as fast as it could.

But she couldn’t keep looking. Evanora had growled and heaved Rio around, making her face her. Rio stumbled where she’d been crouched. She fell backwards and caught herself last second, jamming her right palm onto the floor to catch herself.

She heard Nicky gasp out and looked as he began to run back down to her but she shook her head no and the boy stopped in the middle of the stairs.

“Nicholas. Here now.”

Rio grimaced as she pushed herself up and stood to her full height. “Esta bien, mellizo. Rápidamente.”

Nicky looked unsure but Rio nodded again and he turned to face back up the stairs. When he was out of sight Rio’s head was tugged backwards, a sharp, vicious movement that made her gasp in shock and pain.

She fought to keep her face neutral and made to grab at Evanora but the old woman removed her hand. She’d got the reaction she wanted.

She was nothing like Agatha, in the way she looked or the way she behaved. Agatha’s furies were bright, a sun with infinite storms. But Evanora was different. Her fury was dark, like oil bleeding across an ocean, infecting and forever changing everything in its path.

Only Rio wouldn’t let her poison anywhere near Nicky. She could try, she could inject it into Rio’s veins and drown her in it but she wouldn’t touch that boy. Not while Rio still had air in her lungs and eyes to see.

“Listen to me,” Evanora’s hand moved to her shoulder again and she felt the threat of her sharp nails but Rio chose not to flinch. “You will stay away from my grandson, and you will stay away from my daughter. You and your filth. Do you understand me?”

Rio inclined her head just a fraction, no longer attempting to keep her face neutral. She pulled her shoulder back and Evanora raised her brows. Clearly she was expecting a “yes, ma’am.”

Rio had read her right because her next words were: “I see your parents dragged you up.”

Rio’s jaw flexed again and violence was on the tip of her tongue until she heard the heavy footsteps of a frantic little boy hurrying his way back to her. She turned from Evanora and looked up to see Nicky with a backpack too large for his small frame and a familiar looking cuddly toy in the form of some sort of floppy animal in his clutches.

“Ten cuidado, mellizo,” be careful, Rio called out as Nicky raced towards her.

“Nicholas,” Evanora barked again, just as Nicky flew past the first two steps. Her voice was practically shaking with rage now, “I forbid you to go anywhere with this feral woman. You are to stay with your grandmother until your mother gets home. We all need to have a little family talk.”

Rio had started up the stairs already, her arms open to grab Nicky before he could fall in his haste. He threw himself at Rio and she just about managed to keep them upright. His backpack worked as a sort of opposing force that meant she didn’t fall over backwards. He was almost impossible to hold, so she half-held, half-led him down the stairs.

But he was safe. He wouldn’t fall. Rio had him.

Back on solid ground now, Nicky pressed close and squashed his toy between them but kept his eyes on his grandmother. “I-I want to stay with Rio.”

“Out of the question,” Evanora snapped, reaching a hand towards Nicky as Rio turned to look at her, cradling Nicky’s head against her as she did.

“Dile adiós a tu abuela,” say goodbye to your grandmother, Rio uttered as calmly as she could, looking back at Nicky now who felt so tense against her.

Evanora scoffed and stepped closer but Rio stepped her and Nicky away, unwilling to let the woman touch the boy.

“You cannot take him from me, from this house.” Every word was spat, every consonant perfectly enunciated, every vowel rounded and whole. But no real woman with any class or high ground of any kind would have spoken like that.

Rio ducked her head down to kiss the top of Nicky’s head and whispered a quick, and what she hoped was reassuring, “Te tengo, mellizo.” I’ve got you.

She tried to guide him now, tried to direct him around his grandmother so they could leave.

And Nicky tightened his hold then let go so he could begin moving with her. But she’d been too slow, she’d underestimated Evanora. Or perhaps she just couldn’t comprehend that anyone would hurt a kid.

Nicky’s grandmother had reached between them as Nicky had begun to pull away. He was slow, reluctant to move, but he was doing it.

He was being brave and Rio was so proud that he trusted her in that moment that she didn’t react in time.

The old witch had secured her claws around Nicky’s ear, had made him yell in shock and pain. She twisted it, tugged his head backwards.

“Just like your mother.”

Evanora had been a coiled snake up until that moment. A cobra standing tall, primed to strike. And the strike had been precise, vicious, deadly.

Her words were spat at a little boy so terrified and so innocent. And Rio saw red.

She reacted quickly this time. She grabbed Evanora’s wrist and wrenched her hand off of Nicky’s ear, throwing the crone’s arm away without mercy. She could have ripped it from its socket for all she cared. The old woman gasped and held her wrist up like Rio had burned it.

“Don’t fucking touch him.”

Evanora glowered.

Nicky was back to hugging her, back to clinging to her, back to trying to crawl into her skin.

“So the mongrel can speak the language of its betters?” Evanora’s laugh was high, more a cackle than anything else, but Rio didn’t stick around to watch her eyes flame in delight.

She was grabbing Nicky, trying to be firm but gentle, turning him in front of her and hurrying him as quickly as she could towards the door. She could hear her heartbeat in her ears, could feel her body curling towards Nicky, trying to form some sort of barrier between him and his grandmother even as they ran.

She’d touched him. She’d hurt him. She was going to kill her.

“This is kidnapping! You cannot take my grandson away from me!”

If Nicky weren’t there she might have turned around and actually killed the woman. But Nicky was there. So Nicky was instead the priority.

They reached the door, Rio leaning to help Nicky open it when Evanora’s voice sounded again, closer than it had been before. She’d been following. She was determined.

“Take your hands off of him!”

The door was open, Nicky had taken his first step out.

Rio was grabbed back, half-turned now away from the little boy.

Evanora had her claws in her forearm and Rio bared her teeth and raised her fist as Evanora clung to her arm. Her sharp talons were purposefully pressing as hard as she could. But Rio didn’t cry out. She didn’t flinch even as they broke skin.

She wouldn’t give Evanora the satisfaction.

“You have a sickness! You have infected my child with your filth. I will not let you infect my grandson, you you… Mexican DOG.”

Spit flew form Evanora’s lips and landed across Rio’s cheek. She fell from her brain. Everything stopped until it started again.

Until Nicky brought her back to life.

“NO! No! Let go! Let go of her!”

Nicky had joined the fray, trying to tug Rio’s arm away from Evanora but she wouldn’t release her hold and Rio wasn’t attempting to pull away. She just let her cling, let her think she had the upper hand.

But she’d lost already.

Rio had Agatha.

Rio had Nicky.

She stared into eyes of brightest blue and with a mouth full of hatred she said:

“You are not worthy of either of them.”

Evanora’s eyes widened infinitesimally and she pressed her nails in harder. But the pain of it was nothing to Rio’s loathing of the woman before her.

She wouldn’t give in. She wouldn’t cower or back down.

This woman was the reason that for almost forty years Agatha had hidden herself away, had denied herself the chance to be happy. This woman was scum, she was poison, and Rio would not let her win.

“Melliza, melliza,” Nicky began to insist, his hands grabbing Rio’s arm, still trying to pull her free of his grandmother’s hold. Rio didn’t look round but if she had she’d have seen tears falling silently from his eyes as he continued to insist before her, trying to tug her arm back still, “Está bien, melliza. Estoy aquí. Estoy aquí.” It’s okay. I am here. I am here.

Evanora’s bright eyes flashed at the sound of her grandson speaking Rio’s language, the language he’d been learning so he could speak with her in the words of her beloved papa. The language that represented everything that Evanora was not.

The language that contained their love for one another. The language that made them a family, a brood. It had made them what they were now: tres patitos.

She saw something register on Evanora’s face as she looked between Rio’s dark gaze down to the face of Nicky, his own eyes wide, but the very reflection of his melliza’s.

Whether she recognised the stark similarity or she simply didn’t know how else to proceed, she released her hold.

With the loosening of Evanora’s grip, Rio’s arm flew back and Nicky kept a hold on her, beginning to tug her out the door. She felt the warm trickle of blood against her wrist as she turned to usher Nicky out. Nicky was practically dragging her now, holding her injured arm with that same clutching grip.

She wiped her face of Evanora’s venom and made a solemn vow: she’d not let Nicky see his grandmother ever again.

She raced with him, trying to help him by holding his backpack up as he ran with it. They must have looked insane, an Oscar Winner and a tiny boy with a big backpack chasing up the street. But they made it to Rio’s car without seeing anyone else.

Rio turned to check over her shoulder as she ripped Nicky’s door open. The street was empty. Evanora hadn’t followed.

Rio helped Nicky into his seat, made sure his belt was on, that he was secure, and placed the backpack down by his feet, not wanting to waste time getting it in the back.

She checked his ear, made sure he wasn’t bleeding. It was red, hot to the touch, but she hadn’t broken skin.

“Melliza, melliza,” Nicky chanted her nickname, trying to grab at her even as she pulled away. She didn’t have time to reassure him. She only had time to get them out, to get them as far away as possible.

She jumped into her side of the car, barely able to breathe.

“You’re bleeding!”

“It’s okay, it’s okay.”

Rio turned the engine on before she’d even secured her own belt and pulled from the curb as fast as she could.

“Melliza, you’re bleeding!”

“I know, baby. It’s okay. I’m okay.”

“No, no, Rio! She hurt you!”

Rio could feel her pulse in her throat but she had to keep going, had to get Nicky as far away as possible. She had to get to the house, the hideaway, had to get Nicky safe.

She’d fucked up. Twice. She’d exposed him to an over-familiar stranger and now she’d not been able to keep him from his evil bitch grandmother. Agatha would never trust her again. She’d never leave her alone with him.

Her head began to thump. The pain she hadn’t experienced in days now was back. Tenfold.

Nicky beside her was trying to get to her, trying to reach as his desperation took over. He was crying but Rio couldn’t comfort him. She had to keep driving, had to get them safe before she started to see any colours.

“R-Rio! Your arm! You’re hurt!”

Rio shook her head, shook it as if she were shaking off something rather than denying it. Her arm did hurt. It stung, the bitch had buried her claws in as deep as she could manage for the pure thrill of watching Rio suffer.

Punishment, Rio realised as she overtook a slow-moving truck.

The promise Agatha had been brought up with. Be too loud: punishment. Have opinions: punishment. Defy your mother in any way: punishment.

Love someone other than the straight white man I forced you to marry: punishment.

Something in Rio’s peripheral flashed and she turned to see but there wasn’t a car beside her.

“Melliza?” Nicky was breathless, desperate, his hand curling cautiously around her arm.

Rio looked down at it, saw the fierce red marks across her inner forearm where Evanora had plunged her talons. Four. Four gashes across her skin, all bloody and raw.

Nicky’s fingers were curled just by them, a stark contrast to his grandmother. Soft, gentle, cautious.

She looked back to the road again.

“Si, cariño?”

Nicky sniffed, “Why does, why does she hate you? Why did she hurt you?”

“It’s complicated, sweetheart.”

Nicky was silent for a while and Rio was fighting with her foot, feeling too trigger happy on the gas.

“I hate her.”

Nicky was sniffing again, and Rio glanced at him as he used his free hand to wipe at his eyes. He looked miserable, blotchy from tears. She took a breath and moved her arm to take his hand, her eyes already back on the road.

Nicky continued to sniff quietly, and Rio could see from the corner of her eye that he kept wiping his eyes so she knew he was still crying. But Rio kept her eyes on the road, kept checking the rear view mirror every so often just to make sure they weren’t being followed.

She had two options now, take Nicky directly to the hill house purchased to keep him hidden, to keep him out of harm’s way, or take him someplace else.

Anywhere else.

It was a decision she didn’t want to have to make. A decision she felt like she couldn’t make.

She glanced at Nicky again and felt his fingers curl more tightly around her hand. He was looking down at her arm and she caught his frightened stare.

Something about the way his face was now formed reminded her of Agatha. And she knew what she had to do.

She had to trust that the house would remain their sanctuary. High up in the Bird Streets in the hills, far away from the witch with the sharp claws and venomous tongue.

She looked back at the road. She swallowed. She made her decision.

They drove on in silence for a little while longer, Rio focused in on driving as safely as she could but fast, always pushing that little bit just to get them to their destination sooner. In her peripheral vision she could see Nicky clutching at the toy she’d noticed earlier and she glanced at it before she turned back. She was still in a steel deathtrap after all, she had to be extra careful.

“What’s their name?”

Nicky was silent for a second and then said, “Scratchy. I just sleep with him sometimes. I got him when I was little. I didn’t want him left with grandmother.”

Rio nodded silently, keeping her eyes on the road.

“He’ll be happy you took him.”

“Melliza,” Nicky’s voice was quiet still, almost drowned out by the hammering of her heart. “Can you call my mama, please? I don’t want her to get hurt and I want her to fix your arm and… and I want her to be with us.”

“Yes, yes, of course. I-…”

Rio cleared her throat and glanced at the screen on the console between them. She didn’t know where her phone was. Somewhere in her bag which was by Nicky’s feet and now under his backpack.

“Can you get me my phone? Do you know how to use it?”

Nicky scrambled down to reach her bag and just about managed to shift his backpack but couldn’t quite get to it and Rio flew a hand out to make him sit up again. The last thing she needed was for him to hit his head in his haste to get to her phone. Or worse.

“Wait, wait. We’ll call her when we get in, okay? I promise. As soon as we’re home.”

She cursed silently for not having thought of it sooner. Of course Nicky would want his mom. Of course she should have called his mom.

Of course they needed Agatha.

But Nicky had her hand again and had placed Scratchy in her lap. She glanced down at it, recognising now that it was clearly a rabbit. He had floppy ears and that well-loved look most kids toys were never blessed with.

Nicky clearly loved him, had clearly held him many times, cuddled him all through his childhood. She imagined Nicky as a baby with the pristine version of Scratchy by his side in his crib.

And then another flash happened and she looked to see where it had come from but again saw nothing.

Nicky as a baby had reminded her that he still was a baby. A baby who had just been grabbed by his grandmother. A baby who had valiantly defended her, who had tried to save her even when he’d been terrified.

“Melliza?” Rio glanced Nicky’s way. “Are you okay?”

Rio swallowed the lump that had long ago lodged in her throat and nodded, “Let’s just get home, okay? Are you excited to see your new house?”

“Does my grandmother know where it is?”

“No, baby. Only us. Only us, your mama, and Jen, okay?”

Nicky nodded slowly, and Rio looked back at him as he focused on her arm. “And Alice? She can know too.”

“Alice can know too,” she agreed quietly, focusing back in on the road.

“Alice looks at me sometimes,” Nicky whispered, his free hand moving to touch by one of Rio’s cuts. It didn’t hurt but she looked down to see what he was doing. He was just looking, just curious. His brows pulled tightly together in a sad frown and Rio wondered whether he was still trying to understand how someone could do what his grandmother had did.

The apple had fallen very far from the poisoned tree.

“She looks at you?”

Rio knew what Nicky meant but she was too caught up on getting them to the house safely, on fighting the pain in her head, on avoiding flashing lights.

Nicky sniffed, “I don’t think she likes me.”

Rio bit down on the inside of her cheek, she stared out the front window, she cleared her throat quietly, “Did you know I’ve known Alice since I was eighteen? Almost half my life?”

“Really?”

Rio nodded, keeping her eyes forward even as she could feel Nicky looking up at her. “So she knows my face really well. Really, really well. And I think when she looks at you she’s actually just looking because-…”

“Because we look a little the same.”

Rio smiled a little and glanced at Nicky. “Exactly, mellizo.”

Nicky’s hand flexed against her arm and then he held her hand in two of his. “Maybe more than a little, you know. Maybe that’s why my grandmother was so…”

Rio stuck her tongue in her cheek as she took a bend, wending their way up now into the hills. Nicky was wiser than his years. He had his mom’s intellect, her desire to learn, to know more than she was offered.

She remained silent, let him think his thoughts for a little while.

The further into the hills they got the more she felt like she could breathe. But she didn’t have the SatNav on. She had to keep a close eye on the street signs.

“Mama will be upset,” Nicky whispered, and Rio could feel his eyes on her again. She held his hands a little tighter.

“Only because she’ll be worried about you, mellizo. But she’ll be okay. We’ll be okay.”

She took a turn up a steeper hill.

“She’ll be upset that you’re hurt and that,” Rio paused, realising they were on the right street. She slowed down, feeling her heart rate slow alongside the engine. “that you got scared.”

“And that you’re bleeding,” Nicky added so quietly Rio almost missed it as she concentrated.

“Sí, mellizo.” She was distracted, too intent on getting to the right house. There weren’t many on the street, in fact, she didn’t see one for a while and soon became worried she’d forgotten the address.

But then there it was, cresting just over the break of the hill. From the looks of it, it was a mission revival style house. White and terracotta, not quite the Spanish style of Rio’s house across town. Rio pulled up to the large gate and leant out to input a code, her own birthday, chosen because who would guess that knowing the day Rio Vidal first breathed life into the world would be the key needed to access Agatha Harkness and her son.

She pulled in slowly, on high alert for anyone else suddenly appearing. But it was just the house. Just Nicky, Rio, Scratchy, and the house.

Rio parked up, she went to help Nicky, and found that more than that was impossible now the boy had his arms around her neck and his face pressed in against her shoulder. She relaxed enough to not hurry him along, to not insist they get moving.

She relaxed enough to hold him for as long as he needed held and only when he felt ready did she begin to pull back. Her heart was in her throat, the pain in her head subsiding with each second Nicky clung to her, only to be vanquished entirely by his next words: “Te amo, melliza. Está bien.”

“Nicholas River Harkness,” she said slowly, deliberately, wanting him to understand her completely. She pulled back and Nicky’s brows knit together as if he were afraid he were in trouble. But Rio just wanted to say his full name, wanted to speak aloud the pieces of him that were Agatha and the tiny piece of him that was her.

“I love you too. Very much. And I am so proud of you for being so brave. I promise I’ll keep you safe. You and your mama.”

Nicky nodded slowly and took an audible breath in before he said: “Sí. Entiendo. Lo sé.”

Rio didn’t have to force herself to smile. Nicky looked worried still, his eyes ever-wide, but his lips trembled into a half-smile too and she kissed his cheek as a seal of their agreement.

Rio loved him. She’d keep him safe.

She hurried him then, grabbing his bag and her own. They made their way to the front door together and Rio found that the closer they got, the closer Nicky got. But she held his hand firmly, and with her non-dominant hand she found the keys Agatha had left her.

She fumbled in her haste but she managed it.

She let them in, she expected Nicky to go ahead but he stayed back. So she stepped inside first.

The house smelled different, unlike Agatha’s actual home. It hadn’t been lived in by her yet so Rio didn’t know why she was expecting to have Agatha’s stamp all over it. But then she turned her head and on the console table where she placed her keys was a framed photograph of Agatha and Nicky.

And in front of it, lay a light blue origami flower.

Rio swallowed, knowing Agatha had left it for her.

But Nicky hadn’t moved yet and she knew he was waiting for her to do so. She looked up, looked into the quiet house. They needed to call Agatha to let her know what had happened but that they were safe but first Rio needed to make sure they were.

She shouldered Nicky’s backpack and walked him through to find the living room and found it to be open, airy, a pretty space with prettier furnishings. Money couldn’t buy taste but Agatha had both in droves.

They didn’t stop there. She took them instead deeper into the house, passing a guest bathroom, the chef’s kitchen, and through again until she found a smaller family room. It was decorated just as well as the first lounge but was cosier, and she felt safer already.

She placed Nicky’s backpack down by the coffee table and settled with him close beside her on the couch. But something still didn’t feel right.

She stood and Nicky stood too. She’d turned to tell him to wait on the couch but saw his face and said nothing.

Safety was paramount but reassurance was a close second. A very close second judging by the fact that Nicky had been silent since they’d stepped into the house and was still clutching her hand.

So she walked with him round each room of the lower floor of the house and with his help she closed every blind and every drape. No one would see in. No human eyes, no long lens, no flying drone.

They’d be safe.

Only then did she take Nicky back to the couch. Only then did she offer him a drink or some snacks.

He refused both and was soon crawling into her lap.

There, in the dark house high up in the hills of Hollywood, Rio Vidal sat with her frightened mellizo. Nicky was in her lap, his arms around her neck, his head resting against her shoulder. She held him close, held him securely, his little knees pointing up to the sky and tucked in against her side.

He was safe now. No one knew where they were. No one could see in.
She leant over when Nicky was comfortable and with the tips of her fingers managed to grab the strap of her cross-body black bag. She pulled it onto the couch with them and fished out her cell.

When the screen lit she saw that she had the usual number of texts and calls but none from Agatha or Jen. Good. Nothing had happened on their end.

Only five texts from Alice appeared and one missed call.

She didn’t check them.

She instead pressed to dial Agatha and held the phone to her ear. Nicky shuffled a bit to sit up more.

Agatha answered after one ring.

“Rio,” she said her name on an inhale and Rio could feel the worry in her voice.

“We’re safe,” she reassured quickly, needing Agatha to know that at least. “We’re at the house. Nicky is right here with me.”

“What’s happened?” Agatha knew. Of course she did. Why else would Rio, a woman who never picked up her phone, choose to pick up her phone to call Agatha when she knew she was busy.

She took a breath, felt Nicky tangle his fingers in her hair.

“Your mother was at the house. We’re fine, we-…”

“Put Nicky on.”

Rio blinked. It wasn’t usual for Agatha to dismiss her like that. Something settled in her stomach as she passed the phone to Nicky and whispered: “Your mama.”

Perhaps Agatha was mad. Perhaps she was done with her. Perhaps…

But Nicky had begun to speak a mile a minute and she realised what it was instantly. Rio would tell half-truths, seeking to inform but to placate, to soften. Nicky would tell the whole truth, unencumbered by the burden of guilt, not frightened of what Agatha might say to him, simply determined to get her here sooner.

“Mama, she was just in the house and she tried to get me to stay with her but I didn’t want to and Rio wouldn’t let her and, and,” he took two sharp breaths and Rio kissed his temple. “And Rio got me to the stairs but she kept coming and was saying bad things to Rio and, and I went up the stairs but then she pushed Rio but Rio told me to go so I ran I ran so fast and I got my bag and Scratchy and came back down and Rio was waiting for me and then grandmother grabbed my ear and Rio shouted at her and then we kept going even as she kept shouting at us to stop but then then she grabbed Rio and and she’s bleeding mama she hurt her arm but she wouldn’t let go but I tried to make her and and she called her she she called her a dog then we got away and we drove we drove up to here and we’ve closed all the blinds so it’s just us and we want you with us please come please come now we want you mama I want you here please don’t go home please don’t go home.”

Nicky was crying again and Rio waited with bated breath to hear what Agatha would say on the other end of the line. She pulled Nicky close, cradled his head, covering the ear that had been grabbed by Evanora with her hand. Agatha’s voice was faded, and Ro knew she’d be moving already, would have wrapped up the meeting with a simple look to Jen and would be on her way.

“I’m coming, honey. You stay right there with Rio. She’ll keep you so safe. I love you, I’m coming. Pass the phone back to Rio, honey.”

Nicky did as he was told and buried back in against her. Rio took a deep breath before she placed the phone to her ear and as soon as she had she heard Agatha’s sharp voice: “You’re hurt.”

“I’m fine.”

“That isn’t what Nicky said. What did she-…”

Rio shook her head and held Nicky that bit tighter, feeling him silent cry into her shirt. “Just get back as quickly as you can.”

“He said you were bleeding.”

“It’s healed. I promise I’m okay.”

In the background she heard Jen’s voice and Alice’s name being spoken. Agatha said nothing for a second and then whispered, “He’s okay?”

“He’s okay.”

“You’re okay?”

“I’m okay.”

“Tell me what she said.”

Rio shook her head silently again, unable to even think the words she’d said, let alone repeat them with Nicky close.

“No. Come back, drive safe. We’ll see you soon.”

“Rio,” Agatha insisted but Rio could barely stand to hear her voice and not see her face. She closed her eyes, felt Nicky shuffle up until he could lean in and speak to his mama too.

“Mama hurry please. Please hurry.”

She heard Agatha’s breath, heard her struggle with it. Then: “I’m coming. I’ll be there soon. Don’t worry, honey. I’m coming.”

“Drive safe,” Rio whispered and before Agatha could say anything else, she hung up.

Nicky hugged her again and Rio held him through it, wondering what he was feeling and whether Agatha had ever been more scared or angry in her life. She didn’t think so, assumed she must be on the verge of erupting.

It would come. She knew it would. It was just whether it was directed solely at Evanora or whether Rio would be burned by the flames.

Nicky eventually settled down against her again and Rio felt like she could breathe with him close but felt pain with every breath.

What if Agatha realised she was incompetent. What is she found her to be all those things she’d accused her of being: not ready, a child, immature.

She sighed quietly and closed her eyes as she rested back into the cushions.

Her headache was knocking again.

They just had to wait for Agatha.

Rio just had to wait to see how long it would be before Nicky was ripped away from her and Agatha broke it all off.

As they sat there in the near-darkness, Nicky was quieter than she’d ever known him to be. He just held on, toyed with the ends of her hair. It took her back to having him against her when Agatha had been asleep and Nicky had been attempting to fool her into thinking he was.

Only no one was fooling anyone anymore. Everything was out in the open, raw and bloody like the untreated wounds on Rio’s wrist and forearm.

As time ticked on she checked in on Nicky every so often, making sure he knew he was safe, that his mama was still coming, that she was still here. Every soft utterance in Spanish was met with a gentle head nod from the boy but he made no sound.

By the time Rio heard the front door being opened, she’d petrified around the little boy. Her bones had cemented in their position, her muscles frozen in their protective hold. After all, she had Agatha’s heart in her lap. He was safe in her arms. She had to keep him safe, had to keep him protected, and so she didn’t move. Even when everything ached, even when she had to fight the urge to fidget, to stretch, to tear the paint from the walls with her fingernails just to feel try to rid her body of the anger she felt.

She remained still. She held Nicky, protected Agatha’s heart.

By her reckoning it had been close to forty minutes before there was noise again in the silent house. No more than an hour. No less than thirty.

She heard frantic footsteps and Jen’s voice shouting Agatha’s name.

And then.

There she was. Standing in the entrance to the dark family room Rio had holed them up in. At some point in the day she must have shed her blazer because it was no longer on her tense frame. She was wearing her glasses, her hair twice the volume it had been when she’d left that morning, evidence of her hysteria, evidence of her fear.

Agatha’s cheeks were pale beneath the large-frames but creeping down her neck and across what could be seen of her chest through her white shirt, Agatha was flushed. Her sleeves were rolled up and Rio knew it must have been a nervous impulse, something to do as she shouted at Jen to drive faster, for more gas! More gas!

And her eyes, her eyes were what she focused on next, what she couldn’t look away from. Storms of terror were raging in them.

Agatha was drowning even as she stood on solid ground.

Rio’s frozen hold on Nicky broke open as he struggled from her lap and flew across the space to get to his mama. Rio watched as he tried to climb up her, as Agatha bent to catch him, as she struggled to lift the desperate child into the air.

Rio couldn’t move. She could no longer look.

Chapter End Notes

Hope she was worth the wait

Chapter 46: Vaqueros

Chapter Summary

Some wounds are healed.

New ones are formed.

Chapter Notes

This is LONG apologies in advance

Props to Gilly for her Spanish tutoring

I rushed to get this done to celebrate KH at the BAFTAs

See the end of the chapter for more notes

The air in the dark room was still. The only thing moving it were Agatha’s gentle reassurances to her son. Even Nicky was silent bar the soft, desperate noises of a little boy trying to cling to his mama.

He looked younger than his years.

Not that Rio had eyes to see.

She kept her head down. Kept her eyes closed. A childhood habit showing itself in adulthood. If she couldn’t see anyone, no one could see her.

“Did she follow?” Jen.

“No,” Rio managed, more a noise than a word.

“Rio.” Agatha.

Rio didn’t look up but gulped, feeling fear block her airway. Her body was tense, readying itself for the fatal blow that was surely about to be delivered.

Leave. Never come back. Stay away from me and stay away from my son.

But that isn’t what Agatha said. Instead:

“Rio. Please, my love.”

The words were gasped. An entreatment thick with pain.

Rio looked. She saw Agatha crouching on the floor now with Nicky still clutching desperately to her. They both looked small. They both looked unlike themselves and yet Rio thought she’d never seen them so like themselves. Agatha was beseeching. Nicky was vulnerable.

Agatha was holding him with one arm, her left flung out to Rio.

And as Rio looked she realised she’d seen Agatha like this before. But not for weeks.

Not since Berkeley.

She shut her mind off from the memory.

Her body took over. Previously stiff and tight from holding Nicky as securely as she had been, she now moved as if she’d been thrown to Agatha by some invisible force.

She landed against them, around them, on them, and was able to breathe suddenly. It felt like Agatha was able to now too. She heard her take in a sharp breath and felt the press of her face in against her cheek.

Someone was crying. Maybe all of them.

But it was wet and hot and Rio just clung on, squashing Nicky between them, making sure he knew they were there, that they wouldn’t let go.

Agatha’s nails were scratching at the base of Rio’s neck. But they weren’t intent on harm like Evanora’s had been. They were intent on keeping her close, and holding her so she wouldn’t ever leave.

And Rio gasped a promise as she held the two closer that she never would.

Seconds, minutes, hours, lifetimes later, a hand found her head and only then did she look up to find Jen standing above them, her face crumpled under the weight of her own fears. Her touch was gentle and Rio wondered if Jen had ever even touched her before. Certainly not like this. Never like this.

“Alice is on her way. Can you tell us what happened?”

Rio sniffed quietly and felt Agatha and Nicky shift so she pulled back and rested against her ankles. Her hold slowly dropped and her eyes drifted back round to Agatha now checking her son over, holding his cheeks and sniffing through the tears as Rio found her voice again.

“We went to get Nicky’s bag. She was there. She-…”

“Mama,” Nicky. He sniffed, his body moving with every breath he took, jerking with every hiccup that came after every second word.

“S-She hurt Rio. She called her-…” Nicky sniffed again and turned in Agatha’s hold to look up at Rio, hoping she’d help him. Hoping she’d use the words he didn’t really understand and didn’t really want to use.

But Rio swooped in instead of finishing his sentence. She kissed his warm, damp cheek and murmured as he grabbed her shirt to tie himself to her again. “Estoy bien, cariño.” I’m okay, sweetheart.

Nicky shuddered a breath and Agatha asked: “You’re hurt?”

“Just my arm. It’s nothing.”

But Agatha was reaching now, had grabbed her arm, she’d guessed the right one and turned it to see the damage her mother had done. Red, angry talon marks winked up at her and Rio grimaced for the sight of them and for the reaction they would surely encourage.

Silence filled the dark room once again, only broken by Nicky’s soft sniffs as he clung between his mom and his melliza. Rio looked across the bridge between them to see Agatha’s face and saw in it only fury. White hot, burning fury.

Before anyone could do anything Agatha had scrambled to her feet, leaving Nicky on the floor with Rio. Nicky turned to her fully because his mom was no longer available.

“Agatha!” Jen.

“I’m going to kill her. I’m going to-!”

“Mama!”

In the second it took Agatha to begin her eruption, Nicky had stood up. He’d turned from Rio, his fists at his sides. He blocked her view of Agatha as she’d stopped in her tracks and was turning around to see her son.

“No! You need to be here! With us! Tres,” he hiccuped, “patitos!” An infinitesimal pause. “And auntie Jen!”

Jen pursed her lips in Nicky’s direction.

Rio leant up on her knees and wrapped her arms around Nicky’s middle, acting as a lean-to for support as Agatha stared, wide-eyed and unblinking across at them. She took a second, her fingers twitching at her sides as her eyes shed more tears.

“Nicky.”

“No! No!” Nicky stomped his foot, making Rio jolt a little as she held him. “You haven’t even-… you haven’t even-…” Agatha stepped closer and Rio saw how afraid she was. Maybe Nicky did too because his little hands that had been fists had moved to Rio’s arms and he took two deep breaths before she said: “Mama you need to kiss Rio better. You need to fix what grandmother did and you need to-… you need to-…”

Agatha flew back over and Rio released Nicky to let him go to his mom. She watched as they embraced until Jen was in front of her again, crouching now in her immaculate suit. She placed a hand on Rio’s shoulder.

Rio slowly looked around at her.

“You okay, Vidal? You look a little… You able to tell me everything that happened? She’s alive, right? You didn’t kill the bitch?”

Rio shook her head just once. Jen sighed.

“Shame. Tell me.”

“Jen.”

Agatha’s voice was croaky, rough. As if she’d been screaming for hours when in reality she’d barely said anything. Rio looked up as Agatha raised to her feet and saw Nicky turn with his deep frown as she held him to her.

“Will you sit with Nicky? I need to check Rio’s arm.”

“I’m fine.”

“I’m not asking.”

Rio’s answer was for her to stand and Agatha bent to kiss Nicky’s cheek, whispering something in his ear that made him reach out for Jen. Jen took his hand and, glancing at Rio, she walked around her with the little boy to go and sit on the couch.

Agatha hadn’t moved yet and Rio wasn’t sure she knew how to anymore. Agatha was no less furious, that was obvious. Her eyes were wild with unrestrained anger, but when she moved closer, as she brushed her fingers along the outside of Rio’s injured arm, she was tender rather than threatening.

“May I?”

Rio gasped a soft breath of surprise at Agatha asking when she said she wasn’t, she wouldn’t. But she nodded and Agatha danced her fingers down her arm until they were back in their place, holding Rio’s hand. They looked at each other and Rio had never felt longing like it.

Agatha broke the spell first and began to tug Rio through to the kitchen. She wasn’t rushing them and Rio realised that she was trying to be gentle. Out of sight of Jen or Nicky, Agatha turned her and pressed her back against the counter. She’d dropped her hand, placed her hands on her hips.

Gentle. Tender. Soft.

They simply breathed together for a while until Rio was able to raise her hands up to make Agatha look at her. Agatha was fighting the raging inferno inside of her, Rio knew that. She knew the measured softness was guarding something much more fearsome.

She’d briefly let it show until Nicky had tempered it.

It couldn’t be contained forever but for now it could be reassured. Her son could reassure her. Rio could reassure her.

“Nicky’s safe. You’re safe.” She brushed her thumbs across Agatha’s pale cheeks, and took a breath before she whispered, “I’m sorry I-…”

“What did she say to you?”

There it was, bubbling below the surface. Agatha’s fingers flexed slightly against her hips and Rio took a second before she said: “It doesn’t matter. Nothing good.”

Agatha shook her head, “No. It matters to me. It matters. Tell me what she said.”

Rio swallowed and Agatha looked down to her lips. In the fraction of time it took her to do that, the air around them changed and Agatha was no longer demanding answers. She’d leant in to kiss Rio instead and Rio’s world flipped.

Agatha wasn’t being gentle anymore. Her fury was hungry now, desperate to devour. And Rio let it. She was a willing sacrifice to the rage inside of Agatha Harkness.

Agatha’s hands were in her hair and she was tugging at it. Her fingers were woven into the short length, grasping, tugging, controlling. Rio was simply a puppet and Agatha was moving the strings.

A moan was ripped from Rio’s mouth.

And then Agatha stopped it. And then she pulled back and away and tore herself from Rio, as panting and as desperate as she was.

Agatha’s back was to her now, her hands in her own hair again, her head up to the sky. Rio let her stand in it, let her work through it as her tongue tasted Agatha along her lower lip.

Slowly, steadily, Agatha soon turned back around and she was gentler again, her fires hidden once more.

They just looked at each other for a while until Agatha was moving again, but not towards Rio. She was reaching into cupboards in search of something. She was moving quickly, frantically.

She flicked a light switch and the under counter lighting came on, aiding her quest.

Rio just watched as Agatha soon found what she was looking for, a first aid kit in a little green medical bag emblazoned with a plus. Arriving back to Rio’s side she began to search for the wound cleaning wipes, the disinfectant, the gauze or bandaids she needed.

“Mi vida,” Rio whispered quietly, turning her body to face Agatha’s. “I’m okay.”

She placed her hand on Agatha’s upper back, rubbing her there in soothing circles to try and bring her back to herself.

But it was clear Agatha was too far gone.

“Did she hurt you anywhere else?”

“No.”

“Nicky said she pushed you.”

“I lost my balance. I caught myself.”

Agatha nodded slowly and turned then, looking at Rio for just a moment before she was again gentle in taking her arm and applying the antiseptic wipes. It stung more than Rio cared to admit. But Agatha caught her grimace and kissed her palm in apology.

“Tell me,” she whispered as she soothed over Rio’s burning skin with her lips, pressing them to the inch above where the cuts began. “Tell me.”

“It won’t help.”

Agatha turned to look at her and Rio frowned at the sight. Her fury was still there, just dormant. Just waiting. But she looked small somehow. Helpless.

So Rio gave in.

“She told me to stay away from you and Nicky. Told me I had a sickness and I had infected you and I wouldn’t be allowed to infect her grandson too.”

Agatha’s eyes closed and Rio wished she could take back what she’d said but it was too late. She had to see the words wash over Agatha, had to witness them take hold of her head and her heart and then… she opened her eyes again.

“She’s going to try and take him.”

“Mi vida.”

“She’ll try to take him from me. It won’t be Ralph. It’ll be my mother. Encouraging him. Funding him.”

Rio stepped closer and Agatha let her. She pulled Agatha to her and Agatha only protested with a soft, “your arm”, but gave up all the same. Rio found her lips with her own, found her cheek, her crown, her jaw, her throat. She pressed a final kiss the slither of exposed skin at her chest and heard Agatha intake a sharp breath as she did.

She moved back up, kissed her again and whispered, “You will never let that happen. I will never let that happen.”

“Promise me,” Agatha whispered right back, her hold tightening around Rio, “Promise me you won’t give up on us. Even when it gets hard. Even when… please don’t.”

“Give up tres patitos?”

Rio smiled, not because she felt like it, but because she had to. Everyone knows comedy is harder.

She smiled against Agatha’s cheek, pressing in, feeling her glasses dig into the bridge of her nose. “Para siempre, mi vida. Hasta el infinito.”

Agatha turned into her, and Rio pulled back only so she could, only so Agatha could look at her properly, only so she could see how much she meant it.

“I’m sorry about my mother. I’m sorry I wasn’t there to-…”

“I’m glad you weren’t. If you’d have been there and she’d said anything to you I’d have killed her. I was already close. You’d have made sure I did.”

Agatha smiled weakly and Rio took the opportunity to kiss her again. Something about the fear of never being able to kiss Agatha had made her suddenly delirious with the knowledge that she could.

But then. Her desire could be outweighed by only one thing: guilt. Like the good, lapsed Catholic she was.

“There’s something else you should know. Before we got to the house someone had approached Nicky at the park. A woman. She’d lied about being a friend and-…”

“A journalist?”

“She said no.”

“What happened?”

Agatha hadn’t dropped her hold on Rio and that gave her the strength to not fear the worst. “I went to get water from my bag on the bleachers and I turned and she was there with him.”

She could see the fury sparking again, churning its desire to erupt. But Agatha was silent, waiting for her to continue. Her hold didn’t falter so Rio didn’t either.

Agatha wasn’t screaming, she wasn’t pulling away, she wasn’t pushing Rio away. She was just watching, just waiting. Just breathing in and out slowly, her breath tickling Rio’s lips.

Rio swallowed and continued.

“I went back over, took Nicky away, drove him to your house and-…”

“Okay,” Agatha said, barely a whisper, “okay, okay.”

But Rio had to ask, she had to know.

“You’re not mad? You’re not-…” Agatha had released her hold, moving her left hand, her middle finger, to trace Rio’s brow, brushing back her hair from her face and tucking it behind her ear. “You’re not going to-…?”

Rio sighed as Agatha’s fingers moved to trace across her cheekbone, her lashes fluttered and her eyes closed into the touch.

“You protected my son.” Agatha turned, held Rio’s wrist in the air, she kissed each of the claw marks and when she was done she whispered against her skin. “Por siempre, mi amor. Nuestra protectora, nuestro ángel.”

Agatha repeated her journey along Rio’s wrist, sealing each cut with another kiss. It was more healing to Rio than any medicine. A final, lingering kiss was pressed to the centre of her palm and Rio leant closer, shifting her weight onto the balls of her feet. And Agatha turned then, leaning up where Rio leant down. She kissed her softly, their lips meeting at the very last moment, Rio’s curling around Agatha’s upper one.

Releasing a soft noise of surprise, Rio moved her hands to clutch at Agatha’s collar, holding her tight against her. Agatha cradled her face and Rio kissed her so hard that Agatha stumbled backwards.

But Rio followed. Her tongue encouraged Agatha’s, her hands clutched, her heart hammered. She kept kissing her until a voice shocked her into releasing.

Alice.

“Are you fucking kidding me?”

Rio broke away first, gasping from shock and lack of air. “Fuck. Alice.”

“I knew this was a stupid fucking idea. Rio. What if Nicky had walked in?!”

But Rio was distracted by Agatha who’d become the fury she had been moments ago. Rio could already feel her raising up to her full height, her body tense. As she moved to stand before her, Rio grabbed her arm and pulled her to her, holding her back against her as Alice scowled but said nothing more.

Thankfully Agatha remained silent too. But she was no longer trying to be calm, she felt coiled to pounce as Rio said: “We’ll be out in a sec. I promise, Alice. Just one sec.”

“Nicky said you’re hurt.”

Rio cleared her throat quietly and nodded just once. “Just a cut.”

“Four,” Agatha corrected as Alice moved closer, apparently her concern for Rio outweighing her fear of her girlfriend.

Agatha relaxed ever so slightly and Rio released her hold on her as Alice arrived by their sides.

She reached for Rio’s arm and released a quiet breath when she saw what Evanora had done.

“Oh, Rio.”

“It’s fine, it’s just cuts.”

“It’s not fine,” Agatha corrected as Alice looked up to her best friend with a wide-eyed gaze.

“Are those… Nail marks, Rio?”

Rio huffed and watched as Alice lay her fingers out to measure against the wounds. They were small, angry and red where they’d bled but everyone was reacting like Evanora had cut her arm clean off.

“She held on tight. I-…”

“Let her?”

Rio bristled at the accusation and Alice just shook her head, just knew Rio too well to say anything else. Agatha shifted on the spot and curled her fingers around the underside of Rio’s elbow.

“I need to clean them.”

Alice knew she was being dismissed but she waited a second, looking up at her friend.

“She’ll pick the scabs.” Rio resented the implication, felt a strange betrayal in Alice’s words. “She’ll remove the bandaids and-…”

“Alice.”

“I’ll replace them every hour if I have to.”

Rio looked at Agatha and was about to protest but saw something she’d not seen before. A look of mutual understanding was passing between her girlfriend and her best friend. She watched as Alice nodded, as Agatha’s head inclined ever so slightly in return.

They were bonding, she realised with a jolt of surprise, over looking after her. Over knowing Rio wouldn’t want to be looked after. It was as mortifying as it was a relief.

Finally, something to bond over: Rio being a pain in the ass.

Alice then looked to Rio, her fingers grazing her hand briefly before she turned to leave. Rio sighed as she ducked her head down to kiss Agatha’s shoulder. She nuzzled in the spot she’d kissed and for a second everything was just Agatha and nothing else.

“How did she do it?”

Rio cleared her throat as the spell was broken. She straightened up to allow Agatha to turn around. But Agatha didn’t stop there, she moved back to the counter and turned Rio with her. Rio watched quietly for a while as she took out another wipe and it wasn’t until it made contact with her wounds and she hissed at the pain that she gave in.

“She grabbed at me as I was trying to leave with Nicky. She wouldn’t let go. But I didn’t,” she grimaced as Agatha brushed over her wounds again with the wipe. Agatha kissed the apex of her wrist but didn’t stop what she was doing for more than it took to kiss her.

“I didn’t show her it hurt. I didn’t want Nicky to know. He tried,” she swallowed and watched as Agatha debated between gauze and bandaids. “He tried to pull me away. He was so brave, Agatha. He was-…”

“Please don’t call me that.”

Agatha had settled for bandaids. They were plain, beige, and stood out against Rio’s skin. She lay the first.

“Not when we’re alone. Not when, not when you can call me…” Agatha looked up from where she’d been picking up the next one, “Not today.”

Rio nodded slowly, moving her free hand to touch Agatha’s cheek then moving it down to rub over her arm. “Mi vida, mi corazón, mi todo.”

Agatha placed the third bandaid on her arm. They were all at strange angles, all ugly reminders of the devil who had birthed Agatha Harkness. Rio bit the inside of her cheek, and Agatha kept her gaze down, focused on peeling the plastic off the next bandaid.

Rio wanted to say more, wanted to apologise again for where she felt she’d failed, but the only thing she could think to say was the thing she felt Agatha needed to hear more than anything.

“You’re nothing like her.”

Agatha paused what she was doing, frozen in place.

“I saw it the moment she opened the door. You couldn’t be more different. I want you to believe that because I don’t think you do.”

Agatha became reanimated again and with the same soft hands she placed down the final bandaid in the place where Evanora’s little finger had pierced her skin. It was the least deep of the small, crescent moon wounds.

She watched as Agatha sighed, as her eyes closed, as she returned her lips to each bandaid And kissed over them. Rio moved closer, slid her free hand along Agatha’s lower back, until she had hold of her opposite hip, until she could squeeze her, pull her closer.

“We should get back to Nicky.” Agatha’s voice was quiet but she knew she was being dismissed, being shut down, just like Alice had been not moments ago. Only Agatha turned into her and kissed her calmly, as if nothing very interesting had happened that day.

When she pulled back Rio couldn’t help but whisper, “I love you.”

Agatha smiled, but there was a sadness in her eyes that hadn’t been there before. Rio didn’t have time to respond to it because Agatha had turned from her. She was tugging her away, holding her hand as she pulled her back towards the family room where her son and friends were.

At the door of the kitchen Agatha stopped her and whispered, “Did Nicky tell you?”

“Tell me what?”

Rio moved and Agatha turned to her, touched her collar, then the sleeve of her shirt. “That he loves you?”

Rio sucked in sharply. It felt like a distant memory already. But she nodded and Agatha smiled absently.

“He was so worried about it.”

Rio looked up and out to the silent, dark house. Nicky and Jen and Alice were somewhere in that dark but the house was so big, so sprawling, that even in the silence they wouldn’t be able to hear.

“He told me.”

Agatha nodded and lifted her injured arm to kiss the back of her hand and Rio wished she could turn them back around to hide away in the kitchen again. But Nicky wasn’t there and they needed to be with the scared little boy.

Besides, Rio was sure Alice would be freaking him out at best, scaring him at worst, just by staring at him, just by thinking he was Rio’s.

“Let’s go see your boy,” Rio said quietly, unwilling to break the spell as she then took charge and pulled Agatha back out towards the family room. They entered together, hand in hand, and in the dim light saw Nicky curled under Jen’s arm on the couch and Alice pacing up and down by the fireplace.

The picture was eerie, seemed surreal. But she was Agatha’s anchor in the surrealist painting before them. She kept hold of Agatha’s hand as she pulled her around to the couch. Nicky looked up first and Jen next. Alice had stopped pacing.

Agatha moved immediately to take Nicky from Jen and Rio saw in Jen’s eyes a flash of hurt when the little boy pulled away without hesitation.

“So,” Jen said, recovering immediately as Rio remained standing. “We need to talk about it,”

“No,” Agatha snapped, Nicky now tucked below her chin, “Not tonight.”

“Nicky told me everything already, Agatha. I need Rio’s version.”

Rio watched as Agatha froze, as Nicky turned his head, as both of them looked over to her. Nicky reached his arm out to her and Rio went to meet it, taking his hand before she fell onto the couch beside him and found he immediately shuffled to sit more fully between her and Agatha.

He hadn’t said anything yet and Jen took it upon herself to continue: “Any day now, really. No rush!”

Nicky shuffled in his spot and Rio squeezed his hand.

“I’m sure whatever Nicky told you is-…”

“This bitch with the red hair,” Rio stiffened, felt Nicky squeeze her hand too, felt him shuffle a little. On the other side of him Agatha cleared her throat.

“What about her?” Rio glanced at Agatha and saw that she was staring at her hand that held Nicky’s.

“Who the fuck was she? This bitch with a Celtics pin and-…?”

“What?” Rio felt her whole body shift to the edge of the couch. Nicky followed her, scrambling to keep her close. She felt Agatha’s hand fly to her back.

“Nicky said,” Jen motioned to Nicky, her eyes wide. But Rio turned to Nicky before Jen could finish and he looked confused and then incredibly serious.

“You saw it,” he reminded quietly, and Agatha moved closer. “She had a pin on her shirt. A badge. A Celtics pin.”

Rio stared at Nicky’s deep frown which framed his wide eyes. And Rio thought back to the moment of panic and fear in the park. She hadn’t checked the woman over, she hadn’t looked past the smug smirk and red hair.

But she believed Nicky. A Celtics pin would have helped her get close to him, helped him to trust her.

She looked up to Agatha and knew she was thinking exactly the same. Agatha moved closer then, her hand falling from Rio so her arms could instead hold Nicky to her.

Jen spoke before anyone else did. “I’ve called the security firm. The guy’s on his way.”

“Complete discretion?” Agatha asked. The fury was seeping through and Rio couldn’t blame her, was feeling a lot of it for herself.

“Total,” Jen responded firmly. She’d now taken up Alice’s spot by the fire and was pacing.

“Twenty four seven. No one will get near. No one will have the opportunity to get near. He’ll be with him at school, by the house, anywhere you go.”

“Agatha too,” Rio interjected, distracted briefly when she felt Nicky’s curious fingers touching the sides of her bandaids.

“Obviously,” Jen said, “Both of them. Especially with creeps out there on Evanora’s dime.”

“What?”

“Catch up, Vidal. Sometimes two plus two equals a bitch.”

Rio adjusted herself on the couch, torn between standing and she didn’t know what. Nicky’s hand curled around her arm, careful not to touch where she’d been hurt. She remained seated.

“I don’t understand.”

“Rio,” Alice this time, quietly standing by the fireplace, her eyes flicking between Jen and her best friend. “Jen cree que podría haber intentado secuestrarlo.” Jen thinks she might have tried to kidnap him.

Rio stood then but had nowhere to go and it was Agatha who spoke now, and Nicky who reached for her hand.

“Rio.”

Rio just stared across at Alice, still trying to process her words. Alice shook her head and Nicky squeezed her hand.

“I need to go back to the house.”

A chorus responded to her words, all the responses were different but the intent was the same. And one voice sounded above them all, emanating from the littlest person.

“No.” / “Absolutely not.” / “Rio.” / “Melliza no!”

Agatha stood up and Nicky did too, and she found two sets of hands on her, one at her sides, clutching her shirt, the other on her shoulders, holding her so she couldn’t move. Agatha looked close to boiling point, her eyes boring into Rio’s.

“You need to stay. You cannot go anywhere near her. I won’t allow it.”

“I’m not asking you to allow it.”

Nicky held on tighter, Rio could feel his fists in her shirt, matching the tightness of Agatha’s hold against her shoulders. Agatha was seconds from snapping, she could feel the tension, see her ability to keep herself calm evaporating with the heat of her gaze.

“No one is going anywhere near Evanora. From now on everyone does as I say. Me and Alice.”

“You’re not in charge here.” Agatha, still staring at Rio, but speaking to Jen. She pressed down but Rio fought it, and as gently as she could she removed Nicky from her and ripped herself away from Agatha. As she stepped away Agatha grabbed her back, snatching her arm. The moment her fingers wrapped around her right arm Rio gasped in pain and Agatha released her immediately.

That was when Agatha lost it.

She screamed out everything she’d been holding back from the moment she’d answered Rio’s call. No words left her lips, only noise, only pain. She threw her arms in the air. She ripped her glasses from her face and, in throwing them, they shattered against the wall.

The two managers in the room went to their respective clients. Alice found Rio to be tense but immovable when she placed her hands on her arms, careful to avoid her injured forearm that now stung again.

Jen, however, couldn’t now get a hold on a crashing out Agatha.

Nicky had dropped his hold on Rio, had turned around. He just stood, toying with his fingers, his eyes wide and on his mom.

“Agatha! Will you behave like a-…!”

“Do not tell me what to do!”

Rio made to move but Alice held her still and Nicky whispered his name for her which made her stop, her gaze falling to his panicked face as he’d turned back around.

Agatha was on the other side of the room, pulling her hair up into a bun, the flush on her chest now creeping up her neck, spreading itself over her cheeks as she paced like a predator debating on her next prey.

“Agatha.”

“Mellizo.”

Nicky squeezed in between Rio and Alice, and Alice stepped back to give him more space as Rio placed her hands on his shoulders. He was tense too, his right ear pressed against Rio’s front, his left hand against his left. He was trying to block the shouts using Rio’s body to help, trusting she could comfort when his mama was lost to her panic.

Rio placed her hand over his own on his ear and Nicky tilted his head all the way back as he looked up at her.

Rio moved her other hand to his head, her fingers threading through the hair she knew he was so desperate to grow. It was a reminder. A reminder of what Agatha’s mother had done to him, a reminder of the years of torment, of the abuse she’d lavished on Agatha. She was as angry as Agatha was. But Nicky needed her not to be. Agatha had to get this out. She had to experience the crash before she could accept the healing.

So Rio tempered her own furies as best she could and she bent down, she kissed Nicky’s forehead, and then whispered to him: “Go with Alice, show her your bedroom, mellizo. She’ll keep you safe. Take Scratchy.”

“No, melliza, no.”

Agatha was yelling across the room, Jen infrequently yelling back: “I said to you! I have been telling you!” / “Agatha, please!”

“Baby,” Rio was frowning now, crouching slowly before Nicky, “Do you trust me?”

Nicky couldn’t know that her question made her feel sick because the answer could either absolve her of her presumed sins or crush her completely. But he answered immediately, answered with the surety of a boy who never for a second felt unsafe with his melliza.

“Yes.”

Rio breathed out, her hold on his arms flexing a little, “Then I need you to go with Alice and I’ll come and get you soon, okay?”

Nicky’s lip trembled and Rio moved her hands to his cheeks as Alice moved beside them and held out the little toy that had been abandoned on the couch.

“You, me, and this little guy?”

Rio glanced at her friend, her lips forming a sad but grateful smile. She knew Alice wouldn’t want to leave the situation unfolding between Agatha and Jen but between them Rio had the best chance of calming it.

“Melliza,” Nicky uttered, his eyes somehow rounder that they’d ever been, his lip still trembling, “I don’t want to leave you. I want, I want tres patitos.”

“I know, baby. I won’t be long, I promise. Please go with Alice. And soon it’ll be just us, just tres patitos.”

“Do not tell me what to do with my son!”

Agatha’s screaming made Nicky turn his head towards her but Rio turned him gently back, making him focus on her. He gripped her shirt sleeves.

“Tres patitos,” she reassured gently, rubbing his cheeks soothingly with her thumbs.

Rio’s heart was hammering so loudly in her ears, Agatha and Jen going at it so aggressively that she almost didn’t hear Nicky’s words, though he was close, though he was so close she could count his lashes.

“Tres patitos.”

Rio nodded, forced another smile. Nicky dropped his gaze to the toy being held out to him still by Alice and he took Scratchy gently into his arms, petting him as if he were a real rabbit. Rio did the same and brushed over one of his ears.

And then Alice moved in and hurried Nicky away, shooting Rio a quick glance as she did. Rio’s stomach was in her throat as she watched them leave and saw Nicky looking back at his mom now pointing at Jen and continuing to yell.

It wasn’t a pretty sight.

When Nicky was gone Rio looked back over too and tuned herself into the shouting.

Agatha was practically foaming at the mouth. All of her fear and hatred was boiling over, feeding the vicious words she was screaming at Jennifer. Jen just took it, just screamed back, kept trying to get a hand on Agatha’s wildly gesticulating arms.

“Jesus would you just-…!”

“Tell me to calm down one more time and I’ll scream!”

Rio stood up, already taking quick strides over.

“Oh really?! I’m so confused as to what you’re CURRENTLY DOING?!”

She got there just in time. Agatha had made to grab at Jen but instead her body collided with Rio’s and she was walked back a few paces. The great Agatha Harkness was suddenly the great and terrible.

As she clung to Rio her teeth were bared, her hands forming claws. She looked, and was, beyond reason.

Rio was beyond doubt that she wouldn’t calm down any time soon.

“I told you she’d try to take him from me! I TOLD YOU!”

“Mi vida,” Rio insisted, forcing Agatha two more steps back when she felt Jen approach from behind. “He can hear you. He can hear what you’re-…”

“And she didn’t! He is safe! He is-…!”

“JEN!” Rio yelled, releasing her hold on Agatha and whipping around as Jen got even closer. She locked eyes with her and Jen, at least, was reachable. Jen she could tame.

Agatha marched away from the tow of them, storming towards the fireplace. She held herself there, gripping the mantle piece with her pale hands. It could have been a portrait. A portrait of a lady full of fire.

Rio moved cautiously towards her and when she placed her hand on Agatha’s back she felt her flinch. “Querida, try to breathe.”

“How can I breathe when my son isn’t safe?”

“He’s safe here. He’s safe-…”

“Is that why you shut all the windows? Why you closed all the blinds? All the drapes? Why we’re all standing in the dark? Because he’s safe? Because there’s nothing to worry about?”

Agatha had turned her head, and Rio was the one who flinched. Her gaze was fierce still but the longer she looked at Rio the more it softened. She closed her eyes and Rio held her breath. Because Agatha was right.

She didn’t feel safe because Agatha and Nicky weren’t safe.

“Agatha,” Jen said from a few feet away, her voice quieter, the kind of tone you’d use by a sick person’s bedside. “Everything we’re doing we’re doing to keep Nicky safe, to keep him with you. Nothing else matters. We all know that.”

Rio was still not breathing. She simply watched Agatha try to process, try to come to terms with everything that had happened. And only now did Rio realise how hard she’d been trying to be soft earlier, how incredibly difficult she must have found it to be gentle the second she walked through the door.

But it wasn’t acting. Nothing you could win an award for. It was something primal, something instinctual. A mother’s love.

She took a breath because if Agatha couldn’t breathe then she had to be her breath. She stepped closer and Agatha’s eyes opened. Tempests of blue green shone their fury at her but the rest of Agatha’s face was soft. Like Nicky before her, Agatha’s lower lip trembled and Rio moved in to touch it with the pad of her thumb. Agatha grabbed her immediately, fisting the thin fabric of her shirt.

Fire turned to water as Agatha broke down against her and Rio could only hold her through it. She gathered Agatha in and buried her face into her hair.

Elsewhere in the room Jen was now on her phone, checking where they were, what was happening, if news of the divorce had broken.

Rio didn’t know if Jen was waiting for Agatha to calm somewhat but she was silent for a while until she announced:

“TMZ broke it. About ten minutes ago. It’s done. The world knows. It’s started.”

Rio held Agatha tighter after that. Her shirt had absorbed so many tears today. Too many. But she held Agatha firmly against her until she could breathe without sobbing, until she was simply sniffing and hiding.

“I don’t think she’ll try again now it’s out there. She might have known it was coming but surely not today. Surely it was a coincidence.”

Rio glanced across at Jen and saw her clutching her phone, her large eyes full of worry. She knew she didn’t believe it either. Agatha shifted quietly, sniffed her last and turned to Jen too.

Rio could feel her heavy breathing, feel the expansion and contraction of her ribs through her thin shirt. She could feel the fear, knew it wouldn’t disappear until it was made official that she had sole custody.

Which was months away. They’d have to live like this for months.

She felt her take a deep breath, repositioned her hold so Agatha could lean back, standing tall again. Their lower halves were flush and Agatha’s hands slipped below her shirt as she spoke: “Next weekend,” Agatha’s voice was hoarse, broken from all the shouting. “I want you to do as we discussed.”

“Do what?” Rio asked, seeing how Jen nodded silently and began to tap away at her phone.

Agatha turned to her then, her fingers coming to a standstill across her back.

“Take Nicky to Disney. Have the paps ready, make sure we-…”

“He’ll hate that.” The words came before Rio could stop them. She just knew, just knew he would. And the look on Agatha’s face told her that Agatha knew too. Because of course she did. He was her son. She knew better than anyone.

“I know,” she breathed out. “I-…”

“I’ll come with you,” Rio interjected before Agatha could continue. “I can help protect-…”

“You can’t,” Jen’s turn to interrupt this time. “Have you not been listening this whole time?”

Against her, Agatha fell back in, she rested her temple against Rio’s cheek as Rio had turned to Jen.

“It’s to get her positive press. She’s going about as normal with her son. She can’t be seen with resident dyke Rio Vidal in Disney World.”

“Jennifer.”

“Disney Land,” Rio corrected quietly, not that it was important, or the most offensive part of what Jen had just said. Agatha scoffed and Rio felt the breath of it against her jaw. She tightened her hold on her. Agatha moved her hands to her lower back, scraping her nails there back and forth.

“We’ll have security. He’ll be okay. They won’t post his face.”

Rio didn’t know whether Agatha was trying to reassure herself or Rio. But she did know that neither of them were reassured. Agatha’s nailed traced up her back. Rio shivered.

“It’s blowing up,” Jen said from her place on the couch.

Agatha released a breath, and her hands slid back down again until she was pulling away. Rio let her go, watched as she released her hair from its messy bun. It fell across her back.

Her mind was a forest fire, each little piece of her brain set alight with fear, with fury.

Rio went to sit on the loveseat perpendicular to the fireplace.

She put her head in her hands. Agatha was pacing again. Jen was tapping away on her phone.

There was silence for a while and then: “Has he released a statement?”

Rio felt Agatha before she was even touched. A hand nudged her arm and she moved back, lifting her head up to see Agatha standing over her, turned to Jen but seeking Rio’s hand. She held it as Jen responded: “No. He was served whilst out, as expected. His picture’s all over the place. That’s what you fucking get for deciding to file on a fucking Saturday evening, Agatha.”

Rio bit down on her tongue and looked up to Agatha who had stiffened before her.

“It would have blown up either way. Start this again, Jen, and I’ll-…”

“You release the statement! You! File! On! A! Friday! Night! Taking out the trash day! Not a fucking Saturday!”

Rio cleared her throat, watched as Agatha’s jaw flexed, as her eyes darkened.

“You know why I filed late. The paperwork wouldn’t have been-…”

“Because you dragged your fucking heels about it for weeks! You wanted it to be delayed.”

“My son should go to the person I want him to go to!”

Rio felt like there was a huge piece of information being withheld but she didn’t have a chance to ask what was happening.

“You didn’t even fucking ask her! You didn’t even ask. The whole reason you put this off is because you want to make this harder! You think you need to prove that you’re worthy, that your fucking mother-…!”

Rio reacted before Agatha could jump. She wrapped her arms around her middle and tugged her back, forcing them both down into the chair and Agatha into her lap. But Agatha didn’t want to sit down. She was fighting Rio to be released.

So Rio held on tighter.

“You bitch! You CUNT, JENNIFER KALE!”

Rio grimaced as Agatha continued to struggle but she wouldn’t let go. She wouldn’t loosen her hold and Agatha wasn’t giving up.

“How DARE YOU! How DARE YOU!”

“Mi vida,” Rio insisted, gritting her teeth and growling with the effort of hauling Agatha’s back into the cushion of the love seat. The moment it his the cushion Agaha collapsed. She crumpled.

She struggled against it for a second longer, shifting, but barely fighting.

The soft place to land had softened her.

Rio let her breathe for a second and then was able to release her hold and Agatha hid her face in her hands, hiding from Jen and from Rio.

She was panting, breathing heavily, and Rio moved from where she had been trapped beneath her legs, sliding out and unceremoniously moving Agatha in the seat of the chair. She held her side to keep her from falling off the edge and crouched over her, leaning close to where her hands covered her face.

“Mi vida,” she murmured, her nose briefly brushing the back of Agatha’s left hand. But Jen was the one who responded, her volume back to a normal level, her tone clipped but with at least some remorse.

“I just meant,” Rio sighed as she pressed her face in against Agatha’s hand, “I meant that you should have let me take charge. You shouldn’t have delayed. But we’re where we are.”

Rio pressed her lips to Agatha’s hand and then lifted up and found Agatha had grabbed her collar. Blue eyes were watery and Rio was gentle as she pried Agatha’s fingers from her shirt. She turned to look at Jen and Agatha sought out her hand in her lap.

“I want you to apologise.”

“What?”

“Rio.”

Rio shifted where she sat and found that Agatha heaved herself up, sitting sideways in her lap. But she was trying to turn Rio’s head to look at her until she became distracted by her injured arm and lifted that instead, kissing where Rio had hurt herself again in struggling with Agatha.

“Apologise for what you just said. Because why the fuck would Agatha make this harder for herself when-...”

She stopped, choked. She couldn’t make herself finish.

Jen was still looking taken aback but Rio didn’t look away from her. She couldn’t speak anymore but she could still stand her ground, still get Agatha the apology she felt she deserved.

Rio watched Jen open and close her mouth and then, “Agatha. Tell her what you were delaying everything with.”

“Don’t change the-…”

“I was writing my will.”

Agatha interrupted Rio’s attempted to stare an apology out of Jen. She made her pause. She made her stop. She made her turn around.

She looked up and her whole world crashed around her from the look in blue eyes. She was under water suddenly. She couldn’t see. She was drowning. And Agatha’s hands found her cheeks as she choked out: “You’re sick.”

Her throat was constricting. Could it do that? Could it just close? Her watery vision was dissolving into nothing and she went blind. She could no longer feel Agatha’s hold on her. Couldn’t feel the weight of her in her lap. Her whole body was shutting down.

“No,” Agatha breathed, “No no no, I’m not sick. I’m fine. I’m-… Rio. It’s just for the divorce. I just needed a new will to submit, I-… honey.”

Rio gasped, sucked in such a heavy breath that she felt lightheaded with it. Agatha’s thumbs pressed into her cheeks, and Rio blinked until she could see again. And Agatha was there, her eyes were steady, a sea of calm despite everything that had just happened.

“I’m not sick,” she repeated again. And Rio nodded this time.

“You guys are fucking-…”

Agatha’s head snapped around and the softness vanished again. She slipped from Rio’s lap and stood. Rio, now back in her body, slid forwards, and as a precaution she wrapped her left hand around the inside of Agatha’s thigh and reached her right hand to her hip.

“Don’t.”

Agatha had been ready to say something, ready to bark and dive at Jen and maybe it was that she’d just terrified Rio or maybe it was that she was holding her in such a way that if she tried to dive for Jen she’d fall.

“You just need to tone it down, that’s all I’m saying.”

Rio tightened her hold. Nothing mattered anymore. Agatha wasn’t sick. That was all that mattered. She pressed her face in against her hip and Agatha slipped her fingers into her hair.

She thought of her dad.

“This is exactly what I’m saying. It-…”

“Jen.”

Jen sighed but Rio just kept her head in against Agatha, her eyes closed, her breathing slowly returning to normal.

Agatha wasn’t sick.

Her head hurt again. Maybe just the stress of the day. But Agatha’s fingers in her hair, gently scratching her scalp, helped.

“I am trying my best,” Jen said across from them. Rio felt Agatha relax a little and she took deep breaths, trying to calm herself, trying to sink back into her body more fully.

Agatha wasn’t sick.

“I worry you’re going to make this harder than it needs to be.”

“As if it isn’t already the hardest-…”

“I know,” Jen said quietly, and Rio moved then, lifting up to tug Agatha back into the seat with her. Agatha fell without protesting and Rio wrapped her arms snugly around her middle.

Silence. Heavy. It was getting darker now.

Agatha broke it. Rio had her face pressed in against her shoulder.

“I had to choose who Nicky would go to if I died. I had to reaffirm my wishes. My wish was you.”

Rio turned her face upwards and found Agatha had already turned to look down at her. Her calm was gone again, replaced by something much worse than anger. She instead looked anguished, on the verge of something no soothing tone could bring her back from.

“When you say, I’ll post the statement.”

Agatha had turned from Rio, leaving her all alone even as she sat above her. Rio pressed her cheek back in against Agatha’s shoulder, tightened her hold on her. She tried not to imagine a world where Agatha loved and trusted her enough to take her son, but a world that was cruel enough to take Agatha away from her.

She tried not to think about her dad.

“Post it,” Agatha uttered, her hand moving down to find Rio’s. She linked their fingers together. Rio remained silent.

“Okay,” Jen responded, and ten seconds later she said, “It’s up.”

Rio couldn’t find any words to say anymore. The day had drained her.

Agatha soon spoke again.

“Where was he?”

Jen looked up, thought for a second, then said:

“Balthazar.”

Agatha nodded, Rio stared up at her. Her fingers twitched and flexed in her hold.

“Alone?”

“What do you think?”

Rio pulled her closer and Agatha moved her free hand back to run through Rio’s hair.

Rio cleared her throat quietly, absorbing as much comfort as she could get from Agatha’s hold. “A woman?” She knew the answer but had to be sure, had to know more, what the situation was. The inside of her mind felt as dark as the room.

Jen leant over and turned on a lamp. “Yes. Not unusual.”

Agatha took Rio’s hand and lifted it to kiss her wrist. Rio watched her do it, squeezed her where she still held her, felt her lips press over each of her bandaids.
