“They’ll heal,” Rio murmured, seeing the furrow in Agatha’s brow as she returned her lips to her wrist again and lingered there. It made Rio shiver, made her want to cry unexpectedly.

Rio turned her hand in Agatha’s hold, raised it the inch it needed to go to rest across Agatha’s cheek, she was warm, unusually so. Agatha closed her eyes and Rio couldn’t look away.

“Agatha,” Jen called out, a tone that made Rio finally look away from the woman in her lap. “It’s everywhere.”

Agatha was gone before Rio could react. She was up and snatching Jen’s phone away before Rio could even register it. Jen and Rio just watched Agatha react in real time to whatever horror she was witnessing on her manager’s phone.

Then the thunder came.

Nicky, charging down the stairs.

Alice chasing after him, calling his name.

But Nicky didn’t stop until his body collided with Agatha’s and suddenly Jen’s phone was on the floor and Agatha’s attention was on her son, only her son.

Jen grabbed her phone back, huffing about “respect” and Rio looked up to Alice who looked distressed.

“It went quiet. He wanted his mom.”

Rio nodded and smiled sadly, letting Alice off the hook she’d hung herself on. Alice nodded only once and fished her own phone out of her back pocket, and Rio watched as her hang dog expression dropped even further.

She put her head in her hands again, and everything was dark once more. In the dark her headache resurfaced. It started from the back of her head, spreading slowly to her temple where it burrowed and settled, familiar and unwelcome.

It was a soft weight in her lap that made her look up and she saw Alice settling on the arm of the seat beside her, her attention on her phone but her hand lightly grazing Rio’s shoulder. In her lap she’d placed the well-loved rabbit that Nicky had been holding all day. She lifted him and looked at him properly for the first time.

A cream rabbit with brown spots and floppy ears. So obviously a rabbit she wasn’t sure how she’d been confused as to his species before. His nose was pink and she touched it with the pad of her forefinger, looking at the face of the thing that had been by Nicky’s side since birth.

This little creature had undoubtedly been chosen by Agatha to be her son’s companion. He’d witnessed her girlfriend become a mother. He’d been with them when they were hidden away and only had each other for the first few months of Nicky’s life.

She felt jealous of a toy bunny. And for that, she felt stupid.

Her head hurt more.

She placed the bunny beside her, focused down on the floor.

“Go to Rio.” Agatha’s voice filtered into her consciousness and she looked up just in time to see a frowning Nicky make his way over to her. She opened her arms and he dived into them, settling beside her on the couch.

“We’ll be back in a sec, okay?”

Rio nodded and felt the seat dip as Alice slid down beside her and the three left all watched as Agatha and Jen disappeared from the room.

“Let’s take bets on who shouts first?”

Rio scoffed but couldn’t really see the humour in it. Nicky just shuffled beside her and she realised he was reaching for Scratchy. She saved him from being squashed between her and Alice and handed him back.

“Are you hungry?”

“I’m okay.”

“Thirsty?”

“I’m okay, melliza.”

“You sure?” Alice asked, handing Rio her phone as she leant around to make eye contact with Nicky. “I know your mom’s already stocked the fridge and I hear there’s ice cream.”

Rio blinked at the screen and realised what she was looking at.

“Oh,” Nicky said, clearly struggling with wanting to stay with everyone and wanting ice cream. “Well maybe I am a little hungry.”

Rio’s lips twitched at the words but then she zoned in and she missed whatever was said next as she read Agatha’s statement on the divorce.

After careful consideration, I have made the decision to end my marriage.

My priority remains, as always, my son and ensuring that he feels loved, supported, and protected during this transition. I am committed to approaching this next chapter with a great deal of respect for everyone involved.

I ask for privacy for my family during this time.

Rio swallowed thickly, aware she was now alone in the room as Alice had taken Nicky to get ice cream. Agatha’s statement was simple and to the point, but Nicky was at the centre of it.

The other thing, more noticeable than the actual words in the post, was how many likes it already had. Rio blanched at the sight. Sometimes she forgot that Agatha was famous famous.

She dared to go into the comments.

Harkne55 NOOOOOO NOT OUR PARENTS

KimberleyJ Blond guys give me the creeps anyway

V1d4L Maybe she got a taste of something she liked on set…

MovieLuvr Praying for you and young Nicholas !!

WandaMaximoff Sending so much love to you and Nicky ❤️

As if by magic, as Rio’s eyes scanned over Wanda’s comment, she saw the little box pop up at the top of the screen.

Wanda M
Can you get Rio to call me?

Rio put the phone down. Now wasn’t the time to speak to Wanda. She rested her head in her hands until she heard Nicky and Alice return to the room. Looking up she saw Nicky clutching two bowls, Scratchy tucked unceremoniously under his arm.

“I got you some too. It’s chocolate. Your favourite.”

Rio accepted the bowl with a smile but her stomach churned unhappily at the prospect of eating anything at all. She forced herself to swallow a mouthful just to show willing.

Perhaps Nicky’s eyes were bigger than his stomach too because he ate just as slowly as Rio did. Or maybe he just wanted to keep pace with her. Whichever way, they both finished their ice cream and soon relaxed back into the seat, Nicky tucked under Rio’s arm, Scratchy half over both their laps.

Alice had been silently focused on her cell the whole time.

They couldn’t speak about it. Not when Nicky didn’t know what was happening. So they waited. Rio and Nicky fidgeted. One with her hair, the other with his rabbit.

Rio’s attention soon drifted far from the room they were in. She took herself away to a place where they could be free. Where she could eat ice cream without feeling like she was force-feeding herself. She could play basketball in the park with Nicky without anyone approaching or trying to steal him away.

She could kiss Agatha after every point scored and not worry about anyone watching or seeing or judging.

The main focus of her idle fantasy was soon back in the room looking ashen and tired. Rio looked over to her and saw her focus in on the empty bowls on the coffee table.

“Ice cream?”

Nicky nodded and Agatha’s lips twitched.

“Jen and Alice are leaving now.”

“Rio too.”

She’d known this was coming. It had been agreed ages ago. Rio would leave. Rio had to leave.

So she stood and began to walk on autopilot, her body simply doing what she was told to do because she didn’t know what else she could do.

“Is security here?”

The only thing she could think to say as she stepped closer to Jen and Agatha and a little boy collided with her back.

“They’re here. Plain car, waiting out front. They’ll be here all night. The house has-…”

“Rio cannot leave.” Nicky, clinging.

Rio closed her eyes briefly and in the time she was plunged into darkness, Agatha had moved in to take Nicky from her. When free, she moved closer to Jen, Alice now flanking her other side.

They were in a standoff. Only Rio had forgotten her gun and Agatha was equally unarmed. Nicky was standing before his mama, his eyes darting between Jen and Alice but always swinging back to Rio.

“You have to come with us, Rio. You said you’d listen to our advice. You said you’d do as we said.”

“It’s different now.” Rio had found her voice. She’d found her courage again, buried deep under fear and the shame that she could be the one bringing the danger to Agatha’s door.

“It’s not. It’s-…”

“Can she stay, please? I want her to stay.”

Rio wanted to reach out for Nicky but she knew that would make this too hard. And it was already too damn hard.

She looked at Alice first and then looked back to Nicky. She’d made a promise.

“I have to go, mellizo. But I’ll see you soon, okay?”

Nicky’s face fell and Rio realised that although he’d been nervous about her leaving before he hadn’t actually thought she would.

Agatha’s hands slid from his shoulders to cross over his chest and Rio felt sick that she might be trying to comfort him because of something she’d said, something she’d promised.

“Rio? Let’s go, babe.”

But rio was no longer following instructions. She heard the command but ignored it. She’d looked up to Agatha. They simply stared at each other. And Rio opened her mouth to speak, but found nothing came.

So Agatha became her voice.

“I need you to stay. I can’t-… please, you need to stay.”

Rio’s blood ran cold in her veins at the prospect of saying no to that request, to that voice, to that woman. Beside her, Alice turned and knew just by looking at her what her friend was going to do.

“Agatha, it’s really not-…,” Jen began.

“Jen.” Alice stopped her.

Rio was already moving, already making her decision. Her decision was Agatha. Her decision was Nicky. Her decision was their family.

“Sí, mi vida,” Rio breathed out the words and was glad of it because her body was empty of breath just as Nicky flung himself to her. She caught him with a soft ‘oomph’ and then bent down at the waist before him to hug him properly.

Above them Agatha was nodding to herself, her hand splayed out across her chest as if she were trying to control her breathing.

“Agatha,” Jen insisted again, somewhere behind Rio. “You have to be sensible about-…”

“Not tonight. Rio stays tonight. We can discuss it tomorrow. Not tonight, Jen.”

Rio sighed out when she felt Nicky’s fist in her shirt and she closed her eyes as Agatha added: “Alice, can you come get her Monday morning?”

“Sure.”

“Monday isn’t-…”

“Thank you.”

“I really don’t think-…”

Agatha was here now, Agatha’s hand was gently prying Nicky’s from her shirt, worried he was holding too tightly. But he could have torn her precious cowboy shirt to shreds for all Rio cared.

“Jen, let’s leave them. It’s been a rough day.” Alice again, fighting Rio’s corner even against her own girlfriend.

She’d have to thank her later. She’d have to give her a bonus, write her a blank check, kiss the face of her best friend until Alice called her a loser and pushed her away.

She heard Jen grunt but she didn’t argue back.

“Call me. I mean it. If anything happens. Anything at all. And don’t leave this house together.”

The door opened and closed and it was just Rio, Nicky, and Agatha. One wrapped up in Rio’s arms, the other hovering close, her own hands now brushing tenderly through Rio’s hair.

Rio kept her eyes closed for a long while, soaking in the moment. But Nicky spoke close to her ear and her eyes fluttered open again as he did.

“You should stay forever, melliza.”

Agatha moved into view then, her blue eyes full of unshed tears as she crouched beside them both. Rio gasped at the sight and found herself reaching for Agatha before she even knew what she was doing.

Agatha had been waiting for her to do it if the speed upon which she threw herself at Rio meant anything. She practically launched herself the way her son had just done and Rio was tipping backwards, falling over, able only just to catch herself and the other two on top of her before anyone got injured.

Normally she’d have laughed at the urgency of Agatha. But nothing felt funny anymore.

She held on as she was covered by the two clutching bodies and closed her eyes again to just feel what it felt to be needed so desperately by the two in her arms.

Nicky had wriggled to press his face against her shoulder. Agatha was in against her cheek. She could feel her breath, warm and soothing. The antidote to cure all ills was this. Three patitos, all as desperate as the next, all as clutching, all as unwilling to let go.

But they couldn’t stay huddled on the floor all night.

It was Agatha who broke the heavy spell that had settled around them. Agatha who was sitting up to peel Nicky from Rio, Agatha who was now guiding Nicky away. Rio sat slowly and watched as Nicky kept looking back at her, checking she was still there as he clutched his mama’s hand.

Agatha’s shoulders were slumped, her whole body trying to make itself smaller. Rio scrambled to her feet to go and join them and found that as she took a seat beside Nicky on the couch, Agatha moved off to pace.

“It’s okay,” Nicky said, sounding quiet and unsure. “We’re all together, mama. Auntie Jen won’t take Rio away.”

Rio shifted over and draped an arm around Nicky but kept her gaze on Agatha who was now huffing, now running her hands through her hair.

“Mi vida.”

Agatha didn’t respond and Nicky shifted beside her, on the edge of the couch now. “Mama? Mi vida? Are you mad at me?”

“No, honey.” It made Agatha turn, her eyes wide and full, “Never, okay? It’s just…” her gaze moved along to Rio and Rio knew then what was about to happen.

Agatha still had to tell Nicky exactly what why they were hidden in a house in the hills.

They locked eyes again and Rio nodded just once, letting Agatha know she was there. Agatha turned back to Nicky and slowly made her way over again. She crouched before him and took his hands as Rio placed her own on his back.

“Honey, you know how your dad and I have lived separately quite a lot?”

“Yes.”

“And… you know how, how sometimes, how sometimes we fight?”

“Yes, mama.”

“Well, honey, today, I told your daddy that I didn’t want to be married to him anymore.”

Rio turned from where she’d been looking at Agatha to see Nicky’s side profile. His brow was furrowed but he didn’t look upset. He looked patient, a little confused, but not upset.

“So you can marry Rio.”

Agatha made a small noise from the base of her throat, a gentle sound of surprise. Her eyes flashed to Rio and Rio just stared at her, her own eyes wide.

“N-no, no, honey. I-… Rio is my friend. Just my friend.”

It hurt, despite being necessary to say. It still hurt.

But as Nicky turned to look at Rio she realised that someone else was hurt by it too. He looked more than confused now, he looked devastated. “No, no, we are tres patitos. If you marry Rio. If, if,” Nicky took Rio’s hand and held it alongside Agatha’s.

“If you marry her, mama, we can be tres patitos all together and nobody else. Nobody else.”

“Baby,” Agatha tried gently, and Rio watched as a tear fell from her eye. “Baby, listen to me. I’m not marrying Rio. But I am still going to be your mama and I’m going to be here always and I love you so much and-…”

“No! NO!”

Nicky had thrown their hands away, thrown his little fists down at his sides. “No! You said! You said it wasn’t pretend!! You promised me, melliza! Mama! You SAID!”

“Nicky.”

Rio could only watch as Nicky threw his tantrum, his fists furious as they slammed repeatedly into the couch cushions and his shouting uninhibited as he let out his frustration. Too little to contain these big emotions he screamed them out.

He was a tiny Agatha, throwing his weight about the place as his confusion, his anger, his fear took over.

“Tres patitos! Tres patitos! TRES PATITOS!”

“Honey,” Agatha insisted again, and Rio saw her hands were shaking as she reached for Nicky’s. She felt sick with it, sick that this little boy couldn’t get a handle on his feelings. That he couldn’t understand why Agatha wouldn’t just marry his melliza.

Rio was helpless as she witnessed it. But Nicky’s fury didn’t last as long as Agatha’s.

He’d exploded and then fizzled out just as fast.

Agatha managed to pull him down and into her arms and Nicky dissolved into tears against her. Rio didn’t know where to look. She didn’t know what to do or what to say to make this any better. So she simply sat there.

Nicky was shaking through his torment. He was so little still, barely eight. And today had been enough to push Rio, a fully grown adult over the edge, so it was a miracle he’d held it together this long.

She wiped at her eyes just as a hand found her knee and Agatha whispered, “It’s just us. Tres patitos. Me, you, and Rio, okay? Rio isn’t going anywhere. Right, Rio?”

“Right.”

Agatha motioned with her head and before Rio knew it she was on the floor with them again, wrapping her arms around them, covering them with her warmth.

Agatha pressed her lips to her ear. It was gesture of grace, a soft reminder that she was part of this too.

It was overwhelming, the desire to not then turn and kiss Agatha. She wanted to kiss her and announce to Nicky that she would marry her mom. She’d marry her mom right now.

Instead she didn’t kiss her, she didn’t marry her, she just wrapped them both as tightly as she could in her arms and tried to ignore Agatha’s tears as they trickled down her neck.

“Seguro y feliz,” Nicky sniffed miserably, pressed between his two favourite people. Rio ducked her head down to kiss Nicky’s temple, pressing her face in against him. She’d fucked up so badly, so immeasurably that it felt unreal to have him here with them.

Having Agatha here felt like a miracle. Having her wanting to be close, crying silently into her shoulder, it felt like more than she deserved.

Having Nicky… but before she could finish her thought Nicky was wriggling. He’d changed his mind. He wanted out. Rio pulled back and watched as the little boy didn’t actually move away. He continued to cling to Agatha and Rio realised that she’d been dismissed.

He was his mother’s son. Rio could read his body language almost as well as she could read Agatha’s.

Her mouth opened to say something but before words could come tears did instead. She looked from the back of Nicky’s head up to Agatha’s face and saw that she looked as devastated as she felt. But Nicky was the priority. For both of them.

So Rio swallowed down her hurt and slowly, unsteadily, got to her feet.

“I just,” she whispered, “I-I’ll be right back.”

As quickly and silently as she could she left the room in search of somewhere she could breathe. She stumbled her way through the dark house until she found a bathroom and when inside she closed the door and slid down against it onto the floor.

It was only right that Nicky and Agatha have some time alone. It made sense. What didn’t make sense was the pain she was suddenly in. Worse than her headaches, worse than the piercing of her skin by the old crone. This was her whole body. This was agony.

She slumped down, her head resting on her arms as she curled in on herself.

The only power she had was in her ability to wait for them. Here, on this cold floor. Out in the work, publicly single, privately yearning.

But she could do it.

She could wait. She could give them time.

Just as she began to spiral into what her dad would say to her - something kind, something patient - she felt the vibrations of a gentle knock on the door behind her. She peeled herself up, not wanting to be caught curled up on the floor.

Taking a deep breath, she answered it and found herself face to face with Agatha.

They looked at each other for long enough that Rio felt a twinge in her head again.

“I don’t think I can do this.”

Rio glanced over her shoulder, checking to see if Nicky were there. He wasn’t.

“Us?”

“No.” The answer was immediate, urgent, and Rio found her hands being taken. “Lie to him.”

Before Rio could answer - before she even knew how to answer - Agatha was speaking again.

“Jen wasn’t right earlier,” the words tumbled from Agatha’s lips as if she’d been trying to hold them back all evening. “I didn’t delay to make it harder. I wanted you in the will, of course I did. And I dragged my heels on it but I always wanted it to be a Saturday. Because I wanted him to have a really, really good day. Either with me or with you. I wanted him to be free and be a kid and to-…”

Rio stepped in as Agatha began to cry and she wiped the first of her tears from her cheek as Agatha held her wrist.

“I wanted him to have day, good, easy day before it all started. Why couldn’t he just have that?”

“Because,” Rio stepped a little closer, “because when this is all over, all he’ll have will be good, easy days. We’ll make sure of that.”

Agatha nodded miserably and turned her wet face into Rio’s palm, her eyes fluttering closed. Rio sighed as she dropped Agatha’s other hand and held her hip instead, placing a kiss to her temple.

“He’ll be okay. We’ll be okay.”

“Melliza?”

Rio turned in surprise and looked up to see Nicky watching them both cautiously from across the hall. Agatha turned from her but kept her hand in her own.

“Baby.”

Nicky ran his fingers through his hair nervously and shifted on the spot. “I’m staying with you?”

“Yes,” Agatha breathed, dropping Rio’s hand to move towards Nicky. But Nicky did something unexpected. He stepped back. Rio watched as Agatha swayed on the spot, saw the way her shoulders dropped.

She moved to stand beside her. Nicky was avoiding both their eyes.

The wise little boy with the big heart took an even bigger breath and then released everything that he’d been keeping inside. And Rio felt her heart break for it.

“All of my friends have two parents that love them some have three or four and and I just want two and I don’t understand why I can’t have that is it me? Mama? Melliza? Is it me?”

Agatha fell to her knees before her son and Nicky kept his face down but Rio saw the way his knuckles were white as they clutched Scratchy. She saw the tears the size of pearls fall to his feet.

She saw Agatha reach for him and Nicky stumble back.

“Honey.”

Agatha’s voice was shaky, for the first time unsure as she tried to reassure her son. The poison her mother had injected into her when she was young hadn’t been passed down to Nicky.

There was no generational trauma, no inherited curse.

And yet, and still, Nicky felt less than. He felt unsure. He felt undeserving.

Rio crashed to her knees beside Agatha and where Agatha had lost her words, Rio found her own.

“Do you know the first thing your mama told me about you? The first thing she said to me?”

Nicky shook his head, sniffled. He kept his eyes down.

“She told me that you were the best.”

Nicky sniffed, his fingers fidgeting with Scratchy’s ears.

“And you know what else she told me?”

“What?”

“That you were a ham.”

“A ham?”

Nicky looked up, his eyes like planets of pain.

“It means you love to sing and dance and play and that you’re really brave.”

Nicky twisted the bunny’s ear about his finger.

“And I thought, no! This kid couldn’t possibly be the best kid, and fun and brave!”

Nicky sniffed and Rio smiled, only it wasn’t forced this time because she was remembering the polite little boy who’d come to greet her when she first arrived at Agatha’s house. The little shy boy who had shaken her hand, then stolen her jersey, then played the best air guitar she’d ever seen.

“But then I met you and I thought, wow Agatha is so lucky to have a kid like Nicky. And now I am so lucky to have a mellizo like you.”

Nicky sniffed again, harder this time. He wiped at his nose with the back of his sleeve and Rio held her hand out to him.

“Do you know how much your mama loves you?”

Nicky nodded, his eyes briefly moving to Agatha who’d settled back on her ankles and was watching with silent tears.

“So much. To the moon and back. We always say it. Count the stars in the sky.”

“Yes, honey,” Agatha smiled, wiping her own nose with the back of her hand.

“Have you tried?” Rio asked quietly, dropping her hand down because Nicky hadn’t taken it. “Counting the stars in the sky?”

He looked back at her and shook his head.

“That’s because there are so many. Because your mom loves you hasta infinito.”

Nicky nodded a little and sniffed again. Rio watched as his hold loosened slightly on the toy in his hands and he lifted his chin.

“I may not be your mama, cariño,” she swallowed thickly, “but I love you too, okay? And I am not going anywhere. And you know what those kids don’t have?”

Nicky shook his head.

“A melliza. Only you do.”

Nicky sniffed and looked down again. Rio could feel the tension emanating from Agatha beside her. She had to force herself to breathe because she knew Agatha wasn’t.

And things happened slowly then. Because there wasn’t a sudden grand gesture. There wasn’t a big movement, another flying into her arms.

Nicky remained where he stood, his gaze on the floor, his fingers dancing over Scratchy as he held him close still.

“Did you enjoy your ice cream?”

Rio frowned, her head tilting in question as Nicky slowly raised his gaze to meet her own.

“Mama told me you eat chocolate ice cream when you’re sad. Did it make you feel better?”

Rio shifted, her knees sore now from the heavy crash into the floor and the fact she’d been leaning up on them for so long. But she didn’t let it show. She simply nodded, understanding that Nicky had eaten so slowly because the ice cream hadn’t been for him.

He’d tried to make Rio happy again with it.

“Te amo, mellizo,” she whispered without even meaning to. She just needed him to know, just had to say it again.

Nicky did move this time. He walked right over and flung his arms around her neck. Suddenly she had a toy bunny pressed into her face and a little boy clinging for dear life. And when Agatha placed her hand on her back, she decided there was no place she’d rather be.

In the hallway of the house in the hills, Rio felt like a mom for the first time. Properly. Though secretly. The little boy in her arms who’d made her feel that way couldn’t even know.

But Agatha knew. Agatha who pressed her lips to her ear and silently thanked her for being a melliza, privately agreed that she was really a mami.

“Rio?” Nicky, quietly. “Don’t marry anybody else, okay?”

“Okay, baby. I won’t.”

Rio turned her head just the inch she needed to lock eyes with Agatha and saw her watery smile. She was no longer drowning. The woman before her was treading water again, kept afloat by her boy and his melliza.

Nicky was nodding, holding her tighter, and Rio smiled as Scratchy’s face pressed against her own. The rabbit bestowed his kiss, passing the baton to Rio now to look after his charges.

“Te amo too,” Nicky whispered as Agatha gave up trying to be cool about it and leant in to press a kiss to the back of Nicky’s head.

Rio squeezed and then released Nicky, allowing him to peel himself away. He wiped at his nose and Rio wiped at his cheek.

He was shy once more, barely able to look at either Rio or his mom. But both knew he just needed time, time and answers. So when he formed his next question neither was surprised, he’d asked it.

There was still so much to discuss.

“Was grandmother mad because you and daddy aren’t together anymore? Is daddy mad too?”

“Your grandmother was mad because she is-…”

“Mean,” Nicky concluded. It made Rio scoff and Nicky looked around to her in confusion but she cleared her throat and said nothing.

“She called you a dog.” He clearly didn’t find it funny.

“Mellizo.”

Nicky’s earlier frown reappeared and his hold on Scratchy tightened again. “Alice called her a bad word and I think I should get to say it.”

Rio raised her brows in surprise but deferred to Agatha on this one. Agatha sighed and pinched the bridge of her nose but nodded soon enough. “Okay. Just one. What did Alice say?”

Nicky cleared his throat and said, “Well, mama, Alice said that grandmother was a cun-…”

“Wah!!” Rio jumped up, cutting Nicky off before he could totally destroy Alice’s chances of ever being in Agatha’s good graces. She dived at Nicky and began to walk him backwards, ushering him away and back into the family room they’d spent most of the day.

She glanced over her shoulder and saw Agatha following, a heavy frown on her face.

“Mama said it was okay.”

“I know baby but we love Alice and we don’t want her to get in trouble.”

“Okay. Okay, yes.”

“She is in trouble!”

Rio grimaced and jumped onto the couch after Nicky. She landed beside him with her legs curled under her and something miraculous happened. Nicky giggled.

“Mama it ended with a ‘t’!”

Rio barked a laugh just as Agatha jumped onto them both and Rio threw herself over Nicky in an attempt to protect him. And as a result she accepted the fact that Agatha was going to make her suffer through the art of knowing exactly where she was most sensitive.

She gasped and laughed and writhed around with them both until Agatha gave in, until Nicky wriggled to sit by her head, until Agatha perched herself in her lap. Rio saw stars above her and counted them to infinity.

“No more bad words,” Agatha panted softly, her hand innocently resting on Rio’s stomach, both a threat and a promise.

Nicky’s hand had reached around Rio’s face to hold her chin and she grinned up at him as he smiled down at her.

“Maybe you should tell Alice, melliza.”

“Maybe I should.”

Nicky’s smile turned to a grin and Rio beamed back up at him, thrilled he was more relaxed, relieved he wasn’t pulling away anymore. She absently moved her hand to Agatha’s thigh and found Agatha moved off of her the second she did.

Rio’s smile faltered a little but her gaze turned to Agatha as Nicky’s did and she turned her head to watch as Agatha stood before the two of them. She looked so serious that Rio sat up again.

“I think,” Agatha started, sitting down on the coffee table now. She cleared her throat and looked down at her hands. She began to toy with her wedding ring. The fake wedding ring.

Rio watched as something happened to Agatha. As something flickered across her face and then died and was replaced with a hopeful smile.

“I think we should all order some food, get cosy, and have a night for just us.” Her gaze moved from Nicky to Rio and Rio knew she had changed her mind about saying something very different to the words currently coming out of her mouth. “Just tres patitos. So, come on. Pyjamas I got you new ones all ready in your dresser.”

Rio sucked in a breath but Nicky was already moving. He went first to Agatha and gave her a hug and Rio had to watch as Agatha dissolved into it. If the way he clung to Agatha meant anything it meant that his fit of the giggles hadn’t cured his pain and it had barely touched the sides of Agatha’s.

But Nicky turned to deliver the same hug to Rio and she gladly accepted, letting him go eventually so he could run up to get his pyjamas on.

Alone now in the dim, Agatha shuddered a breath.

“This feels like a nightmare.”

Rio looked down, her gaze falling to the bandaids on her arm. She went to peel the first, the deepest of the cuts. A hand flew to her wrist before she’d even peeled it halfway.

“Don’t. They’ll scar.”

Rio nodded and Agatha released her, letting her smooth the bandaid back down but it was loose now, too loose to be effective.

“Tell me what else she said.”

Rio sighed and made to stand, and from this angle, with Agatha still perched on the coffee table, Agatha looked vulnerable again. Small.

She felt Agatha’s hands before she’d even realised she was reaching for her. Agatha had her hands on the backs of her thighs and had pulled her closer.

Rio stumbled but stopped, her fingertips just touching Agatha’s shoulders.

“Mi vida.”

“You were so good with him,” Agatha whispered, changing tact where she realised Rio wouldn’t bite. “So good. I… I want this to work. I want him to have you. I want, I want-…”

Rio bent down and kissed the want out of Agatha’s mouth. She wanted everything she did. Perhaps more. Because Agatha was seeing only her son’s pain where Rio saw hers too.

But she’d carry both of them. Their pain, their fears, their hurt. She’d do it happily.

She moved her fingers to tangle them in Agatha’s hair, and stepped closer to her, kissing her again because it felt impossible not to.

When she pulled back, she whispered against Agatha’s pout. “I am here. You have me. This isn’t a nightmare. It’s just the start of a dream. A dream of you, me, and Nicky.”

“I want you now. I want to walk out tomorrow and just-…”

The thunder came. Nicky running down the stairs. Rio stepped back and Agatha let go. And soon, in his new cowboy pyjamas, was Nicholas River Harkness. He ran into the room and Rio had to bite her cheek to stop her smile.

Agatha stood beside her and raised her brows as Nicky’s strides became quick little steps and he staggered to a halt in front of them.

Rio couldn’t help but grin at him, looking at the little figures and their little horses dotted all over his matching set. “Do those come in my size?”

“Well, mama got me them so maybe?”

Both twins looked hopefully to Agatha and Agatha rolled her eyes, recovering remarkably well from her mood a few seconds ago.

“Second drawer in the dresser. Third door on the right.”

“Are you kidding?”

Agatha shrugged and Rio gaped. “You got me cowboy pyjamas?”

“I figured you’d stay at some point and-…”

But Rio was already running. She was already sprinting up into the hall and up the stairs. Something about cowboy pyjamas. Picked for her. Picked because they were cowboy pyjamas, but equally because they matched Nicky’s. She wasn’t running anymore, she was flying.

She heard both Agatha and Nicky shout after her. Ignoring them, she made it to the third door on the right.

The upstairs of the house felt just as open and spacious as below. And the room she now entered was large, impeccably dressed. She scanned it over, taking a second to breathe in her new surroundings before she went to the second drawer of the dresser and not only found what she was looking for, but a million other things at that.

Cowboy pyjamas, the same style as Nicky’s. A new Celtics sweater, folded so the team name was looking up at her. Below that was another green sweater, plain this time. More pyjamas, some green, some with horses galloping across them.

She opened the next draw, the one above. Underwear. Sleep shorts. Nothing too sexy, not overtly so. Everything designed for comfort, for someone who lived in this house too. And if the little cowboy hats on one pair of sleep shorts were saying anything, they were saying that Rio lived here.

“Hey.”

Rio nearly jumped out of her skin. She’d been reaching into the drawer to touch some of the shorts and accidentally whacked her hand on the wood in her surprise.

“Ow! Fuck!”

Agatha hurried over and gingerly took her hand, “I’m sorry. I came to change and… sorry.”

Rio grit her teeth as pain flashed and the fuzz of it made her body tingle but Agatha was kissing it better and Nicky was right about his mom’s kisses; they were healing.

“You filled a dresser for me?”

“I figured you might be staying occasionally. I’m hoping often. I wanted you to have clothes you could wear.”

“Cowboy shorts?”

“You don’t like them?”

“Oh I love them. I just didn’t think you would.”

Rio grinned as she stepped in closer, fishing the shorts in question out from the drawer and hooking them on two fingers for Agatha to see.

“Save a horse?” Agatha offered quietly, “Ride a cowboy?”

Rio’s grin fell and Agatha bit her lip, her fingers twisting in her hand to lock them together.

“Maybe when Nicky’s in bed,” Rio began, stepping closer. The fuzz her body felt from the sharp pain had turned to a dull, low, constant vibration. Like Agatha had flicked a switch somewhere and her body was reacting to it.

But Agatha was shaking her head, her lower lip still stuck between her teeth.

“He’ll want to sleep with me.”

“Okay,” Rio murmured, her gaze dropping to Agatha’s mouth. She hesitated but soon closed the distance and kissed her slowly. They let it linger, Agatha gasping quietly when Rio pulled back.

“Soon,” Rio promised, nuzzling in where Agatha had stepped closer. “I want to show you everything. I want us to be solid.” She kissed her again. “Happy. Normal. I want to be your girlfriend in every way. Even when everything around us feels hard.”

Agatha’s gaze dropped and Rio ducked her head down to try and catch her eye again.

“Hey.”

“Everything?”

Rio’s lips twitched when she met Agatha’s shy gaze. “We’ve barely started.”

“What if I’m bad at everything?”

Rio glanced at the door then turned around and saw Agatha’s eyes had darted there too. “There is no world where Agatha Harkness would be bad at anything.”

Agatha smiled a little and Rio returned it, leaning in to kiss her until she was stopped with Agatha’s fingers against her lips.

“We should change.”

“Do you have cowboy pyjamas too?”

Agatha’s shyness disappeared entirely, replaced with a look so withering it made Rio laugh. She said nothing as she left Rio alone in the room and Rio rolled her eyes as she turned back to fish out her cowboy pyjamas.

She changed into them and checked herself out in the mirror. They were an exact match of Nicky’s. Long pants, a long-sleeved shirt with buttons, a dusty blue set. She didn’t think she’d ever looked so good in her life.

Stepping out of the room she briefly glanced around to see if she could find where Agatha had gone but saw no sign of her so went back to find Nicky. Agatha had left him on the couch with Scratchy by his side and the tv now on. He was flicking through to find a movie.

He gasped when she entered the room. “They’re the same!”

“Do you like them?”

Nicky nodded and Rio grinned, taking a seat by his side.

“You feeling okay about everything?”

Nicky’s smile faded slightly and Rio’s softened too.

“Will you think about marrying my mama? I know it would make her really happy. I don’t think daddy did. But you do. And I… I wouldn’t mind calling you-…”

He stopped and his eyes went wide as he stared over Rio’s shoulder. Rio frowned at this, and then followed his line of sight.

Suddenly she wasn’t frowning anymore.

“No fucking way.”

“Language, please.”

Agatha Harkness, three time Oscar nominee, one time winner, was standing just a few feet away in cowboy pyjamas. Dusty blue ones. Matching ones. Rio gaped at her. Her hair was back in a bun, messy again, but purposefully so this time.

She still wore her fake wedding ring and was toying with it as she blushed where she stood.

“I didn’t want to feel left out.”

This, Rio knew, was only a half truth. She was sure Agatha had decided that Nicky would take comfort in them all being dressed alike. She was also sure that Agatha had never looked better.

“Mama,” Nicky uttered, with shock and awe, “You got some too?!”

Rio stood from the couch, her body moving her before her brain could tell her not to. Agatha’s blush deepened the closer she got until soon it was spreading down her neck and had rouged her chest.

Rio grinned as it did, unthinkingly pressing her face into her cheek and wrapping her arms around Agatha’s waist. Agatha cleared her throat quietly and placed her hands on Rio’s arms.

“I can be fun too.”

Rio laughed against her as a little boy ran over and wrapped his arms around them both, pressing his face in between them.

“You look so cute,” Rio announced, leaning back to grin at Agatha now Nicky was here.

“You do, mama! We all do! Melliza looks so handsome.”

“Very handsome,” Agatha muttered, narrowing her eyes at Rio, still with a vivid blush across her pale skin. Rio knew Agatha thought she was being made fun of but she could only grin, could only soak up the image of an embarrassed Agatha wearing cowboy pyjamas just to match with her son.

“As handsome as my mellizo.”

Out of sight of Nicky, Rio slid her hand down Agatha’s back and watched as her brow quirked. She kept going until she had hold of her ass and smiled sweetly as Agatha’s lips parted and her lashes fluttered at the sudden move.

“¿Cómo se dice 'cowboy'?” How do you say ‘cowboy’?

Rio hummed quietly, looking down to Nicky, keeping her hand where it was.

“Vaquero.”

“Vaquero,” Nicky repeated, frowning as he tried to memorise the word. “Vaquero. Vaquero.”

“Honey,” Agatha said, her gaze still on Rio as Rio focused on the little boy, her smile now smug as her fingers flexed in their hold of Agatha’s ass. “Did you decide on a movie?”

Nicky shook his head and stepped back, “No. Maybe, maybe Toy Story?”

“Sounds good,” Agatha said absently, shooting Nicky a wink that sent him happily back to the couch and gave her the opportunity to mutter from the side of her mouth to Rio: “Enjoying yourself?”

“Like you wouldn’t believe.”

Agatha rolled her eyes but Rio knew she didn’t mean it because as she moved away she took Rio’s offending hand and dragged her along with her. Once back at the couch Rio was made to sit down before Agatha did. She caught Agatha when she did sit and sat comfortably, smugly, with her arm curled around her on her left side.

But Nicky hadn’t been included in this little setup. And soon made it clear he wanted involved by simply climbing across Agatha to nestle in between them. He was the only person Rio would have moved for.

So now, tres vaqueros, Rio felt a calm she’d not felt all day.

“Rio, could you, would you order, please?”

Agatha was leaning around Nicky, having fished her phone out from her breast pocket to hand to her. The silent addition to her question being: I don’t want to look at my phone.

“Text Jen, she’ll put the order through.”

Rio nodded and when it came to unlocking Agatha’s phone she was told the passcode: Nicky’s birthday. When it was unlocked the calm she’d experienced for no longer than thirty seconds was gone again.

Agatha’s phone had blown up. Her texts, her WhatsApp, her emails, her calls, every single thing that could possibly have a notification against it now did. All little red circles claiming tens, dozens, hundreds, of people trying to reach her or simply talking about her.

It made Rio feel sick.

“What will it be?” She asked as calmly as she could. “Cheese burgers all round? Fries? Milkshakes?”

“Yes please,” Nicky said readily and Rio glanced up and saw that Agatha was chewing her lip. She realised she’d seen her screen, seen the mass of red dots there, lying in wait for her.

She cleared her throat as she oh so casually reached her uninjured arm back around and brushed her nails gently along the back of Agatha’s neck. Agatha closed her eyes.

“Okay,” Rio said in a softer voice, her eyes on Agatha still. “Coming right up.”

With her free hand she sent Jen a message asking her to make the order for them and then she locked the phone again and placed it down beside her on the couch. Agatha had opened her eyes again at this point and had turned to meet Rio’s gaze. She looked small once more, scared, even.

Rio just smiled, stretching her hand until she could curl it round Agatha’s neck and hold her as Nicky loaded up the movie and the Pixar lamp hopped onto the screen. They all soon focused in.

Agatha released her hair from its bun and Rio began to play with it, only half paying attention to the cartoon. She knew Agatha wasn’t interested either because she was still chewing her lip, her arm now around Nicky but her fingers toying with the fabric of Rio’s pants.

The day Agatha had wanted to be easy for Nicky had been so far from it. It had been traumatic and emotionally draining and Rio only realised Nicky, too, was only half invested in his chosen movie when she felt a gentle hand on her injured arm.

She looked down and saw his fingers trailing a route that snaked around each bandaid. Agatha was soon watching it too and Rio, intent on reassuring, whispered, “It’s okay, mellizo. They don’t hurt.”

Nicky stopped what he was doing and looked up at her.

“You don’t need to be brave. You can say.”

Rio swallowed thickly and nodded, briefly looking to Agatha before she looked back at Nicky. “They hurt a little, then. But only a little.”

“Okay,” Nicky whispered, looking back down at her arm and, deciding to steer well clear, he held her hand instead. Rio watched him for a few more seconds before she looked back over to Agatha and saw she was already looking at her.

They exchanged silent smiles and then both turned to pretend once again to focus in on the movie.

By the time the food arrived - Agatha went to collect it, Jen had instructed the driver to deliver it to the security guard out front - Rio felt some of the calm she’d felt briefly before. Nicky ate quickly this time around. And Rio the same.

Even Agatha ate with slightly less grace than usual.

Once full, they settled back where they were on the couch. Rio’s fingers were never far from Agatha’s hair and by the time they’d switched over to Toy Story 2 and were halfway through that, Nicky was spread out between them, his head in Agatha’s lap, his legs across Rio’s.

He fell asleep by the time the old prospector was revealed to be the bad guy.

It was now Rio spoke for the first time in a while. She’d been mulling it over during dinner, after dinner, throughout the whole evening. She wanted to, needed to, apologise again for not keeping Nicky away from danger.

“I should have been better with him today. I should have been more watchful, more aware that-…”

“My love,” Agatha whispered back, turning where she sat, pausing her fingers that had been running through Nicky’s hair. “You couldn’t have been better with him today.”

“No,” Rio insisted, shaking her head, glancing down at Nicky to make sure he was asleep still. “I could have been better. I could have-…”

“Rio,” Agatha uttered, much firmer this time, only there was a pause before she spoke again and Rio could only guess why. “No hay nadie en quien confíe más con nuestro hijo que tú.” There is no one I trust more with our son than you.

“Mi hijo,” Rio corrected gently.

But Agatha responded as if she’d been expecting it, “No. Nuestro.” Our.

Rio didn’t know what to say. Her grammar had never been great. She conjugated all over the place or added stresses to the wrong syllables. She even once told a teacher she was pregnant when she meant embarrassed.

So she should have known when she corrected Agatha. Because her mom was always bugging her to let Agatha teach her how to speak better Spanish. Agatha was better at it. Agatha knew which word to use and how to conjugate.

She hadn’t misspoken.

“Mi amor, ¿me entiendes?” My love, do you understand me?

Rio swallowed, looked down at Nicky fast asleep still and nodded silently. Agatha didn’t push for a response and Rio was able to eventually whisper, “Sí. Claro.”

A pale hand moved from Nicky’s head and raised up to the back of Rio’s. Her finger tips barely caught her but Rio knew what she was asking. She leant in and Agatha did too and smiled as she kissed her.

“Can you just propose?” Rio smiled into Agatha’s lips, kissing her again before Agatha whispered once more, “I’m basically already divorced.”

“That’s not how it works.”

“Who says?”

They kissed again and this time Agatha nipped at her lower lip, making Rio grunt. She pulled back so Agatha couldn’t get her again and was graced with a pout. An exaggerated, ridiculous pout.

“You have an academy award,” Rio muttered.

“And no ring on my finger.”

“That is ridiculous. Today is not the day to-…”

Agatha huffed and scratched gently at the back of Rio’s head, making her hum low in her throat and lean down to rest her head against her arm along the back of the couch. Agatha smiled at the sight and whispered, “Wouldn't it be a good way to end this shitty day?”

“How about instead I carry this boy to bed and then you clamber in with me and I play with your hair until you fall asleep?”

“All I’ve been able to think about is what will happen in six months.”

Rio lifted her head slowly and Agatha smiled, a beautiful, tragic smile. “I want to skip ahead. To know I’ll win. To know we get through this okay. To know everything will be fine.”

“It will be,” Rio insisted softly, frowning where Agatha still smiled. “More than fine. It’ll be-…”

Nicky shifted between them and Rio waited until he seemed settled again before she continued.

“Mi amor, you will get through this. And when it’s over we can live our lives the way we want to live them.”

Agatha dropped her gaze and was silent as Rio’s mind whirred with unsaid thoughts, with fears she couldn’t even name.

“Help me get him to bed. We’ll put him in his room and you will sleep with me.”

“I thought I had a different room?”

Agatha shot her a look that made Rio grin and for a second everything was okay, and nothing hurt.

She soon scooped Nicky into her arms and the boy woke groggily as Agatha turned the tv off. “Is bedtime?” He asked as Rio was careful about lifting him into a sitting position, her arm stinging as his weight pressed into it. But she had him. She was able to lift him, able to stagger to her feet with him with Agatha’s help.

“Your arm,” Agatha chided as Rio moved with Nicky, his face resting against her shoulder as she carried him from the room.

He was heavy and Rio didn’t think it would be long before she wouldn’t be able to carry him anymore, at least not like this, so she didn’t complain, she didn’t even mind that her arm stung from it.

She simply kept him safe in her arms until she was directed to the right room and she could lay him down on the bed. He was half-awake so crawled under the covers with Rio’s help and Agatha swooped in to kiss his temple, to brush his hair back, to whisper I love you, sweet dreams, before they left him to drift back off.

Agatha switched a nightlight on by the door and Rio watched as stars flooded the ceiling and the little boy curled more in on himself in the bed. Agatha stopped with her too, her hand finding Rio’s stomach, her lips finding her cheek as she whispered, “How do I love thee? Let me count the ways.”

Rio turned into her, felt a rush as Agatha kissed her, as her hand slipped below her shirt and found her hip. She kissed her back, buried her fingers in Agatha’s hair and luxuriated in the moment until Agatha pulled back and breathed out: “Bed.”

Rio followed behind, wagging her tail happily as she traipsed along the hall with her hand in Agatha’s.

The main bedroom was larger than Nicky’s, larger than the one she’d been in earlier. The walls were neutral and there was a large, deep green rug beneath the California king bed centred along the wall.

But Rio had eyes only for Agatha and soon found herself pulled then pushed onto the bed, hurried back into the middle of it, and then covered first by her girlfriend and then by the duvet.

“Nicky will come in. When he’s upset,” Agatha rushed out, her hands on Rio’s cheeks, her lips so close to her own, “he crawls into bed with me in the night. We can’t,” she kissed her then, a ghost of a kiss, barely anything and yet everything all the same, “we can’t do anything.”

“Okay,” Rio agreed, her hands already beneath Agatha’s shirt, already tracing the familiar planes of her back. “Okay. We won’t do anything.”

“I want to do everything.”

Rio groaned, her hands stilling at the sound of Agatha’s whisper. They settled at Agatha’s hips and she huffed quietly even as Agatha graced her with another kiss.

“We can do some things? Or maybe, maybe just one thing. Just one thing? Real quick. Please?”

Agatha smiled, her grin growing up her face as she kissed Rio again. “I think kissing is all we can do tonight. But know I want to. Know I want, more than anything, to do everything.”

Rio couldn’t share Agatha’s grin. She could only scowl, only reach down to Agatha’s ass to hold it again, only pout the way Agatha had done earlier.

It made Agatha grin more, and soon arch her back as she placed her hands either side of Rio’s head and lifted her top half off of her. Her grin eased until it was gone and Rio’s pout disappeared too, her hands slowly working their way back to hold Agatha’s waist.

She felt a longing settle in her chest that was nothing like the longing she felt between her thighs. It was heavier, and something that couldn’t be cured.

“I know that,” Agatha whispered, her eyes now darting about Rio’s face, “I know that you’re young.”

“Don’t start this. Not again. I’m not that-…”

Agatha moved a hand to cover Rio’s mouth and Rio obliging went silent.

“You’re young. You have so many options.”

Rio went to protest but Agatha pressed a little harder where her hand lay.

“And every day I wake up with the fear that you’ll take one, take an option that is easier, that isn’t… that isn’t me.”

Rio frowned deeply, the aching in her chest blooming now, spreading its tendrils out across her body.

“Second only to losing Nicky is my fear of losing you. I know it’s soon. I know it’s… I know we’ve only been, been doing whatever we’ve been doing for less than a year, but…” Rio watched helplessly as Agatha swallowed, her throat bobbing with the effort of it. She squeezed her waist.

“You’re it for me. I don’t need anything other than you and Nicky. I want this to work. I want it to work so badly and I-…” To Rio’s horror Agatha began to tear up and she protested by making a soft noise and lifting her hand to Agatha’s wrist but Agatha didn’t let up.

“Tonight you were, I…” Agatha pulled back suddenly, ripped herself away to sit up. The duvet flew from her and she hid her face in her hands. Rio scrambled to sit up, to tug at her wrists, to prevent Agatha from hiding.

“Mi vida…”

Agatha kept her eyes closed even as Rio pulled her hands away. She was crying, a slow tear trickling down her flushed cheek as she took in a shaky breath and continued: “I don’t feel deserving of you. Of how good you are with Nicky. Of how much he loves you. Of how much you love him, how much you love me.”

Rio had so much to say. So much she’d already said. So much she needed Agatha to hear.

But instead she pulled her in. She held her against her. She felt the familiar tears that trickled down her neck as Agatha cried. In the silence she brushed her fingers through her hair, she shushed her, she kissed the side of her head, she cradled her close.

Only when Agatha’s tears had given out, only when Agatha was silent again, did she speak: “I’ve never been a girlfriend before, not really. Not in my adult life. I’ve never been a melliza. I’ve never wanted someone the way, or as much as I want you. I want matching pyjamas. I want to curl up on the couch with you and your son. I want to hear you call him our son every day for the rest of our lives. I want to replace that ring on your finger with my own. I want you. I want you to never question whether I’ll be here today, tomorrow, ten years, fifty years from now.”

Agatha breathed in sharply and began to lift up, until Rio could see her bloodshot eyes.

She smiled, even though it hurt to.

“I don’t have any other options. My only option is you.”

The longing in her chest swelled exponentially as she looked up into Agatha’s eyes. The fury, the pain, the desperation of them made Rio reach for her face. Agatha looked haunted, broken, and Rio held her together the only way she knew how.

She kissed her until Agatha’s body relaxed into her own. She buried her fingers in her hair until they became so entangled they were lost. She let Agatha push her backwards, let her control the kiss, taking what she wanted from her.

They broke apart panting into each other’s mouths, and Agatha raised her hand up to hold Rio’s jaw, sliding her thumb to her pouting lower lip. Rio’s tongue darted out to greet it and Agatha accepted the invitation, pressing in to her mouth and watching as Rio sucked her offering.

Agatha remained silent as she soon pulled her thumb slowly from Rio’s mouth and placed it in her own. Rio groaned at the sight, moving her hands down to hold Agatha’s hips, pressing them into her own.

“Don’t do that. Not when I can’t… It’s not fair.”

Almost in apology, Agatha kissed her again, softly, chastely. She tucked her head down beside Rio’s on the pillow and Rio sighed out, moving her hands from her hips to wrap her arms securely around her once more.

“Six months,” she whispered close to Rio’s ear. “Six months and then I’ll tell the world I’m yours.”

Rio nodded, squeezed Agatha’s middle. “I’m going to be in LA the whole time. I’ve a shoot in Pasadena after this one. And then just press for the movie and then Christmas in Delaware?”

Agatha nodded this time, idly playing with Rio’s hair by her cheek.

“Your mom can show Nicky what a grandmother should be.”

“She’ll spoil him.”

“She’ll love him.”

Rio could hear the pain in Agatha’s voice, could feel the guilt in her words. She shifted until she could turn her head properly and be nose to nose with her girlfriend. Agatha was avoiding eye contact but had moved her fingers around to rest against Rio’s cheek.

“You know it isn’t your fault. You didn’t ask to be born into your family.”

“What did she say? What did she say to you? A dog? What else?”

Rio sighed and watched as Agatha raised her gaze up. She’d find out sooner or later so Rio swallowed and whispered, “She called me feral. She threatened to call the police. She… she called me a mongrel, a dog. I was speaking Spanish to Nicky and she… everything racist. Everything heinous. She let go when Nicky was trying to pull me away, when he spoke Spanish without me even prompting. When he said it was okay, that he was there.”

Halfway through Rio’s admission, Agatha had dropped her gaze again, was intent on her lips forming the cruel words her mother had spoken to her. She looked lost, adrift.

“He loves you so much,” Agatha murmured after a few seconds of processing. “I’m sorry she said… I’m sorry she said those things to you.”

“It’s okay. I’ve heard worse.”

Rio tried a smile then, a slow, hopeful one. But Agatha didn’t return it.

It fell again from Rio’s face and she moved them, rolling so she could be on her side and Agatha before her, her arms still around her, Agatha’s weight on her uninjured left.

“You know,” she tired quietly, nudging their noses together. “I’d be your dog, if, if you wanted me to be.”

Agatha’s lost expression changed to a gentle frown and Rio smiled as she soothed out the furrow with her forefinger. “Bark if you wanted me to, get on all fours if-…”

“Don’t try to make light of it.”

“I’m telling you, I’d do anything for you.”

Agatha’s face softened but her words were firm, “It’s not funny and it’s not-…”

Rio made a quiet ruff sound and Agatha did not look impressed but she did it again and unimpressed turned to annoyed.

“Rio.”

“Bark bark bark,” Rio tried, saying the words without making the actual noise.

Agatha began to pull away, shaking her head, but Rio followed her, rolling with her until she was on top of her. She barked properly this time, as well as she could, and leant in to nip at Agatha’s ear, growling teasingly as she did.

Agatha huffed and pushed at her. “It is not funny.”

But Rio persisted, running the risk of annoying Agatha into another meltdown. She growled into her ear, nipping and kissing, and ruffing until, eventually, she got a response other than “Rio”.

Agatha had grunted quietly, no, she’d snorted.

Rio backed up, lifting her head to look down at her and saw that Agatha was already rolling her eyes, already blushing. Rio bit the inside of her cheek, and risked it all to utter another: “Bark bark bark.”

“You are so annoying.”

Rio laughed in surprise at the grin now on Agatha’s face and in celebration of that fact she barked as best as she could again and then went right back to her half-growling, half-kissing by Agatha’s ear.

Agatha began to laugh, began to push her away, but less persistently this time. So Rio travelled down her neck, growling and kissing until she nipped and Agatha gasped loudly and Rio stopped what she was doing because if she didn’t she’d never be able to.

She looked up and saw Agatha biting the corner of her lip, her eyes wide.

“Not tonight.”

Rio nodded infinitesimally and then placed an apology in the form of a kiss to Agatha’s jaw. She rolled over again, tugging Agatha with her until they were both back on their sides, their noses almost touching.

Agatha was no longer lost, at least, she was smiling, her fingers brushing the hair back from Rio’s pleased face. “You’re an idiot.”

“Your idiot.”

“My idiot.”

Rio hummed as Agatha kissed her and for a second everything was good again. They were just two idiots in love, warm under a heavy duvet, comfortable in each other’s arms. Agatha nuzzled in, nuzzled down until she was pressed into Rio’s neck and Rio had her tucked below her chin.

They were quiet for a while and Rio hoped she could lull Agatha to sleep by toying with the ends of her hair but Agatha soon whispered, “Would you have agreed if I’d asked? If I’d have put you down to take Nicky if I died?”

Rio’s eyes fluttered shut and her fingers paused where they were toying with Agatha’s hair. She felt Agatha shift closer and reminded herself it wasn’t real. It was just a question. Agatha was here.

“Baby.”

“I know. I just… I wanted to.”

“I know,” Rio murmured quietly, ducking down to kiss Agatha’s head. She held her lips there until she was able to say, “Please never speak about you dying again. I’ve only just found you. I can’t lose you.”

“Okay,” Agatha whispered back, her hand slipping below Rio’s shirt at her hip to brush along her skin.

“But I’d do anything for that boy. Anything for you.”

Agatha nodded, her thumb brushing across Rio’s skin until eventually, the movement faded and then stopped. Agatha’s breathing became heavier and Rio knew she was asleep.

Rio held her close but couldn’t drift off. All she could do was lay there, wishing the months would fly by and Agatha’s fears with them.

An hour after Agatha had slipped into sleep, Rio heard the door opening, she heard the soft padding of feet on the plush carpet and soon saw a little boy standing before her by the bed. Nicky rubbed at his eye and Rio reached her hand towards him to welcome him in.

He clambered up and shuffled over to the two in the middle of the bed.

“Mama’s sleeping?”

“Yes, mellizo. Fast asleep.”

Nicky nodded and lay so he was pressed behind his mom, curling around her as best he could. Agatha, whether the noise of him arriving or the dip of the mattress had alerted her, made a soft noise and began to turn towards him, making Nicky shift back.

“Honey.”

Rio smiled idly as Agatha turned fully to her son, as she curled herself around him but reached a hand back to find Rio in a silent request. Rio shuffled back in, tucked her arm around Agatha, and, warm as ducklings, they all soon fell asleep.

In the morning, two of the ducklings were gone, and Rio woke to a dull headache and an aching in her chest. She rolled over, inhaled the soft scent that lingered from Agatha’s perfume. It acted as a relaxant, a remedy to her aching.

But it didn’t cure it.

With little reluctance, because she knew what she was getting up for, she rolled from the bed and went to brush her teeth and wash her face. She looked drawn, tired, and in looking down at her arm she saw the red, tender mark of the first cut. Her bandaid had fallen off in the night.

She hesitated, but not for long. She peeled every bandaid off and grit her teeth at the sting of it. Each little cut was red, the skin around them equally so. She jabbed at the first and felt the pain of it. But, not learning her lesson, jabbed each of them in turn just to see.

All hurt. She ran them under cold water just so she could placate Agatha by telling her she’d cleaned them. Far from healing, they were reminders of the bad day yesterday. And Rio wished she hadn’t removed the bandaids.

Downstairs now, she followed the smell of breakfast and found Nicky and Agatha at the small table in the kitchen. Agatha was sipping coffee and Nicky was tucking into his plate of pancakes, the sheen of syrup across his grinning lips.

“Morning, melliza!”

“Morning, mellizo.”

Agatha held up the green medical bag she’d used the day before and pursed her lips. “Seems Alice was right.”

Rio rolled her eyes but, with her tail between her legs, she went to sit beside Agatha, already offering her her arm. Agatha huffed as she removed the antiseptic wipes and applied them to Rio’s raw skin.

Rio fought the grimace and tried instead to focus on the fact that Agatha had pressed her thigh against her own.

She stole her coffee and took a sip. Agatha grumbled but continued her work.

“You were snoring last night,” Nicky said, grinning around his fork as he took another bite of syrupy pancake.

“I don’t believe you! I don’t snore!”

“Maybe it was mama.”

“Your mama doesn’t snore either,” Agatha pointed out, brandishing a bandaid in Nicky’s direction. He giggled and stabbed his fork into his next bite.

“Maybe I dreamt it.”

“Probably. Like sometimes I dream that my mellizo offers me a bite of his pancake.”

Nicky grinned and offered her his next bite, which Rio gladly took as Agatha placed the third bandaid across her arm.

“Do you think these will last the rest of the day? Think you can control yourself?”

Rio chewed her mouthful and pretended to think about it, “I’m sure I can manage it.”

“Are you?”

“No but I will try.”

Agatha scoffed, placing the last bandaid on her arm as Rio took another sip of her coffee. “I won’t be around today to monitor so I’m leaving Nicky in charge.”

Rio almost choked on her, actually Agatha’s, coffee and her head whipped around to look at the woman now stealing her mug back from her.

“Where are you going?”

“I just need to work,” Agatha said, her tone more gentle now, her hand slipping down to Rio’s elbow where it remained. “I have a few phone calls to make and-…”

“How is it? How is…” Rio glanced at Nicky. “How is everything?”

Agatha looked at her for a second but it was enough time for Rio to know that ‘it’, that ‘everything’, wasn’t good. Rio cleared her throat, she slid her hand beneath the table and held Agatha’s leg, giving her as much reassurance as she could with Nicky happily eating his pancakes opposite them.

“We were just talking about what a divorce means,” Agatha said, pivoting the subject, but only slightly.

“Oh?”

“Nicky was asking about his dad. About whether or not he’ll see him again.”

Rio nodded, looking between Agatha and Nicky. Nicky gulped down what looked to have been a large mouthful of pancake and said: “Mama said I didn’t have to if I didn’t want to. And I think maybe I don’t. Or, maybe, right now I don’t. I don’t think that… I think maybe…”

Nicky frowned down at his fork and Rio squeezed Agatha’s thigh.

“I think maybe daddy will be okay if I don’t see him. Maybe for a while anyway. Maybe forever. I want to stay with mama and… my melliza.”

Rio nodded and felt her heart constrict in her chest at the admission.

As Agatha slid across her mug to Rio she slipped her other hand over to find Rio’s below the table and squeezed it, silently asking her to turn it so they could link fingers.

“Are you okay, mellizo? You look like you’re thinking really hard about something.”

Nicky nodded and stabbed another piece of pancake as he turned over Rio’s question in his mind. Rio began to rub Agatha’s hand with her thumb, and felt Agatha’s other hand land on her arm, holding her more fully as Nicky continued to think.

“I keep thinking I should be sad but… I’m not sad about daddy.”

“You’re not?”

“No. I… no not about daddy.”

Agatha cleared her throat quietly and said: “Will you tell Rio what you told me, honey?”

Nicky glanced up, looking at his mama for a second before he looked around to Rio. “I said, I said that, that maybe, maybe, maybe two mamas would be better than… than mama and daddy.”

Agatha’s hand travelled up Rio’s arm and curled around her bicep, now in view of the little boy staring across the table at her, his round eyes cautious but bravely looking on anyway. Rio nodded, feeling that longing in her chest breathe life into her body once more.

“I think you might be right.”

She felt Agatha squeeze her arm and glanced at her briefly before she returned her gaze to Nicky.

“Tell you what, whilst your mama is working today, we can do whatever you want. We can watch movies or we can play basketball or we can-…”

“Can we play? To infinity?”

Rio smiled, felt another squeeze to her arm, and then Agatha released her.

“To infinity,” she agreed, watching as Agatha stood from her seat, brushed her hand along her back and disappeared from the room. Nicky returned his attention to his pancakes then, a little happier than he had been when Rio had arrived.

The topic of conversation changed to their game and after five minutes of discussing whether or not they’d hit infinity before lunch, Agatha had returned with another coffee and a plate of pancakes.

“Eat. Drink. Don’t smash any windows.”

Rio got a kiss to the cheek and then Nicky did and as Agatha was leaving she looked back from the door and shot Rio a timid smile before she disappeared off.

They didn’t see Agatha for the rest of the morning. Rio smiled and laughed and played but actually worried and stressed and pined. She knew Agatha was dealing with whatever was being flung her way by the press, the fans, Ralph, and Evanora. And she knew she was dealing with it alone.

It was on point eighty seven, just before one o’clock, when the sun was high in the sky and Rio’s stomach was beginning to crave something that she saw someone other than Nicky on the small ‘court’ at the back of the house.

“Hey, room for one more?”

Rio missed her jump shot when she heard Alice’s voice. She looked over and raised her brows at the sight of her friend looking tired and a little frazzled.

“Alice!” Nicky. He beamed at her, “You can play but only if you agree to help us get to infinity!”

“Cariño,” Rio advised quietly, moving over to her manager with a small frown, “How is it?”

Nicky collided with her side, out of breath and excitable. “You wanna play?”

He held on to Rio and Rio placed her hand on his head but focused in on Alice who’d smiled at Nicky and nodded, “In a sec, kid, okay? Can I steal Rio for a bit?”

“Okay, but bring her back please.”

Rio smiled, ruffled Nicky’s hair and then followed Alice into the house. She closed the sliding glass door but kept Nicky in her sights as he ran to fetch the errant ball and continued in his quest for infinity.

“Tell me. I haven’t had a chance to-…”

“It’s hell. It’s everywhere. Jen’s phone’s been practically unusable because everyone wants a quote, everyone wants a piece of the action.”

Rio’s gaze moved slowly from Nicky now taking a shot to Alice. “What’s everyone saying?”

Alice sighed and rubbed the back of her neck. Rio looked back out to Nicky.

“Golden couple bullshit, mostly. There’s think pieces and podcasts and… god fucking knows what. That cunt’s released a statement and-…”

Rio’s eyes flashed back to Alice. “What? What did she say?”

Her empty stomach churned around nothing and she found she’d reached for the glass door, just for something solid, just for something to keep her steady.

“Bullshit,” Alice grumbled, already tapping at her phone to bring up the cunt’s, Evanora’s, statement.

“I am heartbroken to witness my daughter’s very public unravelling. This abrupt decision to dismantle the family she so proudly built was made without my counsel or blessing.

Marriage is not a costume to be discarded when the spotlight shifts, nor is motherhood a role one steps away from when it grows inconvenient.

I raised Agatha to honour her vows, especially those made before God, and I can only pray she remembers the sacred promises she once asked the world to celebrate.

For my beloved grandson, Nicholas’s sake, as well as my adored son-in-law, I hope she finds her way back to God’s love and the values she once held dear. I hope she chooses restoration over spectacle.”

Rio had been growing steadily warmer, steadily angrier with every word from Alice’s mouth. She could feel the heat reach boiling point by the time she uttered the word “motherhood”. Then Alice finished. Sealing the statement with one, final thought: “cunt”.

But Rio was lost, lost to her anger, her desire to rip the throat out of Evanora Harkness.

“Look after Nicky.”

She turned away, ignoring Alice’s shouts, and marched off to find Agatha. It didn’t take long. Agatha’s office was the only room in the house with the door closed. Besides, she could hear Jen’s voice.

She didn’t bother to knock before entering.

“I really think-… Jesus, Rio!” Jen.

“Alice showed you?” Agatha. She spoke as if she’d been expecting it. As if she’d simply been waiting for Rio to barge in here.

She was sat behind her desk, wearing Rio’s cowboy shirt, another pair of glasses on, her face eerily calm.

Rio couldn’t find the words so nodded instead.

“I told her not to,” Jen said with a sigh, moving behind Rio to shut the door so they couldn’t be overheard.

Rio gulped down her fury, unable to look away from Agatha, even as Agatha dropped her gaze to the desk before her.

Jen’s hand on her arm made her jump and she looked around to Agatha’s best friend. Jen smiled, a tight, tense sort of smile. “We’ll get her, don’t worry. The god stuff only plays well with a certain generation, or fucking morons. The internet is on our side.”

Rio nodded absently, her lips sparking to life but not quite managing to form a smile. Jen released her arm and walked back over to her seat opposite Agatha and Rio followed her but went around the desk and crouched beside Agatha’s chair instead.

“¿Estás bien, mi vida?”

Rio reached for the hem of the now shared shirt, rubbing the thin fabric between her thumb and forefinger. As she waited for a response her eyes dropped and she saw a drop of blood on the sleeve.

She hoped Agatha hadn’t spotted it.

“Nothing I wasn’t expecting.”

“That isn’t what I asked.”

She looked back up again and Agatha was avoiding her gaze, but her hand had moved to take Rio’s from her shirt and she raised it to kiss over her knuckles. She was tense, that much Rio could tell. No matter how soft she was trying to be.

“Agatha.”

“Don’t.”

“Rio, why don’t you go have lunch with Nicky and Alice?”

Rio glanced at Jen then looked back to Agatha and saw her working her jaw. She stood up and said: “I can stay?”

“No,” Agatha said quickly, still not looking. “It’s fine. Go be with Nicky. I’ll be out later.”

Rio nodded slowly, absently now tapping the desk beside her. “Will I bring food? Anything in particular you-…?”

“God, Rio. Can you just-…. fuck just stop being so fucking-…”

Rio’s eyes went wide as Agatha slammed her hand down in the desk she’d just been tapping. She remained silent as Jen stood from her seat and stepped from the room, muttering that she’d give them a sec.

Agatha was now pinching the bridge of her nose, her glasses on her head but pushed up in such a rush they now slipped back down and smacked her fingers.

Rio cleared her throat and moved around the desk, taking a second to breathe as she settled into the chair Jen had just vacated.

“I know this is a lot,” she started slowly, leaning forwards on her elbows and placing her fingers together before her. They formed nature’s strongest shape, a triangle. Three points. Tres patitos.

Her thumbs touched then broke apart.

“I know that-…”

“Can you shout?”

Rio looked up, the tips of her fingers still pressed together. Agatha’s glasses were fully off now. They were on the desk, beside where her fingers lay. Rio straightened her back. The top of the triangle broke as she did.

“No.”

Agatha slapped the table again. “Shout.”

“No.”

She slapped it again but the fire was already dying and Rio watched it spark, fizzle, and then fade. Agatha lifted her hands up and hid her face and Rio only watched, she waited. It took a minute, a thousand erratic heartbeats, for Agatha to speak again.

“I’m sorry.”

But Rio wanted to see her, wanted her not to hide. So she remained silent.

Another thousand heartbeats later and Agatha revealed herself, looking across at Rio with storm glass eyes. Rio forced a slight smile and it was enough to make Agatha move. She stood from her seat and came around to be welcomed in to Rio’s arms.

She sat side on in Rio’s lap and rested their temples together, her hand finding Rio’s chest and resting there as she just breathed with her for a little while.

Rio could feel her frustration, feel her shame, feel everything Agatha felt just in sharing time and space with her. It took a couple minutes but eventually Agatha spoke again. Her voice sounded rough, as if she’d been sleeping and had just woken up.

“I’m sorry. I’m sorry.”

Rio nodded, careful not to move too much with Agatha’s temple still against her own. Agatha’s hand moved to curl around the back of Rio’s head and she cradled her there though Rio had no intention of moving.

“Tell me what’s happening. Share it with me. Let me carry it with you. For you. Let me help.”

Agatha sighed and closed her eyes and Rio took the opportunity to lean in and kiss her. Agatha’s lips quirked into a smile, a faint one. But it gave Rio hope. She leant in again and murmured, “Let me be your guard dog.”

“Rio.”

Rio grinned and nipped playfully at Agatha’s lips. She growled, hoping for the reaction she got; Agatha smiling, Agatha moving her hand around to hold her cheek, Agatha kissing her again.

“So stupid.”

Rio hummed happily as Agatha bestowed kiss upon kiss to her lips. She held her a little closer and nudged their noses together, taking a second to enjoy it before she spoke again.

“You don’t need to go through this alone. I’m here. I want to help.”

“I know,” Agatha murmured. “I’ve just never… it’s just always been me.”

“And now it’s us.”

Agatha sighed and closed her eyes. She moved her head down to rest on Rio’s shoulder and Rio pulled her back with her as she lay back in the chair. Agatha shifted against her and Rio was the one who sighed this time. She ran her hand up and down Agatha’s back. She dreamt of a time on a terrace where, warm under a blanket, she held Agatha like this.

Back then Agatha was keeping a secret from her.

Right now Agatha was keeping her pain from her.

The memory of the former wasn’t as painful as the acknowledgment of the latter.

“I won’t run, you know. However ugly it gets. However… however hard it becomes. I’ll always be here.”

There was a knock at the door and Agatha pulled back, looked at Rio, a portrait of hurt and hesitance that made Rio’s heart ache. Agatha’s thumb traced her cheek and she leant into it.

“Your mom called me this morning.”

It hadn’t been what Rio was expecting Agatha to say but she nodded all the same. “She did?”

“She asked if I were going to make an honest woman out of you.”

It took a second to register and then Rio’s mouth fell open. Agatha smiled at the sight.

“I told her I was.”

“Mi vida.”

“I told her I wanted to marry her daughter and I hoped, I hoped she would approve.”

Rio shifted beneath Agatha, lost her breath suddenly.

“She said she always had and-…”

“Agatha.”

Agatha didn’t correct her this time, recognising that Rio was struggling to keep a handle on her feelings all of a sudden. Rio swallowed a gasp, almost feeling lightheaded as Agatha continued to caress her cheek.

“Are you mad?”

It was a different question to her earlier request for Rio to shout. This time she didn’t want her to be. Rio could only shake her head, only hold Agatha tighter.

The idea of her mom calling Agatha because she’d heard the news… calling Agatha and just knowing, calling Agatha and asking.

“My mom loves you. My dad-…”

Rio shook her head, fighting the tears that were already forming. Agatha nodded, understanding what went unsaid. She kissed Rio as the first tear fell. She pressed in, brushed the next tear away with her thumb.

There was another knock.

Agatha pulled back, rested their temples together once more and brushed away the evidence of Rio’s grief from her cheeks. Rio trembled beneath her, and Agatha kissed her again, distracting her nervous system.

Rio exhaled slowly when Agatha pulled away and closed her eyes. She felt Agatha wipe at her cheeks once more, felt her adjust her hair, felt a soft kiss to her temple.

“Go get some lunch. Go hit infinity with Nicky. I won’t hide away all day. I promise.”
