Rio nodded, she opened her eyes. Agatha was smiling, a parting gift as she slipped from her lap and went back around to her seat behind the desk. Rio took a breath. She stood and went to the door.

She let Jen in, acknowledged the hand that touched her arm, and then left without looking back.

When she found Alice again she found her with Nicky in the kitchen, slicing up bread as Nicky washed his hands in the sink.

“Hey. Did, did my mom call?”

“Rio,” Alice said with a surprised smile, “Yes. I’ve spoken to her twice. She,” Alice paused and glanced in Nicky’s direction. “She just wanted to check things were good. Y’know.”

Rio nodded and ran a hand through her hair. A body collided with hers and Nicky was against her, smiling up at her. His hands were a little damp as they held her sides. “Is mama okay?”

“All good, mellizo.”

“Alice said that we’re getting more alike.”

“Did she?”

Nicky nodded and hugged Rio properly, turning his head to look at Alice as Rio draped her arms around him.

“It’s because he is also a show off.”

Rio narrowed her eyes and ducked down to whisper in Nicky’s ear, making sure Alice could still hear. “Alice is just jealous because we’re better at ball than she is.”

“Not true!”

Nicky giggled and Rio grinned as she ruffled his hair.

The early afternoon continued to go a lot like that. Nicky was true to his nickname. He followed Rio around like the little duckling he was. The only time she was allowed to be more than two feet away from him was when she went to the bathroom.

Otherwise he was with her all the time.

Even Alice began to refer to him as “el patito” and Nicky wore it as a badge of pride.

By five, Agatha appeared in the main house again. She slipped onto the couch and threw herself over Rio who caught her readily, held her willingly. Nicky, close by Rio’s side, waded his way in. To make room for ducklings, Rio heaved them all over and ignored Jen’s comment about it being: “so fucking gay.”

Nicky was giggling and Agatha was grinning and that was all that mattered.

“You need to eat something,” Rio said as her hand found Agatha’s stomach and she pressed a kiss to her cheek.

“Happy where I am, thank you.”

Rio hummed as Nicky copied her and kissed his mom’s cheek too, finding the hand that rested on Agatha’s stomach still. “Eat something and I promise we can do this all night. Tell your mama, Nicky. She needs to eat.”

Nicky nodded and did exactly as he was told. “Mama, melliza says you need to eat.”

Agatha huffed, “Turning my son against me?”

“It wasn’t hard to do,” Rio grinned and kissed Agatha’s cheek again before she sat up sharply so she was out of reach of Agatha’s glare. Nicky did the same and it made Rio laugh, made her almost delirious with the joy of it.

They both then scrambled away only to have Agatha shout after them: “You are both in big trouble!”

In the kitchen, with the littlest duckling, Rio set about making food for Agatha. She rummaged about in the fridge after she’d helped Nicky jump up onto the counter. But Agatha was hot on their heels and an arm wrapped around her from behind, a voice low in her ear, just for her.

“Pour me wine? I’ll cook. An apology for earlier. Jen and Alice are leaving. I want to eat and then lay on the couch with you for the rest of the night.”

An offer, it turned out, Rio couldn’t refuse. She grinned and stepped aside. In under ten minutes they’d said their goodbyes to Jen and Alice. Alice had reminded Rio she’d be picking her up at four the next morning. Jen had reminded Agatha about the protocol for taking Nicky to school the next day and Rio had distracted Nicky when words like “security”, “paps”, “perimeter” were being thrown about like it was the most natural thing in the world.

As if any of this were natural

As if any of this were normal

As if any of this were fair.

And then they were alone. Tres patitos dancing in the kitchen to Freddie Mercury.

Nicky turned out to be an exceptional air drummer as well as air guitarist and Agatha surprised them both with her belting. Which led to a pile on against the fridge, benefitting Rio the most as she could steal a kiss when Nicky buried his face between them both.

Turns out ‘I Was Born To Love You’ were more than just lyrics. Rio felt it in her bones as she huddled with her two favourite people, as Agatha kissed by her ear and whispered the bridge to her even though the song had ended, an another had begun: “I wanna love you, I love every little thing about you.”

It was the happiest three and a half minutes of the last two days.

Nicky, as much as he enjoyed the hugging, wanted more. So they moved through Queen’s back catalogue and Agatha soon peeled off the lead vocals to actually make the dinner. But Rio and Nicky picked up what she’d put down.

They rocked that kitchen and the house hidden in the hills became their own personal Wembley.

Even as they ate Nicky hummed Freddie’s finest and Rio teased that when he was older he could grow a moustache just like his new hero. She’d borrowed a piece of Agatha’s hair to give herself a tache which made him dissolve into so many giggles it took him five minutes before he could take another bite.

Their pasta eaten, the dishes in the dishwasher, they all piled onto the sofa. Rio first, Agatha next, and Nicky tucked in with his mom. It was squashed, warm, but more comfortable than Rio could even explain.

Like the night before, Rio soon carried Nicky up to bed and Agatha tucked him in. They stood together as the stars filled the room and Rio silently counted them as Agatha leant back against her and instead watched her son.

“He wants another mama. He wants you.”

Rio nodded, giving up her quest as she rested her cheek against Agatha. “I know.”

“Take me to bed?”

Rio nodded again and slowly pulled away, turning Agatha as she did. She walked her through to the bedroom she knew was theirs, was always meant to be theirs. And she tugged Agatha with her to brush her teeth alongside her, to wash her face and then to kiss all over Agatha’s cleansed one.

They fell into bed in their matching pyjamas and Rio wrapped herself so tightly around Agatha she worried she was making her too warm. But Agatha didn’t protest. She just smiled, just pressed close, just squeezed Rio’s bicep.

“How bad is it?”

She wanted to get it out there, she wanted to get it out the way before the pull of sleep became too tempting.

“Ralph’s helped by being caught out for dinner with some pretty young thing when he was served. The internet seems to mostly hate my mother, apart from a few pockets who adore her. But I’m being accused of using Nicky for sympathy. Of acting the victim.”

Rio looked down and began to toy with the ends of Agatha’s hair.

“Jen thinks we’re winning right now but it’s not really started.”

She nodded, allowed Jen’s assessment of the situation to cool her fires.

“And how do you feel?”

Agatha released a heavy breath and Rio looked back up to see Agatha had closed her eyes. She was pale in the dark of the room. Her features were tightly drawn, as if the artist were running out of ink but needed to finish his masterpiece.

“My love,” Rio whispered, seeing the way Agatha responded with a twitch of her brow. She was far away again, barely within reaching distance. But Rio reached for her all the same.

“Tell me how you feel.”

“I feel like,” Agatha began, “like I’m trying to lay the pieces of a puzzle only all the pieces are blank.” Her eyes flashed open and Rio smiled for it. “But the colour comes back when I’m with you, and Nicky.”

“Your duckling and your dog.”

Agatha seemed to freeze for a second and then she laughed. And Rio beamed and she pressed closer and rolled them until she was over Agatha, her knees by her hips.

“Which is ironic because dogs can’t see colour.”

“Stop with the dog!”

Agatha was pink again, at least, her cheeks were. The colour had come back to the canvas. The artist’s ink had returned because she was smiling, she was practically grinning as she tugged Rio down into a searing kiss.

Rio tasted the colour of Agatha on her tongue. She moaned as it spilled into her mouth, hers alone to swallow.

And when they broke apart she traced their hue across Agatha’s waiting lips.

Beneath the heavy duvet their bodies were warm, too close. But Rio didn’t pull back for air. She could only press closer, her hot tongue finishing its tasting of Agatha’s lips.

“Rio,” Agatha groaned out, squirming a little beneath her, the rogue of her cheeks escaping down her chest. “Please, my love.”

In the dark of the room, Rio found the light. It was in Agatha’s eyes as they widened and ultimately closed when she slid her hands into her pants. It was in the feel of her, soaked and aching, as she traced her favourite pattern. It was in the soft moans and whimpers that escaped Agatha’s swollen lips as she fucked her.

Rio nipped at Agatha’s jaw, nuzzled into her ear, moaned when Agatha bucked her hips into her hand.

Agatha was trying her best to be quiet but her nails were on Rio’s back and scratched where she couldn’t shout. Rio curled her fingers and brushed her thumb alongside Agatha’s clit. She bit the inside of her cheek as a means to steady her own desire and whispered into Agatha’s ear: “Soy tu perro. Ladro por ti. Muerdo por ti.” I am your dog. I bark for you. I bite for you.

Agatha released a broken moan and Rio nipped at her ear.

She began to swirl her clit, being rougher now, intent on making Agatha come as much as she could handle.

As if orgasms could cure the pain of the past few days, the agony of a life lived in secret.

Agatha arched up, her breathing laboured, shallow.

The door opened.

Rio fell off of Agatha.

Agatha sat up quickly, her eyes wide again, the blush across her skin deepening as Nicky stepped cautiously into the room.

“Can I sleep here?”

Rio wiped her hand against her pants and shuffled along slightly, needing space to breathe and calm her racing heart. Agatha beside her just nodded, just held her arms out to Nicky and he hurried over and clambered into the bed beside her, clutching Scratchy to him.

Rio let the both settle, staring up at the ceiling. She knew the ache between her legs would be nothing now to Agatha’s but she could do nothing about either as she curled back around and placed her hand lightly on Agatha’s hip.

Agatha didn’t move for a moment but then she felt her shuffling back, pressing into Rio. Rio took it for what it was, an encouragement to be closer. So she moved in, she curled around Agatha. And Agatha took her hand and cradled it to her chest.

Rio sighed happily, despite the ache.

She kissed the exposed skin at the back of Agatha’s neck. She fell asleep with her fellow cowboys, warm and safe.

At four, an alarm went off and shocked all three of them awake. Rio blindly reached for it, finding it to be Agatha’s phone on the side. She shut it off and then groaned as she curled back in around Agatha, finding she was on her back now and Rio could press in to her chest.

“Why’re we awake?” Nicky, groggily.

“Rio has to go, honey.”

Rio huffed and lifted her head from its favourite cushion. “Not for five minutes.”

“Alice will be here.”

Rio huffed again but as she turned and her eyes adjusted to the light of the early morning she saw the pain in Agatha’s tired features. She didn’t want her to go.

Nicky reached for her shoulder and Rio turned them to him and saw his mother’s pain reflected in his wide eyes.

“You’ll come back?”

“I-…”

“Yes, honey. She’ll be back.”

“Tonight?”

“No, baby.”

Rio cleared her throat and sat up. She’d not thought past last night. Not thought past being curled up with Agatha in their hideaway. Clearly Nicky hadn’t either.

“Mi vida?” Nicky asked, the tiredness and shock to waking making him confused, making his eyes well up as he rubbed at them. “Why can’t you come back?”

Rio leant over Agatha, she rested on her knees to get to Nicky, to pull him to her in an off-balance, one-armed hug. “I’ll be back soon. I promise. I’m never leaving my patitos.”

Nicky sniffed unhappily and clutched to her. She felt Agatha’s hand against her thigh and heard her quiet voice, “I’ll figure something out. We’ll figure it out.”

Even as Rio pulled back from Nicky she didn’t think Agatha sounded very sure. She looked to her, saw the pain and fear as plain as the light of day in her face. But all she could do was kiss her cheek, was be so close to her lips she almost gave up the pretence.

“Call me. I’ll answer. I’ll have my cell-…”

“Take your shirt? Wear it today? I’ll come to your trailer. We need… we can talk later.”

Rio smiled sadly and nodded. Agatha released where she’d been holding Rio’s collar and let her go. Once her feet were on solid ground she found it difficult to make herself move. And Nicky’s whisper didn’t help.

“I love you, m-melliza. Please come back.”

Rio turned and almost climbed right back into the bed. Nicky was now tucked where she had just been against Agatha. They looked cosy and warm and Rio wanted to stay like that with them for the rest of the day.

For the rest of her life.

But her job now was to keep them safe. And being apart from them was part of that.

“I love you too.”

Her eyes fell to Agatha and she managed a smile, managed to mouth the words to her too. She left with the shirt they shared and a breaking heart.

She grabbed the little bag she’d brought with her, changed into her clothes, and went out to find Alice who was standing by the entrance, looking tired again.

But at least she smiled, at least she was pleased to see her.

“That shirt again?”

“It’s Agatha’s,” Rio said by way of explanation.

Alice said nothing as she walked them out to the car. Nearby, Rio could see the telltale signs of security. She counted two unmarked SUVs along the road. It did not make her feel any better.

Once in Alice’s car, Rio looked out towards her own, sitting untouched in the place she’d left it. “Will you get someone to come and tow my car?”

“Tow it?”

“I’m getting a new one. It’s not safe enough for Nicky.”

“What are you even talking about?”

Rio said nothing in response.

“We think it’s best if-…”

Alice’s tone had been soft, as if she herself were reluctant to say anything. But Rio had shaken her head before she could finish. So she’d stopped.

For the first time in two days, not under Agatha’s instructions, Rio had a phone in her hand again. She tapped in her passcode, idly wondering how it was that it was fully charged.

But then: Agatha. She’d have done it.

Rio had promised her she’d be available whenever she needed. That she could call, that she’d answer. Agatha had just anticipated she’d need a little kickstart to make good on her promise.

The threatening dots she’d seen in Agatha’s phone were all present on her own too. And buried in there somewhere were Anna’s attempts to contact her. She’d have to call her today. She’d have to make up for being a bad daughter.

Though, at least, she thought, Agatha was a good daughter-in-law.

But she hadn’t turned on her phone to seek anyone out, or even to call her mom. Instead she’d turned it on to look something up. She’d had something swimming around in her brain ever since Agatha had said it.

It gave her something to focus on now. Something other than Nicky’s tears that morning. Something other than knowing how afraid Agatha was when she left.

Her stomach churned. Her head ached. Her heart yearned.

She tapped into Google and searched.

Alice pulled away. They drove past the men hired to keep her family safe.

Rio read the results, focusing on what she found so she didn’t have to focus on the flash of pain in her head, the aching in her chest, the bandaids she wanted to rip.

Chapter End Notes

I hope this is still interesting/enjoyable to people thank you all for reading

Chapter 47: Happiest Place On Earth

Chapter Summary

A week after the divorce announcement.

Chapter Notes

Started Writing.

Had a breakdown.

Bon appetit.

DISCLAIMER: I've used some oomf's twitter handles in this but they DID NOT write the tweets. All my bad.

See the end of the chapter for more notes

MONDAY

EXCLUSIVE

AGATHA HARKNESS FILES FOR DIVORCE FROM FINANCIER HUSBAND

TMZ has learned the Oscar winner has filed from divorce from her husband of sixteen years, Ralph Bohner.

According to reports, the two have been living separate lives for more than a decade with Agatha living with her son on the West Coast and Ralph living in a bachelor pad in Manhattan.

Sources close to the pair suggest this has been a long time coming.

TMZ can also confirm that Agatha is looking for full custody of her son, Nicholas, 8.

The couple have a prenup.

They say that good news travels fast.

But Rio couldn’t help but think that good gossip traveled faster.

In the makeup chair that morning, coffee in hand, heart stuck somewhere in the hills, Rio Vidal couldn’t get away from the news that Agatha Harkness was divorcing her husband.

She placed her phone down, having been staring at it all morning. Reading, learning, etching into her heart.

She glanced up, her hair now at odd angles, her dark eyes sweeping the trailer around her through the mirror before her.

“Honestly, I know she’s, you know, strong-willed, but to let Agatha Harkness go he must be a fucking idiot!”

Brett scoffed where he was busy fluffing Rio’s hair, only half-focused in on his work as he gossiped with the other stylists.

“And who was that hottie he was with?! Surely she’s the reason.”

Rio looked down at her coffee cup. She wondered where Agatha was now. She wondered if Nicky were being subjected to any of this chatter at school.

She made a note to ask Jen just how much of a security presence would be around him. She hoped a lot. She hoped enough.

The woman with the smirk and the red hair wasn’t far from her mind.

“Let’s take bets on her mood today.”

“No! On how many runners she makes cry!”

Rio cleared her throat purposefully and placed her coffee down on the counter. She made eyes at Brett through the mirror and he had the humility to look a little shame-faced. Though it wasn’t enough shame for Rio’s liking.

“How about,” he spoke again, now running his hands through Rio’s hair and smoothing the lumps and bumps of it, “How about we cut her a little slack? See how she is? Try not to piss her off or-…”

The door opened.

The trailer went silent.

Rio pulled away and turned to see Agatha stepping into the space. Behind her, by the door, she caught Jen’s eye and Agatha’s manager nodded once at her. It was a subtle sign that everything was okay.

Nicky was safe.

Rio settled back in her chair but kept her gaze on the movie star who’d just arrived.

Agatha looked as she always did, as if nothing very interesting had happened to her that weekend. She held her head high, her jaw set.

She was wearing her glasses and her face was makeup free and she still looked like she’d rocked up from some photoshoot Rio would kill to be a voyeur at.

She had a cup of coffee already in her hand, and script tucked under her arm. She didn’t look at Rio. But Rio was already moving to her. She was by her shoulder before the people around them had the decency to pick up the conversation again.

“Agatha,” she said, now with her hand on Agatha’s shoulder and her eyes on her through the mirror where Agatha was now perched in her seat. “How is… how are you?”

“Fine,” Agatha said in a gentler voice than anyone, including Rio, was expecting. “I’m okay.”

Rio nodded and shot Agatha the smallest of smiles. She squeezed her shoulder and Agatha, still watching her, lifting her hand to touch her. It was brief, but it was everything.

Rio went to take her seat back up and for the rest of her time in hair and makeup she could think of nothing other than Agatha’s soft touch to the back of her hand.

She was silent all morning, dreaming of soft touches and softer sighs. No one mentioned the divorce, no one spoke directly to Agatha. Agatha only read her script and looked, every ten seconds or so, across at her phone.

Hair now sitting as hair should, and fingers twitching as she moved, Rio was soon walking past Agatha’s chair again. She reached for her and Agatha knew she would. Their hands met as their eyes did and Rio wanted to ruin everything in that moment by making their lips meet too.

But she held strong. She continued walking.

She let go of Agatha’s hand.

She didn’t get to hold it again until the late afternoon.

Rio was in a scene with Billy that morning. A scene where she was playing the understanding sister-in-law. But being with Billy the first day back on set after Agatha’s big news meant that every second sentence out of Billy’s mouth had either “Agatha”, “divorce”, or even worse, “poor Nicky” in it.

Rio had been mostly tuning him out and talking to the crew for fear she’d stab him with one of the First AD’s pens.

But it was hard going.

At lunchtime she went to find Agatha but found only Jen and was told she was still filming.

Rio looked back up again and saw that Agatha’s eyes were down on where she’d been toying with her ring.

“Ah!” Rio jumped up and startled a few crew members milling about them, but Agatha’s almost shy expression had disappeared to something far more indulgent.

“Mics,” Rio reminded, now blushing for the scene she’d created.

“Mmhmm,” Agatha hummed with more than a hint of smugness. “Gotcha, cowboy.”

Rio scowled and sat back down again. Frankie ran back over and fussed about her for a while until places were called and Rio had to pretend not to feel like a cowboy who’d forgotten his spurs.

Rio scowled and Alice raised her brows expectantly. But then she sighed and turned to let them both in to the trailer. It gave Rio just seconds to try to think on the words to express her intense disinterest in the idea.

Rio hung up and her whole body seemed to sag in her seat. She stared at her knees and just knew Jen was right.

That fucker was making her wait.

So Rio would give her time to heal, time to recuperate.

TUESDAY

Vanity Fair

Agatha Harkness and Ralph Bohner Have Separated

One of Hollywood’s longest-reigning power couples have reportedly split after almost two decades together.

A source confirms that Agatha Harkness filed for divorce this past weekend while, according to TMZ, the couple have been living separate lives for the majority of their marriage.

The couple share a son together, Nicholas, and have long since earned a reputation of being one of the industry’s most powerful and happy couples.

In 2022, Harkness spoke to the UK’s The Guardian about the similarities between working on film projects and marriage: “It’s not all good days. It’s hard and exhausting so you have to focus on the good things within those days. On set that might be one good take after a heavy day. Agatha dropped her gaze and Rio shifted so that Agatha’s hold around her middle tightened and Rio’s heart plummeted.

“What is it?”

“Nothing.”

Rio was still for a second, and as silence descended upon them Rio’s heart rate picked steadily up. She shifted again. She couldn’t have moved more than an inch. She’d moved up, slightly away, but not really. A movement. Not a pull back.

But Agatha’s reaction spoke louder than words ever could.

She’d panicked immediately and that’s how Rio knew that “nothing” was absolute bullshit.

She settled down again, settled closer. Agatha’s panic had resulted in a vicelike hold around Rio’s middle. A natural reaction of someone who gained comfort from having her close, now being afraid she’d pull away.

“What’s happened in therapy?”

“Nothing.”

Rio leant in again, nuzzled their noses like two kittens might. Agatha’s hold relaxed. Rio simply breathed with her for a while and reached down and between them to find the opening of Agatha’s robe.

Beneath the blankets she threw it over herself and in that way got closer to Agatha, sliding her leg between her girlfriend’s so they could be properly wrapped together.

Proximity helped them both. But Agatha still remained silent.

“Okay,” Rio whispered after a little while of watching Agatha’s lashes flutter every few seconds as she struggled to hide from Rio behind them. “When you’re ready to talk about it, I’ll be right here.”

Agatha continued to hide from her and so Rio kissed her and whispered to the woman she knew hadn’t slept the previous night: “Go to sleep.”

Agatha’s lashes fluttered again and then she stopped hiding.

Rio smiled as Agatha let her in, took her in. She smiled even as Agatha applied enough pressure to let her know she wanted her to roll. She smiled when Agatha was gone again, when she’d ducked down, when she’d pressed into her neck and lay her weight fully over her.

Her smile faded as Agatha settled and snoozed.

As Agatha slept she brushed her fingers through her hair and thought of a world in which she’d been doing this very thing for close to a decade. It was a world she’d like to be in. A world where Nicky still existed, technically Ralph’s, but all the way Rio’s.

She thought of how easy it would be to have been with Agatha since the beginning.

She thought of the danger always lurking in the shadows now, waiting for them.

Then the more immediate danger of Jen’s mood when they finally emerged from the trailer, of the producers who would fine Agatha, or Maria who might not appreciate her authority being usurped by a moody actress with a flare for disobedience.

But in the here and now they were safe. Agatha was asleep in her arms and nothing, no one, could harm them now.

It was in this time, this sacred time where she could be the one guardian of Agatha’s comfort, when she decided she’d find Agatha something else to comfort her when she was away.

The ring Agatha had been desperate for. A real one.

Something that contained her promise.

Just as she was making plans to either steal Agatha’s current rings to find out the size or bothering Stevie, a noise alerted her to someone else being in the trailer.

Rio’s heart skipped a beat as she held Agatha tighter against her and she held her breath as a soft knock to the bedroom door happened and then half a downturned head could be seen.

A flash of black and bright red.

Alice.

“Can I come in? Is it safe?”

Rio blew out the breath she’d been holding and released her hold on Agatha a little, feeling her grumble and shift against her.

“Agatha’s sleeping. Come in.”

Alice cautiously stepped into full view then and furtively glanced up before she closed the door behind her.

“Jen’s dealing with… they used her stand in. Lilia kicked up a fuss so no fines, it’s all sorted.”

“Really?”

Alice nodded, still trying her best not to look her friend’s way.

“You need to be on set soon, though. I’m not sure Lilia has enough fuss in her to prevent you from getting fined.”

Rio sighed and moved her arms from where they’d been wrapped around Agatha to hold her at her sides instead.

“Give me a second,” she said to Alice, nudging her head towards the door.

Alone again, Rio went through the motions of waking Agatha up as carefully as possible. Agatha was not gracious about being woken, despite it being Rio’s soft kisses to her temple that eventually roused her.

In fact, even after two orgasms and a two hour nap she was back to being a terror.

Rio was subjected to forced cuddling (which she did not mind) that also involved Agatha cursing about people constantly demanding things of her (she minded this slightly more but the cuddling made up for it).

Eventually, Rio now in her clothes again and Agatha grumbling about that, they made it back into the main body of the trailer and Alice, finally, looked up at them both.

“I think you owe Lilia a new shawl or something.”

Agatha scoffed and Rio thought she heard a genuine spark of amusement in it but chastised herself for presuming she now knew Agatha so well she could tell the difference in her scoffs.

Idiot.

Agatha was made, or more, requested very gently by Alice to wait in the trailer whilst Alice took Rio off to hair and make up. And Rio, suggesting she took a quick shower first, had to be just as quick about saying goodbye.

Agatha’s perma-scowl softened as she kissed her, and disappeared entirely when Rio murmured a soft “I love you” against her cheek.

The warmth of Agatha, the soft surprise that sometimes appeared in her gaze when Rio said those words, both of those things gripped Rio’s heart as she left the trailer that day.

Everything after her morning with Agatha felt hollow. Everything felt unmoored.

Only a look from Lilia brought her back round to the real world and to the role she had to play both in the movie and in her real life. All the world’s a stage, but especially when your livelihood was tied to your ability to act on it.

Time ticked on, lines were read, scenes were shot, and Rio was soon released in the early evening. She stopped by Agatha’s trailer but found she wasn’t there.

She’d managed to get Agatha’s ring size from Stevie before she had to hustle to set and so, armed with this new knowledge of her girlfriend, she headed home.

At home Rio checked where Agatha was and, seeing that she was at what must be her doctor’s office, she held off on calling her. Though she itched to.

She instead did some stretches under the tree in her yard whilst it was warm enough to remain outside with just a sweater on. She cooked herself a healthy-ish meal. She ran herself a bath.

And all the while she thought about Agatha, about Nicky, about getting through these next few months together.

Only, she’d already forgotten that her phone had been promised to be glued to her hand. She remembered when she’d already been soaking for ten minutes.

Half the bath water sloshed over the side when she dived for it and amongst the usual noise she saw a dozen texts from Agatha and three missed calls.

Agatha picked up on the first ring as Rio dejectedly settled back in the bath and turned the faucet to begin refilling it.

“Are you okay?”

“I forgot. I was out back and then had dinner and I-…”

“It’s okay, I was just worried that-…”

Rio rubbed at her eyes and then hissed as the sting of soap hit.

“That I’d died and was being eaten by rabid dogs?”

“No, that you wanted some space.”

“So you called me multiples times and left a lot of messages?”

“Well I had to be sure.”

Rio smiled but was now blind in one eye as she crunched her face up and turned off the water again.

“Now you have me, how was therapy?”

“Fine.”

“You wanted to speak to me just to say ‘fine’.”

“I wanted to speak to you to hear your voice.”

Rio splashed some water, rapidly blinking to try and rid herself of the indignity of having soap in her eye at the ripe old age of thirty two.

“Are you in the bath?”

“Mhm. Got soap in my eye.”

“Maybe next time you’re in the bath, I can be the the bath too and we can… get soap other places.”

This made the pain of Rio’s eyes disappear in an instant.

“That would… that would be good.”

“Just good?”

Rio laughed and rubbed her eye with the back of her hand. “I can think of nothing better than you naked and surrounded by bubbles.”

“Better.”

Rio hummed quietly, lazily stroking through the water by her thigh as she relaxed back.

“Did you get in trouble earlier?”

“I’m an adult I don’t get in trouble.”

“You know what I mean.”

“No,” Agatha sighed heavily and Rio imagined her now tossing her hair back. “There was apparently talk of disruptions to schedules but Lilia went off on one about needing more close ups anyway so actually it all worked out.”

Rio smiled as she continued her movements in the water.

“So, maybe we can get some more-…?”

“I want to ask you something. It’s why I’ve been calling, why I’ve been trying to reach you.”

Rio sat up slowly, feeling cold suddenly whilst steam still billowed from the water.

“Of course.”

“I know you can’t… I know you can’t move in. Not with everything and not with Nicky wanting to tell the world about it but… once a week, just once, can you just be here? Be here when I come home, have dinner with us, play basketball with Nicky, sleep with me?”

“Mi amor,” Rio whispered, taking the new request to not say ‘mi vida’ when anyone was naked very seriously. “Do you want me to come over now? I’ll stay every night if-…”

“No,” Agatha said, faster than Rio would have liked. “No, not tonight. It’s still so early and I want to keep us… I want to be as hidden as possible for as long as possible. But Saturday, come over Saturday. We’ll be at Disney during the day but I’d like to come home to you.”

“Okay,” Rio sighed, wishing her eye would just sting again so she could feel something other than the churning of her stomach. “Okay, I’ll be there Saturday. I’ll make it nice for us. Do something special.”

“And, next week? A day next week too?”

Rio could have dissolved in the very water she was stewing in.

“Agatha,” using her girlfriend’s name was the only option now, she had to make her listen to this.

“Any day. I mean it. Any day you want me over, whether it’s last minute or pre-planned, I’ll be there.”

There was silence down the line and Rio soon checked to see Agatha was still there.

“Do you think I’ll be any good at this?”

“Any good at what?”

“Girlfriends.”

Rio stood from the bath so hastily that she lost another half-tubful to the floor.

“I’m coming over.”

“No, Rio, don’t.”

Rio stood naked and afraid beside her white tub. She stared straight ahead, counted four tiles on the wall before she said: “What if I come just for a couple hours? Sneak in at midnight, leave by two?”

Agatha was silent and Rio counted another four tiles, then another, then her gaze fell to the wet floor. She shivered.

“Tell me what happened at therapy.”

Silence again.

Rio closed her eyes, took a deep breath.

Agatha spoke once more, her voice a little stronger than it had been: “It’s nothing I can’t work through. I just need a little time.”

“I can give you that.”

Again, softer: “I know.”

Rio reached across to touch the skin of her inner forearm where she’d left Evanora’s cuts to scar over.

Battle scars.

“I want to be with you. All the time.”

“I know.”

Rio nodded and waded through the inch of water across her floor to grab a towel and shivered as she wrapped it around herself. Now not naked she said: “Mi vida, it will be over soon.”

“I know.”

“Are you in bed?”

“Yeah.”

“Okay, I’ll lay with you. I’ll keep you on speaker and we can-…”

“You don’t need to do that.”

“I want to.”

“Okay.”

Rio got ready for bed, she kept looking at her phone and the seconds that ticked by, alerting her to how long she’d been on with Agatha.

They said nothing else other than soft ‘I love yous’ when Rio was eventually curled up in bed.

And so Rio and Agatha fell asleep. Together, and alone.

The connection was still live that morning.

Rio could hear noises coming from Agatha’s end and she pressed the phone to her ear to try and distinguish them.

“Hello?”

The noise went away and then, “Baby.”

Rio groaned out a laugh and rubbed at her eyes, “What are you doing?”

“I was just saying goodbye to Nicky and then-…”

“Isn’t it too early for him to be up?”

“You think I don’t kiss my son goodbye before I leave the house in the morning?”

Rio hummed and stretched upwards. “Does he appreciate that?”

“He’s sleepy. Sometimes only half-awake, but you know he does.”

Rio smiled at the thought and then began to grumble as she shuffled from the bed, taking her phone with her.

“Jen’s here, but you’re in my ear.”

“Mm’kay.”

Rio began to hum a tune and Agatha asked: “E.T.?”

“No, it’s Inspector Gadget.”

“It is not.”

Rio grinned as she did it again and then caught herself in the mirror and huffed. “We’re both wrong. It was Indiana Jones.”

“Nerd.”

Rio hummed her response as she began to brush her teeth and then spoke around her toothbrush: “Do you have time for a trailer visit today?”

“Apparently not. But lunch?”

“Depends what’s on the menu.”

“I just know you’re making a crude joke there, Vidal!” Jen’s voice suddenly. It wasn’t as clear as Agatha’s and Rio heard Agatha huff and curse at her manager but it had made Rio smile.

“I like being in your ear.”

“Oh yeah?”

“It’s almost as good as being in your pants.”

“You’re so lucky Jen didn’t hear that.”

”Hear what?”

“Well, I almost said something much cruder so maybe I’ll save that for when she actually can hear me.”

Agatha snorted and Rio grinned for the sound of it. “Maybe we can do this tomorrow? While I’m ring shopping with Alice. I’ll call you and wear you in my ear.”

“Oh will you now?”

Rio hummed her response and as she was leaving her bedroom she spotted something on the side. She went over to it and picked up the necklace Agatha had bought her for Christmas, hanging from her jewellery stand.

As Agatha launched into what she assumed was a rant at Jen (it being about the sides for that day), and not her, she fastened it round her neck and smiled where the jewel sparkled.

“Mi vida,” Rio called out as she hurried down the stairs to find Alice waiting for her below. “I’ll call you later? Sounds like-…”

“Okay. Okay. I love you.”

Rio hung up after repeating it back and Alice raised her brows at her, “We’re going to set in our pyjamas now?”

“Who cares? I’ll shower there and I’ll be in wardrobe soon anyway.”

Alice rolled her eyes and Rio only smiled. The whole way to set she toyed with her necklace and hummed the E.T. main theme.

Rio’s good mood lasted until lunchtime, when she finally saw Agatha again. She’d somehow managed to keep her necklace on through filming and now wore it proudly above her white t-shirt as she sat at crafty with some of the supporting artists.

Agatha eyed them all before she took a seat beside Rio.

Rio had her hand on her thigh before she’d even said hello.

“Mrs Harkness, I mean-… wow, you’re sitting with us?”

“Calm it, Dylan.”

Rio rolled her eyes at the man but smiled as he blushed. “Her ladyship can sit with us. It’s not that-…”

“Hello,” Agatha interrupted, reaching around Rio to offer her hand out to each dumbfounded extra in turn. They all fumbled to take her hand and Rio was just pleased that in the rush Agatha’s free hand had moved down to hold her own.

It was a smooth move, she had to admit.

Rio squeezed her fingers and Agatha squeezed back and then slid Rio’s hand up to the top of her thigh and left it there. Rio slid her hand further to curl around the inside of her leg.

Agatha pressed her thighs together, trapping her.

Rio grinned into her fruit salad.

No one was much interested in Rio from then on. At least, no one actively spoke to her. Everyone was very keen on getting Agatha’s attention and Rio couldn’t say that she minded much.

After all, her hand was currently being crushed between Agatha’s thighs. The only thing that could have possibly been better was if it had been her head instead.

So lunch, for Rio, was a very solitary experience. All she focused on was the feel of Agatha’s legs flexing every so often, reminding her she could still feel her, that she still wanted to feel her.

She ate. She pretended to listen. She mostly just enjoyed.

“Did you sneak that into a scene?”

Agatha muttered in her direction, speaking from the side of her mouth?

“What?” Rio’s voice was a little croaky, having been unused the past twenty minutes.

“Your necklace.”

“Oh.” Rio instinctively reached for the emerald. “Would you be pleased if I said yes?”

“Ecstatic.”

Rio grinned, lamely, stupidly. Agatha grinned right back.

“Ahem.”

They both turned to look up at Jen, newly arrived, classically pissed.

“Did you just say ‘ahem’?”

Rio scoffed.

“Agatha. Lawyers.”

The mood changed then. Rio’s easy, breezy day became something else. Agatha moved away without saying anything and Rio’s warm hand seemed to fizzle in the open air.

She watched Agatha leave and turned dejectedly to her food. Turns out eating was infinitely better with your hand squashed between a beautiful woman’s thighs. But she powered on anyway, trooper that she was.

She even managed the small talk required until she excused herself and went to her trailer.

Shortly after arriving she’d had a text from Agatha.

1:37pm
Agatha Harkness: Everything’s fine. It’s not Ralph. There’s a piece on me and my family being published tomorrow. Will call later.

Agatha did call later. She called as Rio arrived home from a PT session.

“Hey.”

“What’s happening?”

“It’s nothing, really. Nothing that will… nothing that matters. The New York Times have apparently been sitting on a piece about my family for a while now, just waiting on the right time to publish it and… well I’ve just given them that on a plate.”

Rio swallowed. “Is it bad?”

“No. Not anything I’m not used to.”

Rio nodded and looked down at her feet now resting on her coffee table.

“Have you heard anything from Ralph? From your mother?”

“Her lawyers have tried to get in contact with mine but otherwise, no.”

“Okay. And you’re feeling okay about everything?”

“Are you? Have you been to see that grief counsellor yet?”

Rio sighed and rubbed at her temple. “I was wondering when you’d bring that up.”

“I’m taking that as a no.”

“I’m fine. It’s not for a couple weeks.”

“Rio, just because you’re feeling healthier, just because you’re exercising and-…”

“I know. But now I have you and your book.”

Agatha sighed heavily and Rio felt her stomach flip as her hopeful smile faded. “I can make some calls? Try to get-…”

“Mi vida.”

“Okay, okay, I’m just trying to help.”

Rio brought her hand down to toy with the end of her top and she sighed softly, shrugging as if Agatha were in the room with her.

“I get that. I promise I’m okay. I’m at least feeling better than I have been. A little. Not, I mean, I’m still,” she paused, unsure what she even meant let alone what she was trying to say.

“I miss him.”

“I know.”

They sat in it for a while and then Agatha offered something Rio hadn’t been expecting: “Come over.”

Rio moved in her seat but hadn’t found the words before Agatha was saying them for her: “I can’t come to you but you can come to me. Come over.”

Rio looked over to check the time. Nicky would be asleep. The streets would be quiet. If she put her foot down and left now, she’d be there before midnight.

“Okay.”

She left not a minute after she’d hung up and in her little rented Hyundai she travelled the distance to her heart beating away in the Los Angeles hills.

The house was silent and dark as Rio let herself in. She wandered up the stairs after checking and triple checking that she’d locked the door behind herself. And then, sitting up in bed, wearing Rio’s shirt, her glasses atop her head, was her girlfriend.

Agatha opened her arms to her and Rio soon fell into them. They tumbled down together, both desperate to get as close as possible. For a while Rio thought it might turn hot and heavy but it instead became warm and easy.

Agatha’s lips were everywhere across her skin. They lingered along the cuts on her arm, they danced up to her pulse point and hovered close to her temple.

And Rio didn’t know why but she began to cry.

In the silence, in the warm cocoon of Agatha’s embrace, she cried the tears she’d held back all week and soon fell asleep with lips brushing along the tracks of her grief.

The Harkness Legacy

While the Kennedy’s may be America’s “royal family”, lurking in the shadows are another family, richer, and now with more political sway, hidden in plain sight.

Most people have heard of Agatha Harkness. In fact, ask any person in the street in any corner of the world, and the vast majority of them will know Agatha Harkness, if not by name, at least by sight.

For almost two decades now, Agatha Harkness has been a box office draw. Across her - still flourishing - career she’s won over two hundred industry awards and has a respectably strong Q Score.

It’s not well known how involved Agatha is in the family’s continued ties with the business and political worlds. An infamously private celebrity, questions about her family aren’t allowed during press junkets or late night interviews. She’s been known to even deny fans photos if she’s ever spotted out and about with the boy to inherit the Harkness legacy, her son, Nicholas.

Private she may be, but Agatha cannot escape the infamy of her parents’ legacy.

Rio had woken groggily that morning but had had to leave before Nicky woke so he didn’t get excited, so he didn’t tell the whole school that they’d had a surprise visitor in the night.

She left Agatha reluctantly and only did so because she had to.

Agatha’s forced schedule change on Tuesday meant that Rio wasn’t needed on set on today.

Not that Rio minded.

In fact she’d have done her best to fund the whole movie if it meant she could have a whole morning lying with Agatha in her arms again. Particularly if she could have spent more time figuring out how to make Agatha come in new wild and surprising ways.

But instead she took the opportunity to go to a spin class. She worked out the grief she’d attempted to cry out the night before. She made sure to stretch before and after, aware that her body was starting to protest for the amount of work she’d been making it do recently.

The rest of the day was spent on happier things; dreaming up ways in which she could welcome Agatha and Nicky home on Saturday. She’d considered making a lavish meal, but knew her culinary skills were limited. She thought of suggesting an evening of swimming and snacks, but it wasn’t nearly warm enough for that yet.

And then, as she was heading out to the grocery store, she had a spark of inspiration.

She’d build them a home. A literal, made out of sheets and household materials, home. A home within a home. A fort all of their own.

Fort Patito.

She’d gather everything soft and fluffy so after a day of being on show, they could all hide together in their new cosy nest, buried under blankets and covered in cushions.

This idea made for a more exciting than usual shopping trip as Rio gathered everything she’d need to make the fort particularly appealing. Which meant: a basket full of chocolate and more Skittles than was reasonable to buy in any one go.

Ever aware of the people looking her way, as she shopped, Rio had kept her cap on. It was a battered old thing that had once belonged to her dad. She’d picked it up randomly that morning without even really thinking. Tokens like this, talismans, really, made her feel closer to him.

And as she tugged it down a little more over her brow she thought of Agatha and the talismans they shared of each other. Rio had her necklace, Agatha had her rings. And then her shirt, the shirt that was currently being passed back and forth between them.

Rio was wearing it now, fresh from her show after spin, doing her duty to make it smell like her so Alice could drop it off with Jen and Jen could deliver it to Agatha who could get a good night’s sleep with it.

But the talisman on her head worked in more than one way as she caught herself in the little screen above the self-check out. She was reminded to call her mom.

It was as if her dad had tapped her shoulder and given her one of his infamous “speak to your mom more, mija” looks.

She smiled for the memory of his face.

She called her on the way home from her embarrassing rental.

By the time Anna was done with the family gossip and Rio was done with her “mmhms” and “uh huhs”, Rio was onto another missions.

Mission: find a new car.

Only, Rio hated cars. Knew nothing about them. So it was a slog, and it meant she got halfway through a bag of candy before she even got anywhere with it.

She worked at it for three hours, constantly checking where Agatha was and if she’d text whilst she worked. But she hadn’t, and she was still on set.

Still, she produced a semi-comprehensible slide show on the cars she’d picked and saved it down with the intention of presenting it to Agatha the next time she got a chance.

After all, Agatha was the mom here, the real one. She’d know which car was best suited to driving around a little boy.

Though Rio had a favourite. She definitely had a favourite. And she’d checked every one of them could be coloured green especially for the little boy she was buying it for.

So, mission complete, it was soon time for mission number two: finding Agatha’s new talisman. Or, she supposed, finding Jen’s, and sneakily finding Agatha’s too.

Sneakily being the important word.

Since Tuesday, all she’d be able to thing about was the fake rings Agatha took comfort from. How initially it had been a source of great comfort that Agatha had taken to wearing them. But now they felt insulting.

It felt insulting that she couldn’t give Agatha something that in fact she’d promised the very first night she’d met her.

“I’d get you a bigger one.”

By the time Alice had arrived later that evening, Rio was almost gagging for a glass of wine. She’d showered again, changed, and put on makeup for their little date night and was practically buzzing with anticipation as she slid into the waiting Uber.

“I wanted to drink, and drink a lot so,” Alice offered by way of explanation when Rio made eyes at her across the back seat.

“Fair. Did you book this place or are we just gonna-…?”

“Sorry to interrupt,” the driver announced as they pulled away from a street that wasn’t Rio’s, but two over. Alice always made Rio walk away from her house when being picked up by strangers.

“But you’re Rio Vidal?”

Rio looked up to the driver who most certainly was not sorry about interrupting.

“I am.”

“Jeez! In my car?! Man!”

Rio bit the inside of her cheek and from the corner of her eye saw Alice begin to tap away at her phone.

“Dude I am such a fan!”

She didn’t respond and the driver just shook his head, clearly so astounded that he had his favourite actress in the back seat.

Alice continued to tap away.

“Hey, when we stop, can I get a selfie?”

“Ah,” Alice interjected, “Not today, man. Gotta understand we don’t want the place mobbed as soon as-…”

“Aw, nah. I won’t post it. I’ll wait until tomorrow, yeah! Tomorrow!”

Rio shot Alice a look and saw her manager looked full of regret for not having used an official car service. They both sometimes forgot how famous Rio now was.

“How about I sign something for you? Worth more nowadays anyway.”

The guy umm’d and ahh’d and Rio began to chew on her lip as Alice paused what she was doing on her phone. Rio felt a sudden vibration against her thigh and fished her phone out of her pocket.

She saw Agatha’s name light up her screen and without thinking just answered it.

“Hey.”

“I hear you need rescued.”

Rio glanced at Alice who was avoiding her eye contact.

“Something like that. Are you done for the day?”

“Who knew she could type that quickly. But no, all good. Are you ready to advise on some diamonds?”

“How about I promise I won’t hang up if you have any bad opinions?”

Agatha scoffed and Rio heard her say something to, presumably, Jen through the muffling of her hand.

She came back about thirty seconds later. Rio had taken to twirling her hair.

“Will you send pictures?”

“Will you share them with Jen?”

“You can’t answer my question with a question.”

“You are not the boss of me.”

Rio received a threatening look from Alice and smiled in her direction as Agatha said: “I think you know I am.”

Rio rolled her eyes but her smile didn’t falter. Up front the driver was now trying to get Alice’s attention so Rio turned her head to gaze out the window.

“How’s the patito?”

“He likes his new nanny, says she’s smart and nice. Think he’s missing you, though.”

“Oh? Tell him I miss him too.”

“I do. Every time he asks.”

Rio nodded and glanced over her shoulder at the conversation happening in the car around her. She decided Alice could hold her own with the man now asking how to get into the industry.

She turned back to the window.

“I was thinking, on Saturday, I’ll be at home waiting for you when you’re done with the mouse.”

“I wish you could come.”

“Me too. But I’ve got a plan for the evening that’ll make up for it.”

“And you’re not going to tell me?”

“I think it’s better as a surprise.”

Agatha hummed quietly and Rio grinned. “Does it involve you naked?”

“Very much not.”

“Then I won’t like it.”

Rio laughed and turned to nudge Alice’s leg where she’d just kicked it. She pulled the phone a little ways from her mouth.

“¿Él habla español?” Does he speak Spanish?

Alice shot her a look as if to say, “how would I know?”, but turned all the same to the driver and interrupted him mid-flow about his modelling career.

Once confirming that, no, he did not speak Spanish, Rio was free to turn back to Agatha.

“Siempre estás tan desesperada, mi amor.” Always so desperate, my love.

“I have many, many years to make up for.”

Rio hummed and picked some lint off her pants. She knew with Alice nearby, let alone within earshot and kicking distance, she couldn’t pull at that thread. So she took a breath and changed the subject.

“Lo que dijiste el sábado pasado, ¿lo sigues diciendo?” What you said last Saturday, do you still mean it?

“What did I say?”

Rio cleared her throat. “About…” She cleared her throat again. “Riachuelo.” Little river. A diminutive of her own name, to denote Nicky, the boy named for her. She looked down at her fingers.

When Agatha spoke again, her voice was softer, her tone gentler than Rio had ever heard it.

“I’d get you the adoption papers now if I could. And I know Nicky would too. I don’t just think he’s missing you. I know he is. He keeps asking about you and when you’ll be back. I want us… Rio. I want us to be a family.”

The car came to a halt and Rio looked up as Alice motioned for her to get out, and quickly.

She began to just as Agatha spoke again. She seemed to have shaken some of the gentleness off.

“Which is why it would really help if you also picked me a ring today. Just so we can hurry it along.”

This made Rio bark a laugh as she stepped from the car and onto the sidewalk. She was turning round and saw that the driver had stepped out too.

“Jesus fuck.”

“What? Rio? What?”

Alice had rushed around quickly but her arm had only made the interception as Rio was hugged by the driver. There was a strange stalemate where everyone seemed confused as to whose limb belonged to who until Alice came to her senses and Rio was extricated.

“Rio?”

Rio smiled weakly at the man now begging for a picture as Alice led her away and a security guard attached to the store ran towards them to help. Not that much needed doing. The guy was insistent but he wasn’t a threat.

Still.

“Rio Elena Vidal if you do not answer me right now I will-…!”

“I’m fine.” Rio had barely been holding her phone up, barely had it anywhere near her ear. But she’d heard Agatha loud and clear. She fished in her pocket for her AirPods and hurriedly transferred Agatha’s panicked voice into one of those.

“I’m fine,” she repeated as she and Alice were welcomed into the store.

“What happened?”

Rio smiled as she accepted a glass of champagne and glanced around the space, wondering if Alice had used her name to empty out the store for just them.

“Nothing,” she muttered. “All good.”

“Rio.”

Rio bit the inside of her cheek and then muttered to Agatha as they were ushered to a little room where the initial consultation was to take place.

“Guy hugged me, took me by surprise. Alice stepped in.”

Rio tried very hard to concentrate as the lady in the pristine suit with the pristine bun started to make small talk but it was almost impossible with Agatha now ranting about “fucking men”. The hardest part being that she couldn’t accuse Agatha of being “so very gay”.

In the end it became a bit like white noise.

For the first part of their time in the swanky jewellery store, Rio felt very much like she just had a running commentary in her right ear.

Post-rant, quickly learning that Rio couldn’t or wouldn’t respond, Agatha was now telling her what she was going to make for dinner that night. She told her about work that day: “I’m not convinced Quill can actually act”. She was commenting on the wine she was drinking, “notes of apple, pear, citrus, maybe a little honey”. She was even told of Nicky winning an award for learning all of his times tables.

It was like the perfect little podcast.

And Rio realised, as Agatha continued to yap, and the attendant continued her various spiels about cut, colour, clarity, and carat, that this was what the rest of her life would be.

Not Agatha in her ear, hidden away. But Agatha, talking casually about her day, sharing her every thought. And Rio, happily listening to her.

They could be in stores just like this one, side by side, with Rio knowing every thought in Agatha’s pretty head.

And suddenly Rio wished she were here looking for Agatha’s ring.

Though, she reminded herself, she actually was.

Technically.

“Mi vida,” Rio whispered as the lady with the chignon disappeared to get some samples, a teasing lilt to her voice, “why’re you telling me all this?”

“You think I’d be silent now I have your undivided attention? I haven’t even started on how I want you to propose.”

Rio hummed and nudged Alice to point her in the direction of a ring on the side with an emerald cut sapphire in the centre of it.

“It’s pretty,” Alice whispered back, toying nervously with her fingers in her lap.

Rio nudged her again and grinned her encouragement as Agatha said in her ear: “The answer, in case you’re wondering, is immediately.”

Rio snorted on the exhale just as the woman appeared back in the room and she smacked her hand over her mouth, worried she’d spat all over the place. Alice wiped at her own cheek.

They were shown some pretty rings and Rio found she had to warn the woman that she was actually speaking with an “interested party” in her ear just in case she thought she were insane for speaking out loud about how each ring looked.

Agatha took very vocal umbrage to being referred to and “interested party” but Rio couldn’t say much in her defence.

She also sent Agatha pictures, making sure to get each ring in its best light.

Sometimes Agatha said just one word about the rings, sometimes it was as if the ring had committed a personal slight against her and she’d go off on a diatribe.

It wasn’t until the fifth ring that Rio began to lose it for the comedic stylings of her girlfriend in her ear.

“I still haven’t forgiven her for that pear monstrosity.”

Rio bit down on the corner of her lip, watching as Alice was very much looking at the pear-shaped diamond ring in her hand.

“If you gave me that for real I’d throw it in your face.”

This made Rio scoff. Which made Alice turn to her with raised brows. She shook her head a little and muttered, “You would not.”

“I would.”

Rio hummed quietly, now pointing to another ring and speaking to Alice: “That one’s nice.”

“Which?” Agatha.

Rio smirked and ignored her. Alice picked the ring up and the attendant began her spiel.

“You know, its not fun just sitting in your ear when you’re not telling me what’s-…”

“It’s an emerald ring.” Rio moved around to Alice’s other shoulder, peering down at the ring. She snapped a quick picture and sent it off, smiling as Alice tried it on. “It’s beautiful.”

“Green is your colour.”

Rio ignored this too. Alice held the ring up, testing it in the light.

“Do you think she’d like a coloured stone?” Alice, to Rio.

“I think she’d like anything you gave her.” Rio, to Alice.

“Not me. I would not like-…” Rio had to fight not to roll her eyes and interrupted as Alice looked back to the ring.

“You talk a big game for someone who walked around with an ugly ring for days because you thought it was mine.”

Alice looked around to her and raised her brows. Rio heard Agatha scoff but say nothing else.

“Maybe a diamond in that shape?” Rio offered to her friend.

Alice hummed and Rio heard Agatha mutter: “can’t believe Jen’s getting one before I do.”

“I will hang up.”

Alice turned to her then and leant up to speak close to the AirPod in Rio’s ear. “A diamond or a coloured stone? I think diamond.”

“Diamond. The biggest one you can afford.”

Rio smiled as Alice settled back down and she repeated what Agatha had just said to her.

“Mine doesn’t have to be big it just-…”

“I believe I promised you a big one.”

“I’d take a Haribo ring if it means I get one sooner.”

“How romantic. Especially when you just said-…”

But Agatha had interrupted again, clearly not keen on being made to wait.

“Isn’t it? Knowing I’d wear a-…”

But Rio didn’t hear what Agatha was saying because she’d moved on to another jewellery case. She vaguely heard Agatha’s voice calling her name in her ear, was vaguely aware of Alice beside her again asking if she’d seen something for Jen, but she was mostly transfixed on a gold ring in the centre of one of the display cases.

“Rio? My love? Are you listening to me?”

“Which one?” Alice asked, her eyes darted about the display case where there were mostly plain bands, not rings you’d typically associate with engagements.

But Rio’s eyes were on one ring in particular. It was large, larger than most of the rest. A plain gold band, sitting atop a small purple cushion.

The attendant arrived and asked: “Would you like to look at this one too?”

Rio looked to Alice and gestured to her to ask, knowing if she did that Agatha would hear.

“Rio? What’s the ring? Show me.”

Rio bit down on her lip as she watched the exchange take place. She saw the attendant’s white-gloved hand place the ring in Alice’s palm and nodded down at it, having already made her decision.

“Umm, it’s not that great actually,” she announced to Agatha even as she took the ring and placed it on her own wedding finger.

She couldn’t get it past her last knuckle but she could picture it already on Agatha’s finger. It could be a reminder of what she would eventually offer her. A ring that was large enough that it wouldn’t be considered a wedding band, but worn on the correct finger, the wearer would know it was exactly that.

Or the promise of that.

Even as Rio knew she were to buy this ring she slid it from her had and gave it back to Alice.

If Agatha Harkness were to wear this ring, Rio Vidal couldn’t be seen to be buying it.

Alice raised her brows at her and Rio nodded only once.

She held her fingers up whilst the attendant was busy trying to show off different rings and indicated she’d need a size six. Alice nodded just as Agatha began to sound off: “Why am I being ignored?”

“Not ignored, just-…”

“We can have it engraved, if you wish.”

Rio’s heart skipped a beat in her chest at the sound of the attendant’s words.

She began to sweat. Not a neat, delicate misting, but something else. Something that didn’t, surely wouldn’t, look good under the bright lights.

Her weight moved from foot to foot and Alice seemed to understand even as Rio couldn’t quite form the words.

“How long would that take?”

“Rio? What’s happening? Did the connection drop? I can hear someone talking.”

Rio fished her phone out of her pocket just as the answer to Alice’s question came: “We do it all in-house, so really within a day.”

Rio muted Agatha, ensuring she couldn’t hear anything before she blurted out: “Alice would love that.”

Alice sniggered beside her and Rio wondered if the sweat were actually now trickling down her forehead or if it were phantasms of her fear. She glanced at her phone, saw the connection was still live.

Maybe Agatha had had enough and was on her way over.

“She already knows what she wants,” Rio said quickly, before anyone else could say anything and before Agatha could magically appear before them. “She can write it down and we’ll take that one. Provided it can be available tomorrow at the latest.”

It is amazing what can happen if you clearly, concisely, and authoritatively demand it.

Rio and Alice left the store an hour later.
Rio, already with her new ring in its plush velvet box in her bag, and Alice without a ring but with many, many thoughts about what she was now looking for for Jen.

Rio was practically skipping to the bar, despite having spent a good ten minutes of the last hour trying to convince Agatha she’d pressed the mute button by accident. But she had her ring. She had her engraved ring, nothing else mattered.

“It doesn’t even make sense,” Alice said for the hundredth time as she settled into the booth in a dive bar they’d settled on, forgoing fine dining for cheap beer.

“I am not explaining it to you again,” Rio insisted, her hand flying naturally to the small lump in her bag that told her she definitely hadn’t lost the ring between entering the bar and taking a seat.

“Well if you have to explain it to her it’s not really worth it, is it?”

Rio rolled her eyes but clinked their beers together. “She’ll love it. I’m sure of it.”

“Well Jen will be pissed I couldn’t find anything.”

Rio smiled and placed her beer down before she’d even taken a sip.

“There really were some beautiful ones. That last one was incredible.”

Alice shook her head. “I don’t think she’d like a trinity. I just can’t see her wearing a ring like that.”

“She’ll love anything you give her.”

“And will she love that ring? That ring with your terrible handwriting with words that don’t even make any sense?”

Rio rolled her eyes and took a sip of her beer and felt below the table the movement of a foot hooking below her own and Alice swinging their legs together. It made her smile, made her relax a little.

“It’s a promise. A solid gold promise. That’s all.”

Alice hummed and eyed her suspiciously.

The night continued that way. Alice teased Rio, and Rio teased her right back. They drank more beer than they should have. They ate fries and greasy burgers and made use of the jukebox and had a night like they always used to.

In a bar like this, no one cared who Rio Vidal was.

No one but the blonde in the back, nursing an untouched bottle of beer, her green eyes trained on every one of the Oscar-winner’s moves.

 

FRIDAY

DEADLINE

EXCLUSIVE: Apple TV’s ‘Heartburn’ is eyeing a Summer release date amid Agatha Harkness’s very public divorce. The Oscar-winner plays Nora Ephron’s Rachel, in the comedy-drama centred around the writer’s spectacular marriage breakdown.

Rio woke on Alice’s couch.

Her head hurt.

Her body hurt.

She wanted to die.

“Up!”

No. She wanted to kill Jen.

“Go away.”

“No, up! You need to be on set. Actually, you really should have been on set about half an hour ago.”

“Where’s Alice?” Rio grabbed a cushion and covered her face with it.

Jen snatched it back.

“I’m letting her sleep in.”

“And not me?!”

“UP!”

The drive to set was miserable. That was, until Agatha jumped in the car and bundled Rio into the backseat with her. Rio placed her head in her lap and whilst Agatha had grumbled about safety she’d soon given in and instead was now running her fingers through Rio’s hair as she slept off as much of her hangover as she could.

Only Rio couldn’t sleep in Agatha’s lap forever.

She had to get up, had to work, had to leave the warmth of Agatha’s thighs and pretend to be a fully functioning human being, not to mention in-demand actress.

That morning on set was brutal. She spoke her lines and moved to her marks but really wasn’t able to give much more than that.

Because Agatha was in the scene with her she had someone who was willing to demand more takes when Rio shot her a look that said “was I even present in that take?”. But having Agatha there also meant she was receiving soft touches to her lower back, gentle rubs of her arm, and once, after two hours of hard labour, an arm around her that meant she could relax her whole body and use Agatha for support.

“I hear you didn’t even find a ring?”

“Hmm? No. No, no ring.”

Agatha was silent for a while and Rio took the chance to lean fully over, resting her head against Agatha’s. she closed her eyes and Agatha didn’t pull away.

“Sleep at lunch. It’ll help.”

“Would prefer to die a little.”

Agatha’s fingers flexed and tightened and Rio made a small noise from the base of her throat.

Nothing much more was said. At least, that Rio could compute. All her energy was spent on remaining upright and keeping track of the scenes as they were filmed.

With makeup and lighting, she knew she’d look okay. But being on top of her cues, being reactive to her fellow actors, it was all a lot to ask of someone who’d had many, many beers on a mostly empty stomach.

Not to mention, Agatha didn’t join her for her nap at lunch. Nor was she with her in the scenes she had to film that afternoon.

And Rio wasn’t released until well after ten that night.

She all but collapsed when she got in the door of her little Spanish villa. She struggled to kick her shoes off and curled in on herself on the couch, ready and willing for the warm embrace of sleep.

But something vibrated against her thigh. Something tore her from said embrace and Rio grumbled even as the sound of her girlfriend’s voice filtered into her conscious.

“You’re home. What took so long?”

“Mm, Billy couldn’t cry.”

Agatha scoffed, “What? They had to get the tear stick out?”

Rio smiled a little, “Go easy, he’s just a kid.”

“So they did have to use the tear stick. Pathetic.”

“He initially tried pinching himself.”

Agatha snorted and Rio’s smile grew.

“How’re you? Was today okay?”

“I had a shorter day because Nicky had to go to the dentist.”

“Mm?” Rio rolled onto her back and rubbed at her tired eyes. “Everything okay?”

There was a beat, no more than that. But in it, Rio just knew what Agatha’s answer would be.

“Well, I’m suing the practice.”

Rio blinked until her eyes opened and she stared up at her ceiling.

Perhaps she hadn’t known what Agatha’s answer would be.

“What?”

“They tried to get him to agree to braces.”

Rio frowned, rubbed her hand over her face. “Braces? Isn’t he a little young?”

Agatha huffed, clearly annoyed Rio was missing the point. “It’s because he has a gap in his teeth. It’s because his front too are a little bigger and they said they could fix them for him.”

Rio paused, her tongue running absently over her own two front teeth.

“Was he upset?”

“No. He got a sticker and a lollipop.”

“What was the sticker?”

“Rio.” Agatha sighed. “Looney Tunes.”

“He gave a kid whose teeth he wants to shrink and close together a Bugs Bunny sticker?”

Agatha snorted and it made Rio smile.

“What did it say?”

“What?”

“The sticker.”

“We’re still on that?”

“Also, Looney Tunes is a bit old school, isn’t it? What did a-the stickew say?”

Rio slapped her palm to her forehead immediately after her very poor Elmer Fudd impression. But then she heard another snort.

“You do impressions now?”

“Wait until you see my Jack Nicholson.”

Agatha laughed and Rio beamed for the sound of it.

“The sticker said: ‘be very very careful, I’m hunting cavities.’”

Rio hummed and started twisting her hair around her finger. “Exactly like that?”

“I don’t do impressions.”

“Hmm.”

Rio let the hair unravel from her finger, fighting a yawn.

“You did a very good impression of a straight woman for years.”

“That isn’t funny.”

“It is a little.”

Agatha didn’t say anything and Rio, drunk on her enjoyment of teasing Agatha, and maybe also just because she was so exhausted, chanced her arm: “Or maybe a very bad one considering how horny you clearly were for me in Italy.”

Agatha scoffed. Rio grinned.

“You’re changing the subject.”

“What was the subject?”

“Nicky’s teeth.”

“Right.”

“I’m going to sue the dentist.”

Rio scoffed this time.

“Don’t be ridiculous. He was just suggesting what any other dentist would suggest. I had braces, you know. People teased me for my gap.”

“They did?”

“Mmhm. But then I lost my retainer and the gap came back.”

“Nicky likes his gap.”

Rio nodded and continued to twirl her hair, “I’ve grown to like mine too.”

“I’m still going to take them for all they’re worth.”

“Mi vida. The guy was just doing his job.”

“Poorly.”

This made Rio smile, made her display her gap to no one.

“Okay. Maybe sleep on it first before you-…”

“The only thing I want to sleep on is you.”

“Tomorrow. You can do that tomorrow.”

“I want to do it tonight.”

“I can come over again? I can be there in less than a hour.”

“You’re exhausted, besides, Jen’s here. We’re… we’re going through scenarios.”

“Scenarios?”

“For the Park tomorrow. Security and… just scenarios.”

Rio nodded and gulped. “Disney’s got to be the safest place ever, right? It’ll all be fine.”

“He’ll hate it.”

“Why?”

“I just know there’ll be crowds and even if people don’t approach they’ll be looking and pointing and shouting. He hates attention. He hates when people get too close.”

Rio could understand that. She felt the same every time she was on a crowded red carpet, or every time people pointed at her when she walked down the street, or when Uber drivers forced her into hugs she didn’t want.

She dropped her hand from her hair and began to pick at her cuticles.

“I’ll be waiting for you when you get back. Even if the day is hard, the evening can be good. Soft. Just the three of us.”

Agatha sighed out and Rio closed her eyes at the sound of it. She stopped picking at her fingers.

“I should go.”

“That’s all folks?” Rio tried lamely, hoping to hear just one vaguely amused exhale.

It never came.

“I’ll see you tomorrow evening?”

“Of course. I love you. Call me if… just call me if you need me.”

“Okay. I love you too. And for the record, I love your teeth.”

Rio nodded and chewed on her lip, “Yours are cute too.”

“So goofy.”

Rio laughed, “Well say hi to him tomorrow for me please.”

“I’m hanging up now.”

“Okay.”

“Seriously. Jen needs me.”

“Okay, mi vida.”

“Rio.”

“Yes?”

“I mean it.”

“Okay.”

There was silence for so long that Rio thought Agatha actually had hung up. But she checked and she hadn’t.

She smiled and let the silence continue for a while. In it, she forced her brain to function, at least at a low-level, at least to the frequency of Agatha.

She swallowed before she simply said: “If he got braces he would still look like me.”

To her horror she heard Agatha gasp; a great big desperate inhale. Rio sat up, her body going rigid for the sound of Agatha’s continued gasps, as if she’d been holding her breath the whole time they’d been silent.

“Agatha? Agatha? Why are you-…? What’s happened?”

“If you were,” Agatha gasped out, “if I’d… if you were a man… I keep thinking…”

But Agatha didn’t need to finish for Rio to know what she was thinking.

Agatha believed there was no world where Nicky wouldn’t be here. Which meant that in a world where Rio were a man, in a world where Rio could get Agatha pregnant, Nicky would still be here.

Which meant Agatha would always be left wanting with Rio. Because Rio couldn’t have given Agatha Nicky. Despite what she said.

Despite him being her mellizo.

Her body collapsed down from where it had frozen solid and she rested her forehead against the palm of her hand.

“My love,” Rio whispered through Agatha’s soft, stuttering breaths, “Are you-…? Do you wish I were a man?”

Agatha didn’t say anything for a while and in the silence Rio felt her heart shatter in her chest. Her old fears began to gnaw at the fragments, telling her this was all just a bit of fun, just some excitement, that she’d just been a warm body to get Agatha through these past weeks.

The phenomenon that Alice referred to as “the doom” that descended with hangovers now hit Rio solidly in her empty chest.

“No. Rio. Mi amor, I just… I want…”

Rio shook her head, tried to shake the thoughts clean out of it.

“I just wish, I just wish…”

Rio felt sick with it. She felt sick that this was even being discussed.

“I wish it were easy. I-I wish Nicky were yours. I wish-… I wish I’d taken you home that night. I wish you’d never left. I wish-… I wish I didn’t have to take my child on a glorified photoshoot tomorrow! I wish for a different life!”

Rio unfurled herself. She straightened her back, she let Agatha take a breath, take two, take ten. And then, as calmly as she could, she said, “I love you. This is a different life. This is our life. We’re just starting, Agatha.”

“Don’t.”

“My world, my everything, my girlfriend. This is a different life. I can’t…” she shook her head, swallowed down her words, “no, I can give you everything you want. I can give you everything you’ve ever dreamed of and-…”

“You are everything I’ve ever dreamed of. The only thing.”

Rio closed her eyes and counted to ten. In the quiet she heard Agatha sniffing.

“Can we talk about this tomorrow? I want, Rio, I want to talk. I want you to know that I love you. I want-…. I want-…”

“I understand,” Rio whispered, “I get it. It’s okay.”

“I just want you.”

“I know.”

“I just want this to be-…”

“Easy.”

Agatha didn’t respond but Rio knew she was agreeing in the quiet.

“I love you. I’ve loved you for-…” Agatha sighed and Rio felt the pain in her chest recede like the falling tide. “I would love you if you were a worm.”

“W-what?” Rio’s own laugh took her by surprise as she gasped it out, her hand flying now to her chest. “A worm?”

“You told me once that you’d love me if I were a worm.”

“I did?”

“When we were driving back to Berkeley, after my mother cut Nicky’s hair.”

A lifetime ago, then. But Rio had a vague memory of sitting in a car with Agatha’s hand on her thigh, driving back to a house that would soon become the location of her first true heartbreak.

“I would love you if you were a worm.”

“And I would love you too. I’d love you if I had to carry you around in my pocket and feed you dirt.”

“You would?”

“I’d pop you in some Tupperware and keep you safe.”

Rio chewed on her lip and looked down at her lap.

“Can I come over?”

A few seconds of nothing and then: “Not tonight.”

“If I were a worm could I come over?”

“You’d already be in my pocket.”

Rio huffed, and then laughed. “This is so ridiculous.”

“I know,” Agatha breathed, not finding it nearly as amusing as Rio did. “Are we okay?”

“Why? Will you buy me another car if we’re not?”

“That’s not funny.”

Rio sighed and rubbed the back of her neck. “We’re okay. I’m still a human, don’t worry.”

“Still my girlfriend?”

Rio’s hand fell back down and she shook her head a little.

“Only until I can be your wife.”

“And when will that be?”

“I guess once you’re no longer married.”

“Why? Let’s just do it now.”

“I’d rather spend our honeymoon not in prison.”

In the background Rio heard a voice and she knew she didn’t have Agatha all to herself for much longer. She swallowed and plucked at the string of her sweats.

“We should talk. Tomorrow. Talk about… mi vida, about what it means to be with me, if… we should talk about it.”

She heard Jen’s voice more clearly now and knew she probably had seconds, if that. She sat more forwards and waited for Agatha to speak again.

“I can’t wait to see you. I’ve-… I’ve missed you. I want you here.”

“Then let me come.”

“I can’t.”

“Tell me why.”

She heard Jen again, insistent now.

“If you come over I won’t leave the house tomorrow. I’ll hunker down with you and Nicky and-… I’m not strong enough to carry this when you’re here.”

Fragments of a once strong and undamaged heart quivered in a hollow chest and Rio Vidal said the words she knew to be true but hadn’t yet given voice to: “I wouldn’t let you go tomorrow. I’d lock us all away and-…”

She took a breath, felt Agatha holding her own.

“Keep us safe.”

“Rio,” Agatha inhaled her name, barely making it distinguishable. “Ask me not to go. Ask me not to take him.”

Rio closed her eyes. She heard Jen in the background. She heard her name being called, heard Agatha’s soft, insistent breaths.

“Ask me.”

Rio shook her head, shaking away the cursed tattoo her fragile heart produced, echoing in the space between thought and fear.

“I can’t do that.”

“You just said you’d lock us away, that you’d keep us safe.”

Rio twisted the string of her sweats, wrapped it so tightly around her finger she could feel the pull at her hips.

“Mi vida, this isn’t my choice to make.”

“I’m asking you to make it.”
