Jen could be heard still, no longer calling out to Rio but instead trying to convince Agatha to hang up.

Rio wished she never would.

“Please don’t.”

Silence from Agatha, more bargaining by Jen.

“You’ll be safe,” Rio started, trying to convince them both now. “Jen knows what she’s doing. Jen-…”

“I don’t want this.”

“I know. It’s just a little longer, just a-…”

“I want you here and I don’t want to be afraid anymore.”

“Baby.”

Agatha exhaled and Rio didn’t know what else she could say.

The line went quiet then and Rio checked the connection. She couldn’t hear anything and she assumed if she spoke that Agatha wouldn’t be able to hear her either.

Jen, she supposed, was being spoken to.

So she waited. She twirled her pant string, then she twirled her hair.

“I’m back. I… tomorrow. We won’t be back late. You’ll be there?”

“Of course.”

Ask me to come over. Ask me to stay.

But Agatha never did. Instead, it took five more minutes for them to say goodbye. Agatha asked for reassurance three more times. Are we okay?/Rio, are you sure we’re okay?/My love, are we okay?.

Rio only told the absolute truth each time she was asked: Yes./Of course./Forever.

Before bed that night Rio hoped Agatha might call her again but she never did.

At two in the morning she called her, deciding that sleep would never come until she heard her voice again. Unsurprisingly, Agatha was awake.

“Rio?”

“I just wanted to hear your voice.”

“You’re awake.”

“Couldn’t sleep.”

“Are we-…?”

“Mi vida, I miss you. I wish you were here.”

“Keep the line open? I’m wearing your shirt.”

“I’m wearing my necklace.”

She heard Agatha move in the bed and knew she must have put her on speaker beside her.

Rio did the same.

“Are you comfortable?”

“Yes.”

“Have you been getting… have you had any sleep paralysis lately?”

“No.”

Rio nodded against the pillow and tugged the blankets closer around herself.

“Where would our honeymoon be?”

Rio smiled, a dreamy, lazy smile. She hummed. “Venice. Then we’d rent a car and I’d drive us down to Tuscany. We could rent a great big farmhouse in the middle of nowhere amongst the vineyards. We could get a chef in every night and lay by the pool all day. You could bring a million books and I can pretend to read them whilst I’m really just checking my wife out in her tiny bikini.”

Agatha laughed.

“How long?”

“Three weeks.”

“Three weeks of a secluded farmhouse in the middle of Tuscany?”

“A few days in Venice too.”

“For you to feel me up in a gondola?”

“Would you let me?”

“Depends.”

“On what?”

“On how generous I’m feeling that day.”

Rio huffed but smiled, “I think you’d be feeling pretty generous.”

“Is that right?”

Rio smiled, turned her head more into the pillow. All was silent, all was okay.

“What I said earlier,” Agatha whispered, making Rio’s smile fade, “about you being a man. I didn’t mean it the way… I didn’t mean it how it sounded.”

“I know.”

“And talking, talking tomorrow isn’t breakup talking, right?”

“Never.”

“Okay.”

“Try to sleep. You have a busy day tomorrow.”

“I’ll miss you in it.”

“You’ll have me all night.”

“That a promise?”

“It’s a promise.”

Rio didn’t sleep. The sounds emanating from her phone told her that if Agatha did ever actually drift off, she didn’t sleep for long.

By seven, the connection went dead.

 

SATURDAY

VANITY FAIR

 

THE HANDWRITTEN PROUST QUESTIONNAIRE

 

What is your idea of perfect happiness? With my friends on the basketball court. A cold beer waiting for me.

What is your greatest fear? Losing a loved one. Dying alone

What is the trait you most deplore in yourself? My impatience

What is the trait you most deplore in others? Cruelty

Which living person do you most admire? My dad

What is your greatest extravagance? I’m not a good cook so I order in or go out for food too often

What is your current state of mind? Peaceful. I have a couple weeks downtime to see friends and go home to Delaware

What do you consider the most overrated virtue? Self-control

On what occasion do you lie? Interviews

What do you most dislike about your appearance? My teeth. I used to be teased about them in school

Which living person do you most despise? Take a guess

What is the quality you most like in a man? Gentleness

What is the quality you most like in a woman? A sense of humour

Which words or phrases do you most overuse? Nothing I can write in Vanity Fair

What or who is the greatest love of your life? My parents. And the Cs

When and where were you happiest? On the couch, half-asleep after a home-cooked meal by my mom. Or courtside at a game

Which talent would you most like to have? I wish I could juggle

If you could change one thing about yourself, what would it be? Maybe I’d dye my hair

What do you consider your greatest achievement? I paid off my parents’ house

If you were to die and come back as a person or a thing, what would it be? Can’t write that in Vanity Fair either. That or my best friend

Where would you most like to live? Maybe London, Hampstead Heath

What is your most treasured possession? An old cowboy shirt I’ve had since college

What do you regard as the lowest depth of misery? Loneliness

What is your favorite occupation? Acting on stage

What is your most marked characteristic? I probably don’t want to know

What do you most value in your friends? Humor, fun, honesty

Who are your favorite writers? I should read more but in college I remember loving Tennessee Williams

Who is your hero of fiction? Dr Ellie Sattler

Which historical figure do you most identify with? Maybe one of those little dinosaurs who couldn’t quite reach the tallest branches but kept trying. Does that count?

Who are your heroes in real life? My parents, my best friend

What are your favorite names? My middle name is for my yaya so probably that. Elena

What is it that you most dislike? Prejudice and warm beer

What is your greatest regret? Drinking too much one night in a bar in Chicago

How would you like to die? Old, surrounded by family, holding my wife’s hand

What is your motto? Veni, Vidi, Vidal. No I’m joking. I don’t have one. Maybe ‘Go Celtics!’

*Vanity Fair would like to note that since answering these questions, Rio Vidal has lost her father.

“Fuck!”

Rio growled as she hopped on one foot, lifting her other into the air.

“Fuck! Fuck!”

The pain radiated from her big toe up her leg. She had to grit her teeth and bear it. Maybe lifting a king-sized, heavy mattress down the stairs by herself had been a bad idea.

And she hadn’t even made it past the bedroom door.

She waited until she was able to think again, until the pain had subsided to a dull ache. She huffed. She heaved the mattress fully off the bed.

Fuck, she thought.

It took almost thirty minutes of intense, strenuous lifting, pulling, pushing, grunting, but the mattress was was now at the bottom of the stairs. The real struggle had been getting it through the door and only when it was already half out had she realised she’d soon need to get it back in again.

But that was a future problem.

Now, the mattress lying in wait in the large entrance way, she clambered over it and hurried to the den where the real work would begin.

Only, when she got started, she realised she hadn’t actually made a fort in years.

So, one call to her cousin Mateo later, and after a very unnecessarily long guilt trip from him about “not answering her fucking phone, prima!” She managed to get some half-hearted instructions.

First, came the gathering. Chairs, laundry baskets, brooms, heavy books, any kind of clips she could find.

Then, according to Mateo, floor first. She moved the mattress into the room and swept the coffee table aside.

Next was the roof. Sheets upon sheets stolen from the laundry room. Mateo had made it sound easy. But then the last time he’d made a fort had been years ago too.

So either he’d forgotten how hard it was or it was simply easier when you were a kid and less intent on perfection.

It took Rio hours. Mostly because whenever something wasn’t exactly the way she wanted she huffed and became too heavy-handed and often had to start all over again.

But soon, she had something that resembled a fort. She’d used the couch to act as the back wall. Chairs to help prop the sheets of the roof up. The mattress covered the majority of the floor and one side remained open so the tv could be in view.

It wasn’t perfect, but she’d tried her best. Three hours’ worth of her best.

And the next part was the fun part. She added pillows and comforters, cushions and blankets. She stole Nicky’s nightlight so the roof was full of stars.

It looked better now. It looked worthy of the patitos she’d built it for.

She scrambled away, went to organise snacks and drinks. And there, at the kitchen table, she poured out bags of Skittles into a bowl and began the task of removing all the purple ones so Agatha could enjoy them without worry.

While she worked she called her mom and mostly listened whilst she told her the latest family gossip.

“¿Y este tema vaquero? ¿Fue idea de Nicky?” And this cowboy theme? Was it Nicky’s idea?

Rio stopped where she’d been about to drop a handful of Skittles into her mouth.

“¿Qué mamá?”

Anna Vidal sighed and Rio placed the skittles back in the bowl.

“Tu cumpleaños, mija.” Your birthday.

Rio stared straight ahead, doing the mental maths it took to figure out the date. Her birthday was a week away.

“I… cowboys?”

“Sí, mija. Nunca escuchas. Vaqueros. Tu fiesta. Yes, daughter. You never listen. Cowboys. Your party.

“Mom, is… I’m having a party?”

“Sí.”

“Is Agatha throwing me a party?”

“Sí. Creo que es una sopresa, pero saberlo ahora no reducirá el disfrute, estoy seguro.” Yes. I think it’s a surprise but knowing now won’t reduce the enjoyment, I’m sure.

“You’re coming?”

Rio ran her hand through her hair and heard her mom sigh again, though she seemed less frustrated this time.

She’d switched to English, a result of her daughter’s influence, rather than a preference.

“Yes. Agatha’s flying me out on Friday. I tried to argue but she insisted. I’m coming with Mateo and she’s booked us a table somewhere.”

“All of us? Her too?”

Another sigh, a gentler one.

“No, mija. I think just us. Alice too.”

Rio nodded silently, trying to absorb all of this new information, wondering when Agatha had the time to arrange it, to even dream it all up.

“And you’ve been in contact with-…?”

But Anna had cut her off, slipping naturally back into her preferred language: “Tu papa tenía razón sober ella.” Your dad was right about her.

“Cómo, mamá?”

“Ella tiene un buen corazón.” She has a good heart.

Rio closed her eyes, her dad’s voice swimming into her mind, flooding her chest with grief.

“Le extraño.” I miss him.

“Lo sé, cariño. Yo también.” I know, honey. Me too.

They were silent on the phone then. The kind of silence that was comfortable because of the love that filled it. Miguel was there. He was listening in the quiet.

“I should go,” Rio said, sniffing rudely as she wiped at her cheek. “I have to prep the dinner and-…”

“¿La comida?” Dinner

“Sí, mamá. Don’t make fun.”

Anna laughed and Rio found herself smiling despite the fact she was being made fun of.

“You’re trying.” English again, her mom’s attempt to make up for the fact she’d just laughed at her.

“As hard as I can.”

“Agatha said she’s doing okay?”

“Sí. Just okay.”

“Okay, mija. Te amo. Call me soon. I mean it.”

“Sí, mamá. Claro. Te amo.”

When Rio hung up on her mom she took a few minutes. A few minutes of nothing, of silence, of time to just sit in her thoughts.

In them she found her dad. She found his gentleness and his wisdom. She felt his arms around her and she cried because he wasn’t there.

Her dad remained with her as she worked that afternoon, in Agatha’s hilltop house. He was there as she put the finishing touches on the fort. He was there as she made her cheese sauce for the macaroni she was making.

He was there as she deliberated on how many snacks were too many snacks.

He was there as she thought about the two patitos wandering around Disney, with so many eyes on them they’d surely be miserable.

He was there as she now sat in the finished fort in her cowboy pyjamas, tucking Agatha’s ring into the corner so she could reveal it at just the right time.

He was everywhere she looked, and nowhere to be found.

But something made her turn as the velvet ring box was hidden securely away and she covered it was an extra cushion for safe-keeping. Perhaps it had been a noise, maybe it had been a movement.

But as she turned she saw a leaf pressed up against the sunny window. The leaf was shaped like a star, highlighted by the sun’s rays dazzling behind it.

Rio paused. She smiled.

There he was.

“Hola, papá.”

The leaf fluttered in the breeze and fell as the front door opened and Rio turned to the direction of the noise.

She heard Agatha’s voice but couldn’t decipher the words. She heard the sounds of bags being put down, of shoes being removed, of jackets thrown off and carefully hung up. And then, bringing the thunder, she heard Nicky walking towards the little family room that now housed Fort Patito.

She smiled for his heavy steps, the noisiest thing about the shy little boy, and stood to meet him halfway.

And then there he was, eyes wide and expectant as he rounded the corner and entered the room. He was wearing a Toy Story shirt and had a lanyard of various Disney characters dotted all about it.

And Rio grinned for the sight of the boy she’d missed all week.

Nicky threw himself at Rio and Rio caught him with ease, having been ready for the kamikaze that was Agatha’s son.

“You’re here!”

Rio laughed as she kissed the top of his head and looked up to see Agatha paused by the doorway, watching with a sad look in her eyes. Rio straightened and let Nicky just cling.

“Hola, mi vida. Te he extrañado.” I’ve missed you.

Nicky, still with his arms around Rio, craned his neck to get a look at his mama. Rio was looking too. Agatha was yet to move and Rio thought she knew why. Because she felt the same.

Standing here with Nicky she was able to experience what it was to have Agatha return home to her. And for Agatha, she was experiencing Rio there when she came home.

Just as she’d wanted. Just as she’d asked. Once a week.

It would never be enough.

“Ha sido un mal día.” It has been a bad day.

Rio sucked in a soft breath at Agatha’s words and nodded silently, raising her hand towards her to invite her in. But Agatha didn’t move. In fact, she barely responded to it.

“Agatha,” Rio encouraged, using her name because she needed Agatha to listen. But before she could say anything else, Agatha had found her voice again.

“Estábamos en el lugar más feliz del mundo y yo era tan miserable. Hice que mi hijo fuera miserable.” We were in the happiest place on earth and I was miserable. I made my son miserable.

Rio’s hand moved back to Nicky and she held him where he still stood against her, clinging to her. She realised now that his shout earlier hadn’t been excitement. It had been relief.

She was silent for a second, assessing the situation. Nicky was still clinging on, his fists against her sides. And Agatha? She was stock still, her eyes on the little vignette, a visitor to a museum, paying the price to see the art.

“Entonces ven aquí y déjame hacerlo mejor.” Then come here and let me make it better.

It happened slowly, as she expected it to. Agatha took each step precisely when she meant to. She walked as if holding herself back. But every inch closer to Rio she seemed to speed up, as if proximity were an encouragement.

And when they collided the comfort was immediate. Agatha’s hand found the back of Rio’s head and her face found the crook of her neck.

Agatha’s dark puzzle came together then. The colour came back as Rio gripped her and Agatha released a breathy laugh of relief against her skin.

Rio just held her two patitos, one hand on Nicky’s back where he was pressed between them, the other around Agatha. No one moved for a while. And Rio wondered if their heartbeats were in sync, like newborn puppies whose hearts with their owners.

A sign of comfort. A sign of love.

But peace could only last so long.

“What the hell is that monstrosity behind you?”

Rio rolled her eyes as Agatha pulled back but all amusement vanished when she saw her expression. She was deflecting. Maybe for Rio’s sake. Maybe for Nicky’s.

Rio looked down to Nicky then and forced a smile, “Hey, why don’t you go check out the monstrosity? Let me know what you think.”

Nicky nodded and seemed reluctant until Agatha touched his head and he looked to her for reassurance. He hurried away shortly afterwards.

“How bad?”

Rio asked softly, her arms snaking back around Agatha where she’d released to let Nicky slip away.

“He had a panic attack on the teacups.”

Rio’s stomach dropped and she couldn’t speak for a second. “What? A… what happened?”

“Everyone was taking photos. Everyone was just staring. Everyone was-…”

“Mama!”

“A panic attack?” Rio asked, barely getting the words out before she felt Nicky’s hands on her arm. Agatha managed a slight nod before she turned to Nicky.

Everything slowed then. Like moving a spoon through cold honey, Rio couldn’t make her mind or body catch up to the present.

She found herself being led back to the fort she’d made in the hopes of surprising the two now tugging her back to it. But her mind was elsewhere. She was spinning like the teacups Nicky had panicked in.

Only slower. Only infinitely slower.

The hand in her own was what melted the honey stickying up her mind. Agatha had taken hold of her right hand, had squeezed it, had tugged gently for her attention. Rio looked to her as Nicky asked, “Can we sleep in here?”

Agatha looked into the fort. Rio saw the starlight reflecting in her eyes and the tension fading along her brow. It made Rio take a deep breath, made the syrup of her mind fade until all that was left was the taste of sweetness on her tongue.

Agatha glanced at her, her voice mellifluous as she said: “I suppose we could.”

A squeeze of her hand told her that Agatha was asking. But Rio didn’t think she was asking if they could sleep there, she knew she was asking if Rio were staying.

“I pulled down a mattress for your elderly back.”

Nicky laughed and Rio shot him an unforced grin, feeling Agatha tug her back close and her arms wrap around her from where she she stood in against her side. But Agatha didn’t respond to the tease like she usually might. She instead dropped her head to Rio’s shoulder and everything unspoken rang suddenly loud and clear.

“It’s awesome!”

Rio smiled and allowed Agatha to hold her for a second more and then she pulled way, following Nicky into the fort. She was the one to tug Agatha this time.

“I made snacks and-… oomph.”

Agatha had fallen, or launched herself, on top of her. She made her turn and had simultaneously thrown herself at her. They’d landed face to face and then Agatha had, as gracefully and casually as possible, repositioned herself to face away from Rio, her gaze on the stars.

So Rio now sat, amidst all the pillows and blankets, with Agatha in her lap and Nicky by their side. Rio huffed out a breath against Agatha’s shoulder but just wrapped her arms around her and said nothing.

Nicky was busy fluffing up some cushions and Rio watched his little face as he concentrated. He looked so serious that Rio smiled at the sight. But the second he huffed she reached out for him to get his attention.

Perhaps he was still spinning too.

“You okay, mellizo?”

Nicky looked up, looked at Agatha, then at Rio, his brow was still furrowed but it soon relaxed and a slow smile spread up his face. Rio’s hand dropped and she raised her brows as she went right back to hugging Agatha. But that appeared to be why Nicky was now grinning.

“I was looking for our pyjamas but maybe mama just wants to stay here instead of changing.”

“No,” Rio interjected just as Agatha opened her mouth to protest about being called out so immediately by her own son. “You both have you go change. I need to get the snacks in anyway. You were home sooner than I thought you’d be.”

“Fine here,” Agatha muttered as Nicky began to try and tug her from Rio’s hold.

But Rio pushed at her even though she wanted to hold her forever. For doing so she received a glare from Agatha and the gift of hearing Nicky’s laughter all the way up the stairs.

She took a breath, alone again. And then went to sort out the promised snacks.

In the large bowl full of Skittles she realised she must have panic thrown in a couple bags because there were definitely more purple ones than she remembered.

Skittles, and more chocolate that was reasonable, along with chips of all kinds, and no fruit or healthy foods to be seen, now all piled onto a tray, she carried them through and dotted them about the space.

So, snacks laid out, pillows plumped, she settled back to welcome a rushing Oscar winner back into her arms.

Agatha was breathless as she whispered against her ear, “Thank you. Thank you, he needed this. I needed this.”

As Nicky rounded the corner, Rio whispered back, “I needed it too.”

She felt Agatha’s lips ghost over her cheek and turned to look at her. They locked eyes for only a second before a third body collided with them and Agatha received a knee to the side which made her gasp and groan as she caught him.

“Ooh. Sorry, mama.”

Rio laughed as she heaved Nicky away and into the cushions, allowing Agatha to groan more dramatically now she had some space.

Nicky giggled and Rio looked back at her girlfriend with an arched brow.

“You okay over there, drama queen?”

“You should be protecting me!”

“From your son?”

“From your mellizo!”

Nicky laughed so hard he snorted and Rio began to laugh again too, easily diving back for Agatha to pull her down with them.

“So dramatic.”

“I’m an actress! An injured one!”

Rio hummed as she smiled and Agatha managed to wrestle her way back into a seated position. She made a disgruntled noise and grabbed a handful of Skittles.

Rio was busy whispering to Nicky about how “actresses are always dramatic and never to trust them” when she felt a tap on her shoulder and she turned to see a fist being held out to her.

She placed her hand expectantly beneath it from her prone position and Agatha dropped three purple Skittles into it. Rio looked at them for a second and then sat slowly up as Agatha turned back around to face away from her.

With a fist of Skittles and her arm back around Agatha’s waist she kissed her shoulder.

“I thought I got rid of them all.”

“Obviously not.”

Rio hummed, felt a tap on her knuckles, and opened her hand again for the fourth Skittle to be dropped there.

She said nothing as she shuffled back and tugged Agatha with her, purple Skittles still in her hand.

Another tap. Another Skittle.

“You wanna pick a movie, mellizo? We can watch a bit then I’ve made dinner and-…”

“You made dinner?”

Agatha had shifted back, craning her neck round to look at Rio.

“Mmhm. Nothing fancy. Just mac and cheese.”

“From scratch?”

Rio felt a jolt of pride as she nodded, “From scratch.”

Agatha’s gaze softened and Rio’s pride swelled in her chest. A noise on the tv made her look away for a second and Agatha pressed a swift kiss to her cheek.

“Eat your Skittles. You’ll stain your hand.”

Rio just grinned inanely but managed to spark at least one brain cell to eat the abandoned Skittles.

She clapped her hand to her mouth, threw them in there and happily tasted purple on her tongue.

Nicky was sticking his hands in every bowl, happily munching away at every sweet treat Rio had gathered for him. He was so intent on his munching that he’d forgotten entirely about picking a movie.

“Can we have ice cream later?”

“Of course! I got some pecan for your mom too.”

Agatha said nothing in response to this, now fully leaning against Rio, occasionally placing a purple skittle in her waiting palm.

“This is the best,” Nicky said as he ate another chocolate pretzel. “Maybe we can do this every night.”

“But then it won’t feel special.”

“That’s okay, it’ll feel ordinary and that’s good too.”

Rio felt Agatha shift slightly against her and she found that she was moving away, leaving Rio with a handful of skittles and a heart full of longing.

Rio watched as Agatha abandoned her rainbow bowl and she sat the other side of Nicky.

“Does this place have four walls?”

Rio nodded and went to pull the overhanging sheet down so they could be ensconced in stars. Nicky oohed quietly and Rio settled back beside him, looking up at the galaxy she’d made with a little bit of effort and a whole lot of love.

They tangled together then. Nicky reached for Rio’s hand. Both were a little sticky. Nicky’s from chocolate; Rio’s from Agatha’s Skittle offering. Agatha wrapped her arm around Nicky and Rio reached over to toy with the ends of Agatha’s hair.

In another world, in another time, they could have been doing this under the real night sky. Rio might have built a fire for them to gather around. They would have been in warmer clothes, not cowboy pyjamas. They would have been surrounded by nature, trees or mountains or fields.

But they would have been equally as happy.

They would have been equally as entangled.

They would still be a family. In every lifetime, in every place their souls met.

“That’s your sign,” Agatha pointed out, her index finger held high in the air as Nicky followed its line. “Pisces. See the way it angles out? Then there’s Pegasus, the horse. It’s just a little wonky because of the shape of the ceiling. But the other side is Aries. That’s Rio’s. The ram.”

“And you?”

Rio looked down from the ceiling of celestial bodies to the mega star pointing them out. She caught Agatha’s eye and felt a strange glimmer of emotion that made her turn away and look back to where Agatha was now pointing.

“Just here. Near Rio’s. Taurus. Shaped like a bull. Next to the hunter.”

Agatha’s finger traced the shape of both constellations and Rio felt Nicky’s fingers tighten around her own.

“But we’re close to protect you from him.”

“Yes, honey.”

“You know,” Rio said quietly, surprising herself when her voice croaked. “These stars have been there for millennia. Milenios. And the hunter might seem scary but he’s never caught Taurus. Your mama has been safe durante milenios. She’s protected us durante milenios. It’s written in the stars that we’re safe. That we’re together.”

Her hand fell from the tips of Agatha’s hair to her lower back and Nicky dropped Rio’s hand and leant more into his mom.

They sat in silence for a while and Rio only realised that Agatha was no longer looking at the stars when she felt a soft tug against her shirt.

She turned and saw galaxies in sea blue eyes.

Rio had to look back to the stars because if she didn’t she’d float away in Agatha’s gaze. To her left, hidden deep in the cushions, she knew was the thing that could anchor them.

She bit the inside of her cheek and remained quiet for a little while longer before she announced.

“Why don’t I leave you stargazers for a little while and I’ll go sort out dinner? You can pick a movie and we can eat it in here.”

Nicky nodded, smiling dreamily where he was now tucked into Agatha’s side. Agatha offered to help but Rio refused, squeezing her shoulder briefly before she tore apart their celestial world and stepped into the real one.

Alone in the kitchen she swallowed the knowledge she’d been fighting since she’d acquired it. Nicky had been so stressed and so frightened that he’d had a bad day in the happiest place on earth.

Agatha had had a bad day.

She placed the macaroni pot in the oven. She hung her head down, trying not to imagine Agatha and Jen trying to comfort a boy who couldn’t breathe as he span hopelessly around and around on the teacups.

She couldn’t dwell on it. Couldn’t stand by a hot oven all night thinking about his face screwed up in panic, Agatha’s desperate hands, Jen’s frantic reassurances.

She turned and walked back to the starfield.

The fort was closed again. And through the thin sheets Rio could hear Agatha’s voice.

“We can buy one, if you like?”

“We can?”

“Mmhm. And you can name it whatever you want.”

Rio hovered close by, could almost hear the cogs in Nicky’s brain turning as he thought. But then Agatha ripped the sheet back and her eavesdropping was exposed.

“Shadows exist, you know.”

Rio grinned and crawled back in to take up her spot beside Nicky again.

“I just didn’t want to interrupt.”

“Uh huh,” Agatha uttered, a smile on her face now as she settled more back with Nicky.

“You know,” Rio said as she lay down properly and crossed her hands over her stomach. “Maybe we can do this for real one day. Camping, I mean.”

“Absolutely not.”

“Yes, mama! I think we should!”

Rio laughed, a bark of a laugh that made Agatha lean over and push at her shoulder.

“Okay then, mellizo. Just you and me. We can have all the snacks and-…”

“Oh just dropping me so quickly?”

“Back to being dramatic.”

Rio turned her head to the side and raised her brows at Agatha, watching as she struggled with her chosen reaction. Because it was just that: chosen. She was trying to ham things up; trying to make it a game, make it exciting.

She was distracting Nicky using her Oscar-winning talent.

It made Rio love her more.

“Mellizo, we can camp for a whole week. Make fires every night, make smores on them.”

“Really?”

Nicky shuffled down to mimic Rio’s position and lay exactly as she was, his hands crossing over his own stomach.

“And what will I do?”

Rio grinned at Agatha and raised her brows, “Hold down the fort?”

“Very funny.”

“Mama you can call every day.”

“Oh great, thank you. So generous, honey.”

Rio stuck her tongue between her teeth and lazily reached over to pull Nicky into her side, tucking him under her arm.

“Just dos patitos in our little tent. All warm and snuggly and-…”

“Fine! I’ll come! Stop asking.”

Rio laughed and shot Agatha a grin, identifying the tinge of sadness in Agatha’s gaze. She lifted her hand from Nicky’s arm and reached towards her. But Agatha didn’t move, she instead dropped her gaze to her son and reached to brush his hair back from his face.

Rio stopped reaching and curled her arm back around Nicky. She understood that Agatha wanted all efforts for comfort to be on him in that moment so she tugged him a bit closer and he naturally cuddled in.

“We missed you today, melliza.”

Nicky shifted slightly and reached for the ends of Rio’s hair.

“Mama said you could come next time though.”

Rio glanced Agatha’s way but saw she wasn’t looking, she was instead staring at the stars above, on her back beside them on the mattress.

“I’d like that,” she whispered gently, squeezing Nicky’s side. “I love rollercoasters.”

“You do?”

“Mmhm. I like the fast ones and the ones that go upside down.”

“Me too.”

“Yeah?”

Nicky shifted, “Well, no. But I think I’d like them if you were there.”

Rio hummed quietly and found that Agatha’s hand was now above hers, her fingers slotting down to fill the gaps that had always been hers to fill. Rio turned her head, rested her chin on Nicky’s head and smiled as she looked across at Agatha.

“Maybe on our camping trip we can take a detour to some rollercoasters. Tres patitos on tour.”

Agatha’s gaze lifted then and Rio’s lips twitched but didn’t form the smile they threatened. The air felt heavy as Agatha moved in and kissed Nicky’s temple, barely having to move much more to kiss Rio’s cheek.

“I’m going to go check dinner.”

“Mi vida, let me.”

“No, stay with Nicky. I’ll be right back.”

Rio nodded as best she could and watched Agatha crawl from the fort and disappear out from under the sheet. Nicky seemed to hold her more securely now they were alone, his fist clutching at the collar of Rio’s pyjama top.

“I didn’t enjoy today.” Nicky, barely whispering.

“No, mellizo?”

“No.”

Rio pulled cautiously back and gently pried his fist from her collar so she could move down and lay before him, shifting until they were face to face. She touched his warm cheek and smiled for the wide-eyed wonder of his identical face.

“Tell me what happened.”

Nicky dropped his gaze and the fist that had been on her shirt now curled just beneath his chin. He was silent and Rio was too, giving him the time he needed to decide what he wanted to say.

“Can we cuddle again, please?”

Rio nodded and tugged Nicky closer before he could even begin to move. She exhaled slowly and heavily as he snuggled in and pressed a kiss to the top of his head.

They were still and silent for a while until Nicky began to wriggle and Rio loosened her hold to allow him to pull back.

“Te amo, por siete.” I love you, times seven.

“Siete?”

“I didn’t get to say it this week. You told me we could say it every day.”

Rio smiled sadly and bit down on her lip. “Te amo, mellizo. Hasta el infinito.”

“Counting the stars in the sky?”

“Every single one.”

Nicky nodded seriously, a little frown appearing as a little pout did too.

“You look so like your mama.”

“No, I look like you.”

“Mm, but sometimes you look like your mama.”

Nicky dropped his gaze and Rio sighed quietly, “What is it?”

“You’ve been working a lot this week? Mama said you had.”

“I have.”

“That’s why you haven’t come around?”

“It is.”

Nicky nodded and Rio pressed her finger to the tip of his nose. “But I’m here now.”

“You’re staying tomorrow?”

“Maybe.”

“We’d both like it if you would.”

“I’d like it too.”

Nicky nodded and Rio bit the corner of her lip, studying his concerned features.

He was silent for a while and then he took a big, deep breath before he released his words in a blustering rush: “One of the boys at school said I’d have to live with my dad half the time because of the divorce but I was thinking maybe I could live half the time with you and mama could be there every day that would be okay wouldn’t it? It would be okay?”

Rio’s heart constricted, making her breathless for a second before she was able to whisper: “Honey, your mom is doing everything she can to make sure that doesn’t happen, that you’ll always be with her.”

Nicky stared somewhere around Rio’s chin and Rio let him think, deciding forcing a reaction would not be the way to go.

“But just in case, just in case that doesn’t happen, I don’t want to live with my daddy.”

“Okay, honey. I know.”

Nicky looked up then and Rio had to fight the urge to cry even as she looked into dark eyes already welling with tears.

“I want to be with mama every day.”

“And that,” Rio said quietly, moving her hand up to gently brush Nicky’s hair back from his forehead, “is what’s going to happen. You and your mama, every day.”

Nicky nodded and went silent again and Rio was unable to speak any longer for fear she’d sob instead.

By the time Agatha came back in with a tray full of macaroni all dished up into separate bowls, the twins were on their backs, holding hands, looking up at the stars.

Agatha was silent as she distributed the food and Rio couldn’t bring herself to say anything either. The only noise that broke the reverie was Nicky’s soft “thank you” to his mom as he accepted his bowl.

They all sat up, a line of ducklings half buried under blankets. The front sheet was thrown up, a movie was chosen, and Rio’s first attempt at macaroni from scratch was proven to be a hit.

Though, Nicky’s assessment was slightly more enthusiastic than Agatha’s. But Rio took it as a success.

The carby pasta and molten cheese were enough to soothe the ache in her chest and for the first time in her life Rio truly understood the meaning of the words “comfort food”.

She gathered the finished bowls, fetched everyone drinks, and soon no one was half-buried anymore. Everyone was practically hidden in the fort built to comfort and protect.

There was a lot of wriggling too. Agatha, who’d eaten her dinner the other side of Nicky, was now making her way over to Rio and claiming her place against her as she was half-propped up under the pretence of watching Cars.

Rio didn’t comment about this move and neither did Nicky. Which seemed to suit Agatha because she appeared smug as she settled half-over Rio.

“Could you pass me the blanket?”

Nicky moved to grab a nearby, quilted blanket.

“No, not that one, Nicky.”

“Melizzo,” Nicky muttered and Rio smiled as he handed over the other, thinner, blanket that she’d indicated.

“Thank you, melizzo.”

Nicky blushed but smiled all the same as Rio spread the blanket out over herself and Agatha, having kicked off the other coverings the moment she’d arrived.

“Isn’t it a bit thin? We’ll be freezing.”

“Mm.” Rio just hummed and kept her focus on the blanket that she was now brushing down around Agatha’s shoulders.

“Rio.”

Rio sighed and turned her head after checking Nicky was focused in on the movie.

“If you’re cold you’ll stay closer.”

Agatha scoffed hot air against her neck and Rio smiled, pleased her point had already been proven correct.

But a second later Agatha had pulled back and Rio was turning to look at her.

“You’re pouting,” Rio whispered, smiling where she’d turned her head a fraction just to see Agatha’s face.

“I am not,” she lied.

Her pout became poutier.

Rio grinned and wished she could kiss it away. Instead she pressed a finger to it and watched as Agatha’s eyes lifted to meet her own. Agatha wanted to kiss her too. That much was clear.

They hadn’t kissed for three days now. Seventy two long hours. Rio had somehow squeezed in four runs during that time. One weight training session. One half-hearted yoga attempt.

But no kiss.

She was sick of this already and it had only been a week. But it was for Nicky. Nicky couldn’t know, couldn’t even really suspect. They were already flying close to the wire by lying like this.

He already told everyone about Rio so there was no chance in hell he’d not mention that Rio liked to kiss his mama and his mama liked to kiss Rio back.

Hell, he’d spilled the beans to Jen about Alice already.

So Rio didn’t kiss Agatha. She just looked at her lips, brushed her finger along her lower one, and then turned away.

Agatha sighed quietly and snuck down, choosing now to rest her head on Rio’s shoulder, to hold her shirt at her collar, to move away from the danger zone. And soon Nicky joined her, the exact reflection of his mother.

Rio was glad of it. If she couldn’t kiss Agatha she could hold her still. Despite Jen’s protestations. Despite Alice’s warnings.

Despite Nicky nestling in closer below the thin blanket.

Rio hummed. It was a happy little noise of contentment that was only to be shushed by Agatha a second later. She frowned and Agatha pushed up to grin down at her, “We’re watching.”

Rio narrowed her eyes up at Agatha and watched in slow motion as her smile transitioned to a pout again. Nicky shuffled up too as Rio continued to glower.

“You’re missing it.”

Rio hummed again, a more thoughtful sound this time, and Agatha continued to pout, now fluttering her lashes. Nicky giggled.

“Melliza, mama wants some attention.”

Rio barked a laugh at the same time Agatha gasped. It all happened at once. Agatha launched at Nicky and Rio cackled where she lay on the mattress between them. They were a tangle of limbs, a mess of reactions, a cacophony of noise, laughter, squeals.

Rio was the willing and able platform for it all. Nicky squirmed and giggled whilst Agatha lay half over Rio and attacked his sides and Rio just laughed through it all, holding Agatha only because she didn’t know what else to do with her arms.

By the time Agatha was done with her assault Rio could no longer breathe and was gasping for air as laughter escaped her like sparks on a fire.

“You do!” Nicky gasped as he continued to giggle and wriggle away, “Mama wants attention!”

Rio felt Agatha’s hand against her ribs and she turned her head to look at her, her eyes wet with tears and her grin now permanently etched onto her face.

Agatha was fighting a smile but scowling as best she could.

“You are both so mean to me.”

“Not mean, mama!” Nicky laughed again and Rio hummed as Agatha’s fingers flexed against her skin and then slid over to rest on her sternum.

“So mean.”

Rio raised her brows as Agatha’s hand slid further to rest across her stomach and she caught her eye and felt hot all of a sudden. The kind of heat that wasn’t appropriate right now.

“Nicky,” Rio uttered, still staring at his mom, “Could you go get me a glass of water?”

“Mellizo,” he corrected in a quiet voice even as he scrambled from the fort to do as he was asked and soft giggles still escaped him every second breath.

Alone now, Agatha’s hand travelled back up until it was over Rio’s breast, until she was squeezing her there, making Rio gasp quietly.

“Don’t.”

“Didn’t you hear Nicky? I want attention.”

Rio bit the corner of her lip, which helped nothing, because now Agatha was looking down at it.

“If I told you I was ready to give it to you?” Agatha squeezed and Rio groaned.

“Then I’d say when? How soon? Because I’m feeling feral over here. Seeing as I haven’t been able to… release any tension for a few days.”

Agatha’s hand moved down again and to Rio’s horror she began to toy with the strings of her pyjama pants.

“And as sweet as this fort is, sleeping here means I can’t ride you until I’m so sore I cry.”

“That’s-… I-…”

“Here!”

Nicky was back. Agatha’s hand was back above the blanket. Rio wanted to die.

She scowled. Agatha grinned.

Nicky shuffled on his knees with the glass of water held out. “Melliza.”

Rio took it and forced herself to smile. “Thank you, baby.” She sat up and dislodged Agatha from where she’d been trying to rest back against her.

Agatha huffed and followed Rio up and Rio smirked against the rim of the glass as she lifted her arm up so Agatha could tuck into her.

“It’s too cold to move far away.”

Rio shrugged as she drank and then muttered, “Everyone is missing the movie.”

Nicky shuffled closer and Rio felt the rush of cool air as their thin blanket was lifted and suddenly Nicky was leaning against her arm. She felt Agatha squeeze her side, saw Nicky reposition Scratchy into her lap, and suddenly felt warm again.

A different kind of warmth this time. A secure, safe kind of warmth.

A warmth that led to Agatha falling asleep against her as Rio played with her hair. One that soon meant Nicky was too warm so he shuffled away with Scratchy and did Rio the favour of placing her water on the side.

Nicky whispered into the quiet of the fort, above the noise of the movie, “We never did this with daddy.”

Rio turned her head to look at the little boy with his little rabbit and smiled so she wouldn’t cry. Ralph would pay for what he’d done to this family. She’d see to it that he’d pay.

She reached a hand out towards him and the patito reached back.

Neither said anything and soon both returned to watching the movie. Or, pretending to, as Rio was. But Nicky held on to her hand the whole time. And Rio found after a while Nicky began to toy with her fingers the way she was toying with his mom’s hair.

She watched his movements, looked up to his face as he became absorbed in the action on screen. He looked at peace as he focused in and Rio wished she could bottle this moment up with Nicky calm and happy and Agatha fast asleep against her.

But unbeknownst to Rio, Agatha was no longer asleep. Tucked beneath Rio’s chin she was now awake and watching the scene before her. Her eyes first fell to Rio’s hand in her son’s. She then looked up to the way Nicky was engrossed in the movie. And then she took in the cowboy pyjamas, the messy hair that couldn’t be touched by anyone other than her and his melliza.

She dropped her gaze to the rabbit in his free hand, the companion he’d had since he was a baby. Her eyes moved up Rio’s arm, focusing on the scars forming where her mother had held her.

Agatha reached for Rio there and Rio looked down and that’s when she first realised Agatha was awake again.

“It’s fine,” she whispered, knowing what Agatha was concerned about.

“They’re scarring.”

Rio said nothing but watched Agatha’s fingers dance over the wounds she bore with pride. Agatha shifted against her until her head with at the centre of her chest, her body now fully on top of Rio’s.

“Cuatro. Cuatro cicatrices. Cuatro pecas.” Four. Four scars. Four freckles.

“Melliza,” Nicky said quietly, half-glancing towards her and half-still focused on the tv. “Shh.”

Rio tightened her one-armed hold around Agatha but said nothing as Agatha adjusted herself to move up Rio’s body, her face now pressed in against Rio’s cheek.

Rio felt the warmth of her breath and the press of her nose and she closed her eyes as she felt the brush of her lips.

“I know why you’ve allowed it.”

Agatha’s words were softly breathed against her cheek and Rio had to fight the shiver they encouraged.

“I wish you hadn’t.”

Agatha brushed the tip of her nose across her skin and raised her head up more to kiss Rio’s temple.

Rio swallowed thickly, feeling every movement of every part of Agatha’s body as she moved above her. If Nicky weren’t here she might have done something different. She might have moved her hands over every inch of Agatha’s body to feel her more. She wanted to feel her everywhere.

Agatha settled down again and Rio held her son’s hand as the movie continued.

Exhausted from a stressful day and full of mac and cheese and so much chocolate, Nicky fell asleep before the movie finished.

Neither Rio nor Agatha moved until the movie was actually done and when the credits began to roll Agatha slid from Rio to turn off the tv. She pulled the sheet down so they were trapped in their handmade celestial haven and she tucked Nicky in with the deft hand of a natural-born mother.

Rio just watched, just waited, knew that soon she could have Agatha back against her and she could make her promise to her official.

If Agatha allowed it.

Agatha soon crawled back over. She soon took up her spot over Rio, soon kissed her for the first time in three days.

It was a firm, insistent kiss. But both were aware of the little boy not feet away, his right arm flung up above his head, his left hand curled around Scratchy.

When they broke apart Rio saw more stars than before. She saw them in the freckles across Agatha’s skin, she saw them in the light of her eyes.

It had to be now.

She might not get another chance.

She rolled them, half breathless, half choking on air.

Agatha’s eyes widened a little, a silent question. Rio felt her hand slide down her hip, squeezing her. It felt reassuring. It felt like Agatha knew something important was about to happen.

Rio rolled them again.

She hovered over Agatha now. She was diligent about making sure Agatha wasn’t trapping her own hair and Rio wasn’t leaning on it.

She touched her cheek, felt Agatha squeeze her again.

“How do I love thee?” Rio began softly, barely moving the air with her words. “Let me count the ways.”

She leant up and across and Agatha beneath her gasped as Rio covered her entirely. She felt her hand fly up her side, her other move to grasp her pants by her hip. And then she was back again, back on her side, back before an already teary Agatha who she’d tugged over with her.

“I love thee,” she continued just as quietly, feeling a lump beginning to form in her throat.

“To the depth and breadth and height my soul can reach, when feeling out of sight,” she moved to brush the tear from Agatha’s cheek, “for the ends of Being and ideal Grace.”

Her thumb circled down to Agatha’s lips and she watched as she tasted the salt from her skin.

“I love thee to the level of every day’s most quiet need, by sun and candle light.”

Agatha breathed a gasp as Rio flipped open the soft lid of the ring box she’d moved into her line of sight.

“I love thee freely, as men strive for right.” She fumbled it over, using one hand to free the ring. “I love thee purely, as they turn from praise.”

She slipped her thumb into it and prized it from its cushion.

“I love thee with the passion put to use in my old griefs, and with my childhood’s faith.”

Rio sat slowly, peeling away so she could take Agatha’s left hand.

“I love thee with a love I seemed to lose with my lost saints.” She moved the ring to her palm and cupped it as she positioned Agatha’s hand and watched her silent tears.

“I love thee with the breath, smiles, tears, of all my life.”

She slid the gold ring onto Agatha’s finger and felt the first of her own tears mar her cheek.

“And, if god choose, I shall but love thee better after death.”

Rio sealed her golden promise with a kiss to the ring now on Agatha’s finger and raised her gaze up to see Agatha’s eyes were closed and her lips parted. She leant in to kiss them and found Agatha to be barely able to respond, hardly kissing her back.

“A promise,” Rio whispered against her parted lips. “Until I can propose. Until we can marry. I want you to have my promise.”

“Rio.”

“I chose it because I promised you a bigger ring than his. Because you can wear it without people knowing what it is and what it means. I’ve had it inscribed in my own handwriting. ‘Felizmente casada ’. Happily married. It’s a promise. Because we will be. As soon as I can marry you, I will.”

Rio’s hand moved down to hold Agatha’s cheek and she frowned, briefly panicking that she’d done the wrong thing. But Agatha was gathering herself. She was taking slow breaths. She was trying to find the words she soon whispered: “That poem. How… how did you know? I used to read that poem in high school. I read it every day and prayed one day I’d feel that… Rio, I read it every day.”

Rio’s thumb settled at the corner of Agatha’s lip and she looked into the storm of her sea blue eyes as drowned herself in them.

“You said the first line to me last Saturday. I memorised it the moment I left you.”

“I did? You did?”

Rio nodded silently, her lips twitching into a hopeful smile.

Agatha seemed to falter again, her lips forming words she couldn’t say until:

“I wrote a paper on romantic love being compared to the divine. I wrote and read because I didn’t understand. And then I saw you,” Agatha gasped a breath she hadn’t take since she started speaking. “And then I met you and-…”

But her volume was picking up with the tears that still streamed and Rio leant back in to kiss her again and shushed her gently.

“I love you. I want to learn every poem you’ve ever read so I can speak it back to you. I want to read them in bed with you every night and tell you how they make me feel and hear how they make you feel.”

“Rio.”

“I want to marry you and maybe-…”

“Rio.”

“Maybe one day,” Rio stopped herself, took a breath, “cuatro patitos.”

“Rio.”

“We already made a perfect kid.” Agatha gasped quietly. “We can make another.”

“Rio.”

Agatha’s hand made its way to Rio’s cheek and Rio turned into it, her lips just brushing the cool metal of Agatha’s new ring.

“I love you.”

Agatha took a breath and nodded but couldn’t find the words again so Rio kissed her once more. The little boy asleep not far from them meant that everything was chaste, everything was soft and silent, but it didn’t matter anymore.

Agatha wore Rio’s ring. Her real ring. The one she’d bought for her. The one she’d inscribed with her promise to her.

Rio settled down against Agatha soon enough. She aligned their bodies and rolled them so Agatha’s left hand could be free. She watched as Agatha looked at her ring, as she admired it in the light, as she continued to return her gaze to Rio.

They fell asleep. Agatha’s ring could be felt against the skin of Rio’s hip and Rio’s fingers were tangled loosely in Agatha’s hair.

By the time morning came they were no farther apart. Rio was woken by a soft pair of lips against her ear and a sleep-warmed hand that skimmed over her lower back.

“Buen día, mi amor.”

Rio hummed her response, tangling her legs more securely with Agatha’s.

“¿Cómo dormiste?” How did you sleep?

Rio hummed again and she felt Agatha smile against her cheek.

“¿El gato te comió la lengua?” Cat got your tongue?

“Mm’sleeping. Is warm. Cosy. Shh.”

“Wake up.” Rio huffed and Agatha moved down to kiss her lips, smiling where Rio began to pout. “If you wake up now we can make out in the bathroom until Nicky wakes up.”

That made Rio open her eyes.

That made her sit up and immediately feel wide awake.

Only Rio hadn’t been careful. Her rustling in the sheets had made Nicky rouse and as she was scrambling to her feet she heard: “What time is it?”

The wind was blown out of her sails as Agatha wrapped a consolatory had around her ankle.

“Morning, honey. Rio was just getting up to start breakfast.”

“She was?” Rio, grumpily.

“Sí.”

Rio huffed and looked down to see Agatha smiling up at her and fluttering her lashes in such a way that she couldn’t refuse her.

“Coming right up.”

She received a kiss to her thigh for her agreement and couldn’t keep up her frown any longer as she slipped from the fort to go and do as she’d promised.

It didn’t take long for her to have company in the kitchen. Agatha arrived first, her arms around Rio and her face in against her neck. It was brief, but precious in its brevity.

Nicky arrived soon arrived, much louder and bouncier than Agatha. He, too, gave Rio a hug and then made eyes at her so she’d lift him onto the counter where he could more easily help with the whisking of the eggs.

Agatha cleared her throat at this move but said nothing about it.

With the radio on, the eggs miraculously not burnt, Nicky helping where he could, and her ring on Agatha’s finger, it all felt surprisingly normal. Not heavy. Not devastating. Not difficult.

Normal.

They ate like a normal family might. Rio ate fastest. Nicky next. Agatha ate slowest and most delicately.

Rio kept stealing egg from her plate.

Normal.

And then the door went.

And Jen arrived.

And nothing was normal after that.

Rio received a kiss to the temple, and Nicky did too. But then Agatha was whisked away. She was told to shower and change. She was followed upstairs by her manager.

And Rio and Nicky were left alone.

“Okay, mellizo,” Rio said with as much enthusiasm as she could muster. “Dishes, then change, then basketball?”

It took about an hour for Nicky to relax again. He was worried about Agatha being constantly taken away, just like Rio was. But soon he was yelling and laughing and they were making their way ever closer to those infinity points.

But Agatha still hadn’t reappeared even when Rio went inside to fetch snacks and water. She only didn’t go and seek her out because she had a little duckling to take care of.

So she went back outside to Nicky and left Agatha with Jen, hidden away somewhere in the bowels of the house.

Nicky was standing alone in the small space dubbed “la cancha” the court by Rio in her attempt to get Nicky riled up ahead of their game.

He was bouncing the ball, his head down, and in his stance Rio saw a sadness that had not been there before. She approached him slowly, touched his shoulder to break the spell.

“¡Vamos! Let’s eat.”

The ball bounced alone as Nicky hurried after Rio and settled by her side against the house. They shared snacks in silence for a while. Rio had chosen food that wasn’t as unhealthy as she’d like but definitely more unhealthy than Agatha would have liked.

Still, she finished her chips and then stuffed a handful of trail mix into her mouth.

They ate in companionable quiet for a while, Rio silently taking the raisins Nicky picked out of his food and handed over to her.

In the calm of the morning Rio was thinking of the words that had made her heart fall clean out of her chest yesterday.

“Nicky had a panic attack on the teacups.”

She took a breath, watched as another two raisins were placed into her open palm.

“Did you want to talk about what happened on the teacups yesterday? Your mama said you got upset.”

Nicky looked down at the ground and kicked a stone. Rio watched it bounce across the court and finally land in Agatha’s flower beds. She looked at the purple azaleas and began to count the leaves.

“I don’t like it when people keep looking at us.”

Rio nodded. Understandable. Totally. But also not ideal when your mom was the most famous woman in the world.

She let them sit in it for a little, let her eyes drift back down to look at Nicky’s hands now twisting in his lap.

“You know, sometimes I get scared too. Like a tightness in my chest. Like I can’t breathe.”

Nicky looked up then and Rio kept her eyes down.

“How do you stop it?”

A valid question, Rio thought. A very, big, very complicated, but very valid question. She hummed, matching the rhythm of the garden around them. Across the way there was a bee joining in the chorus.

“Well, I think about things I can see, things I can hear, things I can touch. So now, if I were feeling scared, I’d think about that bee over there.” She pointed. “I’d think about the smell of the flowers. I’d hold your hand.” She held her hand out. Nicky took it.

“See? Better already.”

Nicky nodded slowly but was worrying his lip now, staring down at the place their hands met.

“Can you come? Next time? I know mama would like it. I don’t think she was happy yesterday either.”

“Mellizo,” Rio began, already feeling the tightening around her fingers.

“Maybe we can do it in pretend. If that helps. I don’t mind. I won’t get upset. I just want you to be there.”

“Mellizo…”

Rio shifted then, angling her body more towards Nicky. She wanted to pull him into her arms and keep him there until Agatha joined and then hold them both like that until the divorce was final and they could be a family. For real. Not in pretend.

“Did you know I’ve known your mom for a long, long time?”

“You have?”

“Yeah. When I was much younger I saw her in a movie and thought, wow! She is the most beautiful, talented, woman I’ve ever seen.”

Nicky nodded, because of course she was.

“And then I met you and I thought-…”

“I was the best,” Nicky finished for her, and in a blink of an eye he was Agatha’s son, his lips twitching the way hers did when she wasn’t being subtle.

“The best,” Rio emphasised. “Which is why I will never play pretend with either of you. But sometimes I’ll have to be away. I’ll always come back, though. You know that, right?”

Nicky nodded, his little smirk fading to a frown again. He pulled his hand away and held his watch instead.

He pressed a button to make the face light up and Rio looked down to it. Agatha had been in her office for over two hours.

“I have a surprise for you for your birthday.”

“Oh?”

“Mama said not to tell you what it is.”

Rio raised her brows and dropped her head back against the wall. “Will I like it?”

“I hope so. I think it’s very cool.”

“Then I’m sure I’ll love it.”

Nicky lifted his head and shot Rio a smile that made her chest feel hollow suddenly. He looked shy, unsure still, and she held up her hand again to offer it to him. He took it and his smile relaxed until he looked more sure.

“Have you thought any more about marrying my mama?”

“Oh, mellizo. We’re just friends.”

“You could be married friends.”

Rio smiled at this, catching Nicky’s eye. “Tell you what, I will promise to never marry anyone else and be your mama’s best friend forever.”

Nicky’s gaze was unwavering and Rio wondered for the briefest of moments if he knew of the discussion that had occurred late last night whilst he was asleep.

“I think it’s worse. Without daddy, I mean.”

The raisins fell to the floor.

Rio shifted where she sat.

“What do you mean?”

Nicky began to pick up the raisins and place them one by one back into Rio’s hand.

“The people. The people are worse. Someone grabbed at mama and the big man with the frown pushed him away but-…”

Nicky’s fingers froze where they were placing another raisin in Rio’s palm.

“Did he send them? Daddy? Did he send my grandmother and that lady in the park? The men at Disney?”

Rio pulled her hand away and tipped Nicky’s raisins onto the ground, they’d be eaten by ants now. Or the birds fluttering about the bushes.

The natural cycle of things.

Rio turned around to the little boy who was now looking at her, his eyes so like hers and so full of fear.

“Listen to me, okay?” Rio took both of Nicky’s hands in her own. “People are more interested in your mama now because people are surprised that she and your dad aren’t together anymore.”

“Why?”

“Well,” Rio cleared her throat and thought it over for a second, “sometimes things aren’t as they seem.”

“They’re pretend?”

“Yes, baby.”

Nicky nodded and Rio looked down at their hands.

“Mama says we’re safe. Are you safe?”

“Yes, baby.”

“You have scars now.”

Rio cleared her throat and turned her arm so the scars showed. Nicky immediately reached for them and Rio briefly bit down on her cheek.

“Do you have a body guard too?”

“No.”

“Can you get one? Just in case.”

“Okay, if it makes you feel better, I will.”

Rio bit the inside of her cheek again and Nicky smiled a little.

They were both silent for a while. Rio was lost in her own world and Nicky was in his own too. He dropped his gaze once more to Rio’s scars and said: “Auntie Jen said she’d like to marry Alice.”

“Oh? She did?”

“I asked her.”

Nicky went back to his trail mix and Rio watched as he began fishing out more raisins whilst ignoring the chocolate and nuts.

“So if she married Alice then Alice will be my auntie too.”

“I’m sure she’d love that.”

Agatha looked around and didn’t even have to say anything for Rio to correct herself.

Rio kissed Agatha and for a few seconds the nightmare that threatened them every waking minute disappeared and became, instead, the shared dream of two lovers entangled with one another.

She slid her hand around to her lower back and Agatha arched beneath her.

Rio hummed as Agatha leant up to kiss her. The balance tipped then, Agatha pushing her back until she was in her lap, her left hand holding her jaw. Agatha was smiling, her grin wide and unashamed as she held Rio still.

Rio grinned and Agatha slid her hand up her face. Against her warm cheek she felt the cool promise forged in gold.

No star in the sky could match the twinkle in Agatha’s gaze then. Rio’s hands moved to her thighs and she scratched them affectionately, needing to touch, to move, to do something more with her body.

“Monday night,” Agatha whispered. “I’ll ask Jen to take Nicky. You’re not working so come over. Wait for me. We can have a night of just us. Just everything.”

Rio nodded and had to bite down, hard, on her lip to make sure she didn’t grin like an idiot.

“I wish you’d told me.”

That made her grin falter. That made her stomach flip.

She sighed and pulled back a little. In Agatha’s eyes she saw only concern, only the troubles that came from knowing someone was keeping something for you.

“I meant to. I, I mean I didn’t at first. I said no at first and then… I just couldn’t find the right time.”

Agatha nodded and Rio moved her hand to rest it across her chest. She wanted to feel her heartbeat there, wanted to experience the pulse that kept Agatha alive, the rhythm that kept her loving her.

“I’ll do better. I’ll not keep things from you.”

“Things like surprise parties?”

Rio looked up then, her brows shooting up with her gaze.

“Your mom text me. I think she was feeling guilty about telling you.”

Rio wrapped her arms back around Agatha then, unsure where to go with this. So she quietly asked: “Cowboys?”

Agatha leant in and laughed against Rio’s mouth and just as Rio made to kiss her again she found her lap suddenly empty. Agatha had moved off, still laughing, and settled back against the wall.

Ever reliable, Rio hurried to get back close and settled down next to Agatha amongst the sacrificed raisins.

A pale hand hit her thigh before another word could be spoken.

She looked down at it and smiled for the ring now proudly worn.

“We should talk,” Rio said gently, her eyes still on the ring that contained her promise.

“We should,” Agatha agreed, leaning a little more into Rio’s side. “Let’s just be silent for a while. Just breathe, okay?”

Rio nodded and her fingers slipped into the gaps left by Agatha’s. She held on to her hand as the chorus of bees swelled, the leaves rustled, and nature herself sang for the joy of two hearts safely settled in their shared rhythm.
