Fragile as the sun’s rays she’d gone from Rio’s grasp.

Rio watched her go.

Despite not getting what she wanted, despite not hearing Agatha moan her name, despite not having her make a mess over her hard-won abs, she smiled. Because Agatha was gone, Agatha had denied her, but she’d also wanted her, she’d also promised she could have her.

She did have her.

It would always be like this.

Rio hurried after her, sprinting until she could collide with her back and force a bark of laughter from her girlfriend so loud it made Nicky and Jen come running. Rio didn’t notice their audience as she tortured a squirming Oscar-winner in her clutches, trying to get her to turn to her, to share in her grin.

But she did hear the “ahem!” that Jen released just as Rio’s mouth was getting dangerously close to Agatha’s neck.

Rio looked up. Agatha continued to laugh but stopped her squirming.

Tickling hands became gentler as Rio soon blushed and held Agatha against her, now fully turned to her, her arms loosely around her neck as she panted and released soft giggles.

Rio released the final note of their shared symphony as she kissed Agatha’s flushed cheek before she looked back at a grinning Nicky and a scowling Jen.

Rio grinned right back and found Agatha pressing her hips into her, even as she leant back, even as her hand moved to bury her fingers in Rio’s hair.

“I was just excited about my party.” Rio said by way of explanation, as Agatha hummed happily, her laughter dying down now.

Jen frowned her disapproval as Nicky, beside her still, started on the spot and looked suddenly shocked. It made Rio’s grin widen because he looked exactly like her, only smaller, only with slightly messier hair.

“It’s okay,” Agatha reassured as she removed her hold on Rio and tapped her hands to get her to release her. “Rio’s mom told her about it.”

Rio reluctantly did as she was silently told and let Agatha go. It turned out the release meant that Rio’s hand was taken instead, which was a good consolation prize if nothing else.

“Maybe,” Nicky said tentatively, now moving closer and toying with the hem of his shirt, fidgeting like Rio. “Maybe we can still all jump out and yell ‘Surprise’!” He held his hands up a little after he’d yelled the surprise and Rio had to bite her tongue because she didn’t want to laugh at him.

“We’re having it at Rio’s house, honey. She’ll already be there.”

Rio tugged at Agatha’s hand and Agatha turned to her and moved a little closer as Jen cleared her throat.

“You can still yell. I mean, if you want to. Maybe you could aim your pistols at the sky.” Rio pointed at the sky with her newly acquired finger guns and as Agatha rolled her eyes, Nicky giggled, and Jen cleared her throat again, she shouted, “pew pew!”

“So juvenile,” Agatha muttered, making Rio pull her in sharply so she collided with her side and she could tug Agatha’s arm around her back and drape her own across her shoulders. She turned to Nicky as Agatha protested and struggled where Rio pulled her head against her chest.

“Well, partner, this here lady is causin’ an awful ruckus about these parts. What say you and I-…”

“Enough!”

Rio stopped and loosened her hold so a struggling Agatha could rip herself away. Where she’d been smiling and playing along, albeit reluctantly, before she now looked ashen as she stared across at a panicked looking Jen.

Nicky shuffled and then hurried over to stand before his mom and the tres patitos all stood huddled together and gazing with various degrees of confusion across at Jen.

“Pew pew,” Rio said quietly, attempting to lighten the sudden dark mood that had descended.

Agatha, the least confused, cleared her throat and said: “Jennifer. Enough of that.”

Something shifted again as Rio watched Jen work her jaw and she slid her hand down from Agatha’s shoulders to hold her hip, giving her a reassuring squeeze as Jen grit out: “You’re playing with fire.”

Nicky moved before them and Rio could feel the tension in Agatha. It sparked something in her that she couldn’t contain. And like a coiled spring she flew towards Jen, blocking her from looking at the other two.

“You reacting like this is not helping. We’re just having fun.”

She kept her voice low, did her best to keep it firm. Jen met her gaze, and Rio saw her process in real time. She felt a hand find hers but before she could even register enough to hold it, Jen had responded.

“You need to be careful. I know it’s hard. But it’s necessary.”

Rio looked down as the hand in her own tugged at her and she looked to see Nicky looking up at her with a frown.

“Don’t fight,” he whispered, his other hand moving to cover the scars on Rio’s arm.

She felt Agatha come up behind her and an arm snake around her middle. She looked back up to Jen and saw that she didn’t look pissed anymore. She looked tired.

“Rio’s staying tonight,” Agatha said, close to Rio’s ear. Nicky gasped quietly beside her and Rio squeezed his hand. But she kept her eyes on Jen, watching her complicated relationship with Agatha, with Agatha’s queerness, with her decision to be with Rio, play out across her face. “Why don’t you invite Alice over? We can be cinco patitos.”

The offer took Rio by surprise but the fingers that dug into her side suddenly really didn’t. Rio gasped and lurched and burst out a bark of laughter that made Nicky jump back in surprise and Jen roll her eyes at.

Agatha’s attack had been purposeful. It was sneaky, masterful, devastating.

She’d taken the presumed script of what would have been a heady, intense argument and she’d manipulated it around to instead be shouts of surprise and delight. She’d made Rio the willing victim instead of the unwilling Jen.

Rio only benefitted because she had Agatha’s hands all over her, her front pressed against her back. Her fingers digging into the places only Agatha knew she was most sensitive.

The attack ended the moment Jen left the room, and Rio was left gasping as she bent double and Agatha held her around her middle. Nicky was giggling too as he tapped her arm and tried to help her straighten.

“Melliza! Melliza! B-breath, melliza!”

Rio straightened slowly and felt Agatha held her for a few seconds longer, pressing into the back of her shoulder with her whole face. Rio knew then that Agatha’s attack had been defensive, rather than offensive. She’d protected everyone in the situation, even calming Nicky down, simply by forcing laughter, rather than encouraging shouts.

Agatha kissed her where she pressed in and then stepped away. Glancing up, Rio watched her following Jen’s route out and she was left alone with Nicky who was still grinning and tugging at her arm.

“Are you okay? Can we go play again? When you can breathe?”

Rio smiled at Nicky but looked up to where Agatha had left them and pined for a second longer before she became who Nicky needed her to be and they went back outside to play.

They were not that much closer to infinity when Alice arrived on the scene and under the pretence of stealing the ball from Rio she muttered: “Want to wrap up here soon and go save them from each other?”

That was all Rio needed to hear.

Her heart was no longer in the race to infinity but she faked it for as long as she could.

“Okay!” She announced after celebrating another point with Nicky charging about the small space. “How about we take a break for a while? We can get some food and I’ll go check on your mom?”

“Actually,” Alice said, more to Rio than to Nicky who’d run off now to fetch the ball. “Jen’s called for the nanny to come.”

“She has? Oof.” Nicky had collided with her side now he had the ball under his arm. Rio’s hand flew to his hair.

“Val’s coming?” Nicky asked curiously, blinking up at Alice. “Why? Is mama going somewhere?” He held Rio’s shirt a little tighter. “Are you going somewhere, melliza?”

“No, sweetheart. I think,” she glanced at Alice, “I think we’ll just be busy working so, so your nanny can keep you company.”

Nicky was silent for a few seconds until he nodded and said: “Okay.”

“You like her, right?”

“Yeah, she’s… she’s nice. More fun than Lucy was.”

Rio nodded and Alice smiled at him, tilting her head in a way that suggested to Rio that she was studying his face again. Rio rolled her eyes and was quick to usher Nicky inside so he’d not be freaked out again about her friend’s staring.

Nicky ran through to wash his hands and Rio slumped into the couch with Alice beside her as they waited for the new nanny to arrive.

“How bad is it?”

“Not too bad. It’s just a bad time. So even small things feel like big things.”

Rio scoffed, “That’s what she said.”

“Pervert.”

“You have no idea. This morning I could barely get past second base.”

“What is second base?” Alice asked, a genuine curiosity in her voice as Rio huffed and shrugged.

“Boob stuff?”

“Isn’t it fingering?”

“Well if it is I didn’t even get past first.”

Alice rolled her eyes and threw a pillow in Rio’s direction, “I’m done with this conversation now.”

Rio smirked and looked up as Nicky ran back in, now holding a book under his arm as he ran to dive into the nearby armchair.

“Dinosaurs, mellizo?”

Nicky held his book up and Rio saw that it was indeed dinosaurs, “Val said I could teach her all about them.”

Rio grinned, “She’s so lucky.”

“So lucky,” Nicky agreed readily, nodding as he opened his big book and began flicking through to the place he’d left off.

Rio watched him read in silence, and could feel Alice beside her doing the same. Alice’s watching of the little boy was more focused on seeing exactly what made him look so like Rio: the answer being his whole face.

But Rio was watching him for different reasons. She was watching him because instead of reminding her of herself, he reminded her of Agatha.

Nicky was reading silently, mouthing the words as he went. He used his index finger to keep him steady on the page and his brow furrowed as he concentrated. He was Agatha like this; studious, determined, serious.

Just as precious, just as perfect.

After five minutes of Nicky focused on the past and Rio focused on the future - tiny babies with sea blue eyes - the front door opening made Rio turn from him and she looked expectantly at the entrance to the den and soon saw the person who’d entered the house.

Her jaw dropped.

The nanny, it turned out, was not what she’d been expecting.

Rio stood as if on autopilot and stared at the woman now smiling and striding towards her.

One of the most beautiful women Rio had ever seen had just entered Agatha’s house. She was mid-thirties, with long braided hair down her back, high cheekbones, and a confident smile that let Rio know she knew how fucking hot she was.

Rio hated her.

“You must be Val,” Alice said from somewhere beside Rio, her hand already held out to accept the stranger’s shake.

As the woman reached for Alice, Rio noticed something else that made her stomach flip. She was in a sleeveless top and had strong, toned arms that made Rio want to die.

“It’s a pleasure to meet you. You’re Alice?”

Rio stared at the ripple of muscle beneath her smooth skin and flexed her own as a response to the visual affront of Nicky now having a hot, strong nanny. She clenched her jaw and had to look away for fear she’d be caught staring.

A second later Val turned to Rio and held her hand out. Rio wished she could ignore it but she’d been raised better than that.

“And you must be Rio. I’ve heard so much about you from your mellizo here.”

Rio’s face felt tight. Was she grimacing? She felt like she was grimacing.

She shook the woman’s hand.

“Val,” she said, taking the opportunity where Rio remained silent. “Short for Valkyrie. My parents had a thing for Norse mythology. My mum’s a professor of it back in England. You should hear my brother’s name.”

She winked and something about it fired up Rio’s engines.

“Odin?”

Val laughed, it was light and breezy and my god she was gorgeous. Rio’s engines sputtered and she felt the tightness again.

“Thankfully, no. Thor. Which isn’t much better, really. He mostly tells people his name is Tom.”

This made Rio laugh. Which annoyed her.

Gorgeous and funny wasn’t fair.

She cleared her throat after purposefully cutting her laughter short and turned to see Alice hanging by the door in wait.

“I should leave you two to it.”

“You’re staying though?”

Rio looked back at Nicky and her smile was genuine and not tight this time. She marched over to where he sat on the couch with his book and ducked down to kiss his cheek.

“Of course. Your mama and I just need to talk about work for a while and then I’ll be back and we can play more ball, okay?”

Rio saw the beginnings of an Agatha pout appear on Nicky’s face and just as she was about to cut him off at the pass, Val spoke again: “Well, hey, why don’t we try to get close to infinity? Isn’t that what you guys are trying for?”

Rio exchanged a look with Nicky and saw his internal struggle between politeness and being his mother’s son. He’d been raised better too.

“No thank you,” he said slowly, keeping his gaze on Rio who smiled encouragingly. “Only mellizos can play to infinity.” He paused and then said: “And sometimes Alice.”

“Thanks, kid.”

Rio shot her friend a smile and then looked to Val. To her credit, she looked completely unfazed. But then, being a nanny to high profile kids, having a polite little boy gently turn her down was nothing on what she usually dealt with.

At least, Rio imagined her dealing with a kid like James and knew that she’d hit the jackpot with Nicky.

“Oh and I wouldn’t want to intrude on the mellizos.”

Val shot Rio a smile and Rio shot her another tight one back. But she ruffled Nicky’s hair, kissed his temple again and straightened to walk away.

“If you need anything,” she began as she walked towards where Val was. “But, I, uh…”

“Keep a little distance between us and you?” Val asked quietly, already guessing what Rio was about to suggest.

Rio nodded and Val touched her arm. “Don’t worry, not my first rodeo.”

Another flash of a smile and Rio turned from her. Her face fell the moment she knew neither the nanny nor Nicky could see it. This face was just for Alice.

And Alice knew exactly what it meant.

“You can’t be serious,” she muttered as Rio stalked past her, intent on getting to the bathroom down the hall.

She knew Alice was following her so she didn’t slam the door like she wanted to when she stepped inside.

“Rio Vidal, jealous? Never in my life did I ever think-…”

“Did you see her?! Alice did you see how beautiful she is?!”

She was whisper-shouting, doing her best not to be overheard even when she wanted to scream the house down.

Her body felt other. Her brain felt other. Her heart, her lungs, her jaw, other, other, other.

“Rio,” Alice tried in a tone so syrupy it made Rio clench her teeth.

Rio was stomping now in the small space. She would have thrown something if she had anything in her hands. But jealousy was new to her body and she didn’t know what to do or how to get rid of it.

“Don’t pretend. She is gorgeous. Like, gorgeous!”

“Sounds like you want to fuck her, not-…”

Rio growled, a great half-shout of noise and fury. But she contained herself just in time, just in time to continue.

“Of course Agatha will want to fuck her! It’s the law!”

Alice, more amused than anything else, now with her arms crossed as she leant back against the counter, scoffed.

“What law?”

Rio wheeled around then, a burning effigy of her usual self.

“The JUDE LAW!”

Alice blinked, processed, and then a great big guffaw burst out of her little body.

Rio seethed and began pacing again, taking two steps then having to turn about.

It was her only frame of reference. The tabloid fodder from the early noughties that led to the general consensus that every movie star cheats with the nanny. Especially the good looking ones.

Agatha was a movie star. Agatha was a hot movie star. Agatha could have anyone she wanted. Agatha could have the hot nanny with the nice arms and high cheekbones and stupid name in a second if she wanted.

“Rio,” Alice whispered, gathering herself enough to not let the laughter spill over. “Do you know how badly that woman wants to be with you?”

“Her arms are bigger than mine,” Rio huffed, feeling petulant now that she wasn’t being listened to. “And she winked which means she’s flirty. Plus she’s good with Nicky. And if the security company recommended her that means she can fight. Which is hot. Which means-…”

“Which means nothing because Agatha loves you. She’s wearing your fucking ring and I wouldn’t be surprised if she decides it’s never ever coming off.”

Rio scoffed but felt her body relax even as she still paced, still turning every two steps.

She felt a little dizzy.

“What if she’s better in bed than I am?”

Alice scoffed this time. “Look, I’ll say this once and then never again. I shared a wall with you for years. Now either you get girls to agree with you a lot or you’re just good in bed. Besides, it doesn’t even fucking matter because Agatha is literally turning her life upside down for you right now.”

Rio huffed and sank down onto the closed toilet seat.

She put her head in her hands and soon found Alice crouching before her.

“It’s cute that you’re capable of this.”

“Shut up.”

“Seriously, for years I thought you were some kind of sociopath monster who just-…”

“Shut up, Alice.”

Alice sighed and placed a hand on Rio’s knee.

“Seriously. Val’s hot. But you’re hotter.”

Rio rolled her eyes and looked up at Alice. She saw she was smirking so she dropped her head again.

“Come on! Where’s my asshole cocky best friend who thinks she’s the hottest piece of ass in the whole goddamn world?!”

“I don’t know. Gone somewhere with her tiny arms and her goofy smile.”

Alice was the one to roll her eyes this time and she slapped Rio’s hand away, making her head bob down suddenly.

“You’re just fishing for compliments now.”

“Not,” Rio huffed.

Alice sighed as she stood and Rio watched her with a scowl before she stood with her and went to check herself out in the mirror. She flexed and caught Alice rolling her eyes at her in the reflection.

“She’s not with you for your arms.”

“I’m sure they help.”

“Good point. It’s clearly not your personality.”

Rio wheeled round to slap at Alice but Alice had moved too quickly and was already halfway out the door.

“Take that back!”

Alice cackled as she walked away and Rio had no choice but to follow behind, internally seething still but with a little less actual panic swimming around in there.

But she felt on edge. A morning of being denied being able to give her girlfriend an orgasm and then seeing how hot the woman looking after Nicky was did not a happy Rio make.

Her body felt other still as they arrived at the office at the other end of the house. Without even knocking as they stepped inside. In a strange change turn of events it was Jen who sat behind the desk and Agatha who sat in the chair opposite.

But Rio said nothing, wondering if this were another calculated move on Agatha’s part, as Agatha looked up and smiled.

Seeing Agatha made her feel better.

But only slightly.

Still feeling less than, Rio lifted her hand up to scratch the back of her head, making sure to flex as best she could. She got the reaction she was hoping for. Blue eyes darted to the movement and Rio felt a flash of pride when she caught Agatha’s pale cheeks flushing ever so slightly.

Still got it, she thought.

She went to perch on the edge of the desk, crossing her arms over herself to push her bicep up so when Agatha looked her way she could see how hard she worked.

“Negotiating press,” Agatha clarified with Rio’s questioning raise of an eyebrow, her gaze dropping briefly to her arms.

“Not negotiating,” Jen clarified as Rio turned to look at her. “Agreeing.”

Agatha sighed, “They’ve moved it up. They are in breach of contract.”

“Technically, they’re not.”

“Well make them.”

“Can I see?”

Rio looked to her best friend and raised her brows as she moved around to Jen’s side and picked up what she assumed was a paper copy of Agatha’s contract.

Agatha huffed in her chair.

“I don’t have time for it.”

“You’ll have to make time.”

Agatha huffed again and Rio chewed on her lip. “What do they want?”

“Podcasts, late night, articles, the works.”

“Fucking vultures,” Jen muttered as behind Rio she riffled through some papers. Alice was leaning over her shoulder to get a view of whatever email chain she had up on her laptop.

But Rio kept her eyes on Agatha, watching as she worked her jaw and contemplated her next words.

She reminded her of Nicky as he’d been reading. Though Agatha wasn’t mouthing “diplodocus”. She was instead silently considering, obstinately waiting until she had the exact right word to say.

“I want it all done as quickly as possible, before Ralph responds. In the same day, if we can. I’m not spreading it out. The outlets and studios will have to deal with it. I want no mention of my divorce, of Ralph, of my mother, of Nicky. Then I’ll agree.”

Rio turned to check Jen’s response to this and saw her now looking to whatever was on her laptop screen. She looked serious, but there was a hesitance there too.

“Fine. I’ll see what-…”

“No, Jen. You’ll do it. That, or nothing at all.”

Rio was looking back at Agatha now, watching the muscle of her jaw flex continuously. And she knew why she’d let Jen sit at her desk. It was a power move. In this position, Agatha was giving Jen a false feeling of power.

But Agatha was pulling the strings, and Jen was her puppet.

The puppet master motioned with her hand and a different plaything responded. Rio moved from her position on the desk to perch on the arm of Agatha’s chair where she could lean back around her and Agatha could lay her arm across Rio’s thigh.

“Why does the week of the twenty seventh look familiar to me?”

Rio looked to Alice, briefly having been distracted by Agatha’s fingers tapping a soft pattern on her knee.

“Shit,” she breathed, her eyes going wide as she straightened and placed a hand on the back of Jen’s chair.

“They want you for SNL. I’ve been putting them off and haven’t given a straight answer yet.”

Rio shot up from where she’d been leaning across and almost fell from the chair.

“What.”

“Just with your dad and-…”

Rio stopped listening. There was instead a high-pitched ringing in her ears as the news sunk in. Saturday Night Live was always the dream. Beyond the Oscar. Beyond anything the industry could have offered her.

And yet.

“My love,” Agatha had moved forwards in the chair, the hand that was once on her knee was now on her thigh. “Rio, you have to do it.”

“I… what… I? Alice?”

Alice sighed and shook her head, “I totally forgot. I didn’t even think, I… shit. I forgot.”

“They want me?”

“Of course they do.” Agatha.

“I can tell them no.” Alice.

“I-… this month?”

“My love.”

“Rio, I’m so sorry. I dropped the ball on this.”

“Tell them yes,” Agatha said, now looking at Alice rather than Rio. “Tell them she’ll come. She’ll do it. She’ll be glad to.”

“End of the month is when,” Jen started but Agatha shot her a look that didn’t go unnoticed by either Rio or Alice. They looked at each other and both simultaneously realised what that look meant.

“It’s when Ralph will respond,” Rio concluded quietly, the ringing in her ears dying down now, becoming a dull ache in the back of her head.

“It doesn’t mean anything,” Agatha said as she turned back to Rio, a soft, desperate smile now across her features. “This means something. You have to do it.”

Rio couldn’t get a grasp on how she felt about this until her internal barometer pinged and she suddenly knew.

Oh.

Oh no.

It was why Alice looked so panicked, why she was apologising where she’d usually roll her eyes and correct her mistake. It’s why Agatha’s hand on her thigh was now reaching for her hip, why she was turning more to her.

Rio’s lips faltered around the word but unlike Nicky, unlike Agatha, she couldn’t find it.

So Alice did: “Miguel.”

Rio choked on her dad’s name even as it came from a mouth other than her own. Agatha was standing now, was dragging her to her feet and like a limp marionette Rio allowed it and let Agatha hold her around her middle, press into her cheek.

“Please don’t,” Rio uttered quietly, making Agatha slip away from her so she stood alone.

“Rio,” Alice whispered. Rio caught the regret evident in her friend’s voice. How could she miss it? She saw it in her face too. She felt Agatha’s in the fingers that grazed her wrist and in the absence of her body against her own.

“No,” she said softly, shaking her head as her dad’s distant laughter filled her ears.

No one said anything for a while but Agatha’s touch became steadily bolder until her fingers were wrapped around Rio’s forearm and her thumb was tracing up and down in a steady motion.

“I think that a little more laughter in the world is always a good thing.”

The last person Rio had thought would break the silence, had. Jennifer Kale was standing slowly from her chair and Rio watched her as she moved around until she stopped directly in front of Rio.

“He loved it?”

Her words were gentle, gentler than Rio had ever heard her speak before.

Rio nodded just once.

“You watched it together?”

Rio nodded again.

Jen seemed to be considering her, taking longer than she ever had to study her. So long, in fact, that Agatha moved closer in that time, and Rio reached for her as an apology for before. Agatha said nothing but pressed her nose in before Rio’s ear and snaked her arms around her.

Rio took in a deep breath.

“He’s a little young right now, but don’t you want your son to watch it with you too? See you up there? Doing what you do best?”

Rio’s heart constricted in her chest and Agatha’s hold on her tightened as she turned to look at her best friend.

Jen, for once, looked unashamedly earnest. She nodded encouragingly at Rio and Rio sucked in a shaking breath as her limp arms moved up to hold the arm that held her.

Agatha had turned back, had nudged her nose against her cheek, and Rio took it as permission to want something she could no longer share with her dad.

“Okay,” she breathed out, feeling the relief of the word as it floated around them. “Okay.”

She watched as Jen nodded, as she moved back around the desk after looking at Rio a second longer. She saw as she kissed Alice’s temple, as she took her seat back up, as she focused back on her laptop.

She watched as a tear rolled down her cheek and as she wiped it away.

“I’ll make the call,” Alice said quietly as Agatha pressed soft kisses to Rio’s face now, moving to stand more in front of her as Rio’s eyes closed and her heart returned to its usual pace.

“We’ll be fine. You need to do this,” was all Agatha said. Rio just nodded again, heard the door to the office open and close with Alice, and then found herself being tugged into the tight confines of a chair built for one now shared with two.

Alice returned after half an hour, looking less sheepish than before.

She came to whisper the news in Rio’s ear that they’d still have her, that they wanted her, that Rio could fly back whenever she wanted and they’d make it work. She kissed Rio's cheek in an unnecessary apology and Rio was able to smile at her friend and tell her it was okay, that she was grateful to her for managing all this.

Rio was wrapped up in Agatha who was still negotiating with Jen about Heartburn promotion but her mind was back in Delaware, somewhere with Miguel’s laughter and more cowbell.

Alice and Rio were very much spare parts to the discussion in the little office that day.

They were surplus to requirements but required all the same.

Rio, for her steadfast hold on Agatha in the too-small chair, and the soothing way she played with her hair whenever Jen said something particularly unsoothing.

Alice, for her small offerings of wisdom that she could provide on the complex negotiations of an actress with her press duties. Rio couldn’t help but notice whenever Jen got particularly sparky, Alice touched her shoulder or her arm or her face and the sparks almost always instantly fizzled out.

She was pleased Alice had found a love like her own.

When conversations were done, when emails had been sent, and phonecalls made, the tide turned to more exhausting matters: matters of Ralph and Evanora.

Surplus, again, Rio and Alice remained mostly silent through this, with Alice nipping out to get refreshments for the heated discussions continuing in the little office.

Rio’s brain was stuck on her dad for the most part, occasionally on losing Agatha to a hot nanny, but as the discussions got more intense she was soon dragged back to the present, to the reality that was Agatha’s divorce.

“The studio did it to make the most of the situation,” Jen said, huffing as she typed away at her keyboard.

“A show about divorce? Of course they did.” Alice, having dragged a chair around to perch next to Jen.

“Seems like something my mother would have tried to encourage to humiliate me.”

“Won’t be humiliating when you win the Emmy for it.”

Agatha smiled as Rio kissed her cheek.

“Was thinking a Golden Globe too, but thank you.”

Rio hummed and smiled as she continued to toy with Agatha’s hair.

“We’ve moved on from this. We need to talk about visitation.”

Agatha’s small smile faded and Rio’s did too.

“I’ve told you-...”

“Yes, but the lawyers say-...”

“I don’t care what they say,” Agatha snapped before Jen could finish.

Even Rio’s gentle touches couldn’t relax Agatha this time. Rio cleared her throat and asked: “What do the lawyers say?”

“Reasonable visitation,” Jen uttered, Alice’s hand on her forearm, “They say so long as it’s safe, Nicky should keep a relationship with both Agatha and Ralph.”

“The only issue being,” Agatha jumped in again, “he doesn’t have one with Ralph.”

“I don’t want him to see the kid either-...”

“Then stop bringing it up.”

“You know it’ll happen. You know he’ll rock up, he’ll demand to see him. Now, we can get the judge to arrange a schedule or we can make it supervised-...”

Agatha scoffed and Rio turned to look at her tense profile, “Absolutely not. No one is supervising me with my-...”

“Supervise Ralph.”

“And where will I be in this arrangement? I’m not leaving them alone together. Not after that fucking woman-...”

“The woman,” Alice, “did you ever find out who she was?”

Jen and Agatha exchanged looks and Agatha looked away, turning more into Rio. Having barely moved for the past couple hours, Rio was now unreasonably uncomfortable. She peeled away and perched on the arm of the chair.

Agatha immediately took her hand and thread their fingers together as Rio rolled her shoulders back, unconsciously sitting taller as Jen responded.

“No. Not, not really. Current theories are a PI or just some hack trying to pull up dirt on Agatha, or Rio.”

Alice glanced Rio’s way.

“So, not a kidnapper?”
