They didn’t let go even when cameras called cut and Rio found that far from her being the one to fidget or toy with Agatha’s fingers, Agatha was the one toying with hers.

“Chinchillas are weird, you know.”

Rio smiled, knowing their mics were live.

“I think they’re pretty cute.”

“Yeah? Cute enough to… kiss?”

Rio bit the inside of her cheek, wondering just how much of this conversation anyone was paying attention to. She looked over to video village. Headsets were on but no one was looking their way.

“Maybe… cuddle a little.”

Agatha’s hand twitched violently as if it were about to rip away from her own but Rio had anticipated it and held on firmly.

“But I have something even cuter to cuddle, so I’m not much interested in chinchillas at all, actually.”

Agatha huffed, her cheeks a soft pink and her jaw tight.

“In fact,” Rio added, moving from her green mark and closer to Agatha’s purple one. “More of a koala fan.”

Agatha looked up and Rio grinned at her, now the fidgeter rather than the fidgetee.

“Wish I had a koala in my arms right now, in fact.”

Agatha’s eyes darting off to the side told her everything she needed to know: people were looking now. She didn’t much care, though.

She cleared her throat and said: “I’d call her my bamboo.”

Agatha snorted, “Now who’s the nerd?”

Rio shrugged and looked down at their hands, enjoying the way Agatha’s left hand now looked strange wearing her character’s rings because she was so used to seeing her wear her real ring.

“How’s that Stanislavsky technique coming along?” Rio asked after a little while of silence and of being poked and prodded by Makeup.

“Needing any refreshers soon?”

“I think that maybe we have thirty minutes around lunch to review notes.”

Rio looked up as someone was fluffing the back of her hair and grinned as Agatha turned her head towards the woman now lining her lips.

The look in her eye was all she needed to know.

And their lunchtime fuck was all Rio needed to get through the rest of the day.

They’d had to go quickly where Rio would have preferred to take her time. But it meant they both got off twice (with Agatha getting a bonus orgasm to ensure she knew Rio’s preference for koalas over chinchillas).

But there was no avoiding her session with the grief counsellor later.

Alice had been right about one thing. Rio would never be lucky enough to have filming overrun so she could miss her afternoon appointment.

So, right before Rio was about to slip into her little rental to make her way to see her new doctor, she heard her name being called across the parking lot.

Agatha Harkness, in costume as Kate, was running towards her with a stressed looking assistant jogging along behind her.

The sight was arresting.

“I forgot!”

Rio raised her brows as Agatha skidded to a halt and, breathless, she thrust something small into her hand.

A crumpled ball of white nothing.

It took less than a second for Rio to understand everything about this nothing.

“We really need to practice your technique.”

“It’s the best I could do. Just… it’s something to hold on to during your session.”

“She’ll have me sectioned if she sees me holding a ball of paper.”

“A flower,” Agatha insisted, nudging Rio’s hand to curl around the poor excuse for a rose. “Be grateful.”

Glancing at the assistant now caught up with them, Rio knew she couldn’t show her gratitude in the way she wanted. Instead she smiled, she nodded, she gave Agatha a quick, professional, friendly hug.

“Thank you.”

A quick squeeze would have to do. Only, as Agatha had pulled away, she’d kissed her in a slightly less professional place. It had been just below her ear, by the corner of her jaw. A small intimacy that would be cherished as much as the attempted rose now in Rio’s lap as she drove off to her session.

Alice was already waiting for her when she arrived at the modest offices of Dr. Christine Palmer.

But Rio knew that of all the people in the world, Alice wouldn’t require an explanation as to why she was incessantly spinning a ball of paper in her hand.

Alice’s presence was reassuring, though she’d initially not wanted it. And she held her hand as she waited. She held it so tightly, in fact, that when she released it as the doctor came to welcome her into her office, Alice flexed her fingers like they had been bruised.

Doctor Christine, as Rio, Alice, and apparently Agatha, had already determined, was beautiful. She had a smile that reached her eyes, though Rio knew how many times she must have given it today.

She seemed at ease and able to put at ease and Rio had no real interest in her beauty though she appreciated it all the same.

If she were going to have to suffer through this she supposed it was nice to have something pretty to look at.

“Is it okay if I call you Rio?”

“Of course.”

“Some people prefer this to be more formal,” the doctor explained as she motioned for Rio to take a seat on the green velvet couch. “But I think first names are a good place to start. Please, call me Christine.”

Rio smiled a little, enough to be polite, and took a seat.

“So,” the doctor, Christine, started. “Why are you here today, Rio?”

“Well,” Rio cleared her throat, crossing one leg over the other as she did, “I was getting these headaches and-…”

“No, I mean, why are you here, Rio? You can share as much or as little as you would like.”

Rio was holding her makeshift flower between her thumb and forefinger, spinning it with her middle. She watched as Christine’s eyes flicked to it and caught a slight tension in her lips before her face softened again and her easy smile was back.

“My dad,” Rio said quietly. “Miguel. He died. My dad died.”

Her flower stopped spinning. She moved her finger back the way to start it again and dislodged it.

Christine picked it up where it had fallen to the floor. She looked at it before she held it out and said: “When I’m nervous I play with a pen lid.”

Rio reached to take it back and cradled it in her hand, touching the sharp edges that were meant to be the petals.

“It’s a flower,” she explained, glancing at the softly-smiling doctor. “My g-… A friend made it for me.”

“Very sweet,” Christine commented gently. “Is this the same friend who was concerned about your headaches?”

“Yes.”

The doctor nodded and Rio enclosed her fingers around Agatha’s flower.

“It seems to me, Rio, that you have people who care about you. Who is the woman who came with you today?”

“Alice. My best friend.”

Christine nodded, her smile twitching at the corners of her lips. They were both silent for a while, Rio thinking of things that wouldn’t make her cry: the latest scores, how she had no idea what scene she was to be shooting tomorrow morning. And Christine, surveying the quiet movie star before her.

“I’m sorry for your loss. Losing a parent is never easy, no matter your age, or how expected it was.”

Rio dropped her gaze to her hands, and adjusted herself where she sat.

“Whilst you’re here, for the fifty or so minutes we’re together, I want you to know this is a safe space. You can feel free to say as much or as little to me as you’d like. Grief is different for everybody but it doesn’t have to be carried alone.”

“I have people,” Rio responded a little more defensively than she meant to. “I have…” she trailed off, her fingers working to spin the flower again.

Christine let her sit in it for a little while, and Rio wondered if she was waiting for her to finish her sentence.

“Will you tell me about your dad? What kind of man was he?”

Rio took a deep breath. She held it in her lungs. She held it until it burned and then she had to release it in a great gasp.

It was then the tears came; thicker and fuller than she had anticipated.

Doctor Christine remained calm and quiet as she handed Rio tissues and let her calm herself.

Within five minutes she was able to talk. Within ten she was barely pausing for breath. Within twenty she was laughing as she cried.

By the time the session was over, Rio’s eyes were red, and Agatha’s flower even less floral.

Rio felt a rawness she’d not felt since the day of her dad’s funeral. When she left the room and Alice took her hand again, she looked down and wondered why she wasn’t bleeding out into her best friend’s palm.

She sat in her car with Alice and cried into her chest until Alice convinced her to let her drive her home.

Alice put her to bed and Rio was ashamed to admit that she didn’t want Alice there at all.

But Alice knew that.

And an hour later, when the sky was dark and Rio was bone-tired, a hand that wasn’t Alice’s was against Rio’s arm.

“Honey.”

Rio blinked her eyes open and saw Agatha inches away from her face. Her blue eyes were troubled and it took Rio a while to understand why that might be.

“I’m just going to put Nicky to bed in the guest room and then I'll be back. Do you want anything?”

Rio shook her head and waited patiently until Agatha would be back.

Not five minutes later, a littler figure was leaning over her, and Rio blinked sleepily up at Nicky as he leant in to kiss her warm cheek.

“Buenas noches, melliza. I love you.”

Rio lifted up from her cocoon like a lion leaping for its prey and she consumed Nicky in her arms and blankets, making him giggle until her pain lessened at the sound.

She kissed his cheek repeatedly before whispering: “I love you too.”

Nicky giggled still until suddenly he didn’t, until suddenly be began to settle against her and in doing so hugged her back. It took Agatha’s gentle hands to guide him away and Rio caught a flash of a sad, tired smile before she was left alone again.

It wasn’t long before Agatha had returned. Rio hadn’t even needed to count in her head. But if she had, she wouldn’t have hit higher than a hundred.

Rio began to turn where she lay to accept Agatha into her arms but found herself forced back the way and Agatha to be spooning her instead.

“You need to be held,” she said simply, curling her body around Rio in a way that meant no questions were to be asked.

“See,” Rio whispered into the now dark room. “This is why I prefer koalas to chinchillas.”

Agatha released a scoff of hot air along the back of Rio’s neck and Rio smiled into the pillow, her fingers sliding into the gaps between Agatha’s.

“Alice is such a snitch.”

Agatha hummed, “I’m glad she is. I want to be here with you through this.”

“I’m fine.”

Rio tensed for Agatha to argue with her, for her to squeeze or even tickle her. But she did nothing. She said nothing. They remained silent for a long time until Rio eventually was able to find the words that had been stuck in her throat since her session with the doctor: “I miss him.”

“I know, my love.”

Agatha held on for the rest of the night and when Rio woke in the morning she found her hold to be just as tight as it had been when she’d fallen asleep. She suspected that Agatha would have barely slept for her desire to hold fast to her as she had a fitful night.

But Agatha never once complained in the morning. So Rio didn’t say anything and instead took great delight in being able to shower with her before she had to leave for work and Agatha had to take Nicky to school.

Everything was soft in the morning light. Rio suspected it was because Agatha barely took her hands off of her until the very second she had to leave.

But even as she drove to set for what she hoped would be a quick morning shoot before she picked up her mom and cousin, she felt somehow lighter. Maybe it was having Agatha there, or maybe it was that sharing her grief with a trained professional might have also helped.

Work that morning, miraculously, went smoothly. The only thing she really had to contend with was Billy being weird about so obviously trying to keep her surprise party a surprise.

Though it was amusing enough to watch him sweat whenever she brought up her birthday. And she was pleased, at least, that clearly Agatha hadn’t actually revoked his invitation.

But soon enough, she was at LAX pickup waiting impatiently for the two new arrivals into Hollywood.

Anna arrived with all the excitement a mother could possibly have upon seeing her only child and Mateo arrived with all the glee of a man about to attend a Hollywood party with the invite of an Oscar winner he knew to be secretly dating his favourite cousin.

“I just can’t fucking believe it!”

“Esa boca, por favor.” Language, please.

The journey home continued a lot like that: Mateo practically vibrating in the back of Rio’s little rental and Anna switching between rolling her eyes and chastising Mateo for his bad language or insistence that he be allowed to livestream the whole party.

But Rio, uninhibited with her family, shouted her joy back at her mom, back at her cousin, and the raucous little party continued as they arrived at Rio’s house.

The plan, insofar as Alice had managed to communicate to Rio that morning, was for Mateo and Anna to stay with Rio that night. Then, on Saturday, the night of the party, Anna would go home with Jen and Nicky.

Rio found this plan to be a little odd until Alice reassured her that Jen was more than happy to leave the party early and be Nicky’s guardian for the evening. Apparently a well-behaved eight year old boy was more tolerable to Jennifer Kale than a drunken bunch of Hollywood stars.

But that night, the night before Rio’s birthday, they were to be alone. Well, alone with Alice.

Agatha had arranged for them to have a table at Musso & Frank’s, a Hollywood stalwart that was tricky to get into. Especially on a Friday night.

Despite her reluctance to accept the fame she now had, Rio knew she’d be papped either outside, inside, or both. So she made sure to dress up a little for the occasion.

She wore a red blazer above a white t-shirt and a pair of ridiculously expensive leather pants she’d bought on a whim - encouraged by Alice - a couple years ago. Her lipstick matched, a choice by Mateo, who had infinite style, if not infinite wisdom.

She looked good, so she felt good, even as the prospect of her family being photographed and hounded because of her became more and more real the closer they got to the restaurant.

“Estamos bien, mija. Estaremos bien. Así que relájate, es tu noche. Agatha quería que fuese tu noche.” We are fine, my daughter. We will be okay. Relax. It is your night. Agatha wanted this to be your night.

Even her mother’s gentle reassurances and the familiar hand that held her own as she strode with her into the restaurant didn’t help the rush of adrenaline that coursed through her as the paps yelled her name and snapped their photo.

She grit her teeth until she was being greeted by the maître d’ and showed to their table where Alice was waiting. Her best friend’s easy smile and gentle laugh as she fell into her hug was enough to take her mind off of the barrage of photographers outside.

But Alice had something else up her sleeve to soothe, a gentle whisper of: “Agatha’s put security on the door. That big guy when you came in? Hers.”

Rio pulled away and had little chance to look, bewildered, at her best friend because her mom was pushing her out the way to get to her.

So she took her seat instead and glanced around to see if Agatha had filled the whole restaurant with people to protect her but saw nothing that immediately screamed “trained to kill” so relaxed back as Mateo took over from Anna in hugging Alice.

There wasn’t often a time where the Vidal family were quiet. Only, it seemed, when it came to food, or choosing wine.

The latter of which was left to Rio to do, who picked something that sounded posh and so to her mind was posh.

“¡Qué elegante!” This is so fancy! Anna whispered excitedly when the wine was poured and Rio shot Alice a wink over the waiter’s arm.

“Almost as if it wasn’t Rio’s choice and instead someone much fancier than her picked it,” Mateo teased from Rio’s left hand side.

“Watch it. I’m putting you up and can easily univite you from my party.”

“She’d never allow that,” Mateo muttered into his wine glass, convinced already that he was in Agatha’s good graces.

Rio just rolled her eyes and held her own glass aloft, “To dad, I wish he was here.”

“Yo también, mija,” Anna whispered as she chinked their glasses gently together. Beneath the table, Mateo reached for Rio’s hand and she turned to him to see his eyes filled with tears.

“C’mere,” she offered, squeezing his hand only to release it and open her arm to pull him into a sideways hug. “Can’t be crying on my birthday.”

“That’s tomorrow,” he reminded with a laugh.

Rio hummed and released her cousin with a quick kiss to his head.

“Besides,” Mateo said, sniffing softly and taking a quick sip of his wine, “All tears need to be shed tonight because I have a little boy to teach the ways of annoying my dear, dear cousin.”

“Ni se te ocurra enseñarle nada malo a ese dulce muchachito. Es un ángel,” You do not teach that sweet little boy anything bad. He is an angel.

Rio laughed as Alice did and Mateo rolled his eyes with a grin, “So he just looks like you then? None of your nature?”

“Very funny.”

“Actually,” Alice piped up, “My gift for Rio is a DNA kit. Just need to figure out how to convince Agatha to let me get some of Nicky’s-...”

“Alice!” Rio exclaimed as Mateo roared with laughter that, really, was entirely unnecessary.

“Just saying,” Alice shrugged, “He looks too like you for him not to be yours.”

Rio blushed furiously and glanced at her mom who looked almost as displeased as she was. Anna shifted in her seat and Rio watched her mind work it over until she said: “¿El divorcio? Agatha no para de decirme que todo está bien. ¿Es verdad?”, The divorce? Agatha keeps telling me it is all okay. Is that true?

All laughter around the little table died, first from Mateo’s face, next from Alice’s, and finally, and most impactfully, from Rio’s.

“Mamá, sabes que no ha sido fácil. Ella simplemente…” Mom, you know it’s not been easy. She’s just…

She’d trailed off because “doing her best” didn’t sound like nearly enough. Agatha was doing everything. And Rio didn’t have the words for it. Not in English, and definitely not in Spanish.

Anna only nodded and Rio felt her cousin’s hand on her shoulder. She realised then, with Agatha fresh on her mind, exactly what Agatha didn’t have.

Rio had grown up a lucky child of a lucky couple because each of them, together and alone, had support from each other, and from their wider, wild, crazy, family.

If Rio were in trouble she could call her aunt. If she needed someone to smoke a joint with in the park she could call Mateo. If she needed someone to hold her hand through a death, a breakup, a divorce, she had multiple hands to choose from.

Agatha had hers. She had Jen’s. And Nicky wasn’t yet old enough to offer his own.

Rio swallowed the realisation with her wine and, the born raconteur that she was, just like Miguel, she turned the conversation to sunnier climes.

Before long, the table was the loudest and most envied of them all. Rio and Mateo, born to be twins but forced to be cousins, bantered and bickered as Anna and Alice watched in amusement as the two picked on each other and laughed at their own, ridiculous jokes.

Mateo had been born the year after Rio, and upon meeting, they’d been inseparable since.

“I’m moving here,” Mateo announced as the check arrived and Rio grabbed it before anyone else could.

“Yeah, yeah, you say that-...” She stopped. She’d opened the leather check holder and found not the check she was expecting but instead a handwritten note that simply said: On me. I love you.

Rio had been staring for too long at what everyone thought was the check so naturally hands began to grab at it. Mateo, the closest, got there first. He ripped the little black book from Rio’s hands and, expecting to find an exorbitant price, instead let out a little gasp at the words scribbled there.

“Holy shit. Someone should write a novel about the two of you. Or you know what those people write on the internet, fanfictions! A movie, even! Play yourselves.”

Alice grabbed the book next and smiled when she saw Agatha’s note. “Holy shit,” she agreed, “She’s a romantic, who’d have thought.”

Anna, last of the table to see the surprise, looked up at her daughter with tears in her eyes when she’d read it.

“Un regalo de Dios.” A gift from God.

Rio laughed softly and shook her head, “She’s too good for me.”

“True,” Mateo said, earning a punch to the arm from Rio and a frown from Alice. But Anna was moving, making her way round to place her hands on Rio’s shoulders and to kiss her daughter’s face.

“¿Ella te hace feliz?” Does she make you happy?

“Claro, mamá.” Obviously, mom.

Anna’s voice softened, she pressed closer and Rio closed her eyes as she let her mom’s words warm her from the inside out.

“Entonces os merecéis la una a la otra.” Then you deserve each other.

Rio smiled as her mom squeezed her and soon they left the restaurant. Rio was unbothered by the paps still laying in wait now she knew Agatha had provided her with a little extra safety, and the rest of the party was as happy as they had been all evening.

But another surprise was waiting for Rio when they returned to her house with Alice tagging along for a “nightcap” before she went home again.

Rio didn’t notice this surprise at first, mostly because she wasn’t in the room it was housed in. But once she’d popped a bottle of Champagne and had poured out the four glasses, Alice insisted they drink them in the sun room at the back of the little house.

Rio obliged her friend and walked through with her, expecting nothing other than her potted plants and the colourful array of cushions across the couch in here.

But randomly, completely unexpectedly, there was now something else in the room. Rio blinked as she looked across at the standup piano tucked neatly against the wall, opposite the comfortable couch that had been with her since the very first apartment she’d shared with Alice.

“What the fuck?”

She moved closer to it, and Alice, knowing its origins, announced: “Agatha’s gift. She would have been here to see you find it but… she didn’t want to intrude on family time.”

Rio barely registered the words because she’d spotted three little ducklings etched into the fall board.

She felt movement beside her and knew Mateo had come to inspect it too.

“Do you play? You don’t, do you?”

“No, I-...” Rio trailed off, placing her glass down on the top of the piano as she reached for a card left lying there.

The envelope was thick, expensive, and Rio would expect nothing less of Agatha Harkness as she pulled out a piece of cream card with ‘AH’ letterhead in embossed gold.

My love,

An outlet for those fidgeting fingers when I’m not around to hold them.

Rio felt Mateo reading the note over her shoulder and she stared at the gift as her mom moved over to read the note too.

“Ella es parte de la familia. Necesita saber que lo es.” She is family. She needs to know that she is.

“Sí, mamá. Yo… ella es familia.” Yes, mom. I… she is family.

“A freakin’ movie,” Mateo announced, “I’m telling you!”

But Rio didn’t care much for the conversation going on around her anymore. She was no longer Mateo’s partner in crime, nor Alice’s best friend-cum-client, she wasn’t even Anna’s beloved daughter.

She was the woman Agatha Harkness was in love with. She was Agatha’s girlfriend. She was Agatha’s future wife.

As the three people around her continued to talk, to squeeze her, to now play the piano she’d been gifted, Rio excused herself to go and call Agatha.

She made it barely five steps and barely two rings before Agatha had answered.

“You’re home?”

“You’ve been tracking me?”

Silence. Then: “Just to make sure you’re safe.”

“The restaurant. The piano,” Rio breathed, unable to keep it in much longer. “Mi vida, I-...”

“Do you like it? If not, I can get rid of it. I can get you something-...”

“I love it. But Alice, Alice said you weren’t here with it because you didn’t want to intrude on family time? I mean this with all my heart now but, what the fuck? You are family. You are my family. I want you here. My god, Agatha, I want you here so desperately I-...”

Something had overcome her in that moment. Something a lot like desperation and Rio caught herself welling up as she spoke her truth to her girlfriend hidden away from fear she’d be found.

“Rio,” Agatha whispered in a voice that Rio could feel across her skin. “Do you know how important it is to me that your mom likes me? I need her to like me. I need, I… It was the right thing to do, to let you have time with her and Alice and Mateo. And tomorrow, tomorrow I won’t leave your side and we can be a family. A secret one. But a family. I promise.”

Rio nodded, the base of her palm pressed up against her forehead as she took steady breaths.

“She loves you. You don’t have to worry.”

“Well I’m doing everything I can to make sure she does. I-...”

But Rio missed what else Agatha was saying because her phone had been ripped from her hand and she turned just as her mom began to speak: “Escúchame. La familia nunca pregunta. La familia nunca se preocupa. La familia simplemente es. Mientras ames a mi hija y la trates bien, eres parte de la familia. Sin discusiones. ¿De acuerdo?” Listen to me. Family never asks. Family never worries. Family just is. So long as you love my daughter and treat her right, you are family. No arguments. Okay?

Rio watched as her mom listened to whatever Agatha’s response was and waited with baited breath.

“Sí, sí, mi tesoro. Mañana. Estoy tan emocionada. Adiós, tesoro. Que duermas bien.” Yes, yes, my treasure. Tomorrow. I am so excited. Goodbye, treasure. Sleep well.

The phone was passed back to her and Rio raised her brows as Anna patted her shoulder and then disappeared back off to the sun room.

“Your first real taste of Anna Vidal’s wrath.”

Agatha scoffed down the line and Rio smiled for it.

“And she’s given you a nickname already. See? Family. My family. Next time, please just be here?”

Agatha sighed quietly and Rio heard what sounded like a rustle of papers. “I will, I promise. I wish I’d come.”

“Next time,” Rio promised softly, sitting now on the arm of the couch. “Are you working?”

“I’m just… papers… just going over everything.”

Rio nodded and heard the strain in Agatha’s voice. She just didn’t know what to say to soothe it.

“I’m going to learn a song for you.”

“You are?”

“Mmhm. I’m not the best singer but I can hold a tune and… I want to play it for you. You can sit right by me as I do. Let me serenade you.”

“Right by you or on you?”

“On might make it difficult to play the keys.”

“That’s okay, I’ll take a half-played song if I can be closer.”

Rio laughed and slipped until her back was on the couch and her legs dangled over the arm.

“You can’t come over tonight?”

“I can’t keep disturbing Nicky’s routine. As much as he’d love to see you. As much as I would.”

Rio nodded, toying with the hem of her blazer.

“He was okay coming over last night?”

“He misses you.”

Rio sighed quietly, “Family. We’re family.”

“Yes we are.”

When Rio eventually hung up from Agatha - after being chastised for missing the festivities - the new piano was christened with Alice’s playing, Mateo’s shouted song requests, and Rio and Anna’s enthusiastic singing.

All of which resulted in Rio passing out in her bed around two in the morning, two hours after Anna had gone to bed and Alice had gone home. She’d spent the time since gossiping with her favourite cousin and convincing him that, no, live streaming her party was not a good idea.

In the morning, the Rio Vidal of the night before who missed her girlfriend, was entirely a new beast.

Because Rio, like any only child, was particularly irritating on her birthday.

And today, her first birthday spent as Agatha Harkness’s girlfriend, was no different.

Or, actually, it was a little different. Because Rio wasn’t irritating.

Rio was insufferable.

She’d bounded into the kitchen and swooped a kiss to her mom’s temple, swooped again until she was kissing Mateo’s already irritated scowl.

She was swooping and bouncing and not stopping for anything or anybody. Not even for the waffles her mom had made her, which she now ate with one hand as she ran about the yard with Mateo and still easily beat him at her favourite game.

Mateo had never been much of a basketball player anyway.

Still, sweaty and full of syrup, Rio had been forced to sit with a coffee by her side as she gratefully and greedily received her gifts. Because, whilst she’d been tearing up the little court outside, dozens of flowers had arrived all of varying shapes and sizes.

The biggest, most beautiful, most tasteful, were from Agatha. Full of greens and purples the note simply read: ‘For you, from me.’ Rio didn’t know why but she folded the note up and put it in her pocket.

She also received other gifts of the not-floral kind. From her mom she got a framed photo of her and her dad.

It was a picture taken when Rio was around Nicky’s age. She was mid-squeal as Miguel sat with her on the couch and grinned for the camera. Rio remembered the picture being taken. She’d been smiling for her mom behind the camera when her dad had decided to tickle her and history had been made.

She kissed his smiling face and then kissed her mama too.

Mateo’s gift was next and his was, true to form, a little stupid and a whole lot sweet. He’d bought his cousin an Agatha Harkness calendar and had filled it with every birthday of every cousin, aunt, and uncle she had.

“Agatha will kill you for this,” she muttered as she gave him a tight squeeze.

“Worth it.”

The rest of the morning went quickly, with Rio running more rings around Mateo on the basketball court. She hadn’t heard from Agatha but she had checked once, twice, three times where she was and saw that she was in a school gymnasium across the other side of the city which meant she must be at a basketball game watching Nicky.

Still, she was anxious to hear from her and couldn’t help but wonder why she hadn’t even so much as a text to wish her a happy birthday.

By the time they’d had lunch, Rio had showered off the sweat, and she’d steadily calmed down from being the centre of attention, she was getting more and more anxious to see Agatha.

“Why don’t you just call her?” Mateo suggested as Rio plonked some more on the keys of the piano.

“There’s a reason she hasn’t called. I’m just going to wait.”

She plonked some more.

“Can you wait… silently?”

Rio ripped her fingers along the length of the keys and stopped only when her mom shouted through: “¡Basta, Rio!”

Rio was much more delicate about her impatience after that. But she didn’t have to wait long.

By two in the afternoon the front door to the house opened and Rio heard the thunder. She stood from her new piano stool and ran through to see Nicky, in a stetson and cowboy boots, charging through the house to find her.

“¡Melliza!”

With no understanding of how heavy he was as he threw himself into her waiting arms, Rio barked a laugh as she stumbled back a couple feet but just about managed to keep a hold of the growing little boy.

“You’re a cowboy!”

Nicky laughed as she managed to keep the wriggling boy on her hip, groaning dramatically at the weight of him as he placed his hat on her head.

“¡Feliz cumpleaños!”

Rio grinned as she leant in carefully to kiss a ruddy cheek. “Gracias, mellizo.”

“Did you notice?”

Rio looked up from where she’d been smiling at Nicky and saw Agatha in all her glory wearing a green Celtics hoodie and light blue jeans. Truly, a vision.

Her heart stuttered, still so unused to the impact of Agatha goddamn Harkness on it. Rio gently placed Nicky down and straightened, her hand now absently toying with dark brown hair as Nicky remained close.

“Notice?”

Agatha grinned and motioned to Nicky before her, making Rio’s attention drop back down to the boy grinning up at her. She looked over his face, brushed his hair back from his head, and then…

“Holy shit.”

Agatha and Nicky both laughed at the same time. The same cadence, the same rhythm, but entirely different pitches.

Rio dropped to her knees before Nicky and held the collar of his sand-coloured shirt dotted with lasso-throwing cowboys.

“That’s my shirt.”

Nicky laughed again as Agatha marched closer and as little hands rested over her own a chorus of welcome rang through the house.

Rio looked up in enough time to see Agatha turning to greet Anna with two kisses to each cheek and her cousin, the bold Mateo, making a beeline for Nicky.

She stood quickly and allowed Nicky space that he so clearly did not want as he backed into her and managed to step on her foot in the process.

“You must be Nicky? I’ve heard so much about you! And I have so much to tell you about Rio.”

Rio loved her cousin and loved even more that he was trying with Nicky but as he moved closer to ruffle the boy’s hair she was quick to place her own hand there again instead.

“Hello,” Nicky said quietly, not realising the silent way Rio had just protected him. “It’s nice to meet you.”

Nicky held out his hand and Mateo glanced at Rio briefly, mischief in his eyes, before he focused back in.

“Pleasure, Mr Harkness. My name is Mateo. I am so honoured to make your acquaintance, young sir.”

“No seas imbécil.” Don’t be a dick.

“Oh c’mon, I’m just having fun! Right, Nicky?”

Nicky nodded and Rio ducked her head down to whisper into his ear as a familiar hand found the small of her back.

“Mateo is an idiot. But he’s my cousin and I love him so you tell me if he annoys you and I will kick him or something, okay?”

Nicky’s nod was much more enthusiastic this time and Rio grinned as she straightened and shot Mateo a warning look.

“What’s happening?” Agatha’s voice was casual but the hand that had been on Rio’s lower back was now beneath her shirt and she was standing close, her other hand on Nicky’s shoulder.

“Mateo being a dick.”

“Actually,” Mateo interjected, now moving round to kiss Agatha’s cheek. “I was introducing myself to your son and offering my services as knower-of-all-things-Rio.”

“All things?”

Rio sighed as Nicky asked the question and Mateo looked down to him with a grin.

“Oh. All things. Just tell me what you want to know and I’ll-…”

Nicky had looked back at Rio and then at his mama.

“Does she want a wife?”

Agatha’s hand froze against her skin. She’d been scratching at her beneath her shirt, giving her as much affection as she could, given the circumstances. But now her frozen hand was gone, swept away to bury in Nicky’s hair as she ducked down to him.

“Hey, why don’t you go grab Alice and ask if she’ll play some ball with you?”

Nicky hesitated but Anna leant in and held out her hand to the little boy and after Rio had returned his hat, Nicky soon took it and left the room with Rio’s mom, glancing over his shoulder at Rio as he did.

“Smart kid,” Mateo said just as Rio punched his arm. “Ow! Hey!”

“Telling an impressionable kid you can tell him everything he wants to know about me. Idiot!”

“How was I supposed to know he’d want to know if you wanted to get married?!”

“Idiot!”

Agatha grabbed her arm to prevent her causing anymore damage to her cousin but Rio could sense the annoyance in her girlfriend’s voice even as she tried to keep it calm: “Alice is getting everything out the car, maybe you could take over whilst she entertains my son for a bit?”

Mateo, as keen to please Agatha as he was to annoy his cousin, was quick about agreeing.

As he left, Rio muttered her excuses for him: “He means no harm. He’s just-...”

But Agatha had other ideas, other more important things to attend to. She’d turned where she stood beside Rio and draped her arms around her shoulders. It took Rio a second to register because now Agatha was grinning at her, smiling as if nothing much had just happened.

“Feliz cumpleaños, mi amor.”

“Uh,” Rio uttered, that stuttering feeling in her chest starting up again. The girl from this morning who’d been bounding around, bothering her mom, bullying her cousin, bragging about her ball skills, dissolved before the grinning movie star.

“You got my flowers?”

Rio’s body seemed to know what to do even when her brain was lagging a little. She’d slipped her hands beneath the heavy hoodie and was pleased to find no other barrier between her and Agatha’s warm skin.

“You didn’t call this morning?”

“I thought you’d be with your mom and-...”

“Mi vida.”

“I wanted the first time I ever wished you happy birthday to be right here. With you.”

Rio had opened her mouth to argue but found she couldn’t, particularly not when Agatha was now leaning in to press a kiss to her cheek.

She sighed happily, her eyes fluttering closed as Agatha nuzzled against her.

“You’re right,” she said, as Agatha’s nuzzling became the soft patter of kisses across her face. “This is better.”

“Mm. Thought so.”

Rio laughed as she felt Agatha’s teeth against her jaw and her grip changed from her hands resting in the dip of Agatha’s waist to her arms being fully around her so she could hold her impossibly closer.

“Can you just keep it in your pants for one day?”

Jen had interrupted them where Agatha was now reeling back to grin at Rio and Rio couldn’t look away as she responded: “Pants still on, Jennifer.”

“Only because I interrupted just in time.”

Agatha pulled back fully then and Rio hurried to huddle behind her, burying her face into the hood of her sweater over her shoulder. She’d managed to keep her arms against Agatha’s skin.

“Do we have everything?”

“You’re doubting my organisational skills?”

Rio raised her brows and lifted her head just in time for Jen to plant a quick kiss to her cheek and mutter a not unkind “happy birthday”.

“What are we organising?”

“Not you,” Agatha corrected, her head turned now to look at Rio, soon followed by her body which gave Rio the ultimate joy of brushing her hands across warm skin. “You are being locked in your room.”

“You’re kidding.”

“No,” Agatha smiled, her arms loose again around Rio’s neck. “We’re turning this place into the Wild Wild West and you can’t be here to witness it.”

“Why not?”

“It ruins the magic,” Jen said, now admiring a flower from a nearby bouquet. “Besides, I didn’t go to every party store in Hollywood just for you to be trying to hump my client here when everyone’s trying to make your party super lame for you.”

Rio scowled as Agatha cleared her throat, “You’ll be trapped with Jen.”

“That,” Rio huffed, “is so ridiculous I can’t even-...”

“You think I’m happy about it?”

Rio turned to look across at Jen and let Agatha kiss her cheek, as if it would make up for the fact she were about to be a prisoner in her own home.

“Well why with you?”

“Your girlfriend doesn’t trust you.”

Rio turned to Agatha with her eyebrows high and her jaw dropped low. “What do you think I’ll do? Climb out the window?”

“Something like that,” Agatha responded, her smug smile somehow lessening the slight. “Just go upstairs. It’ll be worth it.”

A lot of huffing and stomping of her feet later, Rio eventually found herself locked in her bedroom with a pile of snacks, the memory of a firm kiss from Agatha, and an already irritated Jen.

“It’s so insane to me that this is who Agatha is.”

Rio snatched a peanut butter cup from the mountain of sugar and went to lay on her back on her bed.

“What?”

“This down bad chick who buys fake saloon doors for her girlfriend’s birthday party.”

Rio chose to not rise to the bait and bit harshly into the chocolate. “You’re telling me you wouldn’t do the same for Alice?”

“Don’t speak with your mouth full.”

Rio huffed, swallowed thickly where she was still on her back.

And choked.

She sat up and coughed until she could breathe again and raised a hand to Jen who hadn’t moved in all that time.

“It’s cool. I’m good. Don’t worry.”

Jennifer was watching her and Rio, cheeks now pink, lay back down again and apparently hadn’t learnt her lesson because she was biting once more into the half a cup that remained.

“She’s nervous, you know.”

Rio didn’t say anything, not needing to ask who Jen was talking about and not wanting to choke so soon again.

“She wants to fit into your life.”

“She does,” Rio said firmly, the chocolate beginning to melt against her fingers where she was yet to throw the last bite into her mouth.

“The Rio Vidal who plays the field and parties is very different to the Rio Vidal who-...”

Rio sat up then, swinging her legs over the side of the bed, not caring that in her hands was now a sticky mess of peanut butter and cheap chocolate.

“Don’t start this again, Jen.”

“I’m just saying. Besides, you didn’t play the field so much as just utterly-...”

“Jen. You know it’s my birthday, right?”

Jen huffed and turned her head. Rio ate the remainder of her peanut butter cup and cleaned off her fingers in the process. Somehow it didn’t taste as sweet anymore. In fact, it tasted a little bitter.

They sat in silence for a while, Rio soon busying herself by rummaging through the snacks for something to rid herself of the odd taste on her tongue.

“Alice told me about the super bowl ad.”

Rio paused what she was doing and glanced Jen’s way. “She did?”

“Mmhm. It’s romantic.”

She turned away again and settled on a box of Nerds, the green and purple kind.

“I’m going to donate the money to an LGBTQ+ charity. Did she tell you that?”

“She did.”

Rio nodded, tipping out some of the purple into her hand. She sighed.

“I’ve slept with a lot of women. I’ve done some drugs. I’ve partied a little too hard occasionally.”

She poured out some green.

“I’ve enjoyed my life. I’ve had no responsibilities, and no one to come home to.”

She threw the candy into her mouth, tasting the artificial apple and grape on her tongue.

“I’ve had a crush on Agatha for almost half my life. I’ve never wanted anyone the way I want her. I’ve never wanted to come home to anyone except her. I’m going to marry her, Jen. As soon as I can. Because she’s all I want. All I’ve ever wanted.”

Jen was silent but Rio wasn’t going to be the first to look away as they stared across at each other.

“Not before me.”

“What?”

“You can’t get married before me. I won’t allow it.”

Rio scoffed and caught the twitch in Jen’s lips before she returned her attention to her Nerds.

“I’m not trying to be a bitch, you know.”

With a handful of green now, Rio looked back up. “Just comes naturally?”

“I’m looking out for my friend.”

“I would never do anything to hurt her.”

“I know that. She knows that.” Jen shifted in her seat. “It’s not really you I’m worried about. It’s past you.”

Rio looked away again, that slight bitter taste back in her mouth. She ate her handful of green.

“Nicky’s friend in the park that day?” Rio looked up, so shocked by the words from Jen’s mouth she almost choked again. “I think she was a PI. I’ve been doing some digging.”

Rio swallowed. “Following me?”

“I’m not totally certain but yeah.” She leant forwards and Rio felt alarm bells ringing in the back of her head. “Think about it. Going after Agatha is one thing but going after you…?”

“She’d lose it.”

Jen nodded, slowly leaning back again in her seat.

Rio focused down on pouring purple into her hand.

“I’m going to say this and then we’re not going to talk about it for the rest of the day, okay? It’s your birthday and… despite what you may think of me I want you to enjoy it.”

Rio brushed one of the small balls of purple candy with her thumb, absently counting how many Nerds she now held.

“I want to get the jump on anything that might come from their camp. I want to leak some stories to the press about you so we can better control the narrative. Because I know they’re going to do something. Evanora’s a vicious bitch and I can’t let her have any more power over Agatha. Not when I can help.”

Seventeen. Rio had seventeen tiny pieces of purple in her hand.

She looked up at Jen and saw her frowning across at her. For the first time all day she truly looked at Jennifer and saw the bags under her eyes, though they were expertly covered by subtle makeup. Her lips were drawn into a thin line and there was a frown across her usually smooth forehead.

“Is Nicky safe?”

Jen seemed to consider this for a second, whether unsure or surprised by the tangent, Rio didn’t know.

“Yes. He’s got eyes on him at all times. He’s staying at ours tonight and there’s already someone outside and someone waiting to get us there safely.”

Rio nodded and returned her attention back to her hand where the heat of it was beginning to melt the outer shell of the candy.

“Leak whatever you want about me. Speak to Alice first but… I don’t care. I just want them safe.”

“It won’t be so bad if it comes from us. I promise it won’t…” She sighed and Rio picked one of the candy’s up to eat it.

She held sixteen now.

“The play in London is the best thing you can do once all this is over. Agatha will have full custody and with a clean schedule she can escape with you. It’ll be good for Nicky too.”

Rio ate another candy. Fifteen left.

“And I think, and don’t get mad, New York in a couple weeks will be good for you both too.”

Rio scoffed at this, already jumping ahead to what Jen could possibly mean.

“Some time apart,” Jen said, her voice dropping until it was of a timbre that felt like she was dribbling warm tea over Rio’s ears. “Will do you both good.”

“How did you come to that conclusion?”

She looked up, feeling her whole body become like a coiled spring as Jennifer shook her head. “You have to look at the big picture.”

“The big picture is Agatha getting custody of Nicky and us-...” But her voice had begun to rise, hitting the point of almost shouting when from downstairs they’d heard a bang followed by shouts of laughter. It was enough to make Rio pause, to take a breath, to try again.

“She can’t come with me? Even for a day?”

“She can’t be seen to be taking Nicky out of state.”

Rio looked back down to the mess of purple in her hand. She touched the candy pieces and then threw them up and into her mouth, cleaning where her hand was pressed there with her tongue.

“I hate this,” she muttered as she pulled her hand down and looked at the sticky mess of it.

“That makes two of us.”

Rio released a huff of a laugh that was more a heavy exhalation, just something to fill the silence.

“Throw me something. The less artificial the better.”

Rio tossed over a box of raisins.

“Gross. Nicky’s favourite. Bad taste, that kid.”

“Last time he had them he gave them all to me.”

Jen laughed and Rio looked up with raised brows, touching the sticky inside of her right palm with the fingers of her right hand. The memory of the little pile of raisins that had once sat there making her unconsciously do so.

“You think that boy wouldn’t give you his favourite of everything?”

Rio looked down at her palm again and this time noted the purple and realised something.

“Agatha hates purple Skittles.”

“And?”

“She makes me hold them.”

“...okay?”

Rio shook her head a little, imagining the small pile of raisins she’d once held for the little boy with her same face. He’d been copying his mama. “Nothing. Doesn’t matter.”

Eventually, topics moved to more inane things like how pissed off Maria was with Agatha at this point in the shoot and whether Agatha would win Best Actress or not next year, the conclusion of both these discussions were very and yes, respectively.

Rio began to grow restless during this time, perhaps due to the excess of sugar she’d consumed, but more likely because she knew Agatha was in the house and she wasn’t able to be with her.

Not only that, but despite Jen now continually trying to distract her with other chatter, she kept thinking back to being apart from Agatha for a week. A week where she might need her most.

She was soon up and pacing just to work out some of the energy she couldn’t fully expel.

“This is so ridiculous.”

Jen scoffed, tapping her foot where she sat now draped in the small bucket chair in the corner of Rio’s room.

“You’re telling me. Never did I think I’d see the day where our girlfriends would lock us in a room together.”

“This is supposed to be my party. I should be out there groping my cowgirl.”

“Please,” Jen said quickly, her eyes closed and her hand held up, “Do not call her that. I’ll vomit.”

“Right you are, partner.”

Rio sank down onto the bottom of the bed and stared up at the ceiling.

Jen said nothing back and Rio suspected it might be because she was worried Agatha was going to be called a cowgirl again but really it was because she was now intent on her phone and ignoring Rio entirely.

She lay still like that for nearly twenty minutes and only occasionally flexed an arm out or rolled her neck to make sure nothing seized up in the time she was down. Her mind wandered during this time, self-soothing until thoughts of being apart from Agatha didn’t make her feel queasy and there was, in the very least, no sign yet of a headache coming her way.

But then the thunder came. Nicholas River Harkness could be heard storming through the house and Rio sat up straight to welcome the kamikaze in.

Only he never arrived. Nicky, for all his pounding, urgent feet that could probably be heard the next street over, didn’t even knock on the door. Rio stared at it and then stared at Jen who looked just as confused as she felt.

She stood slowly from her position on the bed and went to open the door.

Nicky was there alright, but so was Agatha.

The three of them blinked at each other, and Rio considered for a second that maybe she’d fallen asleep and this was some weird dream.

“What’s going on?”

“Well,” Agatha said, and Rio was momentarily distracted because Agatha now had two braids in her hair. They fell to just about where Agatha’s boobs were and Rio stared for way longer than was appropriate. “Ah!”

Rio had been caught and she looked up with a stupid grin on her face as Agatha snapped her fingers.

“I have no qualms about putting you in jail for misbehaviour."

“Jail?!”

Perhaps responding by rocking up on her tiptoes and grinning her big grin wasn’t the best way to get back into Agatha’s good books but it did make Nicky giggle and she shot him a wink as Agatha stood with her hands on her hips.

It didn’t help Rio’s grin. But now Rio figured Agatha was doing it on purpose.

“Do you want to come and see or do you want to stay here until everyone arrives?”

“No, no! I want to see it. I want to see it.”

Agatha’s stern face softened enough to reveal an already barely-hidden smirk and Rio rolled her eyes when it came out in full force.

“But first!” Rio announced, holding her pointer finger up. “I’m afraid there, Miss ma’am, you must pay the toll.”

Agatha scoffed but was quick about paying her debts in the kiss she delivered to Rio’s rosy cheek. If Rio had had her way the real price would have been a kiss on the lips but Nicky was there and Rio figured even on her birthday she couldn’t get away with that. Still, Rio’s face hurt now with the strength of her grin.

Something about the exchange had tickled Nicky so he was now giggling maniacally by her side as she followed Agatha down to the first floor and entered into the most ridiculous take on the Wild West she’d ever seen.

All about the hall there were banners with cutouts of cowboy boots and sheriff’s stars. On the floor there was an inexplicable amount of hay.

Rio’s eyes landed on a poster, one of many, that lined the wall. They were all posters of her. More accurately, pictures of her from various red carpets or events. And even some from her teenage years, or some she knew Alice had snapped when she was looking particularly tired or messy in any way. Written around the pictures were the words: ‘WANTED ALIVE: RIO VIDAL. $10,000 REWARD’.

Rio looked at them all in amusement and checked at least five of them before saying: “Isn’t it ‘dead or alive’?”

“Well,” Nicky’s voice came from beside her, “I wanted you alive.”

Rio, who’d turned at this point to look at Agatha, looked down to Nicky smiling up at her from beneath his stetson.

“I appreciate that, mellizo.”

Nicky blushed and Rio indicated with her head as she moved to drop before him and hold her arms back. “Jump up! I’ve got energy to burn from being trapped in my room for seven million hours.”

“Not that long!” Nicky insisted as he threw himself upon Rio’s back and she heaved him into the air.

Agatha only hummed as she motioned for Nicky and his stead to follow her through the rest of the house. It turned out the hay was an all-room thing and the posters were too.

Beyond that, there were signs indicating what each room was in this makeshift Wild West. The living room was dubbed ‘Rio’s Ranch’ in big letters on the wall. The kitchen was the ‘Saloon’ and the den off the back, a cosier space where Rio spent most of her time had a sign that read ‘Jail’.

Though the best sign, in Rio’s mind, was the ‘Watering Hole’ above the door to the bathroom.

“You know,” Rio said, stopping below said sign, “Technically a watering hole means-...”

“We know what it means, cowboy,” Agatha was quick to interject, moving closer to pat Rio’s cheek. “We just didn’t have any other signs to use.”

Rio narrowed her eyes, her grin still bright as Nicky clung to her neck and Agatha kept her hold on her cheek but her eyes on her son.

“Careful not to strangle the birthday girl, honey. She’s fragile.”

“Say that to my face.”

Agatha smiled, her blue eyes moving back to meet Rio’s darker ones. “Fragile.”

“Pistols at dawn!” Rio shouted as Agatha moved away and she jostled a giggling Nicky on her back as she hurried behind.

In the kitchen, gathered around the ridiculous amount of alcohol that had suddenly appeared across every available counter, were the rest of the little party. Which included Alice, who was standing in the corner with Jen whispering something into her ear.

She looked concerned then confused and then, when she saw Rio, she smiled and was quick about moving over to her and hugging her as best she could with a large duckling on her back.

“Happy Birthday! Do you like what we’ve done with the place? I think you should keep it this way.”

“I think so too, melliza. It’s very cool.”

“Even the hay?” Rio looked back around as best she could at Nicky, his hold a little looser after Agatha’s warning.

“Yes I like the hay.”

“Mm’kay.”

“Cuz, we’re going to order pizza and make a toast to you outside before your final gift.”

Agatha slapped Mateo’s arm and Rio raised her brows, bouncing along with Nicky to get closer to the action.

“Final surprise? There’s more?”

“You think these braids are for nothing?”

Rio’s eyes wheeled around to Agatha and she began to rock up onto the balls of her feet again, making Nicky laugh and hold her tighter. Agatha soon rectified this by loosening his arms again.

“Don’t tell me you have a cowboy get up?”

Agatha just looked at her and Rio beamed in response.

“Vale, vale, primero la pizza. La sorpresa después.” Okay, okay, pizza first. Surprise later.

Rio didn’t necessarily agree with this instruction from her mom but she didn’t protest either. Instead she fell into step beside Agatha and walked outside with everyone else. Nicky remained on her back as Rio took him around the garden, with Agatha trailing behind, pointing out all the different plants and trees she’d planted and had been trying to keep alive ever since.

Nicky was listening intently, or at least appeared to be, and that was enough for Rio to continue imparting her wisdom until her mom called for her to come back for food and champagne.

It felt good, Nicky happily now chatting in her ear about the cactus he had on his desk at home, with Agatha’s hand now curled around her arm, to just be with them.

It felt natural as Rio bent to let Nicky slip from her and she was tugged into a seat where Agatha could sit close beside her and keep her hand on her leg.

It felt normal as the pizza that had just arrived hot and ready to be eaten from RIo’s favourite Italian. Rio took a bite of Agatha’s to check if it was too hot for eating before she ate it.

And Rio, despite her earlier imprisonment and the stress she’d felt in her brief conversation with Jen, decided that this was already the best birthday she’d ever had.

With one, notable exception.

“Está aquí. Está con nosotros.” He’s here. He’s with us.

Rio nodded, Agatha’s hand moving from her thigh to her cheek so she could pull her in to kiss her on the other side of her face.

Anna was smiling at them, her eyes watery as Mateo took her hand.

From then on, Agatha’s hand was never far from her. In fact, she was pressed so close that Rio knew that if Nicky weren’t there - and perhaps her mom too - she’d be climbing into her lap.

It was hard not to just pull her into it. Impressionable child and Catholic mother be damned. Not that Anna would have too much of a problem… so long as Rio’s hands stayed in respectable areas.

But it was Anna who was soon causing Rio a lot of problems.

The second bottle of champagne had been popped. Dom Perignon, provided, along with several other bottles, by Agatha. Everyone was in good spirits. Including Nicky, who was as close to Rio as his mother was, and who had been allowed one more glass of soda than he usually would.

But spirits, Rio’s excluded, became particularly elevated when Anna produced another gift she’d bought to the party. Only this gift wasn’t for Rio, it was for Agatha.

“¡Ah! ¡Mamá! ¡¿Cómo pudiste?!” How could you?!

Anna Vidal, perhaps the proudest mother in the whole of LA right now (though she did have strong competition from the woman sitting beside her daughter), had produced a very large, very thick, photo album.

Rio, birthday girl extraordinaire, felt a chill as the spotlight was taken from her and thrown to her mom instead. Because Anna had moved up, gently nudging Nicky until he was in his mother’s lap and Rio was granted the unmitigated joy of having her baby photos thrown into hers.

“Agatha pidió verlos y yo estuve encantado de proporcionárselos.” Agatha asked to see them and I was happy to provide.

Agatha, ignoring the scowl Rio sent her way, instead threw her arm around Rio so she could squeeze even closer. And Jen and Alice, traitors that they were, came to hover behind the couch so they could see too.

Only Mateo, good, loyal Mateo, stayed in his seat.

“Wait until you see her at twelve,” he said, sipping his champagne, “gawkiest thing you ever did see.”

Bad, traitorous Mateo.

The whole thing was torture. Made only slightly less painful because Agatha was so close. But otherwise, torture.

With each new picture revealed or page in the album turned there were accompanying ‘oohs’ and ‘aahs’ and rude bouts of laughter. To the point where Rio stopped looking at them and focused off somewhere in the distance.

Nicky had been surprisingly quiet the whole time, something Rio hadn’t even registered until she caught a movement from the corner of her eye as he reached down to touch a photo.

She looked down to where his finger was pressed against eight-year-old Rio Vidal’s face and saw what he must be seeing.

“DNA,” Alice whispered against Rio’s ear, the one the other side of her from Nicky. But Rio ignored it, focusing instead on Nicky’s deep frown and the gentle way Agatha’s arm had slipped down to now be holding her hip.

She felt Agatha squeeze her and whisper, “What is it, honey?”

Agatha caught it before Rio did, and Rio before Anna. But Nicky’s wide brown eyes had looked up, focusing on the thirty three year old Rio now. And he looked like he was about to cry.

“It’s okay,” Rio whispered, gently taking off Nicky’s hat and holding it so they were enclosed between that and Agatha. “You’re much more handsome than me.”

Nicky’s lips twitched but he still looked, what Rio was beginning to understand was, overwhelmed. Agatha’s hold on Rio was given up in favour of holding Nicky and Anna, a proud mom and hopeful she could very soon be a proud grandmother, ushered Jen and Alice away.

“What is it, honey? Just a little shocked?”

Nicky nodded, his wide-eyed gaze moving briefly from Rio to his mom and then back again.

“Where have you been?”

Rio raised her brows, pretending she couldn’t hear the soft hitch of Agatha’s breath.

“Where have I been?”

“Why did it take you so long to find us?”

Agatha’s hold on Nicky tightened and she had turned her head, resting her own against Nicky’s temple as she looked away. Rio didn’t want to know why.

“Mellizo…”

“We have the same face. Why did it take you so long?”

“Baby,” Rio said quietly, aware now that her mom was ushering everyone inside. “It doesn’t work like that. I hadn’t met your mama until-...” but she stopped herself, because technically it was a lie. She cleared her throat and in a soft whisper, forced herself to continue: “I’m here now. That’s what matters, right? I’m not going anywhere.”

“Tres patitos,” Nicky said quietly as Rio lowered the hat that was giving them some semblance of privacy.

Agatha turned back too and Rio caught the swirling tears in blue eyes so was quick about touching Nicky’s cheek so he kept his eyes on her.

“Hey but you know when we look most alike? It’s when we smile.”

She gave her biggest, best, red carpet grin and Nicky returned it with a much meeker one of his own.

“Okay,” she said gently, “We’ll work on making your smile bigger. I’m pretty sure there’s cake inside somewhere and that always makes me smile.”

It seemed to work. At least, Nicky’s smile relaxed a little and then became brighter as Rio practically heaved him from his mom’s arms and dropped him down to walk with her, his hat back on, into the house. Agatha moved to take Rio’s hand and when they entered the kitchen Rio was relieved to see her mom had been thinking along the same lines she had.

So, with Agatha’s arms wrapped around her middle, with Nicky standing before her, she was serenaded by her loved ones and managed to blow out the candles with one breath.

She wished for Agatha getting full custody.

Maybe it was the distraction of the song or the promise of cake but Nicky was soon grinning again and Rio felt reassured by his presence now as close as Agatha’s was to her. So they moved, from the kitchen to outside again, all now with cake.
