Rio didn’t deny it, too content to be thinking of anything other than how good it felt to have Agatha against her like this, relying solely on her for warmth, and for comfort.

They both fell into silence for a while before Agatha broke it: “I’m scared,” Agatha whispered, and Rio’s gentle touches halted. “About coming out.”

Rio knew she’d been right before. That twinge of intuition earlier now sparked into a flame of fear in her own chest.

But Agatha only nuzzled closer, only pressed in where Rio had been worried she’d suddenly be doing the opposite.

“But tonight… I wasn’t scared. It didn’t feel… I wasn’t scared.”

Rio nodded, releasing a slow breath as she brushed over Agatha’s spine again. Agatha shivered once more and Rio was unable to find the right words so she said now but continued her soft appreciation of Agatha’s body against her own.

Soon Agatha’s shivers became more real and so Rio made them move until they were under the covers and Agatha could be warmer again. And like that, tangled up, they fell asleep.

Only, it wasn’t two hours later that Rio woke again, a little cold, and entirely alone. She looked in the bathroom first, then changed into sweats to venture outside her bedroom and go in search of her missing girlfriend.

She found her in the smaller living room, sat back against the couch with her mom’s photo album open in her lap. She was dressed in Rio’s pyjamas and wore her own glasses on the bridge of her nose.

“What’re you doing? It’s cold.”

“Did you enjoy your party?”

Rio frowned as she moved closer and Agatha’s hold on the album in her lap tightened just a fraction.

She dropped her gaze from it and settled down next to Agatha, facing her with her back to the coffee table.

“What is it?”

Agatha’s gaze faltered and she flexed her fingers around the album.

“Nothing.”

Rio reached to slide her hand across Agatha’s stomach but found Agatha to be suddenly territorial as she snapped the album up to hug it to herself.

“Mi vida,” Rio whispered, ignoring the fact that Agatha had nearly bruised her knuckles with the heavy book.

“Why are you sitting on the floor at five in the morning looking at my baby pictures?”

Agatha, now understanding Rio wouldn’t steal the book from her, relaxed her hold and looked at her properly.

“Maybe we can move to Delaware?”

Rio’s brows raised but she said nothing as Agatha continued.

“Buy a small house, live a normal life.”

“What isn't normal about being a mega star?”

Rio’s attempt at humour, as her fingers curled around the fabric at Agatha’s hip, didn’t work on her girlfriend.

Instead, Agatha had moved her hand up to rub under her glasses at her eye. She looked serious but not closed off. So Rio pulled her hand back and rested it flat across Agatha’s stomach.

She let her breathe for a while until she spoke again: “We can go to Delaware. We can go wherever you want.”

Agatha’s eyes fluttered closed.

“Mi vida,” Rio whispered, leaning closer.

She reached to turn Agatha’s face and found her amenable to it, her lashes fluttering beneath her large-framed glasses.

“We can make our home wherever you want.”

Agatha smiled, a sad sort of smile that made Rio’s chest ache. She leant in to kiss it away because looking at it for any longer would be unbearable.

“Come to bed?”

Agatha nodded and Rio pulled slowly away, standing soon with her hand held down to be taken when Agatha was ready to stand with her.

It took her a little while and Rio turned to watch as she closed the album and placed it like a precious thing on the coffee table.

When she took her hand Rio tugged her close to hold her for a second, which turned into several, when Agatha wrapped her arms around her.

They eventually went back up the stairs together. Rio’s steps were slow and deliberate because, if she were totally honest with herself, she might still be a bit drunk.

She missed the top step and stumbled. Agatha had to correct her where she almost crumpled and laughed against her ear.

She was definitely still drunk.

Now upright and with Agatha unhelpfully walking by her side with her arm across her front, they eventually fell back into bed.

Rio protested when Agatha began to move her glasses but soon acquiesced when it meant she had more access to her face. They kissed slowly, dazedly. Rio moved her lips all over Agatha’s pink face until she settled for her nose and smiled after kissing the very tip.

“I like getting older with you. And I’d like it whether we were in Hollywood or in Wilmington.”

“About that,” Agatha whispered as Rio moved to the bridge of her nose. “Maybe here for now.”

“Yeah?”

“Mm. Unless you get a taste for British cuisine or something.”

Rio laughed and rolled off Agatha onto her back, only to welcome Agatha on top of her the moment she’d stopped moving.

“I doubt that.”

“You don’t want a roast dinner? All the good chocolate?”

Rio huffed a laugh. “Hard to think about food when I have the most delicious meal on top of me right now.”

Agatha hummed, too busy nestling in to chastise Rio for her cheesy come on.

But Rio didn’t mind being ignored because Agatha was making a show of finding her usual spot. Ever the willing audience for her girlfriend’s more dramatic moments, she remained still and silent as Agatha eventually settled against her after a lot of nuzzling and huffing and touching.

“Comfortable?”

“Mm.”

Rio grinned at the ceiling, and thanked her lucky stars that Agatha had fallen for her all those years ago. They fell asleep again.

At least for another two hours.

“Wake up.”

Rio huffed quietly, reluctant to do as she was told. Agatha's voice was as gentle as she repeated herself and her lips brushed along the shell of Rio’s ear.

It made her hum, a low vibration that seemed to pull Agatha to her.

“Rio, your mom wants you to go to Mass. And Nicky wants to come with you.”

The words didn’t register for a while because Rio was only aware that the room was bright, that her head was thumping, and that Agatha was close.

“Mass?”

“Mmhm. You need to get up.”

Squeezing her eyes tightly, she pouted.

“No.”

“Rio.”

“Why does Nicky want to go to Mass?” Rio asked, although it sounded a lot more like: “Why’s Nick wan’ g’t’mass?”

Agatha huffed softly, kissing Rio’s warm cheek.

“He wants to be there when you talk to your dad.”

Rio blinked her eyes open, though still slowly, and looked up at Agatha.

“Your mom mentioned she goes every Sunday and Nicky asked if you did but she said no, not since you were little and you’d go as a family.”

“I-...”

“He knows enough about religion and god and heaven to think you might want to talk to your dad whilst you’re there.”

Rio groaned quietly, rubbing her temple, “That’s too much for me on a hangover to process.”

“Mi amor,” Agatha laughed, and Rio wondered how she was even able to when the pounding in Rio’s head meant she might never laugh again.

“Your mom sent me to get you. Don’t make me disappoint my mother in law.”

That, though manipulative, worked. Rio groaned, louder than she meant to, and threw herself from the bed. But dragged Agatha with her to the bathroom and made her shower with her. Mostly because she could barely open her eyes but also because it meant she could touch Agatha’s naked body.

The only real cure for a hangover.

By the time she was clean but no less furious, her mom and Nicky were already waiting for her by the front door.

Nicky’s greeting was warm but less enthusiastic than it might usually have been and Rio wondered if Agatha had warned him to be quiet and gentle with her.

Still, she let him jump onto her back as a reward for his not making her headache worse, and greeted her mom with a quick kiss.

“Mass? Really?”

“Por tus pecados,” For your sins, Anna said wryly, stroking down Rio’s arm as she shot Agatha a wink.

They left with some more grumbling from Rio and a whispered “I love you” from Agatha, aimed at the two patitos on their way out the door.

It was as Rio was making sure Nicky was buckled in securely that she remembered something she was yet to speak to Agatha about. With an almighty hangover was probably the wrong time to do it but her mom was there too, and she’d appreciate her input as well.

So, with thoughts other than if she remembered the Apostolic Creed, she clambered into the front and let her mom drive them to a local hispanic church.

Anna chattered away with Nicky on the ride over and it was only when they were pulling into the parking lot that Rio realised they hadn’t come alone. Agatha’s body guard, the tall guy she’d spotted the night before, had pulled up behind them.

For that, with her body not exactly fighting fit right now, she was incredibly grateful.

She held Nicky’s hand as they walked up to the little church and felt him shrink closer as they stepped inside. The small chapel was heaving with parishioners and Rio kept her head down to avoid any potential fans as she hurried behind her mom into one of the pews towards the back.

They sat so Nicky was on the edge, tucked against the wall and under Rio’s arm. Not wanting to draw any attention but intent on checking, Rio glanced behind them and saw their guy settled on a chair by the front door.

She smiled at him and he nodded back.

Mass, something she hadn’t been to since her dad’s funeral, was particularly painful that morning. A holy hangover was not all it was cracked up to be.

Rio spent most of her time daydreaming about things other than the ‘lord our god’.

She spoke the prayers when she had to - or when Anna nudged her with her elbow - and sang the hymns gently, watching as Nicky’s finger followed the words in the hymn book and he sang quietly beside her.

But mostly she thought of Agatha and how many more minutes it would be until she could be tucked up against her side again.

Nicky’s hand was warm in her own and became warmer still when he moved their hands to his lap and began to toy with her fingers.

Rio found herself wishing Agatha were there, not an uncommon feeling, but never a welcome one. Because missing was harder now.

Now she knew the depths that missing could take.

Nicky followed her with every movement. He stood when she did and knelt when she did. He experienced the excessive exercise routine of Catholicism with his hand always curled comfortably in her own.

When it came time for Communion, Anna leant close.

“Mija?”

“No,” Rio responded to the question she knew her mom was asking, “I’ll stay with Nicky.”

Anna, not the type to force religion on anyone other than her daughter (and even then it was the gentle kind of forcing), nodded and went to take her space in the line up to the altar.

Rio squeezed Nicky’s hand and sat back on the edge of the seat and moved so she could wrap her arm around him to keep him from sliding back too far.

Nicky took her other hand and they sat together in silence, perched on the edge of their pew so the holy parishioner behind them could lean against the back to pray.

She could feel Nicky watching the line up to the altar and wondered what he thought of it all. The ceremony of it. She figured he might enjoy it, where she had hated it when she was younger.

Then again, he was still fiddling with her fingers, so maybe he was a little more like her than he appeared.

The man directly behind Nicky knelt up against the back of the chair and Nicky glanced behind him before he shuffled closer to Rio’s side.

Rio squeezed him closer and wriggled her fingers.

It made Nicky look up and Rio ducked her head down so he could whisper into her ear, “If you want to come back we can come again.”

Rio smiled and turned back to look into the eyes of her mellizo. They were Rio-shaped but Agatha-built.

“Gracias, mellizo.”

Nicky’s lips twitched a little and then he turned back to the front of the church and suddenly his fingers weren’t twitching.

Rio held him tighter.

Anna soon returned and Rio squeezed Nicky’s hand before she extricated her fingers from his tight hold and reached for her mom’s shoulder.

Anna, recognising the silent support as she spoke to her god, reached a hand back and held her daughter’s.

Anna Vidal was a godly woman. She believed in the teachings of Jesus Christ. She believed that a good Catholic was a sinner who tried not to sin. “Only sinners go to Mass,” she always said.

It was important to her to be there, to say her prayers, to thank God for the good things in her life and to go to him for support when the bad things came.

But more important to her, greater than the faith she’d had since childhood, was the woman now holding her who’d welcomed her into motherhood with that first cry that cold spring day she’d been brought into the world.

When she had prayed for her daughter, for the little boy curled into her daughter’s side, for Agatha, and for the soul of her dearly departed husband, she sat back and Rio wrapped her arm around her too.

“¿Estás bien, mamá?”

Rio looked at her mom, knew that Nicky was looking too because he’d leant around her.

Anna smiled but Rio could see the tears filling in her eyes.

“Sí, mija. Me siento afortunada, porque te tengo.” I am blessed, for I have you.

Rio smiled and squeezed Anna’s arm. Her own eyes filled with tears as she leant in to rest their heads together and in that moment she felt more peace than she had for the whole of Mass.

“I am also hungry.”

Rio lifted her head and turned to Nicky who was looking earnestly up at her mom. There was complete silence between them and then Anna released a soft squeal of laughter and Rio caught it only a moment later.

She bit down hard on her lip not to let it be heard as her mom shook beside her and Nicky made matters worse by whispering: “Did you say something about tuna?”

There was simply no coming back from this.

Never in her life had Rio caught the giggles so quickly and in totally the wrong place.

Anna, too, was fighting for her life beside her daughter, now gripping her knee so tightly as her shoulders shook and she did her best to keep her laughter in.

Nicky was confused, had realised he’d said something wrong, and soon the laughter caught up with him and he released a high-pitched giggle before clamping his hand over his mouth.

Rio turned to him, biting on her own tongue, and widened her eyes which didn’t help Nicky to stop laughing.

“Let’s go, mellizo. Quick, quick.”

Rio began to usher Anna from the pew, and gently pulled Nicky behind her to stand and hurry from the church.

Her laughter was in check, and was contained until she felt the rush of fresh air as they burst into the LA sun. Outside, on the steps of a little church Rio hadn’t even known existed until that moment, she collapsed against her mom and released all the laughter she had.

She would look back on the moment later, with Nicky clinging to her and her mom doing the same, and realise that her laughter was really tears in a different form.

But it didn’t matter at that moment. Because the laughter had dissolved the pounding of her head, and had protected her from another thing.

A worse thing.

With her attention on her mom, on Nicky, and in getting them, still softly giggling back to the car, she’d missed the set of green eyes on them from a bus stop across the way.

Even the hired guard missed them, mistaking the onlooker for any other local going about their day.

Unaware of their observer, the ride home was much more lively than the ride there. Anna had taken to teaching Nicky new words in Spanish and Nicky repeated them three times over before he requested another and then another and then another.

Rio laughed with each new, randomly chosen word and accused her mom of teaching Nicky only very boring words so instead began to teach him more fun ones like: astronaut, vomit, and firecracker.

Soon the little trio rolled back up to Rio’s house and all bounded in with renewed vigour, which was only enhanced by the sight of Mateo, grey and sick-looking on the couch.

Alice, also present and similarly grey, waved her greeting their way. Jen, practically sprightly compared to the other two, smiled her welcome. And Agatha, somewhere in between Alice and Jen in terms of energy levels, opened her arms for Nicky to run into.

“How was it?”

“Nicky’s hungry,” Rio announced with a grin, making Nicky laugh into Agatha’s ear as he hugged her.

Agatha knew better than to question this for fear of getting a full breakdown of the time her son had been away from her so just arched a brow in Rio’s direction as she collapsed down beside her.

Rio, having forgotten with all that had happened that morning, that she actually needed the limelight again, went comfortably mute as conversation about the night before picked up and Nicky scrambled to settle between herself and Agatha on the couch.

With her arm stretched across the back of it and her fingers toying idly with Agatha’s hair, Rio’s slow-to-work brain soon kicked into gear and she announced that she needed everyone’s attention.

Jen rolled her eyes but everyone else seemed at least amenable.

“I’ll provide snacks,” Rio promised, mostly to Nicky, as she stood and noticed the floor was magically missing its layer of hay.

“I cleaned,” Agatha answered before Rio could even ask.

“Un ángel,” Anna announced as Rio smiled at Agatha and then went to fetch her laptop from the next room.

By the time she returned, Nicky already had a banana and a bowl of something that looked suspiciously like ice cream. But she was more focused on connecting her laptop now to the television and Alice, who’d remained mostly quiet all morning, now asked: “What are you about to bore us with?”

“Cars!” Rio said, “I’m about to bore you with cars!”

“Cars?” Mateo groaned from beside Anna. “Can you just kill me now?”

“No,” Rio said, her back to everyone as she struggled to find the right setting on the tv. “This is important. I want your attention.”

From her pocket, once her crudely made powerpoint was up for everyone to see, accompanied by groans from her cousin, Alice, and Jen, Rio produced a laser pointer and handed it to Nicky.

“You can be my assistant.”

Almost immediately a little red dot flew around the title slide which simply read: “CARS”.

Rio, running her hand through her hair as she did, went to stand by the tv and, holding her laptop in her arms because she didn’t know how to do it otherwise, pressed the arrow to get to the first slide.

“Mija,” Anna began, more than a hint of affection in her exasperated voice.

“¡Ay, mamá, déjame terminar primero!” Ah, mom, let me get through it first!

She caught Agatha’s gaze then and saw she looked amused more than anything - certainly more than anyone else in the room.

So, clearing her throat meaningfully, she turned to the first slide.

“The BMW X7 Series!”

“Jesus Christ,” Jen announced, slipping from the sofa, “I’m getting wine.”

Undeterred, Rio continued on, indicating with her free hand, and with the help of Nicky’s swirling laser, the picture of the car to the left of the screen.

She began to read from her notes on the right hand side.

“Pros! It’s big, a commanding presence on the roads but not loud. It’s got a lot of gadgets and advanced driver assist so basically lots of safety features.” She turned to check everyone was still with her and saw Alice’s eyes shut and Mateo’s with them.

They weren’t the desired audience anyway.

“Okay,” she continued, “lots of storage, high seats, pretty elegant and not too flashy.” She dropped her arm to indicate the Cons list: “All wheel drive so not great for any off-roading or those trickier drives up the canyon. And higher maintenance costs because it’s European so-...”

“Honey,” Agatha interrupted, making Rio turn to her in surprise, “You made all this?”

“A week or so ago. In between fort building.”

Agatha bit the corner of her lip but nodded for her to continue.

With a soft blush to her cheeks now, Rio indicated the car again so everyone could get a good look and then pressed to the next slide.

“The Bronco Raptor! More off-road than on, I guess. But looks cool as shit.” Nicky giggled, his laser now doing loop-de-loops over the image of the car. “It’s big again so intimidating on the road. Roof can come off. Cons,” she announced, indicating the list with her outstretched hand, “A little boxy. The safety tech isn’t as advanced as some of the others on this list and generally Fords don’t have a great rep for reliability.”

She turned as if expecting comments or questions but simply saw Agatha watching her with a look in her eye that made Rio’s blush deepen.

Jen had also returned, carrying a tray of glasses and an open bottle in an ice bucket.

Rio cleared her throat and continued. “Okay, next. The Volvo XC90. The best for safety. Some fancy-shmancy collision avoidance tech. Again, large, so loads of space. Maybe more elegant to look at so not as intimidating on the roads as some of the others and not so good off-road. But still, the safest I think of them all.”

She looked around again and still no one said anything but Nicky was grinning, his laser dancing about the slide.

With Agatha, though, something was different. The way Agatha was looking at her had changed.

Rio swallowed, unable to contain the feeling that had taken over her body as she absorbed the look in sea-blue eyes.

She felt her blush creep down her neck as she cleared her throat and just as she was about to continue Nicky’s hand shot up and she looked and raised her brows at him.

“Can these cars be green?”

Rio smiled. “Yes, mellizo. They can be green.”

Nicky nodded and Agatha squeezed him where they sat together.

“Okay. Next up! Land Rover. Defender 110. Pretty cool to look at, modern, rugged. Just like me.” She looked around with a grin but no one acknowledged her joke so she continued like she hadn’t interrupted herself.

“High belt lines, thick pillars, and a sturdy body generally. So strong crash structure and good impact absorption. Cons are: shitty reliability rep. Mostly depends on luck according to the message boards. Again, European, so more expensive. And maybe a bit ‘Hollywood’ for my liking.”

Rio glanced up again and caught Agatha’s eye. Her head was tilted and a smile was tugging at her lips but Rio couldn’t look for long for fear she’d simply look forever.

“Last but not least,” she announced, clearing her throat to get herself back in the zone as Jen began offering everyone wine just for something to do.

“The Lexus GX550. Big and tall, thick pillars again. It’s higher up so harder to see into. Better to escape paps, I’d think. Durable frame, tough structure. Pretty solid all round. Less stand-out than the Bronco or the Defender so maybe more subtle. Pretty solid for any rougher driving and generally a decent car.”

Rio smiled without meaning to, and turned her grin to her audience of three in a room of six.

“So,” she said, rocking up on her toes as she did. “I have a slide with a summary of them all but do you want to go back over any of them? I want to pick the safest one for…” she trailed off, her eyes darting to Nicky then back to her mom and then Agatha, “y’know… precious cargo.”

Everyone was silent and Rio waited impatiently for the result. She tapped her foot, chewed on her lip, toyed with her fingers.

Agatha leant over Nicky to speak quietly to Anna and, Nicky, sandwiched between his mama and Rio’s, was giggling and nodding enthusiastically and Rio wished she could hear what they were saying.

Thirty seconds later, she was let in on the secret.

The people she loved most in the world, the people who were listening anyway, all sat back on the couch and grinned their different grins up at her. Agatha looked charmed. Nicky looked thrilled. Anna looked proud.

“The last one,” Agatha announced. “The Lexus. It’s-…”

“Not the safest,” Rio said quickly, flicking back to the slides and through to the final option to explain her points again. “The rating isn’t bad, it’s just-…”

“Mija,” Anna interjected and Rio turned to see her mom leaning forwards on the couch. “It is your favourite. The Lexus. We all agree. That is your car.”

“But it’s-…”

“Honey,” Agatha added, her voice firmer than Anna’s. “It’s a safe car because you’ll be driving it. Because I trust you with Nicky. Pick your favourite. I want you to.”

Rio raised her brows in surprise and fidgeted where she stood.

“Nicky,” Anna said after a few seconds of looking between Rio and Agatha. “Vamos a preparar el almuerzo.” Let’s go make lunch.

As she stood she snapped her fingers in Jen’s direction and made her nudge at Alice, pretending to be asleep so as not to have to listen to Rio’s droning on about cars. Mateo, however, actually asleep, was left where he was.

Rio didn’t need to look around to know why her mom was taking Nicky away. Because as they moved from the room Agatha was already moving towards her.

“Do you know?” Agatha asked, her hands finding Rio’s hips to push her back against the wall. The laptop resting on her arm clattered against the wall but a new Mac was a small price to pay for the feel of Agatha peppering soft kisses to her jaw. “How ridiculously perfect you are?”

“Mm,” Rio hummed, now smiling as Agatha trailed downwards. “All this for some cars?”

Agatha’s hands moved down as her lips did and Rio’s eyes opened in surprise as her ass was grabbed.

“All this because you’re so worried about keeping my son safe that you make a slide deck. You’re such a dork and I love you.”

Rio’s wide, inane smile didn’t falter. Even when Agatha called her a dork. Even when Agatha lifted her head to smile at her and move so she could raise up slightly on her tip toes to be the exact same height.

She hummed and raised her brows and asked: “Will you still love me if I make the car green?”

“I’d love you even more.”

Chapter End Notes

Jen’s plan, huh? Sure sure sure

Chapter 50: Together

Chapter Summary

Moves are made.

Chapter Notes

Hope you’re hungry…

See the end of the chapter for more notes

It turned out that Rio’s reward for caring so much about Nicky’s safety was that Agatha was attached to her all day.

Or, maybe that would have happened either way, but Rio liked to think Agatha was rewarding her for something. Because it felt like a reward.

As they lounged in the smaller living room and Rio took a cure-all nap, Agatha stroked through her hair and cradled her head in her lap.

When Rio recovered enough to play some ball with Nicky later that afternoon, Agatha watched from the sidelines and soon was tugging Rio into a congratulatory hug to celebrate the two players as they crept closer to infinity.

When Rio disappeared to fetch snacks for Nicky and wine for everyone else, Agatha followed her in and made out with her against the fridge.

Just because she could. Just because she wanted to.

Nicky, too, was as close as he always was. He became shadow-like again. A duckling who had imprinted on his fellow, waddling around behind Rio wherever she went.

Except, of course, to the makeout session in the kitchen. Alice had managed to hold him back with chat about pirates. (She was slowly learning what little boys liked to talk about though the pirate chat somehow slipped back to Mariana’s Trench).

All of this, plus a million other things like Agatha’s continued insistence that she spoke to her mom only in Spanish, where Rio was lazy with it and always spoke back to Anna in English, made for the perfect day.

By evening, Rio had her arm around Agatha on the little bench at the top of the garden, beneath one of the larger trees.

“He bought two more stars, you know.”

“Hmm?” Rio hummed, distracted where she was toying with Agatha’s hair and watching Alice as she played dominoes with Nicky.

“Well, technically I did. But he didn’t want you to be alone up there so… now we have a tiny constellation. Tres patitos.”

Rio turned to look at Agatha and found her to be already looking round at her.

“Why didn’t he say?”

“I think he wanted you to feel special on your birthday.”

Rio smiled and almost forgot where she was as Agatha’s eyes darted to the twitch of her lips.

“You made a perfect kid.”

“He wouldn’t be here without you.”

Rio’s lips found Agatha’s cheek and she kissed her there before she huffed a soft breath against it.

“If only I could actually get you pregnant.”

“Mm, Alice seems to think you already have.”

Rio laughed and pulled away again to look over at her friend as Agatha’s hand moved over to her stomach, sliding up beneath her shirt.

“I’ll have a word with her about that.”

Agatha just shrugged, and as far as Rio could tell, seemed unbothered. Rio smiled as she turned back to look at Alice and check she wasn’t plucking any hairs out of the little boy concentrating hard over his dominoes.

“Maybe you will though…” Rio looked back round again and raised her brows. “You did promise cuatro patitos…”

A sudden movement in the bushes nearby and the burst of a bird from the thicket of leaves couldn’t even distract Rio from the look in Agatha’s eyes. She felt warm, suddenly, and knew she was probably blushing.

But Agatha, always seeking whatever warmth Rio could give her, had slipped her hand further up below her shirt and was moving up to nuzzle in against her burning cheek.

“At least we could have some fun trying…”

As Agatha’s teeth made contact with her ear lobe and Rio’s heart rate soared like the bird from before, she closed her eyes and tried to remind herself they were out in the open.

Her mom was near. Nicky was near.

“On Monday,” Rio said with some effort because Agatha was now kissing behind her ear, trailing slowly down, “When we were fucking I… I was thinking about getting you pregnant.”

Agatha stopped what she was doing and Rio opened her eyes to see her wide blue gaze.

“It’s just a,” she struggled, clearing her throat quickly, “just a sex thing. Just a-…”

“You don’t want to get me pregnant?”

“What? No! No I-…" Agatha's hand dropped down and Rio straightened her back. “I mean, I… what do you want me to say?”

“The truth.” Her fingers curled in and Rio swallowed again as Agatha scratched across her stomach.

“Yes. I…” Agatha’s hand moved back up Rio’s abdomen until it was curled around her ribs, her thumb just grazing the underside of her breast.

“I’m too hungover to have this conversation.”

Agatha smiled, and Rio watched it grow into a fully blown grin across her face.

Her thumb had moved up an inch which meant her stomach was now partially exposed to the elements and her nipples were standing full alert, waiting for the attention Agatha was teasing.

“You thought about getting me pregnant during sex?”

Rio nodded once, finding some solace in toying with Agatha’s hair.

“It turned you on?”

“Agatha.”

“Mi vida” Agatha corrected.

Rio clamped her mouth shut and said nothing.

“When you went particularly hard. When you finished inside me… you were thinking of getting me pregnant?”

“Are you making fun of me?”

Agatha’s brows twitched and Rio watched as her tongue darted out to wet her lips.

“It’s just that I’d really like it if you could.”

“What?”

“Get me pregnant.”

Rio gaped, too aware now that Agatha’s hand was moving to rest in the middle of her sternum and pushing her shirt further up, her fingers visible above the neck line.

“Only I think if you could we’d end up with a million children. All with your face.”

“A bad thing?” Rio asked, her mouth dry and between her thighs decidedly not.

“No. Just a lot of mouths to feed. A lot of me, pregnant with your babies.”

Rio grunted quietly and it made Agatha’s smile turn up in wattage. It was so bright now Rio thought it could probably be seen from space. From that little constellation of tres patitos.

Agatha’s fingers slipped down once more and flexed against her stomach. Her muscles twitched in response.

“You want,” she tried, trying to claw some dignity back, “me to get you pregnant?"

Agatha’s smile didn’t dim but her cheeks did shine with a new blush.

Rio nodded, and Alice picked up the cue to change the subject to the sketches that had been chosen and to give Rio tips on her Jack Nicholson. And soon, despite the agonies of the past few days, Rio was laughing again with her best friend.

But joy, in times like these, could never last too long.

“Don’t,” Alice, her eyes wide and her hand suddenly curled around Rio’s wrist, uttered suddenly. “Don’t react. Please don’t react.”

“Wh-?”

“There she is!”

A hand had found Rio’s waist, large and hot. It slid and curled until it was holding Rio properly, intimately, a great thumb caressing an arch along the back of her ribs that made her shiver.

But not so much as the hot, rum-soaked breath now against her ear.

“There’s the woman who’s been fucking my wife.”

Alice, still holding her wrist, now squeezed it, her nails threatening to add to the white scars already there where her eyes remained frightened.

And Rio stared at her, felt the hand on her side move down an inch. Her body, warmed by the alcohol and the closeness of the basement bar, suddenly felt on fire.

She turned her head and raised her brows at the sight of Ralph Bohner, grinning his goddamn grin just inches from her face.

“Looking good, mamacita. Must be that ‘I’m fucking the most famous woman in the world and think I’m getting away with it’ glow.”

Rio twisted her wrist, turned it so Alice loosened her hold and the tips of her fingers slipped to the cup of her palm.

“Ralph,” she grit out, turning her body to knock Ralph’s with her knees as she faced him. “You’re drunk. You should go home.”

“Haven’t you heard?” Ralph asked as Rio threw his hand from where it had moved to her hip once she’d turned. “Your cunt of a girlfriend has-…”

Rio stood from her bar stool, but Alice had been quicker. She’d slipped an arm between Rio and the man who towered over her.

“Feisty little thing.”

“Rio.”

“Hope you’re not bringing this energy around my son. I’ve seen you’re spending a lot of time with him lately.”

Rio made a move to step closer but Alice now had her arms held down by her sides.

Ralph’s blue eyes darted down to Rio’s fist and he tutted, “Can’t be getting violent when you’re trying to steal someone’s family now, can you?”

“You fucking pig. You fucking shithead bastard.”

“Rio,” Alice tried again, glancing around to see that they now had eyes on them from all angles.

Rio felt sick that her hands, useless fists by her sides, were not tight around this cunt’s throat. She felt sick that he had referred to her family as his. She felt sick that his blood ran through Nicky’s veins. She felt sick that he’d ever touched, ever fucked, ever breathed the same air as Agatha.

“You’ve had me followed?” She asked, unable now to stop herself even as Alice held her tight.

“My mother in law had a suspicion and she knew she was right when she caught you grooming my son a few weeks back.”

Rio saw red. No. Rio saw blood.

Alice didn’t stand a chance against Rio who was taller, stronger, angrier. She’d knocked her best friend to the side and had Ralph’s collar in her clutches before Alice could so much as shout another warning.

Ralph, too stupid to understand that grinning was a foolish thing to do, stumbled forwards where Rio tugged him down.

“You don’t deserve them. They don’t want you. You’re a piece of shit on my shoe and they are-…”

A rough movement, and Rio was jolted back as a familiar man intervened.

Rio scowled as Agatha’s hired security took Ralph away and she made to follow but Alice’s hands were back on her. On her chest, on her face.

“Think straight, Rio. Think about what you’re risking if-…”

But Ralph was laughing, his head thrown back in rapture as Rio felt the pain of a homicidal thirst left unquenched.

“I’ll kill him,” she said through gritted teeth, her fists raised a little at her sides.

“Take a breath and then I’m taking you home.”

Rio growled, a hateful noise that caused her to bare her teeth and imagine how good it would feel to be unleashed on Ralph. She would tear him limb from limb before she was even remotely satisfied.

But Alice, protective and firm, wouldn’t let go. So Rio had no choice but to calm down because people were looking, and Agatha would never forgive her if she lost her son because Rio couldn’t keep a handle on her temper.

She nodded once and Alice let go.

“Let’s get outta here.”

Rio walked on autopilot, pushed by Alice from behind. Ralph was long gone now. Probably sidled up to some chick in another bar already.

But Rio could feel his touch on her body. She could smell his breath. She could see the look in his eyes when he’d said Agatha’s name.

So she didn’t see what happened behind her as she stepped outside the dimly lit bar.

Someone had grabbed Alice as she was following Rio out, someone with a blonde bob and green eyes, though Alice barely looked around at her as she was told: “They’re pulling for affair. Keep her away.”

By the time the words registered, far too late, Alice had turned and the woman had gone.

Rio didn’t know how they got home but they did. And somehow she hadn’t killed anyone on the way.

No one she remembered killing anyway.

Inside her rented apartment Rio went straight for the bathroom and vomited up all of her fury.

Alice stayed by her side through the episode, rubbing her back and tucking her short hair behind her ears.

When her stomach was empty but her throat still full of bile she collapsed back and silently held out her hand for her phone.

Alice retrieved it and knew to dial for Agatha before she even placed it in Rio’s hand.

“Honey, everything-…?”

“He was in the bar. Ralph. He was in the bar.”

“Are you okay? What happened? Did he touch you?”

“God!” Rio exploded out, her back against the porcelain tub, “I could have killed him, I-…”

“Rio. Tell me what happened. Now.”

Rio growled and told Agatha everything. She barely breathed through it, barely stopped to think about how crazy she sounded or how desperate she was to destroy Ralph Bohner.

And Agatha just listened. Agatha was silent.

Until: “Rio put Alice on the phone.”

“What?”

“Alice, honey. Put Alice on the phone.”

Rio looked up at her friend who was sitting on the closed toilet lid and stared at her. Had she missed something? Had she passed out and was dreaming?

“Now?”

“Yes, my love. Now.”

Rio hesitated for a moment, and saw confusion in Alice’s eyes as she continued to stare. But then she reached the phone out and Alice slowly took it from her.

“Agatha.”

Alice was silent and Rio could hear the tinny sounds of Agatha talking on the other end. She just couldn’t hear the words.

“No. Yes. Agatha. No. No. Yes.”

Alice was staring at the floor and Rio could see the concern written across her features. She struggled over them, crawling until her hands were on her friend’s knees and she was close enough to make out what Agatha was saying.

“Did he touch her, Alice?”

“No. Not, not like that. No.”

“Then how? Tell me how.”

“Alice,” Rio whispered, about to reach back for the phone, but Alice held up her hand.

“Someone grabbed me on my way out,” she said instead of answering Agatha’s question. “A woman. I think that woman. I wasn’t thinking so I didn’t look around but she said they were going for the affair angle. She said… she said to keep Rio away.”

Betrayal, Rio realised in that moment, was white hot. It burned her soul so much brighter and fiercer than the fires of hatred that had consumed her from the moment Ralph had laid his hands on her.

She stole the phone from Alice, uncaring that she caught the soft skin of her cheek with her nails as she did.

“Mi vida,” she gasped out, already fearful Alice had delivered her a fatal, treacherous blow. “I… don’t. Don’t let that… no. No. It’s just mind games. It’s dirty play. It’s-…”

“Did he put his hands on you, Rio?”

Rio sat back on her ankles and closed her eyes. She didn’t have the strength to lie.

“He touched my side, that’s all. Above my shirt. He didn’t-… mi vida, I grabbed his shirt. And then your guy came in and pulled him away. That was all. Nothing… nothing else.”

Agatha’s silence solidified around her. It became crushing, calcified stone. But Rio didn’t move or struggle against it. She didn’t even breathe a word that might lessen it, if only for the length of the syllables.

She just waited. She was just crushed.

“It’s late,” Agatha said after too long of Rio simply not breathing. “Take me to bed with you?”

Something in Agatha’s tone told Rio that she was being patronised. It screamed pacification where it whispered comfort.

But Rio didn’t want to fight over the phone. Not now. Not when she was miles and miles from Agatha’s arms.

“Okay,” she agreed, already moving blindly towards her room. Because all she could focus on was Agatha and where she was, what she was thinking, what she was doing.

“I miss you,” Rio eventually said as she crawled into bed still fully clothed. “I want you here.”

“I miss you too,” Agatha whispered, her voice now less purposefully tender and more genuinely so. “So much. Don’t let this ruin Saturday.”

Rio scoffed and she heard some noise wherever Agatha was. “I’m not even thinking about Saturday. I’m thinking about you. And how much I want to murder your fucking husband.”

“Let me do the murdering and you just focus on the show and coming home safe, okay?”

Rio, now with her head down and her hand gripping tightly to her hair, asked: “To you?”

There was silence. Silence for longer than Rio could stand. And then, “always to me, my love.”

It wasn’t that Rio didn’t believe Agatha. It was just that she recognised that something had shifted. Something infinitesimal. Something that if she asked about it Agatha would deny. Something that perhaps even Agatha couldn’t recognise herself.

But, no, Rio thought. Agatha was always in control of everything she was doing. She would know what had changed.

So Rio would have to sit with simply knowing something had until Agatha decided to share with her. Because right now, Agatha was making sure she had water by her bed, was making sure she would brush her teeth, was making sure she’d stay on the phone until Agatha could hear her sleeping.

“I won’t be able to sleep.”

“Try.”

Rio sighed, her breath now minty fresh but the taste of vitriol still on her tongue.

“I want to kill him,” she whispered after what felt like an eternity of listening to whatever Agatha was doing on the other end of the line. “I want to kill him with my bare hands.”

Agatha was silent for a while before she eventually said, “Don’t say things like that. Not when-... you shouldn’t say things like that.”

Rio felt a flash of unspent rage surge through her but it died the instant Agatha said her next piece: “I love you so much. Please try to sleep. Try not to let him ruin this. I can’t stand the thought of him ruining this for you.”

And so Rio lay down, she lay silently, but she didn’t sleep.

Around six she must have passed out for an hour or so, because she woke groggily to Alice shaking her and looked down to where the timer ticked on on her phone screen almost about to die.

So Agatha had stayed on the line. Despite what Rio had sensed earlier she’d remained on the line. Rio whispered that she loved her and then hung up.

She didn’t get to speak to Agatha for the rest of the day.

Not until she was out shooting a pre-tapped sketch on Coney Island where they were singing a song about birds that was a loosely veiled song about girls.

“He’s responded,” Alice whispered in her ear as Rio was taken to reapply some lipstick. “He’s demanding full custody. No change to the prenup. He just wants Nicky.”

Rio could barely lipsync to her own voice. She could barely make the moves of the basic choreography she’d learnt that morning. She could barely see, barely think, barely breathe.

But she made it through. She made it through until she was back in the car being driven to the studio and her phone was pressed so tightly against her ear.

“It was what I expected,” came Agatha’s hoarse voice as she answered. And Rio just knew she’d wrecked it from shouting. Maybe at someone. Maybe just for shouting’s sake.

“I can’t talk now,” she added immediately after. “Nicky’s here. We’re safe. I have to go.”

And she’d hung up so suddenly that Rio hadn’t managed to say a word.

The rest of the journey back she argued with Alice to let her go home. She begged and bargained but Alice insisted she stay, that she couldn’t help, that she had to do this.

So Rio stayed. She did what she had to. She worked her ass off because she knew she had no other choice.

But she was standing on the stage she’d dreamed of since she was a little girl, running through a monologue she’d helped to write that was funny and stupid and smart and all she wanted to do was to run back home to hold Agatha together.

She couldn’t get her that night either. And Jen didn’t answer. Even when Alice rang.

Until, finally, Rio called her mom, knowing she was to be flying out the next morning anyway to see the live taping.

And what her mom confirmed made Rio’s heart break inside her chest.

Because Agatha had answered her mom’s call. Agatha had spoken to Anna for an hour that afternoon. Agatha had cried on the phone to her and let Anna soothe her and listened to her advice.

And she’d not allowed Rio to do the same.

Rio didn’t sleep again and when she rocked up to 30 Rock the next day she was a shell of her former self. But she was there, that was what mattered.

She found her voice five minutes before showtime and used it on Alice.

“How did he know? How did he find me? How did he fucking-...”

“They knew we were there. It’s the only explanation. They came because we were there. They’ve been fucking following us this whole fucking time and-...”

Rio held her hand up, “Please. Alice. I know what you’re going to say and… Please, I don’t want to hear it. We’ll just be more careful. I’ll move out again. I’l…” but even the idea of moving back out of the happy little house in the hills made Rio feel queasy.

“Rio! There you are! We need to hurry, c’mon! Lights up in five!”

Rio disassociated throughout the whole thing. She got through the show because it was what she was trained to do. It was what she knew how to do. What she didn’t know how to do was to live in a world where Agatha was in agony across the other side of the country and she wouldn’t answer the phone to Rio.

How could she ever know how to do that?

The show was a triumph and Rio, as the credits rolled and the cast cheered and bounced behind her, shouted her thank yous to the crowd, and did the only thing she could do to show solidarity with Agatha. She wore a white t-shirt with black block capitals across it reading: AGATHA HARKNESS.

She allowed the cast to envelop her, then backstage she allowed her mom and cousin to do the same. She was handed to Alice who held her through the worst of her sobs and then she was bundled out the back entrance and rushed to the airport.

Anna and Mateo hung back in the city, promising to take Rio and Alice’s things and get them shipped back to them.

Rio, now out of her mind, could focus only on Agatha. She made up excuses for her lack of communication that didn’t really make sense: maybe she hated Rio’s phone voice, maybe she had changed her number and forgot to tell Rio and Alice, maybe she’d fallen down a well and was waiting for Rio to lift her out of it.

But then they landed and all the lame excuses and crazy scenarios melted away to nothing.

Agatha didn’t want to talk to her.

Agatha blamed Rio for Ralph wanting full custody because she’d almost lost it on him in the bar. There. That was it.

Agatha blamed Rio.

But no, her belief in Agatha’s love was too much to believe it for more than a minute.

So what else. What else had kept Agatha from her.

They arrived at the house in the early hours of the morning and Alice said something to Rio that Rio didn’t hear as she hurried into the familiar property to find the woman who wouldn’t speak to her.

And there she was, standing in wait in the dim light of the living room where they spent so much of their time tangled up together.

But it wasn’t Agatha. It was someone who simply looked like her.

“I’m glad you’re home safe,” the person who looked like Agatha but was not Agatha, said. “I’ve been tracking you, making sure you were safe.”

Rio took a step forward. Just a step.

Agatha, the non-Agatha, stepped back.

“We need to talk, Rio.”

Rio felt the blood drain from her face, but where it went, she had no idea.

“We can’t do this anymore.”

Chapter End Notes

… for pain

Chapter 51: Apart

Chapter Summary

Agatha has to ask something she doesn't want to ask.

Rio has to do something she doesn't want to do.

Chapter Notes

IM BACK

See the end of the chapter for more notes

Alice Wu-Gulliver had been a shy kid.

She’d also been a little weird, with an interest in bugs that the other kids in her little Californian town just didn’t understand.

She eventually grew out of the bug thing but she did continue to be weird. And she always picked up and moved worms from the sidewalk when she saw them.

She was one of those people who knew a little about a lot because as much as she had a great capacity for kindness, she was interested in many things.

The shyness, too, had ebbed the older she got. It disappeared almost entirely when got to college and met her best friend, one Rio Vidal.

Rio introduced her two two things that helped kick her shy habits in the teeth: improv and lesbianism.

The first, she’d taken to like a duck to water. She wasn’t the best in the troupe - that was Rio - but she always showed up and tried her hardest.

The second, she took a little while to come around to. And Rio had held her hand through it, for the most part.

Not during any of the practical parts of discovering one’s sexuality. But for the feelings parts, at least.

Rio had been, in those sacred college years, like some crazy, wingman/guru. She’d chatted up girls Alice had shared glances with in class for her. She nudged her whenever she wasn’t saying enough or smiling enough.

She always made sure she kept away from their shared room on nights Alice was sealing whatever deal Rio had helped her get into.

And they rubbed along well together. They laughed far more than they fought. They were best friends within minutes of meeting and sisters before their first year together had ended.

And so Alice knew Rio inside and out. They were honest with each other, excruciatingly so. Rio always told Alice when she needed to lighten up and Alice always told Rio when she had to take things more seriously.

But Alice had a secret. One she’d only ever hinted at before. One that it was now far too late to share.

Rio Vidal should never have been famous.

Fame did not suit her.

She wasn’t built for it, didn’t thrive in it, and Alice knew she didn’t really want it.

They’d worked hard to get her here. They’d had sleepless nights waiting to hear back from auditions and spent their last dimes driving Rio to tower blocks in downtown LA. They’re worked their asses of to get her into the right rooms with the right people.

But at a certain point the “why” had slipped out of it.

In her heart of hearts, Alice had always pictured Rio as a coach of a high school basketball team in a small town; beloved by the kids and their parents. She would have a wife and two kids all with goofy grins and dark eyes. On the weekends she’d garden and attend craft fairs or she’d drag her little family out on hikes when they secretly hated to go but loved her enthusiasm for them.

She could be the best actor in a little theatre troupe in the next town over. She could wow small communities with her ability and be proud every night that she was doing something she loved.

But she did not belong amongst the stars.

And so when Rio’s own secret had been revealed, her affair with the most famous woman in the world, Alice had spun off into a tailspin of fear and panic. She’d had to witness Rio struggle under a power dynamic she simply could never shift.

Because Agatha Harkness, to Alice, was a beast of privilege, a fame monster who didn’t understand what her friend needed. She was the most renowned, most lauded, most loved actress of her generation.

And she was not good for her friend.

Rio needed love, and lots of it. She had been born into a family who loved her deeply, unconditionally, loudly. She needed that same kind of love from a partner, deep, unconditional, loud.

And in the troves of women Rio had dated before, Alice had watched her drop each one even as they gave her that kind of love, or attempted to. She’d watched her enjoy them and then gently discard each one whenever it got remotely serious. And she never understood. She never could fathom why Rio didn’t want to date that pretty dancer or that hot bartender.

Because they were all thrilled to be in the vicinity of Rio, let alone the arms of. But Rio just wasn’t interested in any of them. At least, not for more than a week or two when she’d inevitably drop them and move on. If they ever made it that far.

Only one ever had. Victoria. A wild card of a woman. Beautiful and extreme and fun in all the right, and wrong, ways. But even then Rio had broken it off before it had ever really begun.

And Alice, knowing and loving her friend so well, thought she knew what was missing. That one key ingredient that none of Rio’s dalliances ever had, or been allowed to have: stability.

Because Rio had so much love to give, perhaps more than she even knew what to do with. So she needed someone to dote on who would appreciate and reciprocate the love flowing her way and not ever throw it back in her face.

A person who was steady in her own love for Rio, not simply dazzled by her smiles and charms, and steady in her acceptance of Rio’s as it came her way.

And then Rio fell for Agatha and Alice knew from the get go that it was doomed.

Agatha was too powerful, too famous, too untouchable. And then the unthinkable happened.

Agatha had thrown Rio’s love back in her face.

And now again.

Alice stared down at the text that had appeared. She couldn’t remember the last time Agatha had text her. It had probably been just after Miguel died. Probably during the time when she was blowing up her phone trying to get to Rio and Alice had been a reluctant gatekeeper, torn between allowing her limited access and keeping her locked out.

3:41am
Agatha: Hey, I know you’re on your way here. Please don’t leave when Rio comes in. Jen’s upstairs waiting for you. Can you come in and sit with her? I need to talk to Rio and I need you to take her home when we’re done. Thank you.

Alice knew what the text meant. She’d had a suspicion of it from the moment she’d heard the woman’s words in the bar. And she knew Rio knew too. Which was why she’d shrunk into herself. It was why she looked pale and sick and why, Alice also knew, she’d be experiencing one of those headaches she’d not had in weeks now.

The car pulled to a halt outside the hills house and Alice spoke to Rio as she unbuckled and slipped from her seat.

“I’ll be right behind you. Rio, I love you.”

But Rio hadn’t heard. The door closed and she watched as her best friend stepped into the house she’d been allowed to call home for all of two weeks.

Until Agatha fucking Harkness had ripped it away from her. Until Agatha fucking Harkness had crushed her best friend again.

——

Rio stared at the woman she recognised but didn’t know.

It was Agatha alright. Agatha in her borrowed pink cowboy shirt. Agatha twisting the ring Rio had inscribed with her promise. Agatha with those blue eyes that looked tearful and oh so soft.

“Please don’t do this,” Rio found herself begging before it had even begun. No good, she thought. No good to start from a place of begging. It meant she’d already lost.

But she had to make it clear she did not want this. Would not, could not, handle it.

Agatha stepped closer and Rio gasped as her hands, usually colder but now warm and tender against her cheeks, held her in place so she couldn’t fall to her knees before her like she wanted to.

“Please come and sit. I need to do this quickly or I won’t do it at all.”

Rio closed her eyes and longed to refuse Agatha so that she’d have to go with the latter option. But then Agatha kissed her, a soft, quivering flutter of her lips against the corner of her own and Rio was unable to refuse anything she asked.

They nuzzled, then. Both seeking comfort they’d only ever received from the other. And Rio felt within it an understanding that the comfort would be fleeting. As just like pride, it was to come before a fall.

“Please, my love,” Agatha murmured against her lips.

The request was so gentle that Rio couldn’t refuse it. And so she took charge, knowing Agatha was unable to.

It was the least she could do, and the most at the same time. One last show of strength before she inevitably crumbled beneath whatever Agatha wanted to say to her.

So they moved together then, Rio leading the way, her right hand hung loosely as if a bridge between them where she held Agatha’s left and felt the metal promise on her wedding finger.

In the living room now, Rio took a seat on the edge of the coffee table and Agatha sat opposite her, still holding her hand, now turning it to kiss her open palm.

Rio couldn’t watch it happen. Her head thumped with the dull ache of inevitably even as her lips tingled from the earlier almost-kiss.

“I have been reckless,” Agatha began, her voice as shaky as her lips had been. A noise nearby suggested the front door had been opened and closed and Rio didn’t know a lot in that moment but she knew it would be Alice.

Agatha didn’t react so neither did she. In any case, they were still alone in the room lit by one, solitary lamp.

“I have been reckless with Nicky’s safety and with your heart.”

“Please,” Rio whispered, a tear slipping and the next caught by Agatha’s thumb as she slid from the couch to kneel before her.

“I have to ask you for time again, my love. I… have to. I couldn’t…”

Rio made the mistake of looking at Agatha then. She was shaking all over, as though a sudden gust of icy wind had swept through the room and swirled around on her.

But Rio was burning up. She felt like she was suddenly aflame, suddenly blazing hot as if in active combustion. Perhaps her body just wanted to burn her to ash. Dust could feel no pain.

“I have been blinded by… Rio, my l-love I…”

Rio moved her hands to Agatha’s wrists and held her, feeling the quick pulse that lay just beneath the surface as she did. Agatha’s heart was quivering too. It felt like a trapped butterfly, fluttering desperately to escape.

“I don't want to lose you. I… I can’t lose you. I just need… I need…”

“Please don’t do this. Don’t do this to me,” Rio whispered, forcing herself to speak where only sobs seemed to want to come.

Agatha closed her eyes and Rio watched her pale face as it crumpled in on itself and she just knew exactly what Agatha couldn’t bring herself to actually ask.

“Mi vida, I… I don’t think… I’m not sure I can… please don’t ask this of me.”

Agatha dropped her hold on Rio and even as Rio still held her wrists, her head fell into her lap and her tears soaked through her leggings as she sobbed against her thigh.

Rio held steady. She had experienced too much loss and too much grief to dissolve into the pain of it again. Because, once she did, she knew she wouldn’t be able to keep her head above the water of her suffering.

“Please,” she prayed, the word becoming a lifeline as she began to choke on the tide as it drew closer.

It was inevitable she’d drown.

But Agatha just cried against her and Rio could no longer hold her wrists. The moment she released them Agatha clutched at her hips, her fingers twisting in the fabric of her leggings as she sobbed.

Rio’s fingers fell to Agatha’s hair and she instinctually tangled them in it, but she could no longer hold on.

She stared unseeing ahead of her. And then… the call of the void.

A strange calmness overwhelmed her as if the pain were too much to actually be felt so it lived instead as a concept; as something that would eventually swallow her completely but for now was just a threat.

It was different to before. Agatha wasn’t shouting or pushing her away. If anything she was tangling herself to her. She was glitching and gasping against her, trying to rip open her skin and crawl beneath to live in the comfort of Rio’s body.

She had to believe it was different this time.

And she thought she knew why. If Agatha thought she’d been reckless but didn’t want to lose her then it meant she was terrified of the one thing they both put above each other.

The one person. The one little boy.

“For Nicky,” she breathed, and in doing so agreed to what Agatha had been trying to ask, rather than begging her not to even speak it.

Her drowning would come. But she wouldn’t allow it to happen before she’d let Agatha know she’d use her last breath to push Nicky onto safe, solid ground. And she’d push his mama with him too, with any strength she had left to give.

So she breathed out, long and slow, her eyes fluttering closed as her lungs emptied and her heart filled with fear.

In her therapy she had been working through temporary and permanent things and feelings. She thought of it now, used it as an adrift sailor uses the night sky for navigation.

The pain of a needle: temporary. A tattoo: permanent.

The admiration of a crowd: temporary. The image on screen: permanent.

The pain of separation: temporary. The life they would one day live together: permanent.

Agatha clung to her, her fingers seeking something to latch onto so digging her fingers in around her waistband to better entangle herself when the great unravelling would soon come.

“Mi vida,” Rio cooed, her heart rate matching the thud of her head; a heavy, painful beat. “Mi vida.”

And that was just it, Rio realised as she opened her eyes again and was unable to move her hand to soothe Agatha. Her whole life was sobbing into her lap, asking for time when Rio had thought she’d given all that she had.

My life. My life. She thought, over and over, until the words became, simply: my wife, my wife.

And time moved on as Rio froze in it and Agatha languished in it.

Agatha’s head eventually turned, her cheek pressed against Rio’s soaked thigh and her fingers tightening in the stretchy fabric of the running leggings she’d donned for the flight.

“I can’t risk losing him. Even… even joint custody I… I can’t risk it. I’ve been so reckless. I’ve been so,” Rio’s fingers twitched against dark hair as Agatha took a shaky breath in, “I’ve been so happy.”

“What does it mean?” Rio asked so softly she almost took herself by surprise that the words formed in the air she’d breathed. “What does it mean for us?”

Agatha pulled slowly back and as Rio looked to her, all pink and puffy, she found herself wishing she’d never asked.

“You can’t live here anymore,” Agatha whispered, her eyes down on where she continued to grip at Rio’s leggings, tugging at them like she wanted to rip them from her thighs. “You can’t visit. We can’t be seen anywhere other than… other than on set where we’ll be professional and… nothing more. No more time in trailers together. No more… no phone calls or, or texting. No… no contact unless, unless necessary. Rio, I don’t want this.”

Each subsequent word crushed Rio’s fragile heart that little bit more until she was the dust she’d hoped to be. But she could feel the pain now, and the pain was felt in every particle.

“You can’t sleep without me,” Rio uttered, tugging at the collar of the shirt Agatha wore for comfort and to feel close. “You need me to hold you and to…”

Agatha’s gaze raised up and Rio shook her head as she met it.

“I would never forgive myself if something I had done meant I lost Nicky. He has to come first. I haven’t… I haven’t put him first I-...”

“Agatha,” Rio said, knowing that saying her name would mean Agatha would listen. Instead it made her wince. “You have done everything for that boy. You have made a home for him and-...”

“I’ve given him a home that he can’t yet have.”

Rio swallowed thickly and reached for Agatha’s face.

“But he will have it. You will make sure he does.”

“I’m going to destroy Ralph,” Agatha agreed, her voice still not back to its usual strength as she continued to clutch at Rio. “I won’t let him take my son. Our son. He is our son.”

“Felizmente casada,” the promise Rio had made under a ceiling of stars, buried between their son and her sun. She whispered it now and saw the way Agatha’s eyelashes fluttered for the gravity of the words and felt her hold loosen on her right side until Agatha's hand was raised up and she watched Rio kiss the ring where the promise was written.

“Please… Please don’t give up on us. You won’t give up on us?”

“How could I? The past two weeks, getting to live with you, mi vida, I… I am so happy with you. Even leaving for a week I…”

“You were so good,” Agatha interjected, a spark returning to her gaze, if only briefly. “So funny and quick and bright.”

Rio’s mouth faltered for words that took a while to form.

“I couldn’t breathe through it. I was just thinking of you and,” she leant into Agatha’s hand as it caressed her cheek, “I felt so lost.”

“I’m sorry I shut myself off from you. I’m sorry I didn’t answer your calls or reach back out. I thought that if I heard your voice or if you heard mine you might just fly back to us and ruin your dream.”

“My dream is you. My dream is this family. My dream is the opposite of what you’re asking me to do.”

“I don’t,” Agatha started, her breath catching in her throat, “I don’t want to do this. Rio… Rio they know about us. They know that… they know and I’ll lose him. I’ll lose Nicky I… fuck I’ll lose you. I’ll lose him. I’ll-…”

Agatha’s breathing, catching, rushing, fumbling, made Rio tug at her to bring her up. Agatha, paler than she’d ever been and more tragically beautiful, was framed by Rio’s body.

She was knelt up, but supported by Rio; her hands twisted and twisted Rio’s sweater like she was trying to find the right catch to shut this whole thing down.

Their foreheads were together now, their breathing as if from one body. If pain could be shared, if it could be given, Rio would have gladly taken it all.

“I have,” Agatha gasped as Rio’s thumbs pressed into the soft marble of her cheeks, “I have to lose you to keep him. I have to send you away. I have to… I have to…”

Rio swallowed but felt choked as her fingers cradled her most precious person.

“Nicky always comes first,” she breathed. It was the only thing she could say. Because it was the most simple truth.

Nicky was what mattered. Rio did not.

But Agatha was crying like Rio might matter. She was breathing like Rio mattered. She was twisting and clutching and sobbing like Rio mattered.

And all Rio could do was to hold her as steadily as she could. They cried together, pressed together, until their breathing evened and all that was left of Agatha’s sobs were her hiccups.

Her hands stopped twisting and instead they clutched.

Rio could feel Agatha’s body quaking where she knelt so she was cautious about moving them. She had placed a delicate kiss to Agatha’s pouting lips, a brief act of reassurance, before she made any moves.

But soon they were on the floor together and Agatha was in her lap, her pale hands on Rio’s face where Rio’s hands were now resting on Agatha’s hips.

As Rio stared into the ocean of Agatha’s eyes she tried not to drown herself in them, knowing now what she had to do.

“It’s temporary,” she whispered, half to herself, half to Agatha.

“It’s just temporary.”

Agatha swallowed and nodded once and then the waves were gone as she dropped her gaze to Rio’s lips. Rio realised, far from drowning in Agatha’s eyes, they had been tethering her to life.

“You need t-to know,” Agatha gasped out, a slight hiccup interrupting her cadence, “why I… why we have to..,” she shook her head and swallowed thickly, her hold on Rio slipping until her fingers were aligned with her jaw.

“I need you to know that I… I trust you. This isn’t…” Agatha shook her head again and her eyes closed, blocking Rio out completely. “It’s not a punishment. Not… not for you.”

Rio’s hold must have tightened on Agatha, her nails must have pressed into her flesh, because Agatha made a soft noise but Rio wasn’t cognisant as to why. But she was holding her tighter. She was holding her with a fierceness she wasn’t aware she was currently capable of.

“Your phone,” Agatha continued, her eyes still closed and a pained look on her face. “It’s been cloned o-or hacked or… they have the pictures I sent to you. A-all our conversations. They h-have pictures of us looking a-at each other across parties or touching a-and you and N-Nicky at the park and…”

Rio had heard enough. Agatha made that noise again and Rio realised now she was close to breaking skin.

She released her and Agatha made a noise so full of pain that Rio didn’t know what was real or not anymore.

Her hands found Agatha’s hips again but she made a conscious effort to be gentle and hated herself that she had to.

“I didn’t share-,” she started, but Agatha was too quick.

“I know. I know. I know.” She shifted in Rio’s lap and blindly found her lips to kiss them the way a butterfly flutters to a branch.

“I would never-,” Rio started again, but Agatha was once more already ready for her.

“I know.” Another kiss as delicate as a butterfly’s wing. “I know.”

Rio couldn’t say anything else because there was simply nothing more to say. Her heart was in her lap, as broken as she was.

Agatha soon gave up on being delicate and simply pressed her whole face into Rio’s. She breathed deeply, moving only when her hiccups hit and her body moved with them.

And Rio went right back to clutching, making an indelible imprint on Agatha that no longer caused her to quietly protest. Instead, she pressed closer, encouraging Rio’s hold.

Miguel, Agatha, Nicky. Miguel, Agatha, Nicky.

Papa, Mi Vida, Mijo.

Losing one was devastating. All three? Unbearable.

The pain in her head seeped slowly down until it could be felt so keenly in her chest as well. And soon Rio was burning for it, her whole body alive with a suffering so acute she could no longer remember what it felt like to feel anything like normal.

But Agatha, Agatha felt it, she was aware of the additional loss she was asking Rio to bear.

So, still pressed close, she gave them both an inch of space. Rio’s hold tightened, deepening her mark.

Reaching behind herself, Agatha produced something in the palm of her shaking hand. Together they looked down at it, their foreheads resting against one another.

“I bought this,” Agatha whispered, raising her cupped, shaking hand for Rio to see a silver locket cradled there, “when Nicky was little and I had to leave him for the first time. I-I wanted to keep him with me even on set so I took a lock of his hair and carried him close. I’ve…” Rio made a soft choking noise and Agatha moved her free hand to hold the side of her throat. “I’ve added a lock of my own and I thought that… that you might want it. S-so we’ll be close. Even when… even when we can’t be.”

With shaking fingers, Agatha opened the silver locket covered in intricate embossed vines.

Inside were two locks of different shades of hair. One, darker, tucked into the small clasp on the right side. The other, the exact shade as the hair on Agatha’s head, cradled by the clasp on the left.

Pieces of her family, the only pieces she’d have access to until Agatha had full custody and they could be together again.

Agatha proffered the locket and Rio, reluctant to let go, did. She took the offering and whimpered for the weight of such a tiny thing. But Agatha held her hand to help her bear it.

Rio closed the small locket, protecting these precious gifts. She closed Agatha’s fingers around her own and kissed over them, closing her eyes as she kept her lips to soft knuckles.

Agatha shifted on in her lap and slipped her free hand through Rio’s hair to hold the back of her head.

“Please don’t… I know I can’t ask… I know I shouldn’t but please… please don’t… don’t sleep with anyone else. Don’t… don’t fall in love with anyone else.”

Rio raised her watery gaze and saw through the tears the fear in Agatha’s eyes. She reached for her face and brushed her thumb across her quivering lower lip as she said: “It’s always only been you. I’ll wait as long as it takes, and when it’s all done, we can go down to the courthouse and make it official that I am yours, and that I always have been.”

Agatha’s lips twitched into a pained smile that Rio traced and then tried to match, but her own face simply wouldn’t cooperate.

“Maybe I could write to you,” Rio whispered, watching Agatha’s smile twitch as if trying to remain alive. “Send you letters. Get Jen to deliver them. I’ll write you more poems and tell you about my day and…”

But she couldn’t continue. She made a quiet choking noise as if her throat was rejecting the concept of the very words she was trying to speak to convince herself she could keep away.

How could she keep away?

“Make me flowers,” Agatha breathed where Rio couldn’t go on. “Make me flowers and I’ll fill the house with them. And I will make sure this is over quickly. That we win and I can have you here again.”

Rio found herself nodding, agreeing to something she didn’t want to do. How could she make a flower bloom when the sun was being taken out of her life.

“Agatha,” a voice so gentle it couldn’t have possibly been Jen’s, though it was, sounded from somewhere to their right.

It triggered a response Rio hadn’t been expecting. A sudden leap into her arms as Agatha wrapped her own around her neck and buried her face in its usual, sacred spot.

It became clear that Agatha had been holding back. Because the sobs that reverberated through her whole body made Rio’s quiver from the intensity of them. They were louder than before, heavier, worse. But she held her, held her firmly, undeterred by the audience of two standing in the doorway.

Rio cried silently as Agatha sobbed and as her sobbing became a warbled chorus of “sorry, I’m sorry, my love I’m so sorry”, Rio could only hold her tighter.

“Rio,” Alice now, a little firmer than Jen had been. “We have to go, babe.”

Rio held on a little longer, breathed Agatha in a little deeper, and then forced herself to whisper above the “sorrys” that kept coming: “I love you. I will wait for you. I love you.”

Agatha’s pitiful chanting wavered and then died as Rio’s lips sought her cheek, then travelled to her lips. Agatha tasted of salt and sadness and Rio knew she tasted the same. They kissed as if they’d been starved of the other for decades, and remained close even as they parted.

Agatha, a miracle of flesh and heartbreak, allowed Rio to move her.

“M’sorry,” Agatha breathed, her lips brushing Rio’s still as she pressed close, but now sat on the floor before her where Rio was stooping above her. “I don’t want to do this.”

“It’s for Nicky,” Rio whispered, kissing Agatha where she had whimpered, “It’s so we can be a family.”

“Rio,” Alice again, her voice cutting through the sounds of Agatha’s struggle and Rio’s thudding heart.

And so Rio began to extract herself from Agatha. With every slow, deliberate movement, she kissed the features she had access to: swollen lips, a pink nose, a furrowed brow, then a pale wrist, a clenched fist.

She held the locket and stood properly as Agatha clutched at her leg, pawing at her thigh as her head rested there again and her hands slipped down to her calf, her ankle, just to keep close for the seconds she had left.

“I don’t want this,” she kept saying, over and over until Rio could no longer stand it and she had to step away, and step over Agatha who collapsed down the moment she had.

She’d seen this sight before; Agatha collapsed on the floor in Berkeley screaming at her that she was a coward. But this time was different. Agatha was clutching at her chest just like before. She was quaking and sobbing like she had in their temporary home upstate.

But she wasn’t screaming. She wasn’t shouting through her agony. She was instead begging forgiveness with the repeated words that jumbled in the air around them: “I don’t want this, I don’t want this, Idontwantthis.”

Rio had to keep moving, even as she turned back to see.

Alice caught her around her middle as Rio stumbled blindly towards her and out the room. Jen, as she passed, brushed her arm, and then went to Agatha, still sobbing on the floor.

But Rio didn’t stop for either Alice, nor Jen. She didn’t stop until she was in the back of the car that was waiting; the car that hadn’t left since she’d stepped out of it not that long ago.

She threw herself inside and let out a wail of anguish that split her entirely open from the inside out.

The door had opened and closed again and suddenly Alice was there but Rio couldn’t feel her arms around her. She could only feel the warm metal of the locket in her hand and the crushing, jagged pain of total and utter loss.

Alice held her until Rio gave in to it. She sobbed in her best friend’s arms until the car pulled up to her little Spanish villa.

They got inside but Rio didn’t know how.

She was on the couch with the locket so tightly wound around her hand it was now purple, but she barely noticed.

Alice was pacing as Rio stared at nothing in particular and tried to keep the flashing lights at bay.

“What if I’ve ruined everything? What if it’s already too late?” Her voice was timid, far too timid to belong to Rio Vidal.

“Jen thinks what that bitch said to me in the bar was a tipoff. And she, or they, or whoever the fuck left pictures near the gate. A warning, maybe, showing us what they have. Maybe a gesture of… I don’t know.”

Rio tilted her head in acknowledgement that she’d at least heard Alice., Though she could barely decipher her words over the thumping of her head.

“Your mom’s arriving later, did she tell you? She’s going to stay a couple days.”

“Agatha arranged it,” Rio deduced, blinking slowly in the soft light of the morning that now crept in through the windows.

“Yes. Your mom apparently told her to look after her baby and she would look after hers.”

Rio’s eyes closed but her head angled down, her chin almost dropping to her chest with the weight of feeling.

“She said we can’t even call. No texts. No nothing. I want to die, Alice. I don’t think I can… I can’t do it.”

Silence, heavier than before, befell the living room that had once held a party in her honour, and Rio turned to Alice to see her suddenly ashen.

“Please don’t say that,” Alice whispered. “Please don’t say that again.”

Rio opened her mouth and then closed it. Because how could she live through this? How could she know that Agatha was in so much pain and she couldn’t hold her through it?

How could she live knowing that someone had stolen Agatha’s happiness? Her comfort? And that she had been the means of doing so.

So Rio said nothing because the only thing she wanted to say was that she couldn’t live this way. And Alice didn’t want to hear it.

“Tell me what you need, Rio. Whatever it is.”

Rio shook her head because Alice couldn’t bring her what she needed. So instead Alice moved over to begin the difficult process of unwinding the locket from Rio’s purple hand.

“What if she decides it’s too much,” Rio whispered, watching the way her fingers slowly returned to their normal colour as Alice held them in her own hand now free of the snake of the locket's chain.

“Let’s focus on getting you to bed and-…”

“Alice,” Rio insisted, lifting her gaze to look at her friend properly. “What if Nicky gets taken away and she blames me?”

Alice, as loyal as they come, avoided her gaze. As Rio’s head continued to thump she saw the flicker of anger beneath the calm surface and had to look away.
