“It’s not your fault. None of this is your fault.” Alice said. “You did nothing wrong. This whole fucking thing is such a fucking mess and it’s not your fucking fault.”

Rio’s body made her stand, because her mind and heart were useless now. She placed the locket around her neck and Alice followed her to her little basketball court where Rio, as exhausted and pained as she was, picked up the abandoned ball and began bouncing it with each thud of her head.

“Wanna game?” Alice had asked hopefully after watching for a while. But Rio hadn’t responded. She just kept it bouncing, kept her head down, her brain such a treacherous place now she needed the safety of knowing the ball would always fly back up to her waiting hand to keep her from collapsing.

“She’ll call,” Rio said in response, counting each bounce in her head: twenty, twenty one, twenty two.

“She’ll call. She’ll find a way to reach me. She’ll use Jen’s phone and yours and-...”

Thirty. Thirty one. Thirty two.

“We’ll find a way. I’ll find a way to be there for her.”

Thirty six. Thirty seven. Thirty eight.

“I have to make it up to her. I have to-...”

Forty.

“I don’t think she’s good for you,” Alice said above the noise of the bouncing, making it suddenly stop.

“Alice.”

“It’s the second time, Rio. The second time I’ve had to piece you back together after she-...”

Rio bounced the ball one more time, and much harder. She caught the ball on the up and held it between her hands.

“Don’t.”

“She’s not ready for a relationship. Especially not with a woman. She’s selfish and volatile and-...”

“She made a mistake and I’ve forgiven her for it.” Rio saw a flash in her periphery and felt the oncoming vertigo.

“And what’s this? A promise that everything will be hunky fucking dory and then all of a sudden-...?!”

Rio threw the ball, whipping it from her chest towards Alice. Alice caught it but stumbled back a step.

“Someone has been stalking us. Has cloned my phone. Has approached Nicky in a park. Has sent pictures that were private, has sexually assaulted my girlfriend and you’re accusing her of-...?”

“Hey! I am trying to protect my best friend!”

Alice whipped the ball back and Rio stumbled as she caught it. She’d lost her sense of gravity, of what was real and what wasn’t. But wasted no time shooting it back to her.

“And what a stellar job you’re doing with that! Not only is-” Alice had thrown the ball back at her, Rio shot it back again, “you know what?! I don’t even want to have this conversation with you. Get out of my house.”

“Rio!”

Alice threw the ball at the wall. Rio heard the slap of it but was focusing now on remaining upright. She was stumbling, blind but for several spots in her vision. But Alice caught her. She held her and Rio had no choice but to allow her to help her up the stairs.

At the top of them she vomited. The attack hit so hard and so violently that neither of them had any warning. But Alice hadn’t pulled back or let go. She’d protected Rio from falling backwards, from collapsing into her own vomit, from collapsing at all.

“Here, here,” she encouraged, brushing back Rio’s hair as she brought up what little was in her stomach. The clean up could be done later, and for now Alice focused on getting Rio to bed.

She tucked her in, wiped her mouth gently with tissues, and left her on her side to return with water.

“Try to sleep,” she murmured as Rio’s eyes became heavy and hooded.

“I love her,” Rio whispered, “I can’t lose them.”

“Okay,” Alice agreed quietly, brushing back the sweaty strands of Rio’s short hair. “Try to sleep. I’ll clean up and… I’ll be just outside.”

And Alice, she went outside to clean the mess Rio had made. And then, as dutiful as a soldier, went to stand guard outside Rio’s bedroom. Eventually she slipped down to the floor but she didn’t move a muscle, not even to check her phone.

Alice didn’t move until she heard the front door open and not long after, Anna appeared in the hall.

“Ángel Alice, ¿cómo está?” Angel Alice, how is she?

Alice shook her head, her jaw set and unable to move to give Anna the answer she sought. But Anna, keen on seeing her daughter, stopped first to check on her surrogate one.

And the moment her hand touched Alice’s cheek, Alice began to cry.

She cried for what she had said and for what she’d been unable to do.

But Anna held her through it, rubbing her back and patting her hair. Because all that mattered to her was that Alice loved Rio and that was a crime for which there was no punishment; only a life-long sentence of being an honorary, and beloved Vidal.

She whispered soft reassurances into Alice’s hair until Alice calmed enough to pull back and wipe roughly at her eyes.

“She doesn’t want to speak to me. She’s been sick. I bet her head hurts again, I.”

“Okay,” Anna nodded in understanding, doing her best to hide the fear in her face as she brushed a strand of wet hair behind Alice’s ear. “Come.”

So Alice reluctantly followed Anna into Rio’s bedroom and for a moment couldn’t see her friend. But the lump in the middle of the bed gave her away.

“Mija,” Anna called gently as she placed a hand on said lump, unknowingly finding Rio’s side through the blankets. Or maybe it was simply a mother’s intuition to know exactly where to find her child.

“Todas estamos preocupadas por ti.” We are all worried about you.

“Did she call?” Rio’s voice sounded from below the sheets, muffled and scratchy.

Anna looked at Alice and then looked back to her hidden child, “I spoke with her, yes.”

Rio shifted below the sheets until she had enough leverage to tug them down so she could look up into the eyes of her ever-loving mother. She avoided looking at Alice, who now sat on the other side of the bed with her head angled down.

“What did she say?”

“She is frightened.”

Rio swallowed and found herself almost choking on it. She sat up and Anna moved to rub her upper back as she fought the panic that threatened to overwhelm her.

She couldn’t tell her mom she wanted to die. So she didn’t.

Alice had blindly reached back for her hand and Rio took it and held onto it firmly. Her anger had died in the darkness of being alone.

“Your father,” Anna continued softly, continuing to rub Rio’s back, “would have told you to fight, to find a way to be together through this. But I… I am asking you to stay away. For the boy. For a future you could have together.”

“She can’t sleep without me,” was all Rio could think to say in response.

“And without her Nicky she will never sleep again. A little pain for a lifetime of happiness. If that is what you want. Mija,” Rio looked up, having been staring at the foot of the bed. “If Agatha is what you want, you have to suffer this. Is she what you want?”

“Mamá,” Rio croaked, “I-...”

“Okay,” Anna said soothingly, hushing Rio with a stroke of her hair, “Then here is the good news: she only asked about you. She only wanted to know that you were and would be okay. And,” she smiled a little as Rio sniffed, “she wanted to know if I would ever allow her to marry my daughter.”

Rio felt Alice’s fingers twitch against her own but she ignored it to look instead at Anna and felt again the creeping lights of a continued attack.

“I don’t feel well,” she managed, her streaming eyes giving her away. “I just want to sleep.”

It was a soft lie, one that held the extent of her pain back from her mom.

Anna placed the back of her hand against Rio’s forehead and frowned for the heat of it.

“Sleep, mija,” she whispered, choosing still to speak in English. “We will be here with you.”

Rio didn’t know how to say that she only wanted Agatha with her so she didn’t. She instead let go of Anna and Alice and sank below the sheets into a dreamless, lifeless sleep.

At ten o’clock Anna woke her. She made her eat a little soup, wiped her face with a warm, damp cloth, and then left her to rest again.

By five in the morning, Alice was the one waking her.

“You feel up to work? Schedule says it’s a quiet day for you. You’ll just be needed for-…”

“It’s fine,” Rio croaked out, already forcing herself to sit up. “I’m fine.”

“Well you’re not but-…”

“Don’t. Not today. Can I get a-…?” But she looked properly and Alice was already holding a mug of coffee and she grunted her thanks as she took it from her.

“You know I love you, right?”

Rio said nothing back until she was at the door to her bathroom.

“Did she call?”

“No, babe. No call.”

One foot in front of the other. One sip. One step into the shower. One step out. One shirt, one pair of pants. One hug from her mom. One nod to her driver.

One fake smile at the Grip. Another to a PA. Another to a Producer in his grey suit and thick-framed glasses.

One bounce. Two bounces. Three bounces.

Rio was surviving one thing at a time as her mind tried to keep her from sinking again. At least not until Nicky was pushed to solid ground. At least not until she could fix what she’d unwillingly started by doing as Agatha asked.

Four bounces. Five.

Rio had her back to the door when she’d heard the knock and for the first time that morning she moved quickly. In her haste to turn and answer it she’d somehow managed to lob the miniature basketball directly at her manager’s head.

“Hey!”

But Rio was more intent on seeing who it was. She opened the door expecting Agatha come to say it was all fixed, that the pain was over, but instead found Jen, looking less than excited to be there.

“Mind if I come in?”

Rio nodded once and stepped back to allow it, glancing in Alice’s direction as she did.

“I won’t stay long and it’s nothing… just sit, maybe.”

Rio did as she was told.

“Is… she okay?”

“She’s… been better,” Jen said carefully, her dark eyes on Alice as she silently excused herself to head to the kitchenette.

Jen cleared her throat.

“Nicky’s upset.”

Rio sat forwards, bouncing a little in her indecision to stand or remain where she was.

“Is he here?”

“It’s 11am on a Monday. He’s at school.”

Rio blinked and dropped her gaze.

“Right.”

She twisted her fingers in her lap, wishing she’d said goodbye to him before she left the previous morning.

“Anyway. Agatha’s got a plan. More… a suggestion, if you’re interested?”

Rio did bounce this time but bounced literally out of her seat in her enthusiasm for this, for any, plan.

“Anything. What is it?”

Jen glanced at Alice who was muttering to herself as she slammed her finger against random buttons on the coffee machine.

“Once a week Val takes Nicky to a little park near the house. It’s quiet and there’s plenty kids around with their nannies. You could meet them and spend some time with Nicky?”

Rio was trying to do complicated math in her brain and struggled to find the answer she was looking for.

“Not with Agatha?”

“No,” Jen said carefully, her gaze swinging back around from her girlfriend to Rio. “Not with Agatha.”

“How upset was he?” Alice asked out of nowhere, her finger still jamming one of the buttons. “Nicky? How upset?”

“Alice,” Rio called, detecting an argument brewing when she could do with quiet instead. Her head was still throbbing threateningly.

“No,” Alice said before Jen could give an answer. “I think it’s important to know how upset the kid was and how upset his mother made him.”

“She is not his mother. She is his mom. His mama. Stop it Alice before I-…”

“Before you what, Rio? Before you just lay down and take it? Like you have been with-…?”

“No! Rio! No!”

Jen’s shouts did nothing to stop her. Rio had thrown herself, splitting headache be damned, at her best friend.

And Alice had caught her and crashed down to the floor with her.

Rio starting slapping at Alice just as Alice slapped at her.

“Jesus! Rio!”

“Don’t! Speak!”

“Rio!”

“Argh!”

“About! Her! Like!”

“RIO!”

Rio stopped what she was doing, panting heavily over Alice, her eyes wide and her mouth dry as she stared down at her best friend. Alice’s face was pale, her hands held defensively in front of her face and chest.

“… that,” Rio finished quietly, and now she was still and no longer actively scrapping, Jen could tug her off and Rio allowed her to.

“Are you an animal?! What is wrong with you?!”

“Leave her, Jen.” Alice, her voice heavy and flat.

“What?! Are you kidding?! She just attacked you!”

Rio put the heel of her hands into her eyes. It wasn’t enough anymore not to see. She wanted to darken her whole world until the light came back in.

Maybe if she dug the heels of her hands in hard enough she could go blind until such time as she’d want to see again.

“Jen,” Alice’s voice again, somehow distant even though Rio could tell she hadn’t moved since sitting up when Rio had moved off of her. “Can you give us some space?”

“Absolutely not!”

“Jen.”

Distant as her voice may be, Rio had never heard Alice be so firm with Jennifer. But she didn’t hear what happened next. She’d slipped too far away, too taken over by pain and torment to concentrate any longer.

“Jesus, Rio,” Alice’s voice, much closer, her hands working to tug at Rio’s wrists. “Look at me. You just tried to slap my face off, the least you could do is look at me.”

Reluctantly, Rio let Alice pull her hands away and she blinked rapidly so the spots would disappear and she could see again. And what she saw was Alice staring back at her, her face unmarked by her earlier attack but her frown deeper than she’d ever seen it.

“What was it your mom once called us?” Alice asked quietly, still holding Rio’s wrists as she adjusted her legs beneath her to kneel before Rio.

“Two alley cats afraid of their own claws.”

Alice scoffed and as Rio’s vision returned to somewhat normal she caught the twitch in her lips.

“Did I hurt you?”

“Nah,” Alice huffed, releasing her hold on Rio. “Not nearly strong enough for that.”

Rio remained silent and looked down to her hands now curled in on themselves in her lap. Attacking Alice had been a bad choice, but she’d not caused any real damage and knew by the way Alice was keeping close and now had the tips of her fingers pressed into Rio’s knee that she wasn’t really mad at her.

Though her next sentence made her wish she was.

“I fucking hate what she’s done to you.”

“She’s not-...”

“Don’t defend her on this, Rio. She should have been honest from the start and said she wasn’t ready. But then she lets you fall in love and… Jesus, let’s face it, it’s been so obvious from the get-go that you're head over heels I-...”

Rio shook her head and shifted back to lean against the wall.

“It’s not like either of us had a choice.”

“That’s bullshit. Don’t get all star-crossed lovers on me, babe. She knew what she was getting into, what she was risking and she went for it anyway. She entangled you in it and-...”

Rio was shaking her head, feeling the wall against the base of her skull with each turn.

“We’re doing the right thing now. I’m staying away. I’m-...”

“Miserable!” Alice shouted, her hands flying into the air where she remained kneeling before Rio on the floor.

“You are still grieving! You are barely holding it together!”

Rio shook her head again and rolled it against the wall until she had turned her face from Alice.

“I’m holding up just fine. I’m seeing the doctor, I’m eating, I’m working out.”

“Oh yeah? How’re the headaches? How was vomiting at the top of your stairs last night? How was sleeping for almost twenty four hours? And you tell me the last time we had a conversation about something that wasn’t Agatha Harkness.”

Rio was silent for the length of time it took for her head to throb enough to make her want to blind herself again.

But she fought it off because she didn’t want to prove to Alice that she was even remotely right. She turned back to her, kept her eyes open, and asked: “You wanna go to the movies or something?”

Alice scoffed and nudged at Rio’s knee.

“You’re such a dick.”

Rio hummed but even that gentle vibration hurt her sensitive disposition. She must have winced because Alice was now moving to sit beside her against the wall and Rio heard her take in a deep breath before she spoke again: “Don’t hide it from me, okay? I’m mad as fucking hell but… don’t hide. You’re hiding from enough people as is and… just not from me, okay?”

Alice’s hand, tentative at first, soon reached up towards Rio’s neck. Rio, half-zoned out as she stared straight ahead and counted the tiny dust bunnies on the floor, didn’t notice until Alice had rescued Agatha’s locket from its fabric prison.

Her friend patted it, a surprising show of gentleness from Alice for something that represented the woman she was in such a rage about.

“Maybe we could see a movie,” Alice mused as her hand on the locket was replaced by Rio’s, who now held it tightly. “Take your mind off of everything for a couple hours.”

“My treat,” Rio responded, “make up for jumping you.”

“Yeah, maybe I need to have a word with that dude Agatha’s made to follow you around. He should be protecting me too.”

Rio scoffed and her hold on the locket loosened enough that Alice turned her attention back to it as Rio’s mind wandered back to Agatha again.

“She gave you it?”

Rio nodded and regretted it immediately: “A lock of her hair. And Nicky’s.”

“Think I could get DNA from one of the Nicky strands in there?”

It was stupid. And Rio knew Alice was just trying to make her laugh. But the intent behind it didn’t matter because the fact was that Rio did laugh. Far from the alley cat she’d turned into earlier, she was now barking where she sat. Ache in her head be damned.

And Alice, as angry and frustrated as she was, did Rio the ultimate kindness of not mentioning Agatha’s name for the rest of the day. They both tried their best. They spoke of Anna, of the food they hoped she’d make for them later. They debated what movie they wanted to see and where and if Anna would want to come along. They gossiped about one of the ADs having a barely disguised hickey and whether or not it was Maria’s PA who seemed very smug that day who’d given it to him.

In all this distraction, both knew that Rio wasn’t doing so well. Alice made sure she had water and snacks and was sitting down as often as possible but Rio’s vision kept blurring when she was left alone for even a second.

They never made it to the theatre that night. Rio had held it off until she was back in the car but the migraine that had been creeping in at the edges all day finally took over.

Alice half carried her to bed with the scent of Rio’s favourite Pollo Guisado floating through the house. The woman she’d attacked not five hours ago, curled up on the other side of the bed just in case she needed her in the night.

But Rio didn’t. She just slept, slept until Alice had disappeared from the bed to fetch a much-needed coffee and Anna was there instead, placing a warm, damp cloth on her daughter’s brow and welcoming her gently into the next day.

“Did I dream it all?” Rio’s voice was hoarse, barely a gravely whisper but Anna smiled and simply shook her head as she stroked her cheek.

“No, mija.”

The door to the bedroom opened and Alice stepped in, bringing with her a tray of coffees and the burgeoning understanding to Rio that this was her real life.

She didn’t look around to her friend but instead kept her eyes on her mom who was looking up to Alice and smiling a little as she took one of the mugs from the tray. In the soft light of the morning, Anna Vidal looked tired and paler than usual. And Rio knew she was contributing to whatever pain her mom must be in.

She reached for her hand and Anna was quick to look back around at her, and just as quick to reassure: “Hablé con ella anoche. Te extraña. Pero está bien. Dice que duerme bien y-…” I spoke to her last night. She misses you. But she’s okay. She says she’s sleeping well and-...

“She’s lying,” Rio whispered, her gaze falling to the steam rising from her mom’s coffee cup. “She doesn’t sleep well when-...”

“Mija, este dolor pasará. Eres mi hermosa, fuerte y audaz hija. Y también eres la hija de tu padre. No permitas que este momento destruya a la niña que sé que eres.” Daughter, this pain will pass. You are my beautiful, strong, wild daughter. And you are your dad's too. Do not let this moment in time destroy the girl I know you to be.

Anna’s hand, now warm from cradling her coffee, wiped away the tears that had sprung up in Rio’s eyes and spilled out onto her cheeks. But Rio was nodding, her own hand beneath the heavyset duvet reaching to clutch the locket still around her neck.

“I want to be there with her. I want to hold her through it and-...”

“Time,” Anna whispered in English, “You can give them time. And Agatha will come back to you when she can. When she is safe to do so.”

“Rio,” Alice said quietly, having settled on the bed behind her. “You have a few days coming up. We think it might be good to go back to Delaware for a while, just to get away. Just to breathe.”

Rio closed her eyes and allowed her mom to continue what she’d started earlier with the damp cloth on her forehead. As a child she’d loved being sick. It meant she got more attention than usual. It meant everyone was a little nicer to her and she no longer got in trouble for anything.

But now, now she wanted to run from it. She felt weak when she wanted to feel strong. Because Agatha, and Nicky, they needed strong. Rio couldn’t show up after giving them the time they needed and be a shell of her former self.

She had to be better than she once was. She had to be able to get through a day and not have to be carried to bed by her friend and doted on by her grieving mom.

“When?” She asked quietly, blinking her eyes open again to turn towards Alice.

“We can leave Thursday and come back Tuesday.”

“Will you tell Jen? Let her know that-...”

“Agatha already knows,” Alice said, reaching a hand out to touch Rio’s shoulder, just visible above the covers. “I booked the flights this morning. I figured you’d agree. Once in a blue moon you know what’s best for you.”

Rio nodded, just able to make her lips curl up into a half-smile.

“Did she say anything?”

Alice’s hopeful smile fell.

“She said Nicky will be at Beeman tomorrow after school. That he’s desperate to see you.”

Rio nodded and squeezed the locket in her hand so that for a while after she let go she’d still have the imprint of it against her fingers.

It was arranged then: Rio had to get through two more days of waiting, of working, and then she’d see Nicky, and then she’d be home. Anna stayed just one more night and then left in the early hours of Wednesday morning.

Rio insisted on driving her to the airport herself and shared a teary goodbye, though she’d see her again the next day.

On set, Rio was mostly waiting to be called for something to do. The movie was slowly coming together but this was a kill for her in terms of being needed. But she was part of the ensemble, rather than being a main character, so was needed less.

She saw nothing of Agatha, and only glimpses of Jen. Which either meant Agatha was busy filming all the time or hiding away in her trailer for extended periods. She guessed both but had no real way of knowing.

But her headache hadn’t returned. At least not in the unbearable form of a migraine attack like it had on Sunday morning and Monday night. And Rio did her best to be healthy, which meant carbs and coffee, as well as the occasional protein bar and water that Alice kept pushing on her.

She managed a four mile run in the canyon after dropping her mom off and even managed to do some half-hearted yoga in her trailer. But mostly she pined. Alice started calling her “Shads”, a derivative of the even more derisive “Shadow”, taken from Homeward Bound.

Because Rio was a lost puppy, unable to settle for long on any task or project or even conversation. She was constantly seeking the next thing to distract herself, the next thing that wouldn’t remind her of Agatha or the little boy who’d be waiting for her on the basketball court that night.

Alice was still angry and Rio saw it in the way her face hardened every time Agatha came up in conversation. She could see it in her eyes every time Rio let her guard down for more than a second and her friend could see once again how miserable she was.

But worse still, Rio saw her own anger reflected in her best friend. Because she was sad, yes. But she was growing more and more angry with each minute she had to be separated from Agatha.

Every time she went to check her phone and found it to be the new one Alice had bought her, with a new number, and crucially, without Agatha’s number saved in it, she saw red. When she so much as thought about Agatha having to sleep alone, subjected to night terrors and sleep paralysis, because of an idiot man she’d been forced to marry, she felt homicidal.

And, at night when there was nothing to distract her, when she thought of that same man demanding he have access to a son he didn’t even want, she wanted to scream until her throat bled.

But she made it through with her anger and sorrow as constant passengers in her waking hours to the moment in time she now found herself.

She sat in her little rental car, aware her hired security guy was parked up not far away and only not having a problem with it this time because she’d soon be with Nicky and any additional eyes on him were a good thing.

The mirror told her that she looked tired but not as grey as she had been looking the past couple days; partially due to the makeup she’d left on from work and partially because, despite everything, she was looking forward to an hour or so with her mellizo.

So she got out of the car with her ball and the flower she’d made for Agatha - the first of the ones she’d promised to make her - and walked, shadowed by her security, to where she knew the basketball court to be.

She heard him before she saw him. The steady bounce of a practised hand thumping the ball on the hard ground, the grunt of effort as he made a jumpshot, and the familiar sound of a ball disturbing the net.

“Woah! What a shot, mellizo!”

Nicky whipped around and Rio’s heart stopped in her chest at the sight of his shocked expression. But he was in her arms before she even had time to register it properly. Her ball bounced away, forgotten, and the flower she’d spent so much time on that morning was crushed in her fist as she lifted Nicky into the air and held on tight.

If you’d told Rio Vidal of a year ago, the Rio Vidal who had just spent a whole day trying not to look at Agatha Harkness’s legs beneath a shiny red tuxedo jacket, the Rio Vidal who was sweating when she had to put her hand on said legs for the length of a photoshoot, that she would feel like she was able to breathe again because she had Agatha’s son in her arms, she’d have laughed in your face.

But here she was, breathing because Nicky was here, because he was wrapping himself so tightly around her that she knew without him even saying anything that she’d been missed.

“Where have you been?”

Rio’s easy breath caught in her throat at Nicky’s whisper and she stood stockstill in the middle of the park with him still clutching to her as she tried to find the right words to say.

“I had to go back home, mellizo. I’ve been working.”

“You said it was just a week. That New York was just a week and then you’d be back and you weren’t back you didn’t even say goodbye.”

Rio closed her eyes, feeling the rush of each of Nicky’s words as they hastened to catch up with his now quick breathing. His ribs contracted and expanded rapidly beneath her arms and she knew he was in the beginnings of a panic so she turned with him and walked him to the edge of the court where she could lower them both down.

It was testament to the work she’d put into her body since near-on destroying it after Miguel died by starving it that she could squat with Nicky and not falter as she deposited him gently onto the ground by the chain fence.

With her encouragement, he unwrapped his limbs from around her and clutched instead at her sweater as she brushed her thumbs across his soft cheeks.

A movement behind them made Rio turn briefly to catch the eye of Val, who looked concerned but was at least still giving them a few feet of distance. Rio turned back as little hands twisted in her collar and she felt the tug of the locket around her neck where Nicky had unknowingly caught it as he held tight.

His panic was slowly subsiding but his breathing wasn’t as easy as Rio would have liked so she touched his cheek again and whispered, “Tell me five things you can see.”

Nicky’s eyes widened a little and he looked to her before they darted around the quiet park about them.

“V-Val,” he said slowly, “a basketball, the hoop, a… mama’s security man, trees,” he looked back to her. “y-you.”

“Good,” Rio whispered, a smile tugging at her lips that was soon reflected in Nicky’s face. She settled more before him and slowly extracted his fingers from her sweater as she sat cross-legged and held his hands between them.

“You know your mama’s security guy is now my security guy? He’s keeping me safe. Just like Val keeps you safe and your mama keeps you safe and-...”

“And you keep me safe,” Nicky interrupted, swallowing visibly where he squeezed Rio’s hands. “Mama said even if you’re not with us you’re keeping us safe.”

“She did?”

Rio held her breath as Nicky nodded and smiled hopefully.

“But I’d feel safer if you came home.”

Rio could taste her own beating heart and saw a flash of something in her periphery. It made her turn to it but all she saw was Val watching them from nearby.

She cleared her throat and turned back around to wide eyes so like her own.

“How about,” she said slowly, squeezing Nicky’s fingers where she still held them. “We do this every week instead? We can meet in the park and-...”

“Did you fight with mama? Did… did you…?”

Nicky’s breathing had picked up and Rio dropped his hands to hold his face, “Hey. No. Not at all.”

Nicky nodded and Rio forced a small smile as she brushed her thumbs across his cheeks and just like his mom might he held on to her wrists.

“Your mom let me live with you for a while because I was really, really sad,” she lied, “I missed my dad and you and your mom made me feel happy again. So I moved back home but you and your mom, I…”

Nicky's gaze had dropped and Rio wondered if he was buying any of this at all.

“I love you both very much.”

“Families live together,” Nicky sniffled, “I don’t understand. Why did you leave us?”

Rio’s mouth moved to speak but no words came out and she instead faltered for them, unable to think of any utterance that might make this easier.

“Sweetheart,” Rio whispered, her thumbs moving as Nicky’s hands held tight to her still.

“I didn’t leave you. I just had to move back to my own home.”

“I thought our home was your home. I thought we were having fun and we danced every night and we watched movies and mama was so happy and now she’s not and it’s because you left us.”

For the first time in a long time Rio heard an accusation in Nicky’s tone. He’d looked up again and between her hands he looked so small and so precious that Rio again didn’t know what to say.

“I miss you. I want you to come back. Will you please come back?”

“I can’t, baby. I have to stay-,” but Nicky had pulled his head away and dropped his hold of Rio’s wrists. And Rio’s heart lurched with him as he pulled his knees to his chest and hid his face against them.

“I want you to come back! I want my mama to not look so sad and I want us to be tres patitos again.”

Rio glanced again to where Val was and noticed that she’d stepped closer. It was this, and the soft sounds of Nicky sniffing, that prevented her from simply walking away. Because walking away was what she wanted to do.

But she couldn’t abandon Nicky.

She couldn’t have Val call time and take him away from her.

“Te amo, mellizo. Lo siento.” I love you, mellizo. I’m sorry.

The duckling took flight. Nicky was back in her arms again and Rio gasped for the relief of it as she held him tight.

Rio didn’t need to look to know Val had backed away. She could just feel that she had. Just as she felt her heart rate return to normal and Nicky slowly relax against her.

“Every week?” He asked quietly after a while of silence.

“Every week. Just us. Just dos patitos.”

Nicky sniffed, a great big gross sniff, and Rio laughed for the first time in days without her head hurting as he pulled back and grinned sheepishly at her.

It was strange, she thought as Nicky wiped his nose with the back of his hand, what seeing her own smile was like on the face of someone else. Especially when she’d not seen her own smile for days now.

“Let’s get your nose clean and we can play some ball, yeah?”

Val was already offering Nicky’s backpack her way so Rio took it and as Nicky shuffled back she searched around until she found some tissues for him to blow his nose and wipe it properly.

“So gross,” Rio teased, making Nicky blush and giggle when she poked his side.

She stood up with him, the flower in her hand now squashed to an indiscernible nothing. But Nicky had taken the hand that held it and turned it over to see what was inside.

“Oh,” he whispered, a frown appearing where there had briefly been a smile. “Mama’s been holding hers too.”

Rio swallowed thickly. “She has?”

“The blue one. It looks better than this though. This one is…” Nicky poked the crumpled petals, “Did you squash it?”

“I don’t mean to.”

“It’s okay,” Nicky said as he looked up at Rio, “We can fix it maybe?”

Rio hesitated, her gaze drifting from Nicky to the flower she’d spent so much time on and now ruined in her desire to hold on tightly to Nicky.

“I think mama would like it even if it wasn’t fixed but…”

Rio looked up again and saw a twinkle of hope in Nicky’s eyes.

“Is it for mama?”

Too smart, she thought, too like his mom.

“Yes,” she admitted, closing her hold on Nicky’s hand now and crushing the flower completely to pull him back down to the ground with her. “And your mama deserves only the best flowers, right?”

“Only the best,” Nicky agreed, grinning again as he settled back against the fence.

He leant across to steal his bag and from it he took out a notepad and he proceeded to rip to sheets of paper from it, handing one to Rio.

“It’s okay if it has lines, right? She will still like it.”

Rio agreed and the project began. Project Make Agatha The Best Flower Ever. In the end, after a little chatter about basketball and school, after some help from Rio for Nicky’s flower, and some giggling when the thin paper kept ripping, they produced two perfect little striped roses.

They cheered together as they held them in their respective palms and compared them to the earlier, crumpled flower.

“She will love them all,” Nicky reassured, smiling Rio’s smile.

“Hey, you two,” came the voice of a person Rio had forgotten was there. “There’s snacks packed for you both. You should eat them.”

Rio looked up at the suggestion and raised her brows at a woman already pointedly raising her brows at her.

“Ooooh,” Nicky called, rummaging in his backpack. “I forgot! Snacks!”

He pulled out two small tupperwares. One blue, one green.

Rio accepted the green one and heard the rattle of its contents. Inside were purple skittles.

She choked on a gasp as she looked down at them all, and wondered if Agatha knew how much these tiny candies would mean to her. But of course she would. Agatha always knew.

Nicky had a trail mix concoction and they both settled back to eat their snacks and watch the birds that flew about the quiet park.

Rio’s hand was soon taken and her palm began to fill with raisins. She watched it happen for a while, the taste of artificial grape on her tongue.

“Aren’t raisins your favourite?”

“Yes,” Nicky shrugged, “But raisins are grapes and purple skittles are grape and I don’t have skittles to give you but I can give you my raisins.”

“Mellizo,” Rio whispered, touched by the logic of an eight year old boy, “You don’t need to give me your favourite snack.”

“Well,” Nicky reasoned, “I do love raisins. But I think I love you more so it’s okay.”

He placed another one in her palm and Rio glanced at the small mound before adjusting and moving to turn fully to Nicky.

“You give me them because your mom gives me her skittles?”

Nicky was staring into his snack pot, fishing around for more raisins to give.

“I give you them because you hold them for her and I think… I think my daddy wouldn’t. And it’s nice you hold them for me too.”

“Sweetheart,” Rio breathed out, the urge to cry taking over her thinking mind. “I am so happy to hold your raisins, and anything else you want to give me. But how about this? How about you still eat your delicious raisins and… if you ever have anything gross or anything your don’t want to eat, I’ll take that instead? That’s how it works with your mama’s skittles. I’ll always take away the bad thing for you, so you can enjoy the good thing, okay?”

Nicky considered this quietly for a while and eventually offered his pot up to Rio so she could pour the raisins back into it.

“She won’t be married soon, you know,” Nicky whispered as Rio finished the transfer.

“She won’t have a husband. Or a wife. And… you don’t have a wife. I think maybe that-…”

“Hey, buddy!” Val. Rio didn’t want to admit she’d just saved her from a complete meltdown. “Time to get going.”

Nicky, never not polite, did look like he might edge into impoliteness as his brow furrowed deeply and his cheeks became a ruddy colour.

“Hey,” Rio reassured, tipping the remainder of the skittles into her palm and placing the three little flowers into the pot instead. “Will you give these to your mom for me?”

Nicky’s frown softened as he took the box and Rio smiled at him as his fingers found the white scars still visible on Rio’s forearm, evidence she’d do whatever she could to keep them safe.

“Oh, wait,” she said quickly, pulling her arm away to remove her sweater leaving her in a grey tank top.

“And this is your mama’s,” she lied, folding it in her lap and then tucking it away in Nicky’s backpack. “Could you give it back to her?”

“Wait,” Nicky said quickly, as Val hovered nearby. He rummaged in the backpack and reached below Rio’s sweater to fish for something that turned out to be the very thing Rio expected.

“Mama wanted you to have this.”

Her cowboy shirt. Faded, but still vaguely pink. Rio just about managed to not press her nose into the collar of it to get a hit of Agatha’s perfume. Instead she held it in her hand and stood like any normal person might.

“I’ll walk you to the car?” She offered, mostly to Val, who was watching Nicky as he took Rio’s free hand and shouldered his bag.

As they walked Rio glanced around. There weren’t many people nearby but it made her feel so much more comfortable to know that Val, and her huge arms, was more than just a nanny.

When Nicky was deposited safely into his seat she leant in to kiss his cheek once, then twice.

“One for you and one for your mama.”

Nicky nodded, his smile fraying at the edges now as Rio ruffled his hair and closed the door. Something had happened as she’d been making sure Nicky was securely buckled in and she turned to see Val behind her, closer than she’d been all day.

“Your man’s there,” Val reassured when Rio had turned to check if anyone was guarding the driver’s side door.

As Rio turned back she found herself being pulling into a tight hug that she was not expecting.

"We're working on it.” Val’s English accent was crisp and felt unusual so close to her ear. “Nicky’s safer than he’s ever been. Agatha too. You’re doing the right thing. We’ve eyes on your mum, per Agatha’s request. She’s an elusive little bitch but we’ll catch her.”

Val’s whispered reassurance didn’t make Rio feel any better. Not when she was waving them goodbye. Not when she made her way home. Not when, the next day, she flew to Delaware to spend a few days in her parents’ home.

The first day was spent with her mom and her aunt, sitting silently as Alice contributed more to the conversation than she did.

In times like these, Rio neglected her Spanish even more than usual. Where Anna was concerned, Spanish would always be preferable. But Rio just couldn’t bring herself to do it.

So the house was filled with a strange Spanglish. Most of the English came from Rio, and most of the rest from everyone else.

The first day was the worst day. Because Rio reverted to somewhere between her sulky teenage tantrums and her more childlike need to be tended to.

It was this day where she had a fight so loud with Alice that Anna sent them both for a walk in opposite directions. Alice returned first, less angry. Rio returned next, crying.

After that, things settled.

Rio wasn’t getting even a hint of a headache by the Saturday night. She was eating fine, managed to play ball with Alice all day without any issues, even took some of her younger cousins out for food.

But, really, all she could think about was Agatha.

She tried to make the most of the relative peace she was getting by thinking of the future and how she could plan for a future where pain would be a distant memory. It was hard to do but she had two, solid, good things she could focus on: the car she’d promised to buy to keep Nicky safe, a place for them in London for when she was doing her play.

The thought of them, solid and expensive, helped.

On the third day of wearing her favourite cowboy shirt Anna insisted she take it off for her to wash.

“Oh, I wouldn’t even bother asking,” Alice drawled from her position behind her laptop on the floor.

“Es algo raro de perro.” It’s some weird dog thing.

“It is not some weird dog thing!”

“Scents,” Alice continued with a shrug and a smirk. “They like to sniff each other.”

“You’re making it sound weird,” Rio insisted, flopping down on the armchair behind Alice’s head.

“¡Ah! Tu padre solía olerme todo el tiempo cuando éramos jóvenes y estábamos enamorados. Asegúrate de oler bien. No quiero que mi tesoro tenga que oler tus axilas sudorosas.” Ah! Your dad used to sniff me all the time when we were young and in love. Just make sure you smell good. I don't want my treasure having to smell your sweaty armpits.

Alice laughed but went silent when Anna had left the room and Rio had reached down to take her hand.

Feeling as raw as she was, any mention of Miguel hurt double its usual amount. Alice pressed Rio’s hand to her cheek and held it there until Rio was willing to let go.

Their fights were bad but they were still those ally cats, their claws nonexistent.

It was on their final day in Delaware, a cold and rainy day for the month of May, when Rio was curled up on the couch watching a marathon of Agatha’s movies, that Alice found her way back into Rio’s good graces.

“You can have sex with anyone you want.”

“Alice.”

“But,” Alice insisted, holding her hand up to Rio. She sighed and took in a deep breath, “You can only sleep with one.”

Rio’s defenses fell. Her walls crumbled and her castle was stormed.

“She’s the one. Your one. I don’t like it. I don’t trust her. But I get it. I get it now.”

Rio shook her head and turned away from her friend, she returned her attention to the screen that now housed Agatha’s face. She was crying, the tears spilling from bright blue eyes that had once looked at Rio with nothing but unbridled love.

And Rio shook where she lay. She shivered enough that Alice pulled another throw over her.

“So dramatic when you’re not well,” she said. Rio just rolled her eyes and tugged the blankets tighter around her.

“Go away if you’re going to be mean.”

“No,” Alice said with a huff, squeezing her feet behind Rio where she lay in the fetal position on the opposite side of the couch. “I’ll stop being mean. I just want you to know I understand now. I… I’m trying to…”

Rio glanced at her friend and then looked back to the screen.

“You’re still mad,” Rio said quietly, “I get it.”

They were silent for a while as Agatha continued to live her life out on screen.

“If you asked me a year ago if this would be happening I’d have slapped your face.”

Rio grunted, “Me lying here with an Oscar but no dad, and no girlfriend?”

Alice shunted her with her legs.

“No, you watching a movie that isn’t a Spielberg classic.”

“So funny. Ever thought about taking your talents to the stage?”

Alice laughed and Rio tried to hide her smile.

“We do need to start thinking about London, you know. There’s already press around it. I’ve you on a podcast on Wednesday and they’re going to-…”

“Alice,” Rio said suddenly, sitting up for the first time in at least three hours. “I see Nicky Wednesday. You didn’t book it for-…?”

The answer was written all over Alice’s face. “Jesus, Alice.”

“You can see him next week.”

“Do you understand? Do you really? Because if you did you’d know that he-…!” But Rio couldn’t bring her to say because how could she say the son of the woman she couldn’t even speak to at the moment was her son too.

So she went silent. She bit down on the inside of her cheek until she was able to speak in a softer tone.

“Can you get a message to him? A promise I’ll be there next week?”

Alice was chewing on her lip, a bad habit she’d picked up from Rio years ago.

“I’ll text Jen, see if we can get Nicky there on Thursday.”

“I have therapy on Thursday,” Rio reminded, frowning where Alice was tapping at her phone.

“Saturday? You have to be on set in the morning but…”

She tapped some more and Rio held her breath.

“Saturday afternoon. You, Nicky, ice cream?”

Rio exhaled and flopped back onto the couch. She placed her hand on her forehead and stared up at the ceiling.

“You haven’t said her name,” she said, half tuned in to Agatha’s voice still sounding from the tv.

“What?”

“This whole time you haven’t said her name.”

Alice sighed heavily and wriggled where she sat.

“If you booked the podcast on my day with Nicky on purpose because you’re pissed at Agatha then-…”

“Fine. I did. I figured she doesn’t get to tell you to fuck off and use you as a babysitter at the same time.”

Rio’s jaw clenched so suddenly and so tightly that she could have easily broken it. She sat up using only her core to do so and gave Alice such a glare that her friend shrank an inch or two where she sat.

“Are you fucking kidding?”

Alice rolled her eyes in an attempt to dismiss the accusation in Rio’s tone.

“Look,” she started, her voice flat and letting a little of the exasperation in. “I was trying to-…”

“Alice if you suggest for one second that keeping Nicky away from me is protecting me I might actually kill you.”

Alice rolled her eyes again and this time it was enough to make Rio throw the blankets from her body and stand from the couch.

“Give me your phone.”

“What?”

“Now. Phone. Now.”

“No.”

“Alice.”

Alice fidgeted and then slapped her phone down in Rio’s hand.

Without thinking, without stopping for a second, she opened it with Alice’s passcode and went to Contacts. Right at the top: ‘Agatha 💩’..

Even the emoji couldn’t stop her. She pressed the name, then pressed to call.

Agatha answered on the second ring.

“Alice? Is she okay? What’s wrong?”

Her voice took Rio by surprise. She’d been listening to it all day and yet… it was different to hear it now, in her ear, full of fear and dread.

“Mi vida,” she breathed out, making Agatha gasp and release a soft “oh”.

It shouldn’t hurt to hear Agatha’s voice. It shouldn’t make her chest sting with a pain so close to the pain she felt when she heard about her dad.

It shouldn’t make her have to sit on the low coffee table for fear she’d fall otherwise.

“I miss you,” Rio managed to say. On the other end of the line she heard a door shut.

“You shouldn’t call,” Agatha uttered, a strange sharpness to her tone that formed into a dagger in Rio’s chest.

“I needed to… about Nicky… on Wednesday.”

Silence. Sharpness.

Rio held her hand to her heart.

“I can’t do this if you call.”

Agatha had taken a deep breath, the kind that Rio knew meant she was trying to steady herself.

The kind that meant the sharpness was a front.

“Please, my love, I don’t think I can… I miss you. I want you here. And I know if I ask you to come you will and I can’t, I can’t ask you because…”

“Because Nicky comes first,” Rio whispered, closing her eyes as the pain in her chest increased now that Agatha was crying on the other end of the line.

“I loved my flowers,” Agatha said quietly, and Rio imagined her saying it into her ear, breathing it against her skin.

“I’ll make you more.”

“How did you squash the first one?”

“Nicky ran at me.”

“He misses you.”

“He said you’re not dancing?”

“How can I?”

Rio squeezed her eyes closed, her hand fisting the fabric of her thin shirt.

“If I teach him some new moves, maybe you’ll have to.”

Agatha released a short laugh and then sniffed softly, much more delicately than her son might.

“Robot or nothing.”

“Robot it is.”

“So I have to wait until Saturday to get my shirt?”

Rio exhaled slowly, twisting the fabric above her heart.

“Are you sleeping?”

“Not well.”

“Maybe I… maybe I can get Jen more shirts or more-...”

“My love,” Agatha said in a tone that was so soft Rio almost felt the breath of it, “I don’t need your shirts. I need you. I need…”

Rio hadn’t realised she was crying until she felt her mom’s hand on her shoulder and her voice saying, “Dile que la amas.” Tell her you love her.

And so Rio did.

She took a deep breath and heard Agatha do the same. And for a second they were suspended in time together, caught between the pain of now and the hope for their future.

“I love you. I miss you. I can’t wait to be with you again.”

Agatha said nothing for a while, and Rio could only wait.

“Thank you for being there for Nicky.”

“Agatha.”

“I…,” Agatha started, a soft sob giving her away. “I love you.”

Her mom took the phone then and Rio immediately dug the heels of her hands into her eyes. She couldn’t watch her mom take Agatha away from her so she didn’t. Anna walked out of the room with it, quickly and quietly, already whispering: “Ambos superarán esto. Lo prometo.” You will both get through this. I promise.

Rio inhaled sharply, the oxygen she needed to live burned her throat like her body was trying to reject it.

But she had to breathe. She had to get through this.

A hand found her knee and she took several more shuddering breaths before she spoke again.

“You can’t take your anger at Agatha out on Nicky. It’s not… it’s not… he’s just a kid. He deserves-…”

“I know,” Alice said quietly, “I’m sorry. I’m just… I want to strangle her.”

Rio scoffed and let her hands fall into her lap. She rubbed at her thighs; a slow, heavy, rhythmic push.

“I can’t fucking believe this is happening.”

“I know,” Alice whispered, unhelpful, but well-meaning.

Rio raised her gaze to Alice, momentarily stopping the movement of her hands. Her thighs already felt raw from the assault anyway.

Alice glanced at her stationery hands and then met her gaze.

“If it was Jen,” Rio said. “If it was Jen, how would you… how would you feel?”

She swallowed as Alice looked away again and removed her hand from her knee.

“Do you want to know everything that’s been happening?”

It was so unexpected that Rio made an effort to speak but somehow choked on whatever word she was trying to say. So she nodded instead.

Alice sighed and ran a hand through her hair, sending the feathered red fluttering back down as fierce as a flame.

“Where do you want to-…?”

“Is she sleeping?” Rio rushed out. She felt like she’d taken ten caffeine pills with how alert she suddenly was.

Her fingers tingled where they clutched the sleep shorts she’d slept in, and then worn all day. Her eyes were so wide that if Alice had the courage to look around at her she might have laughed.

And perhaps if she’d have listened hard enough she’d have heard the thwack, thwack, thwack of Rio metaphorical tail whacking the coffee table where she sat.

“No. She’s refusing pills entirely. But she’s dosing herself on CBD during the day. Jen says she’s checked a couple times and found her asleep around four for a couple hours before her call time. When she’s in her trailer… she occasionally naps but…”

Alice looked then. She did not laugh.

“She’ll get sick,” Rio said quietly.

“She’s agreed with Jen that if she doesn’t get eight hours by Friday she’ll take a pill.”

Rio nodded and looked down at where she’d been tugging at a loose thread on her shorts.

“Ralph?”

“Calling every day, multiple times.”

Rio bit down on her tongue.

“She can’t block him because it could look like she’s blocking him from Nicky. At least that’s what her lawyers say.”

“Fuck,” Rio snarled. “The pictures? Has he said anything about them? Have they heard anything about the bitch redhead?”

“No. Nothing at all.”

“Has he tried to see Nicky?”

“Not yet. But he’s within his rights if he wants to.”

Rio shook her head, “So he’s just harassing her.”

“He’s chosen court, rather than mediation.”

Rio shook her head again, staring at the couch cushion in front of her.

“Rio, the California system prefers joint custody.”

“He can’t get Nicky. He doesn’t want Nicky. He doesn’t love Nicky.”

Alice didn’t say anything in response.

“When will they be in court?”

“A couple weeks.”

Rio nodded this time, that strange sharpness in her chest.

“The shit emoji is juvenile, by the way.”

Alice again said nothing and Rio looked up at her.

“I want to talk to you about London.”

“Good,” Alice answered, suddenly all business as she slapped her thighs. “We have some prep to do for the podcast anyway and-…”

“No,” Rio interjected. “Not work stuff. Personal stuff. I want you to help me find somewhere to live.”

“Right, I’ve already got a couple options for rentals and-…”

“Alice,” Rio interrupted again, fisting at the fabric of her shorts. “Listen to me. I want to find a place for the three of us. Somewhere near a good school and a park. Somewhere we can-…”

She watched her best friend deflate and felt her own chest swell in anticipation for an argument.

But it didn’t come.

Alice just looked away, her jaw tight.

“Right, okay. Fine. I can put feelers out and-…”

“No,” Rio said quickly, “I want to make sure it’s the best. When we’ve wrapped I’m going to fly out, with or without you, and go see where would be best for us. I want her to know I’m still planning a life for us. That I will keep away but I won’t stop wanting her.”

Alice sighed and ran a hand through her hair, “Fine. Whatever you want. I’m just glad you’re still doing it.”

Rio threw herself onto her back again and tuned Alice out to focus on on Agatha on her screen. She was about Rio’s age here, and Rio knew it was the movie she was filming in Chicago the night they first met.

Maybe they’d already met by the time this scene was shot. Maybe Agatha was thinking about Rio as she smiled at this man like she loved him.

Maybe she’d never smile at Rio like that again.

By the time Anna returned with news that Agatha was okay, she was working hard with her lawyers and thinking only about Nicky and Rio, Rio was feeling a little calmer than before.

It was like her brain relaxed just from seeing Agatha. Just knowing she was alive and not some figment of her cruel imagination seemed to calm her whole nervous system.

By the time Rio and Alice left Delaware late on the Tuesday, Rio was feeling significantly less calm again.

Flying home meant set the next day. And set the next day meant seeing Agatha but not seeing her properly. She’d have to be professional if she even saw her at all.

It turned out she didn’t. She had just some seems with James. They were filler scenes, scenes shot with little to no dialogue of a busy and loving mom cooking with her wild and crazy son.

But in getting through those scenes she had time enough to prep for the podcast Alice had forced on her.

It was late evening by the time Rio made it to the small studio in downtown LA. The podcast was to be filmed so she had to have a wardrobe change and makeup slapped on her, if only to cover the bags.

She had opted for a plain white t-shirt and a pair of light jeans. Nothing flashy, nothing that screamed movie star or Oscar winner. But nothing that screamed heartbroken loser, either.

Alice had done her one favour; she’d brought with her the emerald necklace Agatha had given her for Christmas. And Rio wore it now, proudly placing it over the collar of her t-shirt so it would be on display the whole time. Beneath it, just for her, lay her locket. The world didn’t need to see it. She just needed to feel it, warm and heavy against her breastbone. Reminders of her family, of why she was in so much pain and of how good it would be when they were together again.

The other thing she had, but hadn’t needed to be given, was her Baby-G watch, exactly like Nicky’s, green and white and obnoxious on her wrist.

The host of the podcast was a friendly comedian Rio had worked with before. She was someone Rio had dinner with occasionally. Someone Rio had once played basketball with her young sons. So she wasn’t nervous, she wasn’t much of anything, actually.

The concept was simple: a few questions, but mostly talking. And Rio had to talk a bit about her upcoming play. The play was the most important part, but a request had come through from Jen, via Alice. And, Rio assumed but hated to think of, probably originating from Agatha.

“If Rio could mention that she’s single,” Alice had quoted Jen, “that would be great.”

Rio hadn’t even reacted to these words as she sat in the makeup chair and allowed someone to put blush on her cheeks.

“I’ve not vetoed the romance questions so,” Alice trailed off, seeing Rio’s defeated expression. “You’ve got this, babe.”

A couple hours then she would be home.

The conversation started easily and went well. And Rio found it was easy to be charming when the person you were with wanted to be charmed. So they riffed and they bantered and it was so simple that Rio almost forgot about her own heartbreak.

She even managed to speak about Snow for a while, and mentioned how much she was enjoying working with Agatha, without feeling like she wanted to throw herself off of something very tall.

She talked about the play in London, about how excited she was to tread the boards of the West End. She even did a shoddy English accent that she knew would be clipped online.

But then the question she’d been dreading landed and she had to hold steady.

“Have you ever been in love, Rio?”

Alice had warned her. Alice had prepped her. She was media trained, she was a natural raconteur. She was Miguel Vidal’s beloved daughter.

So she handled it.

“No,” she lied, not easily, but well. “Come close but, no, never. What is love? Baby, don’t hurt me.”

The host, her old friend, laughed, and Rio knew she’d already got away with it.

People were interested in her dating life, they always had been. She’d never come out like some actors had to. She’d always just been out. She’d always kissed who she happened to be kissing and if the paps got a shot well, they got a shot.

It hadn’t even been a discussion between herself and Alice because Alice would never put boundaries on her friend in that way and Rio don’t think it was a necessary conversation to have.

She was a lesbian who dated who she wanted to date and who slept with anyone she wanted.

She’d dated famous women and non-famous women. But she’d never been in love.

Not until now.

Until it hurt every time she thought about the person she was in love with. Until she couldn’t be with the person she was in love with.

“I’m sure so many women would be more than willing to try and change that.”

In a version of the person she used to be, Rio leant back in her chair, and held her arms out, “Well, c’mon, ladies. I’m available.”

The second the words slipped from her lips she hated herself for them. But she laughed through it and endured the sting of her chest as she played it off like it was some joke between friends.

Maybe a year ago it would have been. Today it was torture of her own creation.

“An invitation if ever I heard one!”

The host was laughing, Rio was laughing. The producers and sound engineers were laughing. Was Alice laughing?

“Listen!” Rio chimed in, shrugging in her best impression of a chill guy. And she nailed it because she used to be a chill guy. “Maybe I should put out an ad in those lonely hearts columns. Do we still have those?”

“Wanted: woman willing to date a movie star and go to occasional basketball games.”

“No no,” Rio protested, “Basketball games optional.”

“Okay, so what else? Tall, short, blonde, brunette, redhead?”

Rio laughed and shrugged again, “I have no preference.”

“Alright, alright, let’s move on before our socials are filled with applications to be your girlfriend.”

Rio laughed again but could feel the strain on her chest as she did. She was able to fake her way through the rest of the interview. She smiled and laughed and charmed.

And when she left, she collapsed into the back of the car and fished her locket out from beneath her shirt.

“Agatha wanted that?” she asked Alice as they drove in the direction of Rio’s house.

“I don't think she wanted it, Rio.”

“This is bullshit. It’s such bullshit.”

Rio thumped the door beside her and threw her head back at the same time. Her discomfort had curdled to rage and she had no real outlet for it.

“He’s a piece of shit.”

Rio’s head whipped round to Alice and she stared openly at her friend.

“Has he done something? Has he…?”

“No, just… he’s a piece of shit.”

Rio scoffed and turned to look out the window. She was still angry, still furious in fact.

“I miss her.”

Because she couldn’t do anything she started to press buttons on her watch, enjoying the infuriating sound of the chirps and cheeps it made.

“I know. Rio,” Alice said, reaching to make her friend stop the incessant noise. “You were great, trust me. People will go wild for it. And it’ll help. Anything to make out that you’re fine, you’re normal, is good.”

Rio turned to look out the window and thought of nothing but Agatha for the rest of the night.

The next morning was no different. And the morning after that, and after that. Her days all rolled into one at a certain point. The only things that broke them up were her exercise routine, her work, getting any news from Alice about Agatha that she could.

Agatha was fine.

Agatha was sleeping.

Agatha was fine.

Rio didn’t believe it. A small part of her wanted Agatha to be as crushed as she felt but the rest of her, everything but her ego, wanted Agatha to feel strong, to feel safe, to feel like she could and would win this war and neither Evanora nor Ralph would ever, ever get their claws into Nicky.

She thought a lot about Nicky too. She thought about him whenever she saw James on set. She thought about him when she put her watch back on at the end of the day. She thought about him when she touched her locket.

She thought about him when she went to the car dealership and bought her green Lexus, and when she drove it home and presented it to Alice like something to be proud of.

And she was proud of it. She was proud of it because it was the first real decision that made her feel like she could be a good mom, and a good wife.

And when Saturday arrived, Rio rocked up to the ice cream parlour excited to tell Nicky all about her new purchase.

Nicky was already there, sandwiched between Val and the wall, his eyes wide and expectant and searching for Rio.

And relief washed over her as his face broke out into a grin identical to the one she now wore. She charged over to him and Val knew well enough to slip out of the way so Rio could slide into the booth and attack Nicky with cheek kisses and side tickles.

Something about having missed each other for over a week now meant that neither Rio nor Nicky paused for breath. They each got chocolate sundaes and kept stealing from the others even as they ate the same mountain of ice cream.

They talked about school, about Nicky’s friends, about his latest A+ on his history project, about his basketball team. They talked about Celtics and what snacks Rio was sneaking onto set to eat between takes (chocolate peanuts and gummy worms), they talked about Rio’s new green car and how maybe they could take a road trip in it. They talked about everything and anything until the subject of Agatha came up and Rio remembered her promise.

In fact, she remembered her two promises. She first handed over her cowboy shirt, neatly folded, to Val. She then handed Nicky a new little rose, green this time, and asked him to keep it safe for his mom.

But then there was the third promise. Crucial, and one she hadn’t been able to prep for.

And so, in a neon booth in the middle of an ice cream parlour in LA, Nicky learnt how to do the robot. He wasn’t great at it, but he was enthusiastic. Even when Rio pointed out that no robot she knew giggled. And Nicky pointed out that she didn’t know any robots.

But it was for Agatha. It was so Agatha would dance with her son even when Rio wasn’t there to encourage it.

They stayed for two hours, and only left because Val informed them they had company and needed to leave. Rio had been so focused on Nicky she’d not noticed their fellow patrons ogling them.

A feeling a lot like brain freeze came over her as Val instructed Nicky to please climb over Rio and come take her hand.

“No. I want to hold Rio’s.”

“Nicky,” Val said gently, “It’s getting busy and you need to come with me, okay? I promise we’ll be fine. Rio will be right behind us.”

When Nicky didn’t look convinced Rio turned to the babysitter and looked her over. She wasn’t as tall as Rio but she was definitely, visibly stronger. And she had a look on her face that told her no one would be getting anywhere near Nicky if she could do anything about it.

“The car’s outside?”

“Right out front, yeah. Made sure of it. Thought this might bloody happen.”

Rio nodded once and cleared her throat as she slapped a twenty on the table.

“He’ll be safe on my back, he has his cap. He can hide his face and I can put him in the car.”

“That’s not protocol.”

“That’s how we do it,” Rio said with finality, and to prove a point she stood from the booth and bent to allow Nicky to climb onto her back and hold her as tightly around her neck as ever.

She felt better about the whole thing the moment Nicky clung to her. Agatha trusted her with him. Agatha knew her son was safe with her.

She would always, always keep him safe.

Val looked pissed but said nothing and instead placed Nicky’s cap on his head.

“I’ve got him,” Rio said quietly, aware that Val had been hired specifically so she could keep Nicky safe. But that was her job too.

“You’ve got me, melliza,” Nicky whispered close to her ear and Rio squeezed his legs as Val nodded once and led the way outside.

It was carnage. There were over a dozen men with huge cameras and a crowd of onlookers who weren’t helping the situation.

The moment Rio stepped outside the crowd roared with recognition and Rio winced as Val reached back and grabbed her shirt to keep her close. She could barely breathe because Nicky was squeezing the life out of her but she kept placing one foot in front of another, determined to get Nicky tucked away as quickly as possible.

As Nicky clung to her she had to angle her head so he could hide his own against her with his cap still on. Val was calm and steady and Rio was glad she was there.

She was gladder still the even bigger guy who’d been hired to shadow her was there to force some of the keener paps back.

Val forged a path for them to the black SUV that waited for them and opened the door so Rio could turn to the side and deposit Nicky on the seat.

But he wouldn’t let go.

Rio stood and struggled with him for all of five seconds before she gave up and heaved them both into the car. Val slammed the door and the tumult was lessened, but they could still see the flashes and hear the shouts of their names.

“Nicky, you have to sit properly. You have to go with Val. I’m going to slip out of-…”

“No! Stay! Keep us safe! Come home with me!”

Val was in the front now and Rio didn't have long. She manoeuvred Nicky into his seat and avoided his clutching arms to put his belt on.

He pleaded some more but Rio kissed his cheek and held his face in her hands.

“I love you. You’re safe with Val. Tell your mama she has to dance the robot tonight, okay?”

Nicky sniffed but refused to cry and rubbed at his eyes as if he could force the tears back inside.

Rio couldn’t watch anymore. She slipped out of the car on the roadside and walked to her own car, aided by Agatha’s bodyguard who protected her every step.

When she got home she called Alice and asked her to find out one thing for her.

Alice called back at midnight when Rio was already in bed.

“She danced with him.”

Rio fell asleep with the image of Nicky giggling as he tried to make his body follow her robot movements. She imagined Agatha snort-laughing at the sight. She imagined carrying Nicky to bed and then snuggling on the couch with Agatha.

When she woke the next morning, her head hurt.

Agatha was visible on set more the next week. Rio was even in scenes with her. But they didn’t speak except to read lines when the cameras were rolling.

Agatha approached her each time with a practiced coldness. She treated Rio no differently to how she treated everyone else on set. Apart from Lilia. She was softer with Lilia.

But Rio wasn’t used to the cold. She hadn’t prepped for it, didn’t have the necessary protection from it, and so suffered for it.

It hurt every time Agatha nodded her greeting at her but wouldn’t look her in the eye. It hurt worse when she’d been with Nicky on the basketball court the night before and he’d asked her to come home to cheer up his mama. It hurt worse because Agatha always packed her purple skittles in his backpack and Rio always delivered her a little, handmade flower.

But day after day she was met with the same, changed Agatha.

Her logical mind knew that Agatha was trying to put up a front to the outside world. She also knew she was trying to protect herself. But knowing didn’t help because she couldn’t get her brain to tell her heart.

Two weeks of it. Two weeks of acting with Agatha, pretending to be her wife when Maria yelled action, and then acting as if strangers when she yelled cut.

It tore her up. It made the headaches worse and a constant heartburn impact her day to day.

But the only way out was through.

So she put on a brave face. She had to pretend she wasn’t constantly furious and constantly hurting. She entertained and reassured Nicky when she saw him. She continued her grief counseling. She started working out with Val, deciding she wanted to be stronger, visibly more capable of protecting Agatha and her son.

She started doing more yoga to quiet her mind.

She did everything she could to not break down about the sort of break up.

But the big, emotional scenes were coming up as the filming came to an end. Rio had to be present for Agatha in them as much as she had to do a good job for herself.

And so the day before one of the first as her time of set began to run out and the day of wrap came closer and closer, Rio spent as much time as possible working on breath work on her yoga mat to try and calm her nervous system down.

She would have to be in bed with Agatha, she would have to kiss and hold Agatha and tell her she loved her.

All normal and easy things to do. Just not when Agatha hadn’t looked at her properly in weeks now. Not when Rio couldn’t even hold her hand in real life.

But she was prepping, just as she was starting to prep for the life they were to have together.

So she would be ready. So that she was ready.

Rio stepped onto an unexpectedly quiet set and made eyes at the First AD as if to ask: “what the fuck?”.

As if to answer, he shuffled over and leant in close to whisper in Rio’s ear, “Agatha asked for a closed and quiet set. She’s been here for about thirty minutes.”

Rio glanced around as if she’d appear from nowhere.

“No,” the crew member insisted, and Rio turned to look at him, raising her brows expectantly, “She’s in position.”

Rio didn’t quite register what he meant for a second but then followed the line of his arm as he pointed to the little bedroom set and Rio saw, all lit properly already for the scene in the faux-dim light of a bedroom at nighttime, Agatha, lying still in the middle of the bed with James, the child actor playing their son.

It didn’t look real for a second, this vision of Agatha lying in bed with a little boy clearly asleep before her.

It looked too perfect, too like it could be her own bedroom, and her own child and Agatha waiting for her.

Or Nicky. Agatha and Nicky curled up together after a long day, both too tired to wait up for Rio, but both leaving her enough room to curl in with them when she finally arrived.

It hurt to look at.

“We’re going from you getting into the bed,” a soft voice came from near her, Maria’s voice.

“James is asleep,” she explained needlessly, as Rio kept her gaze on Agatha who had turned her head slightly to look at Rio.

“I don’t know how she managed it but… we’re going to try and get the scene whilst he is, okay? I think we can nail it in a couple takes. We can get the other shots without him later.”

Rio only nodded, dropping her gaze from Agatha as she focused on the lines she needed to recite and stole the attention of the script supervisor to get him to lean over so she could check exactly where they’d be going from.

She read over the scene just once and then agreed to start.

As she approached the bed, she saw that James was still sound asleep, curled towards Agatha and breathing softly.

But it wasn’t James she was focused on. Agatha looked calm, and Rio’d guessed she might have been the one to lull James to sleep but she couldn’t ask the question, couldn’t figure out Agatha’s tricks of the trade when she had to do her job, and had to do it well so the gift of a sleeping child actor wouldn’t go to waste.

“Action,” the director whispered across the set.

Rio moved seamlessly, easily embodying the character of a woman returning to her wife and child.

She circled to the end of the bed where she stopped and whispered, “He’s nice like this.”

Agatha hummed, low, deliberate, faking sleepy as she blinked slowly.

“Too like his mama to be nice when awake.”

Rio rolled her eyes, but her smile was there too, the picture of a happy wife and mother.

She moved to the edge of the bed and began to peel back the sheets.

“Room for one more?”

“You’ll wake him,” Agatha responded quietly, a pale hand moving to brush back some of James’ hair.

Rio’s chest hurt seeing her like this.

She slid into the bed and leant up on her elbow behind Agatha’s head. Her hand slipped below the sheets and rested respectfully on Agatha’s arm.

Hidden from view, she felt Agatha press her body back a little into her. They were wives, after all.

Rio let Agatha settle her hand back down again, let the scene, and themselves breathe for a second before she whispered, “You okay?”

Agatha shifted again and Rio felt her body press back closer into her own. Her hand slid to her hip and she squeezed it as her heart constricted in her chest.

“It’s been a long day,” Agatha whispered.

Around them the booms dipped down and Rio knew they were checking levels behind the monitors.

The hand on Agatha’s hip had a new job now. It had to move up, and per the stage directions, it had to tuck Agatha’s hair behind her ear.

A miraculous thing, to be able to do something like this, something so simple and intimate with the woman she’d done so many intimate things with already.

The pain in her chest swelled to bursting point as her finger brushed the soft skin of Agatha’s cheekbone, and ghosted around the shell of her ear.

“We should have another,” she whispered, mesmerised by the feel of Agatha against her.
And then Agatha turned as much as she could without jostling James and the light hit her eyes just so. She was breathtaking, this actress, this woman.
And Rio, for too short and too happy a time, had been lucky enough to call her ‘mine’.
For a second they looked, a beat really. A beat that could be emphasised by the editor, or cut entirely. But this wasn’t for the movie; it was for them alone.
And then, Agatha’s lips parted, a soft gasp.
Rio couldn’t believe they were this close again. Close enough to count Agatha’s freckles, to see the exact hue of her ocean eyes.
“You want another baby with me?”
Yes. Desperately.
“Well, this bed can fit at least another two, don’t you think?”
She said her line with a crooked smile, one that made Agatha’s eyes drop to her lips and her own to curl into a smile as well. But hers was less crooked, much warmer.
Rio knew that smile. It was a real smile.
After all this time, she’d made Agatha smile.
“Two?” She asked, her brow twitching with the question she’d asked.
Rio shrugged, playing it as cool as she could when Agatha was this close and this warm.
“You don’t want to be outnumbered by crazy kids?”
Agatha, following stage directions, Rio knew, was careful about lifting her arm out from below the sheets and held Rio’s face in a way that made Rio’s pain dissipate immediately.
“Only,” she whispered, her lips twitching as she did. She moved her hand so her thumb could brush Rio’s lips and without having to think, Rio kissed it as it passed over them. “Only,” she repeated, her eyes darting across Rio’s face, “If they look like you.”
She had to kiss her now. It was in the stage directions to kiss Kate. And Rio hesitated, she took a beat, and as she was about to lean in, she heard Maria again: “Cut.”
The word was soft, but the set was so empty, so small and so silent, that it couldn’t be mistaken.

“Rio.”

Rio pulled back up and turned her head to the director, careful not to move too much or make any sudden noises for fear of waking James. Agatha’s hand slipped from her jaw.

“I’m sorry. I forgot to tell you. We cut the kiss.”

Rio’s heart had been in her mouth and now it had shrunk several sizes, slipping back down her throat until it settled uncomfortably in her stomach.

She felt Agatha shift a little beneath the covers but could only nod, only acknowledge that she’d heard the instruction but not question why.

It was then she saw her, sitting behind one of the monitors with a set of headphones. Pepper.

Their intimacy now was nonexistent so whenever it did exist it had to be coordinated. Of course it did.

There was once a time Agatha went off into a rage at the mere idea that someone would tell her how and when she could touch Rio.

And now she was allowing it. Now she was perhaps asking for it.

“From ‘if they look like you’. Okay? Action.”

Rio shifted back a little, waiting for Agatha’s line read.

But she couldn’t shake the sinking feeling in her stomach.
“Only,” Agatha said quietly, “Only if they look like you.”

But something changed. The way the line was read the first time was gentle, teasing. The way it was read now was an invitation.

Agatha’s thumb had grazed Rio’s lips again but had stopped in the middle of her lower one and tugged it down to expose her row of bottom teeth.

Her blue eyes were focused on where her thumb was and Rio squeezed Agatha’s hip in question before she answered it for herself.

They kissed and no one stopped them. They kissed and Rio felt whole again, felt normal. The pain disappeared and all was Agatha.

Agatha kissed her back.

Agatha’s hand held her in place and it was just two people in love kissing. A chaste kiss. It had to be chaste. They had a sleeping child in the bed with them. They had cameras pointing at them from every direction.

They’d been told not to kiss.

Rio pulled back and opened her eyes to gaze down at the woman before her. Agatha’s eyes were closed. Her lips were parted. She’d never looked more beautiful.

Rio hesitated. There was nothing else to do but stare, but admire, but gaze.
