“I love you,” Rio whispered, the character’s line, but her own too.

She hadn’t been able to say it in so long.

Before Agatha could respond she leant in again and nudged their noses together. They kissed again and Agatha’s hand moved below the sheets and found her own to tangle their fingers.
She was holding her through the kiss, making sure she knew it was okay.

They’d held each other like this the time they’d met at the roundtable. Or, more accurately, the second time they’d met.

Rio’s fingers had been held by Agatha. She’d been trying to tell her something then, and she was trying to tell her something now.

And then she said the thing she was trying to tell her.

“Yo también te amo, cariño.” I love you too, honey.

Rio smiled and, per the script this time, she kissed Agatha again. And then, her lips tingling, all she had to do was settle down behind Agatha as Agatha turned back to the sleeping James.

Agatha’s hair was up in a purposefully messy bun piled on top of her head. It meant Rio had access. It meant her whole body vibrated because she could smell Agatha’s skin. She let her nose caress the softness of the space behind Agatha’s ear.

And Agatha held her hand tighter below the sheets. She pressed back into her.
She was allowing it, she was encouraging it.

Agatha missed her and Rio adored her.

“We should talk about your mom,” Rio breathed, and Agatha shivered for her breath against her neck.

“There’s nothing to talk about.”

Agatha’s voice was low, thick with sleep, and Rio craved more of it. She wanted to hear Agatha’s soft voice in her ear as she lay against her, fighting sleep just so she could talk to Rio for a little longer.

But this was a scene still. This was a small part of a movie. And this wasn’t real. Rio couldn’t hold Agatha like this anymore.

She hummed, and moved their hands from Agatha’s hip to her stomach. She’d moved back from James now. She was properly, gloriously, pressed back against Rio.

“So… this baby thing?”

Rio had to keep it light. She had to be teasing her wife, not lamenting the fact that she might never have a baby with Agatha.

And then Agatha did something miraculous. She released her hold and pressed down on Rio’s hand so her fingers could spread.

Rio now held her where a baby might grow, where Agatha could give them another baby with Rio’s face and Agatha’s heart.

And so, with Agatha’s hand holding Rio’s in place against her stomach, she laughed. It was soft, fake, but somehow so genuine to Rio’s ear.

“Can we talk about it once we’re back home?”

Rio hoped they would, she hoped they could.
She hummed again, forcing a small smile as she nuzzled into Agatha and then said: “Mm’kay. Until then I’ll just think about you all cute,” she kissed behind her ear, “and soft,” she kissed the corner of her jaw, “and pregnant,” she kissed her neck.

Agatha’s hand had curled around Rio’s wedding finger and Rio had to try her hardest not to look how she felt because she felt like she might cry.

“Call me soft again and you’re not getting a-…”

Rio had to react and did so well.

“Hot and beautiful,” she interjected.

Agatha began to shift and Rio was easily able to allow it, moving back and up to be able to look down at her.

Agatha’s cheeks were pinker than they had been earlier and Rio was thrilled she’d opted for not a ‘no make up look’ but actually no makeup.

She was beautiful however she came, however little or much, makeup she wore. But never more beautiful than with no makeup at all and when she was looking at Rio with eyes like this, so soft and so open.

“Do you think Evan was right?”

Rio should have moved her hand to Agatha’s face but she couldn’t bring herself to remove her hand from her stomach. Because touching Agatha there, holding her there, was just for them.
“No, mi alma,” she whispered, gifting Agatha’s character a soft name she often reserved for Agatha. But she couldn’t have ‘mi vida’, that was private. That was theirs.

Agatha reached for her and Rio leant into her touch. She smiled slightly, enjoying the feel of Agatha’s warm palm.

“No, babe. He’s just bitter because he’s a divorced prick stuck in-…”

“I’m serious.”

Rio nodded gently, careful not to dislodge Agatha’s hold. She brushed her thumb over the skin of her stomach.

“So am I. You’re the best mom and an amazing daughter.”

Agatha was looking at her the way she used to be able to in the privacy of Agatha’s house, on the couch, in the kitchen, in their bedroom. She was giving her best and worst performance to date.

Because this wasn’t acting, this was Agatha and Rio. This was them. This was how they should be, curled up together with Nicky asleep beside them.

“And wife?”

Rio wanted to cry. Instead she smiled. She grinned.

Agatha adjusted her gaze, she made her brow raise. Her lips twitched.

“My wife is the best wife in the world. And we’ll get through these next few days together, okay?”

Please, Rio thought as Agatha’s eyes darted about her own face and Rio reluctantly moved her hand from Agatha’s stomach to hold the hand that held her face.

She turned and kissed Agatha’s palm where she held her hand.

“No podría hacerlo sin ti.” I couldn’t do it without you.

Rio breathed out quietly, holding back a louder gasp. She knew the lines, she knew that in the table read Agatha had changed some of them to Spanish. But now, now they meant more. So much more.

All that was left to do was to kiss Agatha, and so she did. She kissed her slower, opening her mouth just enough to envelop Agatha’s lower lip.

But against Agatha’s cheek she felt a tear. It had been scripted but Rio knew it was real.
When they broke apart this time Rio couldn’t pull away. She kissed Agatha again, a much softer one. She nuzzled into her and then kissed her cheek and barely moved away as Agatha turned back around and Rio’s hand tucked around her ribs where she held her against her and Agatha pressed back.

She knew what was coming, and Agatha did too. But she let the moment hold. She let Rio hold her. She let Rio hold her tightly, fiercely, properly. She’d pressed herself back again and as Rio was thinking about how their bodies just fit together her mouth said the lines: “Te adoro. Adoro lo que tenemos.” I adore you. I adore what we have.

Rio pressed in, she inhaled Agatha. God, she missed her. She missed her feel and her smell and…

“Cut. Great job guys. Pepper, can we consult on the kissing? All quiet, please. James is still out.”

Rio didn’t move. Agatha was holding her hand again. She’d pulled it from where it had tucked beneath her and cradled her ribs.

She moved their hands slowly to rest on Agatha’s sternum and Rio wished they were alone. She wished she could feel more of Agatha. She wished she could make her turn around so she could kiss her again, and then she wished she could cradle her against her as Agatha slept and she held her through the night.

“Ladies,” Pepper’s voice somewhere behind them.

Rio turned slowly and her hold on Agatha dropped. She pulled her hand from underneath her shirt and threw her arm above her head.

Agatha moved more cautiously, being closer to James, but managed to turn to her side to face Rio.

Rio felt her hand slip below her shirt and rest on her stomach. She felt Agatha’s fingers explore her skin as if they actually were alone and she had to do her best to focus on the two women talking softly above her.

“The kissing, it’s good but…” Maria.

“It was agreed it would be taken out. We need to make sure that-,” Pepper started.

Agatha finished. “I’m fine with it.” Rio felt her nails against her stomach. “We don’t need to discuss it. Did you get the shots? If you keep talking we won’t get another take before James wakes up. So let us do our job and go sit over there getting paid to think about two strangers kissing.”

Rio arched a brow and tried to pretend like Agatha’s hand wasn’t making slow moves up to settle below her breast, curling around her heart.

Maria and Pepper were looking at one another and Rio watched them for a while as Agatha’s thumb stroked her skin.

If only they knew how she was being touched right now, they’d never have any concerns about whether or not the kissing was okay.

“Positions, everyone,” Maria said quietly but authoritatively.

The two women moved away without looking back and Rio turned to Agatha and raised her brows. Agatha didn’t look her way but squeezed her ribs and then was slow about turning around.

Rio made herself decent again and waited to be told where they were going from. Turned out Maria wanted her to take it from the top. So she did.

They went through the motions, read their lines, and as much as they could they held each other. They kissed in every place they’d kissed before and Rio nuzzled, she held, she cherished.

They ran it for the third time. But this time, James woke up.

It was the breaking of the spell.

James had dived over Agatha once he realised Rio was there and suddenly Rio wasn’t holding Agatha but instead wrestling a five year old.

Only when he was taken away by his mom could they go back to it. The angles were tightened and the camera operators focused on close ups. Which meant they could be close still and Rio could hold Agatha that bit longer.

They couldn’t speak between takes because they were mic’d and being watched from every corner of the room.

But they could touch and hold each other if they were careful not to move the duvet too much. Both their shirts had been pushed up so that it was easier to feel the other’s skin and Rio was soon flubbing lines so she could hold Agatha for longer.

Because it would end soon. She’d have to go back to not touching Agatha.

And it did end.

It ended and Rio had to move from the bed. And Agatha did too.

They didn’t look at each other as Rio went to check out the dailies and Agatha left the set.
Rio did her job after doing her job. She watched what she had to and chatted about character journeys and emotional beats. And when she was done she left the set and changed out of her costume in her trailer.

After that she cried. And Alice sat with her, but didn’t hold her as she did.

It was the end of the week of work. She had a session with Val to let out her stress and fury. She would then go home and have a bath. Maybe a glass of wine to take the edge off.

Then an early night, then just counting down the days until she could be with Agatha again.

She did all those things and still felt the same pain as always.

It didn’t disappear when she woke on Saturday. A run didn’t help. Nothing ever did.
By the afternoon she was determined to meet Alice for a coffee and talk over plans for her next project, and then plans for London, but something interrupted her as she was getting ready to leave.

Rio looked at her phone and her heart stopped.

Chapter 52: Crushed

Chapter Summary

Ralph pays a visit.

Rio receives a message.

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

The drive to Agatha’s was quick. Too quick. Rio was driving too fast, too recklessly.

The car she’d bought so Nicky could be safe was now racing through the streets of Los Angeles to get to Agatha’s old house.

It was the place she’d first kissed Agatha. The place she’d realised she wasn’t insane and that the whole time she’d been pining, Agatha had been pining too.

Rio wasn’t a woman who pined. She was a woman who wanted, and then got what she wanted.

And for a brief, beautiful moment in time, she’d had Agatha.

But now, as she overtook a speeding Maserati with little thought for her own safety, she realised she wasn’t going to the place she’d first had Agatha.

She was going to the place Agatha had called home with her husband.

It made her put her foot down harder on the gas.

It made what should have been a thirty minute journey take twenty. And barely that.

The security at the gate let her in and Rio did the rest for herself until she was striding through the familiar kitchen with one thought on her mind Agatha.

The sight she entered into was not a welcome one. Agatha was standing, one arm across herself, the other with her hand raised to her lips as she chewed on her perfectly manicured nails. She was by the small basketball court at the side of the house, her eyes on the little boy in a Bulls jersey.

“Well well,” Ralph had spotted her first, his broad grin not quite reaching his blue eyes. “Look what the snake dragged in.”

Rio’s gaze flickered to Jen, who was sat on the low wall that cut off the rest of the yard from the court; the snake in question. She shook her head once at Rio and Rio looked away again.

“I heard we were playing basketball so I figured you could use another player.”

Improv, but less ‘yes and’ and more ‘fuck off’.

As Ralph scoffed, Rio turned to Agatha again and saw her lips twitch ever so slightly. A sign she was welcome here. A sign she was wanted.

And then another equally as hesitant sign hit her right in the stomach.

Nicky had thrown himself at her, but not with his usual enthusiasm. He’d come over cautiously, skirting around his dad, until he arrived at Rio and wrapped his arms around her middle.

As Rio ducked down to kiss his temple he whispered: “Mama said I had to be polite.”

“I know baby,” Rio whispered right back, knowing Nicky was talking about the burgundy jersey he wore over his Celtics one. “It’s okay.”

Nicky nodded as Rio straightened up and when he turned with his back to her the balls of his feet rested on Rio’s toes. He was trying to be close without making it so obvious and Rio knew exactly why.

Ralph looked less than thrilled she was there even as he grinned across at them with his stupid handsome face.

“C’mon,” Ralph announced, tossing the ball up in the air as Rio crossed her arms over Nicky’s chest and he held her hands. “I can’t play a kid and a lady.”

“Afraid you’ll lose?” Agatha.

Rio bit the inside of her cheek. Agatha’s arms were now crossed over her chest.

“Nah, afraid I’ll show them why men are just better at sports. Don’t want to kill the little lady’s dream.”

He winked at Rio and Nicky responded before she could. Which was a good thing. Because Rio would have used a lot of expletives if she’d gone first.

“Rio is the best player ever. We can show you our tricks if you want? There’s one where-…”

“Tricks, huh?” Ralph grinned, cutting his son off and raising his brows as he bent at a right angle to look at Nicky on his level. Rio felt Nicky take in a heavy breath.

“Son, there’s a reason boys don’t play with girls in sports. I’ll show you who the best player is.” He straightened and then motioned with his head, “C’mon. Let’s get back to it. Your mom’s friend can play too, I guess.”

Ralph had turned and Rio took the opportunity to look at Agatha who was staring right at her. Her lips parted but she didn’t say anything and Rio squeezed Nicky then let him go and moved to Agatha under the pretence of handing her her phone to keep safe.

She just hadn’t bargained on Nicky following her over.

“You shouldn’t be here, but I’m glad you are.” Agatha whispered, barely breathing the words to Rio as she took her phone and pocketed it. She then ducked down to kiss the top of Nicky’s head.

“Agh!”

Ralph, in his infinite wisdom, had thrown the ball at the back of Rio’s head. She’d been forced to duck and had exclaimed in shock and fury but Agatha had grabbed her wrist before she could turn to throw her fury in Ralph’s direction.

“Don’t.”

“Melliza?”

Rio was biting down in her tongue so hard she could practically taste the blood already. But Agatha roped her in and pulled her to her side, one hand still in a vicelike grip around her wrist whilst her other arm was wrapped around her middle.

“Rio,” she whispered, half warning, half reassurance.

Rio’s teeth were bared, her whole body tense even where Agatha usually calmed her.

“Ooo,” Ralph called as Nicky stood before her and held her arms, copying his mom in trying to hold Rio back. “She’s maaaaaaaad!”

“Rio,” Agatha said again, tightening her hold, “this is a bad idea. You should go. You need to go.”

“Melliza, don’t go. Please don’t go.”

The three voices tugged at different parts of Rio. Agatha was her rational side, Nicky was her emotional side, and Ralph was all of her rage.

But where she was struggling to listen to any one of them Jen stepped in and blocked Rio’s view of Ralph.

“Rio Vidal, you go and play some basketball with Nicky here and his dad, okay? Play nice, you hear me?”

Rio made to lurch forwards as if to break Agatha’s hold on her but she didn’t move more than an inch; Agatha wouldn’t have let her.

She turned from Jen to Agatha and forced herself to relax her body so that she could see that equivalent relaxing in Agatha too. The hand holding her wrist became more gentle and Rio turned to her before she made up her mind about anything.

She came because she thought Agatha needed her but she wouldn’t stay if Agatha didn’t want her.

But Agatha nodded, Agatha slid her arm from around Rio and motioned to the court with her head. She remained silent and Rio knew she was worried, she knew she was furious. But she wanted her there so there she would stay.

She moved away slowly, taking Nicky’s hand in her own to lead him to the court where Ralph was obnoxiously bouncing the ball.

Even as she let go of Nicky’s hand he stayed close by.

“Ready to show me what you got?” Ralph threw the ball so it bounced just before Nicky’s feet so it bounced quickly and at a tight angle to fly towards Rio’s face; narrowly missing Nicky’s as it went. But Rio caught it and saw the look of barely hidden annoyance on Ralph’s face as she did.

“Careful,” she warned, one hand moving to rest on Nicky’s head. “Almost hit your son there, Ralph.”

“I’d never do that,” Ralph hissed, his mask slipping for a brief moment before it returned in the form of a tight grin. “My bad, son. Come over here and let’s get started, shall we?”

Rio let go of Nicky but he didn’t move and for a very painful two seconds Ralph kept motioning at him to come but he never did.

Rio threw the ball back at him and Ralph caught it on the bounce but looked less comfortable about it than Rio who’d caught the ball with ease.

“Oh,” Ralph crooned at Nicky who was tugging restlessly at his new jersey, his wide eyes on his pathetic excuse for a father. “You don’t wanna play ball with your dad? C’mon, Nicky, I’m home! Let’s play ball!”

“It isn’t your home.” Nicky, quietly. “You only visit us sometimes and the last time you did you shouted and were mean.”

Rio didn’t know this. She could have guessed, maybe. But she didn’t know it. A movement nearby told her that Agatha was close again, her hand on Nicky’s shoulder.

She shot a furtive glance at Rio, who was standing to attention like a guard dog just waiting for the instruction.

“Wouldn’t have to shout if your mother was less of a-.”

“Hey!” Rio shouted before Ralph could seal his own fate. Beside her Agatha said her name in warning but Rio didn’t need the warning. She simply moved forwards and stole the ball from Ralph and threw it easily into the net behind him.

“Are we gonna play, or what?”

Ralph scoffed as if to say ‘I meant to give you that ball’ but Rio ignored him and ran around playing distraction so Agatha could have a moment with Nicky. As she easily fended off Ralph from getting the ball back from her she caught sight of Agatha bending to whisper in Nicky’s ear and Jen off to the side tapping frantically at her phone.

She hoped she was contacting Val. With the next best option being Alice.

“Mellizo!” She shouted, as she feinted and Ralph went stumbling in the wrong direction. Nicky had turned after being pushed gently by Agatha and he easily caught the ball she bounced his way. “Aim high!”

He did but the ball got intercepted by his arrogant dad who laughed as he denied his son a point. “Better luck next time, kiddo.”

Nicky’s frown was deep and his lip was dangerously close to trembling so Rio made sure to get the ball back and bounce it in his direction again. She played point guard as best she could and blocked Ralph so Nicky could try once more.

He got closer to the net but this time missed and where Ralph jeered, Rio went to touch his cheek and whisper: “Almost, mellizo. Good shooting.”

“I don’t want to play,” Nicky whispered back, and Rio’s heart was in her throat as she nodded and held his shoulder.

“I know. Just one quick game and we can get some ice cream, okay?”

“What’s all this?” Ralph appeared over Rio’s shoulder, jocular and unfeeling as ever. “You don’t wanna play with your old man?”

Nicky looked from Ralph to Rio and back again.

“Just one game, maybe.”

Rio squeezed Nicky’s shoulder and he looked back to her with a hesitant smile as he toyed with his watch so much it was beeping beneath his fingers.

“One game, Ralph.” Agatha this time, closer again to hear what was being said. “Then ice cream. Then you can go home.”

“This is my home,” Ralph shot back, already straightening up and turning to Agatha. The moment he did, Nicky moved to stand before Rio and took her hand.

“It sure as shit isn’t,” Agatha spat, her cheeks flaming with indignation as Rio looked to Jen who had paused whatever she’d been furiously typing.

“You know,” Ralph started, “I have every right to be here.”

“And I’m upholding my side of this twisted agreement by allowing you to be here. So you’ll shut the fuck up, play a quick game with my son, and then you’ll fuck off back to my mother.”

Ralph flinched and Rio watched as he struggled for a response so said nothing. Coward, she thought. Idiot fucking loser coward.

But because he had no leg to stand on, and no backbone whatsoever, he turned from Agatha and Rio was pleased to see that when he took a shot at the hoop, he missed worse than Nicky had.

“Let’s go, mellizo,” she whispered by Nicky’s ear, encouraging him to let go so they could get on with it.

Rio ran past Agatha and felt her hand as it brushed her side when she did. She looked back at her and saw the fear in her gaze as she stepped off to the side again.

Their game started properly, with Ralph barking ignorant words at Nicky like: “you throw like a girl!” And “you’re too old to be acting like this!”. The latter came every time he scored a point and he’d run to Rio to high five, as was their ritual.

Agatha was chastising him from the sidelines and Rio shouting encouragement over whatever bile Ralph was spewing. And Nicky? He kept his eyes on either Rio or Agatha and didn’t look once at his dad.

Play went on for five minutes and Rio was feeling more and more riled up with every second. Until the unbelievable happened.

Until Nicky received the ball from her and was dribbling it towards the hoop and Ralph, all six foot two of him, stepped around and shoved his eight year old son so hard he went flying off to the side.

Two others took flight instantly.

Agatha to Nicky.

Rio to Ralph.

Rio shoved Ralph so violently that she managed to topple him over, despite him being significantly bigger than she was. He landed on his ass and yelled in fury as Agatha and Jen shouted at Rio to stop. And Rio screamed at Ralph.

“DON’T FUCKING TOUCH HIM!”

But Rio’s pulse was so loud in her ears she didn’t hear them. And besides, she could no longer think straight.

“You broke my fucking wrist!” Ralph yelled as he scrambled to his feet and brandished his hand at her. She made to shove him again but Ralph grabbed her first and fisted her shirt so harshly with both his hands there was no way she’d injured his wrist, let alone broken it.

“Gonna hit a girl, Ralph? Gonna hit me?”

“No! NO! Stop! STOP IT! You’re making him unsafe!”

Agatha’s voice cut through the pulse in Rio’s head. She assumed her shouts were aimed at Ralph but hadn’t looked away from the furious blond to check.

Ralph had though. His contorted features twisted into a sick smile as he looked from Agatha to Rio and Agatha continued to yell: “You’re making him unsafe! Get out! GET OUT!”

Rio looked then as Ralph dropped her and made her stumble back.

Agatha was holding Nicky against her. Jen was beside her, crouching to check on the boy. But Agatha was looking only at Rio.

“GET OUT! GET OUT OF MY HOUSE!”

It was clear who Agatha was speaking to. It was clear who she wanted to leave.

Rio stumbled then, tripping over her own feet to do just that. She didn’t stop until she was inside and for a second held onto the sideboard to breathe as the panic took hold of her and she could hear yelling from outside.

She hesitated. Torn between rushing back to make sure Agatha and Nicky were okay and doing as Agatha had asked. Her rational side won out. So she soldiered on, choking on her own breath as she stumbled through to the front door.

Agatha would never forgive her for this; for losing her temper so viciously. Ralph could twist it. Ralph could make Rio out to be a danger to his son. Ralph could…

A body collided with her own, small and insistent. And Rio turned and ducked down to squeeze Nicky to her. He was trembling and crying and she couldn’t do anything but hold him until she heard more footsteps and looked up to see a pale Agatha standing over them.

“Nicky, come here.”

“Nicky,” Rio whispered shakily, trying her best to unwind his arms from around her neck. “You gotta go to your mom, mellizo.”

Nicky was protesting, trying to clutch at her as she got his arms free.

“N-no, please. No! No I want, I want, melliza don’t leave us. Mama doesn't mean… please don’t!”

Rio just shook her head and swept Nicky into her arms to squeeze him one last time before she passed him over to Agatha. The handoff was difficult, with the soundtrack of Jennifer’s screaming in the background, and Nicky was still reluctant. Rio was being as gentle as she could in trying to peel him off of her but he was too big to be easy to handle and too insistent to be compliant.

“Mellizo. Mellizo,” she tried to beg, soon changing to: “Nicky, Nicky.”

“D-don’t leave! Don’t go!”

Rio sucked in a breath as Agatha tried too but Nicky wasn’t budging and both Rio and Agatha were being too gentle to be successful.

Rio raised her gaze when a shout of “she broke my fucking wrist!” could be heard from outside and locked eyes with Agatha. For a heartbeat they were both still, both holding Nicky, both as terrified as the shaking little boy.

“Take him, take him upstairs. I need… I… take him.”

“Agatha,” Rio breathed, giving up on trying to pass Nicky on and giving in to holding him properly.

“He’s safe with you.”

Agatha’s hand fell to Rio’s and Rio made a high-pitched noise as she swallowed and nodded just once. But as Agatha pulled away she reached out to grab hold of her and Agatha turned back.

She looked terrified.

“I don’t want you left alone with him,” Rio choked out, now cradling Nicky’s head as he clutched at her.

“Mama!” Nicky protested too, catching on to the fact that if Rio wasn’t going, then his mom was.

“Jen’s here. Go. Now.”

Rio stumbled away, reluctantly this time. If Agatha were letting her stay then she’d rather be with Agatha. But Nicky was still crying and Rio had to do something right.

She tripped halfway up the stairs and just caught herself before she fell completely. After that she was more careful. She carried Nicky across the landing and through to his old bedroom where she sat with him on the bed and gently encouraged him to disentangle himself so she could see his tear-stained face.

“I’m here,” she whispered, “I’ve got you. I’m here.”

Nicky’s breathing was uneven, but he was trying to catch his breath now. He raised his hands to his hair and clutched at it, and Rio held his little fists as he attempted to tug it, his eyes screwed closed in concentration.

“He- he’s going to t-take me a-away a-and I won’t s-see my mama a-anymore a-and-…”

“Hey hey,” Rio breathed out, gently but firmly unlocking Nicky’s hands from his hair so he wouldn’t hurt himself. “No one is taking you away from your mama. No one, okay?”

Nicky nodded furiously but made a noise from the back of his throat as he tried to swallow his tears. Rio brought him back in then and let him cry it out as she rubbed his back and whispered soft reassurances.

Beyond the closed door of Nicky’s room she could hear the yelling that continued. Agatha’s voice had joined the mix now, louder than anyone else’s, until it was the only one that sounded.

She heard a door slam and the shouting stopped for a while. And then another sound of a door slamming. And then silence.

The little clock by Nicky’s bed told her they’d been here almost thirty minutes. Nicky’s tears had dried but his breathing was still uneven and he was still holding fast to Rio like she might leave any minute.

Rio waited patiently, still rubbing Nicky’s back, still whispering to him that it would be okay.

And then Agatha entered the room and she dropped down to her knees before them and Rio no longer knew if it would be okay or not.

Agatha was pale, paler than Rio had ever seen her before. She looked exhausted and frightened and all bad, bad things. And Rio couldn’t tear her eyes away from her. She couldn’t not look at her ocean eyes that swirled with a depth of feeling fathoms deep.

Nicky shifted to turn his head and look over his shoulder at his mom as Agatha’s hand rested on his arm and her other sat on Rio’s knee. She squeezed Rio there and Rio felt like she could breathe again.

“Honey,” she murmured, her lips quivering, “It’s okay. He’s gone. It’s just us.”

Nicky tucked his head below Rio’s chin and Rio squeezed him before she held her hand out to Agatha and asked, “Come sit up here?”

Agatha looked at her for a second and then took her hand and used it to help her stand and sit beside her on the bed. Nicky leant across, one arm now around Rio’s neck and the other looping around Agatha’s to pull her in.

It worked only because Rio, and then Agatha, allowed it to. Rio held Nicky and Agatha and breathed out a sigh as they all hugged as best they could.

Soon, Nicky loosened his hold on Rio and stretched fully over to Agatha, who, with Rio’s help, lifted him totally across. Rio took it as a dismissal so went to stand but Nicky hadn’t meant it as one and made that clear as soon as he realised what she was doing.

“N-no! Stay! You have to stay with us.”

Rio looked down at the sight of Nicky blinking up at her and Agatha staring at the floor. She swallowed and then bent to kiss Nicky’s pink cheek.

“I’ve gotta go, mellizo. You’re safe with your mama.”

She straightened and as Nicky began to protest again Agatha spoke: “I didn’t mean what I said. I was scared. I… I was scared.”

Rio nodded slowly and when Nicky reached to her she stepped back closer again. She held his hand as she stared at Agatha and Agatha kept her gaze down on the floor by her feet.

Nicky inhaled shakily and Rio squeezed his hand as she said: “his wrist-…”

“Not broken,” Agatha said quickly, her gaze flickering to Rio’s. “Not with the way he was using it, throwing his hands about and,” Nicky turned to her and she smiled a little, “he’s fine. No evidence of it.”

Rio nodded but didn’t move to sit back down again until Agatha had placed her hand on the bed beside her and looked up at Rio properly.

Rio took it for what it was and sat beside her. Agatha’s hand was now on her thigh, holding her in place so Rio had no means of escape. They sat in silence for a while with Agatha holding them both.

And Rio thought of the fury that had been building in all the weeks she’d had to be apart from the two now curls beside her. She thought of Ralph’s smug grin and cocky belief that he deserved a place in Nicky’s life.

And then she thought of a grown man, so determined to show off that he’d shove a child in an attempt to score a point. And her fury roared in her chest.

She just didn’t know that Agatha had been watching her as it roared. She hadn’t known that Agatha was as close to reading her mind as anyone had ever been.

And so it was a surprise when Agatha whispered: “¿Me perdonas?” Do you forgive me?

“Mi vida,” Rio breathed, her anger dissipating the moment she turned to lock eyes with Agatha. She travelled her warm hand up Agatha’s wrist, all the way up her arm until it curled around her bicep and she held her as tightly as Agatha held her. “I made him unsafe,” she continued, only after she had Agatha in her hold. “I shouldn’t have-…”

“You protected me,” Nicky said quietly, making Rio and Agatha look around to him. “Mama knows that. Don’t you, mama?”

“I do, honey. I know that.”

Nicky nodded as if that was the end of the conversation and Rio smiled a little, and squeezed Agatha’s arm before she leant in to kiss her shoulder.

It was then that Agatha's hold on her changed and she moved her hand up to rest in the back of Rio’s head. When Rio lifted up again it remained there and Agatha smiled sadly.

“You’re stronger.”

“I’ve been working out.”

A flash of something in Agatha’s gaze and then it was gone. It had been a brief moment of teasing, a reminder of what they would soon have again. But right now everything felt too raw for even a glimmer of something to survive.

The door opened and they all turned to see Jen standing there, accompanied by Val and Alice.

“We have to go back to the house. We shouldn’t stay here.”

“Fine,” Agatha uttered, suddenly businesslike as she released Rio and stood with Nicky. “Is anyone-…?”

“A couple,” Val answered quickly, and Rio raised her brows at her new friend only to have her answer immediately. “Paps.”

“Fuck.”

“Might be hard to shake them off but we’re prepared for them to know where the other house is. It was bound to happen at some point.”

Rio didn’t agree with this, nor did she like it, but Agatha had touched her arm as if to say “I know, me too”, so she restrained herself from speaking her mind and instead focused on her best friend’s angry face as she stood in the door.

“We need to leave, Rio.”

“No. Rio has to come home with us.” Nicky, stepping before Rio with a stern look on his face.

Rio bit in her lip but said nothing because the decision seemed to be being made by people other than her in the room already. Agatha had moved to talk quietly to Val and Jen was keeping watch over the situation with a shell-shocked expression.

Nicky was back to standing half on Rio’s toes.

“Rio.”

“No, Alice.” Nicky again, applying a bit more pressure to Rio’s toes than she’d like. “She has to stay.”

Alice was fighting with herself but Rio knew she’d draw the line at fighting with a kid. Especially this kid. Especially Rio’s kid.

“You okay, kid?” Rio sighed as Alice clearly gave in and moved closer. Nicky’s shoulders dropped from where he’d held them about his ears. “What’s with the new jersey?”

Nicky looked down at himself and Rio did too. She helped him as he tried to tug it quickly over his head and then tossed it aside as she answered for him: “A gift. From Ralph.”

“I don’t want it,” Nicky was quick to say as he brushed down the jersey he’d stolen from Rio all those months ago. “Daddy said it was a better colour on me but I didn’t want it and mama said I had to be polite.”

“Politeness is good,” Alice said half-heartedly, now more focused on Rio as she stepped closer still. “Shoving?” She asked, “Really, Rio?”

As Rio crossed her arms over Nicky and he bent his head back to look up at her she shrugged and defended herself as best she could when a child was present: “He shoved Nicky, I shoved him.”

“Dick,” Alice muttered, and Rio nodded in agreement, at least pleased Alice was with her on that.

“That’s a bad word,” Nicky mumbled as he turned back to Alice.

Rio hummed as she said: “Sometimes bad words are okay.”

Nicky nodded and Rio felt him shift on her feet as his hand turned her forearm and his fingers spread to try and cover the pale scars on the inside. She held him a little tighter after that.

The discussions happening on the other side of the room were soon revealed to them. Rio had been right that the decision was being made for her.

Agatha was to go with Val and Nicky, which she didn’t seem thrilled about but her reaction was nothing to her son’s. Nicky protested, but quietly, politely. And it took Agatha’s ability to reassure him for him to eventually agree.

Because Rio was to follow behind with Alice and Jen.

And from the sounds of Nicky’s protestations, it didn’t sound like he was convinced Rio would be following at all.

But Rio did follow. Rio kept close as they left the house. She kept her eyes on Agatha and Nicky even if she couldn’t keep her hands on them.

Nicky was silent, clutching his mom’s hand and turning every couple steps to check Rio was close behind. She nodded at the little boy when he looked because she couldn’t make herself smile.

And when the little troupe got to Agatha’s car, Rio rushed to open the door for her. A small gesture after a big mistake.

Agatha placed her hand on the door in a way that meant their fingers overlapped and Rio’s breath caught in her throat when Agatha whispered to her: “Drive safe.”

Rio swallowed and said nothing in response as she closed the door on the precious cargo now tucked in the back of Agatha’s Range.

One of the hired security was driving them and Rio didn’t move until the car pulled away. Val was already in the driver’s side by the time she got to her own car and Alice was beside her up front so she slipped in the back and turned to see another SUV pulling up close behind them.

“Someone followed Ralph home. Discreetly. He’s in his condo.”

Rio nodded, allowing this info to calm her as they began to follow Agatha’s car along the road.

“Are you hurt?” Alice, twisting in her seat to look back at her.

“No.”

“Do you know what you did was stupid?”

“Yes.”

“Okay then.”

Alice turned to face forward again and Rio returned her attention to her fingers.

“Why wasn’t Val there?”

It was obvious who she was directing the question towards and Jen answered as if she’d been expecting it sooner rather than later: “Agatha didn’t want to give Ralph any reason to act up.”

“You shouldn’t have contacted her,” Alice added, glancing at Jen then Rio again.

“Agatha was shaking. Nicky kept running to her. Ralph was becoming more and more of an asshole. I thought if Rio came then Agatha would relax and Nicky would play.”

“You should have contacted me first, Jen.”

“And, what? You’d tell me to calm down and everything would be fine?” Rio shifted uncomfortably in her seat. “Jesus, Alice. We’re so past fine! Nicky doesn’t understand what’s happening and Agatha is a goddamn mess!”

Rio knew Alice and Jen had hit a rough patch before; caused mostly by the her and Agatha situation. But she’d never been slapbang in the middle of it. She shrank a little in her seat and held her breath.

“Well maybe she wouldn’t be a mess if-…!”

“Don’t start! Not again!”

Rio twitched and looked up to see Alice’s profile, tense and tight as she stared ahead of herself out the window.

There was silence in the car for a while, time for everyone to settle into the awkwardness of the situation as Jen continued to drive.

“I just,” Alice said, slowly and carefully, “I want all this to be over.”

Rio braced herself for another argument but instead Jen reached her hand across and found Alice’s. No one said anything until they pulled into the garage of Agatha’s hill top home.

Agatha’s car was already parked up and Rio was surprised when she rounded it to get to the door and Agatha was standing with Nicky, clearly waiting for her.

Rio moved first and reached for Agatha over the little boy who wrapped his arms around her middle as Rio’s encircled his mom.

“Jen’s a slow driver.” Agatha’s voice was hesitant but having her even speaking to her at all was a miracle.

Agatha broke the hug before it could become a crush and Rio was able to look at her face for only a moment but in it she could see how tense Agatha still was.

Nicky released her and went with his mom and Rio brought up the rear, keeping close watch on the two of them as they traipsed through to the kitchen and Agatha went to find snacks in the cupboards.

Rio leant against the counter as she watched and forced a smile when Nicky turned to see if she was still there. It didn’t take him long to hurry over and Rio ducked down to let him climb onto her back so he could access the cookies they both knew to be hidden on one of the upper shelves of one of the higher cupboards.

And peace descended in the little kitchen, but it didn’t last for very long. Rio had been focused on leaning out of the way so Nicky could rummage for the cookies he liked best - ones with chocolate chips and a chocolate base - when the shouting began.

It had started as a normal-volume discussion, one that Rio hadn’t even noticed, as she played her part as human ladder. But it was Jen who broke the sound barrier and started the yelling, much to everyone’s surprise.

“He was struggling! What the fuck should I have done!”

Rio stood motionless with Nicky’s arms so tight around her neck now she could barely breathe. But that was fine. She didn’t really feel like breathing anyway. She turned with him away from the open cupboard and watched everything begin to unravel.

“That isn’t the point!”

“Jen,” Alice urged, trying to keep her girlfriend calm whilst her best friend was practically catatonic in the corner with a little boy clinging to her back.

“You should not have called Rio over! That’s what you should have done! NOTHING!”

Rio blinked slowly, her eyes trained only on Agatha as she found it hard to contain herself. She was gesticulating frantically with every word, her motions as her wild hair.

As she continued to shout back and forth with Jen, Rio heard another voice, a much softer, much less sure one, against her ear.

“Melliza,” Nicky whispered, “Why is mama still frightened?”

Rio looked then, really looked at Agatha, and knew Nicky was right. She wasn’t angry. She was terrified. Her hands, as they flew through the air or buried in her hair, were quivering with feeling. Her words were trembling as they were so viciously expelled and her eyes were wide and full of fear.

“It’s okay,” Rio managed to choke out, “She’s okay. We’re all safe.”

But Agatha was still shouting, Jen was too, and Nicky was holding her tightly. Rio couldn’t move, was barely breathing.

“Nicky,” Agatha’s stern voice, she’d turned but was looking past Rio’s face to her son’s, “Come here, please.”

Agatha held her hand out to him and Rio saw the way her fingers shook.

She swallowed thickly and began to squat down to help Nicky climb off her back. But he squeezed her throat and she coughed and stopped.

“Nicky,” Agatha repeated.

“Agatha,” Jen said, quieter than she had been since Ralph had left.

“Mama,” Nicky whispered, choking Rio as she straightened up and Agatha moved towards them to loosen his hold. “I’m okay here. Right, melliza? I’m okay here.”

Agatha’s trembling hands were on Nicky’s arms and she was so close that Rio could count the freckles she’d missed in all the time apart but Agatha wasn’t looking at her. Her eyes were focused on her son, watching him as he clung to the woman she wouldn’t make eye contact with.

“Mellizo,” Rio breathed, aware that Agatha’s lower lip had started to tremble. She squeezed Nicky’s legs where she held them at her sides. “Go to your mom. It’s okay. I’ll let you down.”

She saw Val step closer and felt a surge of anger that she believed there was a need to. But she couldn’t look at anyone other than Agatha.

“No,” Nicky insisted, and if it weren’t for Agatha’s hold on his arms she might have been choked again. “No, you’re scared, mama. But Rio’s here and everything is okay.”

“Honey,” Agatha breathed, “Get down now. Come on.”

Rio gulped as Nicky shook his head. “No.”

“Mellizo,” she tried, bending slowly down to try and encourage him to slide off as she let go of his legs. He just held on and Rio began to choke properly now as he put his full weight on her throat.

“Nicholas!”

Rio gasped as Agatha ripped his arms away from her throat and spluttered as Nicky fell from her back and onto his feet.

Val moved closer and Rio looked at her and saw that she wasn’t looking at Agatha. She was watching Alice.

But Agatha was moving around her to get to Nicky so she didn’t have time to check on what her friend was doing. Alice was the least of her worries. And as far as Rio was concerned, Val could do what she wanted with her right now.

Because she’d never heard Agatha speak to Nicky like that and as she looked up at her and saw the horror in Agatha’s eyes, she realised it was probably the first time.

“Okay, mama,” Nicky sniffled as Rio stood to her full height again and a hand flew to her throat that was soft, a gesture of checking in. “I’m sorry.”

“Mi vida,” Rio whispered, her voice hoarse as Agatha’s hand remained where it was, trembling against the side of her throat as she welcomed Nicky in to her and hugged the little boy. Rio swallowed thickly and Agatha must have felt it below her thumb because she glanced at her and for a second looked as though she was going to tell her something but then turned away again and spoke to Nicky instead: “I’m sorry. Honey, I’m sorry.”

Agatha’s hand dropped from Rio so she could hold Nicky properly and Rio Rio stepped back to give them space but found as she did that Agatha looked up to her and for a heart-stopping moment Rio thought she was going to ask her to leave.

But she said nothing again and soon closed her eyes as she dropped down to kiss Nicky’s cheek multiple times and cuddle him closer.

“I’m sorry, honey. I’ve had a rough day and-…”

“It’s okay to be scared, mama. But I’m here and Rio is here and auntie Jen, and Val too. Daddy’s gone. Please don’t shout.”

“And where am I?” Alice muttered from the corner of her mouth. Jen slapped her arm. Val stepped closer.

“I’m not scared, baby.”

But Rio didn’t believe her and she knew Nicky didn’t either. Rio went to step around them but Agatha grabbed her wrist as she did and she turned to see two pairs of shining eyes staring back up at her.

Agatha’s hold on her tightened even though Rio hadn’t moved a muscle since she’d first grabbed her.

“Stay.”

Rio nodded just once but didn’t move otherwise and she realised then that it was imperative that she did. So she moved. The great gasp Agatha released when Rio wrapped her free arm around her was enough to tell her she was doing the right thing.

Agatha was back where she belonged and Rio couldn’t believe she’d ever let go.

With Nicky squashed between them, their friends watching them with wary eyes, and the weight of time around them, Agatha released a soft sob.

It took everything Rio had to not break down with her but she could feel Nicky scrambling to hold onto them both and it became a free for all of limbs and fingers and faces pressed together.

Rio was the ballast that held them all together. Her back hit the counter and yet she didn’t falter in her hold. They were all crouched on the floor now, having fallen with the weight of their desire to be close. Rio’s legs spread wide to welcome two bodies in against her. Nicky was sat on her right leg, Agatha was hovering in the middle on her knees. It was uncomfortable in a way that can only be tolerated when Agatha’s face, hot and wet, was pressed against her neck. And Nicky, he was speaking some strange Spanglish. It reminded Rio of home. And Rio didn’t know whether he was trying to reassure himself, his mama, or her, but it worked all the same.

Above them, the three left standing watched with a mixture of concern, annoyance, and distrust. Jen, the concerned of the trio, was chewing on her lip. Alice, the annoyed, was frowning at the sight. And Val, the distrustful, was half watching her charge and half watching Alice, who had stepped a little closer than she’d have liked.

When Nicky became silent and Agatha had brushed her last kiss to Rio’s hot neck, Rio knew it was time to let go. When she did, Agatha pulled away. She stood inelegantly to her feet and pulled Nicky with her. Nicky hesitated, holding his mom’s two hands but Rio pulled one of the pairs towards her and kissed where their hands were joined in a gesture that meant ‘it’s okay, you can go, I’ll be right here’.

From where Rio sat, Nicky looked bigger than usual, as if the incident had made him grow. Or maybe it was that Agatha looked smaller somehow. She looked scared and more stressed than Rio had ever seen her.

“Just a sec,” Agatha whispered, her gaze briefly flickering to meet Rio’s before she turned away and led Nicky from the room. And Nicky, as usual, turned on his way out with his mom and checked that Rio was still there.

When they were gone, Rio put her head in her hands.

“We should go,” Alice’s voice said, closer than she had been a second ago. She’d obviously crouched down because her hand had found Rio’s arm. “Let’s go, Rio.”

“I can’t leave them like this.”

“You shouldn’t leave yet.” Val.

Rio was shaking now, her skin itchy and hot. She scratched at her arm and lifted her head to stare at the doorway, hoping Agatha would run right back through it and into her arms.

“There’s nothing we can do. Jen will stay with them. Val’s here. It’s okay.”

“Rio,” Jen agreed, Rio could hear it in her voice before she’d even said anything else. “You should go.”

“I,” she began, unsure of where her sentence might take her but knowing she needed to say something.

Though no other words came.

Alice took her arm and helped her to stand. She held her still as she led her gently from the house. There was no sign of Agatha. No sign of Nicky. No sign of life of cognitive thought in Rio’s head.

It was like they’d vanished into thin air the moment they’d gone from Rio’s sight.

Maybe this was it. Maybe this was the end of whatever play they’d been acting in. And Rio would always be in the audience, watching dos patitos perform for her and then ultimately disappear.

Agatha wouldn’t let her near Nicky again. Agatha would break up with her for good.

And she’d be right to, Rio thought. She’d been so fucking stupid. She’d been-…

“Rio, I mean it.” Val again, closer this time. “You gotta stay. Alice. You too.”

Alice didn’t want to listen but Rio turned just as they hit the front door and she tugged Alice back around.

Val was closer. She was close enough to now reach and grab Rio’s arm until Rio was being held by both women, and wanted to be held by neither.

“I mean it. The hounds are here. If you go out now they’ll catch you mid bloody breakdown.”

Rio felt Val’s fingers flex against her forearm and she considered ripping it away and leaving regardless but then she remembered that Val was paid to protect Nicky. And she did her job well.

Rio did not do her job well.

So she listened to Val. She nodded. She pulled her arm away but she didn’t move to leave, instead she marched back into the house and had Alice shouting after her.

It was instinct that took her to Agatha’s office. It was panic that made her stop just before she knocked.

She stood instead on the outside of the closed door and touched the wood with yearning fingers.

Inside she could hear Agatha talking but she couldn’t make out what she was saying. It meant she was quiet, at least. It meant she wasn’t shouting or sobbing or begging.

She listened for a while until she heard something that made her heart stop. It was her name, said louder than anything else.

Agatha was calling her inside and how could Rio refuse.

She opened the door cautiously, unsure what she was about to walk in on. But what was waiting for her wasn’t something she ever had to be afraid of.

Sitting in her desk chair, with Nicky across her lap, was Agatha. She wasn’t smiling, but she wasn’t crying, so Rio had to count her blessings. The room otherwise looked normal, as if this were any other day, or a day where the worst hadn’t happened. But Rio spotted something else that was different, a glass bowl full of various paper flowers. Her heart swelled three sizes in her chest at the sight of them.

Nicky lifted his head from Agatha’s shoulder as Rio shut the door and Agatha said: “I knew it was you.”

“What gave me away?”

“Shadow under the door. The fact that you didn’t knock or shout.”

Rio tried a smile but it didn’t feel right so she stopped pretty quickly.

“You can move from the door, melliza.”

Rio dragged her gaze from Agatha’s pale face to Nicky’s smaller one and chewed on her lip as she closed the distance and stopped at the edge of the desk.

“Scared we’ll bite?” Agatha, a slight twitch in her brow suggesting she was trying for a joke, but her tone hadn’t caught on.

Nicky took in a shaky breath and exhaled slowly, his large eyes still on Rio’s face.

“We haven’t been tres patitos in… in a really long time.”

Rio looked down at where her fingers were tapping at the desk and her throat felt suddenly dry. Her brain felt like it was thumping, like her skull was too small to contain it or something.

She was an animal, and her cage was desperately trying to hold her.

“Rio, Nicky asked you a question.”

Rio looked up sharply at the sound of Agatha’s voice and was startled at the look on her face. She looked frightened again, even more so than when they were in the kitchen.

“I… I didn’t hear,” she whispered genuinely.

“Can you stay with us tonight, please? I don’t want you to be alone in your house when… when you could be home with us.”

Rio’s eyes flickered from Nicky’s face to Agatha’s and back again. She could never refuse Nicky. Agatha knew that too. Which meant Agatha wouldn’t have let him ask if she didn’t want her to stay.

“Mama says,” Nicky started again, leaning forwards a little from Agatha now before Rio could find the words to respond, “That we can have ice cream for dinner tonight. And maybe… and maybe…” Nicky swallowed and Rio shifted to take a step around the desk to be closer. “Maybe you’ll remember how much fun we have and… how safe we are and how good tres patitos is.”

“Are,” Agatha whispered quietly, correcting his grammar as she tucked some hair behind his ear.

Nicky nodded and agreed: “Are.”

“Tres patitos aren’t good,” Rio corrected, and realised how much the two before her were hanging on every word when Agatha winced and Nicky looked hurt. “Tres patitos is the best.”

“Are the best,” Agatha corrected gently, her lips curling at the sides.

Rio hummed her agreement and took a step closer. “But in answer to your question, Nicholas River Harkness, I would love to come home. But not just for the ice cream. For the ducklings.”

“Patitos,” Nicky was the one correcting now and Rio agreed with a brush of her hand against his warm cheek.

“Patitos.”

“Could you…?”

Rio knew what Nicky was asking so leant in even before he finished his question. She kissed his cheek and let him tangle his fingers in her shirt sleeve as Rio then turned to Agatha.

They were nose to nose and it was so tempting to just kiss her. But she’d fucked up already tonight so she moved to kiss her cheek instead. But Agatha had turned into her. She’d pressed her nose into Rio’s cheek and Rio moved back, barely a centimetre and caught the corner of Agatha’s lips against her own.

It was hardly a kiss but it felt like a miracle.

She pulled back fully to avoid temptation and moved to Agatha’s other cheek to kiss that instead. And then her temple. And then the top of her head.

She breathed her in from there and the pain in her head subsided as Nicky tried to tug her back again.

“Sit with us.”

“Nicky,” Agatha said softly, a warning that Rio took and Nicky ignored.

“No, you said it’s important to tell the truth and the truth is that my mama hasn’t,” Nicky’s eyes filled with tears and Rio fell to her knees before them. “Hasn’t smiled properly in a really long time and the best times she used to smile were when you were here and we were together and…”

“Honey,” Agatha cooed as she wiped at Nicky’s cheeks and Rio placed a hand on his knee.

“I’m staying, mellizo. I’ll stay and when it’s just us we can dance in the kitchen and we can watch a movie, okay?”

“And mama?”

“Oh, don’t worry about her. I’ll make sure she dances and I’ll keep her warm as we snuggle on the couch.”

“I’ve been dancing,” Agatha protested quietly, shooting a quick, nothing glare in Rio’s direction.

“Well I’m yet to see your robot so…”

Agatha huffed and Nicky giggled, “It’s not very good.”

“I didn’t think it would be.”

“Hey!”

The door burst open as Agatha had lifted her hand to smack at Rio but Rio had moved suddenly so she was on her feet and blocking Agatha and Nicky from whoever had intruded.

It was Jen, followed closely by Val, with Alice bringing up the rear.

“We’ve got the footage. If he so much as tries to-…”

“Jen,” Agatha cut her off, and encouraged Nicky to stand from her lap so she could stand with him. Rio felt her hand curl around her wrist but she was looking straight ahead at Val’s face.

“He’s stupid but he’s not so stupid that-…”

“The paps are outside,” Val interjected, and Rio relaxed slightly, taking this to be the reason she still looked tense. “I’ve advised Rio and Alice to stay. We think they’ll disperse when they realise there’s no movement and then they can leave.”

Agatha’s hand slipped down to entwine her fingers with Rio’s and Rio finally turned to look at her. The light had changed in the room, or maybe it was knowing they were all stuck and couldn’t do anything about it, but Agatha looked defeated and tired.

She turned to meet Rio’s eye and Rio forced a smile that Agatha couldn’t match.

“Val,” Agatha said quietly, her gaze still on Rio’s attempted smile, “Could you please take Nicky and get him a snack? I need to speak to Rio.”

Nicky had turned to his mama and only then did Agatha look down at him and kiss his temple. She whispered something that Rio didn’t catch but was reassuring enough to make him move off to Val and look over his shoulder at his mom only once before he left the room.

It was tense then. More tense than before. And Agatha dropped Rio’s hand to take up her seat again and place her head in her hands.

Jen closed the door and Rio perched on the desk, her gaze on Agatha and her back to their two friends.

“Should have broken his fucking jaw, Rio.” Jen, unhelpful, but well meaning.

“No,” Agatha insisted. “I shouldn’t have married him in the first place.”

“Got you Nicky though,” Rio reminded quietly.

“You got me Nicky,” Agatha corrected without looking up.

“If he presses charges, Rio,” Alice started, as unhelpful as Jen.

“He won’t. Did you listen to Val? We have evidence of him shoving his own son. And Nicky, the whole time he was out there, was constantly skirting around him or running to Agatha or Rio. He doesn’t like him, doesn’t trust him. We just need him to say that in court.”

“We are not media training my son.”

“It’s not media training. It’s telling him he needs to talk shit about his dad or he might have to live with his dad.”

“I’m not scaring my son. He’s scared enough.”

“He’ll be goddamn terrified when Ralph-…”

“Jen.” Both Agatha and Rio’s voices sounded at once and Jen went silent but shook her head as she flopped into the chair opposite Agatha’s desk.

Everyone was silent for a while. Rio stared ahead of herself, having turned from watching Jen to look instead at the books and awards that littered the shelves in the room.

Evidence after evidence of Agatha’s power, of her prowess, of just how damn adored she was. And amongst them, amongst the trophies and books on acting or biographies of people Agatha admired, were pictures of her ultimate reward: pictures of Nicky.

Nicky as a baby, Nicky as a toddler, Nicky’s first day at school, Nicky in his mom’s arms and with Rio’s smile.

“I took him away earlier,” Agatha’s voice sounded suddenly, gravelly and rough. “Because I needed to make sure he knew I would never let Ralph touch him again. I needed him to know,” Rio reached across and held Agatha’s shoulder. “I needed him to know I was doing everything to keep him safe, to keep him with me. Because I can’t tell him the truth. I can’t… I can’t tell him that he might have to go with Ralph. That-…”

“He won’t,” Rio whispered, squeezing Agatha’s shoulder as she did. “That won’t happen.”

“Please let me just say it,” Agatha responded, turning to Rio with watering eyes, “I’m so terrified he’ll win.”

Rio nodded and turned properly to stand beside Agatha, and squeezed her shoulder as she did.

She could do this. She could be strong and patient and let Agatha say what frightened her. This was the kind of partner she had to be now. She had to wait.

“He doesn’t want to go with Ralph. He’ll be honest on the stand. I raised him to never lie and to always tell the truth. Other than that I’m not going to tell him what to say or do when up there.”

Jen sighed and Rio watched as Alice began to pace back and forth.

“I just think a little training-…”

“Jen,” Rio said firmly, “Agatha said no.”

Agatha’s fingers moved to touch Rio’s where they curled around her shoulder and Rio felt a flash of pride that she was still here, still able to defend her.

“We haven’t heard from that bitch who took the screengrabs, we don’t know if Ralph has seen the pictures, we-…”

“If he had he’d have said something. He did at the bar.” Alice now, still pacing, not looking at anyone or anything in particular. “Besides, they wouldn’t be admissible in court so it’s other angles you’ve got to watch out for.”

“Like what?” Jen asked, twisting in her chair to look at Alice.

“Oh, I don’t know,” Alice mused, raising her hands to the sky, “Assault, maybe?”

“It wasn’t-,” Rio started but Agatha finished for her: “He assaulted my son first. He’s stupid but not stupid enough to go after the tapes.”

“Yeah well, a few stupid things have happened recently.”

Rio went to move but Agatha had already grabbed her wrist and so, tethered as she was behind the desk, she could only shout across at her friend: “Get the fuck out, Alice. I mean it. Get! Out!”

Alice didn’t even flinch which made Rio madder, which made Agatha tug harder at her to get her to turn around.

“Now seems like as good a time as ever,” Alice said, crossing her arms over her chest. “Jen, Agatha? Are you gonna ask her?”

This strange change in topic made Rio blink and shake her head, looking between a sheepish Jen and a furious Agatha. She then turned back to Alice who looked mighty pleased with herself. And her friend sighed when no one else said anything, a big dramatic sigh that didn’t suit her.

“Agatha wants you to do something else for her.”

Rio started, aware of Agatha’s intense grip somehow tightening around her wrist.

Alice continued: “She wants you to date Val.”

Rio felt cold all over. The sudden rush of Agatha standing beside her and trying to turn her didn’t help at all. It was just an all-consuming icy shock that ran through her veins and stabbed her in her battered heart.

“That’s not,” Agatha was rushing to say, “That’s not it. Rio, my love, that is not it. Not that way. Not in the way she… Rio. Rio.”

Rio dragged her eyes from Alice who was now being rounded on by Jen and allowed herself to be turned ninety degrees to be face to face with Agatha, the woman apparently asking her to date someone else. The woman who only a few weeks ago had begged her not to.

Agatha was no longer holding her. She was instead touching her all over with a frantic, panicked look on her face. “It’s not what it sounds like. I don’t want… I’d never want… I just want it to… I want… I want you to see Nicky and I… if you… if you’re seen…”

Her hands weren’t resting anywhere in particular yet. They continued to move about Rio’s body. They touched her chest, her neck, her stomach, her hips, her cheeks. The order was random, as though Agatha intended it to confuse rather than reassure.

But it did neither. It left Rio cold still, frozen in a time and place she didn’t want to be.

“My love,” Agatha continued to try to thaw her, now working overtime as she tried to find the button on Rio’s body that would bring her back to life. “It’s just for show, just so you can… just so when you’re away you can come back a-and see Nicky. He needs to see you and, and-…”

“I can’t do that,” Rio said flatly, her voice unlike her own as she spoke and Agatha’s hands stilled on her chest. “I can’t do that.”

“O-okay, okay,” Agatha whispered, nodding as if Rio had said something important. “Yes, I… okay. Sit with me?”

Rio didn’t move and Agatha nodded again, but slower this time. Her hands remained on Rio’s chest but she dropped her gaze and murmured a quiet: “I’m sorry.”

“It’s just PR,” Jen said, her voice stronger again. “It’s just a calculated,” but she trailed off because Agatha had shot her a look and Rio looked out of it.

Alice picked up her thread, “I fucking hate this.”

Rio turned her head to look at her and found Alice to be staring across at her with Jen clutching her hand and arm.

“I hate that you’re-…”

Rio’s gaze moved to Jen and she asked: “are you serious?”

“It’ll mean you can see Nicky without many questions being raised.”

Rio felt a nudging of her jaw, and recognised the feel of Agatha’s nose as she nuzzled into her. She was still stiff, still not responding properly to Agatha’s touch but she’d already lost an inch in height and had begun curling into her without even knowing she was doing it.

“I don’t want to do it.”

“Okay,” Jen said slowly, her dark eyes jumping from Rio to Agatha. “Then we can… we’ll come up with a new plan.”

“Rio,” Agatha whispered, her name tickling over her skin in a way she hadn’t felt for weeks. “Sit with me.”

Agatha’s warm breath against her skin did more to melt her than a blow torch could.

But the shock of coming face to face with Ralph, the fury that had erupted when he put his hands on Nicky, the shame she felt when Agatha had screamed at her to leave; it all mixed into one painful, malignant darkness in her brain that trickled down and infected the rest of her body

“I’m not doing that.”

She pulled away from Agatha and forced Agatha to have to reach for her as she did. But Rio felt like she couldn’t breathe, and the only thing that could help that was space, and air.

Opening the window she took a deep breath and when she released it she said: “I can’t believe you’d ask me to do that.”

“Like I want to,” Agatha said, reacting to Rio’s dismissal with sarcasm that dripped, thick and viscous from her tongue.

“Then don’t.” Rio spat, something in her firing up before she even knew she’d pulled the trigger.

Silence. Tension so dense you could swim in it. Rio kept her back to the room and her eyes on the sky.

“My rule has always been no PR relationships. I hate the press. I hate them twisting stories. I hate them and their fucking bloodhound gang of-…”

“Jesus, just say no then!” Agatha, her own trigger pulled now.

Rio scoffed a half-laugh, half-growl and turned to see Agatha had rounded the desk and was just a couple feet in front of her.

“Fine. No.”

Agatha threw her hands in the air in a gesture that only managed to work Rio up more.

“The fact you couldn’t even be the one to tell me is-…”

“Is what, Rio? In case you hadn’t noticed I haven’t been able to talk to you! How in the hell was I going to be able to reach out and ask-…!”

“Don’t blame me for what’s happening!” It was defensive, too reactive. But Rio couldn’t help her shout as it flew from her lips.

“I’m not blaming you!”

“Jesus, guys, can we just-…”

“It sure as shit felt like you were blaming me for earlier. ‘Get out, Rio! You’re making him unsafe, Rio’!” Rio was just shouting her fears now, getting them out in the open just like her therapist had told her too. Only this was the wrong way to do it. The worst way to do it.

But the malignancy in her brain made it feel good to be screaming, good to be screaming at Agatha.

Agatha blinked and Rio winced when she noticed the tears in her eyes, coming back to herself for even a moment.

“I was scared out of my mind, Rio! What did you expect me to say?! Yes! Good! Kill the bastard for touching our son!”

Rio choked on the air she needed to breathe and across from her Agatha made a strange lurching movement and a noise that went with it as if she were trying to hold in a violent sob.

But the fuse had been lit, the gunpowder was dry, and so the flame continued to flicker along it, heading for the barrel, creating fireworks that Rio should never have set off.

“This shouldn’t be happening.” Rio whispered, her fury hot but quick to burn out, “This is not-, this is not what I want.”

But Agatha was already alight. She was already sparking off from every angle. And Rio wasn’t ready for the fireworks that came shooting her way.

“Do it then, Rio! Break it off! Break up with me!”

There she was again. The Agatha she had met in Berkeley. The Agatha who screamed and raged about things she didn’t mean.

But this Agatha was meeting a different Rio now. This Rio had been broken. First by Agatha, then by losing Miguel, and again by Agatha. Thrice broken; thrice hardened.

So she came back at her, even when she knew she shouldn’t, even when she knew she should have backed down and rolled over.

“And then what, Agatha? I just call it quits and what? Let that piece of shit get his hands on you? Maybe I break up with you and you decide to go back to him? You decide to let him fuck you again? You decide-…!”

“Yes, Rio! Because what I’m asking you to do with my fucking nanny is exactly the same! Go fuck her! Go fuck her if that’s-…!”

“ENOUGH!”

Jen’s voice splintered across Agatha’s shouts and the whole room rang with silence so loud it created a ringing in Rio’s ears as she turned away and placed her hands on the wall above her head. Someone touched her back, not Agatha, definitely not Jen. So Alice.

She tried to breathe through it, aware someone somewhere was talking but not to her. All she could think about was the mess of the situation and the pain in her head.

It took Jen saying her name a few times for her to come back down to earth. When she did she felt nauseous and turned to see Agatha looked the same where she sat against the desk and stared at the floor. Her knuckles were white with how hard she gripped the wood and Rio winced because she’d once kissed over those knuckles, once held them against her cheek, she’d worshipped them like she’d worshipped the woman they belonged to.

A jolt in her chest, and another sudden wave of nausea, told her she wanted to fall to her knees and worship Agatha again. But this time she couldn’t let herself.

“Fine,” she announced, deciding if she couldn’t do that she could at least do this. “I’ll do it. For the cameras I’ll do it. So I can keep seeing Nicky. But only if Val is comfortable.”

Agatha scoffed, a harsh, derisive nose that burned Rio’s ears.

“She is,” Jen interjected before Rio could say anything else.

“Then, fine. So long as it’s for Nicky. I’ll date whoever you want me to date.”

Agatha looked up then. No, she glanced up. It was barely half a second that they made eye contact and if Rio knew it would be the last time they made eye contact for the rest of the night she might have marched over and forced Agatha to look at her. But she didn’t know. She couldn’t know. So she looked away.

Maybe this way was better, she thought, being angry instead of pitifully sad. Maybe raging at Agatha and having Agatha raging at her could help them in some twisted way. It was all coming from the same place after all, a place of such intense fear that Rio couldn’t stand to think about it for too long.

Losing Nicky. Losing Agatha. Unbearable.

And so, once Nicky was reassured that the shouting he’d heard all the way from outside where he’d been playing with Val was nothing to worry about, both Rio and Agatha did what they did best: they acted.

Agatha played her part with aplomb and Rio played hers with a little less verisimilitude. But it worked because Nicky was pleased they could be tres patitos again and him feeling safe and happy was all that mattered.

They danced. They sang. They ate. They watched a movie. They curled up on the couch together. Rio carried a sleeping Nicky up to bed and Agatha sang him a soft song as Rio hovered by the door.

All the while they barely touched, they hardly spoke, everything was for Nicky. Everything hurt so acutely that when Nicky was passed out Rio didn’t even wait for Agatha before she marched back down the stairs and straight for the medicine cabinet.

She swallowed a strange concoction of pain meds (tylenol, Advil, a rogue naproxen) and ignored the looks of concern from Alice and Jen as she reemerged and Agatha avoided looking at her.

It was still early, so early that the paps were still camped out and Val was still around, but Rio had been having trouble looking at her too. So with fifty percent of the room off limits to her she thought it best to take herself off to hide away in the smaller living room mostly kept for movies or fort building.

The drugs she’d taken made her woozy as she curled up on her side and tugged the throw from the couch over herself. Just as well, because she didn’t feel much like being awake anymore. The call of the void again, louder and more persistent. She answered it by tipping slowly into it, and falling into a strangely blank and dreamless sleep.

Hours later, a soft movement on the couch woke her and Rio grunted quietly as she came back to herself. Someone was with her in the warm room.

Rio blinked into the dark and stared up at Agatha sat by her hip, her head angled down, and her fingers toying with something in her hand.

“Can we… can we forget everything? Just for tonight? Just for a few hours?”

Rio realised what Agatha was doing. She was spinning the ring on her finger, the ring Rio had bought her so she could wear it and know that Rio was a person who kept her promises and her promise to Agatha was that they’d get married, and that they’d be happy.

Felizamente casada.

She didn’t have to think about it. She just reached for Agatha and Agatha fell down against her like she always used to.

The weeks apart faded to nothing as Rio tugged her blanket up and over them. The fight, the pain of a tense evening, it all melted away as Agatha pressed into her and tucked beneath her chin.

Agatha was safe here, safe in her arms. And Rio didn’t feel any of the earlier anger or frustration. She just felt warm and more comfortable than she’d been in a long time.

“I love you,” Rio whispered into the dark, and she felt Agatha clutch at her tighter in response.

Agatha kissed her at the base of her throat and Rio sighed as their legs tangled together below the blanket.

“I love you,” Agatha whispered back, and Rio hummed as she slid her hand down to slip beneath her shirt and stroke over her back.

It was as Rio was drifting off that she thought of the first time she saw Agatha. It was on the big screen, dressed in cowboy boots and daisy dukes. Rio had been infatuated then, and she still was now.

But infatuation wasn’t enough to get them through this. So Rio rolled them and heaved Agatha properly on top of her. And Agatha adjusted like she always did, nuzzling in and finding where she fit against Rio’s body.

Rio could be as angry as she wanted to be. She could rage and fight and scream, but this was where she belonged. She was made to be that soft place to land for Agatha. She was made to hold her and cherish her.

She was made to love her.

They just had to get through this. They were still out at sea and Rio was doing her best to keep them afloat but as Agatha pressed her lips to the underside of her jaw, as Agatha’s hand found Rio’s heart, her palm warm against her ribcage, she realised that Agatha was trying to steer them through the rough waters the best way she knew how.

So Rio lay there, and Agatha lay above her, and they fell asleep within seconds of one another, taken into separate dreams of togetherness.

By morning, Rio was alone. The dawn crept in slowly through the curtains and Rio could feel the lingering warmth that meant Agatha had stayed with her all night and left not that long ago.

It was enough to ease her into the day but not enough to make her forget the mixture of hurt and longing that settled in her chest.

She traipsed through to the kitchen she’d once considered her own and found everyone already there and various reactions to her arrival.

On a scale of indifference to Nicky it went Jen first, Alice a little ways away, Agatha much further along, and then way up in the end zone was Nicky who went to offer her a mug of lukewarm coffee he’d clearly been guarding.

“¡Buen día, melliza!”

Rio smiled and accepted the coffee but gave no other greeting to anyone else in the room. She had no interest in Jen and Alice right now and she couldn’t bring herself to look at Agatha.

“Drink up,” Alice suggested, “We should head soon.”

“Where’s Val?” Rio asked casually as Nicky’s protests died when she ruffled his hair.

A clatter near the sink told Rio that Agatha had dropped something but she was determined not to look and so didn’t.

Nicky went over to his mom and Rio took the opportunity to knock back her coffee as Jen explained she wasn’t needed that day.

Rio figured the real truth was that Agatha wouldn’t want her around now the agreement had been made that she was to be Rio’s PR relationship. But she couldn’t take any joy in Agatha’s discomfort because it was only a reflection of her own.

Leaving that morning was harder than Rio thought it would be. Mostly because Nicky didn’t want her to go and cried when she held him up so his feet no longer touched the ground and she hugged him tighter than ever before.

But the other thing that was hard was hugging Agatha in a move intended to reassure Nicky more than anything else. It was a quick, perfunctory hug. Barely a hug at all. Their bodies had touched, Rio’s hand on Agatha’s upper back, but that was really it.

Nicky hadn’t noticed, though. Maybe he was too concerned his melliza was leaving, maybe he was too convinced everything was okay now.

So Rio left with the memory of Agatha’s warmth but the reality of her coldness.

The paps weren’t there anymore but even this silver lining, Rio couldn’t enjoy. She had a drive home with Alice and two more weeks of intense filming with Agatha. Not to mention the weeks until they could be together; weeks of waiting and pining and raging.

“Can I get out of the movie?”

“Which?” Alice asked, tapping away at her phone as usual as the bodyguard hired to protect Rio, and paid for by Agatha, drove Rio’s car. Alice would come back to collect hers later and Rio was in no fit state to drive.

“This next one. Lucifer. I have no interest in being stuck in Kansas for weeks.”

“Arkansas,” Alice corrected, much meeker in the morning light than she had been yesterday evening.

“Whatever,” Rio muttered, turning her head to look out the window. “How long have you known about the Val plan?”

“A week or so.”

“And you announced it right when it would cause maximum damage. Nice.”

“Your reaction told me everything I needed to know about this whole fucking situation.”

Rio scoffed and turned to look at Alice, finding her already looking at her with her phone forgotten in her lap.

“I get it, you hate her. But I’m going to say this only once, okay? I can be mad at her. I can shout at her and scream at her and I can decide what I can handle and what’s too much for me but you don’t get to. You tell me where I need to be and what lines I need to learn and that’s it. Anything other than work, I no longer want to hear from you.”

“Rio.”

“I mean it, Alice.”

Rio turned away to look out the window again.

“I just think,” Alice said slowly, her tone slick with forced softness that made Rio’s skin prickle. “That loving her shouldn’t be this hard.”

“Then you’ve not been listening. Loving her is easy. Loving her is like breathing. Loving her is,” Rio turned back to Alice and laughed because how could the person who knew her best in the whole world not understand? “Loving her is keeping me breathing right now, Alice.”
