Alice looked away and Rio shook her head as she turned again. “I don’t know how you feel about Jen and I don’t need to know. Just like you don’t need to know about me and Agatha.”

“I do if-…”

“No,” Rio said, her fist hitting her palm. “I… I want to do to her what spring does to cherry blossoms.”

“What?”

“It’s… It’s Neruda! Read a damn book Alice.”

“What the fuck is Neruda?l

In any other situation Rio would have laughed and they both would have found it hilarious that Alice didn’t read and, usually, Rio didn’t either. But instead she rolled her eyes and threw her head back against the headrest and found nothing about it even remotely funny.

“He’s a poet. Quiero hacer contigo lo que la primavera hace con los cerezos.”

“Your grammar is so bad. That’s: I want to do with you what spring does to-…”

“Jesus, I know! I was trying to explain! I’m… Agatha likes poetry. I’m learning it for her. And don’t, don’t make fun.”

She turned to shoot Alice a pointed glare and Alice only nodded, biting her lip as she eyed Rio curiously.

“You’re learning poetry for her? You hate learning lines. And what the fuck does that one even mean? Spring to a cherry blossom? Is it a euphemism?”

Rio scoffed and rolled her head against the headrest to look out the window again.

“It means I can wait through the summer, through the fall, and through the winter. And when it’s spring again-...”

“Are you speaking in metaphors now?”

Rio scoffed and shook her head.

They didn’t speak much after that. And Alice didn’t come home with Rio. In fact, she got an uber back to Agatha’s house to pick up her car and didn’t even come with Rio to set that evening when she had to pull a nightshift to get through some scenes with Billy.

The next couple of weeks, her last on the set of The Price of Snow, were a blur. Each week was broken up by three things: seeing Nicky every Wednesday (she no longer gave him flowers for his mama), seeing her therapist, Christine, every Thursday (they spoke about different kinds of grief and what anger really was), and now sitting down with Alice every Friday morning to discuss future work plans (these meetings were tense and quick because Rio wanted to give in and Alice wanted to cry).

They were still furious with each other. Furious with themselves too. But they were those same alleycats who scrapped without their claws, unable to harm each other properly or for long.

This time they just needed some space because Rio didn’t want to hear anything against Agatha and that’s all Alice wanted to say.

On the second Wednesday after the time Rio was now referring to in her own head as the ‘incident’ had occurred, Nicky had come to set because his mom was working late and otherwise he wouldn’t get to see her.

Rio, who’d finished for the day, stuck around to hang out with him whilst Agatha was busy. And Val too. Val was always there. Their relationship hadn’t changed apart from one awkward and quick conversation that occurred in increments whenever Nicky was running after the ball.

They agreed this was weird, that it was stupid, but they were both okay with it and both had very clear boundaries. Hugging? Fine. Holding hands? Fine. Kissing? No. That was the extent of it, that was the worst of it.

So Rio continued to see her even when Nicky wasn’t around because Val, other than being her fake girlfriend, was chill and cool and her crisp British accent soothed Rio’s wired brain enough that when they worked out together she didn’t feel so unmoored and unhappy.

But this particular day, this warm Wednesday evening, Rio had some rare time alone with Nicky. She took him to the back of the lot where they’d once played basketball and broken an expensive light. No one was around, and there were no lights that could easily be harmed, so they began their game and crept closer to infinity with every point.

But after ten points in as many minutes, Nicky called for a time out and ran to their small pile of snacks. Rio had stopped production on any flowers but Agatha was still, via her son, giving her small piles of purple Skittles. And Rio always ate them and tasted grape with a side of guilt from each one.

“Mama said I should talk to you about something,” Nicky whispered, though no one was around to hear, after finishing off his little box of raisins. “But do you promise not to think it’s stupid?”

“I promise,” Rio said honestly, lowering her voice to a whisper too. “Is it stupid though?”

“I… mama says no. But it feels stupid. It feels… it feels scary.”

Rio nodded once, swallowing her last Skittle and wiping her hands as she turned to look at Nicky square on. She already knew where this was going.

“Then let’s talk about it, let’s see if we can make it less scary.”

“Okay,” Nicky took a deep breath and Rio watched as he dropped his gaze to the little red box in his hands and began to fiddle with it. By the time he spoke again he’d flattened it completely and was ripping the corners. “I have to… I have to speak in the court soon. In front of people a-and I really don’t want to but, but mama says I have to and she’ll be right there but… but I don’t want to do it.”

Rio nodded slowly, having anticipated this might be what Nicky was worried was stupid and scary.

She took a second and then gently stole the box from Nicky’s hands. “You know what? I also get scared when there’s a lot of people looking at me. I get nervous and sometimes shaky and… it doesn’t feel good.”

“Really?”

“Mmhm.”

“But remember that counting technique we’ve done before? Five things you can see? That helps. I also like to think about who I know in the crowd, so you can use your mom. And,” she held up the little squashed box, “the other thing I do is I hold something really tight and I put all my nervous energy into that.”

Nicky nodded and looked at the box.

“Like a toy?”

“Sometimes. Sometimes someone’s hand or a pen, even. Anything I have that I can hold.”

Nicky nodded again and thought for a second and Rio left him to his thoughts as she lay down beside him and looked up at the sky. Nicky soon joined her and cleared his throat.

Rio threw her right forearm up and across her forehead and seconds later Nicky did the same. They were two little ducklings, touching wings.

“Do you think I can take Scratchy to the court?”

“I think so.”

“People won’t think I’m a baby?”

“No, mellizo. What you’re doing is very brave. They’ll think you’re very brave.”

“Mama says so too.”

“And we listen to your mama, right? She’s very smart.”

“Very smart.”

Rio hummed quietly, watching the clouds as they traveled slowly across the sky.

“You know,” she mused, reaching her hand across to squeeze Nicky’s. “Everyone in that courtroom just wants what’s best for you. They all want to make sure you’re okay and happy. Your mom most of all.”

“Apart from daddy. I don’t think he cares that much about me being happy.”

Rio turned her head slowly to look at Nicky’s frowning profile and squeezed his hand. “You know you can tell them that, right? If you want to, you can tell them.”

Nicky nodded and Rio watched him frown up at the sky for a while before she turned to frown up at it herself.

“Mama said I can say whatever I want as long as I tell the truth. And that when we’re done we can have ice cream and…” he trailed off and Rio turned to look at him again. “What if I say the wrong thing?”

“Nothing you can ever say will be the wrong thing, mellizo.”

But Nicky was still frowning and went silent again so Rio turned to him and dropped his hand so she could lay on her side and watch him properly. “Tell you what, why don’t we have a day of just tres patitos when you’re done? I’ll get us the best milkshakes and we can build a fort and-...”

“Can we? And you can stay and we can live together in the fort maybe forever.”

“Maybe, mellizo.”

Nicky scrambled to sit up and just as Rio was about to be pounced on by an excitable eight year old they both turned to the sound of his name and the sight of Agatha standing a few feet away.

“Mama, come here!”

But Rio knew better than Nicky that Agatha wouldn’t come over so she sat slowly and brushed the dust off of her forearm.

“Hey,” she said as she turned to Nicky and he gave up waving Agatha over. “I’ll see you next week, yeah? In the park?”

Nicky blinked at her and then turned back to Agatha, who hadn’t moved since she’d shouted for Nicky. He seemed concerned for a moment and then threw his arms around Rio’s neck and whispered close to her ear: “Come home soon, please. We miss you.”

Rio squeezed him a second longer and then he ran off to his mom and waved goodbye to Rio when he got to her. Agatha, who didn’t look up once Nicky was with her, had already turned away.

Rio collapsed back under the clouds and counted down from a hundred until she was ready to go home. Once she got there she spent an hour making Agatha a flower made of three different colours: purple, green, and blue. It was the best one she’d ever made.

She took it to set the next day, her penultimate day on the shoot, a day she’d be with Agatha from dawn ‘til dusk, and maybe later than. It was one of the bigger scenes, one of the more emotional ones, followed by some background work that should take no more than twenty minutes for their coverage - they could get stand-ins for the rest of the scene.

So, because Rio had spent most of what was left of her evening making origami, she had to frantically learn her lines in the hair and makeup trailer. But she made sure to place her flower on Agatha’s usual chair before she did.

Nose-deep in her script, she almost missed Agatha’s entry. No one else did. Agatha still had a presence about her, and instilled fear and awe in most of the people who’d spent months primping, priming, and preening her. So the room went silent as it always did and Rio looked up just in time to see Agatha register that something was on her chair.

She watched her pick it up and inspect it for a second before she turned to the only person who could have possibly left such a gift. And when their eyes met the anger and tension between them faded into oblivion. Agatha mouthed “thank you” and Rio could only nod as she turned back to her script and felt the plucking of her heartstrings playing an unhappy, uncomfortable tune.

Rio was done before Agatha was and so left the trailer to start rehearsing her lines on set, to find her marks (green, always green), and to catchup with the DP on her latest exploits in the perilous dating world that was Los Angeles.

By the time Agatha was on set, the room was crowded with crew and cast members here to ogle the actress about to perform the big emotional denouement that was sure to be her Oscar clip. Rio could feel the thrum of nerves settling in her stomach as she prepared herself to be a tiny part of this bigger whole, a sounding board for Agatha to bounce her talent off of, and an actor in her own right just trying to match even half of what Agatha was about to bring.

Lilia was in the scene too, and was tucked up and ready in a hospital bed for the scene set in her hospital room. Maria, far more interested in Agatha, than either Rio or Lilia, was talking to Agatha, receiving instructions and notes from her before filming had even begun and as Rio watched her master at work she felt a gentle tug on her shirt that told her Lilia wanted her attention.

“Anger never got anyone very far, dear.”

Rio cleared her throat and looked to the guys hanging around with headsets to check if anyone was bothering to listen to the veteran actress and her co-star.

“Did she tell you?”

“Didn’t have to. You’ve barely looked at her for weeks now but… something changed a couple weeks ago. And nothing good.”

Rio shrugged and began to pluck at the prop blanket over Lilia’s legs.

“We’re doing our best.”

“Full of woe,” Lilia said softly, a gentle reminder of something Rio would rather forget. “Raised in it, married into it, don’t let her live in it.”

“I’m doing everything I can to-...”

“Not in the future, now.”

Rio looked up and Lilia’s dark eyes were boring into her, something Rio had never enjoyed about talking to the actress. She looked away and looked to Agatha instead, just in time to see her turn from Maria and make her way over.

Agatha had her eyes down and Rio knew it wasn’t a character thing, it was an ‘avoid looking at Rio’ thing. So she stepped back to her mark and she tried to quiet the voices that had been triggered by Lilia’s warning, as gentle as it had come.

The scene started and Rio was left to fend for herself as the behemoth that was Agatha Harkness started acting. As angry and as hurt and as lost as Rio was she was still in awe, always in awe of what Agatha could do in front of a camera.

Watching Agatha work was a privilege like no other. Even when she couldn’t bear to look at her under normal circumstances, when Agatha was acting she couldn’t turn away. She couldn’t stop to think about what was happening between them because Agatha was transforming the set around them into her own personal universe, her own terrarium of talent.

Rio’s only job was to react to her in this scene, to do what she could with the little she knew. She had to say her lines and hit her marks and otherwise get the fuck out of Agatha’s way as she delivered each line as if she were a real person, and these were real thoughts and feelings and words.

They ran the scene until the final part, the part where Agatha would have to break down and Rio would have to hold her through it. They ran it again. They ran it one final time at Agatha’s request, because Maria preferred fewer takes to preserve the truth of the scene, and Agatha didn’t much care what her director wanted.

So Rio found herself being moved by the very person she hadn’t touched since the night of their argument. Agatha, as gentle with her as always, moved her from her mark and placed her a good foot away from it. She told her to stay there, to move to her next mark which wasn’t where the green tape on the floor indicated but instead beside where Agatha would be standing. She then told her to stay directly beside her for the scene and then corrected herself and said: “no, stay where you would stay if it were me”.

Rio looked up for the first time to see Agatha looking at her properly. Her blue eyes were oceans of pain and Rio knew it wasn’t from the scene they were running. She could only nod, only silently promise that Rio would be the wife Agatha needed now, rather than just acting it.

And so they ran it again and Rio started from the place Agatha had told her to be, and then, a line before she usually would, she moved to Agatha’s side; directly at Agatha’s side.

She touched Agatha’s lower back, she stepped closer. She tucked her arm around her, she placed her other hand on her stomach.

She whispered her name - “Kate” - when it wasn’t in the script to. She reacted to what Agatha was saying as if Agatha were saying it, not as Kate, but as herself.

And when cut was called she held position and Agatha touched the hand that rested on her stomach and whispered, “Better.”

Rio held firm for Maria to come over with notes, every one of which Agatha rallied against or otherwise ignored. But Rio could only focus on Agatha’s hand over hers on her stomach and the burgeoning realisation that Lilia was right; anger would never help them.

They were told to move back, to run one more time so the cameras could capture everything now it was mapped out with new positions and new movements. So they ran again, with Rio even looser in her performance now; she had to warm up whereas Agatha had fresh legs from the out.

And this time they didn’t cut before the breakdown. Agatha just fell into it. She just allowed the energy of the scene, Rio’s hold on her, and the words she had memorised to flow through her. Rio watched from up close how Agatha turned her talent up to a hundred and knocked everyone onto their asses with a performance so awe-inspiring it was hard not to simply stare.

Agatha had to break down completely. She had to cry and scream and rage against her dying mother and Rio’s job was to hold her. Literally. She had to wrap her arms around her and eventually get her to calm against her body as the other cast members crashed into the room and took over the majority of the scene.

What that meant was that Rio soon had a sobbing, shaking Agatha in her arms. Something she was painfully used to, but equally something she’d never get used to.

And Rio, as the scene continued and Agatha turned into her more, found that she could no longer act it. This wasn’t Dani holding Kate, it was Rio holding Agatha. She held Agatha with all the strength she had in her and Agatha buried herself in Rio’s neck like she would if they were alone. Rio could feel her breath, hot and heavy, making her skin too warm and itchy. She could feel her lips brushing that same skin, making it grow hotter but soothing the itch.

She had a line to say but she couldn’t remember it because Agatha was still shaking, her lips were still against her skin.

Someone said something, Quill, maybe. Rio looked up at him, she frowned, she remembered: “Talk about my wife like that again and you’ll be sorry. I don’t give a shit if you’re her brother.”

Agatha squeezed her and then lifted her head and Rio turned to do what she’d do in any normal situation, in any real situation. She kissed her cheek and then wiped where she’d kissed and under Agatha’s streaming eyes. There was time, the scene would wax and wane with whatever Agatha Harkness or Rio Vidal needed.

It expanded around them, the camera moving to capture the moment of two wives exchanging nothing but a look that meant everything.

Agatha spoke her next line and the scene moved on but from then on Rio held her about the waist, and Agatha pressed back into her, watching her co-stars as her secret girlfriend held her. Rio spoke twice more throughout the rest of the scene and Agatha a good few more times and then cut was called and Rio was reluctant to let go.

But she did, only Agatha found her hand and squeezed it before she marched over to Maria to discuss the scene and have her makeup touched up.

Lilia called Rio over and Rio went to her without thinking.

“See?” She said, a twinkle in her eyes as someone adjusted her blankets for her and someone else fixed her hair. There was a third person mopping up Rio’s damp neck and checking her costume for wet patches but Rio was so used to being poked and prodded by crew she didn’t even look around.

“Better softer. It’s easier softer.”

Rio bit the inside of her cheek as someone took hold of her arm. To this touch she turned because she knew it to be Agatha.

“Closeups,” Agatha said quietly, her blue eyes darting between Rio and Lilia and then settling finally on Rio’s face.

They had to repeat what they’d just done, with no more emotion. Easy, really, when all that had happened had happened. So Rio held Agatha through everything. She reacted rather than acted, and hoped Agatha would be proud she’d somehow slipped her way into the Stanislavsky method without even trying.

The whole thing took five hours, with few breaks in between. Agatha kept marching back over to Maria between takes to demand a different camera movement or to suggest a particular lens when she thought the DP or the Cinematographer were being lax in their duties. And Rio soon found a perch to sit on with Billy and they both stayed there ignoring whatever Quill was yapping on about in favour of watching a master at work.

Because Agatha knew how to do everyone’s job better than even they knew and so it was fascinating to watch, and more fascinating to see how deferential people became when she approached them with demands framed as pointed “suggestions”.

With time running out, and union rules to adhere to, they didn’t have a proper break before they rolled into the next scenes. These were to be filmed with Rio and Agatha in a chair together and Rio knew they were soon to be shot when Pepper appeared on the set; all leggy and blonde and chipper.

“Sit,” Agatha barked just as Rio arrived at the chair by Lilia’s bedside. “Quickly.”

Rio did as she was told and sat, only to have the sudden but welcome shock of Agatha sitting on top of her not a second later. Her arms acted instinctively and she held Agatha tight just as Pepper appeared before them and Rio realised what the hurry was about.

She couldn’t hold back her laugh so hid it against Agatha’s shoulder.

“We should discuss how this is going to work. Maria’s happy so long as-...”

“I think we’re fine, thanks.”

Rio hummed quietly, and was made to move so Agatha could turn where she sat in her lap and slip down instead beside her, curling her legs over her and squeezing her shoulder beneath Rio’s.

Pepper watched them, raised her brows at Rio who just nodded her consent, and then left them well alone and watched from the other side of the room.

“They’re not even set up yet,” Rio reminded quietly, aware there were people who could probably hear them all over the place.

“We’re running the scene.”

“We’re asleep in the scene.”

Agatha scoffed and Rio turned to look at her as she raised a hand to toy with Rio’s collar. She was avoiding eye contact and Rio couldn’t really blame her. Not only had they fought, but since then Rio had gone back on her promise of giving Agatha flowers whenever she could.

“Did you like it?”

“The scene?”

“The… the flower? I figured it could be called el rosa patito. Green for me, purple for you-.”

“Blue for Nicky,” Agatha concluded quietly, her fingers now just making contact with the skin above Rio’s t-shirt.

Someone moved over to remove their mic packs and neither said anything as that happened. Then their hair was adjusted. Then a third person was over by them adjusting the plaid shirt Rio wore open over her grey t-shirt. Rio just held Agatha against her throughout it all. And she managed to remain still and unbothered like any other co-star might.

But shortly after the scene was called to start and when Rio’s eyes were closed she was no longer in a fake hospital room with dozens of onlookers. She was instead in Agatha’s office, sitting in her seat, there was a little bowl full of colourful paper flowers on the side, and there was a sleeping woman in her arms.

As the scene went on Agatha adjusted slightly and Rio with her. She moved enough and Agatha moved in tandem so Agatha’s face was no longer against her shoulder but against her throat. Even in makebelieve, Agatha had found her way home.

The scene started from the top because someone flubbed their lines and somewhere along the way Agatha began to nuzzle and made occasional soft noises against Rio’s skin. By the third go-round, Rio realised that Agatha had fallen asleep.

She could feel her soft, rhythmic breathing against her neck. She could feel the slow expansion and contraction of her ribcage. She could hear the noises that meant Agatha was slipping further and further into deep sleep; the noises that meant she was content and comfortable and safe.

Someone in the scene placed a blanket over them and Rio flexed her fingers, now invisible to the camera, to touch the soft skin available to her at Agatha’s hip.

She wondered if Agatha had slept properly since that night on the couch. Surely not, if she were so quick to fall asleep now, in a room full of people.

Cut was called and a PA came along to say they could leave because the stand-ins could do the work and they could be put in during post but Rio, eyes open now, refused and quietly said they’d stay.

Agatha was still fast asleep and it was the least Rio could do to let her get some rest. Besides, from what she’d heard of the scene Billy would keep them there all night so maybe Agatha would actually get eight hours by the time they were done.

So she settled back down once more and adjusted only slightly to hold Agatha a little more securely and Agatha mumbled something in her sleep when she did but otherwise remained pressed close and totally unaware.

Rio held Agatha for two hours. It was painful, more than it was comfortable. But not physically. Physically, Rio was more comfortable than she’d been in weeks. It was having to endure Billy flubbing his lines again and again that was the hard part.

Thank god Agatha was asleep or she’d have torn him a new one for holding up production.

But they got through it. The crew was moving on and so it was Rio’s job to wake Agatha without anyone noticing that their best actress had gone full method.

“Mi vida,” she whispered, because they were no longer mic’d. Agatha made a soft noise and Rio smiled as she pressed closer into her neck.

“Mi vidaaaaa,” she sing-songed, keeping her gaze up and round them to check everyone was occupied. “You fell asleeeeeep.”

Agatha grumbled and Rio knew she was rousing now so kept her mouth shut as she gave her a gentle squeeze and let her come back to herself in her own time.

“Shit,” she heard her mumble, and felt the last brush of her nose against her neck as Agatha pulled back and blinked slowly. “I fell asleep.”

“I know,” Rio whispered, taking the opportunity now Agatha was awake to slip her hand properly under her shirt and feel the heat of her sleep-warmed skin.

“How long?” Agatha asked, unfazed by the new touch. She was looking around them, trying to gauge the time or where they were in filming, or maybe if anyone was watching them.

“A couple hours. Billy kept fucking up.”

Agatha snorted and her head whipped around to look at Rio as Rio’s hand stilled against her side.

They were just inches apart with Rio’s hand on Agatha’s bare skin and Agatha’s body curled completely into Rio’s. This wasn’t allowed. It wasn’t in the rules of what they were currently trying to do. But it was hard to look away, so hard to do anything other than to lean in and simply give in.

“I need to leave,” Agatha breathed out, her eyes glazed over in the same way Rio’s must have been. “I… good job today.”

Such a formal dismissal for such an intimate time. But Rio watched Agatha leave with no way to call her back or ask her to stay. She sat a while under the warm blanket, and watched the movements of the crew around her, all organising for whatever was next for them.

Billy and Quill were still around which probably meant they had more work to do and Rio found herself, for the first time ever, feeling sorry for Quill. She just hoped Billy had a better grasp on whatever the next scene was.

Rio left the set around an hour after Agatha had. She wasn’t ready to be alone for the night so she hung around and gossiped with the PAs. After that, still reluctant, she went home.

When she got there she made a late night call to the one person she could talk to about all this.

And Val came over twenty minutes later.

Rio knew it was a little selfish, to call someone over to talk about someone else, but Val didn’t seem to mind. In fact she was more interested in Rio’s snack collection than anything else.

Plus it gave Rio a chance to find out how Agatha really was - “tired, quiet, still dances before dinner though, still smiles for Nicky”. Val scrimped on certain details though, telling Rio some things were off limits for them, like any court proceedings or anything to do with the official custody battle.

But still, Rio knew now that Agatha wasn’t eating very much. She knew she was spending most of her time on the phone to her lawyers or in her office with Jen. She knew that Agatha was asking after her when Val brought Nicky back from the park.

She knew that Agatha had suggested they film their latest trick so Agatha could see it and Nicky was excited to tell Rio about this plan next week.

Which meant that, despite their row, Agatha missed her. It meant that, when Val left after an hour of back and forth about Agatha and a million peanut butter cups eaten, Rio missed Agatha tenfold.

The next day on set was to be Rio’s last. So she wasn’t surprised to find that Alice was camping outside her house at five in the morning when Rio went to get her car.

“Truce? For your last day?”

Rio chewed on her lip, and wondered if she asked her bodyguard to jump Alice if he actually would.

“Don’t be like that! Hey, I have a fun pun I think you’ll like.”

“What is it?” Rio demanded, dramatically tapping her foot now.

“Well,” Alice said, a hopeful smile across her face. “You’ve got a Val Pal.”

“What?”

“Y’know,” Alice tried again, “Like ‘gal pal’ but like… Val.”

Rio stared at her best friend and watched the smile slowly fade from her face. Alice was about to open her mouth to say something when Rio began to march to her car and shouted over her shoulder. “I’m stealing that. Get in.”

The drive to set, now a pun had been exchanged between the best friends, wasn’t so lonely for Rio. Alice was still hesitant and Rio was still pissed but one soon got braver and one soon mellowed. Neither of them mentioned Agatha.

And Rio didn’t tell Alice that since her argument with Agatha she’d had near-nightly headaches and her therapist had suggested she go back on beta blockers. She also didn’t tell her she’d refused the prescription.

So her last day on set went relatively easily. Everyone was very excited because she was the first main cast member to be released into the wild. She’d arranged, or Alice had, for gifts to be handed out in the form of custom basketball jerseys with each person's name on them, alongside the name of the movie. And Alice too had arranged a taco truck to come to the set, which was a surprise to Rio who couldn’t help but tell her it was also vaguely racist.

But Alice laughed at her and Rio, softer with her friend again, laughed back.

Through all the joy of soon escaping her months-long commitment, there was an additional, shining light. Agatha was around all day.

She was there in the morning drinking her coffee and picking at her breakfast sandwich in the makeup trailer. She was there on the sidelines when Rio was shooting with Billy. She was there when the cast and crew broke off around lunch to play a farewell game of basketball in Rio’s honour. She was there when a wrap was called on Rio and Rio did the rounds of hugging everyone in sight.

She got to Agatha last, though had been sure she’d been standing somewhere in the middle of the room so she should have got to her ages ago.

But here she was; standing by the boom operator Rio didn’t know the name of but knew he had three kids and a parakeet, looking nervous.

Rio approached her slowly and to the sound of raucous applause she hugged Agatha and Agatha clutched at her in response.

It was common to cry on your last day on a film shoot. Most of the time it was because you were away from home and you’d spent months with these people and they became your surrogate family. But for Rio, on this set, working on this film had been some of the worst times of her life.

The start, when she had broken it off with Agatha. A few weeks in when she lost Miguel. And now, when things were rocky at best with the woman who now clung to her.

Now was when she cried. She cried into Agatha’s shoulder and heard a soft, rushed, “no” just as more hands and arms grabbed at them.

For some unknown reason, which later turned out to be Billy, everyone had decided to pile them into a hug. Rio didn’t want it. Agatha didn’t want it. But it was what was happening.

They were at the centre of it and being crushed by the love everyone had for them. Only it was too much for Rio. She hated attention she hadn’t sought. She hated the feeling of being constrained or restricted in any way and as her breathing picked up so too did Agatha’s hold on her and her sudden shouts to “get off”, “get off of her”, “hey! Off!”.

“Alright, everyone!” Peter Quill sounded above the rest, “Lay off the ladies! Give them some air to breathe! They’re only little.”

“Dick,” Rio growled, feeling a breath of warm air against her ear as Agatha laughed against her. It was all worth it then, the sudden tightness she felt in her body when she was unexpectedly crowded, the rush of blood to her head, the tingling in her toes. It was worth it because Agatha was still holding her and Rio had made this goddess laugh.

They pulled apart without either of them knowing who instigated it but both knowing they had to. But they remained together. Agatha tucked herself under Rio’s arm which remained around her shoulders whilst Agatha’s hold remained around her middle.

They were coworkers again, happy, friendly. Coworkers so deeply in love. It was spring and Agatha’s blossoms were in bloom.

It was Billy who led a charge of cheers for the departing hero. And Rio took it with the easy grin of someone who’d lived a much easier life these past few months than she actually had.

Maria brought out a bouquet of flowers and Stevie presented her with a Christmas sweater featuring a basketball wrapped in tinsel and the name of the movie across the back.

Agatha held her a little tighter when Stevie kissed her cheek.

There was more applause and then: “Speech! Speech!”

Quill. Again. “Dick.” Agatha this time. Rio laughed.

A gentle squeeze at her hip and then Agatha’s arms were gone from around her and she’d stepped back. Rio’s arm slipped from her shoulders but was caught again by Agatha who now held her hand.

Agatha knew, just like she did, that this was the end of their time together. They might not see each other again until everything was over and the battle was won.

So Rio swallowed the lump in her throat and was relieved as tears came to her eyes again that everyone looking thought they were for them. But they belonged to the person she couldn’t now look at, the one who held her hand.

“These past few months…,” she took a deep breath. Agatha moved closer and held her forearm and Rio knew she was covering the faint scars there with her warm hand. To her other side there was also movement and she turned to that to see Lilia arriving. She smiled tentatively as Lilia touched her arm.

She started again.

“These past months… have been the hardest months of…,” a hand on her shoulder, a soft squeeze. Alice now stood behind her.

She closed her eyes and let each woman squeeze her where they held her. Agatha’s fingers entwined with her own and she felt the warm metal of her promise ring as it pressed into her skin.

In turning to her and looking at her face properly for the first time all day she saw that Agatha looked as pained as she felt.

“They’ve been the hardest months of my life,” she said, still locked in on Agatha.

“And I couldn’t have got through them without,” a tear appeared on Agatha’s cheek and Rio must have blinked because she missed it first forming, “you.”

She turned from Agatha and looked to the people who surrounded her and attempted a bright smile but felt herself crumbling at the edges.

“It’s been a ride. A wild one. And I’ll never forget the kindness and the warmth of each and every one of you.”

Lilia squeezed her arm and Rio turned to her and allowed the old woman to rest their foreheads together. She closed her eyes and felt Agatha’s thumb brush over her own.

“Your cup runneth over with those who love you,” Lilia whispered, her breath warm and somehow reassuring against Rio’s flushed face. “Don’t forget that.”

“Three cheers for Rio!” A voice Rio didn’t recognise sounded somewhere before her but she was too focused on a hand as it curled around her cheek and brought her back.

It had been Agatha who’d brought her back. Agatha who now kissed her cheek as the cheers rang out, and Agatha who now stepped away and Rio had no choice but to watch her disappear into the crowd as Lilia and Alice held her in place.

So she’d come to say goodbye and left before Rio could thank her for it. If it weren’t for the hands holding her now Rio would have chased her. But instead she swallowed her feelings and forced a laugh as the cast and crew continued to shout their appreciation.

“And first round on me at the wrap party!”

More cheers, more hollers and wolf whistles and an unexpected teary hug from Billy, and then her time on set was over. It took three hours for Rio to get home that night. Alice was with her this time. Their truce had lasted and they got by by avoiding any mention of Agatha.

They toasted to the movie being over and sent a joint prayer up that Rio wouldn’t have to do any dreaded reshoots. Now free of any early morning obligation they drank expensive champagne and smoked a joint on Rio’s little terrace.

When high, and more relaxed than she’d been in months, Rio made her plans and Alice, just as relaxed, helped her to actually plan them. She would see Nicky tomorrow afternoon in the park with Val and then she would fly to London and plan for a life there where she would return to Agatha every night and take Nicky to school every morning.

It was a good plan, a delicious plan.

A plan that helped Rio on the journey to being ‘okay’; which was a state of being she hadn’t experienced in a long while.

The next day with Nicky was easy and good and she told him she was taking a little trip across the pond but refrained from mentioning that she was doing it for their future as a family. Nicky was more interested in the candy she could bring back anyway.

And in between moments where Nicky ran off for the ball she got tidbits from Val as to how Agatha was: “quieter than usual, the vultures are circling every day now”.

Rio knew this to mean the paps. She’d seen the pictures; the way Nicky’s face had been blurred out of the shots of Agatha taking him to school or the images of Agatha with her dark sunglasses on and her mouth tight as she pulled away from the house she’d bought to avoid this kind of thing.

The weight of them threatened to tug Rio back down into feeling useless and ineffectual. But as Nicky crashed into her for the umpteenth time that afternoon she knew she was doing all she could.

There would be time to defend and protect. But that time wasn’t now.

Now was the time to allow Val to film their latest trick; a maneuver that required Nicky run at Rio’s back and roll off of it like he was James Bond and Rio an Astin Martin. It was barely successful, even after seven attempts, but it was close enough and each attempt was captured on camera, which was really the aim anyway. Besides, she and Nicky were so giggly by the time they tried and failed their final time that neither of them even cared if they ever nailed this particular trick.

She said goodbye to Nicky with an extra long hug and an extra special flower to match. And for Nicky himself, she’d made a dinosaur out of light green card. And Nicky took it from her like she’d given him the keys to the city, or the championship trophy.

It took longer than usual to say goodbye this time round.

But, with a promise to bring back a whole suitcase full of candy (and British Skittles for his mom), Rio said her final goodbyes to Nicky and left with a heart full of knowledge that she was doing the right thing for their future.

The flight to London was uneventful. Rio chose to go alone, though was constantly accompanied by her new bodyguard. She trusted Alice to behave but she decided, as much as she hated to feel alone, that alone was what she needed.

It gave her time to think and feel everything she’d been suppressing or turning into tsunamis of pain in her already broken heart. That was, once she was able to shake off the paps who hounded her the moment she touched down in Heathrow.

She was still the ‘golden child’, afterall. Still an Oscar winner. Still someone the internet loved and the mainstream media used for clicks. Without Alice there to stop her she flipped the cameras off and kept her head down as she was hurried into her waiting car.

But Heathrow was the worst of it. She’d chosen to stay in a house in Dulwich Village that belonged to an old director friend who was filming in mainland Europe. It meant no nosey concierges or paps camping outside her hotel.

Which meant that the rest of her short stay in London went a bit easier. She was able to get around on foot in the warm-ish weather. Or else take the tube, if she was careful about keeping her head down and her cap on. A few times she was aware of people snapping pictures of her standing in the middle of the car but she never said anything and never offered to pose for selfies when she could help it.

She ate dinner out alone, sometimes with her bodyguard and sometimes, when he suggested he wait outside, she simply sat by herself. One night she met with an old friend and had drinks with her but otherwise Rio Vidal was all alone in a foreign city.

Alice kept in regular contact and, as if knowing her daughter was lonely, Anna called twice a day.

But Rio kept pushing through whatever encroaching loneliness she felt because she had a job to do. She had houses and apartments to see and questions to ask the well-meaning realtors who were showing them.

The first house she saw was in London Fields, near enough to the Lido. It was large and within budget at a little over $4.5m. The area was cool but quaint and Rio fell in love with the easy charm of East London until she dug a little deeper and realised the schools she had pinpointed to be the kind Nicky, and more importantly Agatha, would be comfortable with, were too far out.

It was this factor - the question of schools for Nicky - that made the search much harder. Rio fell in love with a lot of the places she saw. She was readily charmed by period features and open living spaces where she could practically smell Agatha cooking and hear Nicky’s squeals when the T-Rex came on the screen.

And so, after several properties across the length and breadth of London, she was close to giving up.

Until she found her house. The house. Their house.

It was located in the leafy suburb of Notting Hill, in the West of the city. Famed for its brightly coloured houses, the market and the Portobello Road, Rio found herself mesmerised from her first step.

Rio had been here before but seeing a place through the eyes of someone visiting was different to seeing it through the eyes of someone who would potentially live here. And now she looked at the fruit and veg stalls and thought of how she would pick up fresh herbs for Agatha every morning. She looked at the busy pubs and wondered which one could become their local.

She looked at the people who traipsed up and down the high street and wondered if she’d come to recognise any of their faces or to know their lives.

And once she finally set foot in the house she was here to view, she knew this was the one.

A Victorian townhouse arranged over four floors, it was all exposed brickwork and large glass windows. Still in keeping with the era it was built in, but with modern flourishes that made it bright and welcoming inside.

The living space had floor to ceiling crittal style french doors leading to the garden.. And the kitchen/diner was full of natural light and high ceilings. The shaker style kitchen was painted olive with cabinets that had fluted glass and a large butler sink sat on the marble worktops.

The dining room had a fireplace with a large marble surround and a cushioned fireguard that Rio could picture their excess of friends perching on when room ran sparse. On the upper floors the bedrooms were generous and Rio walked into each knowing who would be where. Nicky for this one, us for that one.

The garden was private out the back, with high hedges on either side and a taller red brick wall at the back so they’d have protection when the weather was warm and they were creeping ever-closer to infinity.

“It all for now appears to be injuries that will heal with time, but we need to do more tests to be sure. And the wrist, the wrist needs to be reset as soon as possible.”

“Is,” Alice uttered, unable to process the doctor’s words properly, “is she in pain?”

“She’s on a lot of meds right now so her pain will be minimal if anything at all. Before we take her in, would you like to see her?”

“Yes, I… yes.”

Alice grabbed the phone she’d abandoned on the chair beside her and took a deep breath as she followed the doctor out the little waiting room and towards the private room where Rio lay.

People moved past her but no one looked. The inhabitants of this hospital were used to the pre-mourners. They’d seen enough to know that misery doesn’t always love company.

Rio had been rushed into the hospital amongst a great deal of noise and chaos. Alice had missed most of it but she’d heard all about it from a chatty but well-meaning nurse that it had been the most exciting day she’d had on shift since that famous director had a heart attack two years ago.

Alice chose to ignore this and focus instead on getting to Rio as quickly as possible. Cedars-Sinai had a hush-hush policy about treating the very rich and the very famous and were a well-oiled machine when it came to hiding away the celebrities who needed treatment of any kind.

From babies to botched boob jobs, most celebrities could recover in the relative peace and privacy of the luxurious suites at the top of the hospital. And Rio, beaten and bruised as she was, was no different.

So Alice, as frightened as she was, at least knew they were protected up here. The people who rushed by in these corridors were used to the star power that the likes of Rio Vidal possessed. Rio wouldn’t be ogled and observed when she was at her very worst - at least within the confines of this hospital. Besides, Alice had already received word from TMZ that they had photos they intended to publish as soon as possible.

But Jen was dealing with that. Jen had been her very first call when she’d heard from Rio’s shithead security that something had happened.

She took a breath, took one glance at the doctor, and stepped into the room.

Rio was staring up at the ceiling, counting the small dots that were littered across it and in her hazy mind looked enough like stars to be some kind of distraction.

Her right hand, the one she couldn’t feel anymore, lay lifeless on a bracket, tied down by some doctor or other. She’d watched them do it, heard them ask if it was okay, if she could feel anything. But she’d been unable to respond.

Her other rested upon her stomach, tapping a soft pattern over the worst of her bruising, testing the limits of the local anaesthetic that had been injected more times than she could count. But less times than the stars that twinkled above her.

Why were they twinkling? What did they know?

“Rio,” Alice’s voice was tentative, and too soft to mean anything other than her friend was terrified. Even hazy, Rio knew her friend.

Rio turned to her, or, really, she moved her eyes rather than her head. And there she was, looking smaller than usual and so scared.

“Did y’call m’mom?” Rio asked quietly, her words tumbling out in a strange slur as she turned her gaze back up to her stars.

Alice’s mouth opened as she took in the sight of her lying all bruised and pale on the hospital bed.

“S-she’s coming. Rio,” Alice breathed out, as if Rio had done this to herself and she needed to be told how bad this was.

“‘N’Agatha. ‘Lease don’call Aga…. She’ll worry. She’ll be s’upset ‘n’-...” she trailed off, finding it an effort to say anything at all. But she turned her gaze back to Alice.

The instant Alice’s eyes flashed up to meet her own Rio just knew Alice had already made the call. She turned her gaze again to the ceiling and swallowed thickly when she felt a soft touch against her left arm.

“Wha’… wha’ did sh’say?”

“What do you think?”

Rio exhaled sharply, a short burst of energy she didn’t really have.

Agatha was coming. Rio knew it without having to confirm. She just knew she’d be coming. She wondered if she’d be draped in starlight when she came. Maybe the stars could slip down and cover her in their twinkle and Agatha could glow enough that Rio would never see darkness again.

Rio kept her gaze on the man made sky above and thought of the ocean eyes and how they’d look lit by these stars.

“She wanted me to tell you she-...” but Alice never finished her next sentence because the door to Rio’s room had burst open and there, in all her glory, was the madwoman that Agatha Harkness had become.

Rio tried to sit but underestimated how dosed up she was and flopped back onto the bed just as Agatha arrived at her side. Rio cried out but not from pain, from humiliation instead. Her body had betrayed her, nothing she’d done to get stronger had helped. She couldn’t protect herself; how in the hell was she going to protect Agatha? How was she going to protect Nicky? How would she keep her mom safe and her family together?

But Agatha didn’t seem to be worried about her own safety, or even her son’s. Instead she was frantic, her face and body unable to settle as she looked over Rio’s prone form lying in her hospital gown with wires and needles sticking out of her.

Agatha’s hands didn’t know where to settle and her mouth couldn’t form any words even as she tried to desperately say something.

So Rio said something for her, despite the indignity of it, despite the mental anguish: “Mi vida, I’m okay.”

Agatha either couldn’t hear or didn’t believe her. And Rio, despite feeling like she was simultaneously floating and buried somewhere deep within herself, she reached her good hand up and touched the side of Agatha’s face.

“Mi vida.”

“I’ll kill them,” Agatha whispered, her blue eyes finally settling and choosing to do so on Rio’s face. “I’ll kill them all. I’ll make sure they-...”

“Mi vida,” Rio tried again, as the very tips of her fingers traced the sharp corner of Agatha’s tight jaw, “I’m okay.”

Agatha wasn’t looking for reassurance, she was looking for vengeance. She was looking for something that Rio, broken in her hospital bed, couldn’t give her. She’d pulled back, away from Rio’s reassuring touch as if it had burned her somehow.

“Who did it? Who did this to you? Where are the cops? Have you-...?”

“Mi vida,” Rio tried one last time, wincing from the sight of Agatha so out of her mind and no longer paying any heed to the feelings in her own body. She wanted to tell Agatha to kiss her, so she could feel her lips just once last time before they took her away. But the words wouldn’t come.

Agatha swallowed. She stopped. She stood now two feet away from the side of Rio’s bed, staring at her but not really seeing her.

“I’ll kill them,” she said again, her voice back to a whisper, but there was a new tremor in it, and Rio realised that Agatha wasn’t angry, she was terrified.

Rio’s mouth wouldn’t move and her tongue felt heavy so she was silent as she reached with her left hand and held it out to Agatha.

And this time Agatha moved forwards. She surged towards her but stopped at the last second and delivered a kiss so delicate to Rio’s lips it almost felt like nothing at all. How strange, Rio thought, still unsure what her body was doing, to feel everything and nothing all at once.

“Love you,” Rio whispered, because that was part of the everything. And she could say it. She’d made herself say it.

“I love you too,” Agatha responded, adding to Rio’s everything.

Agatha’s shaking hand came to rest on Rio’s chest and she made a soft noise as Rio lifted her face to nudge their noses. It felt like a Herculean effort to do it; a simple gesture that she wanted Agatha to know she was okay.

“Are you in pain?”

“Mm.” Rio nudged her head to the side in a way she hoped read as “no”.

Agatha nodded, so close now that Rio felt the nod but didn’t see it because she’d closed her eyes. Agatha kissed her again and she felt her hand touch her in strange increments as it travelled the length of her abdomen and up to her jaw. The drugs had taken her best gift away from her; they’d denied her Agatha’s touch.

“I will find out who did this to you,” Agatha whispered as Rio began to cry silently. “And I will kill them.”

Rio shook her head again as best she could, trying to stop the tears from falling as she blinked through them to look up at Agatha once more.

“I g’ as good’s I got.”

“Rio.”

“I got in, t’, thr, g’d hits…look f’the guy w’the black eye an’, an’ wound’ ego.”

Agatha was the one to shake her head now and Rio, Rio realised what was at stake here. Agatha, drowned now in starlight that shone so brightly in the room that Rio could barely see her anymore. This Agatha, the one who walked amongst the Milky Way would be ashamed of her.

In her adrenaline-fuelled, pain-dampened, drug-induced delirium, she found herself in another panic that she was weak, ineffectual, unable to defend herself let alone the woman she loved.

She tried to sit up and an alarm went off somewhere that meant Agatha pulled away in a panic and two nurses rushed in and suddenly Rio was held down, was being checked over, and her tears flowed freely because she could do nothing about it.

Agatha, moved out of the way by a no nonsense nurse, raised a shaking hand to cover her mouth and Rio could only watch silently as she was poked and prodded and told not to move.

Rio closed her eyes again and heard the sound of someone else entering the room. Many someone else’s. She knew they’d come to take her away for surgery and she couldn’t stand to look to say goodbye.

She made noises that she meant to be a call out to Agatha - “vida, alma, amor, todo, estrella” - but the words got lost in her throat. Her fingers twitched and her eyes blinked and still above her Agatha was blinding.

But a hand, heavier than the nurse’s touches but infinitely more welcome, found her arm and Rio rolled her head and saw different stars as she did. She blinked again to see Agatha standing there, shaking, but strong. Only she wasn’t looking at her. She was holding on to Rio but looking at someone else.

“Credentials,” she snapped, half fury, half fear. “Now.”

The doctor blinked across at the actress and calmly said: “Mrs Harkness…”

“It’s ‘Ms’,” Agatha snapped, her fingers curling around Rio’s bicep. Rio wanted to say something but her tongue was still heavy in her mouth. “Credentials, now.”

Rio blinked blearily as the whole room fell silent and everyone looked expectantly at the grey haired doctor holding his scrub cap and looking more than a little frustrated. But she had eyes only for Agatha.

“Well, I…”

“If you so much harm a hair on her head I will sue the shit out of you and this hospital so spit it out. Quickly.”

“Estrella,” Rio tried, too hazy to use Agatha’s real name, or her preferred one.

But no one was listening to her anymore. Maybe she wasn’t even saying anything. Everyone was holding their breath and everyone was still. Agatha could change the temperature in every room she walked into. It was like magic. Some meteo magicko that Rio could only aspire to but never quite manage.

She realised she’d been wrong. Agatha was el sol, not just a star. She was the brightest of them all and everyone was lucky to be in her orbit. That’s what this must be, she thought, this spinning of the room. She was orbiting Agatha, stuck in her gravity and grateful for it.

And the room, far from feeling clinical and cold earlier, was now scaldingly hot. Rio felt it in the tips of Agatha’s fingers that curled beneath her arm. She felt it in the press of her palm as she pushed it against her.

Her sun was back. Her sun was focusing on her even as her gaze was elsewhere.

So Rio relaxed in her hospital bed amidst the solar storm.

Rio watched the man talk but could no longer make out his words. She assumed he was rattling off his degrees and the fancy universities from which they came but her attention was on Agatha’s hand as it crawled its way to her shoulder, and then slipped to the side of her neck. Agatha’s fingers were warm, which was unusual in itself.

And they buried themselves down where she could support the back of Rio’s head without even turning to look at her.

Rio’s eyes moved to Agatha and she found that she was looking at her now. When had that happened? A second ago…

Agatha bent down and kissed her, a firmer kiss than before. And Rio didn’t gasp or frown or do anything that suggested she was confused by it.

Because it had always made sense to her that Agatha would kiss her. That she should kiss her. In private and in public.

Her cheek felt wet.

And then Agatha was gone.

And Rio was in a long hallway, staring up at the ceiling as the faces of nurses in scrub caps looked down at her. There weren’t any stars here.

And then she was in a room and there was a blinding light. But it wasn’t her sun.

And then darkness.

Alice watched it all happen like she was in some strange nightmare. She watched the way Rio, her sister, lit up the moment Agatha crashed into the room.

It was the spark that lit a thousand neurones in her brain. Because Rio had looked like she was hell bound when she’d first seen her and when Agatha entered she’d looked halfway to heaven.

Alice knew Rio loved Agatha. She wasn’t blind and she wasn’t stupid, but she was family. And she was Rio’s closest family, the only one in the greater Los Angeles area who could protect her from harm.

Not that she’d been doing a good job at that recently.

For so long now Agatha had been the cause of her harm. Agatha had made her suffer when Rio was already suffering. She’d made her hurt and grieve when Rio had no energy left for more of those things.

But Rio hadn’t lit up when Alice walked in the room. She hadn’t tried to sit up or tried to get stronger or better instantly. And suddenly, the very first thing she’d ever thought about Rio, that she was a show off, was the very thing that made Alice realise that she’d been wrong this whole time.

She’d tried to protect Rio when there was no use, and she was causing her more harm than good.

When Rio was gone and all that was left was for Agatha to continue harassing the doctor in charge of her care, Alice stared at the speckled pattern of the linoleum floor. She heard snippets of the conversation: “I will sue you for all you’re worth” / “a routine surgery” / “the murmur is most likely nothing at all”.

It was another five minutes before Agatha let the doctor go so he could do his job in healing her friend.

The door closed and they were alone together for the first time maybe ever. Alice didn’t move but Agatha began to pace. And Alice, with every step she took, realised the depth of her mistake.

“You love her,” she said eventually, thirty paces in and countless seconds later.

Agatha didn’t respond but she didn’t need to. It hadn’t been a question.

“You called Anna?” Agatha asked, thirty paces later.

“She’s on her way.”

Agatha nodded once and continued her pacing.

“Does she need… Jen can get her a jet.”

Alice shook her head just once. “She’s got a ticket already. Next flight out.”

Silence again. Thirty three steps. The room echoed with the loss of Rio.

“The vultures are circling outside the hospital,” Agatha said quietly, and Alice heard a waver in her voice. “They… who found her?”

“A sick fuck who-...” But Alice didn’t finish her sentence because Agatha had already stopped pacing and was staring at her. God her eyes were blue. How did Rio manage to look at them longer than five seconds? It was like looking into the sun.

“I’ve got people on it. I’ve got Jen on it. The picture won’t see the light of day.”

“They took a picture of her? Before they-...?”

“Yes,” Alice said quietly, tasting vomit on her tongue. “Your man actually deleted it from the guy’s phone. He guessed it might have happened but TMZ have it and we don’t know if-...”

“He’s not my guy,” Agatha snapped, “He’s been fired. Dismissed from the firm. I should sue him, destroy him for-...”

“Rio would have told him to stay behind.”

“You’re saying it’s Rio’s fault?”

Alice shook her head and looked back down at the floor, “I just know her.”

“And I don’t?” Alice sighed and ran her hand over her face. She’d woken the beast. Jen always said that Agatha could turn on a dime, and she’d experienced it a little, but certainly not alone.

She cleared her throat and kept her head angled down like a guilty puppy.

“I just meant…” But she trailed off, not really knowing anymore what to say.

Agatha started pacing again.

“This heart murmur,” she spat after a while. Alice had counted forty paces. “Her dad’s heart attack…”

Alice looked up and saw a glimpse of Agatha’s pale face before she turned on her heel and paced in the other direction. Her fury was instead fear and Alice didn’t know which was worse.

“The doctor said it’s normal, relatively… relatively common but they’re running tests, an ECG a-and an echo and a CT. I gave her history and-...”

“Do you believe in God? Anything? I don’t know… crystals?”

Alice raised her brows and watched as Agatha picked up Rio’s running top that had been cut off of her and left on the side. She was running the thin, smooth fabric through her fingers, and when she lifted it to her face and closed her eyes to inhale Rio’s scent on it, Alice turned away.

She thought for a while, toying with her own fingers. She hadn’t been raised religious but she’d grown up with plenty crystals in the house. She’d gone to Mass with the Vidals but just copied anything Rio did and not thought much about what anything meant or the ‘God’ of it all.

But she believed in people. She believed in being kind and strong and showing up for those you loved.

“I believe in Rio and that she’ll get through this.”

It was the most, and the very least, she could offer to Agatha in the moment. And Agatha said nothing by way of response.

Alice continued to give her some privacy by keeping her head down and her eyes on the floor. So they were silent for a long while until Alice broke it. She’d been thinking about Agatha, about how terrifying she was, but how soft she sometimes became. How gentle she was with Rio, and with Nicky. She was thinking about this woman, so beyond scared and furious. She was thinking about Rio and how tender she’d been with her when she was first struggling to come out.

So she said what she thought was right. She said what she hoped would be a peace offering, an olive branch. Because maybe she’d been too harsh on Agatha, someone who had the spotlight on her, and a custody battle, and a bitch of a mother. Alice had only been an anxious teenager and it had been bad enough.

She swallowed, counted to five in her head.

“Maybe this,” she said cautiously, “maybe this will have been a good thing. A silver lining of sorts.”

“I beg your pardon?” Agatha’s voice was cutting and Alice felt it as it ripped through the air and sliced her square in the chest.

“I mean it… seeing you like this, for her… it’s made me realise…”

“I swear to God, Alice, if you finish that fucking sentence and suggest for one minute that Rio getting attacked and left for dead on a hillside has any kind of silver lining I will kill you.”

Alice looked up and she saw that the semi-tenative peace they’d established between them had been completely destroyed.

She looked away again and chewed on her lip.

Eventually, after what felt like a lifetime, Agatha took the seat beside Rio’s bed. Neither of them had said anything and Alice, in her peripheral vision, could see the way Agatha kept lifting Rio’s ruined shirt to her face, holding it there for a moment, and then pulling it away.

To distract herself from the waiting, she checked her phone. She saw missed texts from Jen, emails from press, from media outlets trying to understand what the hell happened to one of the brightest new movie stars. She saw that Anna had text and was on her way to the airport, and Mateo had tried to call her five times.

She excused herself to call Anna then Jen then Mateo. All were shaken, all but one on their way; Mateo was stuck at his work and unable to get any time off, even to visit his favourite cousin. Jen was already close by. Anna was at the airport

When Alice returned, she found Agatha crying into Rio’s shirt but said nothing about it and took up her seat again against the far back wall of the private room.

The doctor appeared an hour after he’d initially left, when Jen was already there and Agatha had spent the last half an hour barking instructions to her about shutting down any press, about sending out cease and desists, about suing this whole damn hospital and this whole damn staff.

The CT had come back clear, and Rio’s heart was thought to be healthy, at least enough for now for the surgery to go ahead. But she’d need regular checkups and an absence of stress in her life.

Agatha had been very quiet after that.

Another two hours of near-silence, just Alice speaking quietly to Anna and then Agatha doing the same when Anna asked to speak to her.

“Me quedaré con ella.” I’ll stay with her / “Estoy bien, cuidaré mejor de ella.” I’m okay, I’ll take better care of her. / “Gracias. Buen vuelo.” Thank you. Safe flight.

It was painful to hear Agatha speaking her perfect, quiet Spanish. She looked defeated and Alice had the decency to look away from her again when a single tear fell across her pale cheek.

But, three hours after she was taken away from them, Rio was wheeled back in.

“She’ll be out of it for another few minutes or so, max an hour. The damage was… extensive, but far from the worst we’ve seen. We had to put in a small metal plate. She’ll need to keep the wrist elevated and as motionless as possible and in a couple weeks we can take the cast off so she can get used to moving it. She’s fit and healthy and by all accounts,” he looked to Alice, “has an active lifestyle. So a removable splint for six weeks after that, coupled with some physiotherapy and she should be back to full strength in no time.”

Agatha was standing by Rio’s bedside, already holding her left, uninjured hand.

“For now,” the doctor said, unsure who he should be talking to in the room. “When she’s awake, in a few hours time, encourage her to move her fingers to keep them from getting stiff. We’d normally suggest she can go home but…” he looked at Agatha and looked nervous, “we’ll keep her in overnight and should be fine to release her in the morning.”

“Thank you, doctor,” Jen, the only one able to remain polite as Agatha focused on Rio and Alice stared at the floor.

“We can, uh, set up a cot in here if… if one of you is going to stay with her? Not usual, obviously, but we can make an exception.”

“I’m staying,” Agatha said quickly, leaning across to brush a strand of hair back from Rio’s face.

Alice looked up in surprise but the doctor didn’t seem to react in any way that would suggest Agatha’s quick response had alerted him to the fact that he was watching two people embroiled in a months’ long love affair.

“We’ll bring it right in,” he promised and then stepped from the room to leave them all alone, with Rio knocked out on the bed.

“Send for her shirt,” Agatha said after a few moments of silence, “It’s her favourite. She’ll want it when she wakes up. And bring in some snacks for her. The more sugary, the better. She’ll want something comforting. He didn’t say anything about her not being able to eat.”

“I’ll go,” Jen said quietly, standing so suddenly that Alice made a small noise of protest as she did.

Jen looked at her as if to say “it’ll be fine” and then kissed her quickly before she left. Alice knew it wasn’t a totally selfless move on her part. She’d been wanting Alice to talk to Agatha for weeks now. And she knew her girlfriend well enough to know that she was more upset by what had just happened than she was letting on.

So they were alone again, and Alice didn’t know what to do.

She sat in silence for a while, listening to Agatha whisper soft nothings to Rio. But after ten minutes of it, she had to move. She stood and made her way towards Rio, already grimacing for how pale she was. But the moment her fingers raised to touch the upper half of her injured arm, Agatha spoke again.

“Don’t touch her.”

Alice blinked and looked around at Agatha, now sat in her seat again, leaning across and holding Rio’s good hand with both her own.

“Why not?”

“Anyone who thinks what just happened was a good thing doesn’t deserve to-...”

“I didn’t say it was a good thing.”

“You said,” Agatha snapped, straightening up in her seat and releasing her hold on Rio. Alice glanced at her friend and then retreated a good distance away. “That the ‘silver lining’,” Agatha made quotation marks in the air, “to all this was that you now believe that I love her?”

“No,” Alice said slowly, feeling a bit sick, actually. “I just meant…”

But as Alice tried to find her words and Agatha continued to half-shout, half-hiss at her, Rio woke up.

It was slow at first, and her brain came to before her body did. In fact, it took close to a minute for her to be able to blink her eyes open but she slowly came around and saw a goddess in a plastic armchair.

Agatha was here? When did Agatha get here?

Rio grinned lazily, or thought she did. She wasn’t entirely sure what her face was doing. But it felt nice. Everything felt nice, actually.

She hummed, or didn’t, still not sure. But she was looking at Agatha, beautiful Agatha. Why wasn’t Agatha looking at her?

She said her name, or didn’t.

She stretched her fingers, and this time actually felt them stretch. Her right hand felt heavy but her left was closer to Agatha anyway.

She lifted it, and placed it back down. And then again. And one more time.

pat pat pat

Was she missing the bed? Was she not hitting it properly?

She looked down at her hand and stretched her fingers. They seemed to be working okay. Good, strong fingers. Fingers that could play a basic tune on a piano and catch a basketball and fuck a woman.

She smiled to herself as she placed them down on the bed and watched her hand do it again.

pat pat pat

There.

She looked up expectantly and saw that Agatha was still very much in the seat she’d always been in.

pat pat pat

Agatha didn’t move. But she was saying something, her head turned away, angled towards Alice.

When had Alice got here?

What was she saying?

Rio fisted the sheets on the bed and tried to tune in. Agatha looked angry, and not in a good, sexy way. She looked angry in a scared, teary way.

Her face was contorted and her jaw was so sharp it could cut glass. She wondered if Agatha would let her lick that jaw when she moved over. Surely she would. Agatha was generous like that.

But Rio forced herself to focus and watched her mouth move and spit fly from it but she still couldn’t work out the words she was saying.

“Mi vida,” she tried, unsure how loud her voice actually was or if it would carry. Apparently not, because Agatha didn’t turn around.

pat pat pat

Agatha still didn’t turn.

Rio’s heart rate began to pick up. Was she dead? Had that bright light before surgery been heaven? No. Her dad wasn’t here. Heaven would have her dad.

pat pat pat

Nothing. Agatha was still speaking, maybe shouting. Rio couldn’t make herself tune in.

pat pat pat

A beat.

Agatha turned. Sharply. Her eyes wide and her mouth open as if she’d been caught in the middle of a sentence.

pat pat pat

Agatha’s mouth moved.

pat pat pat

She stood from her seat.

pat pat pat

Her hands found Rio’s face.

pat pat pat

“Rio?”

A miracle, Rio thought. That she could hear again. That she could feel Agatha’s hands. That her patting had worked.

“My love? Are you okay? Did you just…?”

pat pat pat

Rio couldn’t hear her hand hitting the bed anymore because her fingers barely moved against it. She was too intent on Agatha, too intent on…

“She’s always been a lightweight.”

Agatha ripped herself away from her and all Rio could do was whine and try to grab her back. Her hand made contact with Agatha’s arm but her grip was too weak to be effective.

Not that it mattered, not when Agatha hadn’t really moved away.

All that had happened was she’d straightened up and was now looking at Alice with that same furious expression.

“I think you should leave, Alice.”

Rio was hazy still, so hazy that her hand was pinching pathetically at Agatha’s wrist where she was trying to hold on as she turned her gaze to see Alice, standing sheepishly at the foot of her bed.

“I just meant…”

“I know what you meant. You meant that Rio nearly being killed was a good thing and I should-…!”

Agatha’s head whipped round suddenly again and Rio beamed because she was looking at her once more; no longer angry, just, worried.

Her hands were on her face again, warm and welcome. Why hadn’t they been like this the whole time? Why hadn’t Agatha been over here the whole time?

“Honey,” Agatha whispered, and Rio realised that she wasn’t smiling like Rio was. Why wasn’t she smiling? What was wrong?

Rio’s own smile fell from her face as Agatha’s thumbs brushed over her cheeks in a steady rhythm.

“Honey, are you okay? Does it hurt? You’re barking.”

Rio blinked. She blinked again.

She suddenly realised why Agatha had turned to her so suddenly, why she’d moved over and was now holding her face. She laughed, proud of herself for getting Agatha’s attention even when she hadn’t been aware of what she was doing.

“Barking mad f’you,” she said, her grin now at full wattage as Agatha’s frown melted into a soft smile.

“Idiot,” Agatha whispered, the word so soft it felt like a caress. Rio moved her hand again, intent on holding Agatha’s to her face but her limbs were still heavy, at least, the three she could move right now, so she missed and caught her wrist instead. Which was okay. Some or any of Agatha was better than none.

“Siwime?”

Rio blinked in surprise at her own slurred speech but Agatha just smiled a little wider and continued the soft touches against her cheeks.

“There are too many wires, you’ve got too many bruises and-…”

“Please?”

Agatha’s gaze dropped to the mess that was Rio’s hospital bed and Rio looked down at the sight too. She was half-sat up, at a forty five degree angle with a pillow placed behind her head for comfort. She was still in her unflattering hospital gown and had the thin sheets tucked up to her waist. But more than that, worse than that, were the wires that seemed to sprout from nowhere all over the bed.

She looked like a puppet with an electronics fetish.

“There’s space,” Rio said, a little more aware and a little more lucid as the sight of herself brought her back down to earth and she could feel the heavy weight of right arm propped up on a pillow by her side. “There’s always space f’you.”

“You have no idea how,” Agatha said, stopping herself when Rio looked back up to her with a grin she thought was soft and hopeful but was instead dazzling.

“I’ll sit closer? Hold your hand?”

It wasn’t enough. But Rio, and the drugs that surged through her system, were dulled to any sense of true disappointment. And a pretty girl was offering to hold her hand, so she said yes, nodding like a dashboard dog.

Agatha, pretty Agatha, kissed her once and then moved away to drag her heavy chair across and she sat closer to Rio’s bed and took her one good hand.

“This is nice,” Rio said, always believing you should acknowledge when things were good, “being together. So nice.”

She looked down at the hand that held hers and hummed quietly, a soft tune that meant nothing much but felt good as the vibrations warmed her throat.

“Rio?”

Rio looked up at the sound of her name and saw Alice watching her from where she still stood at the foot of the bed.

“Are you feeling okay?”

Rio hummed, but not her tune anymore, just a soft noise that suggested she was thinking more than she actually was.

“Lil woozy. Wish I could move m’hand.” She went to move her arm from where it rested on the pillow and both Agatha and Alice made sudden movements that made her turn to the door, expecting someone had arrived.

“Honey, don't move it too much. The doctor said-…”

“That I sh’get what I want ‘cause I’m the patient?”

Rio grinned at Agatha, lolling her head around on the pillow behind it to experience how amazing pillows felt. She should buy more. She should buy Agatha more.

Agatha opened her mouth to say something, her eyes wide and, Rio realised slowly, teary. Her own smile faded and she began to frown as Agatha’s gaze drifted away to her elevated right hand.

Even high Rio knew what she was thinking.

“S’not y’fault,” she said without prompting and Agatha looked back up as Alice cleared her throat.

“R-Rio? I’ll, um, I’ll go see how long it’ll be until you can eat something. I’ll, yeah, I’ll give you guys a sec.”

Rio turned to her friend and smiled but Alice didn’t smile back. Her shoulders were slumped and she looked as if she’d been crying. Which made Rio sit up, only to be pushed back a moment later as Alice slipped from the room.

“Did s’thing happ’n?”

Agatha scoffed softly, her right hand on Rio’s shoulder.

“I’m going to stay here tonight,” Agatha said in response, confusing Rio’s hazy brain. “They’re bringing in a cot bed for me.”

“When there’sa good bed righ’ here?”

Agatha smiled and sat back down in her seat. “There’s not enough room.”

“Y’only little,” Rio countered, already attempting to shift over but stopping when Agatha was on her feet again and reaching for her far side to stop her.

“I’ll make sure the bed is as close as possible, I promise.”

Rio frowned and blinked slowly up at Agatha, suddenly aware that her eyes too looked raw from crying.

It felt a lot like Rio was on some fairground ride, and with every turn of the tracks, she was finding new information, new feelings, new context. And she couldn’t understand how she’d missed the tears that Agatha must have shed to look the way she did.

She didn’t understand why she’d been crying at all.

“M’vida,” Rio cooed, frowning when Agatha looked away, “Will y’love me even if I can’t move m’right hand?”

“You’ll be able to,” Agatha said quickly, “so long as you listen to the doctor and do your exercises and-…”

“Mi vida,” Rio interrupted smoothly, forcing her words out. “Can we laugh ab’t this?”

“Rio.”

“C’we snuggle up an’ m’be I can see las chicas an’-…”

Agatha pulled away then, and Rio felt the atmosphere in the room change as Agatha began to pace up and down along the foot of the bed.

“You went alone,” Agatha said, and Rio, unsure whether she was seeing right, thought she was crying again.

“Alone! Rio.”

“Yes.”

Rio’s left hand flexed and then: pat pat pat. Maybe she could get Agatha to come back again.

“Do you have a death wish? Is that… is that what this is? Your way of… I don’t know, being reckless with your life?”

“I…” Rio swallowed, her hand swirling and then stilling across the sheets. She didn’t pat again and instead watched Agatha wipe roughly at her face.

She used her sleeve to wipe away her tears and Rio blinked slowly as she recognised Agatha’s sweater. It was actually Rio’s sweater, one she’d given Nicky on the basketball court to give to his mom.

It looked bulkier on Agatha, too large to be anything other than comfortable. Too green to be anything other than Rio’s. It was evidence that Agatha carried her wherever she went and evidence that… she looked to the side and released a breath when she saw her locket there, its chain fallen haphazardly over the side, teetering on the edge.

“Death, I think,” Rio said carefully, focusing on each individual syllable, “is no parenthesis.”

Agatha, who’d been swinging this way and that in the small space she had for pacing swung around violently to a halt. And Rio turned to smile hopefully for her.

“Don’t joke.”

“Is a poem,” Rio said quietly, “One of the ones in the book I…” but she trailed off because Agatha hadn’t softened at all. She took a deep breath and then said: “If I die I won’t have you. I… all I want is you.”

Agatha dropped her gaze, her whole body seeming to calm down as she touched the footboard where Rio’s chart hung.

“You’ll do your physio? See the doctor more often? You’ll eat well and no more running the trails. In fact, no more running at all. You’re not allowed to go anywhere-…”
