Rio shifted where she half sat up and reached her heavy left hand towards Agatha.

“Come back? I’ll do anything you want me to if you just,” but she didn’t need to finish her sentence because Agatha was already moving towards her. She’d taken her hand before Rio had even blinked and was now sitting beside her hip, kissing over her knuckles.

“I love you,” Agatha murmured against her skin, a single tear slipping down her cheek that Rio couldn’t reach to wipe. “I’m so sorry.”

Rio stretched her forefinger to stroke Agatha’s cheek where she was still holding her knuckles to her lips and whispered back, “I’m sorry I scared you. I love you too. S’much.”

Rio, a little out of time still, began to frown as Agatha’s lips trailed from her knuckles to her wrist.

“What happened with Alice?”

“She…” Agatha sighed and then kissed the soft skin of the inside of Rio’s wrist and lowered her hand down to hold in her lap. “She said something… it doesn’t matter. I’m just… I feel like I need to kill someone and she was the closest person to me.”

Rio nodded and felt her brain bounce around in her skull.

“It would save me a lot of money if you did.”

Agatha laughed and Rio smiled at the sound. She looked bright again and Rio thought of the sun but she wasn’t sure why. As Agatha’s laughter died and her attention moved to Rio’s loose grip on her fingers Rio asked: “Does Nicky know?”

“No. I… I spoke to Val. I told her… I told her to tell him I had to work late. I’ll call in the morning and tell him you tripped or something.”

Rio nodded slowly and felt her brain bounce again, “And my mom?”

“She’s okay. She’s on her way.”

Rio nodded once more and looked down at the way Agatha was toying with her fingers.

“Tom shouldn’t be fired for this,” Rio said, feeling woozy still but knowing enough to know what Agatha would have already done. “It was my choice to go running alone.”

Agatha shook her head, “He shouldn’t have listened.”

Rio sighed and wriggled her fingers in Agatha’s hold to get her to look up at her.

“I could have taken them, you know. If they hadn’t snuck up behind me. I could have-...”

“Rio.”

“I’m serious. I could have-...” but Agatha had moved her hand up to cup Rio’s cheek and her thumb was brushing over a bruise that didn’t hurt because of all the meds Rio was on. Rio went silent and studied over Agatha’s pale features.

“Ralph will pay for what he’s done. For groping you. For this. I… I’ll make sure he loses Nicky and everything else he’s ever worked for.”

Rio frowned, hearing the danger in Agatha’s voice that was hidden behind a face so soft and so frightened. She would have leant in to kiss her but the door opened and Alice arrived back, carrying a tray full of food.

“I got you the mac and cheese, figured you’d need the carbs.”

Rio cleared her throat as Agatha rather abruptly took the tray from Alice and lay it gently across her lap. Alice gave Agatha a wide berth as she came around to kiss Rio’s unbruised cheek and whisper, “You feeling okay?”

“I’m all good, don’t worry.”

Rio, far from being left alone to feed herself, was treated to Agatha instead doing it for her. Similar to the barking of before, Rio’s little puppy tail was wagging the whole time. Even when she was subjected to the most bland mac and cheese she’d ever eaten.

“Vegetables too,” Agatha instructed as she held up a soggy piece of broccoli and Rio grimaced before she took it from the fork.

“Haven’t I suffered enough?” Rio asked once she’d swallowed it down. But Agatha only kissed her as a reward before she picked up the next piece. It was so worth it.

As Rio ate, a nurse came in to check her over and told her to keep wriggling her fingers to make sure they didn’t get stiff and had plenty of blood reaching them. By the time Rio was on the best part of the meal - dessert - a cot had been wheeled in with enough blankets and pillows to cover a very large King-sized bed.

Rio figured it was to keep Agatha sweet.

But a spoonful of something was being placed in her mouth as Rio’s attention was on the newly-arrived bed and she moaned for the taste of artificial chocolate on her tongue.

“Ohmygod, that is…” Rio’s head whipped around to a surprised Agatha now holding up a second spoon of delicious chocolatey goodness. “That’s so good.”

Agatha looked at it and grimaced, “Seriously?”

“She likes anything that’s bad for you,” Alice piped up, but was ignored by Agatha even as Rio laughed at her.

She was still grimacing as she held up the spoon to Rio’s waiting mouth. As she accepted it she hummed around it happily and Agatha arched a brow.

Rio swallowed and lifted her heavy left hand to poke at Agatha’s turned up nose: “I get it, only fancy sandwiches for you, mi vida.”

Agatha cracked a small smile just as the door to the room opened and Jen arrived looking harangued. “Fucking vultures. Fucking idiot nurses. Fucking, fucking-...” Alice ran to her and took the large bag from over her shoulder.

“Was it bad?”

“They don’t know what’s going on so they're camping out on the off chance they see something. Val said they’ve been outside the house all night and the fucking nurse didn’t want to let me through so I had to Google myself to convince her I knew you both.”

Rio laughed but Agatha scowled.

“Is Nicky okay?”

“Fast asleep. Val said he wants to come see Rio tomorrow and teach her how to tie her laces.”

Rio raised her brows in surprise as Alice chuckled and then stopped abruptly when Agatha shot her a look.

“My laces? I…”

“You tripped,” Agatha reminded gently, squeezing Rio’s hand as she put the pudding pot down on the tray.

Rio nodded quickly but realised she didn’t remember that conversation and blinked owlishly as if it might help her to piece things together. She was feeling tired though, and everything was still pretty hazy.

“Here,” Alice said quickly, watching her friend as she pulled out her cowboy shirt and handed it over. “And your college sweater and plenty of snacks and…”

“Maybe I’ll just…” Rio said, reaching across to grab to pudding on the side. “I think maybe just…”

But Agatha got there first and was already offering Rio a spoonful before she even registered what had happened.

“They’ve given her Morphine,” she explained to Jen as she dug the spoon in for more. “The dosage didn’t sound too much but-...”

“Okay, Dr Meredith Gay,” Jen said, causing Rio to choke a laugh around her spoonful of pudding and Agatha to smoothly flip her off as she fed her. “Forgot how much you loved that damn show.”

Rio raised her brows, enjoying this tiny piece of Agatha lore as she accepted another spoonful of pudding.

“We should talk about what this means,” Jen said soon after, her voice softer than before, as Rio took another mouthful.

“Not now.” Agatha, frowning into the pudding pot.

“Agatha, it won’t be easier later. If Evanora-…”

“It wasn’t my mother. She’s not an idiot. It was Ralph. If I know anything I know she’ll be furious and he’ll be hiding.”

Jen sighed, or maybe it was Alice, Rio was too focused on her next mouthful of pudding and how warm her thigh felt with Agatha sitting against it.

“But what can we do with it, Agatha? He can’t get away with-…”

Rio’s pudding cup splattered against the wall. Rio blinked. Her mouth wide open for her next spoonful. She blinked again. Why was her pudding slipping down the wall?

Something else was different. The bed felt different. She turned around and Agatha was no longer there. And then she realised what had happened and that her mouth was still expectantly open.

Just as she closed it again she tuned in to the shouting.

“You think I’m going to just lay back and take it?!”

Rio blinked, had she suggested she would? A vague memory, a feeling of guilt, had Rio said that?

“Agatha… there are sick people trying to recover from…”

“I don’t give a shit!”

“Mi amor,” Rio tried, her voice catching in her throat as she watched Agatha gesticulate wildly with her plastic spoon.

“Tell me again that I’ll let him get away with it! Say it again, Jen!”

Rio watched and saw Jen respond, saw the way Alice’s arm was across her, the way her friend looked terrified and the way Jen was yelling. Only, she couldn’t hear what she was saying. She could only hear Agatha.

She looked down at herself. Patting the bed was useless now. Her voice wasn’t strong enough. She had no way of making herself heard. At least, not without help.

With her good hand she reached for the IV in her right and thought about it for only a second before she ripped it right out of her skin.

A small fountain of blood squirted with it and Rio watched it like she were a tourist at the Bellagio.

“Rio!”, her name was shouted in such panic that Rio had no idea who said it. But then several shouts of her name sounded through the room and Rio looked up as a hand slapped down on the place where the blood was now trickling lightly down her arm.

“Rio, what the fuck?”

Agatha’s pale hand was pressing hard against her arm as the blood pooled in a slow trickle beneath her fingers. It didn’t hurt at all. In fact, it didn’t feel much like anything.

“I was trying to get your attention,” Rio said quietly, daring to look up and into Agatha’s concerned face as she perched on the edge of the bed.

The door opened and closed.

Agatha just watched her silently and Rio started to worry she’d done the wrong thing.

“I preferred the barking.”

Rio blinked stupidly and smiled brighter than she had all day. She released a little woof just as the door opened and Agatha put her non-bloody hand on her cheek.

“A bleeder? Those suckers need yanked out. Don’t tell me you did this yourself?” The same nurse who’d moved Agatha out of the way marched in and Agatha slipped from the bed but didn’t take any pressure off of Rio’s arm.

Still smiling, even as Alice moved over to Jen and Rio watched them exchange quiet words, Agatha was moved away again so that Rio could be seen to and her arm checked over.

Something was mentioned about bruising but she didn’t pay it much attention as her good hand was taken and Rio realised just how much she’d bled onto Agatha’s pale skin. She blinked down at her palm as she turned it over and frowned deeply at the sight of it.

“You’re bleeding.”

“Honey,” Agatha said quietly, her fingers curling in on themselves to squeeze Rio’s hand, “it’s your blood.”

“I’ll be back to get you hooked up again.”

Rio glanced to look at the nurse and by the time she’d turned back her hand was on Agatha’s cheek, and she could no longer tell whose hand belonged to who.

“I’m bleeding?”

“My love,” Agatha frowned, leaning into her touch, or her own touch, maybe.

Rio tried to focus in, looking between the hands on top of one another on Agatha’s face and the crook of her elbow that had caused the blood spill. There was a large piece of gauze stuck to it with some surgical tape. She curled her arm and it felt strangely tight.

“Rio,” Agatha said quietly, alerting her enough to make her turn back. Their hands were no longer on Agatha’s face but there was blood now, small spots of it on her cheek and jaw.

Rio’s eyes flitted between every spot of red and she frowned for the sight of them, reaching cautiously up to touch one close to the corner of Agatha’s lips.

“You’re bleeding,” she said quietly, feeling somehow woozier than before, maybe more tired.

“My love,” Agatha breathed, a soft gasp escaping her lips when Rio’s fingers brushed them. “I’m going to lay you down, okay? Close your eyes. You need to rest.”

Rio frowned but had no choice as her fingers slid slowly down from Agatha’s cheek and the bed moved back with her in it. The door opened as Rio tried to reach for the blood that splattered over Agatha’s cheek again but soon the nurse was fussing, setting up the morphine drip to Rio’s left arm.

So she just watched as Agatha hovered close and saw as she winced when the needle went back into her inner elbow. And she blinked and the nurse was gone; her hand was up against Agatha’s cheek again, and she was laying flat on the bed.

She blinked slowly, watched her thumb reach down for Agatha’s lips and watched Agatha turn her head to kiss it.

“You should sleep.”

“You’ve got blood on your face.”

“I know,” Agatha whispered, and Rio’s eyes felt heavy suddenly.

“Lemme clean it for you,” she said quietly, tracking her fingers down and along to her jaw. Had she licked here earlier? She felt like maybe she had. Maybe Agatha would let her lick it again.

“Go to sleep, Rio.”

Rio hummed softly, mesmerised by how her fingers danced along Agatha’s jaw. “Send them away.”

Agatha raised her brows and took Rio’s hand to hold so she could turn to dismiss Alice and Jen. Rio watched her do it, transfixed by her jaw and the profile of her nose.

But she felt Alice’s soft kiss to her temple and turned just in time to catch her soft smile as she left. Agatha must have asked them to turn off the lights because the room was now dimmed, lit only by the light on Rio’s bedside.

“Lemme clean you,” Rio said softly when they were alone and Agatha had turned back to her.

“Here,” Agatha whispered, cautiously holding up Rio’s fingers to her lips. Rio’s own parted as Agatha’s did and they became mirrors of each other. Only Agatha was welcoming Rio’s fingers into her mouth and Rio didn’t have the pleasure of tasting Agatha’s.

Rio instead just watched, mouth hung open, eyes wide as Agatha swirled her tongue around Rio’s willing fingers and slowly pulled them from her mouth again.

“Here,” she said again, directing Rio’s hand to her cheek and jaw so she could trace over the residue of her attention-seeking.

Rio closed her mouth and swallowed as she traced the red spots over and over until they faded into nothing. And Agatha, turning her head to taste her fingers again whispered, “all clean.”

She took Rio’s fingers back into her mouth and Rio whimpered for the sight of it, for the hazy way she felt feral for Agatha.

“Take off your pants,” she said quietly, staring at Agatha’s lips as they curled into a smile around her fingers.

She released them with a soft pop and then said, “no.”

“Please.”

“No.”

Rio frowned and looked up to Agatha’s blue eyes that sparkled even in the dimmed light.

“Then take off your shirt.”

“No.”

“Why not?”

“You need to rest.”

Rio hummed quietly and then the humming turned to a soft growling and she bared her teeth.

“Down, boy.” Agatha raised a hand to her jaw. “You’re not getting rewarded for hurting yourself.”

Rio narrowed her eyes but went quiet. “You weren’t paying attention to me. Didn’t think barking would cut it this time.”

Agatha’s eyes flashed and Rio moved her fingers to twist into the fabric of Agatha’s borrowed sweater.

“If I don’t shout I’ll murder someone.”

“I’d bail you out. Run away with you.”

“I know.”

Rio nodded gently, feeling the strange fizz of her brain again.

“Move to an island with you.”

Agatha hummed and Rio smiled.

“Raise Nicky to be an excellent man and have ten more babies with you.”

“And how would you manage that?”

“Spiderman.”

Agatha blinked and Rio’s smile grew.

“Pardon?”

Rio hummed as Agatha’s hold on her jaw slipped instead to her throat and it felt warm and welcome there.

“Pew,” she said gently, turning her fist into a Spiderman web-slinging fist against Agatha’s stomach. “Pew.”

“Honey,” Agatha said gently, a slight frown appearing though she was still looking at Rio with those soft eyes. “The tiny amount of blood loss really made you woozy, huh?”

Rio laughed softly and Agatha raised her brows as her thumb brushed a tender curve up and down her throat.

“Can I see the girls before I sleep please?”

Agatha said nothing for a second and even as high as she was Rio thought she was about to refuse but then, out of nowhere, she’d pulled back and lifted her sweater up to her chin.

“No bra!” Rio grinned, providing the service of a bra herself with one willing hand on Agatha’s right breast.

“That’s all you’re getting,” Agatha said as she dropped her sweater but Rio’s hand remained in place.

“Seems unfair.”

“I already told you,” Agatha said, gently pulling Rio’s hand away from her chest. “You’re not being rewarded for bad behaviour.”

“What if I promise not to be bad again?”

Agatha rolled her eyes and Rio pressed her hand into her stomach and made a soft, hopeful pew noise.

“Maybe Alice was right about you being a lightweight.”

“Maybe you should be best friends and then we can all be best friends.”

“You want to be my best friend now?”

“Actually,” Rio said slowly, staring down at her hand as it twisted the fabric of Agatha’s sweater. “Wife would be nice.”

She blinked slowly, as if she’d only just come to this realisation. And then she smiled, smiled because “wife” sounded nice. Just like Nicky liked “patito” and how “mi vida” sounded.

“Will you marry me,” Rio said quietly, looking up to meeting Agatha’s soft gaze, “Agatha Harkness?”

“Are you actually asking me?” Agatha’s voice was so soft, so incredibly soft that Rio imagined it as a feather, floating down from the stars up above.

“I’ll buy you a bigger ring than Ralph. Really big. So big you’ll-…”

“I don’t want a bigger ring,” Agatha interrupted, and Rio felt the feather brush her cheek as Agatha leant in, “I just want you.”

“You have me.”

Agatha hummed and Rio smiled as she kissed her, lingering for a while to nuzzle in.

“No more reckless behaviour. No more trying to be brave. And yes, I’ll marry you.”

Rio grinned, and Agatha kissed her again, this time pressing against the corner of her mouth whilst her nose squashed against her cheek.

“And we’ll have ten babies?”

“Mmm… as many as you want.”

“‘Kay,” Rio agreed, her eyes closing as she relaxed a little more. “Wife and kids for Rio. Who’d have thought.”

Agatha hummed and Rio felt it against her cheek. “Nicky’s pretty intent on it.”

“Yeah?”

“Mmhm. Mentioned it again just last night.”

Rio smiled but didn’t open her eyes and tugged a little at Agatha’s sweater. “Sleepwime?”

The bed dipped and Rio’s arm was moved up and then she felt the warmth of Agatha’s body against her own. She grinned into the darkness and felt soft fingers against her hip.

“He says he misses you being at home. And,” Agatha paused and Rio felt a hesitant touch over her collarbone, “He could see you everyday.”

Rio hummed and lolled her head towards Agatha and felt her tucked in below her chin. “Love him. Love you.”

“I love you too.”

Everything began to slowly fade away then. Until the only thing that remained was Agatha’s warmth. When Rio’s breathing was deep and even, Agatha moved carefully from the bed to instead sit on the seat beside it.

And she watched Rio for a while, monitoring the rise and fall of her chest and smiling for the soft snores she released every few seconds.

She watched her for close to an hour, unable to take her eyes off of the rise and fall of her chest; evidence she was alive, evidence she was okay.

Agatha sat through two checks on Rio through the night, allowing the nurses to touch her and move her injured fingers for her, when really she wanted to shout at them that no one should be touching Rio but her.

Only as the sun began to rise did she move from her seat again. She touched Rio’s warm cheek and marvelled at the heat from it. Even when recovering, even when she’d been beaten into the dust her skin was so warm.

She traced over Rio’s jaw and down to the curve of her neck. With each inch of skin she chartered she felt deeper and deeper in her bones how critical it was that she not only tore Ralph to pieces but that she pulverised him too.

Rio, the woman who would now bear the scars of her mother’s hatred and Ralph’s alongside them, still wanted her. She still wanted to marry her. She still wanted a future with her.

Her fingers trailed down to Rio’s collarbone, and danced slowly back up to the hollow of her throat where they paused for a moment before she dared to do the thing she’d been frightened of all night. She was careful, slow. She moved the sheets enough to lift them so she could look at the bruises that covered Rio’s legs. There was evidence of a larger one, deathly purple creeping out from under the back of her knee.

She didn’t dare look at her torso but knew there would be more bruising there too. With the sheets back in place and her heart up in her throat, she returned her attention to Rio’s sleeping features and smiled at the gentle sound of her snoring.

The woman of her dreams was battered and bruised because of her. She wondered how frightened Rio had been but knew it was futile to ask. Rio would never tell her because Rio knew that however she answered it would keep Agatha up all night.

Not that she’d been sleeping much anyway. Not that, without Rio, she had been able to get much rest.

Morning came slowly, and Agatha had slept for an hour, maybe two. Her body ached but not more than she could handle; not more than she could hide.

“Hey,” Agatha murmured, her breath warm against Rio’s knuckles, “buen dia, mi amor.”

Rio hummed and felt the scratch of her throat. But her needs were anticipated as a straw was held to her lips and Agatha kissed her temple as she drank some water through it.

“Need the bathroom,” Rio croaked when she was done, and it was then a strangely uncoordinated walk now she was no longer hooked up to an IV, to the small bathroom connected to the room. Rio was supported by Agatha and despite the new aches and pains now she wasn’t loaded with her meds, she enjoyed every second of it. And, Rio, unashamed of peeing in front of Agatha but very embarrassed that she was unsteady on her feet, frowned as she sat down and Agatha squatted by her knees.

“You don’t need to stay.”

“Making sure you don’t fall off.”

Rio huffed but Agatha leant up to kiss her and she was no longer embarrassed of anything. Even when she was done peeing, she’d wiped herself with her non-dominant hand, washed it in the sink with Agatha clinging to her like she was a flight-risk, and then was walked back to her bed.

Rio could feel Agatha’s eyes scanning her as she clambered back onto the bed and only when she sat did she turn to confirm her suspicions.

Agatha’s eyes were wide and glassy as they focused around Rio’s right knee. And Rio looked to it, moving her body to see the angle Agatha could see.

Creeping around the side of her knee was a large, ugly bruise. Before she could say anything Agatha had reached for the very edges of it as if to touch it might make it disappear.

“It doesn’t hurt,” Rio reassured as Agatha’s fingers traced the uneven line of it.

“When I get you home, I’ll run you a bath. I’ll…”

“I get to come home?” She hadn’t meant to sound desperate but what was the use in hiding it now?

“Your home,” Agatha said gently, “I want to stay the night again. I’ll help your mom and-…”

“Sleep in my bed?”

Agatha smiled a little and nodded. It was enough, Rio thought, as Agatha held up the straw again to let her drink, to have the promise of Agatha in her bed again. If only for one night.

“Your mom won’t be long and Nicky’s already on his way,” Agatha said softly as Rio adjusted her sheets when she was done drinking and winced a little. She looked at the mess of wires hanging around the bed and Agatha answered the question she was yet to ask: “The nurse came in in the night and removed them. You kept shuffling and… it made you more comfortable. They’ve checked every two hours so-...”

“You didn’t sleep with me then?”

Agatha looked away from Rio’s wide eyes and Rio reached for her hand, forgetting she had a bad one and using that first. Agatha held her fingers. It felt good that Agatha could hold her fingers.

“We need to move these so you can get used to-...”

Rio’s gaze had drifted across to the chair beside the bed, now she was a little more lucid, and everything hurt a little more, she could see how uncomfortable it looked

“Tell me you didn’t sleep in the chair?”

“It meant I could hold your hand in the night,” Agatha explained, and as Rio looked back up at her she saw how pale and exhausted she looked. Her stomach flipped and she felt a wave of nausea that was new, even with everything that had happened.

“Are you in pain? The doctor said you might be a little more uncomfortable today but in about an hour you can take some more meds but… I think he’s scared of me so…”

“I’m fine,” Rio said quickly, wriggling the fingers on her bad hand as if to prove a point. “Are you okay?”

Agatha didn’t answer immediately but there was a knock at the door that meant she didn’t have to and Agatha simply sat back down in her chair and continued to tenderly play with Rio’s injured hand as Alice and Jen entered.

“Hey! How’re you feeling, babe? Sleep okay?”

Rio smiled at her friend and reached over with her good hand for the styrofoam cup of hospital coffee she handed to her.

“Okay. Not in any pain. Can I be discharged?”

Alice shot Agatha a glance and Rio raised her brows, “Nicky’s coming and… I want to make sure that…”

“Agatha.”

“Don’t,” Agatha whispered urgently, and Rio knew what she was about to say. “Call me that.”

Rio sighed heavily but squeezed Agatha’s hand as best she could with her tender fingers.

“I’m fine. I’ve just got a broken wrist and-...”

“You were beaten up, Rio. You were left in the dust on a hillside to-...”

“The cops came,” Alice explained, looking between Rio and Agatha. “They’ve reports of two men running down the trail with balaclavas on.”

“...Big men?” Rio asked cautiously, hoping Alice would help win her some cool points with her girlfriend.

But Agatha wasn’t in the mood for it and stood suddenly, making Rio jump at the sudden movement as her hand was released.

“Can you be serious for once please?!”

“Agatha,” Jen this time, Rio wasn’t about to use her name again.

She shifted in the bed and watched as Agatha began to pace and wondered if Agatha had slept at all last night.

“You could have-! You could have died!”

Rio sucked in a sharp breath because she realised that if Agatha had been making light of this happening to her, Rio might have had the very same reaction. She swallowed thickly and gestured to Alice so she could take her coffee cup and put it on the side.

She then sat up straighter and felt the ache of her muscles from being laid down for so long and so bruised too. Agatha was at the foot of her bed, pacing back and forth with her hands in her hair and a look of such pain that Rio almost shied away from it.

“Mi vida, come here,” she instructed gently, holding out both hands. Agatha paced back and forth once more, twice more, three times more, before she simply turned on her heel and marched right over to Rio and in as gentle a way as possible she settled on the bed and hugged her.

Rio could breathe again.

Agatha cried against her until she was fresh out of tears and even then she pressed as close as she dared and Rio held her as close as she was able. The other two talked softly at the other end of the room, giving them as much privacy as they could without leaving.

When Agatha eventually pulled back, Rio found her lips before she found her own voice. She pressed into Agatha’s warm, wet face and whispered, “Don’t let this derail you. It’s what he wants. But all he’ll get is me with a broken wrist and what you’ll get is Nicky y estarás felizmente casado antes de que termine el año.” and you’ll be happily married before the year ends.

Agatha sniffed delicately and Rio kissed her again, smiling this time when she did. But her smile didn’t last long because what Agatha said next made her stomach flip and her throat constrict.

“Your heart, Rio. You have a murmur. It’s not serious and it… you’ll be fine so long as you keep healthy and… have no stress. But I want you to get more regular checkups.”

What was unsaid by Agatha read so clear to Rio: I’ve caused you stress, I’ve hurt your heart.

“It beats for you, you know,” Rio whispered, swallowing down her fear and thoughts of her dad. Her mom had always said she had his heart, maybe she’d been right.

Agatha nodded but not in a way that meant she agreed. Rio could tell she had more to say, and her feelings were overwhelming her so she couldn’t quite get it out.

“I’m sorry,” Agatha whispered eventually, “I was so scared… and your bruises, Rio. Those men hurting you and…”

“I know,” Rio murmured, doing her best to silently encourage Agatha to shift into her lap, but she didn’t seem to want to move and Rio wasn’t strong enough to make her. “I know. I’m sorry.”

“Stop trying,” Agatha mumbled against Rio’s cheek, and Rio scowled despite enjoying the closeness. “You’re too bruised for me to sit in your lap.”

“It’ll make me feel better if you-...”

“You two better not be about to get it on while we’re in here!” Jen, making Rio laugh as Agatha pulled back to scowl at her.

“Can’t you give us five minutes alone?”

“Oh?” Rio asked hopefully even as Agatha slid from the bed to sit on the seat beside it again.

“No sex,” Agatha said plainly, taking Rio’s good hand up once more and squeezing it as Rio scowled again.

“Just wait until this hand is-,” Rio held it up but Jen interrupted, “Woah! Enough!”

Rio grumbled but was placated just enough by Agatha lifting her good hand to kiss the inside of her wrist. She looked over to her and smiled, reassured by the sight of Agatha smiling back at her now, and the absence of any fresh tears.

Alice ran across then and adjusted Rio’s bed so she could sit up properly against it and generally started to hover around like an annoying fly. She was initially trying to help Rio drink her coffee but Agatha was quick to take it from her and do the honours herself.

“I can do it myself, you know,” Rio uttered after she’d taken her second sip with Agatha’s help.

“But I want to hold your hand and you need to keep the other one elevated,” Agatha pointed out, squeezing Rio’s good hand demonstratively.

So Agatha helped her finish her coffee and Rio got to hold Agatha’s hand for longer than she’d held it in weeks. She wouldn’t openly admit it, but she’d break another bone if she could get this sort of attention from Agatha again. She’d risk a heart attack if she could count those four freckles up close and kiss those lips.

Their quiet time together with Agatha helping her drink her coffee, and refusing to have any herself, was broken when a knock at the door brought the doctor and two police officers into the room. Agatha stood to attention like they were coming to arrest Rio, rather than ask for a statement, and Rio just held her hand tighter, trying to reassure her without doing so vocally.

The police were polite, and one of them was a little starstruck. Even in her current state it enraged Rio to see the younger officer eyeing up Agatha, who remained standing by her side, holding her good hand in both her own.

She gave as much information as she could but everything was blurry and when it came to describing the actual attack, she found it difficult to speak. Alice was crying by the wall with Jen’s arm around her and Agatha had gone stiff at her side. It was too much.

“Can I be alone, please?”

Everyone left but the doctor and Agatha and Rio had to squeeze her hand to get her attention.

“Hey,” she whispered, shaking their hands between them, “can you-...?”

“No.” The monosyllable left no room for argument and Rio didn’t have the strength so she turned back to the cops and relayed everything she remembered: “My back first,” she said bravely, trying not to look at Agatha as she spoke. “Then my, my knee. It was sharp, sudden. I fell and then,” she tapped her chest with her bad hand and winced for the memory and for the pain, “a boot to my chest. One of them hit my face and I fought back but I… I think they punched me in the, in the stomach and then I couldn’t breathe. I felt like I was choking and I…”

She remembered a deep voice: “A message for you”, but she didn’t tell them. She didn’t want anything that could link back to Agatha.

“Then he stood… he stood on my arm and then I… I don’t remember anything else.”

If it weren’t for her hold on Agatha’s hand, she knew Agatha would have dropped her. She was quivering, at least, her fingers were. She was barely holding on anymore and Rio didn’t know whether it was sadness or anger but she knew it wouldn’t be long before she found out.

A few more questions; ones about clothing or tattoos, eye colour, height, weight, questions Rio couldn’t answer. Then they were gone. The younger one not before looking Agatha up and down again as he left.

ACAB, Rio thought bitterly.

The doctor remained and checked Rio’s vitals before he gave her the new medication. She swallowed it greedily, needing to take the edge off the pain. It wouldn’t be as good as the drip, she was told, but it would help.

It was when he left that Rio found out how Agatha was feeling. She was feeling homicidal.

And she wouldn’t even look at Rio anymore.

Rio watched glumly from her bed as Agatha buried her fingers in her hair and proceeded to dig her nails so harshly into her scalp that she seemed intent on drawing blood.

“That man had his hands on me,” she said, her voice strangely flat. “On my naked body. He’s fucked me. He’s had his mouth on mine. I went back to him and because of that I ruined us. I wasn’t there when your dad died because I went back to him. And now he’s trying to take my son. And now he’s hired men to hurt you. And it’s all my fault. It’s all my-...”

Agatha was over the other side of the room. But Rio was too.

She’d slipped from her bed and made her way slowly across to Agatha and as Agatha had turned to pace in the other direction Rio had caught her. Their bodies collided like night meets day, melding into one another so the exact moment of contact is lost and all that remains is the new creation; dawn.

With their contact came realisation. For Rio, at least. Because she realised the guilt that Agatha carried was a heavy burden and Rio hadn’t been doing enough to help her balance the weight. With Agatha so often pressed against her whenever she could be, with Agatha kissing her as if they’d kissed for millennia, she often forgot that this was new. For both of them.

They hadn’t been together long. Not to mention compared to how long Agatha had been with Ralph, how long she’d been denying herself happiness, freedom, the chance to love and be loved.

And so Rio held Agatha even though it hurt and the pain meds barely took the edge off.

“I’ll kill him,” her sun raged, barely tempered by the swaddling of her night.

“And I will die before I let anything happen to you. Anything that will cause you more hurt or anything that means Nicky gets hurt. My body will heal. I’ll get strong again and you will fight this. The right way. Because you’re not a coward. And because we have barely begun.”

Her words were enough to get Agatha to bury her rage against Rio’s neck. It was enough now for Rio to pull her back to the bed and for Agatha to request to see Rio’s bruised body. It was enough for her to trace her fingers along every bruise and to kiss each in turn and for Rio to whisper she loved her after every one.

And then Agatha rested her head on Rio’s bare abdomen, hardly putting her weight on it. But it was enough to feel her, to be able to reach down and brush back her hair as Agatha looked up at her with her ocean blue eyes and her devastated gaze.

But like always, they didn’t have enough time. A knock on the door made Agatha redress Rio and help her to sit properly again just before Alice and Jen reappeared. This time, when Alice came over, Agatha didn’t intervene before she could hug her best friend.

Not long after Alice had retreated to the shadows again, the door opened and Rio smiled hopefully as a large balloon entered, being held by a little boy. Nicholas River Harkness clutched the string of his ‘GET WELL SOON’ balloon in one hand and held a large gift bag at an awkward angle in his other. Behind him, Val stepped inside and shot Rio a reassuring smile.

Nicky was frowning as he entered, not picking up what Rio was putting down with her expression. And instead of running straight to her he stepped towards Agatha and accepted her embrace even as he kept his cautious gaze on the patient.

“Hello, mama,” he whispered quietly, angling his head slightly into Agatha as she kissed his cheek.

“Are these for me?” Rio asked cautiously, her grin tempered as Nicky continued his frowning. She motioned with her good hand to the balloon and bag and it only drew Nicky’s eyes to her injured wrist.

A kiss to her cheek made Rio turn before Nicky could respond and she saw Val leaning over her with a look of disbelief. “She was right to fire him,” she muttered in greeting as Rio smiled up at her. “The one rule of the job. We’re looking for them.”

Rio shook her head in response just as she heard a noise on the other side of her and turned to see Nicky standing closer now and holding his gift bag up with what looked like a lot of effort.

“Are you in pain, melliza?”

“No, no pain. I’m glad you’re here.”

Nicky nodded solemnly, looking older than his years. “I got you a gift.”

Rio leant up but Agatha was quicker and gently took it from Nicky, reaching around him to do so.

“Come sit,” Rio instructed, making her patented pat pat pat on the bed beside her and expecting Nicky might jump up immediately but instead watching him look to his mom to check first.

“If you’re careful it’s okay.”

Nicky nodded, and, still clutching his balloon, he clambered onto the bed beside Rio and sat on the very edge of it, his back to her.

Rio looked at Agatha and saw she looked worried and then she looked to Val who was sat back in a seat, her eyes on Alice. And finally she looked to Alice who was staring determinedly at her phone.

With what little strength she had, she sat up, heard Agatha say her name in warning, but ignored it as she looped her good arm around Nicky’s middle and heaved him back against her.

It hurt. It ached like she couldn’t even explain. But Nicky had turned into her the moment he’d been pulled in and she knew she’d done the right thing.

“I don’t want to hurt you.”

“A hug from you could never hurt me.”

Nicky shuffled in and Rio shot Agatha a small smile despite the ache it caused to reassure her that it was okay. Agatha didn’t look convinced but she slowly lowered herself down into her chair and let them work it out themselves.

Nicky’s hand reached across to touch Rio’s cast and he asked: “Does this hurt?”

“No, bud. Doesn’t hurt at all.” She flexed her fingers of her right hand to prove a point and slowly raised her arm to angle towards him. “High five?”

“Rio.”

“It’s okay, I can still high five. Gotta keep practicing.”

Rio kept her eyes on Nicky’s frown instead of looking at Agatha and waited patiently for his response. But it didn’t come in the form of a high five.

Nicky had instead made his first sudden movement and twisted against her side to throw his arm over her in a half-hug. And Rio returned it. Fully.

She placed her injured arm cautiously on his back and Agatha stood up as if to tell her not to. But there was no telling her. She kissed the top of Nicky’s head and whispered to him: “Were you worried about me?”

Nicky nodded and Rio’s chest ached as Agatha’s hand touched the fingers of her right hand.

“The doctors and nurses have been taking really good care of me. And your mama too. I’ve already promised I won’t go on any more runs alone.”

Nicky took a deep breath and released it in a long puff of air against Rio’s shoulder.

“It’s okay,” he said quietly, and Rio’s eyes moved round to Agatha who was hovering close. “I bought something to make sure it doesn’t happen again.”

Rio arched her brows and Agatha looked as confused as she felt as Nicky pulled back enough to look up at Rio and Rio had to bite down on the inside of her cheek to stop herself wincing.

“I got you new sneakers.”

“Oh?”

Rio’s eyes darted up to Agatha again before focusing in on Nicky once more.

“So you don’t trip,” Nicky clarified quickly, his frown ever-present on his serious face. He shuffled carefully and reached for the bag that sat by his feet and removed something that was definitely not sneakers.

He instead had pulled out a cowboy hat and turned to Rio with it. “To make you feel better. More rootin’ tootin’.” The tone in which he’d said those last two words was certainly not rootin’ tootin’, but Rio didn’t comment on it.

She instead took it but before she could say anything Nicky had turned back around again and was pulling something else out that was, again, definitely not sneakers. This time it was a folded blanket with random brown splodges on it.

Upon closer inspection, when he handed it over to Rio who now sat in her cowboy hat, it was a blanket covered in horses and it was very, very ugly. So, naturally, Rio loved it.

“He chose it himself,” Val muttered, because Rio looked delighted but Agatha looked horrified.

“To keep you warm,” Nicky explained needlessly, “and because you’re a cowboy.”

Rio laughed and hugged the blanket to her chest with her good arm. “I love it, thank you.”

Nicky nodded seriously and then turned back to his bag to pull out her main gift: a blue shoe box. He rummaged for a minute and then pulled from it a pair of sneakers. They were high tops and white, with green front quarters.

And they were Velcro. They were also ugly.

“He also chose them himself,” Val muttered again, making Rio’s smile grow impossibly wider.

“Do you like them? This way… this way you won’t trip again and get hurt.”

“I love them, mellizo. You’re so thoughtful.”

“Okay,” Nicky said, dismissing the compliment because he had more important things in mind. “Maybe you can try them on and see how they feel and… when you’re all better we can still play basketball please?”

Rio’s shoulders deflated slightly where she’d sitting up admiring her new gifts and she turned to Nicky who was watching her with that deep frown again.

“We’ve got one rule in town, there mister,” she said in her best southern drawl as she transferred her hat onto Nicky’s head. “And that’d be no frownin’, ya hear me? Upsets Miss Agatha over yonder.” She pointed at Agatha who looked like she was struggling not to laugh, but she’d fixed her face by the time Nicky had turned around to her.

He whipped his head back around once he’d confirmed Rio’s words.

“No frownin’,” he repeated with as deep a frown as ever. “Got it.”

Rio laughed and steeled herself as she tugged him back into her side and as he settled in she motioned with her bad wrist to the blanket.

“Somebody tuck us in, please. These cowboys need some rest.”

Alice moved to help but Agatha beat her to it and practically hissed at her to get away. It was as Agatha was tucking Nicky in that Nicky giggled for the first time since arriving and Rio looked to see why, and then she saw that her bare feet were sticking out from under the ugliest blanket in the world.

She wriggled them and Nicky giggled some more.

“Mama could you put Rio’s sneakers on for her please? See if they fit?”

Rio hummed happily, much more content now Nicky wasn’t frowning… not that she could see anyway with his stetson on his head.

Agatha raised her brows but did as Nicky asked and Rio soon had two brand new, velcro shoes on her feet.

“They’ll keep you safe,” Nicky said proudly, and Rio looked from her sneakers to Agatha as she remained at the foot of the bed watching the two twins in their ugly blanket.

“Well I love them,” Alice announced, moving into Rio’s line of sight with a very fake, very large smile. “They look so good, Nicky. You’ve got such good taste. Must get it from your mama!”

Rio raised her brows at this strange fake-cheeriness from Alice. It was a classic brown-nosing technique. A terrible one. And Agatha saw through it immediately even as Nicky grinned and agreed that his mama did have good taste.

“Actually,” Alice announced, drawing attention to herself which was unusual in the first place, “I have an announcement!”

Rio blinked up at her and Nicky sat up straighter under her arm. Val, for some unknown reason, stood from her seat and hovered closer to Agatha. Jen just rolled her eyes and remained where she was. And Agatha looked pissed.

“Rio has a new movie!”

Rio raised her brows, too slow to think of what movie Alice was talking about.

“I do?”

“Mmhm. Next summer.”

“What is it?” Nicky asked excitedly as Val shifted where she stood and Rio turned to watch her motion with her head to Agatha who took the instruction and went to stand beside Nicky.

“Well,” Alice said dramatically, her face unusually contorted with such a brilliant smile. “She’s going to be in the new Jurassic Park!”

Whatever Val had picked up on had been right. Because Nicky had jumped and Rio had screeched when he’d pressed his little hand into her stomach and had put his full bodyweight against her. Agatha had been quick, but not quick enough and the result was Alice being banished from the room as Rio fought against the tears to try and get Nicky to sit back with her under her ugly blanket.

“No,” Agatha insisted, as Alice hung her head and stepped out the room, followed swiftly by Jen. Agatha had a tight hold on a distressed Nicky and Rio refused to stop reaching for him.

“It’s fine, mellizo. It’s just a bruise that… it’s just a bruise.”

“I didn’t mean to. I’m sorry. I’m so sorry. I…”

“It’s okay,” Rio and Agatha soothed together, only Agatha could kiss Nicky’s head and hold him close and Rio was left aching in the bed, frowning across at the sight.

“She wouldn’t have meant to-…”

“Don’t excuse her,” Agatha snapped and Rio shrank back. “She’s trying to win points and I’m sick of people trying to win points from me when-…”

Agatha seemed to know she’d gone too far or was saying too much. She closed her mouth and looked away and Val left, muttering something about checking on Alice, when really she was just too British for the amount of emotion on display.

“Mi vida,” Rio said softly once the door was closed and only the tres patitos were left. “It’s bruising, nothing’s broken.”

“That isn’t the point,” Agatha insisted and Rio’s gaze dropped to her tight hold on Nicky who had his face turned as best he could towards her.

Rio smiled sadly and adjusted herself, so much so that Agatha began to protest. She sat up properly, crossed her legs beneath herself and turned, pleased to be able to do this now she was free of the wires that had previously tethered her.

“You should sit back,” Agatha said firmly, not softening at all as she stared Rio down.

“Actually. I want a hug, please. And I’m not moving until I get one. On top of that I want you to fetch the nurse and get them to come in and redo my cast. I want a purple and green one. And then I want you both to sign it and then I want another hug and-…”

“Rio.”

“No. I deserve this. This is what I want. A hug and a green and purple cast.”

Rio put her hand down on the bed. No one moved. She raised it again and then, pat, pat, pat.

Agatha was first to move. She had to be. She was holding Nicky close. She released him slowly, and Nicky moved carefully to straighten and turn properly to Rio.

pat, pat, pat

“Rio,” Agatha said quietly, the warning there but distantly.

Nicky stayed where he was and Rio wondered why her new summoning technique didn’t actually work.

So she barked. She made a soft, high-pitched ruff sound. And then, a miraculous sound followed it.

Nicky giggled.

And then, as Rio made a soft ruff again, Nicky followed it with a quack.

Rio gasped in delight and Agatha rolled her eyes as she let Nicky go totally and Nicky took strides towards the bed as Rio patted it again.

pat, pat, pat

“You’re going to be in Jurassic Park?”

Rio quacked happily and made a mental note to put it on her resume that she could do a solid duck impression.

She quacked again and then barked when Nicky was giggling and clambering onto the bed. He howled like a wolf and Rio barked a laugh at the sight of his face to the sky and his arms out as if he were soaking up the moon to elongate his howl.

“So good!”

Nicky finished when he could no longer breathe and giggled when he shuffled close and Rio opened her arms out to him.

“You’re being reckless,” Agatha said as Rio accepted Nicky into a gentle hug and looked over at her as she did.

“You can tell me that as you hug me.”

Nicky hummed happily and Rio smiled crookedly, leaning against Nicky’s head. Everything kind of ached. Everything felt hazy still.

“Mi vida,” Rio tried again, holding her injured hand out to Agatha and wriggling her fingers. “Please, baby.”

But Agatha didn't move and soon Rio’s smile faded and she sighed quietly as she gave Nicky a gentle squeeze and then released him.

“Hey, have you tried their pudding here? It’s so damn good. Why don’t you go and get Val? She can get you some pudding and you can find a nurse to help change the colour of my cast, okay?”

Nicky agreed and shuffled back until he could step from the bed. Agatha caught him before he left and said, “let me see you with Val first, okay?”

He nodded and hurried to the door. Rio kept her eyes on Agatha but Val stuck her head in moments later to confirm she had Nicky. But Rio was just focused on Agatha and Agatha was focused on not losing it.

“Mi alma,” Rio whispered, “mi todo, mi corazón, mi ángel.”

Agatha didn’t look at her and instead put her head in her hands. Rio moved the blanket to throw over her shoulders like a cape and held it up and open, hoping it would be inviting.

She couldn’t have realised she looked a fright. Death warmed up, that’s what she was. Her usually bright and warm skin was somehow sallow, edging on grey. Her hair was lank and her eyes only half alive with whatever she felt for Agatha, dulled by pain, fear, meds.

“Mi Vida,” Rio breathed, her arms aching even though they’d barely been held up longer than a minute. “Please.”

Agatha moved, but slowly. She stood from her seat and kept her gaze down as she knelt up on the bed and shuffled close enough so that Rio could close her arms around her and Agatha could lean in and hold Rio’s face.

It felt like something had switched. Or maybe Rio was just lucid enough now to understand that something had. Either way, she remained still, deciding now wasn’t the time to bark or quack.

“Baby,” Rio managed to say, “I’m okay. I’ll be okay.”

“You could have died.”

“But I didn’t.”

Agatha shook her head and her hands fell down to Rio’s chest, her gaze hovering around her collarbone.

“I want you to move in with me,” Rio said softly, unsure why her whispered words had made Agatha’s face scrunch up and her head drop down. “My house is smaller,” she continued, trying to act as if Agatha hadn’t started to cry. “It’s in a busier area. There will be more eyes on you and Nicky. And it’ll be harder to-…”

“Rio,” Agatha interrupted, lifting her head up. “You don’t mean it. You don’t mean-…”

“Come here,” Rio commanded, but gently, pleadingly, she reached for Agatha’s waist and with her good arm she tried to loop her in but it only served to make Agatha kneel up so she was above her but not on her.

“You don’t remember what you said last night?” Agatha asked, wiping quickly at her eyes but not fast enough for Rio to miss the tears.

She forgot sometimes. She forgot that Agatha was so soft and so vulnerable but that she never showed that to anyone other than Rio.

“I’m sure I said I love you,” Rio whispered, reaching for Agatha’s cheek, “and that I wanted you to sleep in the bed with me. And that I miss you and-…”

“Enough,” Agatha said quietly, resting down on the backs of her ankles now.

“Mi vida,” Rio whispered, “don’t pull away please.”

“If I’d pulled away months ago this wouldn’t be happening.”

Rio felt woozier now than she had in hours.

“You did pull away months ago,” she reminded gently, “and you came back. Because we belong together. You and me. You and me and Nicky.”

Agatha’s head dropped once more, but this time against Rio. This time she pressed in and Rio was able to wrap her in her ugly blanket and hold her as best a woman could with a healing wrist and a bruised body.

Agatha’s tears were thick and silent against Rio’s neck but Rio collected them all, a heavy price for such a gift. She held Agatha as tight as she could, and as close as Agatha would allow.

And when Agatha had cried herself out, when she dragged her face up to Rio’s and kissed her lips, Rio knew she wouldn’t pull back. She knew those days were behind them and, hazy or not, their future was them together.

“Let me carry it,” Rio whispered, “all your pain and guilt and fear. Let me help. Talk to me about it.”

“It’s all my fault.”

“Nothing is your fault. I will be better at staying safe. I will let ten men and their guard dogs follow me around if it helps us to be together sooner. I will do whatever I can.”

Agatha didn’t say anything else for a while.

“That blanket needs burned and those shoes are ugly. My son has horrendous taste,” Agatha uttered after so long of silent tears and Rio’s silent hope.

“This blanket is beautiful and it is mine. No burning allowed. Nicky has incredible taste. I’m going to call up Mr Versace and…”

“Donatella,” Agatha corrected, “You can’t be an Ambassador and not know that.”

Agatha smiled, Rio could feel it against her skin, and shook her head but said nothing more about it.

“Think about my place,” Rio said quietly, her own smile softening. “It’s there for you if you ever need it.”

“Let’s focus on you getting home and getting better,” Agatha murmured, pressing a lingering kiss to her throat before she pulled away and wiped her tears on the ugly blanket.

“Hey,” Rio protested gently, “No snot on my lovely gift.”

Agatha soon stepped from the bed and Rio was left alone in it again until Nicky arrived back carrying two pots of pudding and followed by Val, Jen, a nurse, and Alice with her tail between her legs.

Rio shot her a small smile but Agatha didn’t even look round.

For a while it was peaceful in the little room. Rio got her wish of a cast wrapped first in green and then in purple. And Nicky, who’d been silent and polite as he’d watched the nurse work her magic on Rio’s cast, was gifted a coloured piece of green gauze to be safety pinned around his wrist so he could match his melliza.

Agatha was silent for the most part during this time, listening to whatever Val was whispering about in her ear. Alice and Jen were silent too, tapping away frantically at their phones. And Rio, Rio was making conversation with the nurse, trying her best to make everything feel normal, regular, and not as horrendous as it actually was.

Five minutes after the nurse had left her with her fancy new cast, and after Nicky had decorated it by drawing a duckling in black marker and signing his name beside the words ‘tres patitos’ right next to Agatha’s swooping ‘John Smith’ signature, Anna arrived in a flurry of rapid Spanish and touches to Rio’s face and arms. Rio didn’t miss that the moment her mom entered the room, Agatha had stood to attention again and had brushed down the wrinkles in her sweater.

And for a while everything was okay again, because her mom was here. She had her whole family, the most important ones at least. Everything would be okay.

The pudding they had helped too.

Agatha and Anna disappeared for a little while after that and Rio was left to discuss dinosaurs with Nicky and an Alice who was sheepish still but eager to get Nicky on her side if she couldn’t get Agatha.

“It’ll be four months in London. And-...”

“London?” Nicky asked, a soft sort of worry in his voice as he toyed with the fabric of his new arm band.

“Hey,” Rio reassured gently, “I have a house there. Or I soon will,” she looked to Alice who nodded her confirmation. “You can visit whenever you want.”

Nicky relaxed a little after that and they soon made a game of throwing grapes into the trash can in the side of the room. Nicky got a few in but Rio’s aim was totally off and she blamed the meds for it.

Rio had one final checkup before the doctor and physio who gave her some exercises for her fingers and arm. Only then would the doctor allow her to leave but it wasn’t as easy as that. Both Agatha and Anna wanted to talk to him out of earshot of Nicky, and Jen and Val had their heads together discussing exit strategies. So Rio, now with Alice perched the other side of her, and Nicky still under her arm, just sat like three lost boys, waiting on their fairy dust.

The hospital had a back entrance which had paps parked outside but not nearly as many as the front. So that was to be their route. Agatha and Anna and Jen would take Nicky in their convoy and Rio would go with Alice and her already-assigned new bodyguard. Apparently he was bigger than the last, a point Agatha was quick to make when Rio asked his name and whether he liked sports.

Agatha was the one who remained in the room when Rio was to get changed. Jen had brought some clothes with her so Rio could at least have some dignity when leaving the hospital. Agatha was slow and gentle and touched every one of Rio’s bruises as if her touch were healing. And really, it was.

The final piece of the project Put Rio Vidal Back Together was putting her locket around her neck and tucking it below the collar of her favourite shirt that smelled like Agatha.

“You’re not in pain.”

“No, not much.”

Agatha nodded. They kissed. They said nothing else to one another as Agatha gathered her things and Rio hovered close by, wanting to say something but knowing not what.

The journey back home was uncomfortable and more stressful than Rio expected it might be. They managed to shield her and Agatha with Nicky under large umbrellas but the paps were still there, they were still insistent.

Rio’s new bodyguard was indeed huge. He was blonde too and just so happened to be Val’s brother, the strangely named Thor. It meant he could be more trusted, Agatha had suggested when he’d first been brought up. Because Agatha trusted Val with her heart; she protected it, she protected Nicky.

Miraculously, Rio’s home had been spared in the assault. No one was waiting for them on the quiet little street and so they could all pile in, Nicky waiting to take her hand by the entrance so they could go sit on the couch together and compare their new coloured cast and fake bandage.

And for a while Rio was alone with Nicky and they put on Celtics highlights on the tv and Rio felt like she’d been left at the kids table whilst the adults discussed more important things in the next room. It wasn’t an uncommon feeling. She was used to this happening at family events and she didn’t mind it but she wished she could hold Agatha’s hand through whatever hard things they were discussing.

Maybe an hour after they’d arrived, Jen, Alice, and Val left.

And Rio, intent on finding Agatha and making sure she was okay, left Nicky on the couch to do so. She found Agatha sitting with Anna on the small couch in her little sunroom where the piano was and she sat back against it as she watched them ignore her presence and continue their little chat in soft Spanish. They were holding hands and Agatha’s shoulders were slumped, far from her usually perfect posture.

Only when Nicky came in to see where everyone was did they look up. And Rio smiled hopefully, receiving a small smile back from Agatha that didn’t quite meet her eyes.

“I know what we can do,” Rio announced, holding her arm up to wriggle her fingers. “I need to move my hand anyway. Allow me and Nicholas here to treat you two to a beautiful piano recital.”

“I can’t play piano, melliza,” Nicky stage-whispered as Rio pulled the stool out from below the fall board decorated with three ducklings.

“That’s okay, neither can I.”

She plonked herself down and after a quick pat, pat, pat Nicky joined her.

She wondered if Agatha’s smile had reached her eyes yet. She wondered if she were still holding her mom’s hand. She wondered if she could even remember the notes of Chopsticks.

It took a second, and Nicky watched her closely as she tried to get the tune right, both of them sitting with their tongue sticking against the inside of their cheeks.

Nicky was a natural, or, at least, better than Rio. He picked up the bass notes quickly and soon they had run through two rounds without breaking.

Nicky soon got the hang of the base rhythm and his frown became a smile as Rio nudged their shoulders. “A virtuoso!”

He laughed and stopped his playing, “What does that mean?”

“It means,” Agatha said, interrupting before Rio could speak, “That you are so clever.”

Nicky’s laughter turned to high-pitched giggles as Agatha tickled his sides and kissed his cheek. Rio was grinning at the sight until Agatha turned to her and kissed her cheek too, lingering a little longer than she had with Nicky.

“And you’re pretty smart too.”

Rio hummed happily, lifting her chin like a proud puppy. “You think so?”

Agatha tapped her nose, a grin playing at the edges of her lips. “Maybe more like a handsome dummy. A very handsome one.”

Rio laughed and Agatha’s grin won out. It was mesmerising under any normal circumstance but up close, especially now, it was hypnotic. Rio found herself moving to it, she wanted to capture it, to feel Agatha’s grinning lips against her own.

And she almost did. But Agatha swerved at the last second and Rio received a conciliatory kiss by her ear and a tender reprimand of: “dummy.”

Rio cleared her throat as Agatha moved away and turned her attention to Nicky who was gently pressing the keys again, figuring out the rhythm in as quiet a way as possible.

“Okay!” Rio announced, throwing her hands in the air dramatically. “Let’s go, mellizo.”

It took a while but with a little adjustment and a lot of easy patience, they soon got the rhythm of it and Agatha and Anna were treated to the longest continual rendition of Chopsticks ever heard.

A hand on her shoulder is what alerted Rio to anything other than the staccato tune she was creating with Nicky and Rio glanced to the side as she continued to play.

“Siéntate con ella, hija.” Sit with her, daughter.

Rio raised her brows and her fingers faltered as she looked properly at her mom and then turned to look around at Agatha.

Agatha was teary, but there was a small smile on her face and Rio stopped playing the instant she locked eyes with her.

“Okay, mellizo,” she said, turning back to Nicky, “my mom’s going to teach you something even better, okay? I’ll watch with your mom.”

“Si, claro,” Nicky offered up, making Rio laugh as she stood from the bench and Anna say something in proud Spanish as she took her place.

Over on the small couch Agatha had held her hand up towards Rio, impatient to have her close again as she made her way over. Rio was pulled down beside her, but gently, and Agatha adjusted herself so Rio had enough room to get comfortable before she pulled her down.

Rio was a little sore all over, a little out of it still. The mixture of pain meds she was on made everything hazy around the edges. But Agatha’s lips against her cheek, her hand in her own, they softened everything even more. The haze grew gentler, less fuzzy and more welcoming. Maybe it was just that she hadn’t felt so relaxed in so long.

Her mom was playing a soft tune and Nicky was providing the bass notes to it. Agatha was cautiously pressed against her side and toying with her fingers and the sun was streaming in, warming the little room enough to lull Rio into a dreamless sleep.

“Hey,” Agatha’s voice came into her consciousness and Rio grunted. The room was silent now, and not as warm as it had been.

“How long have I been out?”

“A couple hours,” Agatha whispered, her hand warm on Rio’s cheek. “Come eat something. Then I’ll take you to bed.”

“What?” Rio frowned as she blinked her eyes open. “No, I… I’ll stay up. What time is it?”

“Just gone seven.”

“Too early,” Rio protested, frowning up at Agatha’s soft face. “I’ll eat and then we can canoodle on the couch?”

A laugh that Rio grinned at and then: “With your mom and Nicky close by?”

“Oh,” Rio said quietly, “Maybe not.”

Agatha hummed and Rio hummed right back, wanting to feel the mutual hum against her lips. But Agatha only floated near and didn’t allow them to touch.

“Nicky’s excited for dino nuggs,” she said with a winning smile as she pulled away and helped Rio to her feet. Everything ached, everything felt stiff, and as she walked alongside Agatha, also excited for dino nuggs, her gait was strange.

“Are you-...?”

“Yeah,” Rio was quick to say, waving off any questions. “Just my knee… Little stiff, that’s all.”

Agatha didn’t look convinced but said nothing else on the matter as they walked together to Rio’s kitchen and were greeted by a delighted, nugget-eating Nicky and a concerned Anna.

“I gave you the bigger plate, melliza.”

That was all Rio needed to hear to make the pain and aching go away. That, coupled with the sounds of Agatha and Anna yapping away in Spanish over dinner, meant that Rio could sit in virtual silence and munch away on her nuggets and fries.

The only pauses in her devouring of the beige meal were when she swapped dinosaurs with Nicky. He preferred the carnivores and who was she to deny a little boy the chance to rip the head off a T-Rex?

When Agatha and Anna had finished their quinoa salads and Rio and Nicky were done with their nuggets and their large bowls of ice cream, they all moved through to the living room where someone had already laid out blankets and extra cushions.

Anna and Agatha made quite the fuss of making sure Rio was surrounded by soft things from all sides but Rio protested because that would mean she’d be trapped in a prison of fluff rather than anywhere near Agatha. A compromise was made so all parties could be happy.

Rio could sit in the soft middle of the couch, her new favourite hideous blanket over her and her arm in its purple and green cast raised up on a cushion by her side. Nicky could sit beside her, his own arm up and resting beside hers like he’d been injured too. And then Agatha, the last but potentially most important piece of the patito puzzle, sat on Rio’s other side, holding her uninjured hand.

Rio kicked her legs happily, and almost asked her mom to go fetch her new sneakers for her. But refrained because Anna had already done too much.

So, with her broken wing beside Nicky’s unbroken one, and her other feathers being held by Agatha’s, she settled down and focused on the feeling of being comfortable, full, and warm.

“I thought,” Agatha said, speaking in English for the first time since they’d started their meal. “We could watch your SNL episode?”

“Oooooh,” Nicky cooed from beside Rio as Rio looked panicked.

“What? No I think-...”

“Me gustaría verlo de nuevo.” I’d like to see it again.

Rio turned to her mom. Anna was looking at her with a smile that was expectant; as if she knew Rio would give in.

She cleared her throat and Agatha murmured, “You’re so good. Let’s watch it? As a family?”

How could she say no to that? How could she deny Agatha anything when she said things like that?

She nodded once and heard Nicky squeal excitedly beside her. A moment later the tv was on and Agatha was controlling it, settled in close to her side.

Rio watched as she cycled through to find the episode and held her breath as brass sounded and the camera dipped towards her as she entered the stage.

“So handsome,” Nicky whispered so loud they could all hear.

“La hija de su padre.” Her father’s daughter.

Rio grinned toothily at her mom and Agatha kissed her shoulder.

“Sí, el Señor Miguel también era muy guapo.” Yes, Mr Miguel was also very handsome.

Rio’s smile softened as she saw the look on her mom’s face and then dropped her gaze down to the coloured gauze still wrapped around Nicky’s arm.

“Very handsome,” Agatha agreed quietly, squeezing Rio’s arm as Rio moved her fingers to tap Nicky’s gently in thanks.

“Your Spanish is getting good, mellizo. Better than mine.”

“Not hard,” Agatha murmured, but then tugged her sleeve as Nicky beamed proudly and the Rio on the tv started to speak.

Thank you! Thank you! Wow, what a dream. What an honour. I am so happy to be here with you all!

Rio grinned at herself on the tv and Agatha settled closer to her. She remembered how she felt the night of the taping but couldn’t feel anything other than comfort right now. It couldn’t be the meds. This was real, true comfort that could only come from being home, being surrounded by the people she loved.

The sketches moved from whacky and weird to more real and tempered. Rio played a politician with a moustache and a monocle. She played a weather forecaster who cries every time it rains. She was a knight who spoke in corporate buzzwords, a nanny with a fear of children, a basketball player who’d superglued her hand to the ball. And every one of the sketches, to varying degrees, worked. They were all funny. They were all weird enough that they carried and Rio was reassured of that fact with every soft huff of laughter from Agatha and every giggle from Nicky.

“Maybe I’m not so bad at the old comedy thing,” she said as the credits rolled and she stood thanking the cast and audience in her ‘AGATHA HARKNESS’ tee.

“Maybe not,” Agatha agreed, yawning quietly beside her and shuffling a little closer.

Anna came over to kiss her face and after doing so, held it as she whispered: “Tu papá estaría muy orgulloso de ti.” Your dad would be so proud of you.

It was enough to make Rio well up, to make her lean into her mom’s touch and squeeze Agatha’s hand harder for the support. Nicky’s fingers found her elevated ones and she was held by all three of them in some tiny, gentle way.

Anna, not as much a fan of showing emotion as Miguel had been, kissed her daughter one last time and then took her seat up again.

“¿Quizás la película de dinosaurios?” Perhaps the dinosaur movie? She asked after sniffing a little and wiping her eyes.

“Me gustaría mucho,” Nicky said shyly, and Rio laughed a little as he turned to her with a proud grin.

“Good Spanish, mellizo.”

They all settled again and by the time Rexy had eaten her goat, Agatha was laying in Rio’s lap, her head on her thigh as Rio played with the ends of her hair. Nicky whispered continued commentary through the movie and Rio responded in kind, knowing that Agatha had fallen asleep to the sounds of it. Apparently being a mom to a young boy meant you could sleep through incessant chatter and dinosaur noises. Then again, she’d not slept at all the night before.

Nicky, too, was asleep before the end, and Rio tucked him under her arm as her eyes drifted from the screen to her mom who was watching them instead of the movie.

“Conseguí una foto.” I got a photo, she held up her phone and smiled proudly as Rio smiled the same.

“Envíamelo.” Send it to me, Rio whispered softly, resting her head back on the couch as she watched her mom do just that.

When the movie was over and her mom had disappeared into the kitchen to clean up, Rio turned her attention back to the two sleeping ducklings in her arms.

“Mi vida,” Rio whispered, trying for Agatha first as she stroked her fingers through Agatha’s hair.

Agatha didn’t move but made a small noise and Rio smiled as she continued her caressing.

“Mi vida,” she said again, soon adding a soft “Agatha.”

It seemed to do the trick as Agatha sat slowly and grumbled, “Don’t call me that.”

Rio laughed and felt Nicky shift beside her as Agatha, frowning, leant over to brush his hair from his face.

“Honey, let’s get you to bed.”

“Mellizo,” Rio whispered, nudging Nicky gently at her side as Agatha braced herself against the back of the couch and brushed her fingers down Nicky’s cheek.

Rio took the opportunity to nuzzle into Agatha’s cheek, and she smiled when she heard Nicky say, “Mm’kay mama.”

“I’ll carry you, mellizo,” Rio promised gently, angling her face around to look at him as he kept his eyes closed and yawned.

“You can’t,” Agatha corrected, turning so they were close enough for Rio to count the individual lashes that framed each of her eyes.

“It’s only my wrist that’s broken. Everything else is just bruising.”

“Rio,” Agatha whispered, her brows raised as Rio smiled easily.

“I’ll carry you too.”

“It’s okay,” Nicky’s voice sounded, quiet and slow as he reached his arm to wrap around Rio’s neck. “Mama, melliza is strong.”

Rio’s smile widened and until a laugh slipped out of it and she adjusted her hold on Nicky to hold him closer.

“See? Out of the way please.”

Agatha scowled but moved back so Rio could hold Nicky properly to her as she shuffled to the edge of the couch.

“Hold tight,” she breathed, before holding her breath as she lifted Nicky with her good arm tucked beneath him.

Agatha gave her space but protested with a soft “my love” as Anna, who’d heard the commotion from the kitchen, came into the room: “ten cuidado, mija.”

Rio grunted as she stood and wrapped her bad arm around Nicky’s middle. She could feel the way her bruised skin protested against her decision but she wouldn’t back down now. Not when Nicky had so readily tucked himself against her and the fingers of his right hand were now tangled loosely in her hair.

She moved carefully with him, feeling the ache trickle down to her knee as she did. She had to move slower than usual so it wouldn’t buckle and she wouldn’t send them both sprawling.

Not for the first time she thought of how precious her cargo was.

Agatha trailed her as she walked up the stairs with him and into the guest room where she was careful about lowering him down and Nicky did the rest for her, dutifully crawling beneath the covers so Agatha could take over and tuck him in.

Rio stood and stretched subtly and felt her heart beating rapidly in her chest. She realised she was out of breath and so moved quickly from the room to hide it from Agatha.

In the hall, she leant back against the wall and took a deep inhale, closing her eyes to focus on her breathing and calm her racing heart.

She soon found a hand spread out across her ribs and the brush of a familiar pair of lips against her cheek.

“You do too much for us.”

“Not nearly as much as I want.”

Agatha hummed and Rio felt the vibration of it against her skin.

Agatha’s fingers flexed and then travelled to her stomach beneath her shirt and rested there for a moment before she whispered, “Go to bed. I’ll say goodnight to your mom and be with you soon.”

Rio, eyes still closed, nodded her agreement but neither moved for a long time. Rio, because her breathing was still heavier than it should be, and Agatha, because she knew this was a stolen moment.

When they eventually separated, Rio all but collapsed into bed. She buried herself in the blankets and waited patiently for Agatha. But Agatha took longer than she expected she might.

Agatha took almost an hour to return to her. And Rio, on the verge of a reluctant sleep, jerked in surprise when she felt the bed dip and a soft weight land on top of her.

Rio blinked into the semi-darkness as Agatha’s hand found her stomach again and she pressed a kiss to her shoulder.

“Brought that ugly blanket up,” she explained softly.

“Where’ve you been?”

“Mm. Speaking to your mom.”

Rio suddenly felt wide awake. She turned her head to look at the clock on the side. It had been almost an hour since Agatha had left her.

“About what?”

“Plans,” Agatha mumbled non-commitally as she pressed her face in against Rio’s shoulder.

“…what plans?”

Agatha hummed quietly and Rio turned her head back the other way towards Agatha and rested her chin on top of her head. She felt Agatha’s fingers flex against her stomach and then starfish out across her skin.

“You called me Agatha earlier.” Her fingers moved and Rio sucked in a breath as they journeyed up her ribs. “That attached feeling I have sometimes… I feel it now. It’s a little different maybe. Less… frantic.” Her hand moved further up and turned forty five degrees to rest over Rio’s sternum. “I can’t explain how I-…”

Rio shifted, moving faster than she had in two days. She pulled back so she could slip her trapped left arm beneath Agatha and tug her into her body. Because Agatha was crying, she was seeking sanctuary against her skin and Rio tried to gather her in as best she could.

It took some convincing, some soft words of encouragement, and continued tugging, but Agatha was soon lying over her. Rio’s shirt was scrunched uncomfortably up with Agatha’s hand trapped against her and now curled around her neck.

And Rio held her even if it hurt. She squeezed her even if it ached.

Because this wasn’t a breakdown, it was a reckoning. All the time apart, all the forced distance, the attack, it all came out in hot tears that burned Rio’s skin as Agatha sobbed against her neck.

It took minutes that felt instead like hours for Agatha to calm enough in order to be able to speak again.

“I’ll kill him. I’ll kill him for- for you. For us.”

But vengeance did not taste sweet. Rio could only taste the fear that had swelled in her chest the second she’d felt Agatha’s first tear.

She felt her lips now, and the tongue that slipped from between them. And soon Agatha’s mouth was open and needy against her skin. The hand that had wrapped around her neck was now resting against her jaw as Agatha’s fingers sought to curl past her lips.

Agatha’s teeth introduced themselves again to her skin and Rio groaned for how much she’d missed them. It seemed to be Agatha’s mission to make her mark amongst the bruises on Rio’s body.

And Rio had no issue with it. In fact, with the drugs she was on, she hardly felt the pain of Agatha’s insistent teeth against her. She could hardly feel the sharpness of her canines as they bullied her skin and left their mark until Agatha’s heavy breaths were against her throat and Rio was groaning softly.

“Take them off,” she whispered, “your pants. Now. Take them off.”

Agatha didn’t move though and Rio was too dazed and too tired to make her. But she kissed the bruise she’d added to Rio’s battered body, and then raised her head to kiss her jaw.

“We can’t.”

Agatha sat up, sitting tall above Rio and Rio blinked slowly up at her. She rested her hands on her thighs and looked down at them. Her right in the colourful cast, the purple bright and chosen for Agatha.

She was wrapped in Agatha.

“Rio?”

Rio looked up and blinked slowly.

“Are you feeling okay? You… you zoned out.”

“I did? I… I’m tired. I just…” she moved her hands up and down, scratching over Agatha’s pale thighs and pushing up below her sleep shorts.

“You could help me in my physio.”

Agatha sighed softly and raised up onto her knees above Rio, her hands coming to rest on one bare forearm and one purple cast.

“You’ll have another scar,” Agatha said, making Rio frown in confusion. “Another. Straight down your wrist. More evidence of my-…”

“You are my scar.”

The words slipped off Rio’s tongue, the heaviness of them not slowing her enough to hold them before they fell.

“Rio,” Agatha whispered, now bending at the hip to anchor herself by Rio’s head and lean over her.

“I’ll look at my wrist and-…”

Agatha placed her hand over Rio’s mouth and Rio went silent because of it.

“Don’t. I’ll look at it and always think about…”

Agatha couldn’t continue and Rio hadn’t even tried to stop her. Her hand fell slowly from Rio’s mouth and Rio, once free to talk, didn’t.

They looked at one another and Rio slid her hands back down from beneath Agatha’s shorts. She raised them instead to frame Agatha’s face with the very tips of her fingers and whispered as she did: “I was torn wide open and had no idea. And you pulled me back together.”

Agatha closed her eyes and Rio reached her fingers up to the curve of her jaw so she could better hold her face.
