Agatha turned her head into her right hand and Rio had to witness the confusion in real time. Because Agatha’s lips came into contact with the purple of Rio’s cast and her face crumpled as she reared back and sat tall again, covering her devastation with her own hands.

“No,” Rio protested, feeling the pain that had been dulled by the pills stabbing her suddenly in the heart. “Don’t. No.” She sat up and reached for Agatha’s wrists as she choked on a sob.

“I remember now,” Rio whispered, holding Agatha gently. “I remember asking you. I’m going to ask you one more time, when you’re free to say yes and I can actually do something about it.”

Agatha’s whole body was moving with each attempt to quieten her sobs but Rio just held her through it, waiting for the moment Agatha would collapse into her. But it never came. She held back from doing what she ought to, and Rio didn’t know whether it was to avoid hurting Rio or for some other reason.

But the reason became clear around three in the morning, when Rio who had fallen asleep beside Agatha after a long while of coaxing and cooing to get her to relax into her, woke up alone.

Panic took her first. Understanding was quick to follow.

She moved slowly from the bed, taking a pillow with her and moving silently out into the dark house. And there, curled in on herself on the couch, was Agatha.

“Punishment,” Rio whispered into the dark, watching Agatha’s eyelids flutter and her lips part in a silent gasp. “I won’t allow you to do it to yourself.”

“I didn’t want to hurt you.”

“So you came to sleep alone on the couch, in the cold?”

Agatha didn’t respond to that but Rio didn’t need her to. She moved closer and Agatha shifted slightly but didn’t turn to look at her until Rio had placed the pillow above her head and had grabbed the discarded horse blanket from the coffee table where her mom had folded it before she'd gone to bed.

“Move over. I’m sleeping with you.”

“No,” Agatha protested, turning properly to frown up at Rio. “I came here because-...”

“You came here to punish yourself and I am not allowing it,” Rio explained again, forcing her voice to remain soft and steady as she stared down at Agatha.

Maybe it was because she was tired. Maybe it was because there had been too many emotions, too many changes in feeling over the last forty eight hours, maybe she simply wanted Rio, but she moved back and allowed Rio the space she needed to lie with her.

“In case you fall,” Agatha whispered as she climbed carefully over Rio’s body and lay instead on the outside of the couch. Rio dropped the blanket over them both then and made sure they both had space on the pillow as she turned herself into Agatha and draped her bad arm over her, allowing Agatha to toy with her fingers gently.

Rio eventually moved down, when she knew Agatha wasn’t even close to falling asleep. She shifted her body and brushed aside Agatha’s hair so she could nuzzle in at the back of her neck.

“I would break every bone in my body if it meant coming home to you every night.”

Agatha’s skin was warm, and she smelled like the expensive lotion that came in a red bottle that was always sat on the bathroom counter. Rio hadn’t realised how much she’d missed that smell. It had top notes of orange, heart notes of nutmeg and eucalyptus, and base notes of aromatic oils like thyme and patchouli.

She moved her hand from Agatha’s delicate hold so she could slip it below Agatha’s shirt. Rio brushed her fingers delicately along Agatha’s side and skimmed the pads of them along the dip in her waist as she pressed her nose in at the base of her neck.

She’d dreamt of moments like this. She’d fantasised about what it would feel like to have this access. She just hadn’t known it would come at such a cost.

As she trailed the tip of her nose in a line that was then traced over by her lips to the shell of Agatha’s ear, she whispered, “The first night I get you back, the first night you’re all mine again, I’m going to trace every inch of you. First,” she breathed quietly, choosing then to kiss the skin behind Agatha’s ear, as her hand danced back up Agatha’s side, “with my fingers. And then,” she nudged Agatha’s ear again and then slipped down to brush the corner of her jaw, “with my tongue.”

“Rio,” Agatha whispered as Rio’s fingers pushed further and skimmed along the side of her breast. Agatha’s voice was low and heavy as a result of Rio’s careful worship. “We can’t.”

“I know,” Rio whispered back, but she didn’t move her hand away. She couldn’t move it away.

Her fingers flexed and she heard Agatha release a shaking breath as they traced the curve of her breast and ghosted by her already hardened nipple.

“Rio,” Agatha warned again, but softer this time, as if she was reluctant to say it.

Rio hummed quietly and nuzzled in behind Agatha’s ear as she slid her fingers back down and traced across to her ribs.

“I miss you,” Rio said softly, her fingers moving to the dip of Agatha’s waist and along to the curve of her hip. “I need to take as much as I can get.”

“You need to rest,” Agatha returned, turning her head back slightly, “It’s why I left.”

“Because you knew I couldn’t resist?”

“Because I can’t resist.”

Rio smiled as she moved her hand back up but Agatha knew what she was doing and caught it before she got it to where she wanted it to be.

“We can’t.”

“Why?”

“You need to rest.”

Rio huffed quietly, “It’s already so late, I’m still awake. I need to practice with my left hand. I want to make you feel good.”

Agatha brought her hand up to kiss it but held on tightly so Rio couldn’t put it anywhere else. And then Agatha was shifting to sit up and throw her legs off the edge of the sofa.

“You’re not leaving?”

“On your back, patient.”

Rio grinned and did as she was told. “Is this a roleplay thing? I could get into that.”

But Agatha rolled her eyes and so Rio went silent but couldn’t stop her grin as Agatha threw herself over her and caught herself at the last second.

With Agatha’s hands up on the arm of the couch, Rio had free access to slip her hands below her hanging shirt and could run her fingers up and down her stomach.

“If you don’t behave I’ll leave you on this couch and go sleep in your bed. Naked.”

Rio narrowed her eyes. “You would not.”

“I would.”

Rio huffed and grabbed Agatha’s tits. But Agatha just raised a brow and smiled a little.

“You sure you wanna risk it?”

Rio huffed again and then dropped her hands down to hold Agatha’s hips.

“I’m not going to get any for weeks?”

“No.”

“Cruel.”

Agatha hummed and then adjusted her weight to shift down and settle in the crook of Rio’s good arm. After tugging the blanket over them both, Agatha’s hand danced at the waistband of her sleep shorts and Rio knew she was doing it on purpose.

“Nicky’s in court the week after you leave,” Agatha said after a while of silence, “he’ll tell them how much he doesn’t want to be with Ralph, how he doesn’t even know him. And then it’s just deliberation. It’s more arguing and producing evidence. And… I think I have what we need now.”

“You do?” Rio’s heart was hammering in her chest, but for a different reason than before. She stared up at the ceiling and felt Agatha nudge her nose into her neck.

“You’ll call Nicky when you’re away?” Agatha deflected, and Rio knew she was just protecting her in trying to keep her away from all the messy legal procedures. But she wished she’d let her in.

“Of course,” she whispered quietly, following it up with a gentle quack to try and lighten the mood in the room.

Agatha scoffed softly and Rio held her a bit tighter against her. But Agatha was resisting a little and Rio knew she was worried about hurting her.

“I’m on too many drugs to be sore.”

“Another reason you're not getting any.”

“Let it be known that I could be high as hell or drunk off my face and I would still consent.”

Agatha grumbled and pushed her hand further up Rio’s torso to wrap her fingers around her side.

“Go to sleep.”

Rio hummed, too wired and too happy to even think about sleeping. She might not get this again for a while. In fact, she definitely wouldn’t.

“Tell me about your day yesterday, before Alice called you.”

“What?”

“Your day. Just…” Agatha’s fingers twitched at her side, “I’ve missed your voice. Just talk to me.”

Rio knew that Agatha was searching for the trick in her words, the scheme. But there was none. And soon Agatha realised it was a simple request for more of her, in a way Rio hadn’t had her for weeks now.

So she began to speak. She dragged her hand down and rubbed over Rio’s stomach in a soothing manner that helped her to drift off as she told her about the Cheerios she’d made for Nicky, the drive to school, how she stopped at the Pilates studio for a quick class.

And to Rio, the combination of Agatha’s touch and soft, familiar voice was better than any drug. She drifted off to sleep by the time Agatha got to her afternoon spent running interviews for foreign press of Heartburn.

When Agatha realised Rio was asleep she pulled her shirt down and curled her hand instead around her shoulder. She thought of the man she’d married who’d done this to the woman she loved and she fell asleep clutching so tightly to Rio she didn’t let go until morning.

It was Rio who woke first, blinking into the light. The pain had come back in full force; her wrist throbbed, her knee ached and her back and chest felt somehow as if she’d been twisted violently in the night.

But Agatha was still clutching at her, her head resting on her shoulder and her hand holding her shirt. So she couldn’t move. She wouldn’t move.

But a small movement to her side made her turn her head and she saw the back of a head of dark hair.

“Mellizo,” she whispered, smiling when Nicky gasped and turned around to look at her.

“Why did you sleep down here?” He whispered back and Rio hummed quietly, adjusting her hold on Agatha.

“My back was sore so your mama suggested the couch might be better and didn’t want me sleeping alone.”

Nicky nodded like he understood this logic. “I thought maybe we could watch some basketball on YouTube or something again? Because we can’t play.”

“Oh I think I can play with you, mellizo.”

“No,” came Agatha’s voice, so gruff and low it made Rio jump in surprise. But Agatha was pulling back and away until she was supporting herself over Rio to look at Nicky. “No basketball, honey.”

Nicky opened his mouth to say something but then closed it quickly enough that it could have been missed. But Rio was looking at him because watching the little boy look happy took the edge off her pain.

Agatha looked around to her once she told Nicky to go and wash up for breakfast.

“Where are your meds?”

“On the side in the bathroom.”

Agatha nodded, kissed her once, and then their bubble burst and she was gone. Alone now, Rio groaned into the day.

As she stretched her arms up and began the stupid exercises the physio had recommended for her fingers, her mom came into view. And by the look on her face she just knew she was in trouble.

“¿Mamá? ¿Que paso?”

Rio sat up and Anna sat down by her legs.

“Le estás dando a ese chico una esperanza que no puede tener. Sentarse juntos por la noche es una cosa; dormir enredados, otra muy distinta. Todavía no, Rio.” You are giving that boy hope he cannot have. Sitting at night is one thing; sleeping tangled together is another. Not yet, Rio.

Rio swallowed, still absently flexing her fingers to uphold her promise to Agatha.

“We just-…”

But Agatha appeared over Anna’s shoulder and Rio said nothing further. She just watched as Agatha came closer and sat on the low coffee table before Anna.

“Mom says,” Rio started again but was interrupted by Anna almost immediately.

“Los dos tienen que tener más cuidado. Dormir juntos en el sofá…” You both have to be more careful. Sleeping together on the couch…

Rio watched it happen in real time; Agatha’s trauma response. She paled significantly and her eyes turned downward, as if she couldn’t bear to look at Anna anymore. Even as her mom reached for Agatha’s face, Agatha shrank into herself and was unable to say anything other than a soft “okay” when Anna informed her she would be making her famous eggs.

“Mi vida,” Rio whispered the moment her mom was gone. But Agatha ripped herself away before Rio could even reach for her.

And as she went she realised what had happened. Anna was always telling Rio off, chastising her, correcting her behaviour. But it was always kindly meant. It was always done with so much love that it was water off a patito’s back.

But Agatha… Agatha had never had that kind of love. She didn’t know what it was for a parent to tell you off but love you unconditionally.

And Agatha was so worried that Anna liked her, she was so terrified she didn’t. Even on the night they’d separated she’d asked Anna if she could still marry her daughter.

Rio felt sick. Agatha was already so stressed, so inclined to hating herself and to punishment.

“Mi amor!”

But she’d gone already. And Rio could only watch her march out of the room.

She staggered to her feet and only as she did did she realise what a mistake carrying Nicky and letting Agatha sleep on her yesterday had been. Her whole body felt hot and suddenly she couldn’t stand the cast on her arm. She started to push at it, slipping her thumb in at the base and gritting her teeth to try and get it off. But it wouldn’t budge and the pain of any pressure on her wrist made her soon give up.

She swayed briefly where she stood and used the furniture and the walls to take her through to the kitchen where her family was.

And when she arrived Agatha saw her struggle and flew to her before Rio could even say anything.

“I’m fine,” Rio breathed, allowing Agatha to peel her away from the wall she was leaning against.

“You’re hot all over and-…”

“Mm’fine,” Rio murmured, aware that Nicky was watching from his place at the table with his Switch.

“Rio,” Agatha said more firmly, and Rio turned to look at her and gave up on hiding the pain she was in. Agatha’s blue eyes filled with tears but she looked away before they could spill over.

“Come sit, take your meds. I’ll get you an ice pack. Food will help.”

Rio only allowed Agatha to move her to the seat where she’d been sitting and once she was secure in it she went to get water for Rio to wash down her pills.

“You okay?” Nicky, watching Rio carefully from the other side of the table.

“I’m okay. Just a little sore.”

“Here,” Agatha said as she placed the water down and helped Rio tip the pills into her hand. Agatha’s hand was shaking as Rio took them from her and threw them back with the water. Nicky must have noticed it too because he put his Switch down and reached his hand towards his mom who took it and Rio watched as she squeezed it tight.

She felt woozy and achey and still too hot but she didn’t say anything about it though Agatha kept looking. She kept shooting her furtive glances and soon even Anna was concerned. It was agreed that Agatha would call the doctor and Anna would help take Rio to bed.

Nicky, obviously, did his best to help too.

By the time Rio had crawled into bed she felt hot all over. She was itchy and everything felt swollen though it didn’t look it. But she turned away so Nicky couldn’t see that she was struggling. She hid her face against the pillow and within seconds was fast asleep.

A sharp pain woke her briefly. It made her groan but she could register nothing and in fact wouldn’t remember even waking.

When she woke properly she did so with a jolt and grunted aggressively as she tried to come to.

A noise nearby told her that there was someone in the room and she didn’t need to open her eyes to know that it was Agatha.

“Hey,” she said throatily as a hand found her forehead.

“The doctor thinks it’s a bad reaction to the anaesthesia. It can happen that it’s delayed. But he gave you a shot. You didn’t feel it? You didn’t even flinch.”

Agatha’s face was paler than before, Rio was sure of it, and her words had come out in a rush as if she’d been holding them in for hours. She looked ghostly white, almost translucent. Even her lips looked different. They were chapped and chewed and as Rio focused in on them she saw red in the lower one: blood.

“You were scared,” she breathed, frowning as she reached for the hand now travelling down her cheek.

“So fucking scared,” Agatha admitted, her blue eyes shining in the dim light. “Your mom’s going to stay a while and look after you. At least until you go to Arkansas. At least until…”

She trailed off and Rio took her fingers to her lips and kissed them.

“I want you to rest. Really rest. Even if you’re horizontal for two weeks, I don’t care. Even if-…”

“Mi vida,” Rio said quietly, making Agatha begin to protest as she pushed herself up and winced a little as she did. “I’ll do whatever you tell me to do if you promise not to worry so much.”

An impossible ask, she knew. But a necessary one. Agatha needed to know Rio would be okay and Rio needed Agatha to know that more of her suffering would never make Rio any better.

“Punishment,” Rio murmured, the word tasting like bile on her tongue as her thumb pressed near the cut in Agatha’s lip. “I won’t allow it,” she said quietly, repeating her promise from earlier that morning. Her voice sounded so unlike her own and yet she also had never felt more certain of her own words.

Her mind was hazy still but she had to bring it up; Agatha’s guilt, Agatha’s hatred of herself, the years she’d spent alone and suppressing who she really was.

She soon would be away. She’d be away for the length of the trial. She’d be away and Agatha would have no one. So she had to tell her now. She had to make her listen.

Agatha’s gaze was moving about her face but not quite meeting her eyes anymore. Her fingers trembled as they rested on Rio’s arm and Rio knew she couldn’t leave her without saying something, anything to try to assuage Agatha’s guilt.

“I want you. I only want you. Exactly as you are. I want you to get through this and come back to me and for us to be a family. I want it so much. And I want you to not think on anything that’s happened. I want you to think of our future. Of us and Nicky and of how much my mom loves you and how sure my dad was that you were the right person for me. If you don’t trust me, if you don’t believe me, believe him. He was always right.”

“Miguel is a smart man,” Agatha demured, watching as Rio raised her fingers to her lips to kiss them again.

“He is,” Rio agreed, smiling a little for the reminder that Agatha had read a book on grief and so always spoke of Miguel in the present tense. She was so soft with Rio and yet so hard on herself.

“Now,” Rio said quietly, “When can I leave this damn bed?”

Agatha laughed softly and Rio was rewarded for making her do so with a gentle kiss. It felt like a clean slate, like a peace offering, for each other, as well as for themselves.

And something settled in the house as Rio got stronger through the day, feeling more steady on her feet and able to get up and move around unaided, without sweating or feeling faint. It felt a lot like peace, like a silent agreement that they were headed for a better future and this was just the start.

But now, the reality was that Agatha and Nicky would soon have to leave. And even that was taken surprisingly lightly, with Nicky insisting that first they dance together because they’d not been able to in so long and he missed it. Anna was the only one who wasn’t very enthusiastic but was soon being taught air guitar by the shy little boy who’d opened up as easily to her as he had Anna’s daughter.

Rio and Agatha were off to the side, Agatha staying close to ensure Rio was okay but doing her best not to disappoint her future mother in law though Rio kept trying to nuzzle closer.

It became a soft game of cat and mouse; Rio trying to get closer, Agatha trying to keep it so PG they were practically leaving room for Jesus.

After they battled for a while, both watching Nicky and Anna laugh together as the sound of Santana filled the space, Agatha sighed and allowed Rio to move just an inch or two closer.

“You do too much. You shouldn’t have carried him. You should still be in bed.”

“He’ll be too big soon. And he won’t want it. I was just making up for lost time.”

Agatha nodded against her, now even closer, just one slow bob of her head. And as Rio’s fingers dipped to the hem of Agatha’s shirt she realised what she’d said.

Agatha lifted her head up and though Nicky and Anna were still thrashing away at their guitars, one of them considerably more into it than the other, everything went still and silent for Rio.

Agatha was looking at her with those ocean eyes. The current was warm but the tide was high and dangerous and Rio knew if she looked too long she’d drown in their waters.

As she struggled to surface she adjusted her hold on Agatha and pressed into the small of her back so she’d move in closer.

Agatha’s front was against hers. They were stomach to stomach. Rio had watched from afar as this stomach grew. She’d seen Agatha’s body change and swell in pictures and across parties. She’d witnessed Agatha in all her glowing, gorgeous glory.

And now, as she stood still in the middle of the kitchen-cum-dancefloor, she remembered a conversation they’d had under her favourite tree in the garden.

They’d build a life and a home and they’d build a baby together.

Agatha turned from her and looked at Nicky. Rio wondered if maybe she’d been staring too much or too long but the hand around her neck squeezed her gently and she knew then it was a silent reminder of Agatha’s belief that Nicky was already hers.

Rio ducked her head down and pressed her face in against Agatha’s cheek. She smiled and remembered something from the hospital. Against Agatha’s stomach she curled in two fingers and whispered, “pew pew”.

“You’re a dummy, Rio Vidal.”

“A handsome one.”

“Maybe.”

That dance was the last Rio saw of Agatha for two weeks. It was the last she saw of Nicky too. They left shortly after, Nicky teary and clinging because he knew it would be a while before they could dance in the kitchen again.

Agatha had managed to hold herself together for the length of time it took to say goodbye but Rio had heard through Alice who had heard through Jen that she’d locked herself in her office after Nicky had gone to bed and she’d not heard a peep from her all night.

So two weeks went by and went by slowly. Rio was diligent about her finger and arm exercises. She made sure to eat right and slowly reintroduced exercise into her lifestyle. She went on walks with her mom with Thor trailing along behind. She made flowers when she had nothing else to do, or was bored of memorising scripts. She even started to try her hand, literally, at other crafts and soon had a pile of string bracelets she’d made after a trip with her mom to JoAnn’s Fabrics. She checked in with Alice who checked in with Jen who checked in with Agatha, but otherwise it was no contact.

Unless you counted Rio sitting silently beside her mom every night as Anna spoke with Agatha on the phone. She didn’t think it was fair her mom got to call her but she didn’t. But she didn’t protest. And maybe speaking with Agatha daily but not seeing her would make the longing worse.

So she behaved, she was good. She got better.

Two weeks after the surgery she was able to get her cast removed and, once everything was confirmed okay, she had it replaced by a removable splint that was black instead of her bright green and purple.

Her scar was a little itchy and a little pink. But it was healing well enough. It was four inches long, and straight down the middle of her wrist. Beside the four much smaller scars from Evanora it looked practically monstrous but Rio was proud of it; thinking of it as evidence that she was still here, that they were still fighting the good fight.

Soon after her appointment she got word from Alice that Agatha wanted to have dinner with her on her last night before leaving for Arkansas. Naturally, Rio was beyond excited which meant that Alice had to be the one to pack her bag because Rio was bouncing off the walls with the knowledge she’d be with her little family again.

Her mom had left the day before so knowing she could see Agatha on her last night was the lift she needed before she’d be leaving the state for months of filming.

Only, the moment she walked into the restaurant she knew this was a bad idea. There was Agatha, sitting opposite Nicky, her blue eyes on the door before Rio had even stepped through it.

And then Nicky, turning expectantly and grinning at the sight of her. And Val. Calm, decent Val, sitting beside Nicky.

How was Rio supposed to sit with them all evening, behaving properly, and leave them without looking back? It would be the performance of a lifetime if she managed it. It would be a miracle if she could stand it.

She strode through the restaurant, her bodyguard hanging fire by the door. They’d have done a sweep of the space earlier anyway, Rio was sure. And being sure of that meant that Rio could make a beeline for Agatha without having to look around for anyone else.

Agatha got to her first. She’d stood up and had her arms around Rio’s middle before Rio could even say anything. And then Val had moved and Nicky was waiting patiently for his mama to be done so he could take her place.

“Miss me?” Hidden under Rio’s words: I missed you.

“Don’t be smug.” Hidden under Agatha’s: So much.

Rio laughed and gave Agatha a gentle squeeze before she pulled away and was replaced by her son.

“Hey, bud!”

She bent and kissed the top of Nicky’s head before ruffling his hair.

“¡Hola, melliza!”

Rio hummed happily as he let go and the third person appeared before her. Val kissed her cheek and Rio smiled at her, but grinned when she heard Agatha clearing her throat purposefully.

It was hard to hide her smirk as she slipped into the booth beside Agatha but she managed it. Just.

“I hear this place does great pizza,” she said by way of trying to distract herself from the hand that had arrived on her thigh the moment she’d sat down.

“And mama said we can get ice cream.”

Rio hummed happily, glad she’d opted for a dress so she could feel Agatha’s fingers against her skin. She felt her ankle too, looped behind her own.

It was her last chance; their last chance to be close for god knows how long. And Agatha was making the most of it, clearly. Her hand was warm and Rio, even though she’d only just sat down, was already unfolding her napkin to cover it.

Agatha was wearing her ring. Rio could feel it clear as day against her thigh. It made her heart soar.

“My treat,” she offered with a grin, the very least she could offer. “So order whatever you want, mellizo.”

“I’ll get it,” Agatha said quietly, her fingers squeezing to suggest she meant it.

“No,” Rio turned and was surprised by the soft smile on Agatha’s face. “Really. My treat.”

Agatha hummed like she disagreed but the waiter arriving to take drinks orders interrupted before she could say anything. Agatha’s hold on Rio changed then. She put her arm up on the back of the booth and turned a little into her. Her right hand fell just beside her thigh and Rio knew it was because she didn’t want to waste a second not touching her.

“We’ll have a bottle of the Barolo, a small coke, and, Val?” She turned to Val and Rio bit on the inside of her cheek.

“Soda and lime for me, please.”

The waiter nodded and scribbled the order down as Agatha’s index finger became bolder and traced the line along the hem of Rio’s dress.

“The ‘18 vintage or-…”

“Yes. That’s all.”

Rio caught the fear that flickered across the waiter’s face and shot him a small smile before he hurried away.

“Ordering for me now?”

“Making sure you get what you want,” Agatha countered, her hand back to its place on Rio’s thigh, below her napkin.

Rio arched a brow but didn’t say anything and placed her right hand casually across her lap. It took two seconds for Agatha’s fingers to find her own.

“Were you guys waiting long?”

“No,” Val shrugged, “just best for us to get here a little earlier.”

“We have a gift for you,” Nicky said so quickly it was like he’d been bursting to say it. Rio’s head shot round to him so quickly she almost pulled a muscle.

“A gift?”

“Nicky’s idea,” Agatha murmured as Rio leant forwards and Nicky shuffled about to reach for something on the floor.

“Is it another cowboy hat?”

“No! Better than that.”

“Nothing’s better than a cowboy hat,” Rio muttered as Nicky disappeared for a second and then popped back up with a gift bag in his hands.

He looked incredibly proud of himself as he handed it over the table to Rio. Inside, wrapped in green tissue, was the ugliest photo frame Rio had ever seen. But the frame, littered with horse shoes and cowboy hats, contained the best photo she’d ever seen in her life.

The picture was of three incredibly happy people. It was the one taken at Rio’s party where Nicky had pressed his face in against hers and Agatha was holding her like she was proud to. Just tres patitos all so thrilled to be together.

Rio swallowed thickly as Nicky asked: “Do you like it?”

“Nicky chose the frame too.”

Agatha’s whisper made Rio laugh, which was good because she felt like crying.

“I love it, mellizo. I’ll put it up in my trailer so I can look at it every day.”

She reached across to Nicky’s hand and he took it with a big grin, “and I love the frame. You’ve got excellent taste.”

“Thank you,” Nicky said, “I don’t think mama liked it.”

Rio gasped dramatically and Nicky giggled.

“You don't like it?!”

Agatha pursed her lips but said nothing in response as the wine arrived and the drinks were served. Rio sat back and released Nicky’s hand so he could be given his soda and as Agatha’s glass was poured Rio held her new picture against her chest to hide it.

When the waiter was gone and before everybody could lift their glasses to cheers, Nicky disappeared below the table again. Rio, glass half-mast, raised her brows at Agatha.

“Just wait,” she murmured from the corner of her lips as Rio turned back to Nicky, now sitting back in his seat and holding another gift, this time wrapped.

Rio watched expectantly as Nicky knelt up on the chair until Agatha pointed at him and said, “hey, feet”. He nodded and slipped back onto his bum but leant across to pass Rio the gift. This one he did more reverently, like Rio might unwrap it and there would be a baby bird inside.

“Mama found it the other day and we now all have copies of it.”

The gift, now in Rio’s hand, felt strangely heavy now, though it was obvious it was another frame probably with another picture inside. It felt different, though, like Rio might not want to see what the picture held.

“Nicky picked the frame of this one too.”

Rio smiled a little as she cautiously unpeeled the wrapping and did her best not to rip it. In her peripheral vision she saw Agatha reach across and take Nicky’s hand as the first part of the frame revealed itself.

It was wooden, a light wood with square corners. But slowly, inch by inch, she pulled out the frame until she could see what it held.

The image made her gasp. It was a picture of Agatha and her. Only one she’d never seen before and didn’t remember being taken. She was standing with her hands splayed out on Agatha’s round bump, smiling at her like she’d won a prize. She felt Agatha’s hand squeeze her thigh below the table as Nicky said: “You did find us. When I was still in mama’s belly. And mama said I kicked and kicked and kicked because I wanted to say hello to you and I think that’s right. I think I wanted to say hello.”

A vague memory then, frayed all over, worn down by time and what had surely been an incredibly drunken night.

“The FYC event,” Agatha helped it along, “Your first. For Closing Time. You shouted at Stark for coming near my bump and…”

Rio turned to Agatha and saw that her eyes were wet with tears. She remembered now. She remembered as well as you could a night you’d lost to the bottom of a bottle. “I felt him. He kicked.”

“You did. He did,” she said, her face cracking slightly into a smile.

“Why didn’t you ever tell me?”

Agatha’s gaze fell to the picture then and Rio turned back to it too. Written around the frame were the words: “FAMILY where life begins and love never ends”. It was such an ugly thing to be holding something so beautiful.

“I guess I forgot. Or blocked it out or-...”

“Maybe it was because you were so happy that you forgot to remember.” Nicky, forgetting Agatha’s instruction to not put his feet on the seat and doing just that as he leant more over to get a look at the picture too.

“It’s beautiful, mellizo. I knew I knew you from the beginning. How could I not have found you?”

Nicky beamed at this, his cheeks flushing a little in excitement as Agatha gestured for him to sit back down again. And he did.

Rio kissed the picture then, partly for Nicky and partly for herself and then she wrapped it carefully again and placed it in the gift bag with the other picture. She felt lightheaded, knowing now that she had these two treasures to keep with her when she was away.

She wondered if she could get them blown up and put on canvases in her hotel. But maybe that was a little overboard. Too gay, even for her.

“So,” she said with a soft clearing of her throat, trying to keep her cool, “I was going to wait until after dinner but I’ve got a gift for you too.”

She felt Agatha shift her ankle beneath her own and glanced at her and knew immediately what the look on her face meant: you okay? Nodding just once she reached into her pocket and pulled out a small heap of strings and offered them up to the group, “One for each of you,” she announced proudly, bending her thumb to brush over them. “And one for me too.”

No one other than Nicky moved. He’d leant up to lean over the table and made a soft “ooooh” sound as he gazed down at them.

“Friendship bracelets?”

“Sí, mellizo. Verde para ti.” Green for you. She extricated the green and white one for Nicky. “Val,” she said as Nicky ooh’d again, “red, white and blue because, y’know, you’re a Brit.” Val scoffed and said: “cheers, mate” as she took her bracelet from Rio.

And then there were only two left. One with purple, green, and blue, the other with pink, orange, and white.

She held up the purple one to Agatha who was eyeing the pink one. “And for you,” she said happily, “tres patitos.”

“I have to wear it?” Agatha asked as Val helped Nicky to tie his to his wrist.

“That would be nice, yes. At least for tonight. I figured you can just keep it in your drawer or in your phone case or something else.”

Agatha hummed dispassionately but allowed Rio to tie the string bracelet around her wrist.

“These are so cool,” Nicky announced, admiring his new bracelet. “Did you make them?”

“Yup! Had to practice moving my fingers so I’d get better sooner so figured it would be a fun thing to do and you all get cute little bracelets out of it.”

“Definitely,” Nicky agreed as Rio raised Agatha’s wrist to her lips and kissed it softly. But Agatha had pulled away the moment her lips touched her skin.

“Careful. Public.”

Rio nodded and saw the colour drain from Agatha’s face as the waiter appeared to ask if everything was okay and they needed anything else.

“All good, thanks so much,” Val took this one, sending him on his way as Agatha cleared her throat and focused in on tying Rio’s bracelet to her wrist too. Rio reached her hand down to touch Agatha’s leg and found that, far from moving away this time, she shuffled a little closer. When her bracelet was secured properly, Agatha whispered a gentle, “I’m sorry”, and they said no more about it.

As dinner went on, Agatha and Rio grew more bold in their touching. Or maybe they were just more aware of time slipping away from them. Rio certainly was. Because by the time they’d all finished dessert (sundaes for Rio and Nicky, a panna cotta for Val, and nothing for Agatha), they were sipping their coffee and Rio’s hand was across Agatha’s lap, tucked in below her thigh. Agatha was running her fingers up and down Rio’s forearm and tickling the inside of her wrist and Rio couldn’t bear to think that she would soon have to pay the check and leave.

“And maybe I can come to set too? And see all the dinosaurs and the cool costumes and the jungle and stuff?”

“Oh my god, are you kidding me?!” Rio exclaimed, throwing her bad hand up in the air dramatically but keeping her good one firmly in place around Agatha. “I’m not even going to do this movie if you don’t come visit at least once!”

“Hey hey,” Agatha said, leaning around Rio slightly where Rio had angled herself so it wasn’t so obvious as to what she was doing to the people who walked past. “Calm down a little, honey. We need to go soon. It’s almost bedtime.”

Nicky was anything other than calm. He and Rio had dominated the conversation for most of the night. They’d spoken first about how cool it was that they’d met when Nicky wasn’t even born and made a new handshake out of it - Nicky’s fist pressed against Rio’s open palm - they’d spoken about basketball and tried to calculate how far away infinity was given their current trajectory, and they’d discussed Rio’s Jurassic Park movie. All of which meant that Val had mostly laughed at the various things they were saying and Agatha had been preoccupied holding Rio’s thigh or touching her wrist or doing whatever she could to look innocent when really she was trying to get as close to Rio as possible.

“Can we stay out a little longer pleeeeease?” Rio grinned at this, and wriggled her brows at Nicky but it was Val who interjected before Agatha could say anything.

“We should actually think about making a move soon. I think outside is pretty busy.”

The implication was clear. Val’s phone had been lighting up all night so Rio knew she was in communication with whoever was to drive them home. She felt her whole body deflate as she watched Nicky’s do the same. But she had to remain positive. It wouldn’t be long until she was back, until this was all over, until time apart meant nothing.

“Hey,” she said quickly, holding up her palm, half hidden by the cast. Nicky smiled again as he fist bumped it gently. “I’ll grab the check and then I want a big hug before we leave, okay?”

Nicky agreed and Rio squeezed Agatha’s leg before she pulled away and went up to the counter to pay. On her way there she could feel the eyes of her fellow patrons on her but she did her best to ignore them and focus on the task at hand. It never got any easier. In fact, it only got worse.

With every passing day, with each new article or selfie with a fan, with each project or interview, more people wanted more of her. After the attack on the trail, there had been so much media coverage on her it had been hard to leave the house for the first week. People wanted answers, they wanted pictures, and to zoom in on Nicky’s duckling proudly displayed on her cast. But she didn’t have answers, or anything else, to give. And everything she did have was sitting at a table, waiting for her return, waiting for their goodbye hugs.

So Rio paid, doing her best to not react to the extortionate amount on the bill. She sometimes forgot she was rich. And then she went back to her people.

Val first. She received a kiss on the cheek and a hug that was longer and tighter than usual, they were “dating” after all. Next came Nicky, who simply wouldn’t let go. So Rio squatted down before him and held his cheeks as she repeated all her promises: “I’ll come back, I’ll miss you, it won’t be long, I love you”.

Finally, Agatha. She knew she couldn’t cling like Nicky had. So she held her fiercely and whispered a soft, true: “Te amo, mi todo.” Agatha felt tense against her. She didn’t lean in properly, didn’t bury her face against her neck like she usually might.

Instead she pulled away long before Rio wanted her to and she wore a mask that told Rio everything she needed to know: Agatha was devastated. Agatha was hiding it from Rio, and the world.

So Rio did the only thing she could. She turned to Nicky and bent before him so he could jump up. It wasn’t the done thing in a restaurant like this. But it was their thing, so it didn’t matter. Everyone was looking anyway. This at least gave them something interesting to see. So Rio grabbed her gift bag from the side and held them as she held Nicky’s legs and walked out behind Val to the paps waiting for them as they exited.

It was carnage. It was ridiculous. But Nicky had his cap on and was hiding against her neck. She knew Agatha was directly behind, holding his shirt. Their bodyguards were already working on crowd control because paps and autograph hunters were clamoring to get to them. But they were a well-oiled machine now.

Val had them to the car door in no time and Rio handed her the bag so she could work Nicky off her and into the small space allowed them in the open car door. She got him inside, told him to put his belt on and be good for his mama and then she stood by as Agatha slipped past and squeezed her good hand. She smiled at her as the first tear slipped down Agatha’s cheek and then she had to turn, close the door, and get escorted to her own car.

She took a breath, steadied herself as she clutched the two photo frames in their bag. It would be okay. Agatha would be okay. Her family would be okay.

Agatha was wearing her ring again. Rio had her locket. Nicky had his picture. They were tied together by the strings now worn proudly on their wrists.

They had talismans of each other, and soon, they’d have each other.

The door slammed and Rio closed her eyes as she settled in her seat. But a pair of green eyes, as shrewd as they were sharp, remained focused on the car as it merged with the late-night traffic and Natasha Romanoff sighed quietly.

“Keep away, Rio. Keep away.”

Vanity Fair

Agatha Harkness Answers The Handwritten Proust Questionnaire

1. What is your idea of perfect happiness? Dancing in the kitchen
2. What is your greatest fear? Anything happening to my son
3. What is the trait you most deplore in yourself? I’m quick to anger
4. What is the trait you most deplore in others? Entitlement
5. Which living person do you most admire? The woman who cooks the best food and checks in every day
6. What is your greatest extravagance? Security for my family
7. What is your current state of mind? Impatient
8. What do you consider the most overrated virtue? Patience
9. On what occasion do you lie? When necessary or bored
10. What do you most dislike about your appearance? I used to hate my nose but I can think of four reasons now why I love it
11. Which living person do you most despise? I can’t say
12. What is the quality you most like in a man? Humor
13. What is the quality you most like in a woman? Courage
14. Which words or phrases do you most overuse? “Honey”
15. What or who is the greatest love of your life? My son
16. When and where were you happiest? When Chopsticks was playing
17. Which talent would you most like to have? I’d like to be braver
18. If you could change one thing about yourself, what would it be? A decision not made eight years ago
19. What do you consider your greatest achievement? My son
20. If you were to die and come back as a person or a thing, what would it be? A very ugly horse blanket
21. Where would you most like to live? London, Notting Hill
22. What is your most treasured possession? A stolen shirt
23. What do you regard as the lowest depth of misery? Being away from the river
24. What is your favorite occupation? Motherhood
25. What is your most marked characteristic? Four freckles on my nose
26. What do you most value in your friends? Loyalty
27. Who are your favorite writers? Barrett Browning, Morrison, Woolf, Shakespeare, too many more to name
28. Who is your hero of fiction? Anyone who loves deeply and well
29. Which historical figure do you most identify with? Maybe Katharine Hepburn or Princess Di
30. Who are your heroes in real life? She knows
31. What are your favorite names? Nicholas, Mi Vida
32. What is it that you most dislike? Regret. And purple Skittles
33. What is your greatest regret? That’s private
34. How would you like to die? Felizmente casada
35. What is your motto? I love you. I love you. I love you.

 

Missing, her dad once told her, is a stop over to rejoicing. “Lo que falta es una escala hacia el regocijo”. It was a piece of wisdom that was only partially true, however. Because her dad was gone so no joy was to be had at the end of her missing him.

But this, she thought, as she placed the magazine down and grabbed a pair of scissors from her vanity bag in the small bathroom of her small trailer, was maybe more of what he meant.

Missing Agatha felt endless. But there would be joy, rejoicing, at the end of it.

She scored down the spine of the glossy mag and gently ripped off the page. A piece of Agatha. Her handwriting. She held it up for a second, looked at those small letters that spelled out her promise, “felizmente casada”, and then placed the page on the mirror over her desk.

It would do. For now. A piece of Agatha to see every day whilst she waited. A small token to remember that rejoicing would come.

She smiled a little, “always right, papa.”

It had come via Alice via Jen via Agatha; a delivery on the step of her trailer that morning with a sticky note on the front cover in loopy script that Rio recognised as Agatha’s immediately. Page 37. 35. Over and over and over.

Rio’s eyes moved to the answer to Question 35 and her heart skipped a beat because Agaha Harkness, the great, the infamous, the soft and gentle and tender, loved her. And she was telling the world in the only way she could.

She looked back up to meet her captured gaze and the door opened just as Rio was turning from Agatha’s smiling face on the page and Alice stepped in. She hadn’t knocked.

“Ready? Everyone’s crazy excited for you to get to set. Can’t believe the red carpet. Even I got a fancy pastry. I think they want to butter me up so I’ll let them talk to you.”

“You my new security? Thought Agatha only signed off on the new guy because he was bigger than the rest. You’re tiny.”

Alice scoffed and Rio didn’t miss the unsubtle flex of her biceps, even through her black shirt.

“If you’re not careful I’ll call her and tell her you’re misbehaving.”

Rio’s face lit up, partly for show and partly because please. “Really?!”

“Shut up. Pervert. Get to set, they’re ready for you.”

Rio huffed, her metaphorical tail no longer wagging. But she grabbed her tote bag with her essentials, - her phone, some coloured card, her headphones, some snacks - kissed her two fingers and placed them to the picture of Agatha now on her mirror, and ignored Alice’s eye roll as she stepped out the door.

She’d mailed a copy of the magazine to her mom too, thinking she’d like that she was Agatha’s most admired person. And she had; her mom had loved it. She’d teared up on the phone and called Agatha her treasure over and over until Rio started to feel like a pirate, a very proud one.

It had been two weeks since she’d last seen Agatha. Two weeks since she’d received two gifts of two beautiful framed photos from Nicky. Two weeks since it had felt, oh so briefly, that they were a family. But now she was on set after two weeks of slow-going rehearsal and read throughs and stunt training. Now she was so far from Agatha’s world she may as well be on a different planet.

And Alice was right. Sure enough, everyone was very excited that Rio was on set. The production was small, with a couple other crews dotted about the state so scenes could be filmed concurrently with the different actors involved in the project. Rio’s arm of the feature involved shooting in a heavily wooded area on the outskirts of the Ouachita National Forest. It was unseasonably warm and everyone had a slight sheen of sweat about them.

The humidity made Rio’s wrist itch but her injury had been written into the script now and she couldn’t remove her splint.

Her part was to play a cop with little left to believe in and no ties other than the locals she saw and the tourists who occasionally darkened the door of her tiny provincial precinct. It was a story of murder, deceit, everything dark and dangerous about the human condition.

Rio had wanted the role because she enjoyed wearing a uniform. Alice had wanted her to get the role because Apple TV produced prestigious work and Rio needed to be taken seriously.

Despite their differing reasons for wanting Rio to do the project, they both won.

The difference in this production was that Rio was first on the call sheet. She’d been last on the call sheet many times. She’d been in the middle a fair few. And only one other time at the top: for the role she won her Oscar for, All The Wrong Gods.

But that was low budget. Practically indie. And this was… Apple. There was someone for Rio’s every need. There were people who anticipated Rio’s every need and other people who fulfilled it.

Even on Snow, Agatha had been at the top of the call sheet. Agatha had been the asset. Agatha had been who everyone was tripping over themselves to get to, to deliver food or drink or whatever to. Rio was just a spare, slightly shiny, part.

So this, this was new.

It made it hard to have conversations with people when everyone was fawning. It made it hard to get up from her seat and fetch herself a coffee when two people jumped up to go out of their way and get her one instead. It made it hard to relax and make her flowers when everyone wanted a piece of her at all times.

It was a week into rehearsals before she realised this was how Agatha felt every second of the day. It’s why she wanted Rio to call her “my life”, “my love”, “my everything”. Because her name was being said over and over by strangers and people who wanted something from her. Rio knew now. She knew when she was sick of hearing her own name. She knew when she put the finishing touches on the seventh tulip she’d made that week and a PA ran up to ask if she might like some actual flowers for her trailer and in asking managed to say her name five times in one sentence.

She knew why Agatha wanted Rio to call her things no one else could. And she found herself missing the way Agatha called her “honey”, “baby”, “my love”. She found herself missing Agatha full stop.

“Hey,” the First AD called out as Rio was putting the finishing touches on a flower she’d been working on for the past hour. “We’re going for drinks after work if… if you want to join?”

Always tentative, always nervous, Rio didn’t know how to reassure everyone anymore. So she smiled like she always did and checked her watch; pulling the chunky green and white Baby G out of the bag slung over the arm of the little director’s chair with her name on it.

It was three in the afternoon and they’d been working since before four that morning. And Rio looked at the little alarm bell showing at the top of the watch face. A reminder. A reminder of her commitment. Five o’clock every day that little bell wound ring and it would be time.

“What time are you thinking? I’m needed for one more shot and then I can go.”

“Maybe like four? In an hour or so.”

Rio nodded and put her watch back in the bag. “I have a call I can’t miss at five but I can come find you after? Where will you be?”

The First AD, a woman named Jac, seemed thrilled that Rio was keen to join them and Rio regretted that this had been the first time she’d been invited to hang with the crew. Maybe she had to make more of an effort.

“Great! The bar opposite the crew hotel. The Brewery. I’ll, uh, yeah, we’ll see you there!”

Rio smiled as she left and wondered if maybe something had changed in her. She spent a lot of time in her trailer lately, making flowers and on calls with directors and producers. She wasn’t as “on set” as she usually was.

Not to mention, regardless of her schedule that day, when the little alarm went off on her watch, she was otherwise occupied. Even if only for ten minutes she couldn’t be disturbed once that alarm went off.

It was her time. It was time when, everyday, she could speak to Nicky. The arrangement had been made within a week of Rio moving to Arkansas. She’d made Alice call Jen and via Jen Alice had asked if Rio could have time with him.

The response had been: “If I can’t have you, my son should.” Agatha’s words, not Jen’s, a fact Jen was quick to make clear.

So Rio, then via Val, had arranged a five o’clock FaceTime everyday. And she’d helped Nicky with his alarm on his watch so they’d both have a permanent reminder that, although they were far away, they had a moment every day for just the two of them.

On every call Rio, knowing she shouldn’t, always asked about Agatha. Sometimes she didn’t want to hear the answer: “she’s a little sad today I think”/“she misses you we talked about you over dinner last night the whole time”/“we watched a movie last night and she fell asleep on the couch so I played with her hair just the way you told me to”.

Sometimes she could tell Agatha was in the room because Nicky kept looking up and smiling in a way he didn’t when it was just Val or just Jen, who’d lent him their phone.

Sometimes she heard Agatha snort at something she or Nicky had said.

Sometimes she wanted to call her name and see how long it would take her to appear on her screen.

But it was unsaid now that it was best to keep apart, best to not give themselves a tiny piece of a whole they couldn’t yet have.

Nicky wasn’t included in that, though. Nicky, an innocent in the war of custody that still raged. Nicky, who was so pleased to show off his Spanish every time he spoke to Rio. Nicky, who would regale her with stories of his basketball team and his friends who were now all wearing watches just like his and he hated it because it was a mellizo thing. Nicky, who sometimes let slip that he was nervous about his upcoming court appearance. Nicky, who got a A+ in his science test and came onto the call with a gold star stuck to his Celtics t-shirt.

And Rio, Rio loved the calls as much as Nicky did. Sometimes, if she had the time, she’d quiz Nicky on his Spanish. Sometimes she’d make up words and teach him them and the next day Nicky would always come back giggling his face off because his tutor (or sometimes Agatha) had told him that “el muchochocco” was not the word for “chocolate fountain”. Sometimes Nicky was on the basketball court outside and Val was holding the phone so Rio could watch him practice and holler her celebrations whenever he scored, and even when he didn’t.

It was the best part of her day when it was happening, and the worst when it was over.

So she made the worst part better by planning. And after three weeks of constant worsts every evening, she had come up with a plan so brilliant she couldn’t believe she’d not thought of it before. A plan that would fall into place tomorrow, with the help of Alice, and a lot of internet research.

But that evening, after Rio had been released from set around four thirty, the call with Nicky was different than usual. Val, for the first time ever, didn’t answer. Rio watched her face reflected back to her on her screen, getting more and more concerned as she sat in the middle of her bed in her hotel room.

The FaceTime timed out. She pressed to call again and this time, after ten tense seconds, Val answered. Her face filled the screen and Rio smiled in surprise, “Hey! What’s with the delay? Everything…?”

But she didn’t finish her question because Val’s face answered it before she had to.

“I’m going to give you to Agatha. Nicky’s having a bit of a meltdown and he’s shut himself in his room.”

Rio sat up straight. “A meltdown? Why? Is he hurt? What’s happened?”

“The trial,” Val sighed, “They’ve switched the dates and he’s needed tomorrow. We thought we had more time and…”

“He’s scared,” Rio deduced, looking away from Val’s face as she walked through the house to look down at the healing scar on her right wrist.

“Agatha,” she heard through the phone and looked up to see a blur of movement and colour and then Agatha’s face, frowning and full of concern. A small, relieved smile broke across it when she registered Rio staring up at her and her lips formed a word Rio couldn’t hear but knew to be: “Honey.”

“Hey. Is he okay?”

Agatha shook her head and Rio caught the tightness in her jaw.

“They’ve been messing with the schedule. They pushed it out again and now… it’s tomorrow. He’s upset. He’s scared, Rio. He hates crowds and hates attention and…”

“It’s okay,” Rio said gently, feeling her heart settle in her throat and pulse there unhappily. “Can I talk to him?”

Agatha’s lips twitched a little and Rio was witness to her tense profile as she turned from the phone to look to Nicky’s door and knock gently.

“Honey? I have Rio on the phone for you. I’m going to come in, okay? She wants to talk to you.”

Rio held her breath as Agatha went into Nicky’s room and she had to watch her face react to it rather than see from her perspective. But soon Nicky came into view. He was sitting on the floor by his bed, a basketball in his lap and his brow as furrowed as Rio had ever seen it. Agatha settled next to him and already had her arm around him.

“Hey, mellizo.”

“Hello.”

Rio smiled a little, pleased he was at least talking as his gaze fell to his basketball and he leaned into Agatha’s side.

“I hear you’re in court tomorrow?”

“I don’t want to be.”

“I know, bud. But sometimes we have to do things we don’t want to do.”

Nicky nodded but didn’t seem convinced. Rio opened her mouth to say something but didn’t know what to say and Agatha clocked it and said, “I’ll be right there, honey. Just like we discussed. Just like-…”

“Can I ask to have custody with you?”

Nicky’s eyes moved from his basketball to blink up at Rio and Rio felt all the breath leave her body. Her eyes flickered to Agatha but she looked just as breathless, just as devastated.

“Baby,” Rio managed to murmur, half to Nicky, half to Agatha. “That’s not how it works.”

“I don’t want daddy. I want mama and you. I don’t understand why it can’t happen. We’re a family and it’s like you keep lying to me and I wish, I wish-…”

“Honey,” Agatha picking it up now because Rio couldn’t. “We’re tres patitos.” The angle changed and Rio knew it was because Agatha was more focused on her son than where the camera was facing. She was looking at Nicky’s ceiling now as Agatha continued to speak.

“We’re family. Just a different sort of family. Not the kind of family that,” she heard Nicky sniff, “the court can intervene with, okay? We’re making sure you stay with me and that’s it. But staying with me means Rio too. And no one is taking you away from me. From us.”

Another sniff. Rio stood from the bed and went to settle at her desk. She propped the phone up against the mirror and picked up a piece of yellow card.

“I’m going to tell them I don’t want to be in custody with daddy.”

“Okay, honey. You tell them the truth. And I’ll be right there, and you can look at me and it’ll be like it’s just us.”

Rio was chewing on her cheek, her fingers moving faster, making violent folds in the paper, her brain working over time to remember the sequence.

“And maybe… melliza, maybe you can just move in? And… marry my mama and-…”

“Ah, fuck.” A maroon mistake appeared on her finger where she’d sliced herself with the sharp edge of the fast-moving card. She sucked the droplet of blood away and listened as Agatha responded: “Rio isn’t going anywhere, honey. She’ll always be around.”

“She’s away now,” Nicky pointed out as Rio focused back in, ignoring the stinging of her finger and focusing on perfecting the only thing she could perfect right now.

“She’s working, honey.”

“It’s not fair. All my friends have-…”

“There!”

Rio’s shout stopped Nicky and she looked to her phone just in time to see the view change and Agatha and Nicky both came into view. They both looked pale and more upset than Rio could handle.

But she held up her creation regardless and tried for a smile.

“El Patito,” she said hopefully, “I learned how to make them about a week ago because I missed you guys and I wanted to make more than flowers and-…” she trailed off because Nicky was sniffing and rubbing at his eye. “I miss you both,” she said softly, treading carefully around such a sensitive boy, “and I wish I could be there with you.”

She placed the duck down and Nicky sniffed and then said: “Can you teach me? And maybe… maybe I can have…”

Nicky made a noise that Rio never wanted to hear again. It was high pitched, and devastating.

“Sure. Sure. Do you have, um, do you have some card?”

Nicky sniffed and then nodded and disappeared from the frame and Rio was left with Agatha. But she couldn’t say anything. What could she say? Nicky would still hear her. So she just looked, she just forced herself to smile and saw that Agatha was staring after her son, rather than looking to Rio.

It was right, she knew. She’d have her eyes on the boy as well if she could.

Nicky was soon back in frame and Rio waited whilst Agatha moved them to his desk so she could crouch beside him on the chair and had just her head floating above the wood in the frame.

She spent the next twenty minutes patiently teaching Nicky how to make his own patito and when he finally made something that looked very much like a duck he was smiling again, albeit softly and shyly.

“Is it good?”

“It’s perfect, mellizo,” Rio cheered, trying to be happy enough for the three of them. “I’ll send mine to you and you can keep them on your desk.”

“Maybe you can make another for mama? Then I can have all three.”

“Sure can!” She grinned at Agatha through the screen and Agatha smiled as she rolled her eyes.

Nicky was toying with his duckling when he spoke again, “Is there any way you can be here tomorrow? It’s just I’d really like to see you before I have to go to the court.”

Rio sucked in a sharp breath at the request but was saved answering by Agatha’s voice, soft and steady, “Honey, Rio has to work. She’s working hard on her new show and she won’t be able to make it, remember? Right, Rio?”

Agatha was giving her an out, already laying down her excuse so Rio’s guilt-maddened brain didn’t have to come up with one. Or else she was trying to help Nicky, trying to say he would be okay even if she weren’t there. Which was true. Which Rio hoped would be true.

“But hey,” Rio said, nodding when Nicky looked up at her with those wide eyes, “by the time you get back tomorrow there’ll be a gift waiting for you. I’ve sent you something that I think you’ll really like. It was supposed to arrive before you had to go to court but it’s something to look forward to for when you’re all done.”

Nicky didn’t seem phased by this at all and he raised his left fist to rub at his left eye. So Rio waited in patient silence until he spoke again.

“Okay. I know you have to work. It’s okay. I’ll be okay.”

Of course Nicky would be trying to reassure her when he was actively crying about something. She cleared her throat and shifted where she sat.

“You’re taking Scratchy, right? Just like we agreed?”

Nicky nodded.

“And if you get scared you give him a squeeze and you watch your mom, right? She’ll be right there. And as soon as you’re done you can give me a call and tell me all about it.”

Nicky nodded again and then looked down at the paper duck in his hands.

“How much longer?”

The question was open-ended but Rio knew what he was asking.

“A couple months. But I’ll come home for a couple days soon, okay?”

“Okay,” Nicky sniffed quietly and Agatha raised herself up where she had been sitting back on her knees beside him.

“And we can plan a big movie night? We’ll make a fort and get all the best snacks in.”

“I still have some British chocolate left,” Nicky added, rubbing at his other eye now. “We can share it.”

“Oh I couldn’t take that from you!”

“It’s okay,” Nicky said as Agatha kissed his temple and he blushed a little. “It can be your welcome home gift.”

Rio felt the pang of it then, more acutely than before, how much she missed the people who were now her home. She missed how Nicky giggled sometimes even before he got to the punchline of his joke. She missed how she could sneak up on Agatha when she was cooking and Agatha would simply hum and melt back into her. She missed how, for stolen moments of time, they were allowed to be an actual family.

“It won’t be long,” she promised quietly, doing her worst impression of a woman who wasn’t about to cry, “I’ll be home soon.”

Nicky nodded and began tying with his new duckling. It was Agatha who spoke next: “We should go, Rio. Need an early night ahead of tomorrow.”

“Hey,” Rio said quickly, wanting to make the most of the time they had left. “Can you send me a picture of you in your outfit tomorrow? Show me how handsome you are?”

Nicky sniffed and nodded, a small smile playing at his lips as he turned to Agatha.

“Tell Rio what you said the other day, about my new tie.”

Agatha rolled her eyes affectionately and turned to Rio, “I said he looked double handsome in it.”

“Woah,” Rio announced, “Double handsome is crazy!”

“We can get you a matching one,” Nicky offered up, a light switching on in his gaze again, even if the whites of his eyes were tinged with red. “And we’d look double handsome together. Quadruple handsome!”

Rio laughed and agreed and they signed off, Nicky the first to say “I love you” and Rio saying it back whilst Agatha blew a kiss and then they were gone.

“Hasta banana,” she said to the empty screen, repeating Nicky’s preferred sign off with a soft sigh.

She didn’t enjoy drinks with her cast that night. And she didn’t sleep well either.

But then again, neither did Agatha, and neither did Nicky.

Nicky woke groggily, rubbing at his eyes, tucked up in his bed, with Scratchy lost somewhere under the covers and his mom smiling down at him.

She looked tired, he thought, as he sat slowly and she pressed a kiss to his cheek.

“Buen día, mama.”

“¿Español hoy?” Spanish today?

“Sí, para Rio.” Yes, for Rio.

His mom smiled and Nicky tried to smile back but he couldn’t make himself. His eyes stung and he looked away quickly but his mom was too quick. She was alway too quick.

Her fingers dug into his sides and he released a squeal of surprise and delight as she tickled away his tears and he wriggled away after a while of struggling to.

“¡Basta, mama!” Enough, mama!

He giggled his last and held his hands up defensively as Agatha grinned and made grabby hands at him.

“¡Vuelve aquí!” Come back here!

Nicky squealed and ran away, making it down stairs and to the kitchen until he slowed and his laughter died. Agatha had caught him up and had his hand on his shoulder now as Nicky, in his Spiderman pyjamas, blinked up at the two people staring at him.

Auntie Jen and a strange man in dark glasses.

“You must be Nicholas?”

Nicky nodded gently and cleared his throat as he held his hand out expectantly. “Hello. It’s nice to meet you.”

The man didn’t move and Nicky frowned a little as Agatha squeezed his shoulder, “Mr Murdock is blind, honey. He can’t see your hand.”

Nicky felt his cheeks flame and he dropped his hand immediately, worried he’d done something incredibly rude. As the man smiled and approached him, he blinked slowly when he dropped before him and held out his own hand.

“Very polite of you to want to shake my hand. Very grown up.”

Nicky hesitated, wondering if his mom had lied about his man being blind when he’d known exactly where to crouch in front of him. But his mom never lied so this man must just be very smart.

He shook his hand, trying to make sure his grip with firm even though he still felt frightened.

“I hear you’re a little nervous? Your mom here has told me all about how bright and brave you are so I’m sure you’ll be just fine.”

Nicky nodded and then remembered Mr Murdock couldn’t see him so he said: “Thank you.”

The man smiled and then stood up again and Nicky watched him look straight at his mom as he reached back to take her hand.

“We need to be there early. There are a few things we should discuss and Nicholas can wait with Jen or Val in the holding room.”

Nicky didn’t like the sound of that. A holding room sounded like a place you go when you’re naughty, when you talk in class or throw your food in the cafeteria. He shrank back into his mom and shot a glance at Jen who was busy on her phone.

She was always on her phone now and Nicky wondered if she was ever speaking to Rio. He shifted a little and his mom squeezed his hand and then touched his shoulder to let him know it was okay to go. So he carefully stepped around the stranger and passed over to Jen, hovering silently by her side for a second as his mom continued her conversation.

“Auntie Jen?”

“Yes, babe?”

Nicky shifted from foot to foot and then said, “is Rio around maybe?”

Jen looked at him and Nicky lifted his chin slightly, sniffing and quickly rubbing at his eye to make sure he was pushing back the stinging he could feel there again.

“She’s working today. You want me to text her?”

Nicky nodded quickly and pulled up the chair beside her to sit close. “Yes please. But say it’s okay if she doesn’t text back, I know she’s busy.”

Jen hummed and Nicky sniffed again, reaching for a glass of orange juice he knew it be his because it was in his Celtics cup.

He took a sip as Jen said: “What shall we say?”

“Umm. Could you send a little green heart please? And then say, melliza I feel a little nervous but I-…” his eyes filled suddenly and he took another sip of juice to try and focus on that instead. But then Jen’s hand was on his head and he shrank from it, putting the glass down quickly as he sniffed and wiped at his eyes. “Or, or maybe-, maybe-, I-…”

“Hey,” Jen said firmly beside him, making him glance at her briefly before he turned away. “It’s okay to be scared. You can tell her you’re scared.”

Nicky sniffed and nodded and then another hand, a more welcome one, was on his head and his mom was kissing his cheek again.

“Are we texting Rio?” She asked gently, confusing Nicky as to how she’d know that. His mama was so smart.

“Yes,” Nicky sniffed, wiping at his eyes again. Why was he crying still? His mom scratched his head gently but said nothing about it as she leant over to see the screen Jen was showing them.

“Okay,” Nicky said after taking in a long, slow breath. “The green heart, please. And then, tell her I don’t feel very brave today but I… I’m going to try my best to be brave. And that… that I hope she has an awesome day at work and… and… and that I love her. And maybe another, another green heart. So she knows it’s me.”

Jen tapped his message and Nicky nodded when it was done and pressed the little blue arrow button to send it when Jen offered it to him.

“You are very brave,” his mom said close to his ear, making him turn with a small smile and his watery eyes.

“And I’m so proud of you.”

Nicky nodded because his mama said it all the time and he knew she was. It helped. At least enough so he could eat his cereal and drink his juice with no more tears.

And by the time he’d changed into his new suit and Agatha had helped him with his new tie, he felt a little better. Taking pictures for Rio helped too. He posed by himself, smiling as big as he could and doing his best to show off his teeth just the way Rio did when she smiled big.

But when his hand was back in his mom’s and Val met them at the door to come with them in the car, he didn’t feel so good anymore.

He was in the back seat, sandwiched between his mom and Jen and both were on their phones, both texting someone he didn’t know or tapping way at something he didn’t understand.

Until, as he petted Scratchy in his lap and stared straight ahead, Jen nudged his side and said, “hey, Rio.”

Nicky turned so quickly he saw stars.

“Mellizo! You look so so handsome! Double handsome!”

A wave of something warm washed over him then, and he knew it wasn’t just the flush of his cheeks. He thought for a second and it felt like when his dad left or when the ball circled the hoop and then fell in or when the final bell rang at school and he could go play with his friends.

Relief.

He smiled, and it didn’t feel forced finally. Maybe he wouldn’t be happy today, but relief felt pretty nice too.

“Thank you,” he said, adjusting his tie nervously. “Did you get my text?”

“I did. I don’t have long but I wanted to call and tell you that you are so brave and that you will be fine.”

Nicky swallowed and nodded and dropped his gaze because his eyes were filled with tears again and he didn’t want Rio to see. Brave boys didn’t cry.

“Hey,” Rio’s voice was soft and Nicky worried she was disappointed suddenly. “I love you, mellizo. I’ll call later if I can, when your bell rings, right? I wish I could be there to give you a big hug.”

Not disappointed then, just sad. Both were bad. Both made Nicky feel bad.

But he nodded because he couldn’t do anything else and then, sniffing softly he raised his gaze again and rubbed at his eye.

“You’ll be home soon?”

“As soon as I can be.”

“Okay.”

Rio held her palm up to the camera and Nicky smiled a little as he raised his fist to meet it. He hiccuped as Rio said “I love you” and managed to whisper it back, and then she was gone.

His mama held him a little closer after that and he leant into her, only a little worried that everyone in the car would think he was a big baby. But Rio had told him he wasn’t, that even with Scratchy with him he was brave.

So he focused on that, as well as the way his mom stroked gently through his hair until they had arrived and nothing felt quiet or gentle anymore.

There were people there waiting for them, familiar people, friendly ones and scary ones with cameras. Paparazzi, Nicky knew. He also knew them as “vultures” and words he wasn’t allowed to repeat that Auntie Jen had said.

He held tight to his mom’s hand as she pulled him close outside the car. Val was there too, her hand on his shoulder, keeping him safe. He wished Rio were there as well so he could jump on her back and he could hide against her. Maybe she could have carried him into the court and he could speak from her back. He was sure he’d feel braver if he could be held high above everyone with his arms around his twin.

When they got through the vultures he was pleased his mama kept him close. He held on tight until he had to walk through a metal detector and place Scratchy on a little tray to go through without him. He looked sad all alone so when Nicky got him back he squeezed him extra tight to make sure he was fine.

They were taken through a tall hallway, led to a little room Nicky assumed to be the holding room and there was where his mom left him, kissing his cheek and reassuring him she’d be back and telling him to be good for Jen and Val.

And when she was gone Nicky looked around properly. The room was bare but it had a few chairs and a couple tables in it. There was a water cooler and a basket of what looked like packaged cookies he recognised from hotel rooms he’d been in before. But that was it.

Not so scary, but not so good either.

“Wanna play catch?” Val asked with a smile, producing a small ball from somewhere in her jacket. “Take your mind off of things?”

Nicky agreed and placed Scratchy down on a seat near where Jen was, trusting she’d look after him.

For a while he threw the ball back and forth with Val and he calmed down. This was fine, he would be fine. His mom stood in front of crowds all the time. Rio did it too. Plus he’d been promised there wouldn’t be that many people there. He could do this. He could be brave and tell them he wanted custody of his mom and maybe Rio too if they would please let him.

He dropped the ball.

Something about the act made him choke up suddenly and his Auntie Jen was by his side in an instant, dropping down before him to straighten his suit jacket.

“Hey. What was that I hear about double handsome, huh? Can’t be crying when you’re looking so good.”

Nicky nodded and swallowed, making a small noise he didn’t mean to make when he did.

“What if I say the wrong thing?”

He had to ask, he had to keep asking. His mama said it was impossible and Rio said the same but he often said the wrong thing when his dad was there so what if it happened again today?

“No chance,” Jen said gently, no straightening his tie. “You’re the smartest kid ever, remember? Your mama’s son. You will be so good up there and you will say all the right things. They just want to know who you want to live with.”

“My mama,” Nicky said quickly, “and Rio.”

He watched as Jen paused and then reached to tuck his hair behind his ear and he didn’t shy away this time.

“Right. Your mama,” she said gently, smiling a little but Nicky couldn’t return it.

When Jen was done fussing and had kissed the to of his head, which felt a little unusual, he returned his attention the the game of catch.

They played for a while until Jen disappeared to get coffee for her and Val and a soda for Nicky, but before she returned his mom had arrived, accompanied by the lawyer man and two other people he didn’t recognise.

He took a step back even as Agatha ducked down to her knees before him. She looked tired still, even if she had makeup on now. Her lips were pinker than usual and Nicky wondered why ladies did that, especially ones who were already so beautiful.

“Makes me feel fancy,” his mama had once told him when he’d asked after watching her put some on one night.

“You are always fancy, mama,” he’d said and then received so many kisses to his face that he grinned when he looked in the mirror that night before bed. He had fancy written all over him.

But back now, in this sad, bad room, his mom looked fancy, beautiful, and scared. He touched her face as she touched his hair.

“You got Scratchy?”

“Yes.”

She smiled as he pointed to the chair where Scratchy was waiting patiently.

“All you have to do is tell the truth, honey. It’s as easy as that.”

“I’m scared,” he said gently, keeping his voice low so only his mama could hear.

“I know you are. I’m a little scared too.”

“You are?”

His mama nodded and looked down and Nicky followed her gaze to her wrist. He watched as she removed the string bracelet Rio had made her and as she put it around his wrist, tucking it beneath his watch strap where it was a little too big for him.

“Remember,” she said quietly, leaning in to whisper to just him, “I love you more than there are stars in the sky.”

“I love you the same.”

It was the last thing Nicky said before he found himself in the big courtroom, holding his mom’s hand beneath a dark desk as he stared up at the scary looking old man he knew to be the judge.

On his way in he’d spotted his dad and grandmother but he’d looked away quickly, unwilling to look at the man who had scared his mama and the woman who had cut his hair and hurt his melliza.

He kept his gaze down mostly, clutching Scratchy just as tight as he clutched Agatha.

They’d been made to stand when the judge had entered but other than that he’d kept his head down and his eyes on his mama’s pal fingers and the golden ring she wore on her left hand.

He liked that ring. He knew his mama did too. He knew, though no one had told him, his melliza had bought her that ring. He knew she loved his mama very much. And his mama loved her the same.

“Nicholas?” Nicky’s head snapped up and he gulped, nodding only once as Agatha squeezed his hand.

The judge gestured for him to come forward but Nicky didn’t move, frozen in his seat.

But his mom did. She stood and encouraged him to, walking around with him and keeping a hold on his hand.
