“Highly unusual, Ms Harkness,” the judge commented but his mom said nothing as she took him to a little box beside the judge where a security guard opened a door for him and his mom stopped. He turned to her and she smiled and kissed his temple and then he was alone as she walked back to her seat, all the while glancing over her shoulder at him.

Nicky’s breathing picked up when he saw how many faces were looking his way and he caught the bright grin of his dad.

“Master Harkness?” Nicky jumped and looked to the judge who was gesturing to the little seat in the box and he moved carefully to sit in it, quickly tucking away Scratchy in his inside breast pocket so he wouldn’t be stared at too.

He swallowed thickly as he focused back in on his mom and saw her leaning over to have the blind lawyer man talk quietly into her ear.

“Son?”

Nicky looked up and blinked slowly at the grey-haired judge. He shifted and his hand reached inside his jacket to seek the comfort of Scratchy, hoping touching him would help.

“Yes, sir,” he said quietly, finding the button of Scratchy’s nose with his thumb.

“We’re here for you, alright? This doesn’t have to be scary. Let’s just have a little chat.”

Nicky nodded because it was the polite thing to do but he wanted to tell the judge that this was scary and that he didn’t want to have a chat.

“Now, son,” Nicky looked to his mom, wondering why she wasn’t stopping this man from calling him ‘son’. “Do you have any hobbies?”

His mom smiled a little, but Nicky knew she was scared too. He wished Rio were here. She could hold his mom’s hand and then she would be okay.

He turned back to the judge and swallowed as he felt his eyes fill with tears he didn’t want to shed.

“Basketball. I’m the captain of my team. I also like movies and baseball and I like to read.”

The judge smiled and Nicky noticed he had a gold tooth. He shifted in his seat again and looked back around to his mom. She nodded at him and Nicky sniffed quietly. Scratchy’s nose felt rough against his thumb.

“Very good, son.”

Nicky watched his mom as she leant over to her lawyer and he whispered something in her ear again. He moved his hand to Scratchy’s ear and held it tight. Scratchy wouldn’t mind.

“Do you have a basketball team?”

“Yes. Celtics.”

Nicky looked down at his watch and twisted his wrist to see the little bell in the top of the screen that would go off when it was time for Rio to call. He wanted it to ring now.

“Uh huh,” the judge said, as Nicky kept his head down and stared at the little bell, willing it to ring.

“You’ve been to games?”

Nicky swallowed and looked up again at his mom. She was sitting straight once more, her eyes shining as though she was about to cry. Nicky sniffed and stopped holding Scratchy so he could rub at his eyes.

“Yes, sir.”

“In Boston?”

“Yes, sir.”

Nicky looked back at his watch again and then at his mom. She was trying to smile and Nicky did his best to try to smile at her too but as he did a silent tear fell from his eye and Agatha shifted forwards in her seat, only to be held back by her lawyer.

Nicky sniffed and looked down again.

“No need to be upset, son. We all want you to be comfortable here.”

It wasn’t true, and Nicky didn’t understand why the judge was lying to him. But he nodded because he’d been told to be polite and he’d promised his mama and his melliza that he would be.

“You were last in Boston over your birthday?”

“Yes, sir.”

“Did you have a good time, son?”

Nicky sniffed again and rubbed at both his eyes before saying, “Yes. The best time.”

“What did you do?”

“We watched a game and then had pizza and in,” he sniffed and wiped at his cheek, “in the morning we went to the park and I rode my bike.”

“And you felt safe?”

Nicky looked up, frowning more than he already had been. He could see the gold tooth blinking in the light as he looked at the judge and for a moment he was confused.

“Safe? With… with my mama?”

He looked to Agatha and saw that she was frowning too and he shifted in his seat, moving forwards in the stand. Agatha did the same.

“My mama always keeps me safe,” he said quietly, feeling another tear fall and he reached to wipe it.

“You’re a shy little boy,” the judge said and Nicky hiccuped softly as from beside Agatha a voice called out: “Your Honour!”

Nicky looked around at the judge and saw him hold his hand up to silence the nice lawyer his mom had hired.

“Is that why you’re upset now? Lots of people looking at you?”

Nicky swallowed and turned back to his mom. Her knuckles were white where she was gripping the table and Nicky wished again that Rio were here to hold them.

“I am upset because… because I don’t want custody to happen. I just… I want to be with my mama and I don’t want to be here.”

He saw Agatha’s lips twitch into a tentative smile and he tried to smile back but found it too hard so dropped his head down again.

“Okay, son,” the judge said and Nicky sniffed and then wiped the underside of his nose with the back of his hand.

“Can I ask about someone called Rio Vidal?”

“Your Honour,” the lawyer called again, “I must question relevancy.”

Nicky sniffed but didn’t look up to see the judge had silenced him with just one hand.

“Son?”

Nicky nodded and looked to the screen of his watch again. The bell wasn’t ringing.

“She is… a friend?”

“My melliza,” Nicky said, raising his chin as he did. He was proud of Rio and knew she wouldn’t want him to be hiding right now. “She’s my melliza. She’s only not here with us because she has to work but… I wish she were.”

He’d been told to tell the truth. His mama always told him to tell the truth. But as he said it he wondered if he shouldn’t have. He turned his gaze back to Agatha and saw that her eyes were closed and she looked more scared than before.

He sought out Scratchy again and held his ear.

“Melliza?” The judge asked.

“It means twin in Spanish because… because she’s from Puerto Rico and we… we look a little the same. I’m learning Spanish.” He swallowed, “for her because… because her dad, Señor Miguel died and… I want to be able to talk to her in Spanish so she feels closer to him.”

The lawyer was whispering to his mama again and Nicky wanted to know he’d said the right thing but there was no way of taking it back now so he did nothing but held Scratchy a little tighter.

“And she was with you in Boston?”

“Yes, sir.”

“She carried you to the car?”

Nicky blinked and looked up at the judge. He sniffed and rubbed his left eye, nodding silently as he did.

“She carries you sometimes? When there are big crowds?”

“Yes, sir.”

“Can you tell me why, son?”

Nicky sniffed and nodded again. “She keeps me safe. I don’t… I don’t like it when… when people try to get to us a-and she keeps me safe so I don’t have to see them and they can’t see me.”

“You’re a big boy to be carried by her.”

“Rio is strong,” Nicky said sadly, rubbing at his eye again.

The judge hummed and Nicky looked around to his mom again, and was relieved to see her watching him with a sad smile. He tried again to smile back but it didn’t quite work.

“Son, would you indulge me something?”

Nicky turned back, not quite understanding the question.

“Would you,” the judge leant over towards him and Nicky couldn’t help the crinkle in his nose at the smell of coffee on his breath, “would you allow your daddy to pick you up? Just like your melissa?”

“Melliza,” Nicky corrected quietly. He rubbed his eye again, unsure why he was being asked this.

“Do I have to?”

“I’d appreciate it if you did.”

Nicky nodded slowly and looked to his mom who was frowning, her eyes up on the judge instead of on him.

The judge sat straight again and waved his hand in the direction of Ralph.

“Mr Bohner, could you approach the bench please?”

Nicky watched as his dad stood and buttoned up his suit jacket. He was grinning but didn’t look happy and Nicky shrank back in his chair, already worried about him being nearby when his mom wasn’t close too.

“Would you please give Nicholas here a piggy back? Or, carry him how you usually would?”

Ralph blinked stupidly and turned to look at Nicky who was rubbing at his eyes again. They were red now, raw from the tears he’d shed without meaning to.

“Are you serious?”

Nicky looked down at his watch again. Maybe he could make the bell ring so Rio would just have to call sooner.

“You have a problem picking up your child, Mr Bohner?”

Rio never had a problem with it, Nicky thought. Even when she was injured and was recovering in a hospital bed she was always happy to cuddle him.

He sniffed softly and wiped at a fresh tear as Ralph said: “Sure. Come here, kiddo. Like we usually do.”

Nicky couldn’t remember ever having been lifted by his dad. He didn’t want to be lifted by him. The last time he’d been anywhere near him he’d pushed him over and his mom had shouted at Rio even though it wasn’t her fault so he didn’t move even as Ralph motioned at him to do so.

“It’s okay, son,” the judge said softly, “go ahead.”

Nicky looked back to Ralph and frowned up at his great big smile. It didn’t look real or happy or reassuring and Nicky rubbed at his eyes one last time before he slipped down from his seat and slowly clambered out of the little box they’d put him in.

He looked at his mama as he did this and saw she was standing now, leaning forwards against the table.

“It’s okay, honey. Do as the judge asks.”

Nicky nodded and tucked his fingers back to clutch at the cuffs of his jacket. Ralph was already moving him, his hands on his shoulders in order to do so.

“Right,” he said, umming and ahhing as he turned Nicky to face him and eyed him up. “Uh. I’ll bend and you jump, okay? Like we usually do!” He ruffled Nicky’s hair and Nicky hiccuped softly, taking a small step back when Ralph turned his back on him and crouched.

Ralph was taller than Rio. But even Nicky knew that Rio could have been twice his height and still would have found a way to make herself small enough so Nicky could climb on.

He hesitated, encouraged by Ralph’s wriggling fingers and the eyes that were all watching him. He didn’t want to do it but he tried his best to make his body do what his mind didn’t want.

Nicky jumped forwards, and missed the mark completely. He pathetically slid down Ralph’s back and tried again, trying to lift his leg up so Ralph could catch it.

But Ralph had no experience and was already growing frustrated that Nicky had embarrassed him like this. So he pulled away and Nicky stumbled where he stood, chewing on his lip as Ralph turned to him and in one swoop had lifted him up into his arms and released a loud, fake laugh.

“You rascal! Got you!”

Nicky was horrified that he was up so high, and had his hands on Ralph’s shoulders but felt insecure, and so unsafe he wanted to cry all over again.

“Please put me down!”

“Ralph!” Agatha shouted, making a move to go around the table but prevented from doing so by her lawyer.

Ralph didn’t listen to either his son or his wife and instead turned to the judge as Nicky hiccuped and sniffed, his head higher than Ralph’s and his lip trembling.

“See? Just a little scared, that’s all. Soft. But we do this all the time.”

Nicky shook his head and turned his eyes to the judge who was looking down at something on his desk. Ralph’s hold on his legs was tight, tighter than was comfortable and Nicky regretted how tight he’d been holding Scratchy earlier. He must have hurt him.

“Please put me down,” he whispered, looking down at Ralph as he turned to look up at him.

They made eye contact properly for the first time maybe ever and Nicky gasped quietly for the look in his blue eyes. Ralph hated him. And Nicky swallowed thickly because Ralph had blue eyes like his mama but his mama had never looked at him like that.

Nicky swallowed and then said, “put me down, you’re hurting me.”

“Mr Bohner,” the judge called out, but Nicky didn’t know why. He just knew that his dad was staring up at him and there was nothing he could do to escape. So he looked right back, a courage coming to him from a place he didn’t know he had.

“You are not my daddy anymore. I don’t want you to be and mama-…”

“Your honour!” Ralph interjected, shouting so loudly in Nicky’s face that he flinched. “Can we take a quick recess? I’m feeling quite emotional getting to hold my son again.”

Nicky was dropped down unceremoniously to the floor, his hair was ruffled again, and before he could blink Ralph had left him standing in the middle of the court all alone.

“Darling boy!”

“Mrs Harkness!”

Nicky looked up as his grandmother came towards him and managed to take a step back before her hands were on him.

“Mrs Harkness!”

“Forgive an old lady, Frank, for wanting to see her grandson.”

Nicky gasped in shock when he felt the cruel press of nails against his scalp and then the relief of them retracting and being replaced by a soft, welcome touch. He turned into Agatha, hiccuping as she ducked down to wipe his tears and hold him away from Evanora.

And as he looked up and into her eyes, he knew he’d been brave and said the right thing. His mama loved him and he loved her and as he threw his arms around her neck he squeezed her so tight he pressed a button on his watch without meaning to.

The little bell rang on the screen, his alarm went off, the soft, tinkling noise filling the silent court room as Nicky cuddled his mom. Rio loved him too.

“Mrs Harkness,” the judge said in a clipped but less urgent tone than before, “please take your seat. I’ve seen enough. Son? You are dismissed. Thank you for being here today.”

“Your honour!” A man who Nicky didn’t recognise but assumed would be another lawyer shouted. “We need to cross-examine-…!”

“A child? Not in my courtroom.”

There was a sound of a giant slap and Nicky winced and then hiccuped against Agatha and she pulled away after whispering about how well he’d done in his ear. But he just wanted to be home. He wanted to be cuddled up with his mom and with Rio arriving with her big grin and her warm hugs.

He was taken back to the sad room by Val and remained there for two more hours, plied with snacks by Jen and stories of England and “real football” by Val. But really he was trying not to cry.

When his mama finally came back to him he rushed to her and Agatha lifted him off his feet in a mid-air embrace.

“Let’s get you home.”

Jen said goodbye because she needed to be home to do some work and Nicky gave her a quick hug before he jumped out of the car with his mom.

More paparazzi, more vultures, but the worst was done. It was over with. He didn’t have to stand in front of a room full of people and tell everyone he loved his mama and didn’t love his dad. They knew now.

They were helped inside, helped to keep clear of the man with the big camera who was now permanently outside their house by Val and a few of the other bigger men who always smiled at Nicky but were generally quite frightening.

But his mama froze when they entered the house and Nicky realised immediately why.

“Hi,” Alice said tentatively as Agatha stared across at her and Nicky excitedly looked around the room.

“Rio’s here?!”

“Oh.” Alice uttered, she hadn’t considered Nicky might assume she wouldn’t be alone. “No, kid. Just me.”

Nicky looked crestfallen and Agatha reached to cross her hands over his chest as Alice dropped her gaze to the floor.

“But she’s, uh, she’s sent a gift and I’m the lucky deliver-er.”

She raised her gaze again with a hopeful smile and saw that Agatha had already begun to direct Nicky away from her though he was craning his neck to look back.

“Wait,” she hurried over but it was too late to stop the thing already in motion. And she saw from behind as Nicky gasped and did his best Risky Business impression by sliding on his knees across the floor to the brown and white bunny wriggling his nose at him in his cage.

“She bought all this?” Agatha asked quietly, watching her son as he wriggled his finger through the bars and the little bunny hopped closer to sniff.

“There’s a file with instructions, all handwritten. She made sure to write down everything she thought would be useful. She’s bought toys and food and an outdoor hutch that’s already been set up for you. And,” Alice fished in her pocket as Agatha turned to her expectantly, “here.”

Sitting in the palm of her hand was the 3D heart Rio had made with red card. She offered it up and Agatha took it as gently as if she were picking up a baby bunny.

“You can open it,” Alice said carefully, trying to be as helpful as possible to remain in Agatha’s good graces.

She had to bite her tongue not to correct Agatha when she first went to open it like a fat little book but on her next try she got it, curling open a triangular piece at the top of the heart as Nicky called out to her: “mama, can I take him out?”

“I’ll help,” Alice offered, leaving Agatha to tip the heart upside down so tiny heart babies could fall out along with a piece of purple paper that had Rio’s handwriting on it.

“Look after my heart for me”

Alice looked back as she handed the tiny bunny to Nicky and it continued to sniff curiously at him, twitching its nose into his palm. The actress was staring at whatever Rio had written on the tiny piece of paper and, as Alice blinked, she realised she was crying.

She looked away quickly, pretending to be interested in the little bunny Nicky was stroking gently but really, just trying to give the most famous woman in the world some privacy.

“You know his name?”

“Scratchy,” Nicky said with a soft smile, indicating the name plate on the side of the crate. “He looks like him too. Did Rio pick him herself?”

“She did,” Alice said with an amused grin. “She took ages trying to find the perfect little guy for you.”

“And I get to keep him?”

“Mmhm. She’s got you everything you need to keep him safe and happy.”

“And maybe she’ll come back home sooner if he’s here because she’ll want to see him.”

Alice opened her mouth to respond but found it difficult to find the words. This kid was smart and sensitive and she knew how much he loved her friend. So she said the only thing she could: “She loves you very much, you know? And she’s so proud of you for today. She wishes she could be here.”

Nicky looked up from Scratchy for the first time properly and for the millionth time, Alice was taken aback by how similar he was to Rio.

“She’s proud?”

Alice opened her mouth to confirm but found her words stolen by Agatha, who’d joined them now and was on her knees beside Nicky.

“So proud, honey. She tells Alice everyday, right, Alice?”

Alice blinked and then nodded, trying to fight the way her eyes suddenly were filling with tears. How the hell did Rio do it?

“All the time.”

“Especially today,” Agatha continued, stealing the spotlight from Alice because she was clearly struggling. Nicky turned to her instead. “You were so brave and did so well.”

“I could have done better, maybe.”

Alice watched as Agatha shook her head and realised how hard it must be to keep her plans from her son when all he wanted was reassurance. No, she thought, as she turned back to his wide, tearful eyes, he just wanted Rio.

She bit down on her lip and looked down at the bunny now being fussed by Agatha too.

“You did so well,” Agatha whispered, “And I'm proud of you too. So proud.”

Nicky nodded stiffly and Alice watched his lips twitch and then his tongue stick into the side of his cheek as he visibly tried not to cry.

“Hey,” she said gently as he leant into Agatha’s side and let her put her arm around him. “You know Rio does that? The tongue in her cheek thing?”

She watched as Nicky turned shy again and hid his head against his mom, only daring to peek out at Alice as she sat back slightly, annoyed she’d accidentally put her foot in her mouth.

Nicky’s gaze dropped to the bunny who wriggled and then hopped to settle against Agatha’s bended knee where she was sitting cross-legged. And Alice cleared her throat quietly, making the mistake of looking up and seeing Agatha glare at her.

“Are you staying? For dinner?”

“No, I-… I should get back. Rio asked me to deliver everything and make sure it was perfect and I’ve done that so I should head.”

Agatha nodded and Alice made to stand but stopped when Nicky spoke again: “Is Rio okay? I talk to her and she seems so happy all the time and I just… her job is to play pretend and I want to-…” Nicky cleared his throat and poked his tongue into his cheek and then seemed to think better of it. “Two moms can have a kid. Does she know? Mama do you know that?”

Alice, out of her depth, looked to Agatha and saw the panic and sadness in her but didn’t know how to help so she became bold and she reached for Nicky’s hand to draw his attention back to her.

“Hey. I have never seen Rio happier than when she’s playing basketball with you, or when she calls you on FaceTime, or when she gets to see you, or even when she talks about you. She loves you, and she is so proud of you. And she’s sad when she’s not with you or your mama and she always wishes she could be here. But she’ll be back soon and everything,” she glanced at Agatha who looked starry-eyed but who nodded just once, “everything will be different.”

Nicky smiled for the first time, at least at Alice and not at the rabbit currently sleeping in Agatha’s lap, and Alice knew then she’d said the right thing, or, maybe, she’d not completely fucked up.

“I should go,” she said quietly, and as she stood Nicky spoke again.

“Thank you, Alice. Rio is happy when she talks about you too. I know she loves you. Very much.”

God, this fucking kid. How did the scariest woman in the world make this fucking kid? But then, she realised as he smiled up at her, Rio made this fucking kid. Maybe not literally, but her friend was in there, clear as day. Even if Nicky had been born with bright blue eyes and lighter hair, he was her kid.

And Alice would get that DNA test if it killed her.

She nodded once to Agatha, hoping she had nailed at least this interaction.

Nicky was happy, or as happy as he could be. And Agatha, well, she couldn’t really read how Agatha was feeling. But she wasn’t shouting, and that was something.

As she turned to leave, she stepped on a bag of carrots she’d left on the floor and tripped, nudging the coffee table and disturbing its contents. But she corrected herself before anything smashed or any real damage was done.

She span in celebration and held her hands in the air and looked to Agatha and Nicky who’d both turned to her.

“I’m good! I’m so good! All good!”

But Agatha’s face fell and Alice’s stomach with it. She’d dropped her gaze to Alice’s foot and Alice looked to it too and lifted it slowly to see a crushed piece of red paper on the floor.

Rio’s heart. She’d crushed Rio’s heart.

“Fuck,” she said, loud enough for Agatha to hear and Nicky to gasp at.

“ALICE YOU BETTER GET OUT OF MY HOUSE RIGHT NOW BEFORE I KILL YOU!”

Alice was running already, stumbling her way to the door. She ripped it open and gasped for the warm air of the early evening that hit her lungs. It was confirmed then, as she made her way through the usual security contingent keeping Rio’s family safe, she was destined for Agatha to be pissed at her, she was destined for her to hate her guts.

Fuck.

The first thing she did after kissing Jen when she got home was to call Rio.

“Hey,” Rio breathed, somehow breathless even though she’d just been waiting for someone, anyone to call her. “Is he okay? Is he… Alice is he okay?”

“He loves you so much,” Alice said just as breathless as Rio, which made Rio panic.

“What’s wrong? You sound-…”

“Babe,” Alice said just as Rio heard a door close on the other end of the line. “I… I have to go, okay?”

“Wait! What’s wrong? Why? I-…”

“Rio Vidal,” Jen’s voice came on the line, strong and annoyed. “Nicky did well in court. He was brave and he told the judge and Ralph he didn’t want him to get custody. He didn’t cry too much and he told everyone that he loved you and he loved his mom. Agatha is very proud. They’re home, safe, and the bunny apparently won’t leave Agatha alone he keeps hopping after her so now he’s asleep in the bed with the two of them because Nicky had a big day and is very tired. Now, fuck off because I haven’t seen my girlfriend in weeks and I’d very much like to have sex with her, okay?”

Rio blinked, trying to process such a large amount of information.

And Jen took her silence for precisely what it was so she added: “You did good with the rabbit. Nicky’s fine. Agatha is fine. I’m going to have sex now, goodnight.”

Jen hung up and Rio stared at the wall. She thought for a moment and then stared down at the keypad of her phone. She tapped in the number she’d memorised like it was a line in a movie.

“Hello?”

“Hey.”

“Rio.”

“I’m sorry, I just had your number memorised and I hadn’t heard anything about today and-…”

“No, it’s okay. I’m glad you called. Alice left and Nicky was so excited about the bunny but he’s had a big day and crashed pretty much immediately.”

Rio nodded and looked down at her bed sheets and saw two heavy droplets of tears fall onto them.

“He liked the rabbit?”

“He wished it were you.”

Rio nodded more, and closed her eyes. “It went okay?”

“He was so brave.”

“Is he there?”

“He’s asleep. Scratchy is here too. He’s also asleep. Big day for both of them.”

Rio laughed softly and bit down on her lip.

“It’s so good to hear your voice,” Agatha whispered, making Rio’s heart constrict in her chest. “I’ve missed you. I miss you.”

“I want to be there,” she admitted in a soft voice, “to hold you both.”

“He’s tired,” Agatha responded, “when Alice left he wanted to put on one of your sweaters and go to sleep. He wants you here as much as I do.”

“God, why is this so fucking hard? Why is it so-?!”

“Honey,” Agatha cooed, her voice a whisper so as not to wake Nicky but Rio closed her eyes all the same to imagine she was tucked up in bed with them. “He told Ralph he didn’t want him. He… he was talking earlier about having two moms. He’s sleeping in your sweater. He misses you. We both want you home and I’m working on it. I’ve got something on Ralph that… it’ll destroy him. I just need to get the timing right.”

“You do?”

“Yes.”

A beat and then, “Did Alice tell you she stepped on your heart?”

Rio sighed and ran a hand through her hair. “I made others. They’re-...”

“I know,” Agatha said gently. “Backups. I found them by the instruction manual. I have them all and I managed to salvage the first one. I’m taking good care of it, just like you asked.”

“I thought she might manage to squash one so I-...”

“Gave me four instead. One for each of us.”

“Each?”

“Scratchy too.”

Rio smiled and began toying with the locket around her neck. “Right.”

“You know what I realised?” Agatha asked gently, after giving Rio time to try to breathe. “When he was on the stand he looked so grown up, like he wasn’t just my little boy anymore. He was brave and said all the right things and so, so polite…”

Rio heard Agatha’s voice go and she sucked in a sharp breath as Agatha sniffed gently and the sound of her shuffling and most likely wiping at her tears.

“I-...” A knock at the door meant her call time and Rio closed her eyes as she shook her head, “Mi vida I have to go. Will you tell him I called at our usual time? Can I call again?”

“You shouldn’t,” Agatha breathed out, “Not when we’re so close.”

Rio nodded silently and whispered, “I love you.” Agatha said it back and then she was gone.

Rio didn’t leave her trailer for another ten minutes. She needed the time to recover, to try to be her best self for a cast and crew who were relying on her. But being herself meant pretending her heart wasn’t curled up on a bed in Los Angeles, crying all alone with a bunny and a little boy.

She slept well for the first time in a while that night. Nicky was okay, he was safe at home and his ordeal in court was over. Agatha had her heart, in fact she had all four of them, and was keeping them safe.

And in her dreams she saw Agatha holding all four, one that was crumpled and broken but that had been lovingly put back together by the very woman who held it. The other two snug by its sides, and the fourth, looking strangely smaller than the others. Though Rio was sure she’d made it the same size. She reached for it in her dream and found she was unable to touch it, as though it was just out of reach.

Somewhere around their feet the bunny was hopping around, wearing a locket in the shape of a heart Rio hadn’t made. She looked back to the one she couldn’t touch and saw it beating rapidly, like the wings of a hummingbird, beating two for every one of the other hearts that had started to beat alongside it.

She went to touch it again and found it to be soft and warm and just before she could work out what that meant her alarm had gone off and she forgot all about her dream.

“Hey!” Rio waved her hand and at least five people waved back, sitting in her little chair on the side of the set. The curse of being famous. She laughed and hoped no one would approach other than the woman she actually wanted to. Thankfully they didn’t and just Alice made her way over.

“‘Sup, Shads?”

“Not that again, please. Tail very much not between my legs right now.” She hugged her friend, relieved to have her back with her on the isolated set in the middle of the forest. “I’ve got an idea. Can you log into my Instagram for me, please?”

She handed Alice her phone and Alice took it but didn’t do as she was asked.

“Why?”

Rio shrugged, “It’s my account.”

“You can barely make a post. Let alone…” Alice trailed off and Rio looked away immediately. “You know you can’t be sending DMs, Rio. Anything can be hacked. That’s evidenced by-…”

“I wasn’t going to,” Rio insisted, leaning her elbows into her knees and dropping her head down for a second. “I just… if I make a story for my close friends and add her I can… I want to show her my flowers. More hearts. More of anything that will make her smile.”

She bit the inside of her cheek as she revealed her latest creation, a pretty pale pink tulip that she’d been working on for the past half hour. “I said I’d make her them. It’s… whatever it’s lame but if I can’t even send her flowers every day I at least want her to see I’m making them for her.”

Alice stared at the tulip for so long Rio thought she might have zoned out.

“I just delivered like a whole bunch of paper flowers, Rio. Plus those hearts. I’ve got your shirt, by the way. Jen says it’s starting to smell.”

Rio blinked and didn’t even protest when Alice took the tulip from her hand.

“Don’t you usually make, like, roses? Is this new?”

“I’m learning new ones. Don’t say it’s lame.”

“It’s cute. It’s not lame. She’s got them-…”

“In a bowl on her desk, I know.”

Alice handed her the flower back and Rio began to fidget with it.

“Just a little while longer and it’ll be over.”

Alice kept saying it but the “while” was still going on. She knew next to nothing about the trial or how Agatha was dealing with everything and she wanted it over. She wanted it over now. She wanted it over yesterday.

“Okay,” Alice said, watching the way Rio’s face had fallen. “Close friends. Put me and Jen in there and a couple others you trust and don’t post anything even remotely sexy or sexy adjacent. I don’t want to see your ass.”

Rio had perked up and rolled her eyes as she waited for Alice to log in on her phone. She snatched it back the moment Alice handed it over and then stared at the Instagram app.

Alice had snatched it back after only five seconds and clicked through to set up Rio’s close friends list for her. “Here. Me, Jen, Agatha, Carol, Jessica.”

She handed the phone back and Rio stared at it for a second before she passed it back to Alice.

“Add Val. I want Nicky to see the pictures too so he’ll know I’m thinking of him as well.”

Alice eyed Rio for a moment but did as she was told. When Rio had her phone back in her hand she immediately took a picture of the finished tulip and as Alice hovered nearby, she spent at least five minutes choosing what to say and what emojis to go with it. In the end she deleted everything and simply wrote: “for you”. She posted it and then she waited.

By the time she’d counted to thirty three in her head, Agatha had seen it. It was enough. It was enough to know Agatha could witness in almost real time that Rio was keeping up with her promise.

Particularly when she hadn’t been able to be there for Nicky’s big day in court. One a day, she told herself. That was all she needed. Just the chance one time a day to show Agatha that she was thinking of her, that she missed her, that she was still making her flowers whenever she could.

“Such a romantic,” Alice muttered before jumping up beside her and going into detail about everything she’d already told Rio over the phone. She yawned when she was done, tired from the flight back, but Rio pressed her to repeat everything again, desperate to paint an entire picture so she knew exactly how things had gone.

That night, when she spoke to Nicky via Val’s phone on FaceTime, Nicky said nothing about the trial but as they said their goodbyes after Rio taught him how to make tulips and Nicky had taught Rio how to conjugate the verb “hacer”, Nicky had said: “I love you, melliza. I’m proud of you.”

Rio started, and looked at Nicky’s face to see a shyness that hadn’t been there before.

She took a breath and, knowing what Alice had told her about his reaction to being told Rio was proud of him, she said: “I love you too, mellizo. I’m so proud of you.”

The worst was over, she thought as Nicky grinned and they hung up with a virtual handshake of Rio’s hand held up and Nicky fist-bumping her through the phone. Nicky had said his piece to the judge and Agatha had a plan.

It would work out. Things would be fine. Rio’s wrist was healing and her hair was growing and they would be back together in no time at all.

So life moved on, though slowly with Rio’s insane schedule and the way her heart hurt every time she had to hang up from Nicky of an evening. She continued to make her flowers, posting them every day to her ‘close friends’. Sometimes Agatha responded, but always she saw them within a minute of Rio posting. And it helped. It helped to have some sort of contact.

It meant Rio could live a normal life, with just a little bit of longing on the side.

Her mom called her every day and though Rio always asked how Agatha was - knowing her mom spoke to her every day too - her mom was good about not giving too much detail. She knew her daughter better than almost anyone and knew Rio could get lost in the details if she had too many.

As the shoot moved on, Rio’s schedule freed up enough that Alice started to bother her with other details, details about future shoots and things Rio needed to do, people Rio needed to speak to.

Until one day she announced that Rio was to have a makeover for the part she was to play on the West End. A makeover Rio wasn’t mad at but one she wanted to run past Agatha first.

“Mi Vida,” Rio called out into the empty space behind Nicky, the evening after Alice had told her the news. She cast the nickname out like a lure in the hopes she’d snare an actress.

Nicky grinned and Rio watched his eyes dart to the side of her little screen. She only had to wait five seconds before Agatha appeared there and looked annoyed she’d been caught. Rio could always tell when Agatha was nearby for these calls because Nicky always looked at her when something funny was said, which meant she wasn’t only there, but she was enjoying herself too.

“How do you feel about blondes?”

Agatha’s eyes narrowed and Rio raised her brows expectantly.

“I take it that silence is that you love blondes and think that-…”

“Rio,” Agatha said slowly, making Rio’s grin widen and her heart rate pick up. “What are you asking?”

Rio let the question linger and wriggled her brows to make Nicky laugh. “Well,” she said eventually, her tongue briefly poking into her cheek and Nicky copying the motion with his own, “I have to go blonde for my big West End debut. So by Christmas I’ll be a blonde patito.”

If she weren’t very much mistaken, Agatha’s gaze had darkened a little and Rio’s smile was back to being at full wattage.

“You will look so silly blonde,” Nicky commented with another laugh, his energy levels up to unprecedented heights because the three of them were back together after so long of being apart.

“Silly?!” Rio accused, “I think I’ll look very handsome, actually. Double handsome, even. A beautiful blonde! And if you’re not careful, I’ll dye your hair blonde too so we can continue to be twins.”

“Noooooo!”

Rio laughed and even Agatha broke a smile.

“I guess blonde wouldn’t be so bad…”

“Oh?” Rio asked, her energy levels immediately spiking alongside Nicky’s, “You wouldn’t mind it? Wouldn’t be disgusted or…?”

Agatha shrugged, looking more amused than before, “I suppose I could stand it for a couple months.”

“Just a couple?”

“Mmhm.”

Rio narrowed her eyes and adjusted in her seat to curl her feet beneath her.

“Well I’ll be blonde for a few months so you’ll have to get used to it.”

“We will and we’ll come and see you in your play too. And we’ll get you roses for your bows and then we can-…”

Agatha had laughed, a loud, throaty chuckle that stopped Nicky in his tracks. He turned to grin up at her and accepted the kiss to his temple gratefully before turning back to Rio with possibly even more excitement on his face. “Then we can have those awesome milkshakes from that place we went before.”

Rio, grinning so hard her cheeks hurt, raised her brows, “When we sat at the bar? And you agreed we looked a little the same?”

“Yeah! That place. Only it’ll be just us. And maybe Auntie Jen. And Alice too, if she wants. I think she’d like to see you too.”

Rio laughed, “I think she would.”

“And maybe,” Agatha added, raising her brows at Nicky as he turned to look up at her, “We can calm down a little because we have to get ready for bed soon.”

Nicky’s smile faded and Rio did a very big, very fake yawn. She supposed this was only fair, they’d somehow been talking for over an hour and Rio had almost cracked the conjugation of “jugar”.

“You’re so right, mi vida. I’m very tired and it is getting late.”

“It isn’t that late! I had two more hours before bed or maybe a little less. So can we stay on for a little longer? Mama doesn’t get to speak to you as much as I do and it’s nice that we’re all here. And Val too,” he added, shooting a quick smile above the phone to where Rio knew Val must be close.

“Five more minutes,” Agatha said softly, and she shot Rio a brief smile before she settled down so that she was off to the side but her profile was in view. God she missed that face.

“Okay, okay,” Rio agreed, trying her best to calm herself down too so Nicky would follow suit.

“In the meantime, will we discuss what we’re going to do when I’m back in a few days?”

As Nicky reeled off the plans he’d already made for them which mostly included basketball, movies, and more basketball, Rio’s attention drifted to Agatha and she watched her as she watched her son.

She looked tired, more tired than usual, and it left Rio wandering, even as they hung up with smiles and “I love yous” and a blown kiss and a wink from Agatha, if she was sleeping at all.

Rio didn’t see Agatha on FaceTime again for a couple days. But that was okay. She would be in LA again soon for forty eight whole hours. That was two days with her. Two days to see her face, or at least, see Nicky’s.

Alice hadn’t been able to get a straight answer out of Jen about whether or not Agatha would be joining them in their plans. So for now, Rio knew she’d be hosting Nicky for a sleepover where they’d watch movies and eat snacks and play basketball.

And that was enough to get her through.

It was as she was recovering from a particularly gruelling nightshoot that turned into a long, overrun daytime shoot that she was woken by the unfamiliar sound of a telephone ringing. An actual telephone, not her cell.

She reached across and grabbed the phone from its holder and cleared her throat quickly.

“Hello?”

“Dr. Statler?” Rio blinked and rubbed at her eyes. How long had she been out for? She felt like death.

“Mm?”

“There’s a Natalie here to see you, she’s waiting for you in the bar.”

Rio frowned, turning her head to check the time again. Seven at night. And she didn’t know any Natalies. Not that she could remember anyway.

“I’m sorry, I don’t-…” but as she said it she came back to herself and remembered a husky-voiced redhead saying that name to her on a basketball court in LA. She sat bolt-upright.

“Does… is she a redhead?”

The voice on the other end paused and then said in a lower tone, “Blonde. I’ve been told to tell you she will wait as long as it takes… Doctor.”

Rio groaned, slapping her hand to her forehead.

“Fine. Fine. I. Fine. Thank you.”

She slammed the phone down and stared at it, looking at the way her hand curled around it. The scar on her wrist was fading but remained obvious, remained a reminder of the people she loved, the people she’d die for.

It took less than a second to make up her mind.

She flew across the room, shoved on a pair of sweatpants and a sweater over her tank top, she ran a hand through her hair and wet her fingers to draw beneath her eyes so she could clean up the smudged mascara there.

She looked the least like a movie star she’d looked in days.

But she wasn’t going on a date or to meet a friend. She was walking down the corridor now to meet the enemy, past Thor’s closed bedroom door. And as she checked herself out again in the revelatory mirror, she confirmed she didn’t care at all what she looked like.

The only thing that mattered was warning this woman off, getting information out of her, potentially killing her in a hotel bar.

“Dr Sattler,” the receptionist greeted as Rio stalked past the desk. “Your guest is-…”

She was too quick for him, too determined to find this woman and pulverise her.

Her fists clenched at her sides, she rounded the corner and marched into the low-lit bar. Her eyes scanned the space and she saw people turn to her but ignored everyone that wasn’t a blonde with green eyes.

There, standing up from a booth in the back, was Natalie.

Rio grit her teeth as she marched towards her and it was only when she was within two feet of her that she realised that this woman could be armed because she was definitely dangerous.

“Dr Ellie Sattler?” The woman asked as Rio stood a foot away, seething.

“Very cute. Did Nicky come up with that?”

“Keep his name out of your mouth. What the fuck do you want?”

The woman smirked and slipped back into the booth, indicating with her hand that Rio should do the same. But Rio remained firm and didn’t move a muscle.

Natalie indicated again and then sighed and sat back in her seat.

“I bought you a red wine, I know it’s your drink of choice. That or a martini, but I thought it would be best if we kept our heads tonight, don’t you think?”

Rio’s jaw clicked. The woman before her looked totally at ease, wearing a black, low-cut tank top with spaghetti straps, minimal jewellery, and red lipstick.

“I’m unarmed, if that’s what you’re worried about? Though I hear you’ve put your glock in many a woman’s holster before. And I’m not opposed to it.”

That made Rio sit. She sat down so suddenly and violently that the bench made a noise of protest as she leant forward on the table.

“What the fuck do you want? Why are you following me? Why are you making Agatha’s life hell?”

The woman smiled and casually moved the glass of red wine out of the way of Rio’s tense body.

“I want to talk to you, Rio Vidal. I thought it was about time.”

Rio sneered, actually baring her teeth at the woman before her, furious she wasn’t getting any reaction at all.

The woman smiled and tapped her fingers on the table.

“I’ve been following you because it’s my job. Because it’s what I’ve been hired to do.”

“Evanora,” Rio hissed, and Natalie said nothing but took a sip of her own glass of red wine.

“Quite the injury she gave you. I followed you back to the house that day, saw you leaving with Nicky-…”

“Don’t say his name.”

“It’s going to be pretty tricky to have this conversation without using it.”

Rio said nothing and Natalie nodded, her lips twitching a little, “Okay. El patito then.”

Even Rio slamming her hand on the table didn’t make this woman flinch. But Rio felt hot, was sweating, in fact. She wanted to strangle the woman opposite her and shake her to make her talk, to make her admit more, to give her information she so desperately needed to help Agatha.

“You tried to trick him. You had a Celtics pin and you tried-…”

“To see what your reaction would be to a stranger approaching him, yes.”

Rio scoffed and sat back in her seat, her fingers flexing before curling into fists again.

“Why?”

“Isn’t it obvious? I needed to know what I was dealing with.”

Rio said nothing again and Natalie smiled before continuing. “I was hired to dig up dirt on Agatha. And it turned out the dirtiest thing was actually the cleanest, or at least, cleaner than I was expecting.”

“What do you mean?”

“I looked into your past, looked into all the relationships you’ve had, your family, friends, work, girls…”

Rio’s jaw was so tight she felt she might break it.

“Other than a few stories of making out in clubs or… sex on the beach… nothing. People like you, you tend to charm rather than offend.”

Rio glared at this woman. Was she trying to compliment her? Was she trying to get her on side?

“But your biggest crime, Agatha’s biggest crime wasn’t who you were but actually-…”

“I’m a woman,” Rio concluded before Natalie could.

“Yes. And so I followed you, trying to track your relationship with her, and then with the kid. You were good, at least most of the time, at hiding your tracks. Not so good at the Oscars after party, mind… that one wasn’t so subtle. Otherwise you were okay. But it’s hard to hide a kid. So I watched for a while, and then I approached and it was clear he loved you, that he felt safe with you. I guess I should have known that from seeing you at the games with him.”

“You tracked us at the basketball? In Boston?”

“Yes. Your friend has feelings for you, by the way. I tracked her phone too. She was very upset after your birthday party.”

Rio looked away, feeling a flash of guilt about Wanda. But she had more pressing matters.

“So what?” She asked when she was ready to, “Why are you telling me all this?”

“To explain. To tell you that I sent Agatha those pictures, I let her know I was watching your phone because, despite my job… I have a conscience.”

Rio scoffed and snapped her head back round.

“I think kids should be raised by people who love them, not by people who want them as a power play, to then send them to Eton when they-…”

“Eton? Like… in London?”

“Berkshire, yes.”

Rio put her head in her hands and they were both silent for a while.

“I don’t believe you. This is some trick, some ploy to get more information out of me.”

“It’s not,” the woman said calmly. “I’m being paid by the other side but I don’t agree with what they’re doing. And I haven’t shared with them what I’ve shared with you.”

“You haven’t?”

“No.”

“The pictures, the-…” Rio’s blood went cold. The pictures Agatha had sent her. She reared up and pointed in Natalie’s face. She didn’t react at all to it and Rio wanted to strangle her. “You sexually assaulted her. You had pictures that were private between us and-…”

“An occupational hazard,” the woman said softly, “believe me I didn’t share them with her mother, nor did I look at them for longer than it took to print out and send to Agatha.”

“That’s not the fucking point,” Rio growled, feeling her fury surge again.

“You should take a breath,” the woman opposite her said, not at all helping with the fury.

“I’m trying to help. You can trust me.”

“Trust you?” Rio was practically spitting now, digging her nails so tight into her palms they’d be drawing blood soon. “You assault my girlfriend, you stalk my son, you-...”

“And here,” Natalie said in that frustratingly low voice, “here is the problem. You’re so in love you can’t help but say it out loud even when you don’t mean to. Even when you shouldn’t. Nicky’s the same. He looks like you and he-...”

“Don’t speak about him.”

The woman before her sighed quietly and shook her head. Rio thought about strangling her again.

“All those months ago, in Boston, you called him your kid. It was the first clue, the first hint it was more than sex.”

Rio started. “How did you know?”

“You’d be amazed to find what people put online. You’re not a hard person to know everything about, Rio Elena Vidal.”

Rio bristled and felt the hair on the back of her neck stand up.

“I’ve met Ralph,” Natalie said slowly, watching Rio’s reactions closely. “I know what kind of man he is. I’ve met Evanora too, obviously. I know what kind of woman she is. So I needed to meet you, and… the little boy.”

Rio cleared her throat and despite herself, and all the spy movies she’d ever seen, she picked up her glass of wine and took three large gulps, wiping her mouth with the back of her hand when she was done.

“I was curious. A movie star with a track record for short flings with hot women. No kids, no sign of ever wanting a family, I was interested in you.”

Rio looked away and flexed her jaw.

“Imagine my surprise when, that day on the basketball court I saw a mom and her kid instead of a reluctant babysitter and an uninterested child.”

Rio’s head snapped back around and she saw the smile on Natalie’s face. She wanted to kill her. So badly. Could she do it? Could she reach across and-...?

“Imagine my surprise too, when Agatha’s camp released stories to the press about you, getting ahead of Evanora leaking anything. Because I’d given them some stories, small indiscretions on your part, things to keep them sweet. And they would have leaked them, they’d have leaked them and made sure they made a bigger splash. So now I had a playgirl actress looking a lot like a mom and the camp of the woman I was trying to discredit defending her. And I knew you were both in love and that, apologies, Nicky, was where he needed to be.”

“And yet you kept following? You kept stalking.”

“I was doing my due diligence. I followed you to the church service with your mom. I was there the night you exchanged bracelets and the day you got ice cream. I’ve kept a close eye.”

Rio’s jaw flexed. “The trail? The day I got jumped?”

“That wasn’t me.”

“I don’t believe you.”

“It wasn’t Evanora either.”

Rio scoffed. Jen and Agatha had said as much but why would she trust this woman?

“Ralph hired some goons to do his dirty work. My boss was not happy about it. He’s a liability and she knows it. That’s why she’s desperate to expose Agatha as a lying, untrustworthy lesbian so she can get her grandson.”

Rio couldn’t look at her anymore, she just stared at the half-full wine glass and said nothing.

“Look,” the woman said, “I have something for you that’ll get you to trust me. It’ll also help. But only if you listen, only if you do as I say.”

Rio wondered how much damage a glass of wine could do. They seemed pretty lethal in the movies, maybe they would be in real life too.

The woman was leaning in, glancing to the side to check no one was near.

“There’s going to be a break in at Agatha’s house tomorrow night. They will be looking for any and all tech, any evidence of the two of you, because it’s precisely what I’ve not given them.”

Rio’s blood ran cold and she felt her heart stop in her chest.

“They will be armed, they will be doing their best to frighten Agatha and Nicky, but they won’t harm them. You should get them out, get them away before-…”

“Bullshit.”

The blonde leant back, and Rio felt like she might vomit.

“You’re smarter than that, Rio. It’s going to happen. Evanora’s pissed I haven’t given her much, pissed that her grandson was brave and told the truth in court. They didn’t think he would. They thought he’d just go along with anything, plus Evanora assigned the judge but…” She sighed, “You’ll believe everything I’ve told you tonight after it happens. Get them to leave the house tomorrow.”

Rio shook her head and slammed her fist on the table. The woman, again, didn’t flinch.

“You’re talking-…”

“Another thing,” the woman continued, ignoring Rio’s growing fury. “If they haven’t done it already, get Agatha and her team to get a forensic accountant. In Ralph’s off-shore accounts you’ll find girls, and more powder than you can imagine.”

Rio opened her mouth but couldn’t make herself speak. Her mind was reeling with the change in direction, the information being thrown her way so casually after weeks of being in the dark.

“He uses Agatha’s name to close deals, he sells them access to her and gets them into industry parties. He’s a crook and a conman and not fit to be a parent.”

Rio tried again but the woman interrupted.

“I gave the judge a picture, slipped it to him without Evanora’s knowledge. Several pictures actually. Ones of you carrying him through crowds. Pictures of him and you in matching caps with Agatha by your side. It’s why he made Ralph pick him up in court. It’s why-…”

“He did what?!”

For the first time, the woman showed some sort of emotion. She looked completely taken aback.

“You didn’t know?”

“He held him?”

The woman’s brow twitched, “Seems I’ve made the right choice.”

Rio practically growled, and turned from her only to rip her arm away suddenly when the woman reached for her arm.

“Families protect one another. She was only protecting you by not telling you.”

“Don’t tell me about what Agatha was doing. You don’t know her.”

“Maybe not. But I know enough. I know enough to say that that boy will not recover if he’s traumatised again in his own home. I know what Ralph did, I know about him pushing him on the basketball court, about Agatha shouting at you then forcing Ralph to leave. He won’t recover from a break-in. You need to get them out.”

Rio stood so suddenly that the woman reacted again but Rio didn’t see it this time because she had already turned away.

“Rio,” the woman said, “I’m trying to help.”

“Stay away from us,” Rio hissed, pivoting around to poke her finger in the woman’s face where she’d stood to stop her. “If I see you again-…”

“You’ll what, Rio Vidal?”

“Stay away,” Rio insisted, furious that the woman’s lips twitched.

“My name is Natasha. I have a lot of red in my ledger. I’ve done a lot of bad things, but I’m trying to do the right thing here. And I’m telling you the truth.”

Rio didn’t hang around after that. She turned and left, stalking out of the bar and back up to her room and almost broke the elevator button by jamming it so hard and so fast.

She slammed her fist into Alice’s door because it was closest to her when she hit her floor and walking the extra five feet to her own door was too far.

Alice, confused and concerned, ripped the door open within seconds.

“What the fuck?!”

Rio grabbed the phone from her friend’s hand and before she could think she had it to her ear.

Alice had already been on the phone to Jen.

“Jen. Jen. Are you with her?! Are you with Agatha?!”

“Rio? What’s-…” a noise, and then, give me that, “Rio? Rio? What’s wrong? Are you hurt? Are you-…?”

“Mi vida,” Rio breathed, her hand finding her chest because it couldn’t find Agatha. “I need to tell you something and I need you to listen.”

“What’s wrong? What happened?”

“I…” Rio paled, how could she say this without Agatha immediately not listening and focusing on the fact that she’d met with Natalie, no, Natasha, alone?

She swallowed as Agatha began to audibly panic more on the other end of the line and she said her name over and over accompanied by questions. But Rio needed a moment. She needed to think. She needed to get her love and her son out of their house.

“I need you to listen. And if you don’t listen to me I’m going to hang up and call Val and make her make you listen. Okay?”

The threat was so clear, so unexpected, that it shut Agatha up.

There was some noise, some movement, and then, Agatha’s voice, clear and steady and sharp.

“What happened?”

Rio felt the guilt burn her insides. She’d promised to be safe, she’d promised Agatha she wouldn’t be reckless, and yet she’d done the unthinkable.

She steadied herself by leaning back against the desk in Alice’s hotel room and exhaled slowly before she said in a voice far less sure than before: “I met with the woman who has been following us.”

It was instantaneous, as Rio knew it would be. Agatha’s reaction was cataclysmic. She was Krakatoa on steroids; a deadly volcanic eruption of fear and betrayal and pain.

“YOU DID WHAT?!”

Rio grimaced and closed her eyes and knew she would have to let Agatha scream for a little while but she couldn’t stand to hear it. She brought her phone down from her ear and instead held it by her side, looking across the room at Alice who sat on her hands and looked sheepish.

“Call Val,” Rio instructed quietly, Agatha’s voice sounding from the phone by her hip, “get her to go over, get her to make sure she does as I say.”

She waited until Alice had nodded and disappeared to her room to find Rio’s phone. She returned and Rio still didn’t have the courage to lift Agatha’s screaming voice to her ear. Alice was back by the time she was able to. Agatha was screaming but it was mostly incomprehensible. She wondered if Nicky could hear.

“Mi vida,” Rio tried softly, “por favor, mi amor. Please.”

Agatha was breathing raggedly and Rio knew she’d be pacing. She knew she’d have her hand in her hair and her eyes would be wild.

“Please listen,” she said again, closing her eyes to picture the scene, to imagine herself there with her. “It’s important you listen to me and-…”

“Unlike you listening to me?” Agatha spat back, making Rio’s heart skip a beat at the venom in her tone.

“It’s not like that,” Rio said softly, trying to stop her hands from shaking. Agatha had to listen. She had to make her listen.

“Well it sure as shit sounds like that. Like you went and met the woman who has been stalking us, who is working for my mother, who I have been trying to keep us all safe from! Or is that not what this is?!”

Rio sighed and shook her head.

“She told me-…”

“Oh when you were cosying up to her? Is she pretty, Rio? Is that what this is? A bit of danger? A bit of-…”

“That isn’t fair.”

“Oh? Oh! Pardon me for-…”

Rio hung up. And only after she’d done it did she realise what a mistake that was. She stared at the phone and willed it to light up again and show her Jen’s name. She willed Agatha to call her back.

“Did you just do what I think you did?”

Rio nodded once, still willing the phone to ring.

“Holy shit, Rio. You don’t just hang up on Agatha Harkness.”

“Yes, thanks for that.”

She gave up the willing and looked up to Alice. “Call Jen. There’s going to be a break-in and I need to get them out.”

Alice made a strange choking noise and then stared over at Rio as she waited for an answer, having dialled Jen immediately.

An answer didn’t come. Rio shifted where she stood and nodded once. “Try again.”

Alice pressed to call once more and they both waited. After the seventh ring Jen answered and Alice was quick to say: “She knows she shouldn’t have done it just holy shit Jen you need to make her listen to this it’s-.”

Rio stared at her friend’s evolving face as Jen responded and felt her knees get weak when Alice turned away.

“Jen, you gotta get her.”

Rio cursed under her breath and raised her face to the ceiling. She couldn’t explain why she’d hung up. She was just so, so…

She growled as she marched over to Alice and ripped the phone away from her.

“Put her on the goddamn phone, J-… mi vida.”

“What is it?” Agatha snapped, making Rio flinch again and stare at her feet. “You have ten seconds.”

Rio exhaled as she ran a hand through her hair and then pressed her palm to her forehead.

“She told me there was going to be a break-in tomorrow at your place. Evanora’s pissed about Nicky with Ralph in court so she’s hired-…”

The line went dead and Rio went silent.

In a second she was dialling Jen again but it rang and rang and no answer. So she rang Val instead.

“Hiya.”

“Hey! Where are you?”

“On my way to Agatha’s as previously instructed. I hear you’ve been an idiot.”

“No, I’ve found out that there’s going to be a break-in tomorrow night. They’ll be armed, Val. They’ll have guns. She said Evanora's pissed that-…”

“Woah, hey, woah woah woah, Alice didn’t mention this. What the bloody hell did you just say?”

Rio sighed, beyond frustrated that no one was listening to her.

“Natasha, or whoever the fuck she is told me that Evanora is going to stage a break-in tomorrow night at Agatha’s. She wants to see if she can find any evidence of… I don’t even know. Us! Maybe. Or things that she can use in court and she doesn’t even fucking care that she’ll be scaring her daughter and-…”

“Rio, you can’t trust what she’s said.”

“Oh and you’re confident in that? One hundred percent certain that it won’t happen?”

She heard Val curse and heard the beep of her horn. “Fucking drive on the left like civilised people. I hate it here. Right, fine. I’ll get her to move out for the night. We’ll look into it. If my bastard brother left you alone-…”

“He didn’t. He thought I was napping. He was in his room. I was supposed to be asleep the rest of the night.”

“God, Rio. The boss is going to kill you.”

“I hung up on her and…”

Val inhaled noisily, “Sheesh. Got a death wish?”

“She wasn’t listening. I was trying to make her listen.”

“By hanging up?”

“MY FAMILY IS IN DANGER! WHY DOES NO ONE TAKE ME SERIOUSLY?!”

“Babe,” Alice said sharply, raising up to snatch the phone from Rio. And Rio let her. She let her and she walked away and found herself in the corner of the room where she squatted down and put her head in her hands.

She couldn’t see anything so no one could see her. The room was empty. Alice wasn’t talking to Val. Natasha hadn’t said anything. She’d not even met her. None of this was happening. Agatha wasn’t mad. Agatha was safe. Agatha was safe. Agatha was safe.

Nicky was safe. Nicky was safe. Nicky was safe.

“Rio?”

Rio jumped so hard her elbow hit the wall and she yelled out as Alice approached and touched her knee.

“Val will get her to leave. They’ll clear out the house of anything valuable or any tech that can be hacked. They’ll-…”

“She agreed?”

Alice said nothing for a second and then cleared her throat. “Rio, she’s not there yet. Do you want to try and call her again?”

“No. I just… can you keep in contact with Jen? Make sure she agrees? Tell her, tell her she can have my house. Tell her I want her to have my house. And ask her… ask her if… she can…”

Rio shook her head as the start of hyperventilation happened. Alice settled on the floor beside her.

“They’ll be safe. Breathe. Val won’t leave tonight. Even if-…”

“Alice, I want to go home. I should fly out to-…” she was halfway to standing up when Alice grabbed her and pulled her back and like a ragdoll she collapsed into the floor and smacked against the wall. But she didn’t react. She just sat, staring, silent, determined.

“She’ll leave. She will protect Nicky. Even if there’s a one percent chance what Natasha said is right, she’ll get out of there. I know she will. If she wants to be mad at me, fine. I want her to listen to me. Now. Rather than later. I want her out that house and… I’ll-…”

She groaned and her head was soon back in her hands again. If she hadn’t hung up would Agatha have eventually listened? Surely. Surely she would have. But it was too late now.

“If I hadn’t hung up she wouldn’t know I was serious,” she said eventually, her hands falling so she could instead stare at the floor.

Alice said nothing so Rio just sat there with her in silence. Eventually she was aware of Alice texting and then leaving the room to answer the phone and saying a soft, “babe, hey,” as she did.

Rio just sat and waited. She knew Agatha would put Nicky’s safety above everything else and she knew she would forgive her eventually but it still felt terrible.

She wasn’t alone for long.

“Agatha’s banned them from contacting us,” Alice said carefully, and Rio knew she was worried about her reaction. “Jen just stole away for a minute to call but… Val’s trying to convince her to leave. She’s on your side.”

“She’ll leave,” Rio said firmly, still sat in the corner. “She’s stubborn but she’s not stupid.”

“You’re going to sleep here tonight,” Alice said, apropos of nothing. Rio looked up and frowned but said nothing about it. Jen might call Alice which meant Rio would get more information on Agatha, which meant it was fine if she stayed.

“You need to be up at five,” Alice reminded but Rio didn’t move and just stared at the floor.

“She’ll leave,” Rio said, now vocalising the mantra in her mind. “She’ll leave.”

“Babe,” Alice said as softly as she could, “get ready for bed. I’ll go speak to the blonde god outside.”

Alone again, Rio stayed on the floor for a while, frightened, annoyed, guilty. But when Alice came back in she scrambled to her feet and made her way to the bathroom to splash her face with water and brush her teeth before she crawled into bed.

She did not sleep well.

In her dreams ocean blue eyes melted into green and long brown hair became short red hair which faded to blonde. Agatha’s voice, soft in her ear, making her skin prickle, dropped an octave and became someone else’s.

She woke several times in a cold sweat and each time Alice touched her arm as Rio checked her phone.

“Nothing, babe,” was Alice’s soft reassurance as Rio settled back down again and willed sleep to take her away.

By morning, when Rio was picked up to be taken from set, neither of them had heard anything.

“Val won’t answer?”

“No,” Alice said for the hundredth time, mid-morning when Rio was done with hair and makeup and was squatting on the low step outside her trailer in her cop uniform complete with fake gun on her hip.

She was trailing her fingers through some string she was currently trying to weave into a bracelet but was too tense to make much progress on.

“Nothing from Jen?”

“One text,” Alice said cautiously as Rio sat up straight with wide eyes.

“And?!”

“She said,” Alice held up her phone to read it, “Agatha is fine and Nicky is too. She’s moved in to our house but she won’t speak to me. Tell Rio they’re safe. I love you.” She mumbled that last part but Rio didn’t care anyway, that wasn’t for her. The rest was for her.

Agatha was safe. She’d listened. She was just stubborn and pissed at her. And Rio would take that any day.

She stood from her little stoop and threw her arms around her best friend.

“I’m going to make you the best bracelet you’ve ever seen.”

“Oh,” Alice drawled, “lucky me.”

Rio laughed and released her, feeling so relieved she couldn’t stop smiling the rest of the day. Until, around lunchtime when she’d found herself all alone, miraculously, weaving a bracelet for her best friend, she realised something.

Agatha and Nicky were still being terrorised. They were being targeted.

The rest of the day was worse. Much worse.

She’d text Val for the millionth time and asked her to show Nicky a picture of her in her uniform even though he’d seen her in it before. But she wanted him to know she was working, wanted to remind him if she weren’t she’d be there.

She held up her wrist to show her watch that matched his and posed in the uniform.

Five minutes later she got a picture back. It looked sneakily taken and Rio knew it was the best Val could do for her. It was a photo of Nicky, sitting on the ground feeding Scratchy a carrot, his own watch in full view.

She’d written beneath it: “he’s been telling the rabbit all about you so he knows you when you get home”.

It helped. Knowing Nicky was okay helped.

But the rest of the day went slowly and Rio didn’t sleep again that night. By morning she woke with a jerk as Alice shook her shoulder and presented her with her phone.

She blinked up at it, trying to make her eyes focus.

TMZ

Break-in at Agatha Harkness’s Hollywood Hills Home

TMZ has exclusively learned that Agatha Harkness’s home in the Hollywood Hills was broken into last night. It’s not currently known if the thieves took anything of value and this is an active investigation.

It’s been reported that both Agatha and her son were absent from the property when the break-in took place.

Check back for updates as this story develops.

Chapter End Notes

As always, thanks for sticking with these idiots for so long I love them I love you thank you for reading

Chapter 55: The Pond

Chapter Summary

Tres patitos in a pond

Chapter Notes

This was originally a much longer chapter but for the sake of not making you read 40k again in one sitting I’ve split it

See the end of the chapter for more notes

Expensive? Sure. Bad for the environment? Yep. Worth every penny and every ounce of carbon dioxide released into the atmosphere? Definitely.

Alice had booked her on the first flight out of Arkansas ahead of her two-day trip home to LA. And when Rio had asked when she’d be leaving and when she’d be arriving, she realised she’d be eating into her already limited time with Agatha and Nicky. Because apparently it wasn’t a popular route. Who knew.

So she hired a jet. Or, Alice hired a jet. And then Rio had to endure Alice talking about the “dope PJ” for a whole day before they were now sitting on said “dope PJ”.

The money and the carbon footprint were well worth the extra five hours she’d have with her family. And she had to keep reminding herself of that as she stared out the window into the night sky that twinkled with stars because they’d left after Rio’s last shot of the day which had just so happened to be a gruelling night shoot.

“You want more champagne?”

Rio raised her brows and turned to Alice who was wriggling a bottle across the aisle to her.

“I’m okay. I should sleep.”

“No fun,” Alice grumbled, pre-emptively annoyed because she knew this was the last time she’d be on a Private Jet. Rio had said as much after the first “dope PJ” that had left Alice’s mouth.

There had been an absence of anything joyful in Rio’s life for the past two days. Agatha had taken her rule of not speaking to her very seriously, and it had meant that for the first time since moving away, she’d gone a whole day without any contact with her or Nicky.

Agatha hadn’t even looked at her stories on Instagram to see that Rio had made her three little purple flowers. And Nicky had been “busy with school work” when Rio had tried to call when the little bell on her watch had rung.

But Agatha hadn’t stopped speaking to her mom, so Rio had found out as much as possible from Anna, who always seemed to be on Agatha’s side.

“Ella está asustada y enfadada porque te has puesto en peligro. Y yo también.” She is scared and angry that you put yourself in danger. And I am too.

So Anna wasn’t much help either. Even Jen and Val couldn’t do much. Though Jen text Alice at least once a day to let her know she loved her and that Agatha and Nicky were still safe.

It was via Val that she learned her little family of ducklings had moved into the Waldorf Astoria in Beverly Hills for extra security and easier vigilance. Rio didn’t have the heart to remind her that Natasha had snuck into her hotel so maybe the location wasn’t the issue but instead the people protecting them.

Still, she kept her mouth shut for the most part. She was even good at not complaining too much to Alice. Mostly because she was trying to focus on what was good and what was good was that Agatha and Nicky were safe.

It didn’t matter that she would wake in a cold sweat after visions of Agatha and Nicky cowering in a corner, held up at gunpoint, plagued her sleeping mind.

What was great was that Val had shared their location with them, that she’d told her their room number, that she’d told her to bring a bathing suit and enough energy to play all day in a pool.

These, she knew, were messages from Agatha. Basically: come stay with us, come play with Nicky, I’ll get over myself but not just yet.

So she rejected Alice’s offer of more champagne and she curled up in her plush leather seat and watched as the night sky darkened and deepened and then filtered away to morning.

Landing in the private hangar of LAX was a little easier than landing with the commercial flights, mostly because the apparatus was there to keep Rio enclosed, so that the paps didn’t get much of a shot at her until she was on the ground outside the airport itself.

They were novices at this so hadn’t arranged for a car to pick them up round the back but it didn’t matter. A few camera flashes were the very least she’d had to deal with over the past few months.

Besides, she’d push through a million paparazzo if it meant getting to Agatha and Nicky sooner.

Goddamn aviation companies and their goddamn shitty schedules.

It was five in the morning when Rio pulled up in her hired car with Thor in the front and Alice at her side. The tall bodyguard was quick to open the door for them so they could hop out and be ushered into the grand hotel with as little fuss as possible.

Rio by-passed the reception and only briefly smiled at Jen who was more interested in Alice anyway, and heaved her bag higher up her shoulder as she marched with Thor to the elevators. Once inside, she checked herself in the mirror and tried to flatten down a random bit of hair she’d obviously been leaning on all flight because it was sticking up in the centre of her head.

She gave up just in time for the doors to ping open and for them to have arrived on Agatha’s floor. Along the hallway she could already spot a waiting Val and a man she didn’t recognise but knew to be more security given how huge he was.

“Hey,” she whispered, giving Val a one-armed hug.

“Good flight?”

“Fine. Do you know if-?”

“She’s awake? Yeah. She’s not said as much but she’s nervous.”

Rio raised her brows. She hadn’t expected that at all.

“Nervous?”

“Look, I don’t know her as well as you do but… yeah. Looks like she’s about to have a run in with a bloody firing squad or something.”

Rio nodded once, wishing Val had used a different metaphor considering how close Agatha had just come to being held up at actual gunpoint but she didn’t say anything.

Val didn’t notice either, maybe just more used to violence and threat than Rio was, and instead turned to open the door for her. Rio stepped inside and the door was pulled closed behind her.

It took two seconds for Agatha to appear and when she did, Rio knew exactly what Val meant. Agatha was pale and tired-looking. She stood there in a baggy grey tee and jeans, which should have been enough of a red flag because it was five in the morning. Her skin was almost the colour of her t-shirt and Rio couldn’t even see the blues of her eyes because Agatha kept them down-turned.

She was colourless. And Rio was all out of pigment to offer.

But a flash of gold told Rio that Agatha wasn’t totally lost to her. She was wearing her ring in its usual place on her left ring finger. The sight of it made Rio want to cry.

“Hey,” she said quietly, aware that Nicky would be asleep somewhere in the suite.

“You should go lay down beside him,” Agatha said equally as quietly, forgoing the greeting. “It took ages to get him to settle, he’s been so excited to see you. I’ll wake you both in a couple hours.”

And then she strode across the room and Rio stood staring after her, unsure what to do or say. But Agatha had disappeared, taking all of her fear with her and Rio was left alone, staring at the place she’d disappeared to and not knowing how to make any of this any better.

It was early still, too early to have an intense discussion or else a fraught fight. So she turned towards where Agatha had come from and after trying a few different doors she found where Nicky was, curled in on himself on his side under a large duvet on a very large bed.

She placed her bag down by the door and clambered up beside him, cautiously kissing his warm cheek before she turned over and lay with her back to him. Her eyes remained on the door for a while, hoping Agatha might give in and come to her. She counted to a hundred but she never came.

Sleep took her away before Agatha could appear and so when she woke switch the mattress cool before her, she knew Agtha hadn’t joined her. But as Rio blinked her eyes open, she knew she was here now, sitting at the bottom of the bed on Nicky’s side.

And someone else was leaning over her, most of his bodyweight on her arm as he leant down towards her and grinned a sleepy grin right in her face.

“Wake up, melliza, I’ve missed you.”

Rio blinked slowly, turning around to catch him in a tight, quick, wriggling hug. Nicky laughed at first and then settled and she sighed dramatically before she said: “I’ve missed you too. Did you grow again? You feel bigger.”

“I think maybe I did. You were gone so long.”

Rio hummed, pretending to be unhappy about this as he wriggled away and pulled back.

“Well maybe stop that next time. You’ll be taller than me.”

“Or definitely taller than mama.”

This made her crack a smile and she looked down to Agatha who had her back to them and was sitting ramrod straight on the bed.

Her face must have fallen because Nicky was frowning beside her suddenly and turned on his knees to look at his mom too.

“Mama? What is it?”

Rio cleared her throat and to save Agatha the need to lie she sat up and stretched her arms high above her head, adding a performative yawn to the equation just to draw some attention back to her.

“I hear we’re having a pool day?”

Nicky’s head whipped back around to her and Rio grinned at the excitement that had replaced his frown.

“We are?”

“I’ve shut down the rooftop,” Agatha said, coming back to life but not looking around to them as Nicky beamed so much he giggled with it. “It’ll be just us.”

And then she was gone, she’d left the room without so much as looking at Rio and Rio was left to frown after her, trying her best to hide her disappointment from Nicky.

“Mama likes to be home,” Nicky said gently from beside her, picking up on what Rio was inadvertently putting down. “I do too, usually. There aren’t any other people at home and it’s only us and sometimes Val and sometimes Auntie Jen. But in hotels we have people watching us a lot and sometimes I think it upsets mama but I’ve been trying to be braver about it and I thought I was brave last night when we arrived but maybe not.”

Rio looped an arm around Nicky’s middle, glad to be rid of her splint now but being cautious all the same. She tugged him into her side and there they both sat, one patito in dinosaur pyjamas and the other in grey tracksuit bottoms and a soft black t-shirt, staring at the place the other patito had left them from.

“I think you’re always brave. But there’s a lot going on at the minute and sometimes grown ups get sad and scared too. So your mama is just a little quiet right now but we’ll cheer her up today, right? Just tres patitos and a big pond all to ourselves.”

Nicky relaxed against her and Rio rubbed his arm gently, “Can you give her big cuddles, maybe? She hasn’t had any hugs from anyone apart from me and I’m growing but I’m not that big yet so I can’t hug as well as you.”

Rio hummed and turned to kiss the top of his head. “Not true. You’re the best hugger and your mom is lucky to have your hugs.”

“And yours too. We can both be the best at it, and mama can as well. Auntie Jen is maybe the worst.”

This made Rio laugh. It made the noise bark out of her without her meaning to and as if to make up for it she began shuffling up the bed and turning to offer her hands to Nicky to help him jump off so they could go through to find Agatha in the large suite.
