She was out on the terrace where there was already a plethora of food waiting, some under cloches with other plates of fruit and pastries already out and ready to be devoured.

“I got you both pancakes. There’s extra syrup and cream and berries. It’s a celebration day today so Nicky you can have whatever you want but remember we’re swimming later so not too much please or you’ll be sick.” She paused and then added, “Same to you, Rio.”

Under any other circumstance, Rio would have looked up to see Agatha smirking across at her, maybe trying to hide it, maybe not. But now, as Rio looked up, Agatha didn’t have the faintest hint of a smirk across her face. In fact, she looked impassive, almost bored. Though Rio knew she was far from it.

She took a seat beside Nicky and helped him lift his cloche up to reveal a stack of steaming pancakes already covered in syrup and butter with chocolate chips cooked into them. Her mouth watered. She’d not eaten since midday the previous day so she realised suddenly how hungry she actually was. Grinning in anticipation, she then opened her own and expected the same but instead discovered a plate full of thick, mealy-looking pancakes with no syrup and no butter.

“Banana and oat,” Agatha commented from the other end of the table, her eyes on the disgusting looking discs on Rio’s plate. “They’re healthy. We agreed you’d look after yourself so I assume you still are. Besides, they have protein in them for your tiny arms.”

Oh fuck, Rio thought as she looked down at the nightmare of a breakfast dish, she’s really pissed.

She cleared her throat quietly and without thinking she touched her arm.

“It’s okay, melliza,” Nicky whispered, his face scrunched up as he looked down at Rio’s plate with his fork at the ready, “You can have some of mine.”

“No,” Agatha said firmly, catching the whisper with supersonic mom hearing. “Rio will eat her own, Nicky. Focus on your own plate.”

Rio watched as Agatha glanced at her only briefly and then turned side on to the table, a small side plate beside her with half a piece of melon and a handful of blueberries. There was no cloche waiting for her.

In a call a few weeks ago, her mom had mentioned something about Agatha’s eating habits, but Rio hadn’t paid much attention at the time. She’d said something about her being tiny, and eating well, but not enough, and Rio had clocked it then, knew it to be true, but not thought about it since with everything else going on.

So now, with the evidence of Agatha’s disordered eating habits in front of her, even with her tail between her legs, she stabbed the top pancake with her fork and reached over to drop it on top of Agatha’s tiny plate of fruit.

“Here,” she said triumphantly, “I want to share my breakfast with you, mi vida. So you have plenty of energy to play in the pool with us later.”

Agatha didn’t flinch. Instead she picked up her coffee mug without even looking at it and stood from the table.

“I have work calls.”

And then she left, leaving Rio pining and Nicky frowning.

“What’s wrong? Did you guys have a fight?”

“No, baby. Here,” she pulled the syrup closer and poured it over Nicky’s already sodden pancakes. “Enjoy your breakfast. Eat small bites and chew well and I’ll be right back. Promise me no choking and don’t go near the edge.”

Nicky grinned and nodded, “No choking, I’ll stay right here. Prometo.”

Rio touched his head as she stood up from the table and marched on through to find Agatha. She was being punished, she knew that much. First the silence and now the digusting breakfast food. But Agatha was wearing her ring, so she was looking for a reaction, rather than shutting her out completely. Rio knew it, and clung to what she knew, because looking over the edge was too frightening.

After trying a couple doors again, just like before when trying to find Nicky, she found her in a small room with a large desk and a view of the far hills.

“Are you really that pissed with me?”

Agatha didn’t look up, intent on her phone as she sat at the desk. Rio gave her a second but she didn’t say anything either.

“This is so unfair. I did what I did because-...”

“She’s beautiful,” Agatha said quietly, staring at her phone still. It made Rio start, made her question whether Agatha was talking to someone else on speakerphone.

“I, what? Who is?” Rio shifted from foot to foot and realised she didn’t particularly like Agatha calling someone else beautiful. Especially when she didn’t know who it was.

Rio squeezed his side and then turned to Agatha who was watching her with a wry, amused smile and so much affection Rio almost forgot her own name.

“And I, Rio Elena Vidal, take you, Agatha Harkness, to be in custody with me too.”

“Mama, you have to say ‘I do’ now,” Nicky whispered, rocking up on his toes. Rio hummed suspiciously at this and turned to Agatha who raised her brows and slipped from Rio’s lap to stand.

“Hey,” Rio protested, grabbing the back of Agatha’s shirt.

“I,” Agatha said, grabbing Nicky’s face to tilt it up towards her, “am el patito of tres patitos and I demand that you, el patito, sip some more water and settle down for a while so your stomach doesn’t hurt again.”

She kissed his nose and Nicky crinkled it and then she kissed Rio’s and she crinkled it the same way.

“I do,” Agatha whispered to her, making Nicky grin and Rio melt.

“I do too,” she said back, hoping Agatha would know she meant it and never ask again if this was what Rio wanted. Because she now had everything, sitting out on the terrace, Nicky drinking his water, Agatha eating her melon, and Rio munching her croissant.

Before long Nicky ran back to the bathroom and Rio, now a good two feet away from Agatha, reached across for her and Agatha reached right back and took her hand.

“He’s determined.”

Rio grinned, “Just like his mama.”

“Do you really think it’s obvious?”

Rio tilted her head, toying with Agatha fingers as she took a sip of orange juice. “What?”

“That I want to kiss you? Or that… we’re together?”

Rio laughed so hard she choked and the sweet juice burned the back of her throat as she recovered.

“I don’t know, babe. Do you sit in Jen’s lap and nuzzle in?”

Agatha blushed and Rio grinned teasingly at her.

“I don’t get much opportunity to-...”

“I know, I know. We barely get time together. So being close is-...”

“I want to take you away,” Agatha said suddenly, seemingly changing the subject without any warning.

Rio blinked and raised her brows, “You do?”

“Yes. As soon as this is over. The three of us. I was thinking I could hire a yacht and we can sail around the med, far from land and anyone trying to get to us.”

“Like pirates?” Rio asked, changing the position of her legs to lean her elbows on them and be closer to Agatha. “Is that why my mom keeps referring to you as treasure? I knew it.”

Agatha huffed as if Rio weren’t taking her seriously but softened when Rio kissed her knuckles.

“I mean it. I want to go away with you. We deserve some time, some luxury. I’m hoping the trial will be done and then you’ll just have a couple more weeks of work and we can go before Nicky needs to be back in school.”

“So, what?” Rio asked, doing the complex date maths in her head. “We could have about a month?”

“I haven’t spoken to Alice about your schedule yet but-...”

“Forget it,” Rio said quickly, waving a hand as if wiping her schedule totally clean. “If I have things on they can be moved. I have a commercial to shoot before Christmas and maybe some time in to do some reshoots but otherwise it’s prep for the play next year.”

Agatha hummed, “And press. We’ve got press before Christmas.”

Rio groaned, “Forgot about that.”

“Oh? You’re groaning about the chance to spend three weeks travelling the world with me?”

Rio laughed and wriggled their hands together. “Hadn’t thought about it that way.”

Agatha was already halfway out of her chair when Nicky arrived again, the soft thunder he brought with him before now heavy claps of his heavy feet on the ground. Clearly he was feeling much better.

Agatha stood up fully and Rio couldn’t help but slide forward and pull her between her legs, the jig was already half up anyway.

As she held her and rested her head against her side, Agatha’s hand slipped into her hair and Nicky looked more delighted than ever. So Rio stuck her tongue out at him and he did it right back.

“Feeling better?” Agatha asked after tapping Rio gently on the ear as an admonishment.

“Yes. Very much. Maybe we can get ready and go to the pool now?”

“Okay, honey, go change into your swim shorts and we’ll get going.”

Nicky left immediately, thundering towards his room.

“Giving up completely on being subtle?”

“Deciding he already knows so… what’s the harm in being a little unsubtle for a while?”

“Well we do have the pool all to ourselves so I guess we could…” Agatha turned in Rio’s arms and Rio’s chin now rested on her abdomen. Peering up at her from an odd angle she grinned stupidly.

“Make out while Nicky goes to the bathroom and poops out his pancakes?”

“The two of you are made for each other.”

Rio hummed happily, enjoying the ability to finally be close, to feel Agatha run her fingers through her hair.

“Toilet humour usually isn’t my thing but…”

Agatha laughed and Rio felt her abdomen expand and contract with it before Agatha was moving again, turning to perch on her thigh. Sitting between her legs like this allowed Rio more access and the ability to slide her hand beneath Agatha’s shirt to rub soothing circles over her stomach.

“I wasn’t planning on giving into you just yet,” Agatha announced, making Rio raise her brows in question as her hand paused its movements, now wrapping around Agatha’s ribs. “So I bought a special bathing suit to drive you insane while I ignored you.”

Rio’s attention was piqued and she sat up a little straighter.

“A special one?”

Agatha shrugged, purposefully looking off into the middle distance. “Small, not too small, obviously, with Nicky here. But small enough. Red. Slutty.”

Rio groaned and closed her eyes to better imagine it. “We haven’t had sex in weeks and you’re going to parade around-...”

“I don’t parade.”

Rio scoffed, her eyes back open now and glaring at Agatha who was smirking, her fingers toying with the soft hair at the nape of Rio’s neck.

“Strut, then.” Agatha rolled her eyes and Rio grinned, holding her closer in her lap. It was as if Agatha had cast some sort of spell over her, removing her grief, diminishing her pain, lessening her fear. She instead just felt warm and comforted, the inevitable conclusion to being close once more to her very own sun.

She continued to tease Agatha about the way she would walk in her bikini, getting the most reaction from the word “prance”. But soon Nicky was back, his hand on his tummy and his smile turned up to a hundred.

“I didn’t change yet but I think I got it all out.”

Rio laughed so hard at this that Agatha slapped her hand over her mouth and her punishment was to be made to go shower alone as Agatha tidied up their mess and made sure Nicky would sit for a while and slowly sip his water so there’d be no more emergency bathroom trips.

Alone again, her natural state lately, Rio felt the after-effects of her time with Agatha being back in her arms again as she let the warm water wash away any remnants of heartache. It was in the shower, as she lathered herself up, that she was able to put the pieces of her girlfriend back into place: frightened, unsure, reactive.

They’d not had enough time together for Rio to be able to soothe a lifetime of Agatha believing she wasn’t good enough. And Rio knew her reactivity was a result of that. She knew that it took her five minutes into every call with her mom to bring up the courage to ask if Anna minded that she was calling, and that she could stop if she wanted her too.

She knew that Agatha was so terrified of losing her son, of losing the good opinion of Anna Vidal, and of losing Rio, that she was numbing herself with nicotine and denying herself the simple pleasure of even a bite of buttery croissant.

So as she stepped out, as she dried herself and found her bathing suit crumpled in her old leather satchel, as she changed into it and pulled on her sweats over it, she thought about the girl Agatha had once been. Because she had the same sweet nature as Nicky, though she barely let it show. And Rio knew, if given the opportunity, she’d use Rio to hide in if ever she could. Just like her son. Just like the little boy who, as Rio stepped out into the living room of the large suite, was sipping his water and swinging his legs as his mom brushed down his hair and kissed his temple.

And, as Rio felt the warmth of her sun within her sights, she realised that she was looking at her future. How normal it felt, to see Agatha and Nicky giggling together quietly on a sun-strewn terrace, waiting for her to return to them.

How strange it felt, to have to give this up again until she could have it for real, finally, after months of pain and fear.

Agatha must have felt her staring because she turned and looked quizzically at Rio and moved away from Nicky to come and greet her by way of a tight squeeze around her waist and a kiss to her cheek. A nuzzle, a soft exhale of a sigh against her skin, and then Agatha disappeared to wash away the morning under the same stream Rio had just emerged from.

Rio sat with Nicky until he felt ready to go and change into his trunks and returned before even Agatha did, wearing slides on his feet and a Celtics t-shirt to match his Celtics shorts.

And soon Agatha was back with them, carrying a large tote over her shoulder that had some symbol on it that Rio recognised but couldn’t place. Until, as Agatha began to tell them about the plans for the day, she clocked it was Medusa.

“Versace?” She asked, interrupting Agatha as she was double-checking her bag for the lotion she’d just been telling them they’d need to apply every two hours.

Agatha looked up, looked shyly at Rio and then turned back to her mission.

But Rio didn’t need it confirmed. She might have taken a second to clock it but she was on enough billboards across every city in the world, and every airport fragrance section, to know the brand she was the ambassador for.

To most it would have been nothing. To any other couple, it wouldn’t have even been noticed. But Rio had so little of Agatha, and Agatha had so little of Rio, that Agatha carrying around a bag with the emblem of the brand Rio represented meant everything.

Lecture over and lotion located, Agatha looked back up, her shyness gone, replaced by something a little haughtier that made Rio smile.

“Medusa was misunderstood.”

Okay, Rio thought, random. “Okay?”

“She was harmed by the Gods and made into a monster.”

The way Agatha said “harmed” suggested to Rio that the Gods had done something to Medusa that was too extreme for delicate, eight-year-old ears, so she raised her brows and tilted her head as she watched Agatha.

“Hence the snakes?”

Agatha nodded once, and Rio smiled a little. “If you had snakes for hair I would be friends with all of them.”

“Friends?” Agatha questioned, her brows twitching up in a way that made Rio laugh.

“Yuck! I hate snakes,” Nicky shivered, a laugh escaping him as Rio grabbed Agatha and pulled her closer to kiss her cheek.

“Friends,” Agatha muttered grumpily, but smiled when she got another cheek kiss.

“Okay, time to go.”

Rio hummed happily, taking nothing with her but her phone in her pocket as Agatha marched ahead to open the door. But Nicky appeared before her before she had a chance to follow and Rio rocked up on her tiptoes to avoid tripping over him.

He was standing so close he was almost on her toes. It was reminiscent of the time in Agatha’s backyard with Ralph there, though Rio couldn’t recognise the danger like Nicky apparently could right now.

But she knew that acknowledging his fear might exacerbate it so instead she simply placed a hand on his shoulder and watched as Agatha opened the door.

No one jumped out at them. No one came into view with a fake grin and a Bulls jersey. But still Nicky remained so close it was hard to walk with him as they followed Agatha out the door.

Rio waited a step to let him get away and watched with a small frown of confusion as he turned around immediately and held out his hand to her. Which she took, without hesitation.

Val was up ahead talking to Agatha, walking along with her just a few feet away, and over Rio’s right shoulder there were two hired security guards, each the size of semi trucks.

But still Nicky was hovering close, his small hand tight around her own and his eyes up on her as if waiting for an instruction, or a reassurance.

So she gave both, and squeezed his hand right back.

“C’mon, mellizo. We’re safe. Let’s go.”

It was all Nicky needed, though he remained close still and Rio could see him continuing to glance at her from the corner of her eye. It was only when they reached the elevator and stepped inside as Val held the door open for them that he moved out of step with her and settled in front of her again.

Rio squeezed his hand as the doors closed and wrapped her other around his front as she leant to whisper in his ear: “You okay?”

“It’s just nice to have you back,” Nicky confirmed in a whisper, making Rio’s whole heart grow three sizes like the Grinch whole stole an actress.

She kissed his cheek and pulled back to smile as she said, “It’s nice to be back with you.”

Nicky’s whole body relaxed then, his shoulders dropped an inch and Rio knew he just wanted the reassurance. He may look like her, but he was his mama’s son.

They arrived, with Nicky before her, his heels on her toes, and Agatha’s arm solidly around her waist, to the rooftop where everything and everyone had been cleared away so they could have some peace and privacy.

“Cameras all off,” Val said as they traipsed out and Rio did a strange bend around with her free arm to grab Agatha’s hand and pull her to her other side so she was flanked by her fellow patitos.

“Staff gone, everyone warned not to come up, told it’s an important business meeting so no access. The bar is stocked with whatever and you can obviously just help yourself. We’re keeping a bloke in the lift for you to make sure no one comes up to this floor and if you want or need anything, I’ll be by your suite. Okay, troops?”

Rio raised her brows at the extent to which Agatha had gone to ensure they had no eyes on them for the time they were to spend in the pool but said nothing about it and merely smiled as Val left them to it after Agatha had thanked her.

“So it’s just us?” Nicky confirmed, looking suspiciously around at the empty sunbeds that lined the pool.

“Just us, mellizo.”

Agatha hummed happily and broke away from them to find a sunbed to her liking, one in the centre of the pool, looking out over the view of the hills in the distance and Los Angeles to the east.

Rio dragged Nicky along beside her and stopped at the end of the next sunbed to Agatha, watching as she lifted her linen shirt over her head to reveal a red bikini top.

Nicky’s hand was gone from her own as he removed his own shirt and Rio was left to simply stare at the expanse of pale, lightly freckled skin before her.

“Hey,” Agatha said, unable to hide the smirk from her face as she needlessly wriggled her hips to push her shorts down. “Clothes off, Vidal.”

Rio nodded mindlessly and managed to get enough brain function to lift her own shirt over her head and reveal the black bikini she’d brought with her for the occasion. She immediately felt a hand on her stomach before the shirt was even clean off her head and she smiled at Agatha once she could see again, enjoying the touch far more than she should when they weren’t alone.

“I need help with sunblock,” Agatha murmured, her hand still on Rio even though it had absolutely no reason to be. And her blue eyes looking anywhere but up at Rio’s face.

Rio grinned as she pushed her sweats down and Agatha’s hand remained in place but her eyes dropped significantly further.

“Sure thing. On your belly, Harkness.”

Agatha’s gaze snapped back up and Rio bit the inside of her cheek at the glare Agatha was giving her.

“Need to do your back,” Rio explained with a casual shrug as Agatha released a soft huff and then turned to the lounger and did as she was told.

“It’s in the bag,” Agatha said, turning her head to the side and gesturing vaguely at the tote she’d brought up with her as Rio perched on the edge of her bed and reached for it.

Nicky had padded out to the edge of the pool and Rio turned to look at him as she grabbed the lotion.

“Hey, you’ll need sunblock too, mellizo.”

“Yes, melliza,” Nicky agreed, looking around at the pool and the sunbeds around it as Agatha’s fingers looped into the string of Rio’s bikini at her hip.

She looked around again and saw Agatha smiling up at her, “So daddy of you.”

“Stop that,” Rio demanded, squeezing some lotion into her open palm. “The red is evil, by the way.”

“You don’t like it?”

Rio rolled her eyes as she started from Agatha’s lower back and spread the lotion upwards.

Agatha humming as she rubbed the lotion in wasn’t helping, neither was the way she kept her head turned so she could watch Rio as she did it. But Rio kept her gaze on her moving hands and tried her best not to think too much about how she’d missed the feel of Agatha and how good she looked laying there like that.

Nicky had come back over by the time Rio was massaging it into Agatha’s shoulders.

“Can we have a race?”

“A race? Sure! Only I’m a really good swimmer so it might be unfair on you, Nicholas River Harkness.”

Nicky laughed and Rio shot him a wink as she rubbed the remainder of the lotion from her lands along the backs of Agatha’s arms to her elbows.

“But I’m a really good swimmer too so I think it’ll be totally fair and I might even beat you.”

Rio scoffed, getting more lotion out.

“I doubt that. I think that-...”

“Hey, honey?” Agatha interrupted as Rio had leant back to start on her thighs. “Could you go behind that bar over there and grab us three waters from the fridge? Should be one just behind the bar. You can have a soda later with lunch.”

Nicky jumped up from his bed, and trotted off along the row of sunbeds towards the bar behind them.

“Is there a reason you got rid of your son?”

Rio asked, already forgoing the thighs to slide her hand up to Agatha’s ass and not so much rubbing the lotion in as simply groping it.

“Yes,” Agatha said, pushing up onto her elbows, “That.”

She indicated with her head what she meant and Rio grinned, shuffling a little to squeeze some more lotion into a neat little swirl on Agatha’s right ass cheek.

“Pilates really is the best sport in the world,” Rio said reverently as she began to massage her ass with two hands now, moving from her seat to hover so she could get a better angle to view it.

“Enjoy it while you can because-...”

Sure enough, Nicky came thundering back, and the sound of his heavy footsteps made Rio move immediately down to the safe zone of Agatha’s calves.

Agatha laughed and Rio punished her for it by swiping a finger along the sole of her foot which made it jerk and she squealed.

“I got them!”

Rio hummed her thanks and then slapped Agatha’s thigh gently to make her turn around. When she did, and she was sat up, Rio took her place beside her again and immediately started to lotion up her chest and smirked when she saw the bruises she’d left there earlier.

“Excuse me?” Agatha asked curiously as Nicky giggled from his own sunbed.

“Yes?” Rio asked nonchalantly, keeping her fingers up near Agatha’s collarbone.

“I think I can do my front.”

“Huh,” Rio said, taking a few more seconds to enjoy the feel of Agatha’s skin before she looked up and pulled her hand away. “And there I was trying to be helpful.”

Agatha narrowed her eyes at her and Rio grinned but turned away to squeeze some lotion into her hand again and work on her own arms.

They kept swapping the bottle about after that. Nicky did his own arms but Agatha did his face, neck, and body. Then she helped with Rio’s back, which she did whilst Nicky was walking up and down the pool, running through diving options for Rio to pick so they could do them together.

Agatha very much took her time in massaging the lotion into Rio and Rio didn’t mind in the slightest.

“You know,” Agatha said quietly, standing behind Rio and working on her shoulders as Nicky debated the benefits of a pencil dive versus a bomb, “on our yacht, we can make sure we do this in our room so we can take our time with it, make sure we don’t miss an inch.”

Rio lost track of whether the pencil or bomb was winning then as Agatha snuck a quick kiss to the back of her shoulder and then gave her a little push out towards the pool.

“Whatever dive you do,” she shouted out, “be safe please! And only in the deep end, remember? And Nicky, remember the rule?”

“Every two hours I have to get out, have some water, and get more sunblock.”

“That’s right.”

Rio grinned as she stepped towards Nicky, now standing at the deep end of the pool.

“You too, Rio,” Agatha called out, as if it hadn’t been abundantly clear that Rio would be doing exactly as she was told for the rest of the day, not to mention her life.

“Yes, ma’am,” Rio saluted and Agatha rolled her eyes but couldn’t hide her smile as she sat back on the bed and fished out a book to read.

It was just them, then. Two excited mellizos and the patito who was pretending to read. They’d decided on the pencil dive first because Nicky thought it would get them used to the water before they did the bomb, which was a showstopper more than a first introduction.

And so they did the pencil dive, and then scrambled out so they could do another. And then, amongst the giggling, came a proper dive, and then another, then another pencil, and then the bomb.

Rio paddled to the surface, gasping and laughing as she did.

Nicky was right beside her, doing some sort of strange doggy paddle that made Rio swallow some pool water as she laughed at it.

“Okay, okay,” she announced, catching her breath as she clung to the side. “Are you ready to race yet?”

Nicky was gasping for air, exhausted as well as giggling still. “One second. I just… go!”

He’d pushed off so suddenly that not only did Rio get a face full of water but she took a second to realise that she’d been duped. And Agatha was laughing at her. Cackling from where she’d been watching, now at the edge of her sunbed, book abandoned.

But spluttering would have to come second because Rio certainly was.

She pushed off when Nicky was easily four feet away from her already and could have caught up with him but what was the fun in that? Instead she got until she was halfway along the pool and proceeded to put her acting skills to good use.

She started to drown.

It took Nicky longer than she would have liked, and Agatha almost no time at all, but eventually her spluttering, crying out about sharks, and general flailing caught Nicky’s attention.

He swam back to her and shouted for his mama who was now standing with her hands on her hips at the edge of the pool as Rio was flailing dramatically in the water, taking big gasps of air as she bobbed up and down.

Nicky got to her as she bobbed up and Rio gave in to let him see that she was okay but he still dragged her (with her help) to the edge of the pool to not only save her life but let her get a full admonishment from Agatha.

“That wasn’t funny.”

Rio laughed and Nicky paddled beside her, not quite able to touch the ground like she was. He was grinning so Rio knew she wasn’t in trouble with him, at least.

“Oh, c’mon,” Rio drawled, turning to look up at Agatha on the pool edge. “It was impressive, though.”

“You’re not allowed to fake drown or fake be attacked by sharks. Even Nicky knows that.”

“It was funny, mama.”

“No, you panicked too, honey. Don’t be on her side for this.”

“Whose side?” Rio asked innocently, batting her lashes up at Agatha as she seethed down at her, hands still on her hips.

“Nicky,” Agatha said, her jaw jutting out dangerously as Rio continued to grin up at her. “Splash your melliza for me.”

Rio gasped as a wave of water came her way. She spat some out and narrowed her eyes up at Agatha.

“That was mean.”

“Sorry, melliza.”

She shot Nicky a wink and turned back to Agatha, allowing herself only a second of enjoyment of her towering above her before she focused on the more important point: winning.

“Why don’t you come in the pool with us? And if you drown I can save you and give you mouth to mouth.”

“Nicky,” Agatha said, and another wave of water came Rio’s way. She got more than a mouthful this time and coughed slightly, wiping it off her face with her hand.

“Sorry again, melliza.”

“I see how it is,” Rio announced, turning properly to a sheepish Nicky who wasn’t very good at hiding his delight. “Two against one.”

“Noooooo!” Nicky protested, “I am on your side!”

“Pardon?” Agatha asked dramatically, hand on chest and leaning back. “Not your mama’s?”

“Well,” Nicky said, as Agatha scowled at Rio’s smug grin. “Maybe both your sides. Definitely both your sides.”

Rio laughed and pushed back, keeping herself afloat in the water using only her arms and the occasional round kick of her legs. Nicky had pushed off too to paddle beside her, his arms and legs working overtime to keep his little body up.

Agatha seemed to know that her son’s allegiance was now, permanently, split. So she just waved a hand and said: “No more fake drowning.”

Rio laughed and then dunked herself under the water and soon Nicky did the same. They messed around for a little while longer, discovering the joy that can only be found in a pool with your favourite person and no one else to bother them.

They raced up and down and even across and diagonally. They splashed and squealed and dived more than necessary. And Rio taught him how to float without paddling so much, even though he always went back to the mad paddling whenever they stopped in the middle of the water to chat.

About halfway through their allotted pre-sunblock-reapplication time, Nicky devised a new plan.

“Can I stand on your shoulders?”

Rio raised her brows, gently swirling the water around herself to remain afloat.

“On my shoulders?”

Images of Ralph in a courtroom, holding a struggling, scared Nicky came to mind immediately.

“Yeah!” Nicky announced, paddling furiously, despite what Rio had taught him.

“And then I can jump off! I’ve seen it in the movies. Kids do it with their dads all the time.”

Rio’s brows moved another inch up her forehead, and she caught a slight movement at the edge of the pool: Agatha.

“Mellizo,” Rio started, unsure where she was going with her sentence but sure she needed to say something.

“I don’t think you’re like my dad,” Nicky was quick to say, mistaking Rio’s surprise for hurt. “I just mean… I mean… I mean I’d like to try it. Like in the movies. And I think you could hold me, like a movie dad does. Like a… like a good one. A good dad, I mean.”

“C’mere,” Rio motioned with her head towards the edge of the pool and made her way over to it, Nicky splashing behind after her. She waited until he was clutching the side and ducked her head down to meet his gaze.

“You know what I used to do with my dad?”

“What?” Nicky asked cautiously, his shy eyes on the water between him and the wall.

“He used to hold me on his shoulders and when I was standing tall I’d shout,” she took a breath and then whisper-screamed, “I’m the king of the world!”

It made Nicky laugh and he shot her a smile. “Yeah?”

“Mmhm. And only after I did that would I dive off. So if you want to try it, then we can. It can be a new tradition. Just my dad, you, and me.”

Nicky nodded frantically and Rio grinned at how keen he was.

She pushed off the wall and swam out to find a spot where she could balance well enough squatting down some with her face turned up just above the water line.

Nicky paddled out after her, and Rio smiled as he got close enough to hold her shoulder.

“I really didn’t mean you were like him.”

“I know, mellizo. I am much more handsome.”

She heard Agatha snort from the side and Nicky’s smiling eyes bounced from his melliza to his mama and back again. “Double handsome.”

Rio agreed and grinned as she held out her hand to Nicky who took it but then didn’t seem to know what to do. They figured it out together, Rio making sure Nicky was safe and knew she had him as she ducked down to let him easily step onto her shoulders.

It wasn’t as tricky as she thought it would be because Nicky seemed confident enough in her hold that he barely wobbled and sure enough, he was on her shoulders with his hands on top of her head in no time at all.

Rio was blowing bubbles in the water from the air she was exhaling from her nose. She had Nicky’s ankles, she knew she did, and she moved slowly until she could get a good stance in the deeper water, ready to drop and push up when Nicky was.

It was fine, she did this all the time.

She’d never dropped a cousin. Not even some of the bigger ones. Not that she’d be mentioning doing this with her cousins to Nicky. This was now just a Miguel, Rio, and Nicky thing. Officially. And her dad had never dropped her. But Nicky was so precious, even more precious than the other kids. And he trusted her so completely.

All this was made so much worse by Agatha watching from the end of her lounger, her blue eyes sparkling like the water Rio had lowered herself in. Would she drown her if she dropped Nicky?

“Okay, melliza! I’m ready!”

Nicky’s voice was so sure, so determined, that Rio felt some of that determination flow through her too.

She started to raise herself and Nicky remained firm, no sign of wobbling yet.

From the corner of her eye she saw Agatha shift where she sat but she kept her gaze forward so she wouldn’t tilt and lose her hold.

But she was doing it. She was raising up and Nicky was doing so well to remain still. She was almost fully standing now and Nicky was lifting up too. When she was at her full height she held one hand in the air for Nicky to take and keep his balance.

It all happened so slow and yet so fast.

“Honey,” Agatha cautioned, and Rio didn’t know whether it was to her or Nicky but she couldn’t look because this was the most dangerous part.

But Nicky had her hand now and he was straightening up.

“I got it! I did it! Melliza I did it!”

Rio cheered and laughed her relief and dared to hold her other hand up so she could hold Nicky’s there too. Their fingers met and Rio grinned as Nicky hollered above her.

“I AM THE KING OF THE WORLD!”

Rio laughed louder and something about the movement of her body as she did made Nicky wobble a little and she shouted, “Jump, Nicky! Jump!”

She sank some just in time for him to push off of her and land with a ginormous splash a few feet in front of her and Rio was quick to swim out and make sure she had him up against the side in as quickly as possible.

They laughed and spluttered together and Rio felt such relief that he was beaming at her with his growing hair a mess about his head and face.

“You nailed it!”

She held up her palm and he smacked his fist into it.

“Can we try again? I think I can jump better next time.”

Rio groaned in amusement but then pushed off the wall to swim back to the middle of the pool.

“Okay, let’s go!”

“Woah,” Agatha’s voice sounded from the edge of the pool. Rio looked up at her and swallowed a mouthful of water because she was so distracted by the red bikini. Nicky arrived on her back and she managed to keep them afloat by placing her tiptoes on the pool floor.

“I think once was enough. You were very high, Nicky.”

“Oh please, mama? I’ll wave at you this time. Or maybe you can try it? Rio can carry you?”

“Yeah, mi vida, come stand on my shoulders.”

Agatha narrowed her eyes at her but then crouched down and sat with her legs in the pool. Rio wasted no time bounding off to get closer with Nicky giggling happily on her back. She arrived and already had her forearms laid out by Agatha’s thighs and lifted both of them up with the buoyancy the water provided. But the intended effect was achieved immediately because Agatha’s hands found her flexed biceps and Rio watched her swallow.

“I’m fine right here.” Rio smiled and lowered herself again. “You won’t come in?”

“Please, mama?”

“No. I don’t want to get my hair wet and you’re both splashing around like maniacs.”

Nicky giggled his protest, “not maniacs! Very good swimmers!”

“Yes, mi vida,” Rio hummed smugly as Agatha squeezed her arms again and Rio flexed them for her. “Very good swimmers.”

Agatha narrowed her eyes but Rio knew she’d already given in. She moved back enough for Agatha to be able to slip down into the water before her and then trapped her there with her hands either side of her head on the wall.

“Welcome, mama. It’ll warm up soon, it’s just a bit cold when you get in.”

Rio grinned at Agatha who was frowning still and she counted in her head: one, two, three. The pout appeared when she got to three and before she could say anything Nicky had stage whispered, “I think she wants to float with you.”

Rio turned her head towards Nicky, “I think you might be right, mellizo. Mind if we swap?”

Nicky shook his head and let go of Rio to doggy paddle to the wall and the moment he was there and safe, Agatha latched on to Rio. It made her bark a laugh, and Nicky giggled along with her as Agatha lightly splashed him with water now Rio was turning them around to place them in the middle of the pool.

“Don’t laugh at your mama!”

“But you’re so silly,” he accused, paddling his best to follow them out while Rio made the most of being able to hold Agatha’s ass under the water.

“Not as silly as the two of you.”

“Very silly patitos,” Rio said with a smirk up at Agatha as she avoided looking down at her. Which gave Rio the perfect opportunity to glance down at where her chin was aligned with Agatha’s cleavage.

“Hey,” Agatha snapped, literally, clicking her fingers and firing droplets everywhere. “Eyes up.”

Rio laughed but didn’t dare glance down again with Nicky so close.

They floated about for a while, Rio doing slow, bouncing pirouettes in the water with Agatha perfectly wrapped around her, occasionally squeezing her thighs around Rio’s middle.

They talked about nothing and everything and Nicky paddled his way around them, too excited to sit still as they discussed basketball, where Jen and Alice were, how Mariana was getting on in her Trench, and whether Nicky’s tummy could handle chicken tenders for lunch.

All the while Agatha was touching Rio in some small way that was just for her. She stroked her thumb along her jaw when they discussed movies for later, she toyed with the hair at the back of her neck when talk turned to snacks, she kissed her cheek four times in quick succession when they spoke of their next trip and a yacht that was to be hired.

“I can’t wait!” Nicky announced, splashing around them still in his effective but crazy looking paddle. “Mama and I always used to have swimming competitions. It’s how I got so good.”

Rio raised her brows and laughed at this as Agatha hummed quietly and her hand slid down to rest at her collarbone.

“In the hotel pool?”

“No!” Nicky shouted, “The sea! We love the sea and seeing all the fishes and sometimes I get a snorkel and I can breathe when I look at them and mama sits on her float and-…”

But Rio had been distracted by something, frowning at the water as Nicky spoke.

“But… you don’t like the sea?” She turned back to Agatha and Agatha seemed to be avoiding eye contact.

“Mama loves the sea!”

Rio glanced at Nicky and raised her brows, “Your mama was once on a jetski with me and she told me she was scared of the sea.”

“Actually,” Agatha started but Nicky had interrupted, “ooooh, can we go on a jetski?”

Rio turned back to Agatha, “You lied to…” she lowered her voice, “feel me up?”

Agatha scoffed and turned her head away and that is how Rio knew it was true. She’d pretended to be scared to feel her up. All those months ago when Rio thought she was going insane for thinking Agatha might be into her and there she was… feeling her up.

“You dirty dog,” Rio accused with a laugh, squeezing Agatha’s ass where she held her.

Agatha scoffed again and turned her head even further away but Rio noticed that she hadn’t released her tight hold on her.

“Mama, that means you need to bark. Like this!” Nicky proceeded to yap in the middle of the pool and Rio laughed at him as she added her own to the mix.

It was that that did it. Agatha dropped her hold on Rio in protest at the bark fest and said: “Okay! Lunchtime maybe?”

Rio was still laughing as she did her best to get them to the steps and had Agatha laid back against them with her legs still very much around her waist.

“You’re not carrying me out?”

“Were you always this demanding or is this new?” Rio wriggled her brows down at Agatha, taking the opportunity while Nicky was paddling along behind them to gaze down at her bikini-clad girlfriend.

Red was her colour. But then again, Agatha looked good in everything.

“Stop staring and start carrying,” Agatha demanded demandingly, making Rio laugh as she did her best to scoop her up and lift her into her arms again.

The angle wasn’t great but what physics made hard Rio made easy with her consistent workout regime and she had Agatha up and in her arms no problem within seconds. She walked them out of the pool and straight to the loungers where she turned them and sat back heavily with Agatha above her.

Agatha kissed her cheek as a thank you but then pivoted off of her and Rio only didn’t protest because Nicky was so close.

He was walking hurriedly over, grinning brightly, “I have an idea for after lunch!”

“What’s that, mellizo?”

Nicky accepted the towel his mom handed him and rubbed his face quickly before he said: “If you throw things in, I can dive down and get them!”

Rio laughed and threw her own towel over her shoulders like a cape, watching Nicky now doing the same with his.

“That sounds like a plan!”

“Yesssss,” Nicky agreed, bouncing a little where he sat.

Rio hummed as she turned to Agatha and offered up her cape to cover them both but Agatha only smiled and settled properly beside her wrapped in her own towel.

Rio pouted dramatically and Nicky giggled.

“Anyway,” Agatha insisted as Rio wrapped her cloak back around herself again and she poked her side. “What does everybody want for lunch?”

“Chicken tenders, please,” Nicky said, having decided earlier in the pool with Rio’s help that chicken tenders were worth the risk of an upset tummy.

“Me too,” Rio chirped, grinning when Agatha rolled her eyes. “And fries. Lots of fries. And a milkshake.”

“Oooo,” Nicky agreed, “me too!”

Rio laughed as she shuffled up the bed and opened her legs and her cloak to tug Agatha back and into her. Agatha allowed it to happen as she sent her order to Jen to put through for them.

When she was done she made herself smaller in Rio’s hold and Rio grinned as she tented her towel around them to hold in one hand so she could slip her other arm arm properly around Agatha’s middle.

Nicky was soon talking about all the things they could throw into the pool for him to fetch and Rio was only half-listening, otherwise occupied by Agatha’s soft hum of contentment as she pressed her face into Rio’s cheek and snuggled in closer.

Rio looked up when Nicky stopped talking and raised her brows at him. Even Agatha turned to check he was okay but he was simply smiling dreamily at them.

“Are you in love, mama?”

Such a big question for such a little boy.

Rio felt Agatha inhale sharply, the breath catching in her throat as she did. She turned to see her face and saw that her eyes were watering and her cheeks had a pink flush about them that hadn’t been there before.

“Yes, honey.”

Rio was the one to gasp this time and Agatha turned to look at her with a sudden fear in her soft gaze.

She’d just outed herself, vocally, willingly, for the first time ever. And to the most important person in the world to her. And Rio was so proud of her, more proud than she’d been of Alice when she’d announced it in their freshman dorm, more proud of Agatha than she’d ever been of anyone in her life.

She smiled at her, gave her a gentle nod, and then turned to Nicky because apparently Agatha couldn’t tear her gaze away from Rio. Nicky’s tongue was sticking into his cheek and his eyes filled had with tears just like his mama’s.

“Really?”

“Yes, mellizo, come here,” Rio said softly, as Agatha closed her eyes and hid against her cheek.

Nicky scrambled to his feet, an unsure little bat flying over to them with his too-long cape trailing along the floor behind him. He stopped just in front of them and Rio adjusted her hold on her towel to open it up so he could clamber on to them and sit staring up at them with wide, watery eyes.

Rio did her best to hold them both within the reach of her towel, though it was a stretch.

They were three little ducklings in swaddling clothes, two rendered mute for their big emotions and one in charge of steering them safely back to the bank.

“I love your mama, very, very much. And I want to be a part of your family. But right now, for a little while, your mom and I have to just be friends, just until the trial is over, okay?”

Nicky shook his head and pulled away from Rio’s hold, and when Agatha moved forwards with him, Rio knew he’d ripped himself away from her too.

“You… you love each other?”

“Honey,” Agatha tried, ripping herself from Rio and standing only to crouch before her son and hold his wrists.

Nicky’s eyes were like saucers. Rio had never understood that expression before. Firstly what the hell was a saucer? Other than the flying kind or the kind you see people put their tea cups on in a period drama? But Nicky’s were like those; perfectly round, and holding so much in them.

“Is that… is…”

Nicky’s saucer eyes moved from his mom to Rio and he gulped as he asked, “is that why you… do you still love me?”

Of all the questions that could have come out of that little boy’s mouth, this was the last one Rio expected. She began to stumble with her words because Nicky’s large eyes were not only tearing up but spilling the tears down his round cheeks.

“Honey,” Agatha said again, and Rio could hear the tears in her voice but couldn’t see them. “Rio loves you so much.”

“So much,” Rio managed to breathe out, knowing it wasn’t enough.

Nicky blinked and sniffed and looked away to his mom who was still crouched before him.

“I’ve wanted this for so long.”

“I know, baby. I’m sorry I didn’t tell you. I was trying… I had to make sure the trial was going okay and… do you forgive me?”

“Yes, mama,” was all Rio heard because Nicky was pulled so quickly into Agatha’s arms and she watched as they hugged each other and heard the all-too familiar sounds of Agatha crying.

Nicky patted her head gently as he squeezed her tight and said, “it’s okay, mama. It’s okay.”

Rio placed her head in her hands, her fingers slipping into her hair. Had they ruined it? Would Nicky not want-…?

“Melliza?” Nicky sniffed her name, and Rio looked up to see him blinking owlishly across at her, still in the midst of hugging his mama. “I… maybe you can hug us? Please?”

Rio fell to her knees faster than she ever had. And she pulled them both in. She wrapped her arms around them and took in a deep breath as she did.

“Tres patitos,” Nicky said quietly, barely above a whisper. “Maybe forever?”

Rio kissed Agatha’s shoulder and raised her hand to the back of Nicky’s head and held him a while before she said, “I’d like that, mellizo.”

Nicky nodded and smiled, and soon the smile became a toothy grin that Rio matched with her own.

“Is it real? Not pretend?”

“Yes.”

Nicky’s grin became a giggle, a soft burst of laughter. And Rio raised her brows as the short giggle became a waterfall of giggles and before Rio knew it she was laughing along as Nicky was crumpled over with his laughter.

Agatha soon caught it too, totally bewildered as to why both her son and her girlfriend were now cackling beside her.

The delirium lasted until Rio encouraged Nicky to run and jump into the pool with her and then the laughter dissolved into splashing and then shouting until Agatha jumped in with them and was in Rio’s arms the moment she surfaced.

And Nicky, exhausted from the laughter and all the paddling, climbed on too, slipping his arms around Rio’s shoulders to keep himself above the water.

“You’ll get married?”

“I hope so, mellizo.”

Nicky nodded keenly, barely able to talk because he was grinning so wide and the splashing of his arms meant he kept swallowing water.

“Mama? Will you please marry Rio?”

Agatha hummed quietly and released one arm from around Rio’s neck to wrap around Nicky’s middle. They were a puddle of limbs, a floating mass of easy joy and hopeful excitement.

And then a sound like a car back firing reverberated across the rooftop.

No, Rio thought, not a car back firing.

A sound like a bullet from a gun.

Chapter End Notes

Uh oh

Chapter 56: Blood in the Water

Chapter Summary

Rio has to face up to her trauma.

Chapter Notes

so sorry about that cliffhanger

See the end of the chapter for more notes

There was blood in the water.

Pigment everywhere.

And then there was Nicky, his little body thrown forwards, dislodging even Agatha’s tight hold so he could be in Rio’s arms.

Rio fell back with him, slipping beneath the surface of the water and gasping for air when all she could inhale was chlorine. And still Nicky clung on. Still he remained in her arms. Still he was as close to her as if they were one body.

They already shared a face, after all. Rio would give him everything else she had.

Still the water they were drowning in was claret rather than translucent blue.

Rio’s next act was to give Nicky his breath back. She forced her right foot down and used it to push them up again. And when they surfaced the red was there, brighter and more dangerous than before.

Rio was coughing and spluttering and her hands were seeking, searching, but there was no bullet wound in Nicky’s back, nor in his sides, down his legs, in the back of his head.

But the red wasn’t on him, it was on Agatha. Bright spots in the water, hugging her hips and pelvis. And across her chest, near her heart. Rio swallowed a mouthful of water as she reached to feel the damage, to coat her fingers in the life of Agatha Harkness.

She felt her hips first but found nothing but soft fabric. And then her chest, her chest she held in her hand, curling her fingers around Agatha’s breast.

No blood, she thought. No blood.

It had all taken less than five seconds.

“What’s wrong? Rio? What’s wrong?”

Rio couldn’t breathe. Someone had shot Nicky. Someone had shot Agatha. She was sure one or both of them had just been shot, that Nicky had been bleeding in her arms as she’d been drowning, that Agatha had been bleeding from her heart.

But her eyes, stingingly wide, were on Agatha’s who was now brushing her thumb over her cheek. Agatha, who had taken the red from the water, from her bikini, and siphoned it into her cheeks and nose.

Agatha, who was unharmed, and alive.

“What the fuck just happened?”

Rio swallowed as she looked from Agatha to the source of the shout and saw, not a gunman, but Jennifer Kale, standing in a dark dress, hands on her hips and an impatient look on her face. Jen’s eyes were down on Rio’s hand that still rested around Agatha’s breast.

She dropped her hold on her girlfriend and instead tightened her hold on Nicky as Agatha whispered her name again and drew her attention back to her.

Nicky was wriggling against her, retreating from the place he’d hidden against her neck, spluttering a little as he did so. But spluttering was good. Spluttering was better than…

“No one got shot?”

Her voice was unlike her own and she hated the sound of it but more than she hated it she needed to hear Agatha tell her that no, no one was shot, everyone was okay. They were here. They were safe. They were together.

Agatha’s brows pulled in tight as Rio tightened her hold on Nicky and he could look up at her, and soon pressed his little face in against her cheek and wrapped his arms around her head as if to protect her from her own thoughts.

“No, my love,” Agatha whispered, her hand on Nicky’s head now, her other hand on Rio's arm as she moved back flush in the water. “We’re here, we’re safe, we’re together.”

Rio nodded and took in a shaking breath, unwilling to let Nicky go properly when she’d just had to experience losing him.

“You’re hurting me, melliza,” Nicky whispered, his warm breath tickling her wet cheek. So she let go, released him totally and he still clung on, pressing a clumsy kiss to the place he’d just pressed himself into as he slipped from her hold and looked up at her with the same look of concern as his mama.

Rio felt dazed and like someone was ringing a bell close to her ear as Nicky took her hand and began to pull her towards the steps.

“Come on, maybe too much sun, right, mama? We should get you a towel and more lotion and some water too.”

Rio nodded absently but the ringing was so loud she could barely hear anything. She just knew Nicky was pulling her out of the pool and Agatha was now clutching her arm and her fingers had found their home again between her own.

“It’s okay,” she kept whispering, “you’re okay.”

Only Rio didn’t feel okay. She kept looking around for the blood she’d seen. She kept looking back at Nicky, to the tanned skin of his back to check for bullet wounds she might have missed. She kept turning to Agatha and seeing the red she was wearing that, for a moment of pure terror, had looked so much like blood.

What was happening? Why was her heart rate so fast? Why was her mind running like a freight train and why was she crying?

A momentary nightmare. Over now. Leaving its imprint on Rio’s heart. She’d lost them both in the time it took to die and come back to life again. She’d lost both Nicky and Agatha in a moment and had them back again the next.

She was disorientated still but Nicky was there, and she tugged suddenly at his arm to make him stop and look. She ducked down to kiss his head and he smiled up at her as she straightened. Agatha was on the other side of her and so she turned to try to kiss her cheek but missed and hit her lips instead. Agatha kissed her back. Rio felt her hand on her face. She felt her close. It was enough.

They made it onto dry land and Jen was saying something but Rio could see her mouth move, only she couldn’t hear a thing she was saying; the ringing was so damn loud.

“Baby.”

Agatha, of course Agatha would get through.

“Baby,” she said again, “My love, you’re burning up. Let’s sit you down. You look like you’ve seen a ghost.”

Nicky had let go of Rio’s hand when they were by the beds again and waited at the end of them for Agatha to do the rest, knowing his mom would know what to do. Rio found herself being wrapped in a towel and guided to the bed. Her legs were covered by another towel and Agatha was at her hip as Nicky settled nearby on the next bed.

“Everyone’s okay?” Her own voice barely cut through the ringing but Agatha heard it, and Agatha nodded as she brushed hair back from Rio’s wet face and traced her fingers along her jaw.

“Safe,” she smiled, “here,” she nudged their noses together, “together”, she kissed her.

It was like a mantra. A mantra Rio needed to hear and Agatha just knew to say.

“What the fuck is going on?”

Rio blinked, transfixed by Agatha’s attention, her lips tingling with the memory of Agatha’s own. The ringing was lessening, but she felt hollow still, like there was a tiny bell trapped somewhere in her empty body. A death toll bell.

And then Agatha kissed her again and everything was silent until suddenly it wasn’t.

“You are such fucking morons.” Jen.

“True love’s kiss.” Nicky.

“Jesus, Rio. Really?” Alice.

Rio blinked but apparently this wasn’t the response Agatha had been looking for because she’d broken the kiss but she hadn’t pulled away.

“Alice, Rio needs some water.”

Rio blinked again and suddenly an open bottle of water was against her lips and Rio was drinking it but she was also floating high above the little scene as she watched the players slowly turn their attention to her body in a play she didn’t really want to be part of.

“She high?” Jen.

“Mama, what’s wrong with her?” Nicky.

“Rio? Babe? Why do you look like that?” Alice.

“Baby, it’s okay. I’m here. Take a deep breath.” Agatha.

“I feel weird.” Rio.

Agatha nodded and changed her position on the sunbed, moving to sit before her, still holding her face.

“Lay back.”

Rio swallowed.

“I swear to god if this is some acting shit just to get out of-,” Jen snapped as Rio did as she was told and Agatha rounded on the other woman.

“Finish that sentence and I will fire you, Jennifer Kale.”

“What, for the fifth time this month?!”

Agatha growled her response and Rio just blinked at her, fighting off the strange floating feeling that was trying to creep its way back.

“Babe?” Alice asked, holding out a fry and hovering it a couple inches from Rio’s lips. “Maybe eat something. Did you eat today?”

“No,” Agatha snatched the fry from Alice’s hand, inadvertently crushing it. “Not enough anyway. She’s been jumping about the pool like a madwoman.”

Rio’s eyes moved to the limp fry in Agatha’s hands and she managed a smile before she opened her mouth to accept it. Her gaze fell to the red of Agatha’s bikini as she bit down and her stomach churned unhappily.

“She was just hungry,” Nicky’s soft voice floated across, full of worry, “right, melliza? Too much sun and not enough food. Here, have one of mine too.” He leant forwards and held out not one but two fries he’d taken from the plate Alice had delivered to his side not moments ago.

Rio smiled a little and took them from him, looking a bit like a walrus for two seconds as they dandled from her lips before she ate them.

“Right,” Rio managed to say as she swallowed and turned back to Agatha, reaching out to touch the string over Agatha’s shoulder, just to reassure what she already knew. Just fabric. Just a bikini. She turned to take Nicky’s hand.

Agatha had been watching her the whole time, moving the hand that held the string down to her hip so Rio could wrap her fingers in the bow and in that way tie them together.

“You with me, my love?”

Rio nodded, her lips twitching into a smile again as she accepted another fry from Agatha and soon Agatha was sat crossed-legged and facing her between her legs, the towel pushed up to allow her to do so. Rio was in no position to argue, physically or mentally, so she continued to eat everything offered to her as Nicky held her hand and her fingers remained tangled in Agatha.

The floating feeling was gone now, replaced with only a vague sense of embarrassment. But no shame could ever get in the way of being fed fries and chicken tenders by a beautiful woman.

“Anyway,” Rio was tuned in now to everyone, having been focused for a while on making her mouth chew, and taking advantage of being able to stare at Agatha’s tits in her red bikini under the pretence of being still a little out of it, “spilling secrets when swimming around starving, are we?”

Agatha sighed heavily, raising a half-eaten tender to Rio’s lips and swatting her gently to get her to raise her gaze up again. “It’s none of your business, Jen.”

Rio looked up at the woman standing with her arms crossed and a scowl on her face.

“We agreed that-…”

“We agreed we would do what was right for my family. The only thing that’s right is that we’re together.” Agatha paused and Rio eyed the tender in her hand as she absently twisted the string at Agatha’s hip. “Besides, we’ve got what we need. This’ll all be over in-…”

“Have you heard that pride comes before a fall?”

“No,” Nicky interjected, “no more falls please.” He looked at Rio, holding two ketchup covered fries up to his face. Rio smiled her reassurance at him, squeezing his other hand in the process.

“You have to trust me on this.” Agatha continued, glancing briefly at her son before looking back up at Jen.

“Well I don’t, okay? This whole thing has been such a fucking mess and you haven’t been sleeping or eating and I just knew today would be a mistake. I knew you’d do something stupid and I can’t just sit back and watch you-…!”

Jen stopped her tirade because to her surprise, and everyone else’s, Agatha had ripped a chunk of Rio’s chicken tender and was chewing it obnoxiously before shoving the rest of it in her mouth and swallowing it only half-chewed.

“There,” she choked, coughing a little as Rio leant to smack her back gently, inadvertently feeling for any bullet wounds she may have missed earlier. There were none. Agatha was here, whole, and hers. “Is that enough? Get me a whole fucking bargain bucket on your way out, Jennifer.”

Rio sat properly and released Nicky, moving upwards the few inches she needed to be able to wrap her arm properly around Agatha’s middle. It was better this way; better to hold her, to be her protector.

She glanced at Nicky and saw his ketchup’d fries still floating in front of him, his wide eyes up on Jennifer.

“You’re such a bitch,” Jen snapped. “Do you know what I’ve sacrificed for you? Do you know how hard it is to be your friend? How hard you are to love?”

The world stopped and as Jen realised what she’d said and Agatha stiffened in Rio’s hold, Rio’s empty body filled suddenly with boiling blood.

“I’m sorry, I-… I didn’t mean that.” Jen began to stutter.

Rio was standing but someone else had stood up first. Nicky, with his ketchup-stained fingers, had stood from his sunbed and was squaring up to Jennifer who only had eyes for Agatha.

“Auntie Jen, I think you need to leave. Please. We were really happy until you came along and then you scared Rio and now you’re being mean to my mama and you’ve ruined it.”

Rio stood behind Nicky, placing a supportive hand on his shoulder as she stared across at Jen, silently daring her to object to the little boy’s words. Nicky’s heels moved onto her toes and Rio squeezed him gently, letting him know that her protection of Agatha extended easily to him too.

She’d face a whole firing squad before anyone got near her boy.

Jen was hesitating, clearly deliberating. And her wide eyes moved from Agatha to Rio before she said: “I didn’t mean it. You know I-…”

“Nicky’s right. You should leave, Jen.” Rio said, her voice much more like her own again, though it was hoarse still from all the water she’d inadvertently swallowed.

“C’mon, babe,” Alice said quietly, moving to take her girlfriend’s arm. “Let’s go.”

Jen nodded just once, visibly gulped, and then turned to leave with Alice who glanced around at Rio briefly before focusing on getting them out.

Rio remained where she was, watching them go, as Nicky moved around her and went to sit beside his mom. She didn’t move until the door was closed much more gently than it had been earlier opened. No more shots were fired, so Rio remained in her body, drowning from the inside out in her fury.

When they were alone again, Rio turned back to see Agatha holding Nicky’s hand and leaning over to hold his face and kiss his temple. She watched for a moment, watched a loving mother and a beloved son.

And then the fury took hold.

“Fuck it,” she announced without another thought in her panicked brain.

She stormed off, marching her way beyond the pool as she heard Agatha shout after her. Her earlier fear had transformed her into a seething, raging, thing. She was alight with fury and had no one but Jen to take it out on.

Because she couldn’t just let Jen get away with it. She couldn’t just let her go and not face the consequences of telling a woman who believed she was hard to love that she’d been right the whole time.

She ripped the door open with enough force that the sound of another gun going off ricochet across the roof. But she remained steady with it. She didn’t drown this time.

Instead she stepped inside and she stopped in her tracks because Jen was there, bent down so Alice could swaddle her as she sobbed against her chest.

“Don’t, Rio,” Alice warned, her voice soft but sure.

“It was a cruel fucking thing to say, Jen.”

“She knows that.”

Rio realised that her hands were fists at her sides and her jaw was so tense it could snap any moment.

“She thinks she’s hard to love. And there she is just-!”

“Jen knows.”

“Then she shouldn’t have fucking said it.”

“She knows that, Rio. Just-…”

Jen sniffed and raised her head, wiping quickly at her streaming eyes as she focused on Rio.

“Did she tell you her plan? The evidence she’s got?”

Rio nodded stiffly, knowing if she opened her mouth she’d scream at the woman.

“She was going to wait, going to get more, build a firmer case, and then you met with that bitch and she grew terrified she’d lose you suddenly and so she’s hurrying it along because she’s so scared she’ll-…”

The door opened again behind Rio and Rio didn’t need to look around to know who it was. She could feel Agatha just behind her, feel her presence even though she stood just over her shoulder, not yet touching her.

But Agatha was her sun, and so she felt her rays even when she wasn’t with her. So, close now, she was warmed from the outside in. Her fists relaxed and her hands instead curled loosely by her sides as she went from boiling to simmering.

“Go ahead, Jennifer. Finish what you started.”

Agatha moved a little closer and the sun’s rays got warmer. Rio’s arm moved out to the side, covering Agatha from either attacking or being attacked.

“I want you to be happy,” Jen said, raising herself to her full height.

“And you think I’m doing something that will jeopardise that?” Agatha deduced, her hand curling around Rio’s elbow.

“I think… I think you’re rushing because you’re scared.”

“You weren’t there,” Agatha snapped. “You weren’t in the courtroom when Nicky was panicking when his dad picked him up. You weren’t there when the judge was watching my son struggle and fight off tears because he was trying to be brave even when he was scared out of his mind. So you can’t know that I don’t need more time because I have what I need to destroy Ralph’s life and my son, our son, has already won this trial for us.”

Jen looked affronted but Rio thought she also looked ashamed.

“I’m sorry, okay? I’m trying my best here.”

Rio felt Agatha’s hold tighten on her arm.

“Clean yourself up,” Agatha hissed, “you look a mess.”

Jen scoffed and wiped at her cheek.

“And go get Nicky some ice cream. Chocolate. Extra sauce.”

Rio was pulled then, turned away before anyone could say anything else. And she followed Agatha back out to the pool, dragged along behind her like a naughty child.

Nicky was back on his sunbed, quietly eating his lunch. But he looked up the moment they got close and frowned his deep frown at them.

“Did Auntie Jen apologise more?”

“Yes, honey. Auntie Jen says she’s sorry to you too. And she’s bringing you ice cream.”

Nicky didn’t react to this news with anything other than a quick nod and Rio chewed on her lip as she was pulled down beside Agatha on the bed.

“Eat your lunch,” Agatha directed absently, releasing her hold on Rio’s arm as she turned to reach for her shirt to tug over her head.

Rio watched as Nicky did as he was told and then reached across to place Agatha’s salad bowl in her lap. But Agatha pushed it away before it could settle and was soon standing.

“I just need a second.”

Her sun had disappeared behind a rain cloud and Rio was left alone with Nicky, who had stopped eating to watch his mama too.

“Auntie Jen loves us,” Nicky said quietly as Agatha walked away. “Why was she being mean?”

Rio shook her head as she watched Agatha stand by the clear barrier at the edge of the roof and looked out over the hills beyond.

“Sometimes, when we’re scared, we say things we don’t mean. Because being angry is easier than being scared.” It was a generous reading, Rio knew. But she couldn’t tell an eight year old that Jen was actually just a cunt.

“That’s stupid.”

“Isn’t it.”

Nicky nodded as he dunked a fry into his ketchup.

“If I saw a snake I wouldn’t call it names I would just be scared.”

Rio smiled a little, enjoying this logic and the break from her furious, frightened thoughts.

“Yeah? Wouldn't you call it a stupid slimy idiot?”

Nicky giggled and then clearly made a choice to stop himself and continued to frown again, “well, maybe. But then I’d be scared again and maybe run.”

“Definitely run,” Rio agreed, turning to look at Nicky now. She saw his frown and decided to try and make it disappear. “But would you scream like this?” She raised her hands above her head and waved them like a maniac, doing her best impression of a screaming idiot, running from a stupid slimy idiot snake.

Nicky giggled some more and nodded enthusiastically, forgetting his earlier decision, “yes exactly like that!”

Rio laughed as she brought her hands back down. “Let’s hope no snakes get us up here. We can’t run by the pool.”

“No, it’s too slippy and dangerous and we could hit our heads,” Nicky agreed, nodding very seriously as he bit into his fry.

Rio grabbed a tender from her own plate and spun where she sat to lean back against the sunbed, her gaze on Agatha again.

After a beat Nicky asked, “are you feeling better now? I got a fright too when Jen banged the door but… you got a bigger one.”

Rio swallowed thickly and turned to see Nicky with his deep frown again. “I’m fine, mellizo. The noise scared me and… I’m a little tired from work lately and we’ve done a lot today.”

Nicky nodded and shifted where he sat, “We can do less? We can have a quiet night.”

“That sounds good, mellizo.” Rio smiled at him, coaxing a smaller smile from the boy as she turned the conversation around to the scariest animals that might make them run even around the pool.

When they both agreed that the snake was tied with a hungry dragon, about twenty minutes after first bringing up even the concept of a dragon, let alone a hungry one, Agatha was back with them looking down at their empty plates.

“I saved you my biggest chicken tender,” Rio offered as Agatha sat down on the end of her bed.

Agatha smiled a little and took it gingerly, peeling off a small bite and examining it before she put it in her mouth.

“Did you enjoy the view?” Nicky asked hopefully, smiling his best smile at his mom in the hopes she'd return it with her own best smile.

“I did, honey. I just needed some air.”

“Okay, mama,” he said as if it made complete sense to him and they weren’t currently surrounded by air. “Do you want to talk about what Auntie Jen said?”

Agatha inhaled slowly and Rio watched with a sad smile as she dropped her gaze back to her chicken tender.

“Here,” Nicky said, standing from his bed to take Rio’s hand and hold it out to Agatha, “take Rio’s hand and tell us how it made you feel. You always get me to tell you how I feel when I’m sad, remember? It helps.”

Agatha sniffed and nodded as she took Rio’s hand and smiled shyly.

“When did you get so smart?”

“I think maybe I just know you’re sad and I don’t want you to be.”

Agatha smiled as Rio squeezed her hand and shuffled to sit a little closer along the bed as Nicky sat on the one beside theirs and sat on his hands.

“How do you feel, mama?”

“Sad, honey. Very sad.”

Rio watched as Agatha dropped her gaze again and focused instead on their joined hands.

“Sometimes,” Nicky said slowly, his gaze down on their hands too, and then moving to Rio, “sometimes grown ups say mean things because it’s easier to be mad than to be scared. Right, melliza?”

Rio’s lips twitched as Agatha sniffed. “Right.”

“And, and… maybe Auntie Jen is scared about the custody stuff? Because…” but here is where Nicky ran out of fuel and Rio stepped in as he searched around for a reason.

“Because she loves you both so much and wants to see you together still.”

“Right,” Nicky agreed quickly, “she wants us in custody.”

Rio’s lips twitched again as she turned from Nicky to Agatha and saw her looking across at her son with watery eyes.

“Can I-...?” But she didn’t need to finish her sentence for Nicky to know what he was being asked and he launched himself at Agatha, throwing his whole body into hers as Rio released her hand so Agatha could give him a tight, one-armed hug as she held her chicken tender away.

“I love you,” she heard her whisper.

“I love you to the moon and back and all the farthest stars,” Nicky whispered right back.

It wasn’t long before Nicky was turning to Rio and ushering her over and Rio was quick and eager to oblige. She wrapped her fellow patitos in her wings and kissed the back of Agatha’s neck as she covered them both as best she could.

Breathing the scent of chlorine in, she thought back to her panic in the water. The blood she’d seen, the ringing in her ears, the hollowness. And yet here she was with two intact, safe patitos.

Nicky wriggled backwards and Rio pulled away to watch him kiss his mama’s cheek and smile hopefully at her, not relenting until Agatha smiled back.

“Can I play with my switch while you eat?”

Agatha smiled a little and nodded, turning to pick up her salad and drop the majority of the chicken tender into it as she began to poke around at the greens.

Rio sat and watched as Nicky rummaged for his switch in Agatha’s bag and then turned to Agatha and opened her legs to see if she’d assume her usual position between them. Within a second Agatha had begun to shuffle back, not even looking at where she was going but using one hand against the bed to move herself until Rio could wrap her arms around her.

“Thank you,” Agatha said, barely a whisper but enough for Rio to smile and kiss her shoulder as she settled further back and Agatha began to eat.

Nicky was generous with his game, providing commentary for Rio so she could feel like she was playing along too, even if she couldn’t see his screen from her current position.

And Rio was more than happy to provide encouragement and advice because Agatha had eaten her salad, though not the chicken earlier provided, and was now fully reclined against her, caressing her arm.

Rio changed the position of the bed so they were laying almost completely flat and the moment she did, Agatha changed her position too. She was on her side now, curled up as best she could be, her face against Rio’s neck and her knees up over her hip.

Nicky, without acknowledging it, lowered his volume and Rio followed suit, knowing Agatha would soon be drifting off to sleep.

He moved to sit on the floor, arranging a towel so he had a cushion, and angled himself against Rio’s sunbed so Rio could see the screen and soon words weren’t needed because Rio was able to simply watch the action as Nicky played it.

Agatha was asleep by this point, snoring soft against Rio’s chest, and Rio was playing with her hair, focusing on the screen and the rhythmic breathing of Agatha Harkness in her arms.

Jen arrived after ten minutes of this new silence, and brought with her nothing but ice cream and a quiet dignity. She said nothing as she handed it to a grateful Nicky but she locked eyes with Rio and Rio saw in her the same fear she felt in her chest whenever she thought too hard about the custody battle.

But then she was gone, and Rio was fed two large spoonfuls of Nicky’s ice cream as she lay there with one patito safe in her arms and the other close enough that she could ruffle his feathers.

And as Agatha slept on, and Nicky got further into his game, Rio realised something. Agatha knew she was loved. Agatha knew Rio loved her and loved her easily because she hadn’t worried about simply turning into her and closing her eyes. She’d just done it. She knew she was loved.

“Melliza,” Nicky whispered after close to an hour of quiet gaming, “I’ve been thinking.”

Rio turned her attention to Nicky where she’d been watching the wispy clouds roll past.

“Yeah?”

“Mmhm,” Nicky nodded as he kept his eyes on the Switch. “About us being a family.”

“What about it, mellizo?”

“Well,” Nicky said slowly, “I was wondering if maybe the next time you have to have a pretend kid at work you can tell me first. Mama always tells me if she has to play a mama and I was wondering if you could do the same, please. I didn’t like it when you had to be that stupid James’ mom. So… maybe if you can tell me first I can think about it and soon be okay with it.”

A smile tugged at the corners of Rio’s lips, because of Nicky’s words and because she could feel Agatha waking against her.

“Okay, mellizo. I promise I’ll run it past you first.”

Nicky nodded and Rio could see enough of his face to see him frowning just a little. “Okay, gracias."

Agatha made a soft noise and Nicky looked around at it, raising his brows in surprise as Agatha rubbed at her eye and tried to hide against Rio’s neck. She groaned as her legs stretched out and she turned to lay flat against her, tucking her arms down either side of Rio’s body.

“I think your mama is tired.”

“Sí, mucho.”

“Stop talking about me,” Agatha protested, flat as a pancake now against Rio, grumbling into her neck.

Nicky giggled and Rio grinned as she continued to play with her hair. Agatha eventually drifted back off and Nicky eventually asked if he could go back in the pool. Rio agreed so long as he put more lotion on and he was careful.

She watched him doggy paddle around in his goggles, constantly diving down to collect a penny he was throwing in for himself to find. He’d always hold it up triumphantly for Rio to see when he found it, unaware that every time he ducked below the surface, Rio was holding her breath with him so she’d know exactly what was too long and what was just enough.

“So daddy,” Agatha murmured, having shifted enough once she’d woken again against her to have her hand across her ribs so she could experience Rio’s breathing against her palm.

“Just making sure he’s okay.”

Agatha hummed and was silent for a while before she asked: “Does it bother you? The daddy of it all?”

Rio thought for a moment, enjoying Agatha nuzzling as she held her breath until Nicky was back in her sights.

“You mean Ralph? Or Miguel Vidal?”

“Both. Either.”

“It bothers me that he’s such a piece of shit, that he ever laid hands on you, that Nicky had to even be brave just to be held by him.” Agatha kissed her throat and Rio held her breath again as Nicky ducked down.

When he was back she said, her voice much softer, none of the vitriol of before present in it, “my dad was my papa. Or just dad. I can be daddy without associating it with him, if that’s what you’re asking?”

Agatha hummed against her, opening her mouth against her throat as Nicky disappeared and Rio held her breath again.

“Same for me,” she said gently, still hiding away against her as Rio’s hand slid down to rest on the small of her back, just touching the fabric of her bikini. “I’m mama to Nicky, and my mother…,” she trailed off and Rio held her tighter, “Mommy makes me think of you getting me pregnant, and I really, really enjoy thinking about that.”

Rio coughed as Nicky resurfaced and she felt Agatha grin against her skin.

“Please don’t,” she said quietly, her fingers itching to move towards Agatha’s ass.

“Especially not while you’re-…”

“Between your legs? In a bikini?”

“Exactly.” She held her breath again and felt Agatha’s tongue dart out against her neck.

She took a shot and smacked her ass whilst Nicky was underwater and grinned when Agatha twitched and yelped against her.

“So inappropriate,” Agatha chastised.

“Unlike tonguing my throat?” Rio questioned as Nicky bounced about in the water and waved his penny in the air.
