She laughed at the sight, spurred on by Agatha shuffling and grumbling against her, but remaining hidden. She understood. If she didn’t need to keep an eye on Nicky she might hide too.

“What happened, Rio? In the pool?”

Rio was holding her breath again, watching the pool carefully for Nicky to reappear. When he did she exhaled slowly and offered him a thumbs up before she wrapped her arm back around Agatha.

“I’ve not been sleeping well,” she admitted as Nicky pulled off his goggles to rid them of the water they’d collected. “And I’ve had dreams of…” she trailed off and Agatha nudged her nose in against her throat, a silent gesture of reassurance. “Of you and Nicky, held at gunpoint by these faceless intruders. I… I guess the sound of Jen arriving… it sounded like a gunshot and I…”

“Hey,” Agatha breathed out, no longer hiding as she leant up and out of the corner of her eye Nicky had dropped down again so Rio was no longer breathing. “We’re safe. We have so much protection now, no one will ever get close.”

Rio nodded, glancing to see if Nicky was up yet. He wasn’t.

“I shouldn’t have cut you off. I should have-...” Nicky was up again and Rio caught the movement so she released her held breath and Agatha’s lips twitched only slightly as she moved a hand to caress her cheek. “I should have been there for you.”

“We’re past it,” Rio whispered, her eyes darting to check on Nicky and seeing him bopping about near the shallow end of the pool.

“I told you a long time ago I wanted to be a good girlfriend to you and I haven’t been.”

“Mi amor.”

“You’re still grieving your dad and-…”

“I’ll be grieving him forever.”

“I know,” Agatha was quick to say, “I know.”

Rio’s gaze fell for a second and then she moved it back up to look towards Nicky in the pool.

“And I know I make it hard to love me.”

Rio’s eyes jumped back to Agatha and she frowned deeply as Agatha’s gaze fell from her own.

“Jen was right about that.”

“She wasn’t.”

Rio wanted to say more but Nicky was in the water again, splashing like a madman to get deeper. She debated and then decided not to hold her breath this time, she needed to use it to reassure Agatha, rather than herself.

“Loving you is like breathing. And you know it is. You know I feel that way about you because you can’t sleep and yet you just turned into me and knew I would hold you so you could. You know you’re easy to love because I love you like you are.”

Agatha’s gaze had moved up to meet Rio’s again and her lips had parted, her eyes glassy and unsure and so Rio kissed her so she didn’t need to say anything and Agatha kissed her back until Rio knew they would both be okay.

They broke the kiss and Rio glanced at the pool, seeing Nicky grinning with his hand in the air. She smiled right back and then looked at Agatha with raised brows and a crooked grin that she didn’t quite match.

“That boy is so perfect. You made a perfect little boy.”

“And we should make another.”

Rio gasped gently as Agatha’s finger brushed from her lips to her cheek and she looked lost for a moment before she whispered, “I will win this case, I will keep my son, and then we can be happy.”

“Felizmente casada,” Rio agreed quietly, watching in awe as Agatha’s lips twitched and she moved her hand up to kiss her own ring, maintaining eye contact as she did.

“You saw my interview?”

“I cut it out and put it on my mirror in the trailer.”

“Anna told me.”

Rio rolled her eyes and looked around Agatha to check on Nicky, watching as he leant up on the side of the pool and was looking out over the view.

“I said we’d visit,” Agatha said, watching Rio closely as Rio turned her attention back to her. “Before we go away. I said we’d spend a couple days with her in Delaware.”

Rio nodded and brushed a loose strand of hair from Agatha’s face to behind her ear, “See? Already a better daughter than me.”

“I have a lot to make up for,” Agatha whispered, slipping down again to hide against Rio’s neck.

Rio sighed softly, her gaze drifting back to Nicky as she began to play with Agatha’s hair again.

“She loves you. You’d know if she didn’t. She’s not as good an actress as me.” Rio squeaked as Agatha poked her side.

She felt Agatha breathe out steadily against her and she smiled as Nicky began to practice his backstroke, not doing so well by the amount of times he had to stop and start again.

“The way he trusted you earlier,” Agatha whispered after a little while of comfortable silence, “it was the exact opposite with Ralph. He could barely hold him. He didn’t even know how to give his son a piggy back. And then when he lifted Nicky up the fear in his face… but with you… he knows you’ll keep him safe. Even earlier, when you thought… you were holding him so tightly. And he got a fright too. But he didn’t jump into my arms. He jumped into yours. And I love you for that. For the way you let him love you, for the way you love him, for the way you put yourself in danger just to keep us safe.”

Rio had stopped breathing again, but not because Nicky was underwater. She’d stopped breathing because she’d felt like crying the more Agatha spoke.

“I love you,” she continued, “I don’t want you to ever feel afraid for us again. We have so many eyes on us, and at your house there will be a constant guard, I’ve made sure of it. We’ll be safe. We’ll just be waiting for you to come home.”

Rio squeezed her eyes closed but knew she couldn’t do it for long because she had to keep a lookout for Nicky. When she opened them again he was back to looking out at the view and Agatha had shifted to lean up and kiss her cheek.

“I want you to talk to your therapist about what happened today.”

Rio nodded, knowing she would.

“I don’t want my mother to ruin your life like for forty years she ruined mine.”

Agatha’s head was blocking the sun and so she was instead haloed by it, beatified by the very thing she was to Rio. And Rio raised her hand to hold Agatha in place and smiled sadly as she whispered.

“The next forty she won’t touch. It’ll just be us. Just tres patitos.”

Agatha grinned and chuckled as she leant in to kiss Rio and hummed as she did.

“Maybe four soon? I’m getting old, remember? You can’t make me wait that long.”

Rio rolled her eyes but grinned all the same.

Agatha was soon tucked back in against her again, hiding against her skin. And Rio, as her gaze drifted over to Nicky once more and she started to hold her breath every time he disappeared below the water, could feel her whole body relaxing.

“This is the start,” Agatha said quietly, toying with the ends of Rio’s hair that she was now allowed to grow out again. “This is the start of it. Of us being a family.”

Rio nodded, focusing on Nicky’s grinning face as he held up his shiny penny like it was a precious diamond. She’d need to find Agatha a diamond, one she hold up for the world to see, just like Nicky and his penny.

Time slowed down then, expanding to the size of their love. Rio and Agatha remained curled together for a little while longer but soon Nicky was requesting their presence in the pool and Agatha wouldn’t let Rio go without her close by.

She didn’t say it, but Rio knew she was more concerned about Rio’s earlier panic than she was letting on.

They helped each other with their sunblock, Rio focusing more on Agatha’s paley-freckled skin and pink nose than she did with her own sun protection. And Agatha, now free to, thanked her with a soft kiss before she took her hand and dragged her to the water.

For a while Nicky and Rio dived down for the penny and had multiple splashing fights while Agatha lingered by the steps, keeping an eye on them both, but mostly on Rio. And Rio didn’t have any more anxiety attacks. She instead was exhausted with play and thrilled when Agatha swam over to her and wrapped her limbs around her in a silent: “enough now, hold me for a while” request.

Nicky, being eight and full of energy still, paddled furiously in circles around them, asking all very important questions: “would you rather be a water dinosaur or a land one or maybe a sky one?”/”Mama, how many laps of the pool do you think you could do before you got tired or bored?”/”Can we buy a diving board so me and Rio can practice our dives?”

And Rio, when she was diving for the penny and when she was floating with Agatha, was fully back within herself. Her little glances towards the door had lessened, helped along by Agatha’s frequent kisses to her cheek and temple whenever she did look.

Her heart rate was slower again, with Agatha’s hand curled around her ribs as if to guide it along.

And her hands, they no longer sought to find bullet wounds or gushing blood, but they instead cradled and caressed. They were used to comfort and hold rather than to seek and protect.

This did feel like the beginning. It felt like a life she had only dreamed of having. But a life that was as real as the little boy now attempting a handstand in the water, and the woman now whispering repeated “I love yous” into her ear.

When they left the pool, Rio’s hand never once left Agatha’s touch. She held her fingers on the way out, she touched her side as Agatha helped Nicky dry off and then turned to do the same with Rio. She kissed her over and over again until Nicky giggled and said they must have really wanted to kiss each other seeing as they were doing it a lot now.

And even when they were making their way back, dried and clothed, Rio had Nicky in one hand and Agatha in the other.

Val was there to greet them the moment they opened the door and Jen was stood by the elevator, looking sheepish but standing tall. Rio didn’t look at her and the only one to greet her was Nicky who said a soft: “Hello, Auntie Jen.”

He was back on Rio’s toes in the elevator again and this time Agatha was tucked fully into her side until the doors opened onto their floor and they were greeted by the two semi-truck-sized bodyguards.

Rio took a slow breath in as they made their way back to Agatha’s suite and only released it once more when the door was closed on them and they were alone.

“Hon,” Agatha said almost the second it was just them. “Go shower and change into your pjs, we’ll have a movie night tonight.”

Nicky nodded and the thunder faded until Nicky was tucked away deep in the suite and Rio was pressed up against the closed door. Rio’s brows raised as Agatha reached to hold her cheek and her opposite hip.

“Feeling okay?”

“Much better now.”

Agatha smiled as she raised up on her toes and Rio’s hands slipped to grab her ass and hold her flush.

“No red bikinis from now on,” Agatha said, and Rio immediately shook her head, stealing a quick kiss.

“No. Maybe just speak to Jen about her entrances.”

Agatha scoffed and Rio took advantage of her being distracted by kissing her cheek and then dipping down to nip at her neck.

“Baby,” Agatha said quietly, humming low and slow, “You gotta stop.”

Rio exhaled heavily against Agatha’s skin, feeling it against her face and warming her nose before she lifted up and moved her hands to Agatha’s hips instead.

“I have something to show you later.”

Rio’s brows shot up and her hands moved back to their previous post, making the most of their hold to lift Agatha up and smirking when Agatha immediately wrapped her legs around her waist.

“Show me now?”

“No,” Agatha said, shrugging her shoulders and throwing her hair back, momentarily elongating her neck and making Rio want to sink her teeth into it.

“You can’t be a clit tease when I’ve just had visions of you-…”

Agatha’s hand was over her mouth and Rio scowled for it.

“It’s just something I didn’t realise you might like until I…”

Rio’s brows were so far up her forehead she knew she’d need to get Botox just to fix the permanent indents they’re surely leave.

“Something for when we’re alone. Properly. When I can have you all to myself. Okay?”

Agatha removed her hand from Rio’s mouth and she nodded slowly, barely able to form any words and instead just about remembering to breathe.

Her hands were on Agatha’s thighs now, holding her steady despite feeling a little unstable herself with thoughts of having Agatha all alone swimming in her brain.

“I’ve missed you,” was all she could say because it was all that was true and the only thing that wasn’t incredibly inappropriate.

“And I miss you,” Agatha said back, her thumbs pressing into Rio’s cheeks, “even now. Even being right here with you I miss you.”

And Rio knew what she meant. Even as she placed Agatha back down and kissed her slowly, she knew what she meant. She missed her when they agreed to shower separately, when they changed in different rooms, when Rio came in last to the room Agatha and Nicky were in carrying the ugly horse blanket she’d bought with her from Arkansas, and climbed onto the bed, taking the spot they’d left for her in the middle of them.

She missed her constantly because, as she settled down, she realised she’d not yet truly had her. Not really. Not all to herself. Not officially or publicly or openly. And she’d probably miss her too even then. Because no amount of having Agatha would ever be enough for her.

But now, with Agatha and Nicky safe and warm beside her, she relaxed and felt a wave of exhaustion wash over her. The adrenaline that had kicked in earlier had taken all her energy reserves and she now lay, empty and yet so full.

This tired patito opened her wing up and Agatha curled in the moment she did, grumbling about the ugliness of the blanket. But Nicky, he was sat with Scratchy, petting his head and keeping his eyes on the screen. Rio didn’t reach for him because she knew he’d come closer if he wanted to. Besides, he was with Scratchy and Rio wouldn’t want to disturb that.

Agatha ordered snacks to the room and had to move in order to do it, so now, when she was back on the bed, she was laying back against Rio, settled in her favourite spot between her legs.

Val brought them in, announcing herself with such a jaunty knock that there was no disputing who it was. Much to Rio’s relief, Agatha barely moved from against her when they arrived.

It wasn’t that she was thinking of earlier, though her mind still swam with the memory of it, but she was aware now of time. That it was moving still, as slow as it had tried to be for them.

She thanked Val, shooting her a quick smile over Agatha’s head, and they were left alone again.

It took ten minutes for Rio and Nicky to demolish the bowl of popcorn, Agatha helping with a handful of pieces hand fed to her by Rio. And then the snacks were ignored at the end of the bed in favour of comfort, and of being close.

Nicky had been shuffling closer for five minutes now but Rio, and Agatha, were both pretending not to notice. Rio was toying with Agatha’s hair whilst holding her around her middle, her gaze on the screen and a soft smile on her face.

He’d get there eventually.

And soon enough he did, yawning dramatically with his arms up in the air and his mouth wide.

“Wow I could really do with snuggling down and-…”

Rio had already looped her arm around him and tugged him in against her side. He wriggled and then settled almost immediately and Rio turned her head to kiss the top of his head as Agatha reached to drape her arm along his legs.

“This is nice,” Nicky said quietly after a little while of more silence, settling Scratchy on Rio’s hip beside his mama. “I’m so happy you found us, melliza.”

“Are you kidding?” Rio asked, “I’d find you in every universe.”

“Yeah?” Nicky yawned properly this time. “Even the universe where we’re dinosaurs?”

Agatha scoffed and Rio squeezed her waist, “Oh, yeah. I’d be the biggest T-Rex in town and I’d come find my little mini T-Rex and his maiasaura mom.”

“That better be a cute dinosaur.”

Nicky giggled, “They’re the best mama dinosaurs, silly. They have nests and they stay with their babies and bring them food.”

Agatha harrumphed but said nothing more as Rio squeezed her side.

Nicky must have been sitting in this alternate reality for a while because it took him a little time before he next spoke: “What about if we were planes?”

“Planes?”

“Yep.”

Rio hummed in thought, “Well I’d write in big letters in the sky ‘I love my mellizo and his mama’ and then I’d bring you both into my hangar and I’d have green wings and your mama would have purple and you’d have blue ones.”

“That sounds nice.”

“Yeah.”

“What about-…?” But Nicky’s next question was interrupted by a sudden, sharp knock at the door. A knock that was definitely not Val.

All three looked up and Rio tightened her hold on her two loves even as Agatha said: “It’ll just be Jen.”

They heard the door open and the voice of Agatha’s manager float through the suite.

“Agatha?”

“I’ll just be a sec,” Agatha whispered, hearing something in Jen’s tone that Rio heard too, something that she didn’t like.

But Rio let her go, and still Agatha took her hand at the very last second and kissed over her scars on her wrist. Nicky received a reassuring wink as his parting gift, and then she was gone.

“Maybe we should go and make sure Auntie Jen doesn’t say anything mean.”

Rio smiled and shuffled back in the bed to sit up properly, Nicky shuffling with her.

“I think your mama can handle it.”

She heard the door go again and then turned just in time to see the door to the bedroom close without warning and she knew that Agatha had done it because she’d never allow Jen to shut them up here.

“What’s happening?”

Rio squeezed Nicky’s side and kept her eyes on the door for a while. There were voices on the other side of it, multiple voices. It wasn’t just Agatha and Jen, she could also hear men speaking.

She sat up straighter, her heart hammering in her chest, and held Nicky a little tighter. Val wouldn’t let anyone in who she didn’t trust, she knew that much. In fact, Val was probably there with them, by Agatha’s side, making sure no one touched her.

“It’s okay, people just want to talk to your mama.”

“Fans?” Nicky asked quietly, “They shouldn’t be in here.”

“No, bud, not fans. It’ll just be work stuff. Nothing to worry about.”

Nicky nodded but his arm was suddenly thrown over her middle and he was more tucked in than ever. Rio just knew his eyes were on the door as he rested his head on her shoulder so she changed her hold on him to toy with the ends of his hair and hold him close.

“Don’t be scared, bud.”

“Just want to be close, is all.”

“See?” Nicky asked, now palm to palm with Rio. Agatha moved to drape herself over the couch they’d slept on and Rio continued to glare at her. “My fingers are long too. Just like yours are.”

Rio reluctantly looked around to their joined hands and huffed. She guessed he was right. Her arms were always just a tiny bit longer than they really needed to be for her height but she didn’t want to give in just yet. Not when Agatha looked so smug about it.

“You know who is small?”

“Mama.”

“Hey!”

Rio’s scowl disappeared instantly and was replaced by a grin as she slipped her fingers between Nicky’s and held his hand in midair.

“Well, I guess we have the same face, mellizo. So it makes sense our bodies are similar too.”

“Like twins,” Nicky nodded, grinning as Rio wriggled their hands. “Or like a mama and her son.”

The wriggling slowed and Rio’s breathing hitched as Nicky’s grin turned hopeful. The little shit. He’d done it on purpose. He’d come out all bright and wriggly and walloped Rio over the head with a genuine, gentle, sneaky as shit, request for her to be his mama.

The irony that he looked like her but was a whipsmart as his mama was was not lost on her.

She opened her mouth to speak but Agatha’s voice sounded out instead.

“Honey, come over here and give your mama a good morning cuddle please.”

Nicky did as he was told, but not before shooting Rio one last grin and then hurrying off to throw himself into Agatha’s arms. Rio stood and watched, making eye contact with Agatha as she held Nicky tight. Agatha knew it too; how smart he was and how much he loved them both.

It was a conversation they’d need to have eventually, what Rio would be to the little boy who trusted her as much as he trusted his mom. But right now, as Rio settled at the breakfast table and waited for her pancakes to arrive, she didn’t know what to say about it.

Nicky joined her soon and they began talking of everything under the sun, as Agatha took a work call. Their food arrived shortly after she’d stepped away to answer her cell and Rio and Nicky ate their pancakes to the soundtrack of Agatha taking the call on the couch, occasionally wandering over to steal a grape or to kiss Nicky’s head, or Rio’s, whichever one of them was lucky at the time.

And Rio, cautiously broached different topics with Nicky, trying to keep things away from what they now were to one another, or what they would eventually be.

But Nicky’s mind, bright and quick for his age, didn’t linger on one topic or another for long. So they were free to discuss what Rio’s job was for the next couple weeks, how she was enjoying it, how many friends she’d made on set, and the fact that Arkansas had a Dinosaur Park.

By the time they were done agreeing that every town across America should have a Dinosaur Park, Agatha was back at the table, done with her call, and picking at a bowl of fruit.

Their leisurely morning was spent with an excitable Nicky talking a mile a minute and Rio and Agatha stealing glances at one another across the table.

It was Rio who reached for her first, and Agatha who tangled their fingers as if she never wanted to let go.

“Did you buy mama that ring, melliza?”

Nicky really needed to work on his whispering. But Rio grinned all the same, looking at their joined hands and watching the thick gold band twinkle in the sun.

“I did. Do you like it?”

“I think it’s her favourite.”

“I’m here, you know. As much as the two of you are in a total world of your own.”

Agatha’s brows were raised, indicating her totally accurate appraisal of the situation, but her lips were curved into a smile, indicating her total ease and general amusement. And Rio felt like she’d never loved her more as she teased her son who now ran around to protest and kiss her cheek gently, following the gesture with a request that they put some music on and all dance together.

The song that blared across the terrace was an Agatha choice, influenced by Nicky’s general stance on dance parties. I Love to Boogie bounced off the low wall and sounded in the atmosphere of the mid-morning as they danced their pancakes off and laughed at one another’s move, each more wild and crazy than the next.

Nicky was trying out his robot and Rio was clicking her fingers to the beat like an extra in West Side Story. Agatha, a little more dignified, but enjoying the beat as much as the other two, was dancing with her arms in the air and her smile so wide she was tearing up for the joy she felt.

As the song faded into the next, Rio gathered her in her arms and pressed into her cheek, shimmying with her to the next beat. Nicky was off on his own now, filled with the confidence a child can get when he’s in a space where he knows he’s adored.

Five songs later, all out of breath, all happier than they’d been in weeks, they were ordered away by Agatha to change and report back for more patito time. Rio lingered a whale after Nicky left for additional, less child-appropriate kisses. She only left when Agatha reminded her the faster she was to change the quicker they could cuddle on the couch.

Beneath the hot stream of water, Rio smiled to herself because everything felt right again. Three patitos high in the air, shaking their tailfeathers to the beat of their own drum. And Nicky, keen for her to be his officially, especially now he knew what Agtah and her really were to one another.

She made a decision as she stepped from the shower to dry herself and change into the same sweats she’d been wearing all weekend. She’d ask him if she could marry his mama. She’d make sure he was involved, make sure he knew Rio loved him and wanted him just as much as she wanted his mom.

And so, when she stepped from the bathroom, freshly clean and newly clothed, she went out to find Agatha and Nicky and found them whispering to one another where they sat on the couch.

Nicky peeled away from his mom the moment Rio entered and cleared his throat, looking happy in the Celtics jersey that was still too big for him but always so proudly worn.

“Want to play Mario Kart?”

“Like you wouldn’t believe.”

Rio settled on the floor in front of Agatha and as she raced the Rainbow Road with Nicky, she had her hair played with, Agatha’s legs draped over her shoulders and Rio’s arms locked around them.

When she lost pretty badly, she blamed Agatha for being a distraction but Agatha didn’t rise to the bait because she was sat quietly reading her book behind her, barely aware of anything other than Rio’s soft hair and the words on the page.

They played for most of the morning until lunch was brought to them and they ate on the terrace. And, when Rio noticed Agatha kept checking the time when they were finished, she reluctantly checked her watch when Nicky excused himself for the bathroom.

“I want you to take us home.”

Rio smiled a little, feeling hope creep in at the sides as she looked across at Agatha. “Really?”

“Mmhm. It’ll make Nicky feel safer and he wants to talk to you about his room.”

This made Rio grin. “Yeah?”

“Wants to know which he can have and if you can help him decorate it.”

Rio raised her brows, “Really?”

“He wants to make sure you’re happy with him calling it his own rather than-...”

“It’s his home now. I want it to be his home.”

“I know, honey. He just wants to make sure, is all.”

Rio nodded, seeing the logic in that.

“Okay, I guess then that’ll help decide which can be your room.”

She got the exact response she’d expected; a pillow in the face, ripped from the couch they sat on. It made her cackle as Agatha tackled her and they scrapped like children until tears were running down Rio’s face and both were panting heavily with Agatha pinning her arms above her head.

“I knew you needed to eat those pancakes. Tiny arms. Barely any strength at all!”

Rio laughed some more, hardly even trying to dislodge Agatha.

“Fight me,” Agatha insisted, making Rio’s grin widen so much it actually hurt now.

“You can’t be serious.”

“I’m not a delicate wallflower. Fight me.”

Rio was laughing again, laughing so much that Agatha released her wrists and went for her ribs instead, making the laughter become another cackle as she tried to bat Agatha off. Nicky rushed in, bringing the thunder with him, and he stopped in the middle of the room to watch the assault.

“Mellizo! Help! H-help me!”

But Nicky shook his head and giggled and so Rio had to help herself and managed to extricate one arm from Agatha’s hold to wrap around her waist instead.

Agatha rolled her eyes and much to Rio’s surprise she gave in by flopping down over her and rendering Rio useless because her natural instinct was to hold rather than to fight more.

Nicky was giggling still, and Rio could tell Agatha was grinning across at him, making his smile grow because his mom was so evidently happy.

“No escaping,” Rio said, moving her arms tight. “I’ve trapped her, mellizo! She cannot escape the might of Rio Vidal!”

Agatha snorted and Nicky ran over in an attempt to tug her arm off his mama. He gave up pretty quickly.

“That’s okay. I think mama would stay there forever if she could.”

“I would not.”

Rio hummed in disbelief, ignoring Agatha totally.

“I think you’re so right. Let’s talk about basketball, mellizo. Your mom can stay here and listen.”

Agatha huffed a breath against her and strained to try and push herself up.

“That’s such a good idea!” Nicky sat on the edge of the table opposite. “I heard that John Smith had a really bad season.”

“He did not,” Agatha protested suddenly, the combination of that and Nicky’s very faux-serious frown making Rio bark a laugh again and release Agatha so she could sit up above her and scowl.

“The two of you are-!” But Agatha’s admonishment was interrupted by the sound of a jaunty knock at the front door and Rio strained her head up and back to look towards it as Val let herself inside.

“Alright?” She asked casually, “I’ve been told we need to get you back.”

Rio raised her brows and looked around at Agatha who seemed to have shrunk an inch or two where she sat above her hips.

“I want to have an hour or so with you at home before you leave,” she explained quietly, looking at Rio and then turning to Nicky with a smile. “Go get your things, honey. We need to leave and then Rio has to go.”

Nicky, frowning for real now, ran off to do as he was told as Rio sat up and draped her arms lightly around Agatha. Her hand raised to brush Rio’s hair back and Rio was treated to a quick kiss before Agatha was off her and pulling Val back out onto the terrace to talk to her about what Rio was sure would be their escape plan.

She watched for a moment and then turned to traipse through to the other room to grab her precious blanket and pack it into her bag. As she folded it up and squeezed it into her trusty duffel, she caught a glimpse of something shining up at her. She reached for it and smiled as she ran her thumb along the front of the locket Agatha had gifted her weeks ago. She kissed it and then hung it around her neck, where it would be safest, and closer to her heart. By the time she was ready, Nicky was too, standing near the door with his backpack on and his frown permanently etched into his face. Scratchy was in his hand.

“Just think,” Rio said lightly as she arrived in front of him. “You’ll see the real Scratchy again soon.”

“He is very cute,” Nicky said, looking down at fake Scratchy now tucked in the strap of his bag against his side. “He loves to follow mama around and she gets so annoyed.”

Rio grinned at this. It figured that the bunny she bought for them would love Agatha, it was so easy to love her, how could it not? As the thought crossed her mind there was another, sharper knock at the door and Jen appeared suddenly, making Rio frown almost as much as Nicky.

“Still holding that grudge?” Jen asked, aiming for light but landing right in wrong.

Rio scoffed as Nicky said, “hello, auntie Jen.”

“Hey, Nicky,” she said, choosing to focus on him where she knew she’d get nothing from Rio. “Had a good time?”

“The best.”

Jen nodded and forced a smile, daring to steal a glance at Rio again as Alice appeared in the suite and smiled more readily up at her.

“Got everything?”

Rio nodded and stepped to the side when she heard Agatha and Val arrive back at their little group.

Nicky was on her toes again, which was difficult, because his spiderman backpack was bulky and in the way. So Rio had reached around and he was holding both her hands too.

“You want up?” She asked as Val opened the door for them and Agatha turned to look at them.

She saw Agatha exchange a look with Nicky, offering him a small smile and a smaller nod before he turned his head towards her and nodded too.

“Please?”

“Sure thing, mellizo.”

She moved around to offer her bag to Val, rather than to Agatha and shot her a smile before she ducked down so Nicky could get a running jump at her back. He landed with a soft “oof” and Rio laughed as she heaved him higher up and wrapped her hands securely around the backs of his knees.

“Got it?”

“Sí, mellizo. Estoy bien.”

Rio hummed, jumping him up a little more for her own comfort, and receiving a gentle touch to the cheek from Agatha for her efforts.

They followed out then, Rio coming up the rear behind Agatha, Jen, Alice, and Val with the two guards behind them. Nicky’s hold on her was easy, meaning her felt safe enough for now, but she knew if they were to be greeted by paps or anyone else, he’d soon tighten his hold and hide his face beneath his cap as best he could.

They made it to the elevator with no issue, and Rio kept Nicky on her back as they rode it down to the basement level where they were to pick up their car. No one was there to greet them, either. Alice and Jen peeled off to another car, already with a bulky looking driver. So Nicky, silent on her back, was deposited gently into the car with no fuss whatsoever.

He thanked Rio as she slipped in beside him and Agatha came round the other side to help buckle him in first and then see to her own belt.

“Easy peasy,” Nicky commented, adjusting his cap on his head as Rio smiled over him at Agatha.

“Super easy. Almost too easy.”

Agatha rolled her eyes, “Oh now you want danger?”

“No, just,” Rio shrugged and grinned, “Maybe some things to jump over or some dragons or something.”

Nicky giggled, “That’s so silly.”

“Would be cool though…”

Val jumped in the front before anyone could say anything else and turned in her seat to look at Rio. “You might wanna duck down.”

“Seriously?”

Agatha’s arm flew out to cover Nicky and hold Rio’s thigh.

“Why?”

Rio glanced to her then looked back at Val. Beside her, Nicky shifted in his seat and sought her hand to hold tightly in both of his own.

“It’s busy,” Val said, and Rio knew she was playing it down for the sake of the nervous little boy in the back with them. “Might want to hide under a blanket or something.”

Rio looked at Agatha, waiting for her assessment. When she nodded, just once, Rio wasted no time and ripped her bag open to find her horse blanket. She held it for a second like a cape high above her head and shot a reassuring smile down at Nicky before she doubled over and covered herself with it so there was just a Rio shaped lump beside Nicky. And Nick’s hand reached under to find Rio’s hand again, which she took the moment she felt it and squeezed gently.

“How’s it looking out there?” She asked after a while of the car moving through tense silence.

“It’s busy, melliza,” Nicky said softly and Rio felt him shift beside her as Agatha spoke up.

“Vultures. Trying to get a shot at us.”

Rio’s stomach lurched and she felt a hand on her back suddenly and knew it was Agatha before she said anything.

“We’re safe.”

Rio nodded where she was, and Nicky squeezed her hand tight. It was warm under the blanket, too warm. So warm that she felt sweaty and claustrophobic, but Nicky’s hand in her own and Agatha’s on her shoulder helped. She focused on them and on Nicky talking strangely loudly about what kind of yacht he hoped they’d get (“a big one with green and white sails”) helped a lot.

“Hey,” Agatha again, speaking directly to Rio now she wasn’t humouring Nicky with his maritime musings. “Come up, Rio. We’re here. No one’s followed.”

Rio lifted up immediately and Nicky giggled, telling her she looked like E.T.

Rio didn’t mind this comparison but Agatha did mind that she put on the voice the whole way into her house.

“Irritating,” Agatha muttered when Nicky was almost doubled over with laughter, his index finger pressed against Rio’s.

“There’s been a sweep already. There’s extra security cameras outside and bodies on the entrance as well as down the street. You’ll be safe as kittens.”

Rio, more interested in Nicky now, shot Val a grateful smile as Agatha asked a million questions and Rio decided it was best to take Nicky outside to play some ball. Alice and Jen were there too, hovering around like they didn’t know what to do or where to be. Rio was just grateful they didn’t follow them out to the small space that called itself a court outside.

As they were beginning their quest for infinity, she noticed the new cameras around the place but said nothing that would alert Nicky to them. By the time they were ten points closer to their goal, Agatha had joined them, and they played thirty more points until Rio called for a time out so they could do the next most important thing; choosing rooms.

Nicky may as well have had a whole bag of candy to himself. In fact, by the time he’d run around the largest guest room and pointed out all the things he could do in it, Rio asked Agatha if he’d eaten all her purple Skittles.

She got a small slap to her arm in response and Agatha said: “there’s a bag of them for you to take back with you.”

Something about Agatha saving them all for her, about Agatha still eating Skittles when she didn’t seem to be eating much of any else, helped as they were rounded up to say their goodbyes. An hour to help settle Agatha and Nicky in suddenly didn’t seem like long at all. But they were settled, and they were safe. That was all that mattered.

Rio hugged Nicky for longer than she had ever hugged him because he simply didn’t want to let go. By the time he did Rio held his cheek as he blinked away the tears in his large round eyes and she smiled sadly, promising him she’d still call every evening and in no time at all she’d be back home.

He sniffed and blushed furiously when a solitary tear fell but wouldn’t let her wipe it for him and instead turned away to do it himself. It meant she could kiss the top of his head, whisper that she loved him, and then turn before her own tears fell.

Agatha was in her arms before they could. She clung to her like she wanted inside her skin and Rio smiled into her hair, breathing her in as she whispered: “your turn to be the koala, huh?”

Agatha’s laugh was soft and welcome and she clung for almost the length of time Nicky had but managed to gather the strength to pull back to instead kiss Rio, making it last as long as she could before she whispered a quiet “I love you” and Rio whispered it back. She had to leave immediately after the words had left her lips for fear she’d never be able to and as she turned at the door and looked at Nicky standing on the tips of Agatha’s toes, she felt her heart lurch in her chest.

But the only way she could return to them is if she left first. So she did, repeating over and over in her mind that they were safe, they’d be here, they’d soon be together.

Alice, unlike when they’d first flown out, was useful this time around. She was distracting, which is exactly what Rio needed right now. They were on a commercial flight, had battered through the crowds and the paps together, and were now seated beside one another in First Class.

“Please,” Alice said to the smiling stewardess who was offering everyone wine. “She’ll have one too. As large as you can make it.”

Rio had rolled her eyes but thanked the woman all the same as she sipped her Chardonnay.

“You wanna talk about Jen?”

“No,” Rio said, cheersing Alice’s plastic cup with her own.

“Okay, how about how good a manager I am for getting the schedule moved up. You’ll be exhausted but-...”

“I’ll be home sooner,” Rio finished for her, smiling around her plastic cup. “I know. Your Christmas bonus will be huge this year.”

“Better be. Jen told me what Agatha pays her and you’ve got a lot of catching up to do.”

Rio scoffed, shooting Alice a playful glare across the rim of her cup as she took another sip of the woody wine.

They made it to Delaware without any major fallouts and without Jen’s name being brought up again. In fact, the time spent at thirty five thousand feet together had felt a lot like it used to feel with her best friend.

So when they arrived back to the hotel, when Rio had showered and was in her pyjamas, ready to do her best to have an early night before work early the next morning, everything felt good again.

By the time she woke up in the morning there was a text from an unknown but recognisable number:

I miss you. I can’t wait until you’re home again.

For the next week, Rio received a similar text every day. Not to mention, Agatha was a regular feature now in her calls to Nicky. She always gave them time alone together, always allowed them to talk about Nicky’s Spanish lessons that were continuing in the summer vacation, or whatever dinosaur nonsense they wanted to spout. But she'd always, always appear at some point and despite Rio enjoying her chats with Nicky, the highlight was always when Agatha was there.

They were still cautious with it, they still only sent one text a day, and never used the words ‘I love you’ but it was always implied, always said in the ‘I miss you’ and ‘I hope you have a good days' that they shared. And they used Val or Jen’s cell for the video calls.

But Val, and Agatha, were convinced it wouldn’t much matter, which meant they were less cautious, and Rio’s anxiety was settled again, even as exhausted and overworked as she was.

The day after she’d arrived back, after a long day on set, she had a call with her therapist, the kind Christine who listened silently to what had happened in the pool. Rio was told things like “trauma response”, and, “the mind can’t comprehend the fear you’ve been experiencing and so made its own narrative to try and reckon with it”. It was a rough hour, filled with tears, but it helped.

A second text from Agatha waiting for her after she’d done helped even more: I’m so proud of you. Your koala x

Rio didn’t know how she knew but the most obvious answer was Alice. So that must have been the correct one.

It was two days after her call to Christine that Rio had come up with a new way to interact with Agatha, in the afternoon after an early morning shoot when she’d been done up by her hair and makeup team and dressed by her stylist in a grey knitted, figure-hugging skirt and an open matching cardigan with a black bralet beneath.

She looked hot, and that was mostly the reason the idea had sparked.

“Please.”

“Your big brown eyes don’t work on me, lady.” Alice pointed at her accusingly, raising her brows. “None of that.”

“Please,” Rio tried again, going for the Agatha classic of a pout too.

“No. You need to concentrate on the interview.”

“I can only concentrate if I can message her. Please.”

Alice began to mutter soft curses under her breath and Rio knew she was giving in. She pushed the pout out a little more and fluttered her eyelashes for good measure. Sure enough, Rio soon had Alice’s phone in her hand and the ability to contact Agatha unencumbered was secured.

She opened Alice’s text conversations with her, knowing Alice’s password was Jen’s birthday, and saw that Agatha was curt with Alice but that Alice was fawning over Agatha.

“Actually,” Rio said, reading a message from about a month ago that read: Hey, Agatha. It’s Alice. Was wondering whether you could mention Rio in your next interview? Would be super duper cool if you did. Hope you’re well. Give my love to Nicky. Agatha hadn’t responded.

“Will you call Jen? Get her to give Agatha her phone?” She looked up at her best friend and smiled hopefully at her.

“Why?” Alice did not smile hopefully back.

“Well… otherwise it might look like you’re trying to get into Agatha Harkness’s-…”

“Yuck! Stop! Gimme that!”

Alice snatched the phone from Rio’s outstretched hand and Rio laughed as she walked away to check herself over in the mirror again. Her watch told her she had ten minutes but all she needed to do now was to get Agatha’s attention, to make sure she had Jen’s phone, and to make sure she looked good on camera.

She fluffed her hair and checked herself out. That last one was fine. She’d look great on camera.

Taking her seat in front of the set up for the interview with Variety on Snow she looked up at the ring light that had been positioned just so to make Rio look effortlessly glam - despite the fact it had taken three people and two hours to get her to look this way.

But whatever, she thought, taking a quick sip of iced coffee with just a pinch of thc in it, she didn’t care how long it had taken or the amount of lights aimed her way, she’d soon be staring at Agatha on the screen, and Agatha would be staring at her.

“Here,” Alice said over her shoulder, handing back her cell. “She agreed. But don’t be too gross, okay? And when you’re done please delete all the messages. I need you to focus in. This is the start of it, Rio. If this goes well, we could be talking another nomination. We could be talking another win.”

“Yeah yeah,” Rio agreed absently, already tapping a message to Agatha.

Rio: Hey it’s me 😀

Alice sighed beside her, framed in the screen of the open laptop that was set to the Teams screen. “This is serious, Rio, please. Just… try to listen enough to at least answer your questions, okay? And no jerking it on camera!”

Rio actually laughed at that and swatted Alice away. She avoided her hand and disappeared into the bathroom so she’d be nearby enough to hear but wouldn’t disturb the actual interview that was the first of many ahead of the movie’s big release.

It was a quick and tight turnaround but Stark, and his studio, was determined to get the movie out for Christmas and get as much buzz around it beforehand as possible. After all, this was his big ensemble feature. Lilia Calderu and Agatha Harkness were big enough draws but adding Peter Quill and Rio Vidal meant the whole thing could go stratospheric if they played it right.

Not to mention the Awards buzz already floating around it.

The criticswere yet to see anything and were already foaming at the mouth to get to it. Besides, Alice had been whispering in her ear every chance she got about the talk around the movie, which meant Rio would be pushed to the front of every interview Alice could get her in on.

Like this one, for instance, a whole cast interview with one poor journalist who hadn’t seen the unfinished movie and who was going to have to do their best to make each huge Hollywood star shine.

Not that Rio cared. She’d be more interested in pinning Agatha’s video to her screen to see her up close and text her the whole way through. She didn’t often get an opportunity to flirt with her and she missed being able to.

Agatha: I hope this is Rio.

Rio: Yes 🤠

Agatha: Tell me how many freckles I have on my nose.

Rio: You don’t trust me?

Agatha: How many?

Rio: Four. And four on your left tit too.

Agatha: Las chicas miss you.

Rio almost dropped Alice’s phone as the noise of the call started and her mouth went dry. Alice, from the bathroom, shouted through: “Answer it!”

And Rio did, reluctantly, having to momentarily pause her flirting with Agatha to grin for the journalist as all the cast slowly filtered into the call. And there, last but definitely not least, was Agatha. And Rio watched as her mouth fell open in her little video box.

Agatha was in a blue man’s dress shirt and oversized glasses. Her hair looked disheveled in the best way, as if Rio had just been around and had done unspeakable things to her to make it so.

Agatha:: Are you drooling over there?

Rio jumped, already annoyed she wasn’t playing it cool as she quickly went to pin Agatha’s video and enlarge it for herself. She couldn’t look away. Alice’s phone vibrated again.

Agatha: Like the shirt?

Rio’s eyes darted down to read it but she tried her best to look like she was just adjusting herself and quickly tapped her response.

Rio: would look better on my floor

She saw Agatha’s cheeks flush slightly on the screen and grinned to herself, sticking her tongue in her cheek as she tried to calm it. The host was now done explaining how this would go - an hour of “casual” questions about the movie, their characters, their hopes for it and then they’d be done. It sounded incredibly boring but Rio knew she’d be the most entertained person here.

Agatha was asked the first question and Rio sat and watched her answer it, for a while enjoying how smart and eloquent her girlfriend was but soon growing bored with what she knew was mostly lies from her gorgeous mouth.

She started to fidget where she sat and soon enough noticed that Agatha’s eyes were focused on one specific part of her screen and realised that Agatha mustn’t have pinned her. So she’d be small, she thought, which meant she needed to move so Agatha could enjoy more of her.

She sat up more, stretching her arms above her head to give Agatha a view of her bralet and her abs. Agatha stuttered briefly and as Rio smirked she cleared her throat. She then twisted, acting as if she was just twitching or getting a kink out or something but really she was trying to show herself off from every angle. She threw her hair back a few times, exposed her neck, she let her cardigan fall off her shoulder and slowly picked it back up.

In short, she did everything she could to throw Agatha off her game and if the slight pauses and soft throat clearings meant anything at all, then she knew it was working.

The interviewer soon moved to Lilia and Agatha was able to go silent again, pretending, like the rest of them, to listen.

Rio: wish you were under this desk rn

Agatha: You do?

Rio: yes very much

Agatha: What would I be doing under your desk?

Rio: 👅

Agatha: What is that?

Rio: ur not v good at sextjng

Agatha: And you aren’t very good at spelling.

Rio looked up at the screen and had to bite her tongue because Agatha’s gaze was down on her phone as if she were waiting for Rio to text back and she’d forgotten she was on a live interview.

She glanced at her phone, and, eyes up again, she tapped out:

Rio: eyes up babe

Agatha looked up the moment the message came through and Rio could see the flex of her jaw and the flash of annoyance that made Rio grin stupidly at the screen.

Agatha didn’t text back for a while but Rio was watching her and every ten seconds she’d purse her lips and glance down at her phone.

Agatha Harkness was anything other than subtle.

And subtlety went completely out the window when Agatha’s left hand was suddenly visible on the screen as she answered a question randomly thrown her way about characterisation. Rio wasn’t much interested in her answer. She was more interested in the fact that Agatha was removing her ring and placing it on the side, briefly wriggling her ring-free fingers and then pulling her hand off screen again.

Rio arched a brow and caught her smirk in response.

Rio: put it back on

Agatha didn’t respond but Rio saw that she’d looked at her phone so she knew she’d read it.

“Rio?” Her name jolted her back to life and she smiled because she had been media trained and because Alice would kill her otherwise.

“Obviously your beloved father died during filming. How do you think that impacted your performance?”

Rio could feel the colour drain from her face. Alice had warned her about this, though she’d said she’d made sure the studio and every media outlet knew her dad was off limits. Though clearly, they’d decided that rule didn’t extend to live interviews that couldn’t be edited. So Rio was caught. Caught between her dad and the screen before her where all she could see was Agatha’s furious face and the ring she was now picking up and placing back on her finger for all to see.

“I think we can skip that question, don’t you?” She said before Rio could even form a coherent response in her mind.

“Apologies,” the interviewer said quickly, clearly taken aback that Agatha had answered for Rio, “I only meant-...”

“It’s fine,” Rio said softly, regaining her voice just in time. “All I know is that I got through that time with the support of my cast.” Alice would be so proud. “Agatha in particular was there for me in ways I can’t even explain.” Agatha’s face softened and she tugged her lower lip between her teeth. “This movie is a testament to her power as an actress and her compassion as a human. Even now she’s supporting me through it and I-...” her voice cracked without her meaning it to and Agatha twitched as if she wanted to reach through the screen to her. “When you see the movie, you’ll understand. It’s an ensemble piece but Agatha is the heart of it.”

They moved on, the interviewer avoiding Rio as much as possible, apparently for fear Agatha would snap at her again. But Rio didn’t move on, and Agatha didn’t either.

Five minutes after her speech, five minutes spent watching Agatha continually glance down at her phone, she received a text.

Agatha: My heart is yours.

Rio smiled at the screen after reading it, and caught Agatha smiling back at her. She knew it wasn’t technically possible that they were making eye contact but it felt that way anyway.

She’d wanted to flirt, to tease, to distract, but instead she’d somehow fallen deeper into her love for Agatha and had experienced her in a way she had never really had the chance to before. Because this was Agatha openly defending her to the world. And this was Rio being able to do exactly the same right back.

The call ended soon enough, with Rio’s mind half on her dad and half on Agatha. When she took her last look at her girlfriend and closed the laptop, Alice appeared in the room.

“I’m so fucking sorry, Rio. Are you okay? I’ve fucking told them-!”

“It’s fine,” Rio reassured softly, seeing Alice’s phone already lighting up with Jen’s name and face. “Did you hear?”

“Yeah. I heard Agatha jump in and you pivoted so well but it shouldn’t have…” Alice shook her head and motioned for Rio to answer the call.

“Hey,” she said, knowing it was Agatha.

“Are you okay?”

“I’m fine. Wished I could have flirted a little bit more but…”

“I saw you flexing and showing off. Saw you trying to distract me when I was trying to answer.”

Rio grinned, “I heard you stutter.”

“Jen wants to speak to Alice,” Agatha said, her way of not confirming or denying that she did indeed stutter. “And I want you to send me pictures of you later, okay?”

“Only if you do too.”

Agatha scoffed but Rio knew she would.

“I love you.” And she was gone.

Rio handed the cell back to Alice and Alice swooped in to kiss her cheek in an act of further apology that Rio didn’t need. She had only a few hours before she was needed back on set so she went to do as she’d been asked and sent pictures to Agatha that weren’t too risque but just risque enough that they could still be explained if found.

Agatha sent some right back and Rio made one of them her knew contact photo; Agatha with the arm of her glasses in her mouth, her lip tugged down with them, her blue eyes bright and hair that messy way she loved.

She stared at it for longer than she meant to and fell asleep in her makeup and fancy outfit and woke to her alarm and Alice in the room with her again, softly shaking her with a coffee in her hand.

And that was how it was for a few more days. Alarms, coffee, falling into bed, calls with Nicky. Monotonous, but time would move anyway, no matter how Rio spent it.

The shoot was exhausting but the cast and crew knew they were making something good. Which made it easier to put up with the gruelling schedule and the lack of sleep.

Still, Rio was grumpy that people still wanted to talk to her, even if she had nothing new or exciting to say because no one really wanted to hear about all the new words Nicky had learnt and no one wanted to see her latest origami creation, a lotus flower that could start closed and be opened if you pulled the right petal.

Four nights after the disaster interview, Rio was woken at an ungodly hour. She grumbled, annoyed that Alice was waking her up already. She had two more hours before her alarm, what the fuck could Alice want.

She scrambled from her bed, throwing her duvet to the end of it and groaning as she thumped her way to the door.

Ripping it open she growled: “What?!” Her breath caught as she looked up. “Oh. Mom.”

Rio’s heart constricted in her chest and even as Anna moved in to hug her she felt like she couldn’t breathe.

“Come in,” she said weakly, stepping back to let her do just that. “I thought you were Alice.”

But Alice always just let herself in. She should have known. She should have prepared herself in those few steps it took to get to the door.

Rio ushered her mom in, seeing that it was only three in the morning. She stumbled over her words but offered her a coffee she refused and soon stood awkwardly as her mom perched on the side of her messy bed and ran her fingers over the soft fabric of the horse blanket that was a permanent feature of the room now.

“Me entero de que Nicky lo sabe.” I hear Nicky knows.

“Sí, mamá.”

“Y ella va a ganar.” And she’s going to win.

Rio nodded slowly, unsure why she felt nervous all of a sudden. But her mom visiting her without warning, without even telling Alice, was so unusual, it couldn’t have meant anything good.

“Mamá,” Rio asked carefully, swallowing where she stood opposite her, “who died?”

Anna’s brown eyes widened and for a moment Rio thought she’d got her. She thought she’d figured it out and Anna was about to reveal the name of the next person Rio would have to mourn: Mateo, Aunt Elena, any of her little cousins.

“Nobody, mija. Nobody died.”

Anna came forwards and cupped Rio’s cheek, brushing her thumb over it tenderly as Rio’s mind ran away from the tenderness.

“You’re sick,” she said quietly, a forgone conclusion to a traumatised heart.

“No, mija.”

Rio swallowed because what was she to believe? Her mom had turned up unannounced and no one was dying? No one was about to be taken away from her?

“I came,” Anna said quietly, in her less preferred language, “to give you something.”

Rio frowned more deeply than before, watching as her mom reached into her front pocket to produce something she hadn’t expected.

It was a ring, her abuela’s ring. A ring Rio had grown up seeing sitting in her mom’s jewellery box, a ring she knew her mom treasured above even her own engagement ring. A plain gold band with a small stone cut of a gem that sometimes looked purple and sometimes green. Her mom had once told her it was alexandrite. She’d remembered the name because her abuela’s name had been Alejandra and it was close enough for Rio to draw the mental connecting thread.

“For Agatha. From you, and from our family. She has been nervous this last week, actually, every day I speak to her. Everyday she asks if she will be accepted by me and everyday I have to reassure her that she already is.”

From death to life again, Rio’s brain could barely keep up. But her eyes had already filled with tears and the image of the ring sitting in the palm of her mom’s hand swam before her.

“Are you ready, mija? Ready to take on that boy as your own?”

It was so unusual for her mom to be speaking in English to her for more than a couple sentences at a time. Her dad had always laughed with her about it; Anna’s insistence that Rio improve her Spanish, so her insistence she speak with her in her mother tongue.

But now, now Rio knew Anna was using English because she wanted to make sure she was understood. And because Rio’s brain had more to think about than the meaning of words she’d known when she was younger but had forgotten through her own laziness with the language.

“I think so,” Rio admitted, her voice small as she picked the ring from her mom’s palm.

“You need to know so,” Anna said, her voice gentle still. “You need to know you are ready. Or I will take the ring back and not allow you to make a promise you are not sure you can keep.”

“No,” Rio said quickly, slipping the ring down to her first knuckle of her wedding finger. She closed her fist and protected it with her other hand as she raised her gaze to her mom. “I am ready. I’m ready for it all. I-...”

“Love them,” Anna concluded for her, holding Rio’s face up with a knowing smile. “I know. You get that same look in your eyes that your papa did when he looked at us.”

Rio’s heart broke in her chest and Anna seemed to know because she’d pulled her in for a hug before she could even feel it properly.

“He saw it in you before I did. He saw it in Agatha too. You are so alike and I miss him so much.”

Rio sobbed into her mom’s shirt, her hold on the ring tightening as she gripped at her mom as well, dissolving in her arms in a way she hadn’t done in a very long time. Anna held her through it, stroking her hair and whispering softly to her that it would be okay, that she was there, that she loved her and her papa loved her too.

Anna stayed over that night and Rio placed the ring on the chain of her locket, keeping it close to her heart, where she knew it would be safe. Alice was allowed into their little family night and more tears were shed by her than by anyone.

And Rio, not for the first time, realised that the loss of Miguel was felt by more than just her blood relatives. He was Alice’s dad too.

They all shared the same bed that night, Rio in the middle, too hot to sleep and too focused on thoughts of Agatha, of her reaction to a ring, of how much her mom loved her to come all this way and deliver something so precious to her.

By midday Anna was gone again and Rio felt her loss more acutely than ever before. Time with her mom felt sacred now because she knew how fleeting it was. She cried without meaning to in her trailer with thoughts of one day having to mourn her mom too plaguing her as Alice held her hand and rubbed her back.

She called her therapist to talk about it, to discuss why death felt so close when her future was now hanging from a delicate chain around her neck. And it helped. It helped to speak to someone who didn’t love her. Because Christine wasn’t biased, and she was able to listen without reacting in a way she thought Rio would want her to react.

So her grief wasn’t cured but it was soothed and a few days passed where Rio was able to call Agatha and Nicky every evening. And everything was okay. Everything was normal, everything was just as it was.

Until, a Friday afternoon when Rio had just finished on set and was gathering her things from her trailer to head home, her phone went and Agatha’s number lit up the screen.

“I need you to come h-home,” Agatha’s voice cracked. And the next thing she said made Rio drop her phone.
