Agatha felt sick.

The moon was up in the sky already, distant but there. It felt strange to see it when all anyone could talk about was how hot it was, what a beautiful summer’s day it was, and how lucky Agatha was.

She stared up at it, and wished she could reach out to it and hold it in the palm of her hand. What power it had, the power of all life. Her ability to control the tides but to forever watch, never thought of anything other than a silent constant to be looked at.

There was a quote she couldn’t remember. Something on the tip of her tongue, encouraged by the pale beauty in the sky. Dickinson? The moon was but a Chin of Gold? No. Shelley? Art thou pale of weariness/Of climbing heaven and gazing on earth? No. Though Shelley’s melancholy felt more fitting than Dickinson’s awe.

She turned from the lonely wanderer and wandered herself down to the beginnings of the party where people were milling about on the ground floor and terrace of the house her mother owned.

The place was palatial but soulless and Agatha had spent many a warm summer here passively wondering about throwing herself from the cliffs. She’d vowed from an early age that wherever she lived as an adult would be warm and welcoming, a sanctuary. She would build a home book by book and have furnishings soft enough to sleep in, colours that soothed rather than startled, and music, always music playing.

Ella, Toni, Billie, and Freddie and Dolly on good days.

She would rather live in a happy shack than a miserable mansion.

“There you are!” Ralph’s booming voice made Agatha fight off a shiver and soon his lips were pressed to her own and instead the shiver became a grimace, truthfully meant and quickly hidden.

“My dear future wife!”

Agatha fixed the mask of pleasure on her face as she was dragged from the confines of the house to the confines of the estate. Here she was greeted and gushed over. Here she showed off her new ring. Here she thought again about how many steps it was to the cliffs.

Now fifty.

Now forty.

Now twenty.

So close. So close. So close.

Agatha felt hot all over. Not warmed by her fiancé’s touch but smothered by it. Ralph’s hand was warm and large and firm against her body. He was so demanding, so insistent that she always be held by him. It felt suffocating.

She saw other couples, other women in couples, happily clinging to or being held against their partners, and she never understood how they could act through it.

Surely, even if she were attracted to Ralph, she wouldn’t want his hot and heavy hand on her all the time. It was demeaning, an affront to feminism. No woman should need to be held by another to feel whole and safe.

In spite of what she knew was best, inspite of the appearances she knew she must keep up, she pushed his hand away from her hip and it fell when she did. She took a breath, felt like she could actually breathe again. And then it was back. This time on her lower back, still hot and large and heavy.

She wanted to scream.

“Hey,” Jen touched her arm and Agatha flinched away, earning an unamused scowl from her friend. “What’s up with you? So happy you’ve looped around to bitch?”

“Well hey, that’s my wife you’re talking about,” Ralph interjected, magnanimous in his attention as he turned from whoever the hell he’d been talking to in a dark suit. “Only I can call her a bitch.”

Agatha almost flinched again as she saw Jen’s face screw up in disgust.

“Excuse us,” she said quickly, not bothering to look back as she dragged Jen away before she had the chance to say anything to her dear, beloved fiancé.

“He’s had a couple drinks,” she uttered dismissively when she caught Jen staring at her as they arrived at the bar.

“We’ll make sure he doesn’t talk to anyone important, then.”

Agatha hummed, accepting a glass of champagne as she turned to see Ralph talking to that Thanos guy her mother had invited. He was aiming for a job at his firm, its all he had been talking about the last couple weeks.

“You’re happy though?”

Agatha raised her brows and glanced at Jen, taking a small sip of champagne as she did.

“Why wouldn’t I be? Huge rock on my finger, handsome guy on my arm, more nominations and awards than I can count… what’s not to be happy about?”

Jen eyed her for a moment and Agatha felt uneasy again. But the moment was fleeting and Jen soon smiled, rolling her eyes at herself. “You’re right. I won’t ask again.”

Agatha turned from Jen and steeled herself. Jen couldn’t know. No one could. She had to be a closed book, a locked box. This was her life. She was happy. She’d soon be happily married.

“First comes love,” Jen sang by her ear, after a while of Agatha observing her kingdom, “then comes marriage,” she moved closer and clinked their glasses, “you’ll be off that soon enough. Because next is a baby. We’ll have to talk about timings for it, obviously. Can’t have a kid at your stage of career but… I’m sure we could squeeze one in for you. Give your husband his blonde, blue eyed boy.”

Agatha swallowed, imagining a little boy that would grow up to look like and be like Ralph. She could think of nothing worse.

“I hope he has his eyes,” she lied, taking a quick sip to hide any falter in her face or voice.

“Super cute,” Jen said absently, checking her cell quickly as some more well-wishers descended.

Agatha went into work mode, and so did Jen. Though it was soon clear that these people had no power in the movie business and instead were hangers on from some business dealings Ralph was working on.

They were boring people asking boring questions and Agatha soon switched to a different part of herself, the part that was able to function like a normal human but be thinking of different things altogether. Over the taller woman’s shoulder was the thing now that caught her attention: the moon.

It was still out, still silently watching over the little party in the backyard of a Cape mansion. And Agatha remembered suddenly what she’d forgotten earlier as she laughed at some joke she didn’t find funny at all.

“Just say the word and I’ll throw a lasso around it and pull it down”. A kind of romance she’d never experience. Ralph would never lasso the moon for her; she wouldn’t even want him to.

As she laughed and smiled at these women before her she felt the clenching of her heart in her chest.

Was the moon too much to ask for? Was wanting someone to pull it down for her too much? She looked at the women she was humouring, and knew the answer.

Yes. Too much. Never allowed.

She forgot about the moon. Or, maybe, she chose to not think about it. Instead she thought about how sad these people were that they were fawning over her. She thought about how ugly their dresses were and how much she hated her fiancé.

She could see him now, grinning his big grin and laughing that booming laugh he thought was boyish and charming. But it wasn’t. It was irritating and sycophantic.

She hated him. She hated him. She hated him.

“Darling,” Agatha turned, momentarily forgetting herself and grinning when she did. But it wasn’t anyone she needed to waste her grins on.

“Mother.”

“Keep that smile up, Agatha. You know how it saddens me when you look less than your full potential.”

Agatha cleared her throat and instead of smiling she took a sip of champagne, turning back to the party.

“You know, I’ve been watching you all afternoon.”

Agatha said nothing, her eyes drifting back off to the moon still visible in the pink sky even though she’d just decided to forget about its presence.

It felt impossible that it was still there, this mysterious, far-off thing. She shivered in the warm air as she thought of the person that might offer to snare it for her; a woman with soft skin and eyes just for her.

But, no. She had to lock that thought away too.

“You should look friendlier. I’ve always said so. You can charm when you want to but you so seldom want to, Agatha. You must be better.”

Agatha nodded just once, barely able to glance around at her mother before she went to do her bidding. She turned the charm up as she swanned about the place, a picture of elegance.

But as the sun set, the crowd swelled and closed in. And Agatha shivered again though it wasn’t yet cold.

“Here, my beautiful bride,” Ralph’s voice hit her a second after his jacket did, thrown as it was over her shoulders.

She did her best not to flinch or grimace as his arm wrapped around her and once again wondered how she would deal with this for a lifetime. It was only in public, she reminded herself. But she was a public person now, a person people would expect to see with her loving husband and their 2.4 blonde babies. Sons, if she could possibly manage it.

The white picket fence was closing in and Agatha was trapped behind it.

She could withstand it for only so long. Ralph’s hand was heavy and hot again. It had traveled below his jacket that hung like a noose around her. He was holding her hip, then her waist, then his hand was on her ass. And she could do nothing. She had no power.

It happened until suddenly it didn’t. She had ripped herself away under the pretense of going to the ladies’ room.

Several people tried to stop her as she marched away; congratulations were thrown at her from every angle. Agatha smiled for them, she nodded and acknowledged them but she never stopped.

She needed a second, needed some time to breathe away from the crowds, from her mother, from her future as Ralph’s wife.

Upstairs in the safety and solitude of one of the many bathrooms, she spilled her fear and hatred into the toilet. It happened without encouragement. Agatha’s body simply rejected the promise of a life it did not want.

When she was done, when there was nothing left to give, she collapsed back against the side of the tub and looked up helplessly to the darkening sky.

There she was, brighter now, illuminated by the darkness around her. Agatha, weary and exhausted, smiled because she was still there.

The moon, distantly beautiful, ready for the taking. She might laugh if someone actually offered to pull it down for her. She might cry if someone thought her worthy of it.

She turned away from the heavens. She stood slowly then brushed her teeth. Her smile was gone as she stepped out of the bathroom.

In the garden it returned. She smiled so brightly when Ralph had his hand on her again and she tried not to look at the moon. Who would lasso it for her anyway?

 

——

 

The sun was still up as Rio ran to find Alice. She could barely breathe as she slammed her fist into the white wood of her room door. Nothing was quick enough, she wasn’t moving fast enough.

She broke the news to her best friend as her bodyguard appeared behind her. Maybe he’d heard the banging. Maybe Agatha had contacted him.

Her words tumbled out as Alice stared at her and she felt Thor move closer. Everything was a rush. Even as Alice pushed her down the hall, even as Thor followed them out, she couldn’t breathe, couldn’t think, couldn’t believe.

They made it to the car, then the plane. No one had brought anything. They were just there in their sweats and old shirts, unprepared, totally unprepared.

“I should have known. I should have been ready.”

“You couldn’t have been. You couldn’t have been.”

The conversation went round and round; always the same thing, always the same response. Rio never heard it though. All she could hear was Agatha’s voice. It had been so shaky, so unsure, and Rio knew she needed to get to her as quickly as possible to make her sure.

If only she’d been ready. If only she’d not taken this job. If only she’d funded the production of it to hire a new actress so she could have been with Agatha this whole time.

And Nicky. How was Nicky. Where was Nicky.

She couldn’t breathe again and rather than offering champagne this time, Alice was instead offering water, encouraging small sips as the Private Jet took off for Los Angeles.

It was a miracle they were even in the air now. Alice had done the negotiating when they’d arrived at the terminal. She’d got them a plane, she’d just not been able to haggle the cost down. But Rio didn’t care about that right now. She’d have given all her money to get to where she needed to be.

She’d give anything to have Agatha in her arms now. Agatha had asked for her and Rio hated that she even had to.

“Is Jen with her?”

“I don’t know. I can’t get a hold of her.”

It was pointless now. They were in the air and there was only so much plane wifi could do.

Rio’s phone was on the table before her. She kept tapping the screen and every time she did the strange blurs of a precious picture lit it up. It was the picture her mom had taken of the three of them wrapped up together on the couch when Rio had returned from hospital that night.

It was a bad picture, they were barely discernible in it, but it captured her whole world.

Her phone background, when she was single, had been a sunset taken when she’d been on a run. Then it became a picture stolen from a photoshoot; Agatha in a red dress, her legs spread where she sat tall and dominant in the frame, her hand in her hair and her eyes piercing. But now, now when it was so much more than sex and the thrill of an affair, it was a picture of her family.

Tres patitos, all blended together in a blur of captured love.

She tapped it again the second the screen faded to black. What if this was the last heirloom of their time together?

Again. The screen flickered on and the more Rio stared the more she could make details out. Nicky’s little button on his nose, just like her own. Agatha’s hand, curled around her, pale and strong in its hold. Rio’s own, softly assured face; because she had them, they were always safe when she had them in her arms.

And for so long she’d had to let them go. For so long she’d been swimming around waiting to be allowed back to them. For so long they’d been unsafe and unsure and she’d not been able to do anything about it.

She turned from her phone and looked out at the night sky.

It was a strangely moonless night though there was a strange glow in the air from somewhere. Reflections of stars, the whites of clouds, she didn’t know. The air looked and felt different somehow.

Maybe she was just exhausted. Maybe it was the adrenaline. Maybe it was the fear that she’d misheard Agatha.

Maybe it was that she was about to arrive from the sky and she had no way of bringing the moon with her.

Her hand moved to her chest and curled around the chain that hung there, and there it remained for the rest of the flight; she looked between the sky and her world, lighting up her phone with every touch.

Alice could barely get a word out of her the rest of the way to her house, even though Rio knew how hard she was trying.

“I’ll drop you off then go straight to Jen’s, okay? And you call me if you need me. I mean it, babe. Anything at all. Even if you get a papercut or-...”

“Alice,” Rio said, her voice a little hoarse from not being used for a few hours as she turned in the back of the blacked out SUV to look at her friend. “I promise I’ll call.”

Alice nodded, her lips pursed together in a thin line. She looked tired, Rio realised sadly. She’d been up at every call time with Rio these past few weeks. She’d been working as much as she had, worrying as much as she had, she’d been missing Jen as much as she’d been missing Agatha.

“I love you,” Rio said suddenly, offering her hand out to her best friend who took it immediately.

And for a moment it was just them. The two of them as they once had been; stupid, goofy, carefree. They grinned at each other even as Alice’s eyes filled with tears and she squeezed Rio’s hand so tight Rio wondered if she’d been waiting to do this for a while.

“Go get her.”

Rio nodded, she kissed the hand that held her own so tightly and as she released it and stepped out the car, Alice’s voice sounded again.

“Rio!”

Rio looked around, the door halfway to being closed.

“Your dad would be so proud.”

Rio’s heart jumped to her throat and as she closed the door she heard Alice’s gentle, “I love you” before it shut. She could no longer see her friend with the damp cheeks and soft smile and instead saw herself reflected in the dark glass.

Her hair, growing now it was allowed to, was messy and full of static from the flight and the amount of fidgeting with it she’d done. Her lips were swollen from being chewed; her cheeks pink from fear; her eyes wide with expectation.

She turned from herself and heard Alice drive off as she looked up at her home. It looked the same as it always had. Maybe those flowers in the little window box were new. They had green petals and Rio’s heart told her they’d probably have been picked by Nicky and planted by Agatha.

Because it was her house now too. It was their home.

Maybe not forever, but for now.

Rio took a breath as she raised her gaze from the new blooms to the rest of the house. All was dark from the outside, apart from a strange glow in the first window on the right. It was eerily similar to the view from the plane window.

Maybe she was imagining it, though. Maybe it was her belief that Agatha was her sun creeping into her dark, moonlit night.

The door felt heavy as she pushed it open and for a moment she was surprised she didn’t need her key. She thought back to a time where Agatha had snuck in the very same way because it had been Rio who had neglected to lock the door behind her.

Their roles were reversed now. It was Rio who had come to seek Agatha.

There was a small, white candle on the small console table beneath a curved mirror in the hall. Its flame flickered with the gust of Rio entering its domain and Rio watched it dance for her as she closed the heavy door behind her.

Instinctually, because safety meant everything to her after so many months of uncertainty, she turned the lock and felt the heavy mechanism click beneath her hand.

The house was silent, which was so unusual now. Because this house now homed Agatha, who talked and talked when she was comfortable and she was endlessly comfortable here. And Nicky. Nicky who brought the thunder wherever he went, who giggled so much lately it was if he only stopped giggling to pause for breath. And the music. The music that was always now playing whenever Rio called because Nicky liked to dance with his mama and he loved to dance with his melliza.

But she couldn’t hear any of that. She took a step further inside, her fingers sliding from their hold on the metal of the lock to the wood of the door.

And then she was unmoored, floating towards a light emanating from the archway that led to her living room.

Inside it was the source of the light; her sun, surrounded by so many candles their flickering flames became a circle of warming fire with Agatha at their heart.

“I don’t want to wait any longer,” Agatha breathed, visibly trembling where she knelt on both knees holding a small, open velvet box in her pale hands.

“I… I couldn’t… I need to be… y-yours,” Agatha offered by way of explanation, when Rio’s body hadn’t moved from her position by the door and Agatha’s continued to tremble all over.

If Rio had been able to look anywhere but at Agatha she’d have been able to count almost a hundred candles, all lit by the shaking hand that held out an open ring box containing a singular, custom, diamond ring.

“I,” Agatha said, inhaling sharply on the one syllable. “I have Nicky now, now all I need is you to… to make our f-family.”

The first tear fell as Rio took her first step.

“Please be mine, I… I don’t want you a-anymore I n-need you… I…”

Agatha had made a high-pitched choking sound that had made Rio burst through the flames and fall before her. And finally, ring box dropped and forgotten on the floor, Rio had her in her arms again.

She was safe. Agatha was safe. Rio hadn’t misheard her.

The sobs were thick and fast against the home Agatha had made in the crook of Rio’s neck and her nails were sharp and desperate as she clutched and clawed at her as if it were possible, finally, to climb into Rio’s skin and make a home for herself there too.

But the feel of Agatha desperately gripping her, the sound of her heaving sobs, none of it was as painful as the weeks and months spent apart.

Rio was crying now, but her tears were silent votaries at the altar of Agatha Harkness. They slipped from her blinking eyes and landed in dark hair as Agatha’s ragged breathing slowly began to soften and her clutching became instead grasping.

Rio swallowed thickly, and Agatha seemed to know she needed to relax around her so she dropped her legs down onto the bed and loosened the hold around her waist.

“Can I ask him?” She whispered hoarsely, “Before we tell him… I… can I ask him if he’s okay with us getting married?”

Agatha shifted a little, moving her hand along her side, “You know he’d love us to.”

“I know I just… I want to include him.”

“How very traditional of you, Miss Vidal.”

Rio smiled a little as she stared up at the ceiling and tried to say something but all thoughts went out of her head as Agatha’s fingers slipped down to press against her lower lip and request entrance to her mouth.

“Maybe…” she mused, pushing her fingers past Rio’s teeth, “maybe one more. And then I’ll let you sleep.”

That last part meant it most definitely wasn’t a request. But Agatha’s soft demand only made Rio smile. And as she reached down between them and Agatha scratched along her back, she soon made her demanding fiancée groan as she fingered her slowly, doing her best to not overstimulate her on an already overwhelming night.

Agatha, as quick to come as she was to ask for it, came slowly this time around. Rio wouldn’t let it happen any other way. And when she did she captured the last of her panting breaths against her tongue, sliding it slowly into Agatha’s mouth.

When they eventually settled, Agatha’s sweater practically useless against whatever chill Rio was afraid of Agatha catching as Rio had pushed it all the way up to feel as much of Agatha’s skin against her own as possible, it was Agatha who drifted first.

Rio fought sleep for a long while because holding Agatha was better. To the side was the little flower Nicky had left for her, with the expectation that she’d be home soon and find it. And Rio, as she drifted, though about home and what it now meant.

For years home had been wherever she’d lay her head. It was always still Delaware, of course. Always where her family was. But now, on the other side of the country, in a house she’d bought with her first real paycheck, it was here, beneath the woman she was to marry, tangled in her love.

She slept for all of two hours before she heard a noise on the lower floor of the house. The front door had opened and then closed and Rio frowned into the darkness because, even in her bleary state, she knew she’d locked it.

Her family was too precious for her to not lock doors.

So she blinked towards the door in the mottled light of the candle-lit room and felt Agatha shift against her, breathing out heavily into her neck.

“Don’t let her take you from me,” she murmured, her lips tickling Rio’s skin enough to set her body on fire again.

“I have to go,” Rio breathed out, her whole body telling her not to, because she tightened her hold on Agatha even as she said it.

“I’ll pay the studio to replace you. Stay with me.”

Rio swallowed because how could she refuse the woman she’d just asked to marry her. How could she let go of her, put her clothes back on, and just walk away? But Agatha was shifting now, Agatha could feel the indecision in Rio’s very bones, and so she pushed up and blinked sleepily down at her worried face.

“Go,” she whispered, raising a warm hand to touch Rio’s cheek. “And we’ll be right behind you. I’ll fetch Nicky and… we’ll make a home for a while in Arkansas. I’m free to do what I want now and what I want is to follow you.”

Rio’s mind was reeling from Agatha’s insistence that she stay and now her reassurance that she could go. And Alice now knocking gently on the bedroom door didn’t help matters.

“Have you ever been to Arkansas before?”

“Never,” Agatha whispered, both of them ignoring the next gentle knock and soft call of Rio’s name.

“There’s a dinosaur park I could take you to.”

Agatha smiled, leaning in to press it to Rio’s hopeful one.

“Get dressed, the quicker you leave the quicker we can be together again.”

Rio, for all she was in favour of slow because slow meant more Agatha, moved as quickly as she was able. She rolled them, she kissed Agatha, she kissed her again, and then again, until Agatha was cackling and pushing her away as best she could.

So Rio got changed, aware of the woman sitting propped up against the cushions with her legs open wide and her gaze on Rio’s slowly disappearing body as she changed.

“Leave it,” Agatha said quickly as Rio went to shove on her t-shirt. “Wear mine. Leave yours.”

Her black t-shirt fell to the floor per Agatha’s request and Rio instead scooped Agatha’s much fancier, much richer feeling shirt and put that on. She got a waft of her perfume and moved while it lingered to tug Agatha towards her in the middle of the bed, guiding her legs to wrap around her waist as she knelt between them.

“You’ll come?”

“Once I have Nicky, I’ll be right behind you.”

It was enough, she thought as she kissed Agatha another time and then one more for luck, to have Agatha’s promise against her lips and to be sat between her thighs as she gave it. So she left soon after, checking that Agatha was covered before she opened the door to her manager. But the last look she got of her new fiancée was a look of sheer sadness, of which she had no power to cure.

“Did you leave those candles burning all night?” Alice hissed the moment Rio had closed the door to her whole heart.

Rio said nothing as she grabbed Alice’s hand and dragged her from the room to fly with her down the stairs.

“We’re engaged,” she hissed back, glancing briefly at the extinguished candles as they arrived in the hall.

“Yeah, well, you’ve been-...” Alice tugged her hand and Rio skidded round to a halt, now facing her. “Wait. HOLY SHIT!”

Rio laughed and flapped her free hand, inadvertently flashing the massive sparkler on her finger. “Shush. She’s just rousing. Play it cool or-...”

“Holy fucking shit, Rio!” Alice yelled as she grabbed Rio’s left hand to inspect the ring. “That’s-...”

“Beautiful?” A voice sounded from the top of the stairs and Rio looked up at the goddess standing there.

Alice jumped and dropped Rio’s hand immediately. “Holy shit, I mean… Agatha.”

Rio stood still as Alice panicked and began to spew random congratulations that mostly sounded ridiculous and some like she’d just vomited up a Hallmark card. But Rio didn’t much care because Agatha was walking down towards her, somehow in a pair of Rio’s running shorts, somehow looking better in them than Rio could even dream.

She was in her arms before Rio could think to say anything and before Alice had run out of new ways to say she was happy for them.

“I’ve changed my mind again,” Agatha said against Rio’s ear, “Stay with me.”

“Okay,” Rio breathed, intoxicated by the very woman who was now nipping at the shell of her ear.

Alice’s congratulatory messaging had gone quiet now and Rio suddenly wished she weren’t here at all.

“I know it’s a big day and all but…”

Rio groaned, one arm tightening around Agatha’s waist and the other slipping to her ass, just because she needed one last feel before Agatha would surely ban her from it forever.

“I have to go,” she said quietly, barely able to form the words.

She turned into Agatha who was turning to look at her and for a moment she was hypnotised by those blue eyes, completely stuck on how deep they were even in the strange light of the early morning.

“Then make it up to me when I arrive,” Agatha said after a while of Rio wondering if she’d protest some more.

The demand was enough. It was enough to send Rio off with a grin on her face and a skip in her step because she was going to marry the girl of her dreams and the girl of her dreams just so happened to be sexy, brilliant, and oh so demanding.

The plane ride back to Arkansas was much louder than the plane ride out. Rio was bouncing off the walls, telling Alice in excruciating detail about her night, and just holding back enough information to protect Agatha’s blushes.

Alice, for her part in all this as the best friend right now, rather than the manager, convinced Rio that one glass of champagne would be okay for her workday ahead and so they toasted to her new bride and spent a lot of time admiring Rio’s new ring.

“You think it cost over a mil?”

Rio scoffed and then frowned deeply, “god I hope not.”

“I’m sure it did. She’d have spent so much on it just because ‘so much’ to Agatha Harkness isn’t really that much at all. Plus she loves you and wants to show off for you and-...”

Alice had trailed off because Rio had taken off the ring for the first time since having it placed on her finger so she could inspect it properly and when she’d held it up to the light she’d noticed a tiny inscription along the inside of the gold band.

al infinto

She’d spent weeks now, months maybe, running around a basketball court with Nicky trying to reach it and yet here it was, nestled in the palm of her grateful hand. Agatha had gifted her infinity. She’d made her love for her infinite, etched into the very gold that would symbolise their union.

A sudden gasp left Rio’s body that she hadn’t known she needed to expel. Everything had been comfortable and easy; no crescendo to speak of. And yet here she was, hurtling through space, holding infinity in her hand.

“We’re getting married,” she whispered, when Alice had moved closer to check on her, “she’s going to marry me and I’m going to marry her.”

“Yes, babe. I know.”

Rio blinked and the moment she did she felt the tears form and she looked up to Alice before her as she said: “I need to call my mom when we land. But I wish I could…” she trailed off because Alice would know what she wanted to say and the words simply wouldn’t come.

“He’d be so proud,” Alice whispered into her hair as she wrapped an arm around her and pulled her into her side. “So fucking proud.”

“Do you think,” Rio began after a couple minutes of quiet, as she wiped at her tears at put her ring back on, “that I had to lose him to get her?”

“No,” Alice was quick to say, “the universe isn’t that cruel. It’s just bad luck. It’s just shitty, shitty luck.”

Rio nodded mutely, looking back down at the round diamond that represented her whole world. The rest of the journey was much more demure after that. Rio was contemplative, and Alice watchful. But when they landed and Rio could inhale the fresh air again she felt a little lighter.

Maybe it was her manager’s hand in her own, maybe it was the ring she could now twist with her thumb, maybe it was the knowledge that Agatha was coming. Whatever it was, it helped.

They made it to the set only an hour after the wheels hit the tarmac and Rio was rushed to her little trailer to shower and change into her costume for the day. As per usual, the superstar wasn’t needed for a while, so it was unclear to her why she even had to be here. But here she was.

She called her mom and had to hold the phone so far away from her ear because Anna was screaming her excitement at her. And she wouldn’t stop. But soon the screams became sobs and Rio cried with her over the loss of her dad and how happy he would have been for his beloved daughter.

Ro spoke to Anna for an hour before she hung up. To distract herself from her lingering grief she willed away the time by making little flowers while sitting on the floor in her cop uniform. She worked mostly in silence, with Alice tapping away at her computer and only the radio for company. It seemed odd that they were playing Top 40 rather than love songs on repeat but Rio knew the DJ hadn’t been given the heads up about her engagement so she couldn’t hold it against him.

It was five minutes before her call time that there was a knock on her trailer door and Rio shot up so quickly that all the flowers in bloom dispersed and created a meadow about her feet.

She wrenched the door open, and was blinded by the light.

“Hey,” Agatha said as simply as if it meant nothing at all.

And Rio, barely able to breathe, simply stared at her as Nicky threw himself at her and pressed in at her stomach, his head pulled back to look up at her even though she couldn’t tear her eyes away from Agatha.

“We got custody, melliza. I’m staying with you and mama.”

Agatha was smiling at her, her eyes sparkling but from something other than the tears she’d been holding back when Rio had had to leave her that morning.

She fell two feet back, partly because Nicky’s whole body weight was against her, and partly because stepping back meant pulling in, it meant bringing her family inside where it was cosy and safe; where she had flowers to welcome them with and her arms could hold them closer.

Agatha fell with them. She took the two small steps to be in the door and then closed it behind herself. The next thing she did was kiss Rio. As she did, Rio realised what the sparkle really was in Agatha’s gaze.

“I’ve missed you.”

It was relief.

She felt it as Agatha kissed her again, and then again, and then… she’d pulled back and her hand was on Rio’s face as Nicky squeezed her middle tighter.

“Will you be in custody with us?”

Agatha’s grin was teasing, her voice low and soft and Rio knew it was because she was tired, but it felt like it was that way too because she was so unbelievably happy that if she spoke any louder their happiness might be revealed and someone would take it away.

“I would love to be in custody with you,” Rio breathed out, one hand on Nicky’s back, the other reaching to hold Agatha’s at her cheek.

“We’re going to live with you for a while, melliza. We bought Scratchy with us too. So we can be a real family.”

Agatha’s thumb brushed her cheek and Rio wasn’t aware of it but she was wiping away a tear that had fallen at Nicky’s words. She couldn’t look away from Agatha, clearly taking to heart Agatha’s request for eye contact just a few hours ago.

Nicky was straining to look up at her though and soon Rio could only look down at him and grin.

“A real one?”

“Yes please,” Nicky said earnestly, “Mama and I would really like that.”

Rio laughed as she ducked down to kiss the top of his head and held him close for a while before she straightened up and smiled at Agatha. “So,” and here Rio realised they hadn’t discussed the whole marriage piece of it all. She instinctively pulled Agatha’s hand down to kiss her ring and when she did caught the slight shake of Agatha’s head. “You brought Scratchy, huh? I’m not sure he’ll fit in the hotel room.”

“Oh, we’re not staying in a hotel room,” Agatha said with an easy smile, her fingers curling back around Rio’s hand. “Jen’s sorting a place out as we speak.”

Rio’s response, other than surprise, was just to roll her eyes because of course. Not that she minded. Being in an actual house with Agatha and Nicky rather than one room would mean more privacy, which would mean more sex, which was always a good thing. Especially hot, soon-to-be-wives sex.

She tried to clear her mind of that thought because Nicky was still between them but still… it was a nice thought to have.

“Rio,” Alice called out tentatively, and Rio knew it was her cue to leave. She was reluctant to, but knew that leaving would mean returning and what could be better than that?

“There’s a playstation below the tv,” she began, talking more to Nicky now that Agatha, “and snacks in the kitchen and there’s a bed if you’re tired and-...”

“Hon,” Agatha said with a smile, “we’ll be fine. Go, do you work, and then come back to us, okay?”

Rio nodded eagerly, a dashboard dog with a wagging tail. She gave Nicky a gentle squeeze and then her attention was fully on Agatha, mostly because Agatha had peeled the little boy off of Rio and moved him to the side.

“My turn.”

Rio laughed as she kissed her and wrapped her arms so solidly around Agatha that soon little hands were trying to pry them open as giggles could be heard from beside them.

“No more kissing!”

“Oh kid, you don’t know what you’re in for.”

As Rio pulled back she shot her manager a smirk and found Agatha’s face pressed into her cheek and the murmured words, “But I know what you’re in for tonight.”

Rio could have screamed when Alice insisted she needed to leave because how was she supposed to leave after her fiancée said something like that to her. Stupid Agatha and her stupidly high libido that Rio loved so much.

She left with a scowl but a promise she’d be back as soon as possible. But possible was hours later and Alice was the one to deliver the news that Agatha had taken Nicky to their new place and she was to go and fetch all of her things from the hotel so Rio could go straight over when she was done.

So Rio languished on set, half-phoning in her performance due to exhaustion and yearning. But it was done within seven hours and she was soon in the back of a car on her way to the little house Jen had managed to find them. It wasn’t huge, it wasn’t luxurious, but it had a neat front yard and was neat inside too.

It wasn’t the house. It was the people inside it.

And inside Rio found them, standing with wide grins beneath a banner that read “Welcome Home” as she was sprayed with a confetti cannon that Nicky obediently aimed above her head to avoid any injury.

Rio yelled in surprise and before the confetti had even settled, Nicky was on her, squeezing her around her middle enough to squeeze out a bark of a laugh as she stumbled back a few steps.

She had them. She had Nicky, she had Agatha too, who had marched right over, clearly not wanting to be left out. This whole thing was real, and it was happening to her. She was shown about the house once the hugging was over, then shown the meal they’d prepared for her, then the little fort they’d built that wasn’t as good as the last one they’d had but would do for now.

And when Nicky was fast asleep in bed, Rio had Agatha again. Five times.

When she left for work the next morning she was still exhausted, still yearning, but she knew what she had to go back home to, so everything was rose-coloured, and everything was easy.

On the third day, when Rio had time off and could no longer hold back on what she wanted to ask Nicky, they arranged for them to take a big walk through the nearby forest so they could go the scenic route to the dinosaur park and spend the day together.

They were sent off with their backpacks and matching shirts and Agatha kissed each of them five times; Rio enjoyed it and Nicky squirmed a little. But it felt good to be sent away like this, like Rio was just a regular mom with her son, saying goodbye to their wife and mother, off on an adventure for just the two of them.

Thor drove them to the entrance to the forest trail and promised to be close by, keeping track of them using Rio’s live location on his phone, but otherwise giving them enough distance so they could be alone and enjoy just each other out in nature.

They walked a while, pointing out every bird or bunny they saw, and Rio felt light as she traipsed through the trees with her favourite kid. After a while she began to plan how she’d approach the big question and soon sought out a place to pause for snacks.

Just up ahead was a log, large enough to have been a very old tree, and dry enough to be a bench gifted by Mother Nature. Rio led Nicky to it and as she sat down she patted the space beside her, smiling as Nicky turned around and heaved himself up, his little legs dangling above the ground.

“You want some snacks?”

“Yes please.”

Rio nodded seriously and opened her backpack to seek out everything Agatha had packed for them. She gave Nicky an apple and a small pot of trail mix with more chocolate than she was expecting. And then she rummaged some more and found exactly what she was expecting: a small tub of purple Skittles.

They ate in silence for a while, Rio with her Skittles and Nicky taking alternate bites of his apple in between eating only the raisins and chocolate from his trail mix. The forest around them did the talking for them. Without the crunch of leaves and twigs below their feet they were able to hear every birdsong for miles around.

“Can I talk to you about something very important, mellizo?”

Nicky nodded and turned to Rio and Rio smiled a little at his big frown.

“Nothing bad?” He asked cautiously, pausing with his fingers dipped in the tub seeking more raisins.

“Nothing bad. Actually I wanted to talk to you about your mom and how much I love her.”

Nicky’s frown disappeared immediately and he instead grinned, now popping a raisin into his mouth.

“I know that.”

“You do? Good. Because I also want to talk about how much I love you.”

Nicky blushed but his grin didn’t falter. “I know that too, melliza. I love you too. Mucho, mucho.”

Rio laughed and looked down at her pot of purple, now half full.

“That’s good news because I was kinda hoping you wouldn’t mind if maybe I married your mom?”

She looked up again and the grin that had once been so bright had now faded and Nicky looked hesitant all of a sudden, almost scared.

Rio’s heart jumped into her throat and she swallowed but couldn’t dislodge it.

“Really?” Nicky asked softly and Rio could only nod in response.

He looked concerned, as if Rio had said something that had frightened him, and turned away from her as if to think it through for a while and Rio, to her horror, soon realised that he was crying.

Her Skittles fell to the floor as she jumped to sit right beside him and wrapped an arm around his back.

“Hey,” she reached to wipe at his tears, “none of that, huh? Why you’re you crying?”

Nicky sniffed and rubbed his fists into his eyes and then wiped them again with his sleeves.

“I just… I think it’ll make my mama really happy and she’s missed you so much and… and…”

“Baby,” Rio exclaimed, moving to rest on her knees before the little boy on the large log. “There’ll be no missing necessary anymore, okay? It’ll just be us. Tres patitos together forever. If you’ll let me? If you’ll let me marry-...”

Nicky had an uncanny ability, like his mother, for cutting off Rio when she was trying to be sincere. Not that it really mattered because Nicky was in her arms again, strangling the life out of her as if he never wanted her to say anything at all ever again; let alone anything sincere.

Coughing, she soon laughed. The sound came from deep in her belly, a heavy, hearty laugh that was more relief than actual good humour.

And she held Nicky as tightly as he held her because he deserved that. He deserved all the strength Rio had just as much as he deserved all the love.

“Why’re you laughing?” He whispered soon enough, having waited for Rio’s laughter to die down to a soft chuckle.

He relinquished his hold and Rio’s neck to slip down, and Rio shuffled back along the ground so he could kneel between her and the log. His gaze had dropped too, lingering on her locket that he now stroked with a touch much more gentle than the one that had just been around her neck.

“I’m happy,” Rio said softly. “I’m so happy to have you and your mama.”

Nicky’s brow furrowed a little and Rio’s smile fell as the concern rose in her chest.

“It’s why my mama had to get us custody together?”

“Yes.”

“Because she wanted custody with you?”

Rio’s lips twitched a little and her concern simply fell away.

“Yes, mellizo.”

“Mama said the judge gave us custody together. Does that include you? Did he say you too? Did he tell my dad?”

“Well,” Rio said slowly, meeting Nicky’s gaze now as he looked up. “Not exactly… You and your mama have custody of each other, that’s official. And I am free to have custody of whoever I want.”

“And… you want us? Officially?”

Rio’s brain, so conditioned now to remember lines from a script, was now also full of poetry. It was Agatha’s fault; Agatha’s doing. She’d read and memorised dozens of poems for her so that if she ever needed them, Rio could speak the words of the dead poets she loved so much.

And now, as Nicky, who had her face and his mama’s sensitive heart, looked up at her with so much hope she thought of a line from one such poem.

Hope is the thing with feathers

This tiny duckling, this innocent little boy who had opened his heart up to Rio from the day he’d met her, was checking again that Rio wanted him.

Because his dad never had and he knew it.

Because Nicky was innocent but he wasn’t stupid. He was smart and kind and funny and devious. He just wanted to be loved.

“We’re tres patitos, how could I not want you?”

Nicky made a strange noise. It was half an exhale, half a sneeze. And then it became clear what it actually was.

Nicky was laughing.

His arms were back around her neck and Rio pulled him all the way into her until they were crashed out on the forest floor. Something jammed into her back but she didn’t care because Nicky was laughing. Nicky knew he was loved so much that he was laughing about it.

Nothing else mattered.

The puddle of laughing ducklings soon ended up splayed out beside one another. They were both panting heavily, grinning up at their shared sky where the sun grinned back at them and Rio thought of Agatha and of how much she loved her.

“Melliza?”

“Yeah?”

“Was my dad sad? I didn’t want to ask my mama in case it made her sad that I did.”

Rio turned her head where it lay on the ground and looked at Nicky who was still blinking towards the sun.

“I don’t know, buddy. Do you want him to be sad?”

Nicky frowned and Rio watched his whole face scrunch as he thought.

“No… I don’t think so… Mama said I can see him twice a year if I want to but… I don’t want to. Is that okay?”

“Yes, of course it is.”

Nicky nodded and turned onto his side, and Rio smiled a little as he searched for something in her face.

“Do you think that… that you would maybe… maybe after a while… maybe uh… do you think I should maybe someday… call you my mama too?”

Rio’s whole face must have lit up because Nicky grinned at her. Shuffling closer until he could tuck in against her.

And Rio wrapped an arm around him and tucked his head under her chin.

“Tell you what, you can call me whatever you want to.”

Nicky shifted slightly and Rio rubbed his back.

“And if, if you ever do want to call me mama or mom or… anything at all then you can, okay? But I’ll always be your melliza and your fellow patito, and someone who loves you very much.”

Nicky shuffled again, squeezing his arm out from between them to wrap around Rio too. He nodded as he did it and Rio kissed the top of his head as she held him in her arms on the forest floor.

There was definitely something jaggy sticking to her side but she’d take all the jaggy sticks in the world if it meant having Nicky safe in her arms. So they lay there a little while longer until the smallest duckling began to flutter his feathers.

“I think we should finish our snacks and then keep going. I know mama will want us back before it gets dark.”

“So thoughtful.”

Nicky smiled as he scrambled up and Rio sat up and looked at the mess she’d made of purple skittles all around her. And then there was Nicky, taking his spot back on the log and patting it to encourage Rio to claim her place beside him.

“Raisin, melliza?”

Rio hummed as she pushed up and sat beside him.

“No, they’re all yours.”

Nicky, taking this to mean he could do whatever he wanted with them, dropped a couple of his biggest ones into Rio’s hand and smiled at her as he did. When their snacks were done, or half of them at least because Agatha had been generous in her snack-packing, they continued on their walk through the trees.

Not much walking was done, though. It soon became a game of how many steps could they skip from tree to tree. So Rio and Nicky were leaping through the forest, making up their own game of jumping around and exploring just off the beaten path. It was the most alive Rio had felt in a while, out in nature with her little patito following her every move and doing his best to show off as he did.

Because of their larking about they made it to the dinosaur park a little later than planned but they agreed to run across the parking lot to make up some time. Rio made sure to hold Nicky’s hand as they did and she kept him on the inside so if a car came, it would have to deal with her first.

In the dinosaur park they came face to face with the very lizards they spent a good part of their waking day discussing. Only, they didn’t run between each one. Thor had been waiting for them at the entrance and Rio noticed, when they fell into step with him, that Nicky had become quiet again and his little hand remained on her own even when there was no imminent danger from errant cars.

From the side of her backpack she unclipped the hanging cap there and placed it snugly on Nicky’s head to give him a little more security as they bought their tickets and entered the park itself.

By the time they got through the herbivores, it became clear that word had got round that a famous person was there. Nicky was now holding her hand a little tighter and Rio was sure he didn’t even look up at the Spinosaurus.

Still, she held her ground, she kept talking to him about the dinosaurs and reading off the fun facts on every signpost beside each model. She’d be damned if a few people looking at them would ruin their day together; especially now they were in agreement that they were a family.

Beside the Tyrannosaur, which looked like it had seen better days, a young couple began to approach and Rio winced as her left foot was trodden on.

“Can you tell them no please?” Nicky asked urgently, looking up at Rio with a deep frown.

Rio sighed and placed her free hand on his head, then turned to Thor to give him the universal sign of “get them”. He moved to intercept and Rio shot an apologetic smile to the woman who looked deeply disappointed and then shuffled her and Nicky away a little, giving his hand a quick squeeze as she did.

“It’s like this with mama too and I wish people would just leave us alone to be people. Mama is a person and you are a person and I don’t get why people want to ruin our time out together.”

Rio hummed quietly, aware of what was happening in her peripheral vision as she looked up at the large dinosaur in front of them.

“It’s a bit like coming to the dinosaur park. People want to see us because they’re interested in us. Ninety nine out of a hundred of them just want to say hello and maybe get a picture. But I know it’s annoying. But we have Thor to-...”

“I wish we didn’t need Thor. I wish it was just us.”

Rio ducked her head down and Nicky glanced at her sheepishly before he dropped his gaze to the floor.

“Not in a mean way…”

“I know, mellizo. Let’s go see the other dinosaurs then we can get an ice cream and then hit the gift shop and then go see your mama, okay?”

With that, and skirting around the couple who’d retreated per Thor’s request, they hit up the rest of the dinosaurs and Rio was able to work her magic enough to get Nicky to relax into taking selfies with some of their favourites. She even got him to stick his head into the mouth of a Gigantasaurus and sent it to Agatha immediately with the caption: Safe and sound!

The response back she got was: You’re an idiot. Which made Rio smile much bigger than it should have.

By the time they got to the gift shop, Nicky was comfortable enough to let go of Rio’s hand and she lost him for a while amongst the plethora of toys and replica bones. Not that she was worried at all. The shop was empty apart from the bored looking teenager behind the counter in the far end. Plus Thor was on the door.

After five minutes of wondering the aisles alone and admiring the work of capitalism, Nicky appeared to her again, holding up a bone.

“Can we get this for mama?”

Rio scoffed and took the bone from him, inspecting it was an untrained eye. “You think she’ll want a bone?”

“It’s from a Maiasaura and it’s her rib.”

Rio raised her brows and flipped the bone over. It was a small thing, no larger than the length of her hand, and underneath where it lay in a piece of heavy, excavated rock, there was a smooth bed so it could sit on display, complete with the price sticker of $300.

“You sure she’ll want it?” She asked as she turned it back to look again at the little bone, which, now she thought about it, looked like a whole lot of nothing.

“Well I was wondering if you could propose with it?”

Rio blinked and then raised her gaze to Nicky’s hopeful smile. “See because on the back it’s smooth so you can write something maybe, something nice and romantic and then because it’s a rib it means it was above the Maiasaura’s heart which is romantic too and mama is a Maiasaura so it’s sort of like a symbol of her and you because you protect us so you protect her heart and you love us.” He paused and his eyes flickered between the bone and Rio’s shocked face. “Right?”

“Mellizo,” Rio breathed out, unsure how his little brain had even come up with something so wild and yet so sweet. “I…”

“If it’s stupid we don’t have to. I just thought she’d like it better than the toys or the little pencil cases or-...”

“I think she’ll love it.”

“You do?”

“I think she’ll be so pleased she has such a sweet son and I think it means she’ll just have to say yes when I propose.”

Nicky rocked up onto his toes. “Could you maybe ask tonight? And can I be there please?”

Rio laughed and pulled him in for a hug. “You’re just like your mama.”

They left soon after with Agatha’s new rib bone, and piled into the back of the SUV where they admired the bone as well as the matching t-shirts they’d bought that read ‘Dinosaur puns are pteroble’. The whole journey back, Rio was grinning because Nicky was practically bouncing in his seat, and she couldn’t wait for Agatha to receive her two new gifts; though she assumed she might prefer the bone to the t-shirt.

When they arrived, they thanked Thor, Nicky’s thanks being quieter than Rio’s, and let themselves into their rented Akansas home. Dinner was on, if the smell of a sofrito cooking was anything to go by and there was the soft sounds of Anita Baker playing that meant Agatha must be in the kitchen somewhere.

Sure enough, as Nicky burst in to give his mama a hug and Rio came up a little slower to join after placing her backpack on the table, Agatha was oven-warmed and smiling as she hugged them back.

“What took you so long?”

“Oh, Nicky got eaten by a Gigantasaurus but I got him back eventually.”

Nicky giggled and Agatha rolled her eyes but Rio received a kiss all the same.

“Rio has something to ask you, mama. Could you sit down maybe and hold my hand?”

It was ridiculous how the shy little boy who liked basketball and dinosaurs was sometimes, just sometimes, exactly like his mama who liked neither of those things and who was anything but shy.

Agatha shot her a quick glance as she did as Nicky was told and Rio knew she had to act her best to make this as romantic and seemingly the first proposal of her life. So she went to fetch the little rib bone and when she had it and Nicky was done fussing about Agatha sitting in the right way to look up at Rio, Rio sank down to her knee.

Agatha gasped and placed her free hand on her chest and Rio smiled when she saw her abuela’s ring sparkling back at her. Not the best actress of a generation for nothing, she thought, as Agatha’s eyes filled with tears.

“Mi vida, I love you, and Nicky,” she added with a quick smile in his direction, “very, very much. Would you do me the honour of being my wife?”

She held up the bone and caught the flicker of confusion in Agatha’s gaze that soon disappeared to be replaced with total, utter, joy.

“Yes. Yes! Yes, I will marry you!”

It was the best performance Agatha had ever given; sponsored by Nicky, though unknowingly. And Rio laughed as Agatha launched herself at her, narrowly avoiding smacking into the bone because of Rio’s quick removal of it. Nicky was fast behind and soon they were a pile on the floor, the Maiasaura bone held high in the air to avoid hitting any one of them.

When the giggling died down and Nicky extricated himself to take the bone and find the sharpie they’d bought in Rio’s bag, Agatha, now curled half on top of Rio on the floor took the opportunity to whisper in her ear: “What the hell is that ugly rock about?”

Rio burst out laughing at this and Agatha, too pleased with not only her own performance but the very fact that they were openly engaged to Nicky now, huffed her own laugh against Rio’s cheek.

“Melliza,” Nicky called, standing by their feet with the rock and the pen. “You need to write something!”

Rio, her laughter subsiding, nodded and eventually sat with Agatha beside her. Rio took the rock and Nicky knelt by Agatha’s other side, as they both watched Rio as she wrote “tres patitos para siempre” and signed it just below.

“Here,” she said as she passed it across to Agatha, “sign your name.”

Agatha looked at her with a glint of wry amusement but did as she was told and then passed the rock to Nicky who scrawled his name rather than any attempt at a signature. Rio said nothing about his ‘N’ being very similar to her own.

“It’s official,” she announced as she took the rock back and turned it bone-side up. “On this, the rib of a Maiasaura, we all agree that we’ll be tres patitos forever.”

“A rib?” Agatha asked suspiciously, reaching to touch the small bone preserved in the rock.

“It protects the heart,” Nicky whispered reverently as he followed Agatha’s touch with one of his own. “It’s for you and Rio. Best mom dinosaur and our protector.”

The tears that came after that were realer than any tears Agatha Harkness had ever shed and Nicky frowned his big frown as he was pulled into the tightest hug of his life and Rio cuddled in from the other side.

Maybe it was Nicky’s sweetness that softened Agatha that evening, maybe it was that Rio had proposed again, maybe it was that the rib bone now sat pride of place on top of the mantel piece, whatever it was, something had softened Agatha enough that she’d put on her new t-shirt without a word of fuss.

On that first night, the one Rio would count as their first night as an official family, they sprawled out together in their matching t-shirts, her and Agatha with their rings, and Nicky playing with his new plastic tyrannosaurus as they watched Jurassic Park.

Life as Agatha Harkness’s fiancée was the best kind of life. And Rio, in her most generous moods, felt sorry for everyone who’d never been Agatha’s fiancée before. Until she remembered Ralph had been. And then she fell into a foul mood and the only way she could even remotely get out of it in a healthy, constructive way was to ravage Agatha in bed at night. But quietly, always quietly, and with the door locked because Nicky was down the hall.

She always regretted it the next day though because twice she’d had to leave for work now with Agatha teary at the prospect of a day without her. So she called every hour when she could and text when she couldn’t. And came back with flowers every evening or whenever she was on a nightshoot and returned with the sunrise she’d greet Agatha with a coffee and remain awake for long enough that Agatha got her fill of her before she had to start her day.

During this time Agatha had begun to call her mi costilla in honour of Nicky’s proposal gift and Rio walked around with the confidence of a woman who was named for the thing that protected Agatha Harkness’s heart. Alice told her she was “swinging it around” one night over dinner where Rio was being particularly obnoxious and showing off and when Nicky asked what she was swinging around they had to pivot quickly until they’d somehow agreed to a baseball tournament in the local park the next day.

So, apart from the moments in time where Agatha became needier due to Rio’s exertions the night before, everything was total, utter bliss.

There were only two other, tiny things that were even a blip on her radar. She sometimes caught Nicky looking at her with his deep, contemplative frown, but every time she asked him what was wrong he would blush a little and say nothing was. When she spoke to Agatha about it, Agatha had reassured her he was okay, that he was thinking about something, and working through it properly until he was ready to talk to Rio about it.

So Rio let the frowning happen. But most days, she couldn’t stop him grinning so wide he was in danger of pulling a muscle.

The third thing, much smaller and fluffier than the others, was Scratchy. Because Scratchy had somehow imprinted on Agatha and Rio couldn’t really blame him but she could have sworn that the rabbit blamed her for getting in his way all the time. Which was unfair, she thought, because she had been the one to find him in the first place. But everywhere Agatha went in the house, the bunny seemed to appear too. He’d sit with Nicky whilst Nicky was reading but he’d rather be in Agatha’s lap or by her side or at her feet. And Rio kept swearing he was nipping her toes whenever she got close but Agatha didn’t believe her and neither did Nicky.

A week into their new life with the little rib now in their world, a cataclysmic event equivalent to the destructive force that had killed all the dinosaurs hit their happy home.

“You know,” Agatha said quietly against Rio’s collarbone as she swirled her left ring finger in figures of infinity against Rio’s opposite bicep one night after a slow fuck, “we can get married tomorrow. Arkansas has a twenty four hour wait period. Just us. I’ve had NDA’s written up and we just need a couple witnesses so we can use the blonde and the bald,” Rio knew she was talking about the bodyguards, “and be married by midday.”

Rio, sticky from the workout she’d just put into putting Agatha through the mattress, frowned up at the ceiling, trying to process this suggestion. Clearly not giving Agatha the response she’d expected.

“You don’t want to,” she said flatly, the infinity symbols apparently finite because she’d stopped drawing them.

“It’s not that,” Rio whispered, beginning to brush her fingers along Agatha’s warm side before the inevitable happened and Agatha had ripped herself away.

Rio just watched, as helpless as the poor dinosaurs had been as the meteor hurtled through the sky. Agatha stumbled from the bed on shaky legs and made it across the room until she rounded on Rio, all fury and flames with her pink chest and her sprinkling of small bruises.

“You’ve changed your mind? You hate me now?”

“Baby,” Rio said sadly, sitting up in bed, “I love you.”

“So you have changed your mind?” Agatha asked again, her voice getting louder.

“Nicky’s just down the hall,” Rio whispered, glancing to the locked door before looking back at Agatha, “Come back to bed.”

“You don’t want…” Agatha began, her fists at her sides, “you don’t want to marry me anymore?”

Rio’s hand, held out towards Agatha, now fell down amongst the sheets and Rio sighed quietly, her frown deepening with every furious second that passed.

“More than anything I want to marry you.”

“So why won’t you?! Why won’t you come with me tomorrow and make it official?!”

Rio glanced at the door and then looked back round to Agatha. She took a breath, tried to make sense of her own feelings on the matter, and then said, “It doesn’t feel right; going down to city hall and doing it so secretly doesn’t feel right.”

“It’s not a secret. We’ll both know. Nicky will know. I’ll tell Jen and you can tell your short friend and we can tell Anna together.”

There it was, Rio realised. Her mom. The small circle of trust they’d formed. The engagement was hard enough to keep from screaming about but being married to Agatha, making it as official as official could get, she wanted that to be written across her skin and screamed from the Hollywood Sign.

“You deserve a wedding that isn’t fake, that isn’t forced upon you, by your mother, or by the need to keep it quiet. You deserve one that’s romantic and for us, rather than-...”

Agatha growled and threw her hands into the air, turning from Rio. As he did her knee gave way and her body jerked before she could right herself. It was Rio’s cue to move, to stride towards her and press up against her from behind. Agatha didn’t fight her off but she didn’t lean back either.

Agatha was warmer than usual, warmer than she’d even been when they had been tangled up in bed together with Agatha drawing infinity across her skin. She sighed out against Agatha’s exposed neck and ran her hands delicately across her torso, touching and caressing the hot, sticky skin that she’d just spent the better part of three hours worshipping.

She was breathing heavily, taking in long, slow breaths and exhaling them just the same. Her body was tense and stiff and even under Rio’s gentle touch she wasn’t relaxing.

“You’re not backing out?”

Rio’s stomach flipped, her heart skipped a pained beat, “Never.”

Agatah dropped a hold on her own hair and her arms hung down by her sides, no longer with fists at the end of them but not touching Rio yet either.

“I want to be your wife,” Agatha said flatly, turning her head into Rio’s.

“I know. I want to be yours.”

“Then why won’t you marry me?”

Rio smiled a little and adjusted her hands to Agatha’s hips so she could turn her around and walk her back into the wall. It was a sign of Agatha’s thaw that she didn’t protest this and instead allowed it all to happen with a sad frown on her face.

“Because being engaged to you is a miracle in itself. Being open with Nicky is too. Getting to come home to you and kiss you and annoy you while you’re cooking or play with your hair on the couch while Nicky teaches me Spanish or… it’s all just a big miracle. One we should be allowed to enjoy. One we should get to enjoy just like any other ordinary couple.”

“We’re not ordinary,” Agatha insisted, her frown still present on her face, “We’re more than that. We’re-...”

“Mi vida, I want to give you a wedding you can look back on and-...”

“I want it now. I want…” Agatha trailed off because she’d closed her eyes but that hadn’t been enough to prevent the singular tear that escaped as Rio reached to wipe it away with the pad of her thumb. “I want everything.”

Rio smiled sadly and leant in to kiss the track the tear had left.

“Your mom will be mad because we’re living in sin.”

Rio scoffed and caught the twitch in Agatha’s lips as she sniffed.

“She has a lesbian daughter, she knows I sin.”

Agatha grimaced at that but her hands soon moved to hold Rio’s arms as Rio stepped in closer and kissed along Agatha’s tense jaw. “We’ll get married, I promise. But I want it to be the right way. I want it to be not because we’re hiding or because-...”

“I’ve had enough of talking now,” Agatha announced, “Carry me back to bed I’m feeling… I need to be coddled.”

So Rio carried Agatha back to bed and wrapped her up in her arms and the blankets and Agatha hid in her neck for a while before she surfaced enough to whisper, “Okay, I suppose I can wait.”

The meteor had been close to hitting but right before impact it had dissolved into nothing and was now scattered in the atmosphere around them, as harmless as the stars.

Rio was particularly attentive the following couple days, to which Agatha didn’t comment or complain about but instead became increasingly more demanding of her. Even Alice noticed, though she didn’t say anything for fear of being killed by a movie star.

Rio did take great delight in telling her that Agatha had referred to her as her “short friend” though and Alice appeared the next day to take Rio to set in boots with a two inch heel that Rio said nothing about but that Agatha referred to as her “Tom Cruise shoes”.

The shoot came to an end just over two weeks after Agatha and Nicky had first arrived and Rio attended the wrap party she’d helped to fund but left after two drinks to be with her family. She couldn’t talk openly about who she was living with or that she’d promised Nicky she’d work on her Spanish spelling that night, but the people around her noticed she was rocking up in the morning with ironed t-shirts and more pep in her step than before.

The next day, the plan was to go to Arkansas for a few days to see Anna and take a weight off there before they were to go on their big Euro trip. Agatha had done all the organising with Rio’s mom and Val had been involved, if only to make sure they had all the right security in place and a dark-windowed SUV instead of the hire car Rio would usually get.

Val even flew out to help with the airport because the paps would know the shoot had wrapped and the various stars would be leaving the state as soon as possible to return to their families. They just didn’t know that Rio Vidal would be leaving with her family.

But Agatha had covered that eventuality too. She’d hired a Private Jet and Alice was bummed she wouldn’t be coming with them on this little trip because of it. But still, Val helped as an extra pair of eyes around Nicky, even though he was on Rio’s back as they moved from the private lounge around the back of the airport up the steps to the swanky jet just for them.

“You’re not coming?” Rio asked in the doorway, looking down at Val at the bottom of the stairs.

“No, just Thor and Wilson. You’ll be fine. Your mom’s got her guy too and there are plenty eyes on the house and-...”

“I was asking more as a friend than a client,” Rio clarified, raising her brows in amusement at Val’s professionalism.

“Well bloody hell, Vidal, I’m flattered. But, no, special request of el jefa to not.”

Val shot her a look and Rio rolled her eyes with a smile, “Got it.”

“Safe trip, folks. I’ll see you in a couple days.”

She saluted and Nicky waved as Rio smiled her goodbye and then turned to walk into the body of the plane. With the littlest patito now back on his own two feet and the ability to lean over Agatha in her chair and whisper in her ear now she said: “Jealous of Val?”

“Your girlfriend? No, what gave you that idea?”

Rio smirked and kissed Agatha’s cheek before she took the seat opposite her and Agatha scowled at this choice, the scowl deepening when Nicky took his seat beside Rio instead of her.

“Always last choice,” Agatha sighed, inciting a pile-on in her luxurious chair that had to be interrupted by the embarrassed steward because the plane was about to take off. Nicky was beside Agatha for the take off now and Agatha was still doing her best to scowl at a smug Rio as the plane reached altitude and they were able to get out of their seats.

The flight, like their lives now, was easy and fun. They soon had music on and Rio was teaching Nicky how to make a flower that bloomed with the card she’d bought with them whilst Agatha lounged in the glasses that made Rio’s knees weak as she read a well-thumbed penguin classic.

Getting out of Wilmington Airport wasn’t as simple as arriving into Arkansas. But they managed it with as little fuss as possible and Nicky tucked in on Rio’s back. The drive too, was easy, with Wilson taking the wheel and the three ducklings in the back, Agatha in the middle so she could be indulged in being the chosen one for the other two to sit next to.

When they arrived at her parents house Rio felt a wave of grief wash over her that must have been anticipated by Agatha because she squeezed her hand and brought it to her lips and whispered: “I know it’s hard.”

Acknowledgement of it was enough to give Rio the strength to slide from the car and move with the others up the short front path to the familiar house. She paused at the door, between knocking and simply walking in. And when Agatha touched her side gently she settled on the latter and stepped into her family home with all its comforting smells and sights.

“Mama!” She called out the moment she stepped over the threshold and Agatha and Nicky were in safely behind her. Rio moved further into the small hallway and three steps in, her mom appeared round the door to the kitchen.

Anna Vidal, the woman who had birthed Rio, marched past her with her arms open to get to a woman she’d known for just a few months. And Rio couldn’t even be mad about it because as she turned to see her mom pull Agatha into a tight hug, she saw Agatha’s beaming face.

She’d happily be second, or even third place after Nicky too, if it meant Agatha would always look like that.

“Mom, you’ll crush her.”

Anna tutted as Agatha laughed, and Rio noticed her eyes had filled with tears as Anna turned away to dismiss Rio with a wave of her hand. It was Nicky’s turn next and Anna went a little easier on the little boy who now stood before Rio, the very backs of his heels just touching Rio’s toes.

“Hola, señora Anna. Le hice un regalo por haberme recibido.” I made you a gift for having me.

Rio squeezed his shoulder and caught Agatha smiling warmly behind her mom as Nicky held up the little flower he’d been perfecting on the flight and Anna took it as if it were something precious.

Nicky rocked up on his toes and then used the downward motion to step back again until he was fully on Rio’s feet. Anna, desperate as Rio knew she was to give the little boy a big squeezy hug, instead simply smiled and touched his cheek briefly.

“Gracias, ángel.”

Nicky nodded and smiled up at his Rio, pleased his hard work had paid off.

Rio was next in the lineup of greetings and received a kiss to the cheek and a squeeze of her arm before her mom yelped in her ear and Rio got a fright from it.

Anna’s arms were in the air and she spun on the spot, spouting incomprehensible Spanish as she grabbed Agatha’s hand to see the ring she’d suddenly remembered would be there.

And Rio, she crossed her arms over Nicky, bracing him for what was to come.

“¡Ah, mija! ¡Mi hermosa y preciosa hija!” Ah my daughter! My beautiful and precious daughter!

Rio stuck her tongue into the inside of her cheek as Nicky grinned at the sight of his mama being tugged down into another fierce hug.

“Gracias, Anna. ¿Estás contenta?” Thank you, Anna. You’re pleased?

It took everything in Rio not to roll her eyes at the soft question she barely caught from Agatha’s lips as Anna laughed happily and continued to squeeze the life out of her fiancée.

“Mama,” Rio called out, “you’re killing her.”

Nicky giggled and Anna rounded on him, breaking her own rule and swooping down to hold his cheeks and kiss him between the eyes. Rio moved her fingers to capture Nicky’s hands as they flew to her own but she knew he was just shy, not scared.

“Y mi nieto. Tan guapo y tan listo, igual que su mamá.” And my grandson. So handsome and so smart, just like his mama.

Rio grinned proudly up at Agatha and saw her wiping her eyes hurriedly. She sighed out through her nose, knowing Agatha would be feeling unworthy of this attention and more emotional about it than Rio could ever truly understand.

“Come here,” she said as Anna left Nicky alone and stood to the side with her hands on her head, muttering excitedly about how they could celebrate. Rio reached for Agatha when she stepped closer in the tiny hallway and tugged her into her other side as Nicky held tight to her other hand and smiled up at his mom.

“¿Lágrimas de felicidad?” Happy tears?

“¡Ah! ¡Y su español es buenísimo! Mucho mejor que el tuyo, mija.” And his Spanish is so good! Much better than yours, daughter.

Rio rolled her eyes as Agatha laughed and Nicky seemed to grow an inch or so in front of her.

“Gracias, señora.”

Anna made a noise Rio had never heard her make before and she stared at her with wide eyes, wondering what the fuck had happened to her mom. But as she made to reach for Nicky again and then pulled her hands back, she realised what it was.

Anna had decided that this was her grandson, and was holding herself back from embracing him as such. Because Nicky was shy, because he was polite, and because he was still calling her señora instead of abue.

Agatha picked up on this too and pulled away from Rio to take Anna’s arm and direct her into the house.

“Déjame contarte todo al respecto.” Let me tell you all about it.

Agatha turned to shoot Rio a watery wink and Rio smiled at her before turning her attention back to Nicky who was watching his mama and Anna walk away.

She changed her hold on him to squat down before him and turn him so she could smile up at his blushing face.

“You okay there?”

“She’s really happy,” Nicky whispered, a grin tugging at his lips. “She must love mama very much.”

“She does, mellizo. And I think she loves you too.”

“Me?” Nicky blinked slowly, looking from Rio to where Agatha and Anna had disappeared into the living room.

“Mhm. She thinks you’re smart and handsome and the sweetest boy she’s ever met.”

Nicky bit down on his lip as he focused back on Rio. “Handsome because I look like you.”

“Exactly,” Rio agreed, poking Nicky’s stomach to make him smile again.

“I want you to consider this like a home now, okay? My mom wants that too. You’re safe and so so welcome here. And you know you can call her just Anna if you want to.”

Nicky shifted where he stood, looking back up to the place the other two had disappeared for a moment before he looked back to Rio and whispered: “It’s not rude?”

“No, baby. We’re family now. I know it’s a lot of change lately and I know-...”

“Does she know I come with my mama? That if you marry her then…,” he looked down and Rio’s smile faded as she took both his hands in her own and squeezed them tight.

“Hey, what did I tell you on our walk?”

“That you love me and we’re family.”

Nicky was trying to hide his smile but Rio wouldn’t let him and tugged at his hands. “Exactly. In this house you’re a big bonus. You’re family. Because when I was your age my Spanish was so bad my mom used to get so mad at me every time I spoke it and yours is so good that she’s just so excited to have you around.”

Nicky hummed, a toothy grin following the noise as Rio lifted his hands to kiss them both in turn.

“Let’s go inside. I’m sure she’ll want to show you more pictures of me when I was-...”

Rio’s words, and breath, were cut short. She was suddenly being choked by Nicky’s love for her as he’d thrown his arms around her neck without warning and held her tight. She coughed a laugh and then held him to her, squeezing his little body as he squeezed her own.

“I love you,” he said softly, the words tickling her ear. “Mucho mucho.”

And Rio breathed out a sigh of contentment, something she was only recently getting used to feeling.

“I love you too, mellizo. Mucho mucho.”

Rio had been right about the pictures. She sat, drinking the expensive champagne Agatha had bought for them all and grimacing as she curled up in her dad’s favourite chair and Agatha, Nicky, and Anna, crowded round the coffee table to ooh and ahh at the pictures of Rio as a kid.

It had been two champagnes in when she realised something and stood from her comfortable seat to move closer and look down at what actually was being shown. There, laid above one of the pages of the album they were all admiring, was a picture of Nicky when he was about three, in blue dungarees and with a goofy, gap-toothed grin.

And Rio realised without having to have it confirmed for her, that Agatha must have sent this picture to Anna. Not least because it was in a small gold frame. She looked up then, her eyes scanning the room that was full of pictures of her family; her mom and dad, herself, her cousins and aunties and uncles, and there, on the right hand side of the fireplace, was a picture of her and Agatha and Nicky at the basketball game in Boston all those months ago.

She placed her champagne down and picked it up and stared down at the grinning faces that stared back at her.
