It had been a time of such uncertainty in her life, a time of secrets she didn’t want to have or to keep. And now everything was certain, everything was as open as it needed to be, and so she could look back with hope at the face that smiled back at her because the Rio in the frame would be just fine.

“Mi costilla,” Agatha called out, earning a soft chuckle from Anna, because Agatha had told her all about the dinosaur rib that had given Rio her new nickname, “Ven a ver.” Come see.

Rio placed the picture down and moved back around with her glass of bubbles and took a seat behind Agatha on the couch so she could lean back against her legs and Rio could lean over to see what her family was seeing.

Rio in a park, Rio on a basketball court, Rio sticking her tongue out at the camera, Rio on her dad’s shoulders in a pool with her arms out and her mouth open wide.

“King of the world,” Nicky said in recognition of the familiar position. Rio ruffled his hair affectionately in acknowledgement and smiled at the grin she received as he turned to look at her.

The evening was a soft one, with Rio and Nicky soon left to their own devices in the living room as Anna and Agatha worked on dinner and gossiped in the kitchen. From what Rio could hear filtering through the small house, they were rehashing things they’d already discussed several times before: Rio’s cousins misbehaving, her aunt getting her nails done by the woman who had cheated on her husband with the local priest and caused a scandal, and how Nicky was getting on at school.

Rio and Nicky watched tv and Nicky kept shuffling closer until Rio performed his usual move and pretended to yawn so she could wrap an arm around him. It was just how it went now, both totally comfortable in each other’s company enough to be silent and at ease as they watched basketball videos on youtube or cartoons on the tv.

They all ate dinner together, Rio’s favourite pollo guisado, prepared by Agatha and supervised by Anna. It became clear as they all ate and chatted over the dinner table how close her fiancée and mom had become. Agatha laughed more than she did around other people, she was quick with a joke, and quicker still with a compliment. And Anna was smiling more than Rio had seen her smile in a long while, so she went to bed more grateful than ever for Agatha’s love for her mom and for the woman herself.

At Nicky’s bedtime, Rio showed him to her room, which was to be his for the time they spent there and he spent a lot of the time he should have been brushing his teeth and washing his face instead inspecting everything in the tiny room, reading every plague on every trophy and raiding the small wardrobe for things he could steal.

It was only when Agatha came to investigate and found Rio looking guilty in her old school sweater and Nicky in an even older Celtics one that he actually did agree to do his teeth in the bathroom down the hall.

Rio was sent back down the stairs in her new sweater and Agatha finished bedtime, making sure Nicky was all tucked in before she left him in the comfort of Rio’s childhood bed.

As Rio settled on the couch again and her mom asked her about how work had been, her eyes drifted to something she hadn’t spotted before. On the countertop, beside her dad’s old record player was a Golden Globe.

She tilted her head as she stared at it. “Is that mine?”

“¿Qué? Ah. No. Es de Agatha.” What? Oh. No. It’s Agatha’s.

Rio blinked and turned back to her mom, “How did you get it?”

Anna shrugged and had the decency to look a little sheepish, “Pedí el premio. Quería lucirlo. Estoy orgulloso de ella. Orgulloso de ambos.” I asked for it. I wanted to show it off. I’m proud of her. Proud of you both.

Rio looked around the room and confirmed her suspicions, “None of mine are out on display.”

Agatha appeared in the doorway at precisely the wrong moment, at least for Rio. Because Anna used it as an excuse to change the subject and soon Rio was ignored again as Agatha and Anna discussed Miguel’s new boyfriend as Rio sulked about her mom showing off about Agatha but not her. It took another glass of red and another hour before she came round to the idea.

She supposed she’d show off about Agatha too. Maybe it was genetic.

In bed that night, though, Agatha wouldn’t let her show off in her usual way. Rio had been cockblocked by her parents’ house. Because Agatha refused to let her touch her in her mom’s guest room, which was enough in itself for Rio to be frustrated by but the fact that Agatha was rubbing all over her abs and kissing her neck made it much, much worse.

“You can’t tease when you’re refusing to let me fuck you.”

“Don’t say ‘fuck’ in your parents’ house.”

“Fuck,” Rio huffed, glaring at the ceiling as Agatha’s hand slipped down to her hip and she flicked her tongue out against her throat.

“Just enjoy it.”

“No. You’re doing it on purpose. It’s like you want me to-...”

She felt Agatha smirk against her neck, and her sudden realisation was confirmed. The flip onto Agatha’s back was swift and silent and Agatha did nothing but grin up at her once her hands were pinned over her head.

“Took you long enough.”

“You said no,” Rio insisted, frowning where Agatha was still grinning.

“And then I was practically humping your leg,” Agatha retorted, too much smugness in her voice for Rio to enjoy the visual.

“If I can’t say ‘fuck’, you can’t say ‘hump’.”

Agatha scoffed but was in no real position to argue with Rio above her hips, holding her wrists taught.

“So… can we?” Rio asked after a moment of deliberation.

“You want permission?”

“Well…” Rio said slowly, “Kinda.”

To her surprise Agatha went beet red as she turned to look at her and Rio raised her brows because what could she possibly be-?

“You always have permission,” Agatha said, seeming to force the words out despite her better judgement.

And Rio, as realisation dawned, grinned at her red-faced fiancée and then bit down on her lip to try and hide her total delight.

“I do?”

Agatha struggled against the hold on her wrists but quickly gave up.

“Don’t be smug about it.”

“Oh, I’m very smug about it.”

And Rio proceeded to show Agatha just how smug about it she was for the rest of the night, until Agatha was whimpering quietly, clawing at Rio’s chest to make her stop, to make her slow, to make her curl in to her and let Agatha hold on.

They fell asleep, Rio in her smugness, Agatha in her attached way, curled in on one another, barely an inch or a breath of space between them. But when Rio woke the next morning, she woke alone, frowning for the chill in the bed that suggested Agatha had been away for a while but when she looked it was only seven thirty. But there was a hot coffee by the clock on the side, placed there by Agatha, waiting for her to wake up.

She padded to the bathroom and noticed Nicky’s door, as well as her mom’s, was open, so everyone but her was awake. She brushed her teeth and washed her face and then went down to see why everyone was up without her.

“Hey,” Rio said softly, blowing out some cool air over her steaming coffee. “You were gone this morning.”

Agatha’s cheeks flushed and she avoided Rio’s eyes as Nicky said a bright “buen día, melliza”. Rio shot him a wink and then returned her gaze to Agatha, watching as she kept her face turned down and was focusing in on… her shirt?

“Mija, buen día.” Anna walked in and suddenly Rio realised why Agatha was blushing. Her mom always did like to get up early. Agatha must have known. She spoke to her every day, there was no way she wouldn’t have already known that Anna was always up at the crack of dawn.

She pushed off the doorframe and walked around to scoop up Agatha’s jaw from behind her and turn her head at an angle so she could kiss her cheek sweetly.

“Mornin’, ma’am,” she whispered, like an old-timey sheriff might. Agatha smiled just as Rio turned to ruffle Nicky’s hair and he giggled at her, blinking up at her from beneath his messy bangs.

She grinned and went to take a seat beside her mom at the dining table, which wasn’t covered in the food she was hoping for.

“What’re we doing?” She asked curiously, eyeing her shirt suspiciously as Agatha thumbed at it.

“Arreglando la camisa de mamá.” Fixing mama’s shirt.

“¿Arreglada?” Fixing?

“It means fixing,” Nicky explained needlessly, making Rio narrow her eyes playfully at him.

“I know what it means.”

“Just checking, melliza.” Nicky giggled as she stuck her tongue out at him and he shifted in his seat.

“There’s a hole in it,” Agatha offered up, her voice low for the early morning and Rio looked down at the spot she was indicating to see a hole smaller than the size of a penny just below the armpit.

“Baby,” she said gently, “that’s barely a hole.”

“It needs fixed,” Agatha responded, more defensively than Rio was expecting.

She looked up and Agatha was blushing fiercely and Rio softened at the sight.

“Precious things need taken care of,” Anna said, making eyes at Rio pointedly across the table as if Rio didn’t know. As if Rio weren’t taking care of the woman she was soon to marry.

Rio rolled her eyes and then swooped in to kiss Agatha’s burning cheek again and whispered, “I love you.”

Agatha still wasn’t looking at her and so Rio smiled and kissed her again.

“I’m going for a run,” she announced, straightening suddenly.

She hadn’t expected the panic this would cause. But Agatha had jumped so quickly she’d somehow spilled the coffee Rio had left on the table and it spilled all over her shirt.

Her mom screamed and Agatha yelped like she’d been bitten by a snake. Nicky yelled a loud “oh no!” and Rio blinked stupidly at the sight. The soft, dull pink of her favourite shirt was being dyed a deep brown.

But it was like the world was imploding.

Agatha had ripped the shirt up and was flapping it in the air as Anna moved around to try and pat it dry with the piece of cloth she’d been using to demonstrate the stitching technique. Nicky was on his feet, his eyes as wide as Rio’s hopeless ones were.

“¡No pasa nada! Hay una lavandería estupenda en el pueblo. Todo está bien. No te preocupes.” It’s okay! There's a great laundromat in town. It’s okay. Don’t worry.

The guilt that settled was overwhelming, soon curdled to worry as Rio looked from the stained shirt to Agatha’s bereft face.

“I’ll go with you,” she offered gently, “we’ll get it out.”

Agatha nodded silently and seemed to swallow down something as she looked at Rio, “We should go now.”

Rio agreed and rushed away to change with a tight chest and a dry mouth. Waiting for her by the door when she reappeared was Agatha, looking pale, her mouth drawn into a thin line that only loosened when Rio kissed her softly.

“Thor’s outside,” Agatha breathed, the shirt in a plastic carrier that looked ancient but would do the job of keeping the damp shirt protected from any other elements.

Rio waved goodbye to Nicky as he stood with Anna in the hall and they stepped out together, making it to the SUV with no issue.

“It’ll be fine,” Rio kept repeating, and Agatha was mostly silent for it, though she kept checking on the shirt as if hoping it would miraculously heal itself.

“I noticed the hole a couple days ago,” she said quietly, “I’m not good at… at things like that but I know your mom is so I was hoping she’d teach me and…”

She’d trailed off and Rio squeezed her hand to reassure her. If Agatha’s attempts at origami flowers were anything to go by, Rio could only imagine how bad her sewing was, but she didn't voice that. Instead she said nothing until they’d arrived and she stepped first onto the sidewalk and helped Agatha out the car.

“Mom’s been to this guy for years. Brian, I think his name is.”

Agatha nodded silently and stepped into the small laundromat first, glancing around at the different detergents and signs for quick and deep cleans that cost only five dollars per bag of clothes.

There was a little bell on the side that Rio tapped to alert the owner of their presence and soon a portly man appeared with a warm smile and arms open as he recognised Rio.

“Ah! Rio Vidal! How’s your mom doing?”

“Okay, thanks, given everything. How’re you, Brian? How’s the-...?”

“We need an urgent wash,” Agatha interrupted, placing the bag on the counter between them. “This shirt is old and delicate and it’s already got a rip in it and its got a large coffee stain so-...”

“Oh, let’s see what we have here,” Brian said warmly, taking the shirt from the bag with less care than Rio knew Agatha would like.

He inspected it for all of five seconds before Agatha was speaking again: “Can you get it out?”

Brian didn’t say anything and Agatha huffed in response.

“Are you listening to me?”

Rio chewed on her lip, adjusting her stance beside Agatha to hold her hip subtly below the counter.

“Ma’am, I-…”

“Don’t ‘ma’am’ me. Are you listening or not?”

“Agatha,” Rio breathed out, daring to shift her hand ever so slightly so her finger could feel the warm skin of Agatha’s midriff beneath her shirt.

“He’s not listening,” Agatha hissed. “This shirt is very important to me. This shirt is worth more to me than your entire business so you’d better-…”

Rio’s hand moved around, fully below Agatha’s shirt now, wrapped tight against her opposite hip. She’d moved in, no longer being subtle, because what good was that doing. She placed herself between the owner of the local laundromat and her rabid fiancée and forced her to look at her.

“Mi alma, it’s just a shirt. I’ll buy another one.”

Agatha’s jaw flexed and then she dropped her gaze and moved to the side with her hand on Rio’s wrist.

“It’s precious to me, very precious,” she said to the frightened man in a much softer voice. “I’ll pay your rent on this place for a year if you can get the stain out. I… it’s a very precious shirt. Please take good care of it.”

“Baby,” Rio whispered, because Agatha had looked at her again and almost the moment she had she’d pulled away and marched right out of the little store.

Rio watched her go and swallowed thickly. She turned back only to collect their ticket, nod once at the owner, and then leave the way Agatha had gone.

She was waiting just outside, standing a few feet away from Thor, her head down and her fists clenched at her sides. And Rio swooped in immediately because she knew that Agatha was trying her best but the tears were coming anyway.

So Rio held her as they did. In a public street in a suburb of Wilmington, Hollywood actress Rio Vidal held her future wife as she cried into her neck.

No one got near but Rio knew they were being watched. She knew people were taking pictures. Only she couldn’t even begin to care.

Because Agatha was crying steadily against her and Rio didn’t know why she was having such a big reaction to her shirt but the fact is that she was. So she could only hold her through it until Agatha was able to tell her what was wrong.

And as the first flash triggered, as Thor moved in to crowd them towards the car and the other body guard, Wilson, moved around to their other side, Rio remembered.

“I’m worried you’ll leave the house one day and just won’t come back and all I’ll have of you is a shirt and a ring and our son.”

Rio’s shirt was part of the trifecta. It was one of the things that Agatha could hold on to when Rio wasn’t there, when she was scared she wouldn’t come back.

They moved slowly to the car, Agatha as turned into Rio as she could be. As they made it inside, Rio hated that Val had been right about the SUVs. But Agatha was beside her, wiping her eyes and clutching her hand. They’d lost a shirt, maybe, but not each other.

“It’s so ugly,” Agatha said through her tears, making Rio blink in surprise.

“It is not.”

“It’s so ugly, I can’t believe… I can’t believe Nicky inherited your taste. How did… how did that happen?”

A wall, perfectly built, using the same brick and mortar Agatha had been using all her life; cruelty and humor, only dialled down because of her love for Rio. But it was a wall all the same.

Rio reached across but not to wipe Agatha’s tears, Agatha was already doing that. Instead, she reached for her belt and buckled her in.

“Well I picked you, so my taste can’t be that bad.”

Agatha just sniffed but Rio could see the twitch of her lips and so lifted her hand to her face so she could touch them rather than kiss them.

“We’ll talk when we get home?”

Agatha nodded silently and Rio’s hand was taken to be tucked in around Agatha’s thigh. She then koala’d around her arm and for the duration of the journey, Agatha sniffed softly and Rio held her tight.

They drove the long way home, with the driver explaining they needed to make sure they weren’t being followed.

But Agatha, now no longer crying, reminded him that people would already know where Anna lived. And if they didn’t, they could find out. When Rio had shifted uncomfortably at this, Agatha had squeezed her arm and whispered, “she’s safe. We’re all safe. Safe as kittens.”

“Patitos,” Rio corrected gently, forcing a small smile in Agatha’s direction.

When they arrived at the house, Rio stepped out first, and held her hand out to Agatha to take the moment she was on the sidewalk with her. They walked in together, and Agatha hung back a little when the thunder came and Nicky appeared in the hall to welcome them back.

“Did you fix it?”

“It’s being fixed,” Rio reassured, smiling warmly at the anxious little boy as Agatha kissed her shoulder and then stepped past her to get to Nicky.

Rio watched as she swooped in and kissed the top of Nicky's head, ushering him back into the house straight after. Following then, Rio stood in the doorway and looked at the scene of Agatha and Nicky on the couch, them both looking at the Spanish homemade flashcards he’d been running through with Anna.

And then there was the teacher in question, sitting on the floor on the other side of the table, her knowing eyes on Agatha.

Rio knew Agatha would hate that her mom knew she was sad. But Anna always said it was a mother’s job to know when their child was unhappy and so, naturally, she knew how Agatha was feeling.

“Mellizo,” Rio called, “can I steal you mom for a bit please? I’ll bring her back, I promise.”

“Okay but then can I show you my new words?”

Rio smiled and nodded once, already holding her hand out to take Agatha’s when she got closer. It didn’t take long. Rio shot her mom a smile that let her know she’d be bringing Agatha back soon, and happier, if at all possible.

She pulled Agatha out to the backyard and towards her dad’s favourite tree where she turned to settle on the ground and tugged Agatha, who fell willingly, down with her.

Rio transferred Agatha’s hand from her right to her left and draped her other arm around her back.

“You shut me out in the car.”

She said it softly, aiming for a fact rather than an accusation.

“I didn’t. I… I didn’t want to be overheard.”

Rio nodded slowly, placing her chin on Agatha’s shoulder. “It’s hard having people around all the time. I’m not used to it yet, I-…”

But Agatha had pulled away. She was standing again and Rio’s arms were empty.

“Baby,” she called, frowning as Agatha began to pace up and down and Rio soon had her knees in her arms just for something to hold on to.

“That shirt is… that shirt is freedom. When I didn’t have you I held it to my face every night just so I could sleep. I, I pictured you on the beach in it, grinning like an idiot in it. I heard your voice doing that stupid accent when you wore it. I… it was all I had of you for… for so long. It was my freedom.”

Rio nodded slowly and placed her hand cautiously on the ground beside her where she patted the grass three times in the hopes it would be enough.

pat pat pat

Agatha had stopped pacing, she’d looked over and seemed to hesitate for a moment before she took a step and then sank down heavily beside Rio. A moment later, Rio had her arm around her again and Agatha had turned to sit with her back to her so she could be held properly, and Rio could press a soft kiss to her warm cheek.

“Nicky has a matching one,” Agatha trailed off softly, looking down at the ground and reaching to rub along Rio’s forearm that sat across her front.

“But you have me now. You’re free. And I’m not going anywhere. Regardless of how much coffee gets spilled on me I’ll still be here.”

Agatha scoffed softly and leaned back more so she could turn to look at Rio properly. She held her hand up to her face and traced a line along her cheek.

“I gotta pay that man’s rent just so he doesn’t tell your mom how I acted.”

Rio raised her brows, “oh, she’ll already know.”

Agatha looked mildly panicked but then rolled her eyes because Rio was grinning so hard and turned away.

“You’re so irritating.”

“That right?”

“Yeah.”

“Hmm. Can I irritate you into sex tonight?”

“Absolutely not.”

Rio huffed and muttered, “you let me last night.”

Agatha side-eyed her. “Maybe a quick one.”

“Really?!”

“Very quick and very quiet and-…”

“You’re always quick,” Rio reminded, receiving a slap to the arm for her cheek.

Rio laughed and relaxed back into her dad’s tree, her eyes on the sky as she held Agatha close to her. She watched the clouds roll by for a while and felt infinity being traced along her skin before she asked: “Is it me? Are you worried I’ll leave?”

“No,” Agatha’s word was quick and quiet, “I’m worried you’ll be taken. I… when you said you were going for a run earlier… It just brought back…” Agatha trailed off.

Rio nodded slowly, lolling her head to the side to look at Agatha’s profile as she focused on her ring.

“Happiness is new to me,” Agatha said slowly, choosing her words carefully. “I’ve felt it with Nicky, the day he was born was the happiest day of my life but… otherwise… not so much.”

Rio pulled her arm slowly from around Agatha to raise it so she could turn her cheek towards her and could meet her gaze, “We’re together now. We’re engaged. I’ll do my best to make sure you’re happy everyday for the rest of your life.”

Agatha’s lips twitched into a tentative smile and she leant in to rest their foreheads together, “I know, I know you will.” Rio smiled and Agatha held her hand against her cheek and for a second everything was silent apart from the wind in the leaves and the birdsong in the trees.

“It is ugly though,” Agatha whispered, making Rio reel back with a laugh, her head on the tree again.

“Such bad taste.”

Agatha gasped indignantly and Rio found her sides suddenly attacked by powerful fingers until she was squealing on the ground and the thunder came to check on the stars.

Once saved from Agatha, Rio was taught the Spanish words Nicky had just learnt. She knew them already, of course, or thought she did. But apparently she was pronouncing “arcoíris” wrong and wasn’t allowed another coffee until she nailed it.

The rest of the day went by a little easier, with Rio throwing out her new vocab every chance she got an being particularly attentive to Agatha, sneaking in extra kisses whenever they had a second to do so. And Agatha, true to form, curled in every chance she got. When Anna was buried in the pantry seeking some tin of something for the dinner, Agatha was quick to press in to Rio’s throat and kiss her there before she returned.

And Nicky, back to his usual bouncy self now he was more comfortable with Anna, was speaking only in Spanish, being gently corrected by his mom and Anna whenever he stumbled. Rio was always quick to point out that the corrections to her own Spanish were never gentle but everyone ignored her.

They ate at the table again that evening, never running out of fresh gossip to discuss or stories from Rio’s childhood to rehash, and when Nicky asked if Anna had any home videos of Rio - she didn’t - they all agreed they could watch one of Rio’s first jobs that evening with dessert on the couch.

So Rest & Relaxation was put on the tv, because Anna had the box sets signed by the entire cast to hand in the little cabinet beneath it, and they all took their seats to enjoy.

After the first episode and after Rio had gotten over the cringe of seeing her mid-twenties self, Rio’s gaze drifted slowly from the television and instead took in the view that was just for her. First, there was Agatha, at the other end of the couch, on her side, playing idly with Nicky’s hair as he sat on the floor. Both of them were glued to the tv, both in their own worlds enjoying the action on screen.

Then came her mom, curled demurely in her dad’s favourite armchair, her smiling eyes on the tv too.

Two of the three people, three of her favourite people in the world, were dressed like her. Or, at least, wearing her clothes. And as Rio looked now, she realised, perhaps for the first time, just how loved she was.

Nicky had raided her wardrobe in LA and again in this home, and had chosen one of her old sweaters from childhood. And Agatha was fully draped in her clothes. She’d have to check later but she predicted that her bag would be full of them because right now she was wearing Rio’s sweater, her sweatpants, and even her socks.

She wondered if Agatha was wearing her underwear too. And maybe her fingers were as well because she soon found her hand creeping up to the waistband of her stolen sweats and she was just shifting them down an inch to check when Agatha’s hand reached to catch her.

Much to Rio’s surprise, instead of slapping her away, she squeezed her fingers and tugged her hand up, placing it behind herself and without having to say a word Rio knew what she wanted.

As she began to scratch Agatha’s back she turned back to the screen and watched her younger self sauntering across it.

She wished she could tell that Rio what this Rio now had. But she’d never have believed her.

The Rio on screen was a Rio who’d met Agatha Harkness but couldn’t even believe her own memory about a bathroom in a grimy bar in Chicago. The Rio in the picture smiling at her from the fireplace was a Rio who had been tangled up in Agatha Harkness but would never believe they could make it. And the Rio now scratching the back of her fiancée, believed everything.

They spent two more days with Anna, going for walks around the neighbourhood, little trips to nearby parks so Rio and Nicky could play ball and Anna and Agatha could be impressed with their respective child’s athleticism. They drank wine at the dinner table, they reminsicied about Miguel, they watched movies and laughed together.

And on the final day, wrapped in special brown paper and hand delivered to the door, Rio’s shirt arrived back in pristine condition with the hole no bigger than it had been when it had been handed in at the laundromat. Though Agatha insisted it was twice the size and she’d sue.

Rio later overheard her on the phone to Jen, instructing her to pay the rent of the local laundromat in deepest Delaware.

So the last evening, Agatha sat with Anna at the dining table now clear of any liquids that could possibly spill, and learned how to stitch up a small hole in delicate fabric. The thread she’d chosen was a forest green and Rio thanked her for it when it was present to her to try on, with a proud Anna watching on from the sidelines.

Rio slipped it over her t-shirt and dipped Agatha into a movie-worthy kiss to show her gratitude.

A dance party to celebrate was insisted upon by an enthusiastic Nicky and so, on their last night together, Rio danced with her little family and collapsed into bed later that night with an aching face from all the smiling she’d done.

Agatha, insistent as her son had been earlier, wanted to celebrate in their own way, and so Rio, still grinning, now in only her shirt that hung open so Agatha could see her own las chicas, fucked her finacee the best way she knew how.

They panted together, Agatha two orgasms in her tally, Rio one. And Agatha koala’d in, her left hand curled around Rio’s rising and falling ribs as they settled together.

“I’m so happy,” she breathed into warm skin, “you make me so happy.”

Rio drifted of with Agatha’s soft breath against her throat, and by the time she woke she was aching all over for a night spent crushed below a needy Agatha who in the night had rolled totally on top of her to fulfill her desire to be closer.

Not that she minded.

Breakfast was a little more subdued than usual, because soon Jen and Alice would be arriving with Val to help take them all to the airport that evening for their scheduled jet to get them to Europe.

Agatha kept close all day, because she knew Rio was already sad about leaving her mom all alone in the small house that was too big for one person. But Anna insisted she didn’t want to come with them, no matter how many times both Rio and Agatha, and even Nicky, had asked.

So, after a couple hours spend in the company of Alice and Jen, Anna waved them all off at the door. And, in a total reverse of how she’d greeted them, she held Rio the longest as they said goodbye and very nearly squeezed the life out of her in the process.

She managed to hold back her tears until she was settled in the first SUV next to Agatha and only let them come silently, turning to get a last look of her mom waving from the door as they pulled away.

Agatha squeezed her hand and kissed her cheek and it was enough acknowledgement for Rio to take a few deep breaths and calm herself, aided by Nicky, who delivered a new little handmade rose into her lap for this very occasion.

“Gracias, mellizo.”

“De nada, melliza.”

Getting to the airport was easy, getting on the plane was easy too. Everyone carried their own small bags, and Rio had the additional baggage of Nicky. The jet was larger than any Rio had been on before, not that she’d been on many. It had a bedroom in the back, and the seats were far more luxurious than the ones she’d seen before. Not to mention the buckets of champagne about the place and the promise of chef-prepared meals and plenty of snacks.

“It’s a palace!” Alice, very uncool about the whole thing, announced as she first stepped on just ahead of Rio.

And Rio heard Nicky gasp by her ear as they moved through the space, Rio shooting a grin at the staff as they greeted them with champagne. She didn’t miss that there were two chocolate milkshakes on the tray too and she took one she knew Agatha would have arranged for her as Nicky took his own.

“Mi vida, this is insane.”

Agatha, reading glasses piled on her head and her book in hand, smirked as she chose her seat in the middle of the plane and Rio was cautiously let Nicky down onto his feet.

“You like it?”

“Are you kidding?!”

“Everyone’s on an NDA,” Jen reminded from her own seat, her own glass of champagne somehow already half-finished, “But still… no canoodling.”

“What does that mean?” Nicky asked happily as she sucked his shake through his straw.

“It means,” Agatha said with a glare in Jen’s direction, “we have to all behave.”

Nicky nodded seriously as if this were his plan all along.

And Rio, not happy to just sit just yet, marched up and down the length and breadth of the plane, looking into every nook and cranny and soon inheriting a shadow who did it with her as the others settled in and the staff busied themselves with preparing for takeoff.

The place was like a palace, Alice had been right about that. Everything in the highest spec, the most luxurious fabrics, the best food and champagne all laid out for them to indulge themselves on the long trip over the Atlantic.

As she arrived back to take her seat with Nicky for take off, she caught Agatha watching her and raised her brows in response.

“Happy?”

“Beyond.”

Agatha grinned and the engines kicked into gear as the plane began to taxi along the runway and they all buckled up, Rio doing a quick check of Nicky’s belt before she settled properly.

They were soon in the air, soon at altitude, soon able to get up and move around and grab whatever they wanted in terms of snacks and food, though most of it was already brought out to them.

For a while, Agatha was silently reading with her glasses perched on the tip of her nose and her legs curled beneath her. Jen was typing on her laptop and Alice was watching a game on her phone. Nicky was reading his book too and so Rio, antsy to get moving again, went ot explore some more and soon found herself up in the cockpit with the Captain who showed her all the buttons and let her have a shot in his seat.

This, she decided, was much better than flying commercial.

Nicky was soon up front too and got to do just as Rio had, but he got to wear the hat and Rio felt a little cheated that she hadn’t also been given that little perk. It was Agatha who stole them back, apparently missing their company now she was done reading and she only had Jen for entertainment.

So they went back with her and for a while they talked about all the buttons and Nicky proclaimed her saw a cloud that looked like a duckling, which Rio readily backed up even though she’d seen no such thing.

The champagne was flowing and conversation moved on until Rio decided that something needed to be done that hadn’t yet been done. Something very important.

“Oh god,” Alice said as Rio stood up, “here she goes.”

Rio laughed loudly as she stood in the aisle with her glass of champagne, doing her best to ignore the fingers that had magically appeared at her hip, dipping into her loose sweats to hold her steady. Not that there was any risk right now of turbulence.

“To my little family!”

“My love,” Agatha chided gently, still holding on when there was absolutely no need to.

But then suddenly someone else was holding on. Nicky had put down his Switch and had run over to collide with Rio’s front, wrapping his arms around her to grin up at her. She laughed as she brushed a hand through his hair.

“To my mellizo and his beautiful mama!”

“You’re so gross,” Jen said from across the way, sipping her champagne without toasting to anything Rio was saying.

“And!” Rio announced loudly because Agatha had rounded on Jen and looked about to snap. “To my wonderful manager and her just okay girlfriend.”

Nicky snorted just like his mama and Agatha whipped her head around to grin at Rio as Jen scoffed from her seat.

“Cheers!” Rio shouted, holding her champagne up as Nicky tucked his head in against her stomach and cuddled in properly. Agatha was out of her seat in a second, coming in hot to press Nicky between them and steal a kiss from Rio with a mouthful of champagne.

“To us,” she said quietly, wrapping her arms around Rio to hold Nicky’s hands across her back.

“To jetskis,” Rio teased, wriggling her brows at an eye-rolling Agatha.

“To big yachts and big fish,” Nicky added, lifting his head back up to grin at them both from his side angle as he was squashed between them.

Rio laughed as Agatha hummed happily and pulled back in a way that allowed her to duck down and kiss Nicky’s cheek.

Nicky’s nose scrunched and Agatha scrunched hers right back as Rio, feeling drunk suddenly at just the sight of them, said: “You too are the cutest people on the planet.”

Agatha looked back up at her and raised her brows as Rio grinned stupidly.

“Enough! I’m not watching this for thirteen hours.”

Rio laughed as Agatha pulled away to point a threatening finger in Jen’s direction.

“I’ll push you out of this plane, Jennifer.”

Rio ushered Nicky back to his seat, giving him a quick squeeze of his shoulder as she followed along behind him and flopped down into her own chair across the aisle from Jen.

“I would trust her on that one, Jen.”

Jen rolled her eyes, “Can’t believe the two of you are engaged before me. So ridiculous.”

Rio was laughing again, apparently unable to stop herself. She felt so giddy.

But as Jen and Agatha started to bicker, Nicky was curled up in his seat beside her with his Switch and Alice was in Rio’s eyeline, as happy and amused as she was.

She raised her glass to her and Alice raised her own back and for a moment they silently congratulated one another on both bagging two total babes who just so happened to be two total mentalists.

The bickering lasted until Rio’s glass was empty and Alice went to pour her another.

“Don’t you do that for her,” Jen said quickly. “We’re not on the clock right now. This is our vacation too.”

“Oh so she can’t pour my fiancée and her friend a glass of champagne? That I am paying for, need I remind you.”

Alice raised her gaze to Rio as she topped her glass up and Rio rolled her eyes at her, neither of them saying anything as Alice made the rounds with the bottle and Jen and Agatha continued to snipe.

Rio relaxed back, watching Agatha for a while with a dreamy smile on her face as they charged a course for Europe in their sleek jet. Alice was doing the same with Jen, watching her as though if she looked away she might actually be thrown from the window.

And Nicky, soon putting his Switch down was yawning dramatically with his hands in the air and making soft, performative mouth noises after his poorly executed yawn.

Rio counted to ten before he was yawning again. Another ten and then he was slipping into the space beside her on her seat and yawning for a third time. This time, Rio wrapped her arm around him after leaning over to place her glass in the little holder on the arm.

“Ready to sleep?”

“Just sleepy. Can I stay here a bit?”

“Of course.”

The bickering had stopped now and Rio didn’t have to look around at Agatha to know why. Though she did. Of course she did. Any excuse to look at Agatha and Rio would take it. Opposite her, sitting in her same seat was Agatha, toying with her new engagement ring, her eyes on the two patitos in their now shared chair.

Jen would have shut up when Agatha had turned her attention to them, she was sure of it.

Bickering was their love language, which meant it would always stop when Agatha was more focused on her littlest and best love who was now curled into Rio’s side, yawning properly for the first time.

“I’ll get you a blanket,” Agatha said, standing from her chair.

“The horse one please, mama. It’s the best one.”

Rio grinned as Agatha grimaced but Rio knew exactly what blanket she’d be returning with.

“We should get some sleep too,” Alice said to Jen who nodded and then knocked back the wine she’d been drinking. “Wanna share?”

Jen shot a glance at Rio briefly and then nodded, which made Rio smirk because the moment her head moved even an inch, Alice was running to her. She hid her amusement by turning more into Nicky and soon enough was covered by the ugly blanket that she loved so much.

“Room for one more?”

Rio looked up at Agatha’s hopeful gaze and grinned at her. “Isn’t there a bed in back? Maybe we should-?”

But Agatha was already clambering on beside her, squeezing herself in as she pressed the button to recline the chair all the way.

“Close is better,” she said with a look that told Rio she better not protest because this was happening.

Rio sank down with the chair, smiling as Agatha remained upright until the seat was fully reclined and only then did she shuffle down and settle into the crook of Rio’s arm.

“Sickening,” Rio heard Jen mutter from across the way. But she didn’t care and apparently neither did Agatha because she didn’t say anything and instead had reached across to touch Nicky’s cheek.

It soon became clear that it was too hot like this. Nicky was too wriggly and the only person who seemed to be comfortable was Agatha.

Rio and Nicky suffered for ten minutes, occasionally giggling together and giggling harder with every one of Agatha’s harrumphs at their giggling. But it wasn’t tenable. They would be giggling all night but neither of them would get any sleep.

So Nicky clambered off and settled in his own seat beside them, curling himself into the corner of it as Rio reached to help him lay the chair flat.

“Mama needs more cuddles than I do anyway.”

Rio just knew Agatha was glaring at her son.

“She really does, mellizo. Very desperate for-…” she yelped because Agatha had dug her fingers into the exact spot that always elicited that exact reaction.

Rio groaned as she shuffled in the makeshift bed and Agatha was doing her best to throw one half of the horse blanket towards her son.

It was like that, comfortable like that, they all slept for a while. They were woken halfway across the Atlantic by the crew who were offering them specially prepared meals. Rio gladly agreed to hers and said Agatha would too because she knew Agatha was pretending to still be asleep but that she needed to eat.

Dinner was served against the black of the night sky, lit up by distant stars. Nicky had his dino nuggets and Rio had a pollo guisado that was almost as good as her mom’s. She did steal a dino nugg, though, and Nicky took a mouthful of her food in exchange.

The bickering between Agatha and Jen had kicked off when the food had been served and Alice and Rio exchanged glances as if to say “the whole trip, huh?”. But mostly the rest of the journey was smooth, with more naps, more time for Nicky to play his Siwtch, more reading time for Agatha, and more snacks and offered booze than any of them could handle.

It was the airport that was bad.

They landed in Italy, far from any private terminal. And when this had been communicated to them from the pilot via the groundstaff, Agatha had torn into him immediately. It had taken Jen and Rio to calm her down and remind her they had not only their own security, but the airport staff to help.

So, the little group with Val in front and the two largest of them, Thor and Wilson, up the rear, all made it out into the terminal. Nicky was on Rio’s back, his head down and his cap on and Rio was glad of it because somehow their presence was already known.

It wasn’t paps that were the problem, but instead, people. They were everywhere, swarming towards them as the staff and security pushed back. By Rio’s count there must have been at least fifty of them trying to get close, offering picture of Agatha’s smiling face to be signed and filming their arrival for their TikTok or Instagram followers.

It was hell.

But they got through it together with the help of Val leading the way and Agatha’s reassuring, close presence helping Rio not to panic in the crowd with her precious cargo on her back.

After that, everything was okay. Jen was a little jumpy about so many people already knowing where they are but she kept repeating “private, not secret” to herself like a mantra in their seven-seater SUV with Agatha, Nicky, and Rio, squeezed in the back - as was Nicky’s preference. And Rio had to admit riding in the back of such a large vehicle did feel more fun.

Agatha complained only until she realised she was practically on top of Rio in this seat and then she shut up pretty quickly.

They made it to the port after a short car ride and were directed to a private entrance round the way. Rio leant with Nicky to gape at the huge ships they were passing; some with big sails, some without.

But it wasn’t until they spotted a ship with a uniformed crew waiting on the deck with a tray of champagne and what looked like a soda for Nicky.

They all piled out and Rio stood with her mouth open as she looked up at the yacht named My Dragon and felt utterly breathless for the sheer size of it.

“Holy shit,” Alice gasped, and Rio agreed with that sentiment entirely.

“Do you like it?” Agatha’s voice floated into her consciousness, and Rio looked around as she slipped her arm around her waist.

Her expression was hopeful and Rio couldn’t believe she had any doubt in her mind that Rio wouldn’t like the superyacht that they were about to spend a month travelling around the Med on.

Nicky arrived before them, his eyes more on the uniformed crew than the yacht now. But Rio only had eyes for her Agatha.

It still felt like blinking into the sun sometimes when she looked at her. She was so beautiful and radiated so much warmth that Rio always turned to her, wherever she was.

But Agatha’s gaze drifted slowly from her own, distracted by something that wasn’t the yacht, and wasn’t the crew.

“The moon,” she said in a whisper, “it’s out.”

Rio turned to see and sure enough, high in the sky, translucent above the water, there it was.

“Wait right here,” Rio said as she looked up at it, “I’ll lasso it for you; put it right in your hand.”

Rio turned back to look at Agatha and saw her ocean eyes were drowning in their own tears. And there, on their private dock, in view of the crew, their friends, and their son, Agatha thanked her with a kiss.
